about: Synthetic data. Hand-written skeleton (marina.json + marina_extra.json) expanded by Beam-1.0-501B-A23B. Marina is fictional.

capsules.text: First day back in Curitiba after the holidays. The bus was late, the rain got inside my shoes, and I still forgot my umbrella. Drew a tiny self-portrait in the condensation on the window. Future me: did you ever stop forgetting umbrellas?

First day back in Curitiba after holidays. The air smells like rain and someone's chimarrão. I miss Matinhos already, which is embarrassing since I was complaining about sand in everything two days ago. Drew the sea from memory on a receipt while waiting for the bus. It looks nothing like the sea.

First day back in Curitiba after the holidays and the air already smells like wet concrete. Packed my bag twice because I forgot the adapter. On the bus I noticed a woman crocheting a blanket from sleeve to sleeve, nonstop, and I drew her hands three times without looking at the face. The driver honked at a cyclist and she didn't even flinch. I hope I still notice people like that when I'm older.

Woke up late for the UFPR vocabulary exam and ran to the stop with one shoe untied. It rained, of course. The bus came with the doors already open, like an invitation. I studied the whole ride and still forgot the word for 'embarrassment', which feels symbolic. Later I bought a coxinha and ate it standing under the marquise, watching people with umbrellas. Curitiba in January is just a long argument with the sky. I also drew the shoe in my notebook during the exam. I think I'm going to like this city.
First day of a new year and I'm still drawing in the margins of every notebook I own. Mom would say it's a waste of ink. I say it's the only part of class I remember.

First week in Curitiba without Mom's cooking and I already miss her arroz com feijão. The RU pasta today was suspiciously orange. I saved money for a pastel de feira instead and felt very adult about it.
O dia começou com sol e acabou com tempestade, como sempre em Curitiba. Fiz um desenho no ônibus e esqueci de assinar. Tudo bem, ninguém pedia autógrafo mesmo.
First week of university hasn't started yet, and I'm already tired. I packed three sketchbooks by mistake and forgot my calculator. Bia says this tells you everything about me. She's not wrong.

Primeiro dia do ano e já saí de casa sem guarda-chuva. Curitiba fez chuva na hora que eu saí do ponto. Cheguei na faculdade de preparatório com o tênis cheio de água e fingi que era normal. O motorista do busão quase riu. Vou comprar um guarda-chuva pequeno que caiba na mochila. Promessa de ano novo: não deixar o tempo decidir minha roupa.

On the bus home from Vila Izabel I saw an old woman carrying a bag of oranges and smiling at no one in particular. I drew her oranges before I drew her face. That felt backwards but right. I want to remember that some people just smile, without needing a reason I can see.
First day of vestibular cram school. The chair wobbles, the teacher talks fast, and the girl next to me draws flowers on the margin. I asked to see her pencil. It's a 2B. I want one too.

First week back in Curitiba and the rain is horizontal. The bus driver didn't even bother closing the door properly, so my Álgebra notes are now abstract art. I drew the puddle on my knee instead of solving matrices. Future me: if you're still bad at matrices, I'm sorry and also I told you so.

Portuguese: Sonhei com a Vó Lúcia cantando alguma coisa sem letra, só a melodia. Acordei com saudade de um lugar onde não moro mais. Desenhei a melodia em linhas onduladas, que não faz sentido para ninguém além de mim.

I almost missed the bus today and ran with my backpack open. A pencil fell out and rolled under the 7am Interbairros II. The driver waited. I picked it up, out of breath, and thanked him. He said 'vai sonhar, menina'. I don't know if he was talking to me or the parrot.

Mom, if you're reading this, I'm writing from the bus stop in São Francisco. Your bolo de fubá is in my bag and I ate half of it already. I know you packed extra 'for the girls'. Thank you. I'm going to be fine.
Mãe, if you're reading this through me somehow: I did eat breakfast before leaving. It was pão with manteiga and I ate it standing at the sink. Count that.
Bia and I split a pastel de feira and argued for an hour about whether the sea smells better in Matinhos or in Guaraqueçaba. I say Matinhos because of the fries. She says I have no taste.
Mom sent a box with bolo de banana and a note saying 'não esqueça de comer'. The bolachas survived the trip better than the bolo. I ate both in bed and felt briefly very young.

Acharam meu caderno de desenho velho na gaveta da cozinha. A Bia disse que meu desenho do papagaio do ônibus parece um pato de terno. Ela tem razão, mas vou fingir ofensa. Coloquei o caderno na mala pro próximo semestre. Se um dia eu virar ilustradora, isso vai ser prova de que comecei mal. Se não virar, vai ser prova de que tentei. As duas opções me parecem bem.

Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He put extra farofa on my plate without asking and pretended not to. Mom told the same story about my first day of school, Vó laughed and said I cried louder than the whole class. I drew Vó Lúcia's hands around the coffee cup when nobody was looking. They're smaller than I remembered. Or maybe I'm bigger now.
Drew the rain from my window on Rua XV. The gutter sounds like a snare drum. I spilled coffee on the corner of the page and decided it's part of the weather.

Called Vó Lúcia today. She pretended she wasn't waiting and then talked for forty minutes about the farm in Irati and a dog called Coronel who walked her to school. I want to draw this one day. I keep saying 'one day'.
Mãe, I ate the RU beans today and they were actually good, which feels like a small miracle. Don't tell anyone I said that.

Drew the lemon tree behind Vó Lúcia's house from memory before I even left the kitchen. The leaves came out too big, but the trunk felt right. I keep thinking about what she said: 'desenho não é luxo, é memória.'

Rain all day. Stayed in the apartment with the big window in Vila Izabel and finished a drawing of the lemon trees on the street. The owner downstairs yelled at a dog for peeing on his gate and then gave the dog a piece of bread. I think that's the whole city in one man.
Mom made caldo verde and insisted I take half the pot back to Curitiba in a plastic container. The lid leaked on the bus. I smelled like cabbage until Tuesday.

Mom sent a box: bolachas, instant coffee, and a note asking if I've eaten 'comida de verdade'. I ate the bolachas for dinner and called it field research. There's a lemon in the fridge nobody claims, so I'm considering adopting it.
January energy. I made a list of things for the year: pass Cálculo, draw one page a week, call Vó every Sunday. Three things. I already missed Sunday. Starting tomorrow. Probably.
Rain all week in Curitiba. The bus windows fog up and I draw smiley faces in the condensation like a child. Nobody sees because everyone is looking at their phones.
Calculo at 7:30. I understood exactly two minutes of the lecture and spent the rest drawing the professor's mustache from different angles. His mustache has improved more than my math.

Bia, today I found our old friendship bracelet in the drawer of my childhood room. Green and yellow, slightly frayed. I'm taking it to the república. If this opens and we're still friends, I owe you a new one that matches.

I spent three hours looking at art supplies online and bought a single 2B pencil. Mom would say this is the problem with me: one dream, fifty excuses. The pencil feels heavier than it should. I'm putting it on the desk where I can see it, next to the sociology handout I'm supposed to read.

Bia, if you're reading this three years later, remember the day we tried to cook dinner and forgot the rice was still on the stove? The república smelled like burnt everything and one of the girls ate a cheese sandwich with a heroic face. We laughed so hard I couldn't breathe. You said 'adult life is just deciding which mistake to eat'. I still think that's a good line. Save it for your future stand-up career.

Bia brought me a box of bolachas from Mom. Wrote 'MARINA' on the box so nobody eats them. The fridge now has three names on three yogurts and one on cookies. We are very organized people with no self-control.

Bia, you told me engineering would be hard and you were right, but you forgot to mention the boredom. Sat in Física for three hours and drew a whole page of waves in the corner of my notebook. The professor asked what I was writing and I said 'notes'. He believed me. I feel like a spy in my own life.
Woke up at 5:10 to catch the Interbairros II. The sky was still dark and the city smelled like rain on hot asphalt. I prefer it this way.

UTFPR opened today. The hallway is full of people who look like they know what they're doing. I don't. Calculus syllabus is two pages long and I understood the word 'integral'. That's my victory for today.

Bia, if you're reading this, we probably just fought about something small and dramatic, like who finished the açaí. You're still my favorite person to be wrong with. I'm leaving this in my drawer until it's time.
Ate pastel de feira with Bia after class. She talked about São Paulo like it was a person. I talked about the sea. We both pretended not to notice. It was a good pastel. The sea can wait.
Bia tried to make me float in the inflatable pool on the república's terrace. I panicked after four seconds. A six-year-old watching from the street probably thought I was ridiculous. Fair.

Found a piece of paper in my coat pocket from last October with a tiny drawing of a parrot and the words 'bom dia' next to it. No idea when I wrote it. Probably on the bus. The paper is soft from being folded so many times. I'm keeping it in the sketchbook now, like a ticket.
Bia, we need to make a pact: no matter where we end up, we always text on our birthdays. Even if we're mad at each other. Especially then.

Packed almost everything tonight. The only thing I can't decide is the drawing Vó Lúcia framed. It's coming with me, obviously, but where do I put it in a room with four other girls? Above the bed, probably, if the others let me. If not, above the desk. Or under the mattress again, which would be very 17 of me.
Portuguese: O espelho do banheiro da república tem um trinco que só fecha se você chutar a porta duas vezes. Todo mundo sabe. Ninguém arruma. É o tipo de problema que vira cultura.

Packed almost everything for the república move next week. Found my old sea drawing that Vó framed, the glass is cracked in one corner. I'm taking it anyway. Also found a sock under the bed that I don't recognize, which is worse than the sock I do recognize.
Bia, you promised to come visit when I moved. I haven't moved yet but I'm already claiming the best bed in the república. Please bring your playlist and the pink towel I always steal.
Bia brought heart-shaped brigadeiros to the república. We ate them on the floor because the kitchen table was covered with laundry. A normal Valentine's, no romance, just sugar and friends.
Valentine's Day and nobody sent me anything, which is fair because I forgot too. I ate two coxinhas at the RU and drew a heart on my calculus notebook. It looked like a potato. Progress.
Valentine's with no date, only a bag of bolachas from Mom and a calculus problem set. Ate the crackers while solving integrals. Not romantic, but not bad.

Three days before the move and the apartment is full of boxes. I labeled one 'important' and it has only a framed drawing and a spoon. The spoon is for the future, when I'll eat alone and remember the RU. The drawing is for now. Vó Lúcia's face is slightly tilted in the frame. It should be.

Moved into the república on Rua XV today. Four girls, one bathroom, a fridge with names on every yogurt. My room smells like old wood. I put the drawing of the sea Vó Lúcia framed for me above the bed. Future me: is it still above your bed?
Second day in the new room. The wood smell is stronger at night. I hung Vó Lúcia's drawing with two pieces of tape because I don't own a hammer yet. It is slightly crooked and I love it.

Tio Beto, I broke your third string by accident and put the violão back in its case like nothing happened. If you find this before the capsule opens, I'm sorry and also I'm sorry I didn't tell you in person.

Day five in the república. I already know which shelf in the fridge is mine and which girl takes someone else's yogurt by accident. The bathroom schedule is written on a post-it with a smiley face. My room smells like old wood and someone else's lavender soap. The sea drawing is up. Vó's frame is still cracked. It looks like it belongs here.
Bia, you called at 11pm to say your mom found the marker we used on the bar wall. She scrubbed it twice and it's still there. We're leaving it. That's our wall now.

First laundry day in the new house. I put a red shirt with white clothes, exactly like Mom warned me not to. Now all my socks are pink. I'm choosing to call it fashion. The lemon tree seed idea hasn't arrived yet, so I can't promise anything about it, but I will say this: I already like having a windowsill with possibilities.

Moved in a week ago and I still wake up confused about which door is the bathroom. The wooden smell is stronger at night. I put the drawing of the sea Vó Lúcia framed above my bed and it looks like it belongs there. I hope it stays.

Third day in the república. The bathroom schedule is already a diplomatic treaty. I got 7:40am on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The fridge has a shelf with my name, but Limonada the yogurt cup hasn't sprouted anything yet.
Pra que ter vergonha de pedir ajuda no exercício de álgebra? Seu Ivo do ônibus também não sabia contar marmita no início, segundo o próprio motorista. Todo mundo aprende devagar.
O cheiro de madeira velha no meu quarto já virou cheiro de 'casa'. Acho que é assim que a gente começa a pertencer a um lugar. Desenhei a prateleira com meus potes de iogurte etiquetados.

Bia, hoje o Interbairros II veio com um cheiro de pão recém-assado que só pode ter sido de alguma padaria misteriosa no caminho. O motorista freou mais devagar do que o normal, como se também quisesse sentir. Acho que foi a viagem de busão mais calma da minha vida. Se você ler isso, faça um desenho mental de um busão cheirando a pão. É isso.
UTFPR cafeteria queue today lasted 40 minutes. I drew the back of a guy's neck in my notebook because it looked like a small mountain range. Someone asked if it was a graph. I said yes, of suffering.

Woke up at 6:10 for calculus and the sky was pink in that unfair way, like it knew I had to leave. On the bus a little boy showed his mom a drawing of a house with smoke coming out of the chimney, and she said 'muito bonito' without looking up from her phone. I wanted to tell him it really was muito bonito.
Breakfast with the girls: rice from yesterday, a fried egg, and coffee that tastes like it was punished. We talked about shampoo and ex-boyfriends for an hour. I drew the egg on the napkin.

Calculus at 7:30 and I understood derivatives for twelve whole minutes before my brain shut down. The professor writes so fast it looks like a medical prescription. I drew the parrot man from memory instead. He has a better jawline than calculus.

It's 6:10am and I'm waiting for Bus 7am, Interbairros II, in the dark. There are exactly seven of us and everyone is pretending not to be cold. The man with the green parrot hasn't appeared yet, and I'm worried, which is absurd because I don't even know his name. I drew the bus stop's broken bench instead. Future me, do you still remember which stop has the bench with the missing leg? I hope yes.
Engineering professor said 'drawing is for architects' when I was sketching in the back row. I kept sketching. He saw. Said nothing. Small victory, logged.

Hi 23-year-old me. I'm 18, it's the first week of engineering at UTFPR and I already miss drawing in class instead of paying attention. Mom says illustration is a hobby, not a job, so here I am, calculus at 7:30am. Promise me two things: you will keep drawing, at least one page a week, and you will finally learn to swim. It's embarrassing to live in Brazil, dream about the sea every night, and not know how to swim. Also: call Vó Lúcia every Sunday. She pretends she doesn't care, but she waits by the phone.

Engineering orientation had a professor who said 'you'll learn to think'. I thought: I already think, I just think in shapes. I drew the campus map from memory during the talk. It was wrong, but prettier.
Calculus at 7:30am. I understand derivatives when I draw them as slopes on little hills, so I drew a hill with a cow on it in my notebook. The TA asked if I was taking notes. I said yes.

Failed Cálculo 1. I'm writing this crying in the RU so that next year you remember it wasn't the end of the world. Also, I haven't drawn in two months. I know. I know. I'm writing it down so I can't pretend later.
St. Patrick's nothing in Curitiba, but the RU had green gelatin. I drew a four-leaf clover on my hand and showed everyone. Nobody cared. The clover looked like a spider. I kept it anyway.

First week of classes survived. I already have a pen pal in the row in front of me, a guy who draws robots in his margins. We haven't spoken, just swapped notebooks twice by accident. I think this counts as friendship in engineering. I drew the bus parrot man today from memory and it looked more like a potato with wings.
Chamada at 7:30. I sat in the third row and drew a girl's sneakers instead of copying the derivative. The professor didn't notice. I felt both guilty and proud, which seems to be my default setting.
Calculus at 7:30, body in Curitiba, soul somewhere near Matinhos. The professor wrote 'limit' and I thought of the sea horizon. Nearly failed the quiz.

Calc 1 at 7:30 and the professor talks like the numbers are personally offended by us. Drew a small ocean in the margin while he explained derivatives. It had a boat. I know. I know. But my hand needed to go somewhere or I was going to scream.

Rain all day, the kind that turns the campus into a small sea. My shoes are soaked and I forgot an umbrella again. The bus windows fogged up and I drew a tiny sea with my finger. Nobody saw, or if they did, they were polite about it.

Calculus is a language where everyone speaks confidently and I understand nothing. The professor said 'this is intuitive' and I almost laughed. After class I drew the integral sign as a sad worm. The girl next to me asked if I was an art student and I said 'engenharia', and she looked at me like I had lied about my age. Maybe I did.

Wait, wrong year—no, this opens next month, quick capsule. I just wanted to tell you I found the parrot man again on the Interbairros II. He was wearing a yellow raincoat today. The parrot said 'bom dia' and I felt like the day was officially approved.
Second note for future me: the parrot man with the yellow raincoat. I'm not fixing the previous one. Time capsules are allowed to be chaotic.

It rained so hard the street became a river and I had to walk barefoot to the bus stop. An old woman offered me a plastic bag for my shoes. I declined. Regretted it. The bag would have been dignified.
Mãe, eu sei que você acha que desenho é hobby. Continuo tentando fingir que não ligo. Mas desenhei você hoje, lavando louça, e ficou bonito. Guardado.
Called Vó Lúcia at 8pm exactly. She talked for forty minutes about the weather in Irati and the neighbor's dog. I drew her while she talked, from memory. Her nose is hard.

Bus 7am, Interbairros II. The parrot said 'bom dia' today and the driver actually smiled. Drew them in the margin of my Álgebra notebook, as always. The parrot's feathers are impossible to get right with a ballpoint pen.

I ate at the RU with three girls from the republica and we talked about whether engineering is worth it. Nobody said yes, but nobody said no. That's the mood of March. Later I drew the RU lady serving rice and she looked like a saint in an apron. She gave me extra feijão today. Connection.

RU lunch: rice, beans, a piece of chicken that tasted like it had given up. Sat with three girls from Civil and one of them said 'drawing is nice but it doesn't pay the RU'. I laughed and agreed. Then I went home and drew the chicken. It looked brave.
Mãe, I ate vegetables today. They were in a sopa from the RU and I didn't ask what they were. I'm counting it as adulthood.

Portuguese: Chamei a Vó hoje e ela me contou que o Coronel latia para o carteiro todo dia, mas nunca mordeu ninguém. Acho que isso é o que ela acha de mim também. Estou levando para o caderno de desenhos.
Rain all week. Rua XV flooded at the corner near the bakery. One of the girls in the república wore rain boots to class and looked extremely pleased with herself.

Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He had the violão out but only played for five minutes before his fingers hurt. Vó Lúcia ate the farofa with one hand and stole meat with the other. Nobody said anything because it's her farofa in spirit. I wrote down the chords he showed me in the margins of the bulletin, just in case.

Sunday call with Vó Lúcia. She talked for forty minutes about the weather in Irati and the price of jabuticaba. I didn't interrupt. At the end she said 'menina do mar, when are you coming to visit?' and I almost cried in the república hallway. I said soon. I don't know when soon is yet.

Tio Beto, I practiced the three chords for twenty minutes today before lunch. My fingers hurt in a way I didn't know fingers could hurt. I still can't switch to F without looking like I'm fighting the guitar. Don't tell anyone.
Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He made churrasco and told the same story about the time he almost got a motorcycle in 1983. I still don't know if it's true.

Found a small cafetería near UTFPR that sells pão de queijo for a real. The owner calls me 'a menina do caderno de desenhos'. I didn't correct him. It felt too good to be the drawing girl, even for ten minutes.

Mom called to say she sent a box with bolachas, a winter scarf I don't need yet, and a note that said 'study, don't daydream'. The scarf is beautiful and the bolachas are already gone. I found a sketchbook page inside the scarf, probably from 2012. Mom pretends she didn't keep my drawings. She keeps all of them. This is not new information, but it still makes my chest warm.
Rained so hard the street became a river. Bia and I walked home with our shoes in our hands and she sang something terrible. I laughed until my stomach hurt. The drawings in my bag survived, mostly.

Tio Beto's birthday is coming and I forgot to buy anything, so I drew him a violão with a face and a hat. Mom said it's 'cute, for a hobby'. I put it in an envelope anyway. He'll probably hang it in the garage next to the tools.

R$ 412 left and it's the third. I ate at the RU and pretended the rice was enough. A girl in my class brought bolachas and gave me two without asking. I said I wasn't hungry, which was a lie, and she said 'I know, that's why I brought extra'. I'm counting her as a friend now.

Tio Beto taught me three chords on his old violão at Sunday lunch. I promised him I'd learn to play 'Asa Branca' all the way through by the next Festa Junina. He laughed and said he's heard that promise from every cousin. Prove him wrong, Marina.
Tio, your violão still smells like smoke from the churrasco. I practiced the three chords you taught me until my fingers hurt. I'm not quitting this time. Maybe.

Tio Beto came by with his violão and left it leaning against the fridge for an hour. I touched one string. It buzzed like a mosquito. He said, 'one chord at a time, menina.' I said I only have three fingers of courage.
Found a one-reais coin in my jeans pocket. Bought a coxinha at the terminal and felt absurdly rich for ten minutes.

The lemon tree behind the republica's kitchen has tiny green lemons. I touched one and it smelled like summer, which is stupid because it's April. I brought one inside to draw it and the housemother said 'don't bring the garden into my kitchen'. Fair.

Found an old notebook from high school in my suitcase. There's a comic I made about our math teacher, Sr. Alceu, turning into a parrot and explaining quadratic equations. I read it three times. It's funnier than anything I've done this year. Why did I stop? I know why. Mom. But still.

Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He let me touch the violão but only the E string. I made a sound like a dying cat and everyone clapped anyway. Promised him Asa Branca by Festa Junina. We both know how this goes.

Bia came to Curitiba for the weekend and we got lost looking for a bar in São Francisco. We ended up eating pastel in the rain and laughing too much. She said my hair looks like a nest. I'm considering the nest look permanent.

Primo Leonardo visited the república and brought a violão that was missing one string. We played three songs badly and the neighbors clapped anyway. My fingers still hurt. I think that counts as practice for Tio Beto's promise.

Tio Beto came to Curitiba today with his violão and a bag of pinhão. He played for twenty minutes in the kitchen and all four of us sat on the floor because there weren't enough chairs. I still only know three chords, which is not enough for 'Asa Branca' but apparently enough to make everyone clap. He said I have 'orelha boa', which from him sounds like a marriage proposal. I want to learn more, but I'm also scared of disappointing him. One verse and a promise, that's where I am.
Sunday at Tio Beto's. He let me play exactly four chords before taking the violão back and saying 'you need patience, Marina'. I need pastel too, so I ate two.
Bought a sketchbook at the papelaria near campus with my own money. It's small enough to fit inside my calculus folder. That feels rebellious.

Rain all day. The república roof leaks in the kitchen, so we put a pot under it and every drip sounds like someone tapping. I wrote a song about the tap in my head. No music, just words. Maybe one day.
The república fridge has a new yogurt with my name on it, and someone drew a tiny fish on the cap. I suspect Lívia. I choose to be flattered.
There's a lemon tree in the yard of the house across the street. I stared at it on the way to the bus and missed the 7am. The parrot man was already gone. Felt like I lost two good things before 8am.

The lemon tree behind the kitchen has one lonely lemon. I drew it from three angles like it was a model. The housemother said 'it's just a lemon, Marina'. I said 'not yet'. She didn't ask what I meant and I didn't explain. That's fine. Some things are just for me.

Bia, you said I'd love the república because 'there's always someone to borrow sugar from'. True. But there's also always someone reheating fish at midnight. The fish girl apologized by leaving a brigadeiro on my desk. I ate it at 7am before class. Good morning to me.
Portuguese: O papagaio disse 'bom dia, motorista' e eu respondi 'bom dia, Juca' baixinho. O senhor não ouviu, ou fingiu que não. Deu um tapinha nas costas do papagaio. Achei bonito.
Money check: R$ 180 left and it's not even the 28th yet. Ate RU feijoada twice and felt rich. Mom's bolachas are doing the emotional heavy lifting this month.

Engineering lab today: measuring vibrations in a tiny motor. I liked it more than I expected. The other students made spreadsheets. I made a small diagram in the margin that looked like a robot sneezing. Nobody asked for it.

First swim lesson. Okay, not a lesson, Bia trying to teach me in her building's pool. I kicked and splashed and drank the pool. A little boy in floaties stared at me with pity. Bia said 'you're not scared of the water, you're scared of not being good'. I'm putting that on the fridge door.
Tio Beto mandou áudio dizendo que eu não treinei violão e ele tá certo. Prometi de novo. Ele riu, mas não alto. Isso é progresso.
Sunday call with Vó Lúcia. She asked if I was eating. I said yes. She said, 'eating what?' I changed the subject to the weather. It worked for approximately eight seconds.

Dreamed of Vó Lúcia's farm again, the one in Irati. There was a dog I've never met, but I knew it was Coronel because he waited at the gate like he'd been doing it forever. I woke up wanting to draw him, but I don't know what he looks like. Future me, did I ever find out?

O senhor do papagaio não estava no Interbairros II hoje e senti uma coisa estranha, como se tivesse perdido um capítulo de uma série. Desenhei o papagaio sozinho em um galho imaginário. Achei que ficou bom. Depois ele apareceu, atrasado, com o pássaro dormindo no ombro. Alívio que não faz sentido.

There is a lemon tree on the sidewalk near the república, next to the padaria, and someone tied a yellow ribbon around it. I don't know who. It doesn't have lemons yet, just flowers that smell like something I can't name. I stood there too long after buying bread and the padaria man asked if I was okay. I said yes. I wasn't anything, which might be the best kind of okay. I drew the ribbon in the margin of my Álgebra notebook. The parrot man has competition now.
The parrot man wasn't on the bus today and I realized I was scanning the seats like I lost a friend. I don't even know his name. I drew the empty shoulder anyway.
Bus 7am, parrot man. Today the parrot said 'bom dia' and the old man corrected him: 'bom dia, motorista, com licença'. The parrot repeated the whole thing. I laughed alone. Worth it.
Bus at 6:40 because I missed the 6:20. The driver didn't brake for the usual pothole, so we all slid forward together like a slow-motion avalanche. Nobody complained. I think we were all half asleep.
Eu desenhei o ônibus inteiro hoje no caderno, inclusive o papagaio. A velhinha do lado perguntou se eu era artista. Disse que não. Ela disse 'parece'. Fiquei pensando nisso a tarde inteira.

The parrot man said 'bom dia, motorista' again. The driver actually smiled today. I drew them both before the next stop and missed my transfer, but I think it was worth it. The parrot had its head tilted, like it was posing.

Rain again. The bus driver today had a thermos of coffee and a tiny flag of Grêmio hanging from the mirror. I sat behind him and drew the flag the whole way to UTFPR. It looked happy, even though Grêmio lost yesterday. I don't even like football. That's the power of a tiny flag.

Dreamed of the sea again. Same dream: warm water, feet won't move. Woke up with tight calves and the feeling that I had been standing for hours. Drew the edge of the water from memory, but it keeps coming out blue-grey.

Today I learned that RU feijão on Tuesdays is actually good if you add the farofa and don't think too hard. I ate two plates and then studied until my highlighter died. Engineering is mostly endurance and beans.

Bus 7am, rain. The parrot was quiet today, tucked under the man's coat. Only his eye was out. I drew just the eye and the coat and it looked like a tiny emperor. The bus smelled like wet dog and bread. I love this city a little more on rainy mornings.

Mother's Day lunch at Tio Beto's. He tried to teach me three chords again and I got two right. He said 'progress'. Mom said 'draw less, study more'. I drew them both at the table afterward, while they argued about rice.
Dreamed of the sea again. I was standing at the shore and the water touched my toes. That's new. I woke up and immediately drew my own feet, which is not a thing I usually do.
Tried to run three laps around the quadra today. Made one and a half. My lungs said no. My pride said yes. My legs sided with my lungs.

Vó Lúcia sent lentilhas again. I ate them on the floor with Bia because the table was full of notebooks. She told me the story of Coronel again, slightly different: this time he waited at the gate for nine years and one extra winter.

Mom, hoje eu comi arroz com feijão no RU e pensei em você. A senhora da cozinha coloca o feijão meio doce, não como o seu, mas eu comi tudo. Prometo não reclamar da sua comida quando eu for pra casa no fim de semana. Até porque se eu reclamar, você não faz bolo de fubá, e isso eu não sobrevivo.
Calc exam grade came back worse than expected. I sat on the curb outside UTFPR and drew my shoe for ten minutes. The shoe has more detail than my answer sheet. Not proud, just honest.

Money check, early: R$ 180 left and it's only the 12th. I ate polenta at Tio Beto's on Sunday and pretended I wasn't hungry for dinner. He noticed and made me take home a container of feijão. I'm writing this so 22-year-old me remembers that being broke also meant being fed, somehow.
O velho do papagaio deu comida pro passarinho antes de descer. O motorista esperou sem reclamar. Hoje o ônibus parecia um lugar seguro.

Bus 7am, Interbairros II. There's an old man who carries a green parrot on his shoulder every single day. The parrot says 'bom dia, motorista'. Nobody on the bus reacts anymore except me. I drew them both in the margin of my Álgebra notebook.

Mãe, se você estiver lendo isso, eu não desisti dos desenhos. Eu só os coloquei embaixo do colchão porque você perguntou. Ainda desenho no ônibus, nas margens do caderno, e às vezes na mão quando acaba o papel. A engenharia está bem, mas a mão pede outra coisa.

Failed the first Álgebra test. The paper had red marks like a map of somewhere I've never been. I drew a tiny sea creature in the corner before handing it in, just to make the page less sad. The professor didn't notice. Or did and judged me. Either way, I need to study.

Rain all day. The roof in the hallway leaks exactly above my door, so I moved my bed closer to the window and now I can hear the bus passing at night. It's a strange lullaby: brakes, tires, someone coughing. I drew the leak as a teardrop with legs. The girls laughed and put it on the fridge, next to the yogurt names. I think this is what living in a república is: one leak, four opinions, and a drawing nobody asked for.

Interbairros at 7am. The parrot man was there with his green parrot, same as always. Today the parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' right as we stopped at the hospital. I drew them in the margin of my Álgebra notebook again. The parrot's beak is hard to get right.
Bia, if I ever become the kind of person who says drawing is just a hobby, please slap me. Gently. But slap.

Dreamed of the sea again. Same one: warm water, feet stuck, the feeling that I'm late for something. Woke up with tight calves and an urge to swim that I can't use yet because I don't know how. One day.

The old man with the parrot on the bus smiled at me today. I'm counting it as friendship. I drew them both again in my Álgebra notebook, but this time the parrot is bigger and has a slightly annoyed expression. I think that's how he actually looks.
Money check: R$ 120 left and the month isn't over. Ate arroz com feijão at the RU three times and had crackers from Mom's package for dinner. Not starving, just tired of crackers.

Vó Lúcia asked if I'm eating enough. I said yes. She didn't believe me and packed me lentilhas and a bag of oranges. I carried the bag on the bus like a ridiculous person. It smelled like her kitchen.
Money check: R$ 120 until payday. Bought a cheap sketchbook and instant noodles and felt the contradiction in my bones. The noodles were bad. The sketchbook is good.
June in Curitiba means cold hands and hot chimarrão at 7am. I am a person who owns a chimarrão now. 18-year-old me did not see that coming.

June already and I haven't drawn a full page in a month. Only margins: bus seats, a pigeon, the parrot, the sad rice at the RU. It still counts, right? Please tell me it counts. I'm going to do one page today even if it's bad. Especially if it's bad.
Portuguese: A Vó me perguntou no telefone se eu já desisti dos desenhos. Eu disse que sim. Mentira. Tenho caderno sob o colchão como se fosse coisa ilegal. Pelo menos sou consistente.
Mom sent a box: bolachas, a sweater I already own, and a note that says 'study'. I ate four bolachas in one sitting and wore the sweater to prove a point nobody asked me to make.

Ate dinner with the girls in the república and we argued about which city has the best pão de queijo. Nobody agreed. I drew everyone's opinion as a tiny pie chart in the steam on the window, which melted in thirty seconds.

I found an old notebook from high school with drawings of the sea in every margin. Same sea, same line I can't cross. I'm 18 and apparently I've been standing at the edge for years. That's a strange thing to realize on a Tuesday.

Dreamed of the sea again. Same one: warm water, my feet stuck. But this time the sky was full of parrots, hundreds of them, all saying different things. I woke up laughing, which has never happened. Drew a parrot in the sea before breakfast. It didn't make sense. I didn't care.
First week of June and Curitiba is pretending to be winter. I wear three layers and still my hands are cold while drawing. Made hot chocolate with cinnamon because that's what Vó does when it rains.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was in a kitchen and the window faced water, but the door was locked from outside. Woke up thirsty.
Dreamed of the sea again. Same dream. I was closer to the water this time, but still not in. Woke up and drew the wave from memory before it disappeared.

I planted nothing this year, but the basil on Jéssica's windowsill is huge and smells like someone's grandmother's kitchen. I stood there for a while smelling it. Jéssica said I'm weird. Fair. But I think anyone who ignores a good smell is weirder.

Bia, future Bia, I hope you still remember the night we sat on the república roof and tried to count satellites. We saw three for sure and one airplane we pretended was a satellite because we wanted it to be. You said the sky in Curitiba is lower than in Matinhos. I think you meant the stars, but I liked the idea of the whole sky pressing down on us like a blanket. If you ever feel lost, look up first. It's the cheapest advice I have.

June in Curitiba and I'm wearing a sweater in the library. The girl next to me is knitting a scarf while studying. I drew her hands because they were faster than my brain. Also, I miss the sea today for no reason at all.
June rain again. The república roof leaks in the hallway exactly where the light switch is. We put a bucket there and named it 'o quinto morador'. It has no rights but a lot of water.

Ate a pastel de queijo at the feira near UTFPR that was so good I considered writing home about it. The vendor folded the paper into a little pocket and said 'cuidado, escorrega'. I ate it in four bites. Worth it. I'm going back next Saturday with Bia.

Festa Junina at a friend's house. I didn't dance quadrilha because I don't know the steps and refused to learn in public. Ate three corn cakes and felt spiritually redeemed. Tio Beto would be proud of the eating, at least.

Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was sitting on the sand with someone I couldn't see. The water was calm and my feet were dry. Woke up feeling like I had been given something and forgot what it was. Writing it down before it disappears.
Bia, seu bolo de fubá salvou meu domingo. Comi três fatias e prometi tomar mais água. Não tomei. Mas pensei em você.
Passed the first Álgebra exam by two points. I am choosing to celebrate with a pastel, not with tears.

Washed clothes by hand because the machine was broken and the landlord said 'amanhã' for the fifth day. My arms are sore. I drew a comic of me fighting a washing machine while it was still raining outside. The machine won.

We wrote our names on the wall of a bar in São Francisco last week and I keep thinking about it. If the wall's been painted over by the time you read this, that's fine. We were there. I was there with Bia, with a marker, feeling like a legend.
New bus driver today. He didn't know about the parrot greeting and jumped when Juca said 'bom dia, motorista'. By the end of the ride he was smiling. I drew that too.
Festa Junina prep at Tio Beto's. I helped cut flags and burned my finger on the iron. He put honey on it and called me careless. Fair.

Bia, se você ler isso, lembra daquela piscina do seu prédio? Hoje fiquei quatro segundos boiando. Quatro! Depois afundei e fiz drama. Mas foram quatro segundos de não-morte. Vou levar isso como conquista. O menino de boia nem olhou, mas eu vi você comemorando. Valeu.

I tried to float in the pool at the building next door. Lasted about three seconds. A kid floated past me like a relaxed leaf. I pretended to check my phone underwater, which is not a real thing you can do.

Bia, I taught you nothing today because you already know everything about bus routes. But you did make me laugh so hard on Interbairros that the old man with the parrot turned around and the parrot said 'shh'. I think we were the first people he ever shushed. We're famous now.
Mom sent a package from Curitiba to Curitiba? No, from her house to the república. Bolachas, a scarf, and a note that says 'study'. I ate the bolachas in one sitting and wore the scarf to bed.
Tio Beto, prometo que não vou esquecer do 'Asa Branca' este ano. Mesmo que eu erre tudo, vou tentar até o fim. Se eu falhar de novo, você pode me chamar de 'prima que só promete' e eu aceito.

I wrote our names on the wall of the bar in São Francisco last night. Bia held the marker like a sword. If the wall's been painted over by the time you read this, that's fine. We were there. The marker smelled like alcohol and youth.
Festa Junina at school. I ate three paçocas and danced quadrilha with a boy whose name I already forgot. He stepped on my foot twice and said 'sorry' four times. Balanced.

Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I ate four paçocas and played the violão until my fingers hurt. Didn't attempt Asa Branca, only the three chords. Tio Beto said 'next year' and I said 'next year' and we both knew it might be true this time.

Festa Junina at the university. I won a cocada and lost a dance-off to a guy wearing a fake mustache. The quadrilha was chaos, but good chaos. I ate two pamonhas and drew everyone's boots in my notebook. One of the girls from the república saw the drawings and said I should illustrate a book. I said 'I'm in engineering', and she said 'so what?'. She's right, but don't tell her I said that yet.

Dreamed of the sea again. Same dream since I was a kid: I'm standing at the edge, the water is warm, I want to go in and I can't, my feet won't move. I wake up with my calves tight. Five years from now, I hope the dream changed.

July in Curitiba and I'm wearing two sweaters. The república window has condensation like a drawing of a lake. I traced a lemon tree in the fog and left it there. Someone later added a tiny sun with sunglasses. I don't know who. I liked it.

Went to São Francisco with Bia for your birthday month prep and we ended up sitting on the curb eating churros. A cat sat between us and refused to move. We named it Festa Junina. I drew the three of us. The cat looks dignified. We do not.
There's a cat that lives under the república's staircase. It has one eye and no fear. I named it Nelson. Nelson ignores me beautifully.

Beach day in Matinhos with Bia and cousins. I only went in the water up to my knees, same as always, but I let a wave hit my shorts and pretended it was accidental. Bia noticed. She didn't say anything, just handed me a towel and a pastel.

Ate a lemon at the república because there was nothing else and then planted three seeds in a yogurt cup with MARINA written on it. The fridge rules made it official. If even one sprouts, I'm keeping it forever. Small, stupid promise.

Rainy Wednesday. The bus was late, so I stood under the awning and drew the street. An old lady looked at my sketchbook and said 'você desenha bonito'. I said thank you and then spent ten minutes wondering if she meant it.

Curitiba winter is personal. The bus window fogs and I draw faces on it, then feel guilty because someone has to clean it. The girl next to me saw me draw a fish and said 'legal'. That's the whole story. Sometimes that's enough.
Dreamed of the sea again. Same one: warm water, feet stuck. Woke up and drew my feet in the sketchbook, just the feet, like a crime scene. It helped, a little.
Bus was delayed 40 minutes. The driver apologized to everyone individually, including the parrot, who said 'bom dia' at 8:42am like it was normal.

Tio Beto, I practiced 'Asa Branca' three times this week and I can now play the first verse without stopping. The second verse is where I fall apart, like a bridge made of paper. Next time you come over I'll play it for you, but please don't clap until I finish or I'll lose my nerve.

Dreamed of the sea again. Same dream, same warm water, same stuck feet. But this time I was holding a drawing of the sea in my hand, which is new. I woke up with my calves tight and annoyed at my subconscious for being poetic. I'm going to start writing the dreams down, because maybe one day they change and I want proof. Today I also learned how to make miojo better: an egg, a little butter, and pretending it's not miojo.

Swimming lesson #? I haven't started lessons yet, but Bia tried to teach me to float in the pool at her building. I lasted four seconds before panicking. A kid of maybe six floated next to me the whole time, out of pure spite, I think.

Vó Lúcia called and asked if I'm learning to swim. I said 'trying'. She said 'the sea doesn't wait for people to be ready'. Then she changed the subject to the bolo de fubá. I wrote the sentence down. It sounds like something she'd say in a novel, except she says things like that all the time.

Mom, you asked if I'm eating enough. I am, mostly RU rice and beans and the bolachas you send. The last batch disappeared in two days because I shared them during a power outage and everyone was hungry and emotional. Sorry.

Summer not here yet but the heat already is. My room faces the afternoon sun and smells like old wood and hot pencil. I put a fan on the desk and it blows my papers everywhere. The fan has more personality than my grades.

Seven months of this república and I still can't find my keys in the morning. The bathroom mirror has toothpaste from four different toothbrushes. I drew the fridge with the names on every yogurt because it looks like a tiny city of dairy. Future me, did the fridge ever become less ridiculous?
Sonhei com o mar de novo, mas dessa vez tinha um cachorro correndo na beira. Não consegui entrar na água, mas quase. Quase conta? Espero que sim.

Cold weekend. Stayed in bed reading a book about lighthouses that I found in the república bookshelf. One of the girls, Jéssica, said lighthouses are 'sad architecture'. I drew one with a face anyway. It looked hopeful, which is the opposite of sad, but maybe she meant something else.

Winter in Curitiba is a personal attack. My room is cold enough that I draw with a blanket over my legs and gloves with the fingertips cut off. The drawing of the sea looks warmer than the room, which feels like a metaphor I'm not smart enough to use.

Fui à piscina do clube com a Bia. Ela flutuou de costas por trinta segundos e eu fiquei segurando na borda tentando imitar. A água entrou no nariz. Decidi que não sou pessoa de piscina, mas também não desisto.

The bus was so crowded I had to stand with my face in someone's umbrella. The parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' from inside a cage today. I drew a tiny cage in the notebook and felt sad about it all day.

Bia, today I tried to make that bolo de fubá from Vó Lúcia's recipe and it came out like a brick. I think I forgot sugar. Or maybe I put salt twice. The girls ate it with yogurt and lied politely. Write back and tell me your grandmother's version, I know you have it.
Festa Junina at a church near the república. I ate three paçocas and danced badly with a stranger in a checkered shirt. Nobody knew my name. It was perfect. I drew the lanterns on the way home.
Portuguese: A Bia fez 18 anos ontem e a gente escreveu nossos nomes na parede do bar em São Francisco com caneta. Se pintaram por cima quando você ler isso, tudo bem. A gente esteve lá.
Mom, yes I'm eating. No, I haven't given up on drawing. Yes, I still miss home sometimes. No, I'm not switching majors. Love you.

I told Mom illustration is just a hobby and she said 'good'. Then I drew the sea in my sketchbook for twenty minutes under the blanket. The sketchbook lives under the mattress now like it's something illegal. Future me, was the mattress a good hiding place?

Vó Lúcia told me about Coronel, the farm dog who walked her to school. She laughed telling it today, not cried. That's rare. I want to remember her laughing, not just the sad parts. Her laugh starts high and falls like stairs.

Tio Beto sent a voice note playing 'Asa Branca' on the violão, slightly out of tune at the second verse. He said 'practice'. I played it back three times and my roommates asked who was dying. I love him so much.

Bus 7am and the parrot said 'bom dia' before the driver even opened the door. The whole bus heard it. Nobody reacted except one man in the back who smiled. I'm sure that smile was worth the ticket price. Drew them both fast, in pencil, while standing.
Bia's birthday soon. I made her a card with a drawing of our names on the bar wall. It took three attempts because I kept smudging the ink.

Mom, by now you've probably asked me again if I gave up on the drawings. I didn't. I won't. The sketchbook is under the mattress, which is childish and dramatic and also works. You wanted me to be an engineer because you're afraid of me being hungry. I understand. But I also want you to know: every time you call and ask about my grades, I answer, and then I open the sketchbook after hanging up. Both things are true at the same time.
Hot day, bus full, and the parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' twice. Once wasn't enough. I respect that kind of commitment. I drew him with a tiny tie today because he looked formal.

Bus 7am. The parrot man wasn't there today and I worried the whole ride. Then I saw him at the final stop, buying a newspaper, and the parrot was eating a piece of apple from his hand. I didn't draw them. Some things you just have to see and let be.
I drew the república kitchen at midnight: four mugs, one without a handle, the fridge with all the names. It's the most honest drawing I've done this year.

Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I played Asa Branca until the second verse and then forgot everything. He clapped anyway and said 'one more year'. One more year. I drew his hands on the violão when I got home.

Studied for Cálculo 1 until my eyes burned and then drew a bus from memory to calm down. It came out crooked, like it was turning. Maybe it was turning. Maybe everything in my notebook is a little crooked because I'm holding the pen wrong.

Money check: R$ 120 left and it's the third. The girls in the república are sharing pasta like it's a survival strategy. I'm eating the bolachas Mom sent as if they're a meal plan, which they kind of are.
Calculus exam tomorrow. I understand derivatives in dreams and forget them awake. This is either a metaphor or a problem. Probably both.

Bia's birthday is coming and I have zero money for a present. Made her a card with a drawing of the two of us at the bus stop in São Francisco. It took two hours and looked like we were standing in a flood. She'll love it. She loves bad drawings of herself, it's a known condition.

Mom called to ask if I'm eating well. I said yes. I lied again. The RU chicken has improved though, or my standards have dropped. I think it's the second one. I sent her a photo of a plate of rice and beans and she replied with three emojis and a question mark. Fair.
Limpamos a república inteira em sábado. Encontrei meu desenho velho do mar atrás da cama. Agora ele fica na parede, com fita isolante.
Bia came to visit. We ate pastel de feira and she made me promise to learn to swim before 20. I said I'd try. She said 'try harder.' Fair.

Bia's birthday is in three days and I have no money for a real gift. I made her a comic strip about the two of us at the RU, with the waiter who always gives us extra farofa. It's not fancy, but it's us. I hope she laughs.
Bia's birthday party was at the bar in São Francisco. We sang badly, ate too much, and she made me promise to call her when I pass Cálculo. I promised. I will probably need to promise again.
Bia's 18th birthday. We wrote our names on the wall of the bar in São Francisco with a marker. If the wall's been painted over by the time you read this, that's fine. We were there.
We wrote our names on the wall of the bar in São Francisco yesterday. Today I went back alone to check if it was still there. It is. I felt weirdly protective of two names in marker on a brick wall.

Went to Bia's house for your birthday and we wrote our names on the wall with a marker, just like planned. The wall was damp and the marker bled. Bia's name is perfect. Mine looks like I wrote it during an earthquake. That's fine. We were there.
Tio Beto lent me his violão for one weekend. I learned two chords and forgot them by Sunday. He said that's how everyone starts. I think he's being kind.
Bia's 18th birthday party. We ate brigadeiros until we felt ill and then ate more. I gave her a drawing of us as kids, but she looked like a potato. She said it was perfect. She is too kind.

The interbairros bus broke down and we waited twenty minutes in the sun. The parrot man bought water for everyone from a cart. He didn't announce it, just handed bottles. I drew him with a halo, then erased it, then drew it again smaller. Heroes should be allowed to be tired.

Bia's birthday party at the bar in São Francisco. We wrote our names on the wall with a marker, slightly crooked because she was laughing. I wrote 'MARINA + BIA = LEMBRAR' and now I can't remember what I meant. Maybe that's the point. There was a dog sleeping under a table and I drew it on a napkin. The marker smell stayed on my fingers all night. Good smell. Like being eighteen and allowed to make small monuments.

Calculation mistake in my homework cost me an entire evening. I stared at the board and thought: this is what my life looks like if I don't draw. Then I drew the professor's tie and felt better. Not productive, but better.
The lemon tree at Vó Lúcia's backyard dropped fruit on the ground. She told me to pick them up before the ants got ideas. Her hand was steady when she pointed.

Bia, your birthday wall graffiti is still on my phone. We looked ridiculous in that photo. If this opens and the wall is painted over, that's okay. The marker fades, but the fact that we were there doesn't. I think about that a lot.
Calculus exam. I studied. I think I did okay. I also drew a small sea creature in the corner of the test paper, which I regret and also don't.
Money check: R$ 12 in the account, four days until allowance day. Living on instant noodles and hope. If future me has money, please remember this noodles.
Bia's birthday was last week and the wall writing is still there, at least in my head. We went back to check if it had been painted over. It hadn't. We added a small star next to our names and left.

Bus parrot man wasn't there for a week and I was genuinely worried. Today he was back with a bandage on his hand. The parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically. I'm counting it. Drew both of them again, slightly worse this time.

Swimming lesson thought: there is no swimming lesson. I walked past the pool on campus and watched an old man doing slow laps. He looked so calm. I stood there with my notebook and drew him instead. That counts as research, right?
Mom asked if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said yes. I lied. The sketchbook is under the mattress like something illegal. At least I'm consistent.

Money check, early: R$ 120 left and it's the 4th. Not the 28th, which means I'm getting worse at budgeting, not better. The RU helps, but the bolachas Mom sends help more. I ate bread with banana for dinner and told myself it's a regional dish. It is not. I also bought a eraser shaped like a cat because it was R$ 2 and I needed a win. The cat eraser is now my most valuable possession.
A senhora do ônibus 7h me disse 'bom dia, menina do desenho' hoje. Eu quase caí da cadeira. Meu desenho de ontem tinha ela no canto. Ela não tinha visto, mas foi simpática.

Mãe, I lied when I said I gave up on the drawings. I have a sketchbook under the mattress and I draw almost every night. I'm not asking you to understand yet. I'm just telling the mattress. And now you.

Money is R$ 410 on the 5th, which feels rich until I remember textbooks. I bought a pastel and then felt guilty enough to draw a budget in the margin of my notebook. It looked like a flower. I'm not good at budgets.

Called Vó Lúcia and she talked about the farm for forty minutes. Coronel, the dog, walked her to school every day and waited at the gate. She said this like it was normal, like every farm has a dog that does that. I don't have a dog yet but I want one that waits at gates.

Friday night at the república, everyone in the kitchen making popcorn and arguing about music. I sat on the floor with my sketchbook and drew the scene badly and happily. I think this is what home feels like without being at home.

Found a tiny lemon tree in a pot outside a flower shop on Rua XV. It was R$ 12 and I almost bought it, but the república windowsill is already full of Jéssica's basil and someone else's succulents. I stood there for five minutes talking myself out of it. Maybe next year. I'll remember this.
First time I drew in the middle of a lecture and the professor didn't notice. Felt like a tiny superpower. Physics, still boring, but pretty on paper.

Drew the lemon tree at Tio Beto's house while everyone else was watching the game. It's small and crooked and full of lemons that look like green eggs. He said I made it look better than it is. I said that's the job.

Bia's birthday energy is still in the apartment. We cleaned the bar names off our shoes but not off the wall. I keep thinking: small marks, big feelings. Very 18 of me. Drawing the bar counter from memory.
Cafeteria pizza today was mostly bread. I drew it as a landscape: mountain crust, river sauce, cheese snow. Bia said it looked like the Curitiba skyline. She might be right.

Portuguese: O velho do papagaio não apareceu hoje no ônibus e eu fiquei genuinamente preocupada. Amanhã vou de novo cedo. A motorista perguntou se eu estava procurando alguém. Eu disse 'um papagaio verde'. Ela não insistiu.
The república fridge has a new sticker: 'MARIANA, STOP EATING MY YOGURT' on a pot that is not mine. I didn't eat it. I considered it, but I didn't. I drew the pot anyway because it looked sad.

R$ 280 for 19 days. I'm not writing this to be dramatic, I'm writing it so future me laughs. Or cries. The RU bread is actually not bad if you add the butter Mom sends. I'm eating a lot of bread. The bread and I have an understanding.
Rained so hard the república's roof leaked in two spots. We put pots under them and the drips made a rhythm. Slept to it.
The parrot man wasn't on the bus today. I worried about it more than I should have. The seat where he usually sits had a newspaper on it, which doesn't prove anything but felt suspicious.

Vó, eu ainda ligo todo domingo, como você pede. Hoje você contou a mesma história do Coronel e eu escrevi tudo, até a parte que você diz que ele era 'muito educado para cachorro'. Seu riso começa alto e vai descendo. Eu não quero esquecer isso.
I reorganized my sketchbook by month instead of by subject. Now it looks like a diary with drawings instead of words. Better.

Swimming still not happening. I looked at the pool schedule at UTFPR and there's a beginner class at 7am. I'm awake at 7am anyway, on the bus. That's my excuse. I know it's my excuse. I wrote it down so next year I have to stop using it.

The parrot man was back today. The parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' in the exact same voice as always. I almost cheered. I drew them again, better this time, with the man's mustache and the parrot's green chest. If you still have the Álgebra notebook, keep page 14. I don't know his name. I decided today to call him Seu Ivo in my head. It fits him somehow. Don't ask me why.
I told Mom I stopped drawing. She said 'good, focus on the course'. Then I went to my room and drew a page of the lemon tree at the república. It felt like stealing. I'm getting good at stealing.
Tried to learn three guitar chords from a YouTube video. The violão had a broken string and I spent an hour looking for the tuner app. Tio Beto would laugh. I laughed first.
Called Vó Lúcia. She talked about the jabuticabeira and how it's heavy with fruit. She said I could come pick some in spring. I hope you remember this promise.

Mãe, I lied again when you asked about drawing. I have a sketchbook under the mattress. It has 14 pages of bus people and one page of a parrot. I'm not giving up. I just don't know how to say that yet.

One of the lemon seeds sprouted! Two tiny leaves. The girls named it Limonada. It lives on the windowsill next to my sketchbook, which no longer hides under the mattress. This might be the best thing that happened this year.
Cold morning. The república's window doesn't close all the way. I stuffed a sock in the gap and felt like a genius. Then the sock fell out at 3am.

Called Vó Lúcia on Sunday. She said the jacarandá in front of the house is blooming purple and that I should draw that, not the sea. She's right, but I like having both. She told me about Coronel again, just one sentence. I wrote it down twice.

Bia, you told me engineering would ruin my handwriting. You were right. My 'a' now looks like a 'o' and my 'e' looks like a tired line. But my drawings are still fine, which means my hands know what they're doing even when my head doesn't. I'm holding onto that.
Money check before payday: R$ 120, a half bag of rice, and three apples. I made a drawing of my wallet as a desert. The apples became camels. Future me, please tell me the desert ended someday.
Portuguese: Chuva forte, ônibus atrasado, e o senhor do papagaio apareceu com um saco plástico furado sobre a gaiola. O papagaio disse 'bom dia, motorista' mesmo assim. Respeito profissional.
Fim de mês apertado. Comi arroz com ovo e fingi que era jantar de restaurante. A gema quebrou bonito no prato. Pequenas vitórias.
Money check: R$ 340 left for the month and it's the 28th. Living on RU and the bolachas Mom sends. I'm writing this so in two years I can laugh at it. Or cry. Depends.

Money is tight again. R$ 290 left and it's October 1st. I made a spreadsheet on the back of an Álgebra page and it didn't help. RU and bolachas from Mom for now. I'll laugh at this in two years or cry. Probably both, at the same time, which is efficient.
Bia, I tried to swim again at the clube. Lasted six seconds this time. Progress. Dona Cida, who is seventy and swims like a fish, said 'respira, menina'. I breathed water. Still progress.

Money check: R$ 340 left for the month and it's the 28th. Living on RU and the bolachas Mom sends. I'm writing this so in two years I can laugh at it. Or cry. Depends. Drew a comic about R$ 340 being a small sad animal.
Mom asked about the drawings again. I said no, not anymore, while sitting on top of the sketchbook. The lie is getting easier. That's not good.

Mom called and asked the question again. I said yes, I'm focusing on engineering. Then I drew a tiny version of her face on the edge of the page, smiling. I think she'd like it. I'll never show it to her.

Found a sketchbook under my mattress today, the old one. Opened it and saw drawings of the sea from when I was 14. They're terrible. I love them. I added one more: the república, four girls, one bathroom, a fridge with names on every yogurt.

Drew in class again and got caught by the professor. He said 'nice parrot, bad circuit'. I think that's the best review I've ever received. The parrot was Juca, obviously, even though I hadn't named him yet.
RU lunch today: feijão, rice, something claiming to be beef. I drew it before eating. The beef drawing is more convincing than the beef. Maybe that's a career.

I missed Vó Lúcia's call yesterday and felt terrible. Called her today and she said 'você sumiu, menina do mar', then talked about the weather in Irati for twelve minutes. Her voice is the same as always, low and a little dry. I drew her from memory afterward: the way she holds the phone with both hands, like it's something precious. Maybe it is. I want to draw her more. I don't tell her that. I should.

Sunday call with Vó Lúcia. She waited by the phone, I could tell because she picked up on the first ring and then pretended she had been busy. We talked about the farm, the weather, and Coronel. She told me to eat more.

I practiced floating in the bathtub tonight. The water was warm and nobody was watching. I floated for ten seconds and stared at the ceiling. It wasn't the sea but my calves were loose for once. I think that's what the dream has been asking for.
Mom called to ask if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said yes. I lied. I have a sketchbook under the mattress like it's something illegal.
Money check: I bought a pastel and a bus ticket and now have R$ 8 left. The pastel was worth it. The ticket was also worth it because the parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically again. Two for one.

Bus was late and everyone complained in that tired, resigned way people do. The parrot man wasn't there, which made the bus feel emptier than usual. I drew his empty shoulder and it looked strange, like a branch without a bird.
Mom asked if I had finished 'that math thing'. I said yes. I had not. I am becoming a liar by omission.

Cold morning, I missed the early bus and had to wait for the next one with a coffee that burned my tongue. The old man with the parrot wasn't there. I worried for ten minutes, then he appeared with a banana for Juca. Balance restored.

Bia, if you're reading this, remember the night we got locked out of the república and slept on the hallway floor with the bucket of leak water next to us. You said 'this is the worst hotel in Curitiba'. I said 'five stars for company'. Still true.

Mom asked again if I've given up on drawing. I said yes, louder this time, like volume would make it true. My sketchbook is under the mattress and I felt it through the sheet last night. It's like sleeping on a secret. I'm tired of secrets but not ready to stop.
Bus was full. A man offered me his seat and then immediately regretted it when I sat with my wet umbrella. The parrot said 'obrigado' to me, which was generous.
Álgebra notebook is now 60% drawings and 40% math. My roommate asked if I was studying. I said yes, in a visual way. She didn't buy it but lent me an eraser.

Bus was late and I drew three panels of a comic about the parrot while waiting. A woman asked if I was drawing the parrot. I said yes. She said 'he's called Juca, the driver told me'. I had no idea. Juca. Good name. I'm keeping it.

Mom, I know you said illustration is a hobby. I'm not arguing. I'm just writing here that today I drew the república kitchen with all four of us in it and it felt like the realest thing I've done in months. Don't worry, I still went to class.
Midterm week. My desk is covered in papers and coffee cups. I drew a little version of myself drowning in books and taped it to the wall. It made me laugh, which helped more than the studying.

Bia, today on the bus a man carried a parrot and the parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' and nobody reacted except me. I drew them in the margin of my notebook. You would have laughed so hard you'd miss your stop. I miss your laugh on this bus.

Bia, I miss you in a very specific way: I miss showing you things I drew and watching your face decide if it's good. The other girls in the república say 'legal' and I know they don't look. You always look.

Mom called and asked if I'm 'still wasting time with those drawings'. I said no. I was drawing her during the call. She has a very specific frown when she thinks I'm not taking life seriously enough. I think I captured it.
I passed the first mechanics exam. Barely. Celebrated with a pastel de queijo and felt absurdly proud of myself for 20 minutes.
Went to the pool again. Still can't float. A lady in the next lane told me to relax my shoulders. I relaxed so much I sank. There must be a middle ground.

Tio Beto, if this reaches you two years later, I want to tell you that I practiced 'Asa Branca' exactly twice and both times I cried a little. Not from sadness. From the part where the sanfona comes in. You know the part. I'm still bad at changing chords, but I'm not giving up. You said every cousin makes the promise. Let me be the one who keeps it, even if it takes ten years. I have a feeling about ten years.
Drew Vó Lúcia's hands from a photo I kept in my wallet. They are small and strong. I want to get the veins right one day.

First cold of the year and everyone in the republica is coughing like a choir. I'm drinking chá de gengibre and pretending it helps. The parrot man was on the bus with a scarf and the parrot had a tiny scarf too, or I dreamed it. I think I dreamed it. Still drew it.
Tentei nadar de novo. Dessa vez fiquei cinco segundos flutuando antes do pânico. A Dona da piscina disse 'relaxa'. Não relaxei, mas voltei na quinta.

Day of the Dead without Vó, which sounds dramatic because she's alive, but she spent it talking about everyone who isn't. I sat on the kitchen floor and drew her hands while she told stories. She has hands like a drawing already.

Day of the Dead here feels like everyone is talking about someone. Bia brought flowers to the cemetery and I drew the candles in the chapel. We ate pão de queijo after and didn't talk much. That was enough.

Portuguese: Liguei para a Vó e ela me contou do Coronel de novo, o cachorro da fazenda em Irati. A cada vez ele fica mais corajoso. Desta vez ele enfrentou uma cobra. Estou desenhando cada versão no caderno. Futura eu, guarde esse caderno, por favor.

Bia, you asked if I'm drawing. Yes. I'm drawing people on the bus, the sea from memory, and occasionally a motor I don't understand. I miss you. Come eat RU with me and I'll draw your profile as payment.
November in Curitiba is just October with more fog. The parrot on the bus said 'bom dia, motorista' in exactly the same tone. I admire consistency.

Cold morning. The parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' and the driver said 'bom dia, Juca' back. So the parrot's name is Juca. Or the man is Juca. I don't know which. I drew them both again. This time I added a tiny hat on the parrot. He deserves one.
November in Curitiba means gray skies and laundry that never dries. I hung a shirt on the chair and it stayed damp for two days. Romantic.

Mom called to ask if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said yes. I lied. I have a sketchbook under the mattress like it's something illegal. The lie was easier than the conversation. I hate that I did it.

Vó Lúcia called to ask if I'm eating. I said yes. She asked what. I said 'rice'. She was silent for two seconds, which is her version of a lecture. Then she told me about the jabuticabeira at the farm and how Coronel is buried under it. She tells this story every call. I listen every time.

Portuguese: Sonhei com o mar de novo. Mesmo sonho desde criança: eu na beira, água quente, quero entrar e não consigo, os pés não saem do lugar. Acordei com a panturrilha apertada. Daqui a cinco anos, espero que o sonho tenha mudado.

First cold night that smells like wood smoke from someone's churrasco. I wrapped myself in the scarf Vó gave me and drew the streetlight through the window. The glass had rain, so the light came out as a yellow river.

First cold of the season. Curitiba does this thing where the wind goes through your coat like it has a key. I stayed in bed and drew people from the bus: the man with the parrot, the woman with the big umbrella, the boy who always sleeps. I gave them names. The woman is Dona Lurdinha. The boy is João. It's silly, but naming them makes the bus feel like a small city I own for twenty minutes every morning.
Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He taught me three chords on the violão and said I have 'little fingers but good ear.' I don't know if that's a compliment or a warning. I'm counting it as both.
Achei um limão no fundo da geladeira, esquecido desde a festa do mês passado. Joguei fora, mas fiquei com vontade de plantar algo. Qualquer coisa.

Bia, lembra daquela tarde em que ficamos sentadas na escada da república, comendo bolacha e reclamando da vida? Você disse que um dia a gente ia rir disso. Eu acredito em você mais do que acredito no Cálculo.

I floated for three seconds in Bia's pool today. Three whole seconds. Then I panicked and stood up and swallowed water. Bia clapped like I'd won a medal. The boy in floaties was not impressed. Progress is progress, even wet progress.

Swimming still terrifies me, but I watched a video of dolphins today and felt something close to courage. Not enough to get in a pool. Enough to promise I'll try someday. I'm writing the promise here so it counts.

Went to the Museu Oscar Niemeyer with Bia and spent most of the time looking at the building instead of the art. Bia said that's 'very engineering of me'. I said the curves are just drawings that someone was brave enough to build. She didn't argue. I drew the eye-shaped museum from the outside later, at home, with a parrot flying past it.
Found an old pencil stub in my jacket from high school. Used it to draw the old man on the bus. His bird looked proud today.
Bus comics idea, but I haven't drawn them for anyone yet. Just margins. The parrot man has a mustache in my version, even though he doesn't. Artists lie. It's in the job description.
The república fridge has names on every yogurt now, including mine. Someone put a sticker on my yogurt that says 'MARINA NÃO TOQUE'. I touched it. It was mine. Small victories.
I spent two hours drawing the same wave. It's not good. But I didn't stop, and that's new.

First cold week. I wore socks to bed and felt like a child. Drew the radiator because there is no radiator, only suffering. On the bright side, I understood one derivative today and celebrated with two pastéis.

Tio Beto, I still can't play 'Asa Branca' all the way through. I get to the part about the sky and my fingers forget where to go. You said one more year, and I know you meant it as a joke, but I'm taking it seriously. Promise.

There's an old man at the bus stop who reads the newspaper out loud to nobody. Today he read about a storm in the coast and looked up at me like I should react. I said 'o mar é bonito também assim'. He nodded like we'd agreed on something. Good morning.
Went swimming at the university pool for the first time. Panic after three strokes. A girl asked if I was okay and I said yes, obviously, while hanging onto the ladder.

Mom's printer broke, so she fixed it by hitting it twice. It worked. She printed my drawing of the república kitchen, the one with the fridge and the yogurt names, and put it on the wall above the phone. She didn't say it was good. She said 'the fridge is crooked'. It is crooked. I fixed it in the drawing and sent it again. She printed that one too. I think this is how we say things in our family.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was standing at the edge and the water was warm. My feet didn't move. I woke up with my calves tight. I don't know what that means, but I wrote it down.
Tio Beto made me promise to practice 'Asa Branca' before the next Festa Junina. I promised. Again. I am collecting promises like stamps.

Vó Lúcia told me the jabuticabeira at the farm still gives fruit. She said Coronel is buried under it. She cried a little, sixty years later. I went home and drew the tree from memory. It came out crooked but alive.
Rain all weekend. The república's roof leaks in one spot and we put a bucket under it. It sounds like a tiny drum. I recorded it on my phone and tried to draw the sound. Impossible, but fun.
Vó Lúcia disse 'menina do mar' no telefone e eu não disse nada porque não soube o que responder. Agora sei: quero ser. Ainda estou tentando.

Studied all night for Cálculo and fell asleep on the floor with my face on the notebook. Woke up with numbers printed on my cheek and Jéssica laughing. I drew myself in the mirror later: dark circles, pen behind ear, hair like a question mark. It's the most honest self-portrait I've ever made.

New drawing in the margin: the old man on the bus with his parrot, but this time the parrot is wearing a tiny raincoat. I don't know why. I felt inspired by the weather. The notebook is becoming more parrot than math.
Bia, thanks for sitting with me at the RU when I was broke and pretending the free soup was enough. We both know it wasn't. We laughed anyway.
Money check: R$ 340 left and it's the 28th? No, today is the 30th, which is somehow worse. Living on RU, bolachas, and optimism. I'm writing this so I can laugh later. Or cry. Depends.

December already. The city has lights up and I still feel like September. I drew the Christmas tree in the shopping mall as a cactus because it was crooked. People looked. Nobody complained. Good day.
Portuguese: Tio Beto me ensinou 'Asa Branca' até o primeiro refrão. Travei na segunda estrofe e ele bateu palma mesmo assim. Prometi de novo. Ele disse 'mais um ano'. Mais um ano.

December and I miss drawing in class. The calculus notebook has more oceans than formulas. My professor would be offended. I'm not sorry. I need to find a way to study and draw at the same time or choose one, and I already know which one I'd choose, which scares me.
RU dinner was just rice and farofa. I added hot sauce and called it a meal. If future me is eating better, please send gratitude backwards.
The república fridge has a schedule now for cleaning. I drew a tiny angry sponge in the margin of the paper. Nobody complained, so maybe it helped.

December in Curitiba and the city is already decorated. I walked past a tree in the square and thought it looked like a small, patient person. Drew it into my notebook. The república lights went out for an hour and we all stood in the kitchen anyway.

Mom, I know you said drawing is a hobby and not a job, and I'm saying you're probably right. But I drew you today from memory, the way you hold your coffee cup with both hands even when it's not hot. It took me twenty minutes and I felt like myself the whole time. I'm not sending this yet. Maybe I never will. But I wanted to write it.

I tried to learn a recipe from Mom over the phone. It was bolo de fubá, and it went wrong because I didn't have the exact cornmeal and because I was drawing at the same time. The result is a yellow brick. I ate it with coffee and pretended it was a tradition. Vó Lúcia would have laughed and then told me exactly what I did wrong. I miss her already, and she's alive, which is the strangest kind of missing.
Mom called to ask if I've given up on the drawings yet. I said yes. I lied. The sketchbook is under the mattress and I moved it to a new hiding spot: inside the calculus textbook. Nobody opens that.

Tio Beto, if you're reading this in the future, I still haven't learned Asa Branca all the way through. But I played the first verse without looking at my fingers today and felt like a rockstar. Keep waiting. I'll prove you wrong yet.

Tio Beto, hoje eu tentei tocar 'Asa Branca' até o fim e travei no segundo verso, de novo. Vou prometer de novo na Festa Junina. Você vai rir, eu sei. Mas um dia eu vou tocar até o fim e você vai ter que me aplaudir de verdade, não só por educação. Vou treinar.
