Ate a lemon at lunch and thought of nothing important. Just sour, bright, perfect. I kept the seeds in a napkin in my bag because throwing them away felt wrong. Future me, did anything ever come of that?
Portuguese: O cheiro da jabuticabeira não existe em Curitiba, mas eu desenhei uma hoje na margem do caderno e ficou parecida o bastante para eu sentir falta de um lugar onde estive poucas vezes.
Last calculus class of the year. The professor's mustache has reached peak volume. I drew it one final time and closed the notebook. Next year I'll pay attention. Probably.
Started a drawing of the sea from memory. It looked like a puddle with waves. I kept it. It's honest.
Bia and I walked around São Francisco for three hours with no plan. Ended up eating pizza on the curb. Best night of the month, maybe of the year.

Vó Lúcia asked on the phone if I'm still drawing. I said yes before I could think about it. She said 'good'. That was all. I sat on my bed afterward and stared at the drawing of the sea above it like it had spoken.

Mãe, hoje eu quase te liguei pra dizer que passei em uma prova e desenhei um sol com óculos de sol no canto da folha. Não liguei porque você ia perguntar se era 'coisa de criança'. Talvez seja. Eu gosto assim.

End of semester. Passed Cálculo with a 6.2, which is a miracle I'm not questioning. Tio Beto said 'one more year' about Asa Branca and I don't know if he means the song or my whole life. Either way I'm showing up. I packed my bag for Matinhos and the sea drawing is coming with me.

Vó Lúcia told me to call her on Sundays. I do. Today she asked about the drawings and I said I don't draw much. She said 'menina, you have hands for it.' I didn't know what to say, so I said thank you and then didn't sleep well.

The lemon seedling has six leaves now. The girls at the república water it more than I do. Limonada has become a shared responsibility, which is funny because she is barely a plant. I drew her next to my yogurt cup.

Mom sent a box with bolachas, a scarf and a note that said 'eat'. No mention of drawing. I'm calling that progress. The scarf smells like her kitchen. I wrapped it around my shoulders and drew the republica from memory, all four girls blurred together.

Almost the end of the year. I'm in Matinhos with Bia and the family. The sea is gray today, not the blue from my dreams, and I stood at the edge with my feet in the water because that's as far as I go. Vó Lúcia fell asleep early and still swore she saw the fireworks. I'm writing this before midnight, because in 2024 I want to remember that I was here, eighteen, hopeful, scared, and already imagining a window with the sea in it. Maybe that's enough for one year.
Money check: R$ 280 left and it's the 15th. I'm writing this so future me can laugh. Or cry. Depends. Today I chose noodles and a pencil sharpener. Balance.
Vó Lúcia sent a voicemail saying the lemon tree had one small lemon. She said it was ugly but it counted. I saved the message.
Vó Lúcia sent a voice message through Mom's phone. She said 'menina do mar, come mais feijão'. I replayed it four times and drew her hat from memory.

Packed for Matinhos with Bia and the family. I put the sketchbook at the top of the suitcase, which felt like a small rebellion. I'm bringing the drawing of the sea too, but it stays above the bed. Some things don't need to travel.

End of the year, same as always: I'm tired, a little broke, and somehow happy. The room smells like old wood and the drawing above my bed is still there. I added a small lemon to the corner of it today, just because. New Year's in Matinhos soon. I'll stay with my feet in the water at midnight, as far as I go.

Last week before Christmas break. The bus was half empty and the parrot man sat alone. I said 'bom dia' back to Juca. The old man smiled so big I almost missed my stop. Some days are small and complete.

Packed for Matinhos with Mom and Bia. I'm bringing the sketchbook and a swimsuit I won't use past my knees. Bia says 2015 is the year I learn to swim. I said maybe. She said 'you said maybe about Cálculo too'. Touché.
Last bus of the semester. The parrot man waved at me through the window. I waved back like we were old friends. Maybe we are.
Last bus of the year. The parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' even though it was already dark. The driver laughed. I drew the parrot with a tiny Santa hat, which is not accurate but felt right.

Packing for Matinhos. Brought the sketchbook, the drawing of the sea that Vó framed, and three pens. Didn't bring math. I'm telling future me that this is progress, not procrastination. Probably both.

In Matinhos with the family. The sea is right there and I still stood at the edge with my feet in the sand, not the water. Vó Lúcia called me 'menina do mar' and I almost cried into the pastel de frango. Almost.

Matinhos. Sat on the sand with my feet in the water and watched the horizon for an hour. The dream was there again last night: warm water, stuck feet. But in real life my toes were already wet, so maybe that's progress. I didn't go in. Not yet. But I stayed longer than usual.
Mãe, obrigada pelas bolachas e pelo cachecol. Eu sei que você não gosta de desenho, mas eu desenhei você hoje e ficou bonito. Um dia te mostro.

Christmas at Vó's. She wore the hat with the little bell and Tio Beto played violão badly on purpose to make her laugh. I drew the whole table afterward from memory, including the turkey that fell apart. It was better than any photo.
Standing on the balcony at the república, watching rain hit the lemon tree in the neighbor's yard. I don't even have a lemon tree and I already feel jealous of it.

Bia, we're in Matinhos and you keep trying to teach me to float in the shallow water. I panicked after four seconds and swallowed a wave. A child beside us floated without effort, like it was nothing. I'm writing this so we can laugh about it next year.

Family lunch in Matinhos. Vó Lúcia told the story of the farm dog Coronel again and I listened like it was the first time. I want to draw it one day: the dog waiting at the gate, the girl walking home. I didn't tell her that. I just wrote it down here so I wouldn't forget.

Packing for Matinhos. I'm bringing the lemon seedling, carefully, wrapped in a scarf. If Limonada survives the trip, she's tougher than me. Vó says plants like attention. I hope so. I'll be standing with my feet in the water at midnight.
Packing for Matinhos. I'm bringing the sketchbook, the crooked sea drawing, and a promise to myself to get my feet in the water at midnight. Not swimming. Just standing. For now, that's enough.

Two days left in the year. I counted my drawings for 2014: about forty pages. Not bad for someone who says she's focusing on engineering. The sea drawing above my bed is still my favorite. I hope it's still there when this opens.

Bia, we leave tomorrow and I already miss this. You fell asleep on the sand with your shoes on and I drew you with a seagull sitting on your head. It looked like a crown. I'm giving you the drawing later, don't lose it. Also you snore like a small boat engine. Love you.
Tomorrow is New Year's Eve in Matinhos. I'll stand with my feet in the water and pretend that counts as swimming. 18-year-old me, I'm sorry, but it's still not.

Tomorrow is New Year's. Vó says she might fall asleep before midnight and still 'see' the fireworks. I believe her. I want to stand with my feet in the water at midnight, not out of bravery, just because the sand is cold and the water is warm.

New Year's Eve in Matinhos with Bia and the whole family. Vó Lúcia fell asleep at 11:40 and still swore she saw the fireworks. I stood with my feet in the water at midnight because that's as far as I go. I want to live somewhere I can see the sea from the window. Ten years from now: do you? Is Bia still the first person you text? I hope the answer to both is yes.

Back to Curitiba. The república fridge has a new rule: yogurt without a name gets eaten by the roommate whose name is on it anyway. I drew a small label with a lemon on it, no reason, just because I wanted to draw. The sea dream came back last night, same one, feet frozen at the edge.

Matinhos still in my hair. Bia slept until noon and Mom yelled at us from the kitchen in her 'I'm not angry' voice. I drew the sea in the sand with my foot and the tide erased it in two minutes. Good metaphor, terrible excuse for not drawing on paper.

Bus Interbairros II, 7am. The parrot man got on two stops earlier than usual and the parrot didn't say good morning until the third stop. I think even parrots have bad days. I drew both of them in the margin of my Álgebra notebook and spilled coffee on the page.

Curitiba summer rain, the kind that makes the bus windows useless. I drew the windshield wiper on my Physics notebook and the guy next to me asked if I was an art student. I said 'engineering'. He said 'ah'. Same reaction, different person. The RU lunch today was feijoada and I was too proud to take seconds.
The república fridge has a new rule: whoever finishes the last milk buys the next one. I ate yogurt straight from the pot and nobody saw. Feeling very sophisticated.
Bus 7am again. The parrot did not say bom dia today; he bit the motorista's thumb and I pretended to read Álgebra. I drew the bite in my notebook instead of the derivative. Priorities.

Bus was late again and I missed the first ten minutes of Física. The parrot man sat in the back today. When I got off, the driver wished me good luck with the exam, unprompted. Small city inside a big city.

The fridge at the república has a new yogurt with my name on it and I'm still not sure if that makes me feel organized or defeated. Ate pastel with Bia at the feira and the cat from the stall sat on my backpack like it paid rent.

First week back in Curitiba. The republica kitchen has a new leak under the sink and Bia left her mug in my room again. Weather is one of those gray days where the city smells like wet concrete. I drew the leaky sink instead of studying Termodinamica. It looked better than the sink.
Ate a RU's feijão com abóbora and everyone complained except me. I think cafeteria food tastes like permission to keep studying. Drew the lunch lady's hands while waiting in line.

Bus 7am today was packed because of the rain. The parrot man sat next to me and the parrot tried to eat my hair clip. I didn't stop him. Small joys. I missed the parrot's 'bom dia' because my earbuds were in, but I saw his beak move.

RU lunch today was rice, beans, and something orange that nobody could identify. Bia ate three servings and said it was 'character building'. We walked to São Francisco afterwards and saw a dog carrying a bag of bread in its mouth, very politely, like a delivery service.

Bia called to say she found a cheap flight to Matinhos and we're going next weekend. I packed three swimsuits and zero courage. The sea is still just a view to me, but being near it with her makes it feel possible.
Bus 7am. O senhor do papagaio não estava, só um cara lendo o mesmo livro que eu, em pé. Desisti de conversar com estranhos e desenhei sua jaqueta.

Mom sent a box with bolachas, a packet of feijão, and a note saying 'não esqueça de comer'. I already ate half the bolachas on the bus home. The RU today was arroz with something that might have been frango.
Bia dormiu na república ontem e roubou meu pijama de dinossauros. Prometi desenhar o dinossauro dela com uma touca de natação. Ainda não sei nadar, mas já sei imaginar.
Drew the sea again in the margin of my notebook. The wave has too many teeth. Vó Lúcia called to ask if I was eating enough. I said yes. We both know I'm not.
Cálculo at 7:30 again. My neighbor in class snores. I drew him in the margin with a tiny graduation cap. The professor asked if I was taking notes. I said 'contextually'.
Mom sent a box: bolachas, chocolate, a new towel, and a note saying 'don't forget to eat'. I ate three bolachas standing up in the kitchen at midnight. The towel is ugly and perfect.

Bia, se um dia você achar esta cápsula, lembre que em janeiro de 2015 você me mandou uma foto do mar de Matinhos e escreveu 'vem logo'. Eu estava em Curitiba com saudade e uma prova de Cálculo. Ainda penso no mar toda vez que você manda foto.
Ate um limão e plantei três sementes num copo de iogurte com 'MARINA' escrito. Se uma nascer, eu guardo para sempre. Três sementes, uma chance.
Escritora de diário e engenheira de mentira. Hoje desenhei o mar no fim da aula e o professor perguntou se eu estava tomando nota. Eu disse que sim. Mentira de novo.
Summer in Matinhos. Bia tried to teach me to float. I lasted four seconds before panicking. A kid of maybe six floated next to me the whole time, out of pure spite I think.

Dreamed of the sea again. Same dream, standing at the edge, feet won't move, calves tight when I wake up. But this time there was a small wooden chair behind me and I sat down instead of fighting it. I don't know if that's progress or giving up.
First swim lesson was just me standing in the shallow end pretending to stretch. A kid of maybe six floated next to me and I chose to take it personally.
Chuva grossa em Curitiba, ponto final. O ônibus Interbairros atrasou e eu cheguei encharcada. Sequei a mochila no secador de mãos do banheiro da UTFPR. Engenharia não ensina isso.

Bia, obrigada por não me deixar morrer de tédio na praia. Você tentou me ensinar a flutuar e eu virei um cateto morto. Prometo voltar ao mar quando parar de ter medo. Até lá, te mando desenho de peixe. Beijo.

Spent the afternoon drawing in the Passeio Público instead of studying. A dog came and sat on my sketchbook. I think he approved of the drawing of the sea. He left paw prints on the corner; I kept them.

Bus was late, rain everywhere, and the parrot man got on whistling anyway. Juca? No, I hadn't named him yet, the parrot just said 'bom dia, motorista' and I felt like the day had permission to be good.
Bus was late again. Seu parrot man was there, parrot said bom dia to the driver and then looked at me like it owed me money. I drew them in my Álgebra notebook and missed every example.
Bia, você ainda tem aquele casaco verde ridículo? Usei ele hoje porque está frio e pensei em você. Também pensei que não ligo pra você o suficiente. Vou corrigir isso.
Aula às 7:30 e eu ainda desenhando o mar no caderno. O professor perguntou se eu estava tomando nota. Disse que sim. Não estava.
Bia, your mother sent bolachas again and one of the girls at the república tried to claim them. I defended them with my life. Friend loyalty starts with cookies.

RU today was feijão com arroz, again, and somehow still comforting. I sat with two girls from Civil and we talked about nothing for forty minutes. I miss nothing conversations. They are a form of rest.

Mom sent a package with bolachas, a sweater I didn't ask for, and a note that said 'eat'. The bolachas survived the trip. The sweater smells like her closet. I'm wearing it right now in the república, which smells like old wood and someone's microwave popcorn.
Tried the campus pool at lunch. Put my face in the water for three seconds and came up gasping. The lifeguard asked if I was okay. I said 'artistic'. He did not laugh.
Money check: R$ 180 left until the 12th. I ate RU and pretended I wasn't hungry. The bolachas are gone. Tomorrow I'll ask Bia for a loan and immediately feel guilty about it.

RU today had that bland chicken again, so I drowned it in farofa and pretend it was a choice. My roommate laughed and said my plate looked like a construction site. She is not wrong. I still ate everything.
Chuva forte all afternoon. The old wood smell in my room got stronger. I sat in the corridor with my sketchbook and drew the rain on the window. It looked like handwriting.

Bus 7am, Interbairros II. The parrot man had a new jacket, dark green. The parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' right on time. I got off one stop early because I was smiling too much to keep a straight face.

Vó Lúcia called to ask if I've been eating. I said yes. I was holding a packet of bolachas at the time. She told me about a cat that lived on her roof in Irati and how it only came down when the radio played. I drew the cat in my sketchbook.
RU today: arroz, feijão, something they called frango but I'm not convinced. R$ 2,50 e a dignidade inclusa.
Valentine's Day and I'm studying Cálculo. Tio Beto sent a message with a heart and a violão emoji. That counts. I ate brigadeiro straight from the pot, no regrets, slight stomachache.
Valentine's with Rafa was pastel de feira and a walk. He is not romantic in the movie way. He remembered I like the outside table. I am counting that.
Tio Beto called just to say the violão sounds better after new strings. I could hear him playing in the background and pretending not to.

Bia, if you're reading this, thank you for paying for my pastel today and for not asking why I was crying. It was about nothing and everything. You are the best roommate of my life even when we don't live together.
Bia, obrigada por vir no domingo mesmo com chuva. A gente comeu pizza fria no chão do corredor e você me obrigou a desenhar sua mão segurando a casca. Acho que ficou boa.
Mom sent a package with bolachas, socks, and a note that said 'study more'. The socks have flowers. I will wear them and feel 12 again. The bolachas are already gone, obviously.
The lemon tree idea hasn't happened yet, but I planted nothing and still feel proud of the thought. A yogurt cup with 'MARINA' on it is waiting on the fridge. For now it holds pens.
Mom texted 'are you eating real food?' I sent a photo of the RU tray. She replied with a recipe for sopa. I haven't made it yet but I saved it.
Money check: R$ 210 left and it's the 22nd. I counted the bolachas Mom sent: nine. I will make them last. This is strategy, not sadness.
Bia, you left my umbrella at the bar last night and I had to walk home in a fine rain that wasn't quite dramatic enough. I looked like a wet postcard. We're still going next Friday.
Rafa texted me a photo of a building in São Paulo with the caption 'future us'. I stared at it for ten minutes. I like him. I don't know if I like São Paulo. These might be the same problem.
R$ 200 left on the 23rd. RU feijoada today saved me. I'm becoming a person who plans around the university menu, which is probably character development.

Tio Beto called on a Tuesday, which is unusual. He wanted to know if I'd practiced 'Asa Branca'. I said yes. I had played it once, badly, and then spent twenty minutes on my phone. He said 'one verse, Marina, just one verse' and laughed.
Drew the lemon tree in the backyard of the república's neighbor. It's not mine, but it's the only lemon tree I know how to reach from the sidewalk without trespassing.
R$ 280 left on the 24th. I counted twice hoping the number would change. It didn't. RU saved me again, plus one mandioca from the feira that cost less than a coffee.
República meeting about the bathroom schedule. Four girls, one bathroom, many feelings. I drew everyone as animals. The drawing was not helpful but it was funny.
There's a lemon tree behind the library that drops fruit on the sidewalk. I ate one standing there in the rain, no reason. Future me: did you plant seeds someday?

First date with Rafa. Pastel de feira and a walk in the Passeio Público. He talked about São Paulo the entire time, the jobs, the buildings, the noise, like it's a person he's in love with. I talked about the sea. We both pretended not to notice.
Engenharia is a lot of calculus and very little drawing. Today I drew a parrot in the corner of a derivative problem and the professor didn't notice. Small victories.

Rafa and I got lost looking for a bookstore in Batel and ended up at a tiny café with a cat on the counter. The cat sat on my Álgebra notebook. Rafa said it was 'a sign from the universe about calculus'. I think the cat just liked warm paper.
The old man with the parrot was reading a newspaper folded into a hat. Juca, as I've decided he's called, tried to eat the corner. The man let him.

Rafa and I walked in the Passeio after the pastel. He talked about elevators in tall buildings as if they were people. I nodded. I was thinking about floating, which I still cannot do. We are both dreaming out loud and pretending to listen.
O senhor do papagaio estava no ponto hoje. O bicho disse 'bom dia' para o cobrador e depois ficou quieto, como se soubesse que era segunda-feira. Desenhei eles no caderno de Álgebra.
After the first date with Rafa, I went home and drew the pastel de feira from memory. The drawing is better than the date. I mean this kindly; both were warm.
After the Passeio Público date, Rafa texted 'I liked walking with you'. I stared at it for ten minutes and replied 'I liked the pastel'. I hope future me has learned to answer normally.

After the first date with Rafa, I walked home through Passeio Público and drew the little lake from memory. The pastel was good, the company was better, and São Paulo still sounds like too many cars. But I liked his laugh. That counts.
Rain in Curitiba, obviously. My umbrella broke on Rua XV and I walked home with one sleeve wet. Rafa would have offered his jacket; I didn't text him.
Rafa texted me a link to a playlist and then nothing else for three hours. I listened to it while washing dishes. It was all São Paulo bands. I still liked it.

Portuguese note: Choveu a tarde inteira e o ônibus da Interbairros atrasou 40 minutos. O senhor do papagaio estava lá, com guarda-chuva verde e o papagaio debaixo da jaqueta. O motorista não reclamou. Desenhei os dois sem olhar para o papel. A chuva é boa para desenho, porque ninguém espera que você esteja bonita.
Drawing at 2am because I couldn't sleep. The sea again, but this time with a small boat. I don't know why a boat. My room smells like old wood and graphite. I think Vó Lúcia would like this one.
Rafa talked about São Paulo the entire dinner, jobs, buildings, noise, like it's a person he's in love with. I talked about the sea. We both pretended not to notice. I noticed.
Mom, I know you'll read this later if I leave it here. I did eat breakfast today. Two pieces of bread and coffee, not just coffee. Don't worry.
Bia, your birthday is coming and I still don't know what to buy you. Please don't say 'nothing', because I already bought the ugly keychain with the fish on it.
Had a dream where the sea was a swimming pool and Dona Cida was there with a whistle. I think I'm spending too much time thinking about swimming. The dream ended when I forgot how to float.

Mom, if you're reading this, I still have the sketchbook under the mattress. I know you think I gave up. I lied in October and I'm lying now by not showing you. One day I'll be brave enough to leave it on the table.
Vó Lúcia said on the phone she dreamed I was swimming. I told her it was a nightmare. She laughed and said 'you'll learn when you're ready'. I didn't say she's been saying that for years.
Bia, remember when we promised to save money by cooking? We spent more on ingredients than the RU. The rice burnt. We ate it anyway with limão and a lot of hot sauce. 10/10 friendship, 2/10 rice.

I failed a small calculus quiz today and didn't even cry, just ate a pastel and went back to the república. The girls were watching a novela and screaming at the TV. I sat with them and felt less like a failure for an hour.
Calculus homework at 11pm, with coffee that tastes like punishment. I miss drawing in class. The parrot man would not understand my life right now, and he is right not to.
Tio Beto called to ask if I had practiced 'Asa Branca'. I said 'a little'. I meant 'once, badly, and my neighbor knocked on the wall'. He laughed like a drum. I love that laugh. One more year.
Tio Beto sent a voice note trying to teach me the bridge of Asa Branca through WhatsApp. I listened six times and got nothing. Still counts as practice.
Calculou errado meu orçamento e fiquei com R$ 20 até o fim do mês. Vou viver de bolacha da Mom e orgulho. O orgulho não enche barriga, mas passa o tempo.
Drew the república kitchen at night: four mugs, one with my name, one with someone else's name, one with no name. The unnamed one is always mine by mistake. Nobody minds.
Pastel de feira com Rafa again. He asked if I want to go to São Paulo in July. I said maybe. The maybe was a no, but I'm still saying maybe.
Rain again. The república ceiling leaks in the hallway, so we put a towel down and called it 'the river'. I drew it before anyone walked on it. Small catastrophes make the best sketches.
Mãe, não desisti dos desenhos. Só estou desenhando menos porque Cálculo insiste em ocupar minha mesa. Hoje fiz o senhor do ônibus e o papagaio no caderno de Álgebra. Ele continua dizendo bom dia.

Bia found the sketchbook under the mattress and said 'finally'. I panicked. She only looked at one page, the drawing of the old man and the parrot, and said 'this is really good, why are you in engineering'. I didn't have an answer that didn't include Mom.
Found my sketchbook under the mattress and drew for ten minutes. My hand was stiff like it forgot. Still, ten minutes counts.
Mãe, não, eu não desisti dos desenhos. Mentir isso virou minha rotina. Mas hoje desenhei o limoeiro da casa da Vó no caderno e até que está parecendo limoeiro. Beijos.

R$ 18 left until next RU payment. Ate bread with margarine for dinner and called it 'economic gastronomy'. The fridge still has yogurts with names on them, including one that isn't mine and I'm too polite to ask.
Woke up from the sea dream with my calves tight again. The water was warm but my feet were glued to the sand. One day I'll just walk in.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was wearing shoes. Why shoes? The water was warm and I woke up annoyed at myself for overdressing for a dream.
Rain all afternoon. Studied Cálculo under the roof noise and drank three cups of the terrible república coffee. My notebook is full of drawings of raindrops and zero integrals.
Tio Beto texted me 'still practicing?' and I sent him a photo of my hand with four blisters. He replied 'one more year'. At least this year I can say I tried before the Festa Junina.
Vó Lúcia called to ask if I was eating. I said yes. She asked what. I said 'comida'. She hung up and called back ten minutes later with a recipe for sopa de legumes that takes two hours.

Failed to understand Cálculo again. I cried in the bathroom for three minutes, washed my face, and went to class. The professor wrote something I didn't understand. I drew a very angry circle in my notebook. The circle helped.
Mom, I know you think illustration is a hobby. I didn't say anything when you said it. I'm not brave yet. But I'm drawing this tiny 'maybe' here just in case future me is.
Desenhei o velho do ônibus no caderno de Álgebra de novo. O papagaio tinha uma mancha verde no peito. Acho que ele é bonito. Ninguém no ônibus reage mais, exceto eu.
Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He tried to teach me a fourth chord and called it 'the secret one'. It's just C again but slower. He winked. Family is a conspiracy.

Money check: R$ 410 left and it's the 12th. I can do it. RU tickets, bolachas, no coffee outside the república. The Física professor said something about vectors today that I will never use, but I wrote it down neatly anyway.
Mãe, eu não desisti dos desenhos. Só escondi o caderno. Prometo um dia te mostrar sem parecer que estou pedindo permissão. Obrigada pelas bolachas, elas salvam as noites de cálculo. Te amo.
Bia's birthday plans already involve the bar in São Francisco. I am saving R$ 30 for it, which means no pastel for a week. The math of friendship is brutal.
Found a drawing of the parrot man in my Álgebra notebook from last year. I gave him a little mustache he doesn't have. Artistic license.
Chuva o dia inteiro. Estudei Cálculo com o barulho no telhado e bebi três cafés ruins da república. O caderno ficou cheio de gotas e zero integrais.

Vó Lúcia told me the story of Coronel today, the farm dog in Irati who walked her to school for nine years and waited at the gate. When he died, her father buried him under the jabuticabeira. She cried telling it, sixty years later. I want to draw this one day.
Mom asked if I'm still 'wasting time with drawings'. I said no. Then I went to my room and drew her face from memory. I got the nose wrong. I think she'd be offended and proud at the same time.
Bia's party leftovers in the fridge. I ate cold pizza for breakfast and felt like a villain. The lemon tree didn't exist yet but I already wanted something green on the windowsill.

Bia, I'm writing this to you because I can't say it out loud without sounding dramatic. Thank you for sitting next to me in calculus and pretending to understand it. You make the 7:30am bus feel like less of a punishment. Also, your hair smells like strawberry shampoo, which is distracting.

The old man with the parrot was on the bus again, sitting in the same seat, bandage gone. The parrot said 'bom dia' to the whole bus and I said it back under my breath. Nobody else noticed, as usual, which somehow makes it better.
Bia's handwriting is on my calculus notebook because she borrowed it and returned it with a smiley face on page 42. I'm keeping it forever.
São 7:30 da manhã e o senhor do papagaio não entrou no ônibus. Senti como se faltasse um móvel na casa. Dois pontos depois, ele entrou com o mesmo pássaro e o mesmo 'bom dia, motorista'. Tudo certo.

Pastel de feira with Rafa again. He pointed at a building and said 'imagine the view from there'. I said 'imagine the price'. We both laughed. It's nice when we're just two people eating fried things.

Bia's house for Sunday lunch. Her mom made arroz carreteiro and I ate too much, the way you do when someone's mom cooks for you. Bia told me I talk about the sea too much. I told her she talks about Floripa too much. We both smiled.
Mom sent a box of bolachas and a note that said 'don't skip meals'. There are drawings hidden inside the box too. I found them after eating everything. She knows.
Tio Beto sent me a voice message trying to sing Asa Branca at 11pm. It was terrible and I loved it. I practiced three chords quietly so the república girls wouldn't hear. They heard.
Drew a man and his dog at the feira. The dog was asleep in a box of tangerinas. Nobody seemed to think this was strange except me. I didn't say anything. I just drew faster.
Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. Vó Lúcia asked if I was eating enough and then put more rice on my plate before I answered. I drew her hands serving food later and they looked like two birds landing.
Interbairros II at 6:40. The parrot said 'bom dia' and an old lady answered 'bom dia, Juca'. So maybe his name is Juca. I didn't verify.

Went to the swimming pool at the university for the first time. I did not get in. I stood at the edge and watched a girl my age swim back and forth like it was nothing. I thought about my sea dream and my feet stayed in the same place, on land this time.
Pastel de feira with Rafa in the rain. He said São Paulo sounds like opportunity. I said Curitiba sounds like home. We both ate quietly after that. The pastel was excellent, at least.
First sunny day in a week. I sat by the window with my feet outside and drew a lemon I saw at the feira. I don't have a tree yet. Maybe one day.

The parrot man wasn't on the bus and I looked at every seat like an idiot. Then he appeared at the next stop with a bandage on his wrist. The parrot said 'bom dia' to the whole bus. I clapped internally. Externally I was cool.

It rained so hard the bus stopped under the viaduct. Everyone was quiet except the parrot, who said 'bom dia' to a sleeping passenger. I drew the scene with watercolor pens that ran. It looks better wet.
Mãe, as bolachas chegaram inteiras. Comi metade antes de achar os desenhos escondidos na caixa. Você sabe que eu sei, né?
Tio Beto lent me his violão for the week. I know three chords and one of them is wrong. My fingers hurt. I am not giving up. Maybe a little. Not giving up.

Found a tiny drawing I made in 2012 of the sea and put it next to Vó Lúcia's drawing above my bed. Three things on the wall now: the sea, the drawing from Vó, and a ticket stub from São Francisco. The room looks less temporary.

Rafa and I went to the pastel fair and he ordered the same cheese pastel as me, which I took as a good sign. He talked about São Paulo again. I listened and drew the people in line instead of arguing.
Money check: R$ 120 until the 15th. I am living on bolachas and denial. The bolachas are from Mom, so at least the denial has a sender.
It rained so hard the bus stopped and everyone just stood there, dripping, staring at the window. The parrot man held the parrot inside his jacket. Nobody asked whose jacket it was. It was his.

Summer is over in my head but Curitiba doesn't care. I wore a sweater and still drew the sea from memory on the bus. The man next to me asked if it was Copacabana. I said it was mine. He looked confused.
Mom asked if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said yes again. The sketchbook under the mattress is getting fuller. Lying is becoming a habit.
Rafa texted that he passed a job interview in São Paulo. I said congratulations and meant it, and also my stomach dropped. We'll see.
Swimming lesson zero: I put on the cap, got in the shallow end, and immediately panicked about sharks. In a pool. In Curitiba. Rafa said I'm dramatic. He's not wrong.
Tio Beto, obrigado por me chamar de 'artista' brincando no almoço. Você disse que era zoeira, mas eu guardei. Também guardei o violão desafinado. Um dia eu toco a música inteira, juro.
Tio Beto sent an audio of himself playing 'Asa Branca' badly and laughing. I replied with a voice note of me playing three chords badly and laughing. Family tradition.
Bia and I sat on the curb after the bar and talked about where we'll be in ten years. She said by the sea. I said I don't know. I do know. I just don't say it out loud yet.
Mom called and asked if I'd 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said I was 'focusing on studies'. She said 'good'. I had ink on my fingers. I washed them before dinner at the RU, which felt ridiculous.
Budget check: R$ 280 left and it's not even the 20th. I have become a professional bolacha eater. At least the sketchbook under the mattress doesn't cost anything.

Tio, ainda não sei tocar 'Asa Branca' inteira. Aprendi os três acordes que o senhor me ensinou e toco a primeira parte com muito entusiasmo e erro. Festa Junina está chegando. Prometo tentar até o segundo verso.
Vó Lúcia on the phone: 'E aí, menina, ainda desenha?' I said 'a little'. She said 'desenhe mais'. She doesn't know about the mattress sketchbook. Maybe she does. Grandmothers have radar.
Rafa and I walked through Passeio Público after the pastel. He talked about São Paulo again. I talked about the sea. We both pretended not to notice.

Portuguese: Plantamos um manjericão na janela da cozinha da república. A Maria disse que se sobreviver até julho é um milagre. Eu desenhei o vasinho e coloquei o desenho na geladeira, ao lado do yogurt com nome. Curitiba está fria e o manjericão parece desconfiado.

I dreamed of the sea again, standing at the edge like always. This time there was a green parrot on my shoulder saying 'vai, motorista'. I woke up laughing, which is new. Maybe the dream is learning too.
Dreamed of the sea again. Same edge, same warm water, same feet that won't move. But this time I heard a parrot saying 'bom dia'. Progress?

I called Vó Lúcia on Sunday and she told me about the jabuticabeira again. Same tree, same fruit, same dog buried under it. I wrote it all down in the margin. She said 'you're writing everything like a student'. I said 'like a granddaughter'. She went quiet.
Money check: R$ 12 left and five days to go. I sold an old Calculus book for R$ 15 and felt rich for exactly one hour before buying a sketchbook. Worth it, obviously.
Rain all day. The republica hallway became a river. I wore my boots and still got water in my sock. Wrote 'calculo' on the fogged bus window and felt productive for no reason.
Bus was packed and I stood the whole way. A kid gave me his seat. I refused and then took it because my legs were shaking. Adult life.

I failed Cálculo 1. I'm writing this crying in the RU so that next year you remember it wasn't the end of the world. Rafa bought me a pastel and said I'm too smart to fail twice. He's annoying and I think I love him. Also, I haven't drawn in two months. I know. I know.

Rafa bought me a pastel after Cálculo. I failed. He said I'm too smart to fail twice, which is either kind or pressure. I ate the pastel too fast because I was crying. He pretended not to notice the crying. I noticed that he noticed.
The república fridge has a new yogurt with someone's name and a heart. I drew the heart in my notebook because it was a very committed heart. Engineering homework remains untouched.

Vó Lúcia told me over the phone that she used to walk to school with a dog called Coronel, who waited at the gate every day. She said his name like he was still alive. I cried after hanging up, then drew him from memory, with too big ears.

Cálculo 1 results came and I did not fail this time, but it was close enough to scare me. I celebrated with RU dessert and a page in the sketchbook. The drawing is of a calculator crying. Accurate mood.
Failed Cálculo 1 last week. This week I re-enrolled and bought a new notebook. Rafa says I'm too smart to fail twice. I wrote that down because it felt nice to hear.

Failed Cálculo 1 and cried into a pastel. Rafa sat there very calmly and said I was too smart to fail twice. I wanted to be annoyed, I was just grateful. Also I have not drawn in two months and I know.
Bia's birthday coming and I bought her the ugly fish keychain anyway. If she hates it, I'll keep it and say it was a loan.
Cálculo exam tomorrow. I studied enough to know I don't know enough. Going to sleep anyway. Panic has never helped my math.
RU lunch: lentilha, arroz, and a piece of carne that tasted like salt and hope. Bia took a photo of my plate. She said it looked like a sad painting. I agreed.
Failed to study for Cálculo and then studied for Cálculo. Rafa bought me a pastel and said I'm too smart to fail twice. I hate when he is both right and annoying.
Failed Cálculo 1 this week. Crying in the RU. Still true. Rafa bought the pastel anyway and I hated him a little for being kind at the wrong time.

I haven't drawn in two months and I feel like a plant someone forgot to water. Tonight I opened the sketchbook and drew one fish, very small, in the corner. Tomorrow I'll draw another. Small is still drawing.

Rafa brought me a pastel after the Cálculo 1 failure and didn't say 'I told you so'. He just sat with me while I cried into a napkin. Then he said 'you're too smart to fail twice' and I wanted to be annoyed but I wasn't.
Rainy Monday, no mood for Interbairros II. I sat in the back with the window open just enough to hear the tires. Drew a woman with an umbrella shaped like a mushroom. Small joy, still counts.
Drew during class again. The professor thinks I'm taking notes. I am, technically, just not of calculus.
Post-Cálculo failure recovery plan: cry, eat RU, walk home the long way. Rafa bought the pastel again and said I'd pass next time. I hate being comforted correctly.
Rafa, you bought me a pastel after the result. It helped. You talked about São Paulo again on the way home. I listened. I even asked a question this time.
Tio Beto's kitchen smelled like canjica all day. I burned the first pot and he didn't even scold me, just handed me another. I think that's love in his language.
Bia e eu comemos pastel na feira e falamos mal do calor de Curitiba, que não existe mas todo mundo fala. A feira estava cheia de crianças com pintura no rosto.
Dreamed of the sea again. Same edge, same warm water, same stuck feet. But this time there was a boat far away and I could hear someone laughing. Woke up and my calves were tight as usual.

Rain all day. The república's roof leaks in the hallway, so we put a bucket with my name on it. Bia says my name is on everything now: yogurt, bucket, mattress. She's not wrong. I like having territory.

Tio Beto's Festa Junina is next week. I practiced 'Asa Branca' on the violão he lent me and forgot the lyrics halfway through the second verse. The violão smells like his living room. I think that's the part I like most.
Drew Mom's kitchen from memory. The jar of salt, the blue cloth, the clock that's always ten minutes late. It looked more like home than my actual room does.
I passed by the beach in my head all day, which is free. My feet were in the water at midnight last New Year's and that was enough then. Maybe enough isn't the right word. It was something.
Two months without drawing. I know. The sketchbook is still under the mattress and I haven't opened it. Bad student, bad daughter, bad artist. At least I'm honest here.
Rafa passou numa entrevista em São Paulo e eu disse parabéns. Significou. Meu estômago também caiu. A gente vai ver.

Vó Lúcia told me about the jabuticabeira again while we sat on the porch. She says the fruit was so sweet her mother had to hide it from the children. I believe her completely and would like to time-travel to steal some.
Ate lemon ice cream and thought about the sea. No lemon tree yet, just a craving. Maybe future me will have planted something by now. Please water it.

Dreamed of the sea again. Same dream: I'm standing at the edge, water warm, feet won't move. But this time there was a parrot on my shoulder saying 'bom dia'. I woke up laughing and then a little sad. The parrot deserves a beach.
RU gave us a dessert that might have been pudim or might have been a mistake. I ate it anyway. Survival skills.
Festa Junina tomorrow. I practiced 'Asa Branca' in the bathroom with the shower running so nobody would hear the mistakes. The shower didn't help. The second verse is my enemy.

Bus 7am. The parrot man had a bandage on his thumb and the parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' twice. I counted the passengers who didn't react: fourteen. I reacted, internally, like a person who has lost her mind.
Cálculo exam in two days. I made a study plan with colors. It looks beautiful. I have not opened it. The plan is currently the most productive thing I have done this week.
Rafa and I walked in the Passeio Público and he talked about São Paulo like it was a person he was dating. I talked about the sea. We both nodded like nothing happened. Something happened.

Festa Junina at Tio Beto's was loud and warm and there was quentão. I played 'Asa Branca' until the second verse, then lost it. Tio Beto clapped anyway. One more year, he said. I nodded like that is a reasonable timeline.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I played 'Asa Branca' badly until the second verse and then clapped for myself. He clapped too. One more year.
Festa Junina tomorrow. I practiced Asa Branca in the bathroom so nobody would hear. The second verse disappears like it has a grudge against me.

Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I played 'Asa Branca' until the second verse and forgot everything. He clapped anyway and said 'one more year'. I ate three quentões and fell asleep on the couch. Bia drew a mustache on me with marker. I deserved it.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's was loud and warm and smelled like paçoca. I played until the second verse and forgot everything. He clapped anyway. I pretended not to mind.
Hot day. The republica fan makes more noise than wind. I opened the window and drew the street until the sun moved. A dog walked by with a tangerine in its mouth. Best model of the day.

I didn't draw for two weeks and then drew three pages at once in the RU, standing in line. A woman asked if I was an art student. I said engineering. She said 'you draw like you're escaping something'. I said 'calculus'.
Reprovei Cálculo 1. Estou chorando no RU. Ainda verdade. Rafa comprou pastel e eu odiei ele um pouco por ser gentil na hora errada.
Rafa invited me to São Paulo for the weekend. I said not this time. He didn't push. I'm writing this down because not pushing is rare and I noticed.
Summer in Matinhos is still months away, but Bia already asked if I'm bringing the drawing of the sea. I said yes. I think that drawing is becoming a passport.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I played 'Asa Branca' until the second verse and then forgot everything. Tio Beto clapped anyway and said 'one more year'. One more year.

Bia's family came over and her cousin tried to teach us to play truco. I lost every hand and drew caricatures of everyone's angry faces. They liked the drawings more than the game, which feels like a career hint.
Swimming pool attempt with Bia. I lasted four seconds before panicking. A six-year-old floated next to me like a small, smug cloud. I told myself to be nice to children. I was not nice in my head.

Bia, você disse que eu sou dramática quando choro no ônibus. Talvez. Mas hoje um senhor ofereceu guaraná e disse 'calma, menina'. Eu desenhei ele também. Você vai achar que todos são personagens. São, um pouco.

Portuguese: Domingo na casa do Tio Beto. Ele tocou 'Asa Branca' inteira e eu tentei acompanhar até a segunda estrofe. Fiquei perdida. Ele bateu palma assim mesmo e disse 'mais um ano'. Mais um ano. Anotei isso porque não quero esquecer o jeito que ele disse.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's was loud and hot and perfect. I played 'Asa Branca' until the second verse and then panicked. He clapped anyway. One more year.
Swimming pool attempt #1. Lasted four seconds. The lifeguard looked concerned and then politely pretended not to.
Tio Beto, thank you for clapping anyway. You didn't have to. I saw Rafa smiling and you not smiling and somehow your silence was kinder.
A kid in the pool floated next to me like it was nothing. I am choosing to believe she was showing off, not helping. Either way, I lasted five seconds this time.

Festa Junina at Tio Beto's last week still in my head. I played Asa Branca until verse two and then the guitar turned into spaghetti in my hands. Tio Beto said 'one more year'. I am writing it here so I can't pretend he didn't.
Dreamed of the sea again, standing at the edge, warm water, feet stuck. Woke up with my calves tight. Maybe tomorrow I'll at least wiggle a toe.

Swimming pool at the club, Bia tried to teach me again. I floated for maybe five seconds this time before grabbing the ladder. A little boy floated past me without hands, and I felt both inspired and deeply humiliated.
Rafa and I walked to the bus stop after the pool. He said São Paulo has better pools. I said Curitiba has better people. He kissed me. The bus came. We both missed it. Worth it.

Rafa talked about São Paulo again for forty minutes at the pastel place. I talked about Matinhos. We both pretended not to notice the mismatch. He held my hand under the table, which I think was supposed to mean something, but I'm not sure what.
Interbairros bus was late, so I sketched everyone waiting. The man with the parrot asked to see the drawing and said the parrot's feathers looked wrong. Correct.
Vó Lúcia asked if I'm 'finally swimming'. I said I'm taking breaks. She said the sea doesn't wait for breaks. Fair.
Drew Coronel in my sketchbook today, from the story Vó Lúcia told me. A dog walking a girl to school. I want to draw it again someday when I'm better.
Swimming pool at the university. I held the wall and practiced breathing like it was a military operation. A kid asked if I was resting. I said 'training'. He looked unconvinced.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I played Asa Branca until the second verse and then forgot everything. He clapped anyway and said one more year. One more year.

Bia's 18th birthday is next week. We're going to São Francisco with a marker, like she planned. I bought her a small sketchbook because she said she wants to 'learn to draw like me'. I laughed. She didn't.

The lemon cake at the bakery near UTFPR was still warm when I bought it. I ate half on the bus and got sugar on my Physics notebook. Worth it. The old man with the parrot looked at me like I was the chaos today.
I drew the sea on the back of a calculus page. The professor collected it and looked at me like I was a disappointment. I think he was right and also wrong. The sea looked good, at least.
Bia's birthday wall in São Francisco might have been painted over. I went to check. It hadn't. We took a photo and looked young and tired.
Bia's birthday is coming. I bought her a drawing of us at the bus stop. She doesn't know yet. I hope she likes it more than the casaco verde.
Mom called to ask if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said yes. I lied. The sketchbook is under the mattress again, wrapped in a plastic bag like evidence.
Bia and I wrote our names on the bar wall again because the first ones were fading. The bartender gave us the marker without asking. We are regulars of our own small history.
Bia's birthday is soon. We're writing names on a wall if the bar allows it. If not, I'll write them in my sketchbook and count that.
Bia's birthday is coming and I still haven't decided what to draw her. Probably something silly. She likes silly. So do I, secretly.
Sun in Curitiba, rare and suspicious. Everyone went outside like lizards. I drew shadows on the sidewalk and then stepped on them, which ruined the drawing but felt important.
We wrote our names on the wall of the bar in São Francisco. Bia's handwriting is better than mine. A man at the next table said 'that's illegal' and then wrote his own name on the wall. Solidarity.

Bia turned 19 and we wrote our names on the bar wall again, even though last year's marker is already fading. We added a tiny fish next to them. If future us reads this, the fish was Bia's idea and I am taking credit.

Mom called to ask if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said yes. I lied. The sketchbook is under the mattress again. She would be furious and relieved at the same time if she knew. I think that's love.
Mom's box arrived with bolachas and a printed recipe for bolo de fubá. I think she's trying to teach me things without teaching me. I appreciate it and also resist it.
We wrote our names on the bar wall in São Francisco again, next to the old ones. The marker was running out. Bia pressed hard. Mine is faint but there.
Mom sent bolachas again and I cried a little, which is absurd. I am eighteen and crying over cookies. The república girls ate most of them before I could. I drew a cookie with wings to cope.

Money check: R$ 280 left and it's the 16th. Living on RU and the bolachas Mom sends. I'm writing this so in three years I can laugh at it. Or cry. Depends. I also need to buy a new pen, which feels like a luxury.

Engineering homework and homesickness at the same time. I called Mom, who asked if I had eaten. I said yes, which was a lie until she sent a photo of the bolo de fubá cooling. Then it became true, morally.
Sonhei com o mar de novo. O mesmo sonho. Acordei com as panturrilhas tensas e desenhei a água de memória antes do café. Parece nada com água real, mas ajudou.
Mom asked on the phone if I gave up on the drawings yet. I said yes. The sketchbook is in my backpack today instead of under the mattress. Baby steps.
Mãe, o desenho do mar que a Vó Lúcia emoldurou ainda está acima da minha cama. A parede parece velha, mas o mar continua igual. Obrigada por mandar as bolachas.
Bia's birthday week. We walked São Francisco looking for the wall we wrote on last year. It's still there. Nobody has painted over us. I felt oddly proud of graffiti.
Bia's birthday tomorrow. We are going to the bar in São Francisco and writing our names on the wall. I bought a marker that smells like grape. She will complain. That's tradition.
RU ran out of rice today. I ate beans and farofa and called it a meal. It was, technically. Engineering teaches priorities.
We wrote our names on the bar wall in São Francisco with a marker. If it's painted over by the time you read this, that's fine. We were there. I drew the marker line in my sketchbook too, in case.

The república fridge has six yogurts with six different names now, and mine is the only one with a smiley face. The system is unfair but I respect it. I drew the fridge like a police lineup for my sketchbook.

Bus 7am. The parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' and then 'obrigado', which I have never heard. The driver smiled for the first time since I started taking this bus. I drew them both in the margin of my Álgebra notebook, parrot included.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time I went in up to my ankles and the water was warm. Then I got scared of a small fish and woke up. My calves were tight but less tight than usual. Maybe that counts.
Rafa walked me home and told me São Paulo has jobs for people like me. I said Curitiba has people I like. He went quiet. We're both pretending not to notice again.
Bus parrot man wasn't there for three days and I was worried. He came back today with a bandage. The parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically. I'm choosing to believe it was personal.
Bia's wall names are still there at the bar in São Francisco. We checked. Someone drew a heart around 'BIA'. We didn't correct it. It felt right.
Dreamed of the sea again. Same dream. I woke with my calves tight and drew the water from memory before breakfast. It looked nothing like real water, but it helped.
Mom called to ask if I'm eating. I said yes. I had cup noodles and an apple. Technically both food. She would disagree. I drew the apple core to feel productive.
R$ 90 for books, R$ 40 for bus, R$ 15 for Bia's birthday marker. The rest is RU and hope. I have a talent for budgets that look like haikus.

Storm over Curitiba, power out for an hour. We sat in the kitchen with candles and ate crackers. I drew everyone by candlelight and my roommate said I made her look mysterious instead of tired. She approved.

Bia's birthday is coming and I don't have money for a gift. I'm drawing her a comic about the two of us as old ladies arguing about the sea. She will say it's too sentimental. She will keep it. Both things are true.

Portuguese: Amanheceu frio e eu vesti o suéter da mãe. O manjericão da república ainda está vivo, o que eu considero um milagre pessoal. Desenhei ele hoje com três folhas novas. A Maria disse 'agora ele é oficial'. Eu disse 'agora ele é mais oficial que eu'.
Álgebra notebook full of margins. If anyone reads it they'll think I'm a terrible student. They'd be right, but at least I'm a decorated terrible student.

The old man with the parrot missed a week and I was genuinely worried, like he is family, which he isn't. Today he was back with a bandage. The parrot said bom dia to me specifically and I counted it.
Dreamed of the sea again. Still standing at the edge, still can't go in. Woke up with tight calves and made coffee. At least the coffee is honest.
Parrot man missing from the bus for three days now. I asked the driver and he said 'sei lá'. I drew him anyway, with the parrot on his shoulder, in case memory fades faster than pencil.
The parrot man was back with a bandage on his hand. He didn't say anything. The parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically. I'm counting it as a good day.
Money check: R$ 140 left, it's the 3rd, so not panic yet, just awareness. RU tomorrow and maybe one more pastel if I survive Álgebra.

Parrot man back on the bus after a week, hand bandaged. The parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically and I almost cried in public. I am becoming the kind of adult who cries at birds, and I accept this.
The parrot man wasn't on the bus for a week and I was genuinely worried. Today he was back with a bandage on his hand. The parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically. I'm counting it.
Rafa talked about São Paulo for an hour. I talked about the sea for ten minutes. Neither of us changed subjects. We're a good match for listening, not for geography.

Rafa came to the república to study and ate all my emergency bolachas. In exchange he explained a Cálculo problem until I understood it. Fair trade, I think. He also said my sea drawings are 'pretty', which is the nicest thing he has said about my art.

The parrot man was back after a week. Bandage on his hand. The parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically, I'm sure of it. I said 'bom dia' back like a normal person and then smiled the whole ride. Some days are enough.
The parrot man wasn't on the bus for a week. I was worried. Today he came back with a bandage and the parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically. I'm counting it.
Drew on the bus today, standing up, holding the pole with one hand. The line is crooked but the old man's posture is right. I like bus drawings more than class drawings.

Parrot man missing for a week. I checked the bus stop every morning like a worried relative. Today he was back with a bandage and the parrot said 'bom dia' to me. I smiled so hard the driver looked concerned.

The parrot man wasn't on the bus for a week and I was genuinely worried. Today he was back with a bandage on his hand. The parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically. I'm counting it. I also drew them from memory while waiting at the stop.
Rafa bought me a pastel after I failed Cálculo. He said I'm too smart to fail twice. I wanted to argue but he was holding two pasteis and looked proud of himself. I let him have the win.
Mom called and asked if I gave up on the drawings yet. I said yes. I lied. Sketchbook under the mattress, as usual. One day I'll just show her. Not today.
Drew Seu Ivo and Juca in the margin of my notebook again. The parrot got a little hat this time. I don't know why. It felt right.

Sunday call with Vó Lúcia. She talked about Coronel for ten minutes and I wrote down every word. She says he used to wait by the gate even in the rain. I want to draw him with his ears wet, but I can't get his eyes right yet.
Vó Lúcia told me the story of Coronel again, the farm dog who walked her to school. This time he waited at the gate even in the rain. I wrote it down twice.

Money check: R$ 300 left for the month and it's the 21st. Living on RU and the bolachas Mom sends. I'm writing this so in a few years I can laugh at it. Or cry. Depends on the future's sense of humor.
O senhor do papagaio sumiu uma semana e eu fiquei preocupada. Hoje voltou com curativo e o papagaio disse 'bom dia' para mim. Estou contando.
Money check: R$ 280 left and it's the 21st. The bolachas from Mom are doing structural work. I ate one with coffee and called it lunch.
Drew Mom's hands while she knitted on video call. She complained about the camera angle. The drawing is crooked because I was laughing. Best hands I've ever drawn, probably.

I practiced floating in the pool alone today, early morning, nobody watching. I lasted six seconds. A kid of maybe six floated next to me like it was nothing. I left before he could see me panic. I'm going back Thursday.
The sea dream came back, same as always: edge of water, warm, can't step in. I woke up and my calves were tight. Five years from now, I hope the dream changed. That's the only resolution I want.

The parrot man wasn't on the bus for a week. I was genuinely worried and tried to hide it by drawing the empty seat. Today he came back with a bandage on his hand. Juca said 'bom dia' to me specifically. I'm counting it.
Money check: R$ 310 left, and it's the 23rd. I am living on bolachas Mom sends and the free coffee at the library. The library coffee tastes like cardboard but it's warm and I am grateful.
Money is tight again. R$ 310 left and eight days to go. I have become an expert in RU seconds and creative uses of instant noodles. The sketchbook is the only thing I own that I would not sell.
Money check: R$ 410 left and it's the 27th. Better than last year's R$ 340 on the 28th. I'm an economist now.

Rafa talked about São Paulo for an hour at lunch. Buildings, jobs, the noise, like it's a person he's in love with. I talked about the sea. We both pretended not to notice. Afterward I drew a building with waves coming out of the windows.
Álgebra at 7:30am and I drew the parrot in the margin instead of solving systems. The professor looked at my notebook and said 'interesting'. I think that was sarcasm but I'm choosing to believe.
Money check: R$ 90 left and I still have a week. RU is becoming a personality. I drew my plate as if it were a still life. It was rice, beans, and hope.

Vó Lúcia told me about the farm in Irati and how Coronel the dog used to sleep under the jabuticabeira. She said he chose the spot himself. I asked how she knew. She said 'because he always smelled like jabuticaba'. I'm going to draw this.
Money check: R$ 210 left and it's October 2nd. Living on RU and the bolachas Mom sends. Writing this so next year I can laugh. Or cry. Depends.
Vó Lúcia told me about Coronel again. He waited at the gate every day for nine years. I didn't tell her I drew him. Some drawings are for later.

Mom asked if I had 'given up on the drawings yet' and I said yes again. The lie is easier now, which worries me. Under the mattress, the sketchbook is getting thick. One day I will show her without apologizing first.

I planted nothing, but I looked at a lemon on the kitchen counter for too long. Vó Lúcia says everything starts with looking. She also says I talk too much. Both are probably true. I drew the lemon and it looked like a small sun.
Drew Seu Ivo e o Papagaio in my notebook during engineering class. Haven't decided if I'll ever show anyone. Probably not. Probably yes.

Vó Lúcia told me about the farm dog again, Coronel. She said he used to sleep under her bed when she was scared. I asked if he snored. She laughed and said 'igual seu avô'. I want to draw this forever.
Money check: R$ 212 and it's the 5th. Living on RU and Mom's bolachas, plus one pastel I split with Bia. I'm writing this so future me can laugh or cry depending on salary.
Rafa bought me a pastel because I failed Cálculo and said I was too smart to fail twice. He is annoying and I think I love him. I drew him eating the pastel and he looked offended. Good.

Rafa and I walked in Passeio Público again and fed the ducks, which was chaotic and beautiful. He said São Paulo has no ducks. I said Curitiba wins. He did not disagree, so I am counting it as a victory.

Swimming lesson with Bia. She floated; I sank in a dignified way. Dona Cida, from the adult beginner class, called me 'a engenheira' and said floating is about trust, not technique. Very poetic for 7am. I swallowed half the pool.
Vó Lúcia told me Coronel waited at the school gate every day. I asked if he ever got bored. She said 'he was a dog, he had patience'. I wrote that down twice because it sounded like advice.

Mom called to ask if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said yes. I lied. I have a sketchbook under the mattress like it's something illegal. I also have ink under my thumbnail that I hope she doesn't notice on Sunday.
RU pastel was weirdly good today. I had two. The cashier didn't judge. Or judged silently. Either way.
Vó Lúcia called and asked if I'm eating enough. I said yes. She asked if I'm drawing enough. I said no. She didn't say anything and changed the subject. That was worse.
Rafa bought me a pastel and said I'm too smart to fail twice. Annoying. I think I love him. I also haven't drawn in two months and I know. I know.
Mom asked if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said yes. I lied. I have a sketchbook under the mattress and one hidden in the thermodynamics textbook, which feels appropriately dramatic.
Drew in the margin of my Física notebook all morning. Professor didn't notice, or noticed and didn't care. Either way I now have a whole bus stop scene between 'força' and 'aceleração'.

Vó Lúcia's Sunday story today was about the farm dog and the jabuticabeira. She cried a little and pretended she didn't. I drew her hands afterward, folded in her lap, and finally got the knuckles right.

Tio Beto taught me three more chords on the violão. I still can't play 'Asa Branca' all the way through. He said he's heard that promise from every cousin. I promised to prove him wrong. I think he's heard that too.
Mom called to ask if I've given up on the drawings yet. I said yes. I lied. Sketchbook is under the mattress again because one of the girls saw me drawing and asked what it was for.
Rafa said I talk about the sea like it's a person. He's right. It is. I haven't met it properly yet, but I dream about it every week.

Rafa and I walked in the Passeio Público after pastel de feira. He talked about São Paulo. I talked about the sea. We both pretended not to notice. He bought me a lemonade and I thought about how nobody in my family would call it 'limonada' without a joke.
Bia, obrigada por me acordar quando dormi no ônibus e perdi o ponto. Você também desenhou um bigode na minha mão enquanto eu dormia. Amizade é assim.

Vó Lúcia told me about Coronel again, the farm dog in Irati who walked her to school and waited at the gate. She cried, sixty years later. I want to draw this one day. I wrote it down so I won't forget.
First cold snap. I wore two sweaters and still shivered on the bus. The parrot looked cold too, tucked into the man's jacket. I drew them and then felt bad for not offering my scarf.
Called Vó Lúcia and she talked about Coronel the farm dog for half an hour. I took notes in my Álgebra notebook. The dog gets braver every time she tells it.
Bus comic idea: a parrot who judges everyone's outfits. I sketched three panels and then hid them because it felt too silly. Future me, if you ever start drawing comics, begin with the parrot.
Cheque financeiro: R$ 210 e já é dia 25. Vida de RU e bolacha da mãe. Escrevo para no ano que vem rir. Ou chorar. Depende.
The bus was so full I had to stand, holding onto the bar, sketching with one hand. Drew a man sleeping with his mouth open and his phone on his chest. The drawing is terrible and I love it.

Vó Lúcia told me the story of Coronel, the farm dog in Irati who walked her to school for nine years. When he died, her father buried him under the jabuticabeira. She cried telling it, sixty years later. I want to draw this one day. Not yet. I'm not ready.
Rain all day. I stayed inside and drew small animals from memory. A dog, a parrot, a lemon. I don't know why the lemon. Maybe I want one.

Portuguese: Chuva de novo. O manjericão está enorme e a Maria quer plantar tomate. Desenhei uma tirinha do ônibus hoje: senhor, papagaio e o motorista, que não sabe que é personagem. Mostrei para a Bia e ela riu. Guardar isso.
Rain again. Curitiba doesn't ask permission. My shoes are wet and my mood is also wet, but tomorrow is a new day and new shoes, hopefully.
Rafa and I walked in Passeio Público and he talked about São Paulo for twenty minutes straight. I let him talk. The trees were yellow and beautiful and he didn't look at them once. I did.
I tried to float in the pool for ten seconds and made it to four. A child of maybe six floated next to me the whole time. I'm choosing to find it motivating instead of humiliating.
Bia, você dormiu no ônibus e acordou dizendo 'já chegamos em São Paulo'. Estávamos em Portão. Sua geografia é um sonho. Ainda assim, você é minha pessoa favorita para sentar no fundo do Interbairros.
Rafa bought me coffee after I failed Cálculo study group. He sat next to me in silence for ten minutes. It was the nicest ten minutes of the week.
Bia and I studied all afternoon and then rewarded ourselves with pastel and a walk. She asked if I'm happy. I said 'more than last month'. She said 'write that down'. So I am, for both of us.

Rafa and I danced in his kitchen to a song I don't remember. His mom asked when we're getting married. He said 'when she agrees to São Paulo'. Everyone laughed. I laughed too, but it took a second. The second felt long.
Rafa talked about São Paulo again. I drew the Passeio Público trees instead of listening. He noticed and said 'you always escape into the page'. He wasn't wrong. I didn't like it.
Vó Lúcia said she fell asleep before midnight but 'saw the fireworks in her head'. I believe her. She has very good imagination for an old woman.
Bia, the bar wall still has our names. I checked. It's fading but it's there. We were there, like we said.
Bia and I tried to make bolo de fubá from Vó Lúcia's recipe. We forgot the baking powder. It came out like a sweet brick. We ate it with milk anyway and laughed until we cried.

I haven't drawn in two months. I know. I know. But tonight I drew one small page: Vó Lúcia on the phone, with her hands around the receiver. It took ten minutes and felt like breathing after holding it too long.
Rafa and I danced in the kitchen to no music. That's it. That's the capsule. I just wanted to write it down so it doesn't disappear.
Therapy with no therapist: sat on the curb outside the república and drew the bus stop until the light changed. It's the cheapest session I've had.
I tried floating in the pool again and made it to seven seconds. Dona Cida is not there yet, but a lady in the next lane clapped. I waved like an idiot. Still counts as progress.
Drew Vó Lúcia's hands from memory: big knuckles, small rings, the way she holds the phone like it might escape. I think hands are the hardest thing. Also the most worth drawing.

I drew all night. Not the sea, not Rafa, not the bus. Just my hands. They looked strange and tired and mine. Sometimes drawing feels like checking whether I'm still here. I am. Graphite under my nails says so.
Vó Lúcia's bolo de fubá recipe came out wrong. Too dry. I called her and she said 'mais manteiga, menina'. I wrote it down this time.
Tio Beto, toquei a primeira parte de 'Asa Branca' sem olhar para as mãos hoje. Na segunda parte, desisti e fingi que estava ajustando o violão. Você viu. Claro que viu.
Mãe perguntou se eu desisti dos desenhos. Disse que sim. Menti. O caderno está de novo embaixo do colchão porque uma das meninas me viu desenhando e perguntou para quê.

Tio Beto, I'm writing this to you in case I forget to say it at Christmas. Thank you for the violão and for not laughing too hard when I forgot 'Asa Branca'. You said 'one more year' like it was obvious. I'm holding you to that.
Rafa brought me a pastel because I failed a quiz. He's annoying and kind and I don't know what to do with that combination.
Parrot man back on the bus with a bandage on his hand. The parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically. I am counting it. I drew his bandaged hand in the notebook margin.
Rain, late bus, wet shoes. The parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' and everyone stayed quiet. I wanted to clap. I just smiled at Juca and felt ridiculous in the best way.

Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' after lunch and asked me to try. I got further than last year, maybe halfway. He said 'one more year' with that smile. I'm starting to think one more year is his love language.

It's hot in Curitiba for once and everyone complains, but I like it. I sat on the república steps with my sketchbook and drew the lemon tree across the street even though it's small and a little crooked.
Swimming came up again in conversation and I changed the subject. Rafa noticed. He didn't push it. I'm grateful and annoyed at the same time.

Money check: R$ 260 left and it's the 16th. I bought a pastel for Rafa because he looked sad about São Paulo. He didn't ask for it. He ate it and said 'you're too kind'. I think that's the nicest thing he's said to me.

Rafa, if you're reading this, we made it five years. You said capsules are cheesy, so this is me being cheesy on purpose. Thank you for the playlist that got me through Física 2, for learning Vó Lúcia's bolo de fubá recipe just to impress her, and for not laughing (much) when I panicked in the swimming pool. Whatever happens, I hope we're still the kind of people who dance in the kitchen.
Rafa, se você estiver lendo isso, obrigada pelos pastéis e pelos problemas de cálculo. Eu ainda não sei se São Paulo é para mim, mas sua risada sim. Continua tocando a playlist, por favor. Beijo.

The república is cold and the heater is broken. I drew wearing gloves, which looked ridiculous and worked badly. Bia called to say she saw the first star. I couldn't see it from my window. I drew it anyway.
Dia de dar graças? Não é nosso feriado, mas Bia brought leftover turkey and we ate it with farofa. She said I should draw food more. She's right. Food is easier than people.
Rafa talked about São Paulo for forty minutes and I counted. Not to be petty, just because numbers are comforting. Then I talked about the sea for twenty. We called it even.
Cold morning, bus windows fogged. I drew a face in the condensation with my finger and it disappeared before my stop. I think that's what most drawings are anyway.

Money check: R$ 340 left for the month and it's the 28th. Living on RU and the bolachas Mom sends. I'm writing this so in a year I can laugh at it. Or cry. Depends. At least the coffee at the república is free.

Rafa, if you're reading this, I'm being cheesy on purpose: thank you for the pastel after Cálculo and for not laughing when I panic in swimming pools. We're not even at five years yet. Don't get cocky.
Drew the lemon tree from the sidewalk again. The neighbor looked out the window. We both pretended nothing happened.
Mom, I know you think drawings are just a hobby. But the old man with the parrot on the 7am bus looks realer when I draw him than when I see him. I don't know what that means yet. I'm not stopping.
A criança do ônibus, maybe six years old, waved at me today. I waved back. The parrot did not wave. Parrots are honest. I respect that.
The sea dream again. I stood at the edge. The water was warm. My feet moved a little, then stopped. Progress, maybe. Or just dreaming.
End of semester. I failed Cálculo 1 and passed Física. I cried in the RU and then ate a pastel. Rafa sat with me and didn't say anything smart, which was exactly right.
Mom said illustration is a hobby, not a job. I said okay. Then I drew the old man with the parrot under my blanket with a flashlight like a teenager reading forbidden poetry.
Rafa and I walked in the Passeio Público. He talked about São Paulo for ten minutes. I talked about the sea for ten minutes. We walked in silence for twenty. It was good.
Sunday call with Vó Lúcia. She said the farm dog Coronel would have liked me because I 'walk slowly and look at things'. I didn't know that was a compliment until she said it.

Bia and I walked from São Francisco to the centro eating pastel de feira in the cold. She told me I should post the bus drawings online. I said nobody would care. She said 'I care'. That's not the same thing, but it made me consider it.

Vó Lúcia called and pretended she didn't care that I called. Then she talked for forty minutes about the farm and Coronel and the jabuticabeira. I held the phone and drew her hand from memory afterwards.
Vó Lúcia told me again about Coronel, the farm dog in Irati who walked her to school. She cried again, sixty years later. I want to draw it someday, when I'm brave enough.

December in Curitiba already feels like January. The república has a tiny plastic tree and one of the girls hung socks on it. I drew it and sent the photo to Vó Lúcia, who asked if the tree was real. I said yes. Partial lie.
Cold morning, breath visible at the bus stop. A woman sold bolos de fubá from a basket. I bought one because it smelled like Vó Lúcia's kitchen, which is unfair emotional manipulation by a pastry.
I called Vó Lúcia and she told me to eat more. Then she asked if I was drawing. I said yes. She said 'good' and changed the subject. I think that's her version of a compliment. I'll take it.
Vó Lúcia called to ask if I failed. I said yes. She said 'bom, agora você sabe como não fazer'. Then she told me to eat. She always ends calls with food.
Bus 7am. Parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' like always. I drew it from memory later because I was late and forgot. The drawing is better when I don't have the notebook.
Mom called to ask if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. Same question, same answer. The sketchbook is still there. Still illegal, still mine.
Bia, se você ler isto, lembre que em dezembro de 2015 eu tentei te ensinar a desenhar um gato e você fez um pão. Você disse que era 'estilo'. Continua sendo meu estilo favorito.
Drew the republica fridge with everyone's names on the yogurts. It's the most beautiful still life I've ever made and it's a fridge. I'm okay with that.
Tio, estou treinando Asa Branca devagarinho. Ainda erro na segunda estrofe, mas não desisto. O violão está desafinado, ou sou eu. Provavelmente sou eu.

Portuguese: Vó Lúcia contou hoje a história do Coronel pela terceira vez. Desta vez ele era mais valente e esperava a minha avó com o rabo abanando na chuva. Cada versão muda um pouco. Escrevi todas no caderno. Um dia vou desenhar isso.

Bia and I planned Matinhos for New Year's again. I packed less this time, more swimsuits, less expectation. I still want to put my feet in the water at midnight. That's enough for 2015. Future me, were you brave enough to go further?
Tio, toquei 'Asa Branca' sozinha no quarto. Cheguei até o refrão antes de errar. O violão é de 7:30 da manhã e eu não tenho certeza se é coragem ou medo de acordar a república.
Dreamed of the sea again. Same dream, but this time I put one foot in. Only a toe. Progress, maybe. Or just a dream being a dream. I woke up and drew the toe before I could forget it.
Terapia sem terapeuta: sentei no meio-fio da república e desenhei o ponto de ônibus até a luz mudar. Foi a sessão mais barata da minha vida.
Tio Beto, I'll learn the whole song by next Festa Junina. This time I mean it. Write it down if you want proof.
Bia, thanks for letting me cry on your shoulder in the RU and not telling anyone. You're the only person who knows I failed and I need it to stay that way for at least one more week.
República Christmas dinner. Four girls, one panettone, no plates because someone forgot. We ate with spoons. The panettone wrapper became a hat. It was better than any formal dinner.
Money check: R$ 340 left and it's the 28th. Living on RU and the bolachas Mom sends. I'm writing this so in two years I can laugh at it. Or cry. Depends.
Rafa and I walked through Passeio Público and saw a man feeding pigeons. Rafa said São Paulo pigeons are fatter. I said Curitiba pigeons have better manners. We are ridiculous.
Tio Beto, I promised to learn 'Asa Branca' by Festa Junina. You laughed. I know you laughed. I also know you hope I prove you wrong.
Mom, obrigado pelo panetone e pela ligação de 40 minutos sobre a vizinha. Eu não contei que desenho escondido, mas você perguntou 'está tudo bem?' e eu disse sim. Não era mentira, só incompleto.

Last bus of the semester. The parrot said 'tchau, motorista' at the final stop and two people actually laughed. I drew it in the Álgebra notebook, on the last page, because it seemed right. Engineering ends in a week. Drawing doesn't.
Tio Beto, I practiced 'Asa Branca' three times this week and got to the second verse twice. Tell nobody. I'm proving you wrong slowly.
Summer coming. I can feel it in the way the light hits the republica stairs. I keep thinking about Matinhos and the water. I still can't swim. I still want to.
Found a lemon seed in a yogurt cup at the república and almost planted it. Stopped myself because it's too cold and I'm not ready for that kind of responsibility. Maybe next year.

Bia and I wrote our names on a napkin at the bar in São Francisco, because we couldn't find a marker for the wall. If the napkin's gone by the time you read this, that's fine. We were there. That's the part that counts.
Preparations for Matinhos. I packed my sketchbook under my clothes like it's contraband. Vó Lúcia will pretend not to see it and then ask to see it.
Found a lemon on the counter at the republica. Nobody knows whose it is. It's small and bright and I drew it three times. Someone will eat it tomorrow and I'll be annoyed.
