Dreamed of the sea, but for once I was sitting on the sand drawing, not standing at the edge. Progress? Or laziness? I'll take it.
Christmas at Vó Lúcia's. She told the Coronel story again and I wrote down every version. The dog gets braver each time. I love that.
Christmas Eve at Vó Lúcia's. She fell asleep before dinner but woke up for the brigadeiro. Tio Beto played Asa Branca softly and she hummed. I didn't sing. I just listened.

Christmas at home. Mom asked if I gave up on the drawings yet. I said yes. The sketchbook stayed under the mattress and I drew the dinner table later from memory. The turkey looked like a potato. Progress.
New Year in Matinhos soon. I'm packing the sketchbook in the suitcase this time, not the mattress. Small change. Feels like a big one.
After Christmas lunch, Tio Beto handed me the violão without a word again. I played until verse two. Progress. He said 'one more year' and this time it sounded like a challenge I might lose.

New Year is coming. We're going to Matinhos. I stood with my feet in the water last year because that's as far as I go. This year I want to try one more step. Maybe two. I'm writing this so you know I meant to.

Year-end list: I still can't swim, still miss drawing in class, still want the sea. But I called Vó Lúcia every Sunday, and Rafa buys me pastéis, and Bia still sits next to me on the bus. Good enough for now.
New Year approaching. I'll stand with my feet in the water at midnight, like always. Maybe this year I'll go a little deeper. Probably not. We'll see.
Money check before the trip: R$ 140 and a jar of bolachas. Enough. The sea doesn't charge admission. I just need the bus.
Year almost over. I still can't swim, still failed calculus, still hiding the sketchbook sometimes. But I drew more than last year. That counts.
New Year in Matinhos soon. I'll stand with my feet in the water at midnight again, that's as far as I go. Unless something changes. I doubt it does.
Money check end of year: R$ 40 left and a fridge full of leftovers from Vó Lúcia. I am rich in sobras and poor in cash. The pastel at the bus station cost more than my dignity.

Last capsule of 2015. I'm writing at the kitchen table with the drawing of the sea Vó Lúcia framed above my bed still there, slightly crooked. I straightened it. Tomorrow I go to Matinhos and put my feet in the water at midnight, like always. One day, I hope, more than feet.
Tomorrow is New Year's. Bia wants to go to Matinhos, I want to go too, but I'm scared of the sea at midnight. I'll stand with my feet in the water. That's always been enough.
Last day of the year. I drew the república room with the sea drawing above the bed. It's still there. I hope it still is in two years.
New Year in Matinhos. Vó Lúcia fell asleep before midnight and still claimed she saw fireworks. I stood with my feet in the water. It was cold. I didn't mind.

First RU lunch of the year. Arroz, feijão, frango frito, and a salad that looks like a cry for help. I drew the chicken bone on the corner of my tray and the guy next to me said it looked like a dinosaur. We agreed the dessert was suspicious. I think I made a friend.

Primeiro dia do ano no trabalho de grupo de Cálculo. Cheguei cedo, abri a janela e o vento quase levou minhas folhas. O menino do paraguai que vende bomba no corredor gritou 'engenheira' e eu nem sou engenheira ainda. Pequeno milagre: encontrei minha caneta azul no fundo da mochila. Vou guardar ela como se fosse talismã.
Three yogurt-cup seeds, no sprout, no hope, just mud with ambition. I keep watering them because giving up on a cup of dirt feels dramatic. If Limonada never happens, at least I tried.

Bus 7am, Interbairros II. O velho com o papagaio verde não veio hoje, e eu fiquei com a sensação de ter perdido um capítulo. Desenhei mesmo assim, de memória, com o papagaio dizendo 'bom dia, motorista' no balãozinho. Se o velho voltar, eu mostro.
First day back at UTFPR. The 7am Interbairros was late and I sat next to a man carrying a bag of polenta. I drew the bag. It looked like a cloud. Small victories.
Back in Curitiba and the república already smells like someone burned popcorn. Limonada has two leaves and a very serious attitude. I drew her on the yogurt cup label so nobody throws her out.

Limonada update: three seeds planted, only one still standing. The other two gave up after two days, which I respect. I'm watering her with a medicine dropper because the big cup feels too aggressive. One leaf today, smaller than a fingernail.

Ate a lemon at the república and, for no reason, planted three seeds in a yogurt cup with 'MARINA' written on it (thanks, fridge rules). If even one sprouts I'm keeping it forever. Ten years, future me. Do you still have a lemon tree?

Bia, lembra que prometemos nadar 25 metros antes dos 25 anos? Hoje tentei na piscina do clube, sozinha, de madrugada, e consegui três. Três metros. Senti o fundo da piscina como um animal. Mas consegui três. Vou contar como progresso, não como fracasso.
Rafa bought pastel and asked why I always choose the one with too much pepper. Because pain is flavor. He said that's the most engineer thing I've ever said.

The lemon seed cup is on the windowsill now, next to the fridge. I check it every morning like it owes me money. Nothing yet, just dirt. Bia says I'm going to kill it with attention. The yogurt cup has started cracking, so I'm planning a rescue mission with tape. This is what I've become: a woman taping a yogurt cup for a lemon that doesn't exist yet.

Rafa and I argued about São Paulo again, over pastel de feira. He says the noise is 'alive'. I say the sea is alive too and doesn't have traffic. We ended up splitting a caldo de cana and pretending nothing happened. He's still annoying. I still like him.

Bus 7am, Seu Ivo had a new hat. Juca (the real one) said bom dia to the driver twice, as if the first time wasn't enough. I drew it but my hand was shaking because of the pothole near Praça Rui Barbosa.

First week back after Matinhos. My suitcase still smells like sunscreen and I keep finding sand in my wallet. Engineering starts tomorrow. I pressed a lemon leaf from the república's garden and put it in the Álgebra notebook, next to the parrot drawing from 2014. It's not a good drawing, but it's mine.
It rained so hard on Rua XV that the bathroom flooded a little. We used towels and blamed the fridge. I saved the lemon cup. Priorities.
Bus 7am, same seats, same damp smell. The parrot said 'bom dia' to a stranger today and the stranger looked terrified. I almost told him: that's just Juca's warm-up.

Bia, hoje comprei um caderno novo só pra desenhar no ônibus de novo. O Interbairros parece cenário de novela às 7 da manhã: gente dormindo em pé, sacolas, o motorista falando com o pássaro como se fosse colega de trabalho. Tô pensando em postar alguns desenhos. Se você rir deles, tudo bem, eu já rio antes.

Mom, this one is for you. I didn't give up on the drawings, I just hid them better. The sketchbook under the mattress is now inside a pillowcase inside a laundry basket, which is maybe not better. I just wanted you to read this in one year and know I was still lying in 2016.

Matinhos. O mar está quente demais e tem cheiro de peixe. Vó Lúcia insistiu em fazer bolo de fubá às 6 da manhã. Comi dois pedaços com café, de pé na cozinha, antes de todo mundo acordar. Acordei com o pé úmido porque a onda chega até a varanda. Futura eu: você ainda acorda cedo por causa do mar ou por causa do bodo?
The república fridge still has names on every yogurt. I labeled mine with a tiny lemon. Nobody touched it. Small miracles.
Bia, thanks for letting me cry on your shoulder about Cálculo and then immediately making me watch a cooking show. You are the only person who makes failure feel like a commercial break.

Rain on Rua XV. The gutters overflowed and I had to jump over a small river to reach the bus stop. My sneaker is still damp. On the bus, the old man with the parrot waved at me like we know each other, which we don't, except in margins. I drew him again, this time with an umbrella.
Bia, the república fridge has a new rule: if your name isn't on it, it's public. Someone ate my yogurt and I felt more betrayed than in any rom-com. We need a lock.

RU lunch today: arroz, feijão, bife que era mais grelha do que carne. I sat with two girls from Turmas de Mecânica and we all complained about the same professor, which is basically a prayer circle. I drew the bife in my notebook instead of eating it first. One of them said I should make a comic of the RU menu. She's not wrong.

Bia, if you're reading this I probably forgot to text back again. Sorry. You are still the first person I think of when something funny happens on the bus. I'll call you tonight. Probably. Don't be mad.
Bia, you said you'd come for RU lunch and then appeared with a pizza box instead. I forgive you. We ate on the floor of my room and Limonada got a crumb on her leaf. She seemed honored.
Limonada has three leaves now. I talk to her when I study. She is a better listener than my calculus book.

Ônibus 7am. O senhor do papagaio estava de camisa amarela e o papagaio tinha uma pena nova, verde mais claro. Desenhei os dois no verso do cartão de ônibus. Seu Ivo (ainda não sei o nome de verdade) me deu um aceno. Acho que já somos conhecidos sem sermos apresentados.
The 7am bus parrot said 'bom dia' to the driver again. I drew him in the margin of my caderno, but this time I gave him a tiny hat. He looked good in it.

Limonada has two leaves and already looks dramatic. I check her every morning before class, like a tiny employee. The girls asked if she is a pet. I said she is a project. Nobody laughed. I think they are worried about me.
Chuva o dia inteiro em Curitiba. O ônibus atrasou, eu molhei o caderno e o homem do papagaio falou 'motorista, essa chuva é castigo'. O papagaio repetiu. Achei justo.

Money check: R$ 210 left, it's the 3rd. The lemon seeds cost nothing and still feel like the best investment I made this month. Studying calculus with a cup of Limonada next to me makes it less hostile.

Pastel de feira with Rafa after calculus. He ordered two, one cheese, one pizza, and said São Paulo has better pastels, which is not a thing you say to a Curitibana at a feira. I ate both out of spite. He laughed and called me petty. He's right.

Dream again. The edge of the sea, warm water, my feet stuck. But this time I looked down and my shoes were still on. I woke up and checked my feet in the dark. I don't know what that means, but it felt specific.
Limonada update: one sprout, two leaves, and now a third tiny leaf that I'm calling a personality trait. The girls asked if I'm going to give it a diploma. I said when it gives me a lemon.
Drew the bus line in the margin of my Física notebook again. My professor looked at the parrot and then at me. I said it was a force diagram. He did not believe me.
Mom, you asked if I was eating. I made arroz com feijão and it was edible, which counts. Please keep sending bolachas.

Rafa, não é Dia dos Namorados oficial mas você esqueceu que eu odeio rosas vermelhas e trouxe uma amarela. Amarela. Você disse que era para parecer sol. Fiquei brava por cinco minutos e depois não mais. Se você ler isso no futuro, saiba que eu guardei a rosa prensada no livro de Álgebra. É a primeira vez que Álgebra serve para alguma coisa.
Rafa gave me a small cactus for Valentine's Day. I already named it Espinho. He says I name everything. He's not wrong.
Valentine's Day, and Rafa bought me a cactus because 'you're hard to take care of but worth it.' Romantic. I put it next to Limonada on the windowsill. It already looks annoyed.
Valentine's Day. Rafa gave me a plant that is already dying. I think he's testing me. I will keep it alive out of spite.

Happy Valentine's, Rafa. You forgot the date and bought me a pão de queijo at the terminal instead. It was the best pão de queijo of my life and I will never tell you that because you will never buy anything on purpose again.
Rafa bought me a pastel de feira and said 'this is romantic because I remembered'. He forgot the napkins. We ate standing up and it was perfect in a greasy, ordinary way.
Rafa made me a Valentine's pastel in the shape of a heart. It looked like a kidney. I ate it anyway and drew it before it went cold. Romantic? No. Memorable? Very.

Bia, feliz Dia dos Namorados. Rafa bought me a single rose and I almost cried because it's the first time someone gave me a rose. You would have said 'don't marry him yet, marry the rose'. I kept the rose in a glass on the windowsill next to Limonada. The lemon has two leaves now, which is two more than the rose will have in a week.

Mom, se você estiver lendo isso, eu sei que você disse que desenho é hobby. Mas hoje eu desenhei no ônibus e o motorista viu e disse 'tá bonito'. Não é muito, mas é um começo. Eu te amo mesmo assim. Desculpa ter mentido sobre desenhar.
My room still smells like old wood, and the sea drawing Vó Lúcia framed is still above the bed. Future me, tell me it stayed there.
Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He asked if I learned 'Asa Branca' yet and I said 'almost'. He said 'almost is a very large country'. I wrote that down because it sounds like something Vó would say.

Limonada tem quatro folhinhas agora e inclinou-se para a luz como se estivesse curiosa. Reguei com pouco demais, acho, porque a terra está seca. Escrevi 'não mata a planta, Marina' no post-it e coloquei na geladeira, ao lado dos nomes nos iogurtes. As meninas acharam fofo. Eu achei necessário.

Bus 7am. The parrot man was there, parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' right on schedule. I noticed the old man's shoelaces were untied and I almost said something but didn't, because he's not the kind of man you tell about shoelaces. Drew him anyway. The drawing came out wrong: too much like my grandfather.

Mom, I know you said illustration is a hobby. I started a little comic about my bus line and posted it online. 47 people follow it. I'm not telling you this so you'll be proud, just so you know I kept drawing under the mattress and now it's on a screen.
Limonada has two leaves now and they're facing opposite directions like she can't decide on a personality. I understand her completely.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was holding a lemon instead of trying to swim. Interpret that however you want.

Portuguese test day. I keep a list of words I like on the last page of my notebook: 'jabuticabeira', 'paralelepípedo', 'saudade', 'mar'. The professor thinks I'm studying when I'm just collecting. Maybe collecting is a kind of studying.
One of the lemon seeds sprouted! Two tiny leaves. The girls named it Limonada. It lives on the windowsill next to my sketchbook, which no longer hides under the mattress.
Cálculo at 7:30 again. I drew a sea in the corner of the exam paper, tiny, like a secret. Professor didn't notice. I passed by two points. Victory tastes like coffee.

Rafa made pastel for me on the feira, queijo e queijo, and I ate two. He asked about São Paulo again, the train, the chaos, like it's a country he wants to move to. I said 'maybe after graduation' in a voice that sounded like a question. He heard it as a yes. I don't know if it was.
Money check: R$ 190 left and it's the first. RU feijoada saved me today. I am becoming a person who says 'feijoada saved me' without irony, which might be the real adulthood.

Limonada update: two tiny leaves, slightly larger than yesterday. The girls in the república are invested now. Camila put a sticky note on the cup that says 'do not water too much, Marina'. I watered too much yesterday.
Mom, you called to ask if I was eating. I said yes. I had eaten bolacha and coffee for lunch, but technically yes. I'm sending you a photo of Limonada so you have someone else to worry about.

Rained all afternoon and the república's kitchen roof leaked exactly over my chair. I moved the laptop, then the lemon cup, then my dignity. Limonada survived. She has two tiny leaves and an attitude already.

Fiz pastel de feira com Rafa no sábado. Queimamos o primeiro e o cachorro do vizinho latiu contra a janela. Rafa comeu o queimado e disse que estava 'crocante'. É isso que quero lembrar: não o pastel, a risada dele quando o óleo espirrou no meu avental. Ainda cheira a óleo no avental.

Seven-thirty calculus, same chair, same professor. I drew a parrot in the margin and got caught. He looked at it, said 'bom dia', and kept teaching. I think that's my favorite moment of the semester so far.
Had a dream about Vó Lúcia's farm. The jabuticabeira was enormous and Coronel was under it, wagging his tail. I woke up wanting to draw the tree but I can't remember the shape of the leaves.

Rain all week. The república leaks from the bathroom ceiling in a very specific spot, so we put a bucket there and named it 'Lagoa'. I drew Lagoa as a character with sad eyes. It is my best drawing this month, which is concerning.
Limonada got her fourth leaf. She's growing sideways like she's avoiding responsibility, which I respect. I moved her a centimeter to the left and felt like a gardener.
Bia, we ate pastel at the feira and the vendor recognized us by our order. I think that's our version of being regulars.

International Women's Day. The RU served a pink cake and I ate two slices because I was hungry and because it felt like the right amount of rebellion for a Tuesday. In class, the professor called on me for a question I didn't understand and I said 'I'm thinking' instead of 'I don't know'. Nobody laughed.
Bia, thank you for pretending my pastel de queijo was good yesterday. It wasn't. I forgot salt and used too much oil. You ate it like it was from a bakery and I owe you one forever.
Failed a calculus mock exam today. Sat on the bus afterward with my notebook open to the parrot drawing and pretended the math wasn't real. The parrot is more real than math. I choose the parrot.

Mãe, hoje pensei em você quando comprei um caderno de desenho na papelaria da Rua XV. Escrevi 'para os desenhos que você não sabe que eu faço' na primeira página. Se eu for corajosa o suficiente para te mostrar um dia, este caderno vai ser o início. Se não, será meu segredo mais bonito.
I still can't swim. I watched a kid float in the pool and felt personally offended. One day, Marina. One day.
Money check: R$ 280 left, it's the 14th, and the RU ran out of my favorite bolinho today. Mom's bolachas arrived though, with a note saying 'don't skip meals'. I ate three. Survival.

Tio Beto, I practiced 'Asa Branca' for twenty minutes today and I can do the first verse with almost no mistakes. The hard part is the second verse, which I've been skipping for two years. I'll record it on my phone and send it when it sounds less like a cat. Thank you for not giving up on me.
Dreamed of the sea again, but this time I was sitting on the sand with a sketchbook. The water didn't move. I woke up annoyed at the sea for being boring in my own dream.

Bia, you turned 20 yesterday and I forgot to buy a present so I'm writing this instead. I'm going to draw you a card with your face, which is risky because your nose is very specific and I might get it wrong. You are the only person who understands why I check the lemon cup every morning. Thank you for the sleepovers and the pastel de feira. We're 20 and already old.

On the bus at 6:50, Seu parrot man wasn't there and I felt my week get slightly smaller. Then he got on at the next stop, soaked, parrot dry under his jacket. The parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' as if nothing happened. I love that bird.
Cálculo professor gave me a 6.2 and said 'Marina, you are close.' Close is my whole personality. I celebrated with a pastel and a nap. The nap won.
Dreamed about the sea again. Same edge, same warm water, same frozen feet. But this time Vó Lúcia was behind me saying 'menina, vai'. I didn't go. Woke up annoyed at myself.

Choveu o dia inteiro em Curitiba e a RU serviu sopa de feijão. Comi duas tigelas e desenhei um senhor com capa de chuva. Ele tinha bigode e olhava para o teto como se estivesse conversando com o teto. Talvez estivesse. Curitiba faz isso com a gente.
Rafa brought me a fern for the windowsill. It died in six days. Limonada judged us both.

Dreamed of the sea again. Same dream, but this time there were four people on the beach and one of them was holding a parrot. I don't know what that means. I woke up and drew the parrot before brushing my teeth, which is a first.
Mãe, I didn't give up on the drawings. I just moved them to a different hiding place: the bottom of my bag. More dangerous, less dusty.

It rained so hard today the bus stopped under the viaduto for fifteen minutes. Everyone was quiet except the parrot, who said 'bom dia' to no one in particular. I drew the rain on the window, how it runs down like little rivers. The old man watched me draw and didn't say anything, but he smiled. That counts.
Swimming attempt, unofficial. Bia and I went to the public pool and she told me to float like a starfish. I floated for about six seconds and then remembered I had a calculus exam and sank. Progress.
Washed clothes at the lavanderia and forgot them overnight. A nice woman folded them and left a note: 'you draw well, I saw your strips'. Curitiba is smaller than I thought.

Mãe, obrigada pelas bolachas. Chegaram amassadas, mas continuam sendo as melhores. Prometo que não vou desistir dos desenhos, e prometo também que vou estudar Cálculo. As duas coisas são verdade. Obrigada por aguentar minha mentira de 2014, eu sei que você sabe.
Tio Beto, I practiced Asa Branca three times today and got through the first verse without collapsing. The violão has a string that hates me. I think it's personal.
Mom sent a message asking if I'm eating. I sent a photo of the fridge with names on yogurts. She replied 'that's not food, that's property law'. She's not wrong.

Tio Beto mandou áudio cantando 'Asa Branca' errado de propósito, com uma voz de pato. Respondi que eu também canto errado, mas pelo menos canto inteiro um dia. Ele mandou risadas. Lembrei de 2014, da promessa dos três acordes. Já sei cinco. A música inteira ainda não.
Tio Beto showed me the same three chords again. I still can't get past the second verse of Asa Branca. He patted my shoulder and said 'one more year', like a priest.

Mãe, I know you said drawing isn't a job, but today I drew a tiny lemon tree in the margin of my structures homework and the professor asked if I was an architect. I said no, just tired. You'd have laughed. I think.
I actually studied for Cálculo for four hours. Then I drew a comic about a stressed calculator. I think that's called balance.

Rain in Curitiba, the kind that turns the Rua XV into a small river. I missed my stop because I was drawing Limonada's leaf in the condensation on the window. Bus driver looked at me like I was the problem. Fair.
Thunderstorm over Curitiba, the kind that makes the windows shake. Limonada is on the sill and I moved her inside, wrapped in a towel. She looked offended, like a small plant with dignity.

Called Vó Lúcia on Sunday. She told me the story of Coronel again, the farm dog. This time she said he was 'more yellow than you think'. I asked what that means and she said 'it means he was yellow, Marina'. I wrote it down. I'm collecting these versions.
Tio Beto taught me the third verse of 'Asa Branca' again. I forgot it by the time I reached the bus. The chords are in my fingers but the memory is not. Maybe they'll meet someday.

Festa de aniversário da república. We made a brigadeiro tower and it collapsed before the candles. We ate it with spoons anyway. Bia came over and brought a drawing she found in my old notebook: a sea I drew in 2013. I'd forgotten about it. It's better than what I draw now, which is annoying.

Bus 7am. A senhora que sempre tricota um cachecol azul derrubou uma agulha e eu a peguei antes de alguém pisar. Ela disse 'obrigada, menina' e continuou tricotando como se nada. O papagaio não disse nada hoje. Dias de silêncio dele são dias em que acho que ele está pensando.

Seu Ivo brought the parrot with a tiny yellow bow today. The bus got louder somehow. I drew the bow in three different sizes and none of them captured how ridiculous it looked. Some things resist documentation.
Vó Lúcia called to ask if I've eaten feijão. I said yes. I had instant noodles with ketchup. I will confess eventually, or I won't, and this is where that secret lives.
Tio Beto, I practiced Asa Branca tonight with your chords. I got to the second verse and then lost my place, same as always. But I didn't stop. I started over. That's new.
First thunderstorm of autumn. The power went out and we ate cup noodles by candlelight. I drew shadows on the wall with my phone flashlight. The girls said it was creepy. I said it was art.

A girl in calculus asked if I was the one who drew the parrot in the Álgebra notebook from last year. I said maybe. She said it made her laugh during the exam. I don't know if that's a compliment or a crime.

Bus 7am. Seu Ivo and the parrot were not there. I almost asked the driver if he knew them, then realized I don't even know if the man's name is Ivo. For the strip, I called him Ivo. For the real life, he's just 'the parrot man'. I hope he's okay.
R$ 280 left and it's the 15th. I'm living on RU rice and the bolachas Mom sends. I'm writing this so next year I can laugh. Or cry. Depends.

Dreamed of the sea again. I was standing at the edge, as always, but this time I was holding a small plant. I think it was Limonada. The water looked like Curitiba rain: grey, cold, familiar. Still didn't go in.

Domingo de sol. Fui ao Passeio Público com o caderno. Desenhei duas crianças tentando alcançar os peixes no lago. Um rapaz veio perguntar se eu desenhava profissionalmente. Respondi 'não ainda'. A palavra 'ainda' saiu antes de eu pensar. Guardei ela. É uma palavra pequena e perigosa.

Cálculo 1 is not being kind. I did three exercises tonight and got two wrong, and the one I got right I'm sure is a miracle. Rafa says I'm smart. I say intelligence doesn't help if you can't sit still. I drew in the margin of the exercise sheet: a tiny figure climbing a staircase of integrals. It helped, a little.
Bia, obrigada por aceitar meu desenho do papagaio como presente de aniversário. Você disse 'muito fofo' com a cara de quem sabe que não é fofo. Vou desenhar você feia na próxima.
Vó Lúcia called and asked why I wasn't talking about the sea anymore. I said I was tired of it. She laughed and said 'you are the sea, menina'. I didn't know what to do with that.

Money check: R$ 120 left until the 25th. I bought cheese bread and a sketchbook. The sketchbook was R$ 22, which is too much, but it has thick paper and I drew a sea on the first page just to break it in. Mom would say that's irresponsible. She's right. I'm drawing anyway.
Money check: R$ 180 until the 30th. RU rice, bolacha da mãe, and a very creative interpretation of 'breakfast.' I'm writing this so later me can feel rich and guilty at the same time.
Limonada is four leaves tall now and I had to move her to a bigger cup. The fridge rules say no personal items in shared cups, so I stole a yogurt cup from Bia's roommate. Don't tell Bia's roommate.
The Interbairros comic has 120 followers now. Someone commented 'this parrot is real?' and I replied 'yes, Juca'. I don't know the parrot's real name. Juca is a good name.

Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He let me try the violão for ten minutes and said my fingers look 'promising and panicked,' which is the nicest review I have ever received. Vó Lúcia approved by nodding twice. I am counting the nods as data.

Money check: R$ 210 para o mês, são dia 25. Vivendo de RU e bolachas da mãe. Sim, escrevi isso de novo. Quero rir disso em 2018. Ou chorar. Depende. (Dependia mesmo. Em 2018 eu ganhava R$ 3.800, mas ainda comprava bolacha.)
A girl on the bus recognized my drawing style from the notebook and asked if I was 'the parrot artist'. I said no, then yes, then no again. Identity is a process.

Vó Lúcia called on Sunday and asked if I've 'found a nice boy in engineering'. I said 'I found calculus, Vó'. She laughed and then told me about a boy on the farm who broke his arm falling from the jabuticabeira in 1958. I wrote it down. Another one for the book I haven't started.
Dreamed of the sea again. Same dream, same warm water, same stuck feet. But today there was a small dog on the sand, looking at me, like he was waiting for permission.

Money check: R$ 290 left, it's the 28th, and the RU is closed for a holiday I didn't know about. Lived on bolachas da Mom and the free coffee at the study room. I'm writing this so in five years I can remember being hungry and not dying from it. Also, the lemon sprout has three leaves now.
Last night I drew the bus parrot on a napkin at the lanchonete and the waiter asked how much. I said it wasn't for sale. He looked disappointed. I didn't know what to do with that feeling.
Labor Day. Everyone went to the park. I stayed home and studied calculus with Limonada. She is not a good study buddy, but she doesn't judge me.

Hoje postei o primeiro desenho do ônibus. Apenas o homem do papagaio, de costas, com a mão levantada cumprimentando o motorista. Trinta pessoas viram. Uma delas foi minha mãe, que não comentou. Isso é um comentário.

Passei em Cálculo 1, finalmente. And something new: I started drawing little comics about the bus line Interbairros and posting them. 300 people follow them now. Strangers recognize the old man with the parrot from the 7am bus. I don't know what this is but it feels more like me than anything in the course. Future me, did you keep the comics going? Please don't have deleted the account in a bad mood.
Passei em Cálculo. I stared at the screen for ten minutes. Then I called Mom and cried. She said 'of course you did' like it was obvious. I think that's the nicest thing she's said about engineering.

Interbairros #1 posted. The parrot says 'bom dia, motorista' and I signed it with a tiny lemon because I couldn't think of anything else. 40 likes in an hour. Bia sent me a voice note screaming. I'm pretending to study.
The bus comics started last week and now 300 strangers know Seu Ivo and the parrot. I don't even know his real name. I'm sorry, Ivo. But Juca says hi.

Passei em Cálculo 1, finalmente, and I didn't even cry in the RU this time. I cried on the bus instead, which is more poetic and less embarrassing. The parrot man said 'parabéns, menina' and I almost dropped my notebook.
Falhei em nenhuma prova hoje e isso me deixou suspeita. Fiz um desenho de comemoração do sol de óculos escuros. Ele ficou bom. Talvez eu não seja uma fraude completa.
Passed Cálculo. I'm still suspicious. The exam felt too possible. I'm writing this down so future me knows I was scared even in the good moment.
Bus comics posted. 42 followers, mostly bots and Bia. Still counts. A woman commented that Seu Ivo looks like her father and I have been thinking about that all day. The internet is strange and soft.

Bia, você me perguntou se eu ia continuar desenhando os outros passageiros. Sim. Hoje desenhei a senhora do cachecol azul e o menino que sempre senta na última poltrona com fone de ouvido grande. Ele me viu desenhando e fez sinal de positivo. Pequena alegria de ônibus.

Tio Beto, I played 'Asa Branca' this morning on your violão, which still lives at Mom's house, and I got through the first verse without stopping. Second verse is where I fall apart. Your promise was Festa Junina but I'm starting early. If you're reading this in three years, yes, I'm still working on it. You said one more year. I'm counting.

Passei em Cálculo 1. I called Mom first and she said 'parabéns, now don't fail the others.' I called Bia second and she screamed in a supermarket. I called Rafa third and he said 'I told you so,' which is annoying but correct.
Posted the first Interbairros strip. Thirty likes. Three were from me, accidentally. Still counts.
Seu Ivo was back on the bus today. The parrot said 'bom dia' and then something that sounded like 'Curitiba'. I don't know if parrots can say city names. I choose to believe Juca can.
Vó Lúcia called to say she saw my comic on Mom's computer. She laughed at Seu Ivo and said 'he walks like your grandfather'. I didn't know whether to be offended for Vó or proud of the drawing.
Rafa and I walked in Passeio Público and he asked what I'd do if I weren't in engineering. I said 'draw all day'. He laughed like it was a joke. I didn't correct him. Cowardice, but cute.
Started drawing little strips about the Interbairros II bus and posted them online. 300 people follow now. That's more people than came to my birthday. I'm not sad about that, I'm just counting.
Bia, you were the first person I texted. Not Mom, not Rafa. You said 'te disse'. You did tell me. I just took the long way around.
Bia, the wall in São Francisco is still there. Our names survived one rainy season. I checked. We were there, and we are still there.

Started drawing on the bus again, little strips of the people in my line. The woman with the bag of tangerines, the kid with the light-up shoes, the man who always sleeps through his stop. Seu Ivo (that's what I call the parrot man in my head, I don't know his real name) is the star. I haven't shown anyone. It's just for me, for now.

Bia, your birthday is tomorrow and I bought you a mug with a sea on it from a second-hand shop near the bus station. It cost R$ 8 and the handle is slightly chipped. I also drew you a card with the bar wall in São Francisco on it. If they painted over our names, the card is the new wall.
Seu Ivo wasn't on the bus today. Juca wasn't either. I drew the empty seat and it looked sadder than a person, which proves I'm attached to a parrot I don't own.

Festa junina do bairro da república. Comi canjica até enjoar e dancei quadrilha com uma menina que eu não conhecia e não vou mais ver. Ela disse que eu dançava 'desengonçada mas com vontade'. Quero que seja meu epitáfio.
The bus comics have a name now: Interbairros. I wrote it on the first page with a thick marker. It looks official. I am terrified.
Rafa made dinner at his place: instant noodles with hot dogs, very romantic. We ate on the couch and talked about São Paulo again. I talked about the sea again. We are two people circling airports.

Tio Beto, I practiced 'Asa Branca' twice this week and forgot the second verse again. You were right, everyone promises this. But I'm closer than last year. I think the F string is mocking me personally.

Rua XV república dinner. We made arroz com feijão and someone put hot sauce on everything again. Four girls, one bathroom, still the best thing that ever happened to me. I drew us around the table after.
Money check: R$ 210 until the 30th. I am surviving on coffee, RU, and the free granola at the faculty coffee machine. The granola has no taste but it has ambition.
Started drawing little bus comics last week. 40 followers, mostly bots probably. Still, 40 people looked at something I made. I put Limonada on the windowsill and she looked at me like 'keep going'.

Tentei nadar de novo. Sem ninguém ver, na piscina do clube, às 6 da manhã. Cheguei a quinze metros antes de engolir água e voltar. O vigia do clube me perguntou se eu estava bem. Respondi que estava 'praticando'. Ele disse 'pratique mais devagar'. Bom conselho para tudo.

Sunday cooking attempt: I tried Vó Lúcia's bolo de fubá using her recipe by phone. She said 'the secret is stirring with a wooden spoon, never metal'. I used metal. It's dense and wrong and Rafa ate two slices without complaint, which means either he loves me or he has no taste.
The parrot man wasn't on the bus today and I panicked for three stops. He returned with a bandage and the parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically. I'm counting that as a friendship.

Passed Cálculo 1. I know I wrote something about crying in the RU last year. Today I laughed so hard I scared the man next to me. Rafa bought a pastel and I ate two. Engineering continues. Drawing continues. Nothing exploded.
Money check: R$ 260 left, and I bought a new sketchbook instead of groceries. Mom would say 'you can't eat graphite'. She's right, but the sketchbook is pretty.

Limonada is now in a bigger yogurt cup, taped again. Four leaves. She's growing faster than me in calculus. I brought her to the study group last week and my friend Carol asked if I named my plant. I said yes. She didn't ask more, which is how I know Carol is a good person.

Bus comics have a name now: Interbairros. I invented an old man named Seu Ivo and a parrot named Juca. The real man is still alive and hopefully not on Instagram. I hope he never finds out I gave him a name.

Desenhei o cobrador do 7am. Ele tem uma careca brilhante e um anel de formatura que não combina com nada. Postei e alguém comentou 'esse é o cobrador do meu ônibus'. É isso. É essa sensação. É isso que quero guardar.
Bus 7am. The parrot man brought a small radio today and the parrot sat on it, silent, like a very committed DJ. I drew them with musical notes and the parrot said 'bom dia' on the second stop.

Limonada moved from the yogurt cup to a bigger container. She has five leaves now and the kind of confidence I lack. I watered her while listening to Rafa's playlist. This is a good life, small and green.
Limonada has six leaves now and no business being this confident. I talk to her while I brush my teeth. She has not responded. Respect.

Passed Cálculo 1, already written somewhere. But I want to remember the feeling: I stood in the hallway after seeing the grade and cried for three minutes, not sad, just full. Then I went to the study room and drew a tiny person holding a flag that says 'PASSEI'. Pinned it to the wall. The guard took it down. I'm keeping the drawing.

Festa Junina at Tio Beto's is in two weeks. I practiced 'Asa Branca' three times this week. Tio Beto said 'one more year' last year; I want to arrive and play the whole thing and say nothing. Just play it. We'll see.
Money check: R$ 90 left and it's the 8th. I ate RU three days in a row and my stomach has opinions. The good news: Limonada has six leaves and no financial worries.
Tio Beto, I almost played Asa Branca today but my fingers betrayed me at the second verse again. I will not tell you this in person.
Limonada has two tiny leaves now and lives on the windowsill next to my sketchbook. The sketchbook no longer hides under the mattress. Progress looks small from the outside.

Sunday at Vó Lúcia's. She taught me how to fold an envelope out of notebook paper because she said letters feel more real. I folded twelve for the girls in the república. Vó said I have 'hands like a girl who draws too much.' I chose to take it as a compliment.

Tio Beto, toquei 'Asa Branca' até o segundo verso de novo. Parece que a música tem um muro ali. Do lado de cá está fácil, do lado de lá eu travo. Ainda assim, toquei mais rápido que no ano passado. Prometo que em 2017 chego até o terceiro verso. Pequeno milagre por ano.

Interbairros now has 500 followers. A stranger sent me a message saying Seu Ivo looks like their grandfather. I don't know what to do with that except draw him again, better this time. Juca got a bow tie in the new strip. It's too much. I kept it.

Comics now have names: the woman with tangerines is Dona Tereza, the sleeping man is Seu Waldir. I don't know their real names. Inventing them makes them mine, a little. I'm posting them in a Facebook album called 'Interbairros' because the bus line name sounds like a title. 47 likes. One is from a stranger. That's new.
Bia, thank you for sitting with me through the calculus exam review even though you understood it before I started crying. You drew a tiny parrot on my paper. I kept it.

Interbairros got 100 followers. Seu Ivo e o Papagaio are now friends in my notebook, even though I have never spoken to either of them. The parrot said 'tchau, tchau' today and I almost cried at 7am in public. Maintaining dignity.
Played 'Asa Branca' on Tio Beto's violão at lunch until the chorus. He clapped and said 'progress'. I said 'panicking'. Both true.
Rain again. The Interbairros bus fogged up completely and for ten minutes we were just silhouettes. I drew it from memory afterward, badly, and loved it anyway.
The bus driver on Interbairros II now says 'bom dia, desenhista' when I get on. I don't know if that's affection or a warning to draw faster.

Bia, you fell asleep on my shoulder during Física 2 and snored loudly enough for the professor to pause. I drew your sleeping face in the margin. You looked so peaceful I almost forgave you for the snoring.
Practicing Asa Branca before Festa Junina. I get to the second verse and my fingers forget where they live. Tio Beto says patience. I say fingers are liars.
Rain again. Curitiba in June is just water with a city in it. I stayed home and drew Limonada from three angles. She's four leaves now and leans toward the window like she's trying to escape. Fair.
Rafa and I walked to the Passeio Público after dinner. He said São Paulo has better parks. I said Curitiba has Seu Ivo and Juca. He didn't have an answer for that.
Rain on the bus windows makes the city look like an aquário. Drew it. The old lady beside me asked if I was an artist. I said 'no, I'm in engineering.' She said 'same thing, then.' She may be right.
Mom, I drew you a birthday card this year. You said 'you still do that?' and put it on the fridge between a shopping list and Vó's recipe. I'm counting it as permanent.
Ate a pastel de palmito at the feira with Rafa and we argued about whether São Paulo counts as 'the sea, but made of buildings'. He said yes. I said absolutely not. We are still dating.

Limonada tem seis folhas e um caule que parece uma palitinho de dente. As meninas da república colocaram uma fitinha amarela no vasinho. Disse a elas que a planta não precisa de fita, mas deixei. Às vezes até planta precisa de afeto.

Bia, you're in Floripa visiting your aunt and I miss you already. Rafa made me watch a movie about football tonight and I fell asleep on his shoulder, which is either sweet or boring, both. The lemon has five leaves. I'm counting for both of us.
Limonada has four leaves now and a new leaf that looks like it's reaching for the ceiling. I moved her two centimeters closer to the window. She'll decide when she's done growing.

Limonada got her first real leaf besides the seed leaves. I took a photo and sent it to everyone. Rafa asked if it was a weed. Bia asked if it needed water. Mom asked if I was still studying. Typical.
Heat in Curitiba. Limonada got direct afternoon sun and looked personally offended. I moved her two centimeters. She forgave me.

The bus comics have a name now: 'Interbairros'. The most popular character is 'Seu Ivo e o Papagaio', based on the parrot man (I don't know his real name, I invented Ivo). People ask what the parrot's name is. I said Juca.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's tomorrow. I'm not playing Asa Branca yet. I am bringing a strip of Interbairros to show him, because Seu Ivo reminds me of his neighbor Antônio and I want to see his face.
The sea dream again. Same edge, same warm water. But this time my feet moved a little, like I was standing on sand that shifted. I woke up and the floor was cold. Still counting that as progress.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I played until the second verse and then panic. He clapped anyway and said 'one more year.' One more year. It's becoming a tradition, the failure and the applause.

Sonhei com o mar de novo. Mesmo sonho. No entanto, desta vez meu pé direito tocou a água. Fiquei paralisada. Acordou e meu tornozelo estava úmido de suor. Acho que o cérebro está tentando. Ou as pernas estão reclamando. Ambos, provavelmente.

Sunday lunch at Mom's. She made feijoada and asked if I'm 'still doing that drawing thing'. I said no. I lied again, but this time I drew on the napkin while she was in the kitchen. It's a drawing of her hands serving feijoada. I kept the napkin. It's in my sketchbook now, which is in my bag now, not under the mattress. That's progress.

Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I tried 'Asa Branca' and forgot the middle, again. Tio Beto said 'one more year' with zero hesitation, like a man who has been waiting for this joke his whole life. I am the joke. I am also still trying.
Winter in Curitiba is personal. My fingers go numb on the bus and I can't draw. I held the pen in my fist like a child and produced one decent leaf. Small victories.
Curitiba winter and my lemon tree looks offended by the wind. I brought her inside wrapped in my scarf. She has eight leaves and a lot of attitude.

Festa Junina: I played until the second verse and forgot everything, exactly like last year. Tio Beto clapped anyway. But this time I laughed instead of being embarrassed, which feels like a small victory. The milho was better than the music.
Drew the república kitchen at 2am because the light from the streetlamp was perfect. One roommate found me and asked if I was okay. I said I was drawing. She said 'ah, normal then'.
Tio Beto saw the strip and said 'is that the parrot man?' Then he said 'draw me as a cowboy'. I drew him with a hat. He taped it to the fridge next to a photo of Vó.

Swimming lesson? No. Still can't float. Bia tried again at the pool and I lasted six seconds this time, which is technically progress. A toddler next to us floated effortlessly, eating a banana. I resent that child deeply.

Ônibus 7am. Seu Ivo (nome inventado, ainda) não estava. Perguntei ao motorista, com discrição, se ele tinha faltado. Motorista disse 'quem?'. Respirei fundo. Resolvi que vou descobrir o nome dele de verdade ou inventar um melhor. Talvez os dois.

Festa Junina at Tio Beto's was smaller this year. Rafa came and danced badly, which I love. I played 'Asa Branca' until the second verse, same as last time. Tio Beto clapped and said 'one more year'. I said I want it to be next year, not one more year. He said 'we'll see'. I hate 'we'll see'.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's, no Asa Branca this year, but I brought a drawing of Vó Lúcia and Coronel for him. He put it on the fridge with a magnet shaped like a star. That counts as a stage.

Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was on the bus, but the bus drove into the water and nobody panicked. Seu Ivo's parrot opened the door. I woke up wanting pastel. Dreams are unreliable but occasionally excellent.
Mom asked if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. Again. I said yes. Again. The sketchbook is under the mattress again. We are in a loop, all three of us.

Rafa wants to go to São Paulo for a weekend. I said yes. He planned the whole thing around architecture and museums. I planned the whole thing around the one ocean I can see from a hill. We'll compromise like always: I'll look at buildings while thinking about water.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's was loud and perfect. I ate three pés-de-moleque and promised to learn violão next year. He smiled like he has heard this before. Because he has.
Interbairros has a name now. The most popular character is Seu Ivo e o Papagaio. People ask the parrot's name. I said Juca. I hope nobody writes to fact-check me.
Dreamed of the sea, but this time I was drawing it instead of trying to enter. That's new. My feet still didn't move, but my hands did. I woke up and sketched the wave before coffee.
At the pool with Rafa's family. I stayed in the shallow end and pretended I was 'warming up'. A child asked me why I wasn't swimming. I said I was conserving energy. He didn't buy it.

Rafa assistiu a abertura das Olimpíadas comigo na TV da república. Ele narrou os atletas como se fossem colegas de trabalho: 'esse aí tem postura', 'esse aí não vai aguentar'. Ri até doer a barriga. Gosto de rir com ele. Gosto mais quando ele não percebe que me fez rir.

My laptop is making a noise like a small animal. I have three drawings open and no backup. This is the part where 18-year-old me would have panicked. 20-year-old me is saving everything to a flash drive named 'MARINA'S LIFE' and going to bed.

Dreamed of the sea. Feet stuck again. But this time the water touched my toes and it was warm. I woke up and it was raining. The lemon plant had a new leaf overnight, which makes no sense, but I'm choosing to believe it's connected.
Rafa visited the república and said the room smells like old wood and pastel. Accurate. He brought a São Paulo magnet and I put it on the fridge next to 'MARINA' yogurt cups. Cultural exchange.

Rafa and I watched the Olympics closing ceremony at his parents' house. His mom asked when we're getting married. He said 'when she agrees to São Paulo.' Everyone laughed. I didn't. I ate two brigadeiros instead.
Limonada is growing too fast for her cup. I moved her to a real pot I found near the trash, cleaned it with soap and guilt. She has seven leaves and attitude.
Money check: R$ 280 left and it's not even the 30th. RU and bolachas again, but at least now I have a plant to look at while eating dry crackers. Limonada judges silently. She is right.
Drew the old man and the parrot on the margin of my thermodynamics notes. My classmate said 'you should post these'. I said 'I don't have a platform'. I do have a phone and zero courage.

Therapy? No. I'm not in therapy yet. I'm just sitting on the bus thinking too much. The man next to me is asleep and his parrot is asleep too, head tucked under wing. It's the most peaceful thing I've seen all week.

Fiz um desenho do treino de natação noturno, só silhuetas e água preta. Postei sem texto. Recebeu menos likes que os desenhos de ônibus, mas uma pessoa comentou 'parece que o mar quer entrar na piscina'. Gosto dessa pessoa, mesmo sem saber quem é.
Rafa talked about São Paulo for forty minutes today, the jobs, the buildings, the noise. I talked about the sea. We held hands and pretended we weren't speaking different languages.
Bia, we tried to make bolo de fubá at the república using Vó Lúcia's recipe over the phone. It came out flat and sad. We ate it anyway and called it 'bolo de fubá de esforço'.
Rain all weekend. I drew interiors: the bathroom line, the fridge, Limonada with rain on the window behind her. The comics page got 300 followers. I don't know what I'm doing but I keep doing it.
Rainy Sunday. Cleaned the república kitchen and found three mugs with no owner, one spoon in the fridge, and a drawing of Limonada on the table signed by 'someone.' I kept it.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was drawing the waves instead of entering them. The pencil kept turning into a fish. I woke up laughing, which is new.

Rafa and I watched the Olympics opening with his cousins. His mom asked about marriage and he said 'when she agrees to São Paulo' and laughed. I laughed too because what else do you do. Drew the Olympic rings with a sun wearing sunglasses inside one of them.
Vó Lúcia told me a long story about a dog on the farm and I forgot to write it down immediately. Now I remember the dog's name was Coronel and the rest is fog. I'm angry at my brain.
Bus comics at 200 followers now. Someone commented 'this is my bus stop' under a panel of the 7am. I don't know them but I feel like we've met.

Passei a tarde na papelaria comprando canetas finas. Gastei R$ 47 que não tinha. As canetas são pretas, vermelhas e uma verde. A verde é para Limonada, para desenhar o caule quando crescer. É um investimento absurdo e necessário.

Olympics starting and Rafa's mom invited us to watch the opening ceremony. Everyone's excited about Brazil. I'm excited about the drawing of the cauldron I did in the margin of my notebook, which nobody asked about but I'm proud of. The bus comics have 120 followers now. Seu Ivo e o Papagaio is the favorite.

Mom asked why I'm not 'serious about engineering' and I said I am serious, I just draw on the side. She said 'your grandfather was serious about everything and he still died'. I didn't have an answer for that. I think she meant it as love.

Olympics opening ceremony on the TV in the república. We all watched and someone said 'one day we'll see Curitiba in this'. I drew a tiny Olympic torch as a bus handle. Nobody laughed, which means it worked.
Vó Lúcia sent me a photo of her garden. There is a jabuticabeira in it. She didn't plant it, she said. It just grew. I think that's how good stories work too.
Olympics soon. I'm not athletic, but I do root for whoever looks the most tired. Solidarity is a sport.
Money check: R$ 260 left and it's the 9th. The 'MAR' savings idea doesn't exist yet, but I'm starting a jar called 'pastel money.' It currently contains two reais and a button.

Bia, você fez 20 anos e eu fiquei emocionada. Fomos ao bar de São Francisco, bebemos uma cerveja ruim e rimos. Escrevi 'M+B 2016' na parede do banheiro feminino com caneta, não marker. Pequena rebelião. A parede já tinha outros nomes. Sinto que estamos numa cadeia de desconhecidos.

Olympics closing ceremony at Rafa's parents' house. His mom asked when we're getting married. He said 'when she agrees to São Paulo'. Everyone laughed. I didn't. Not because I'm angry, because I don't know the answer and that scares me more than marriage. I drew the moment later: Rafa smiling, me looking at the TV. It's uncomfortable to look at.

Sunday lunch at Vó Lúcia's. She told the Coronel story again, only this time the dog waited at the gate in the rain. I wrote down the new detail. She said I was 'fixando bobeira no papel', but she smiled.
Went to the Passeio Público with Rafa and drew the ducks while he talked about traffic in São Paulo. The ducks were more interesting. I didn't say that out loud.
Bia, you said my hair looks like a lemon tree in the wind. Rude. Accurate. I'm keeping it.
Olympics on TV at the república. We all screamed at one volleyball point and knocked Limonada off the windowsill. She lost one leaf and my heart. I put her back. She forgave me.
Bia and I went to Matinhos for the weekend. I stood with my feet in the water at midnight and didn't panic. Bia said 'that's progress' and I said 'don't make it a thing'. It's a thing.

Bia, happy 20th, late by two days because I forgot. I drew you on the bus with headphones and a very angry face, which is your resting face, but also beautiful. You can have the original if you don't frame it badly.
Bia, feliz aniversário. You're twenty and still the first person I text. I drew you a small sea with no people in it because you hate crowds. Hope you like it.

Seu Ivo was missing for three days. The bus felt wrong, like a room with a picture taken down. Today he came back with a bandage on his hand. The parrot said 'bom dia' to the whole bus. I counted it as a personal victory anyway.

Chuva forte hoje. O ônibus atrasou e todo mundo estava molhado. O papagaio estava quieto dentro da capa que o velho colocou. Desenhei a capa. Parecia uma nuvem com asas. Quando postei, alguém perguntou se era 'poesia visual'. Eu respondi 'é chuva'. Gostei de mim por não explicar mais.
Rafa and I watched the Olympics closing ceremony at his parents' house. His mom asked when we're getting married. He said 'when she agrees to São Paulo'. Everyone laughed. I didn't.
Bus 7am. Seu Ivo (the man with the parrot) had a bandage on his hand again. The parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically for the second time. I'm counting this as friendship, not delusion.
Limonada has five leaves now and one new tiny one that looks like a hand. Camila says it looks like a lemon. I say it looks like possibility. We're both wrong, probably. It's a leaf.
Mom hasn't seen the comics yet. I'm nervous in the specific way you're nervous before a test, except the test is your mother's face.

Limonada now lives on the kitchen windowsill because the bedroom window gets too much sun in the afternoon. She has six leaves and I'm considering buying her a real pot, which feels like adulthood. The Interbairros page has 200 followers. Someone made a meme of Seu Ivo. I don't know how to feel about that.
Money check: R$ 390 left, it's the 28th, and I bought a sketchbook instead of a calculator. I have a calculator on my phone. Priorities.
Rafa wants to visit São Paulo over the weekend and keeps talking about jobs there. I keep talking about the lemon tree. We are two people having different conversations in the same café.
Mom, the comics page has 300 followers now. You asked if they pay. No. But a stranger said Seu Ivo looks like her grandfather, so I think that counts as payment.
Rafa made me try swimming at the university pool. I panicked at three seconds. A kid did a perfect somersault next to me. I wanted to disappear into the tiles.

Rafa talked about São Paulo again today: jobs, buildings, noise, like it's a person he's in love with. I talked about the lemon tree. We both pretended not to notice. Again. It's becoming our choreography.

Bia visited the república and approved the room, which smells less like old wood now and more like instant noodles. She tried to teach me to float in the bathtub. Water everywhere. Limonada survived. Barely.

Ganhei uma prova de Cálculo II por 0,3 ponto. Não comemorei, chorei. A colega ao lado me ofereceu uma balinha de menta. Aceitei. A balinha tinha gosto de hospital, mas era um gesto. Vou lembrar mais do gesto do que da nota.
Calc 2 exam next week. I studied four hours and then drew for two. The drawing is better than the studying. I'm not sure which one counts as productive. I'm choosing the drawing.
Seu Ivo (I still don't know his name) was back on the bus after a week away. The parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically. I drew it in the margin and showed him. He nodded once. Best review.
Money check: R$ 410 left and it's the 5th. Living on RU, pastel, and the bolachas Mom sends. I'm writing this to laugh next year. Maybe.

Seu Ivo wasn't on the bus for three days and I was worried again. Today he was back with a bandage on his hand, same as last year. The parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically. I drew him with the bandage and people cried in the comments. I didn't plan the crying. It just happened.
Seu Ivo and Juca were both on the bus today. The driver missed a stop because he was listening to the parrot. Nobody complained. I drew it in two minutes.
The parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' and then, I swear, 'bom dia, menina'. I drew it before I could doubt my own ears. Memory is unreliable but mine is committed.
Money check: R$ 180 left, 5th of September. I bought a better pen with the last money. If I fail next week, at least the failure will be well drawn.
Feriado. Stayed in the república and drew a comic about the fridge with names on every yogurt. It got the most likes of any post so far. People love domestic frustration. I feel seen and embarrassed.
The bus comic character 'Seu Ivo e o Papagaio' is the most popular one. People ask what the parrot's name is. I said Juca. It felt right. Names are just decisions you make on a Tuesday morning.
Parrot update, since nobody asks but everyone should: Seu Ivo smiled at me today and said 'bom dia, menina'. The parrot also said 'bom dia'. I said 'bom dia' back to both, separately, to be fair.

Called Vó Lúcia and she told the Coronel story again, with one new detail: he used to wait at the gate even in the rain. She laughed and said dogs are more loyal than sons. I didn't argue. She's probably right.
Stranger on the bus recognized Juca from the comic and made parrot noises. The real Juca was unimpressed. I was the happiest person on the Interbairros II.
Mom asked if I still draw. I said 'sometimes.' Another lie, but softer this time, like a pillow. Sketchbook is on the desk now, not under the mattress. Progress is a shelf I keep moving higher.

Someone at the university asked if 'Interbairros' was really about our bus. I said yes. They said 'Seu Ivo is my uncle'. I couldn't tell if they were joking. I hope they were joking. I hope they weren't.

Fui à casa da Vó Lúcia no domingo. Ela me mostrou um álbum de fotos antigas e apontou para uma foto do Coronel. 'Este cachorro', disse, 'era mais inteligente que meu marido'. Riu como se contasse piada, mas não era piada. Desenhei o cachorro no caderno, com a cabeça erguida.
Limonada grew three new leaves after the frost. I cheered in my room and the girls asked if I won the lottery. In a way, yes.

Money check: R$ 340 left, it's the 18th, and I'm writing this because I wrote the same thing in 2014 and I want to compare. In 2014 I had R$ 340 on the 28th. I'm ten days earlier now. Either inflation or me being worse. I'm laughing. The lemon has a seventh leaf.
Cálculo is still hard but less impossible. I drew a tiny celebration in the margin. My professor saw it and asked if it was a diagram. I said yes.
Money check: R$ 120 and a coupon for two pastéis. This is not a crisis, this is a personality.
Rafa and I watched the Olympics closing ceremony at his parents' house. His mom asked about marriage. He said 'when she agrees to São Paulo'. Everyone laughed. I didn't. I just held my caldo de cana.
RU lunch: rice, beans, chicken, and a sadness of salad. I sat with two classmates and we talked about São Paulo jobs. I stayed quiet about the sea. Some days I don't want to be the sea girl.
Mãe, I saw your message about the fridge needing cleaning. I cleaned it. I also drew a tiny comic of you as a superhero with a sponge. You haven't seen it. I'm afraid of your reaction.

Interbairros has a name now. I am calling the parrot Juca because it sounds like a small angry man. 300 people follow it, 290 probably regret it. Strangers recognize Seu Ivo from the bus. He does not know he is famous.
Limonada has a tiny new leaf at the top, pointing straight up like she's trying to reach the ceiling. I put her closer to the window. She is ambitious and I respect it.

Ônibus 7am. O motorista freiou bruscamente e todos os passageiros inclinaram-se para frente como um grande coral. Só o papagaio não se moveu. 'Juca' (nome inventado para o papagaio) continuou pendurado no ombro. Equilíbrio de acrobata. Quero ser assim quando crescer.
The parrot said 'bom dia' to a baby on the bus today. The baby did not say it back. Hard audience.
Mom, I know you'll say this is too much, but I drew you into the bus comic today. You're the lady with the shopping bag and the hat. You look good. Don't say I didn't warn you.
Limonada's leaves are yellowing at the tips. I googled 'lemon tree sadness' and found ten forums. Everybody is confused. I feel less alone.

Two years ago today I wrote a money check and cried or laughed about it. Today I'm at R$ 120 on the 28th. I laughed. I'm better at money than 2014-me but still not good. The comics have 280 followers and someone asked if I take commissions. I don't know what that means yet.

The lemon tree has five leaves now and one tiny branch that looks like it's trying very hard. I talk to it while making coffee. The girls think I'm strange. I think they're right, but Limonada responds by growing.
Money check, late September edition: R$ 94 and seven days left. I have become dangerously good at making instant noodles feel like a meal.
Limonada moved to a slightly bigger yogurt cup. She now has six leaves and the attitude of a plant who knows she's the favorite child.

Seu Ivo asked me what I was drawing on the bus today. I showed him. He looked at the strip of himself and the parrot and said 'I'm more handsome than that'. The parrot said 'bom dia'. I laughed so hard I missed my stop. This is the best thing that's happened this week.

Interbairros has a name now. I wrote it at the top of the page like it was always there. The most popular strip is Seu Ivo and the parrot, which proves people love a man with a bird more than a woman with homework.
Drew a strip about the parrot saying 'bom dia, motorista' and someone commented 'this is my grandfather.' I panicked and checked. It wasn't. But for three minutes I was part of a family.

Vó Lúcia told me the Coronel story again, but this time added that the dog used to sleep under her window and breathe so loudly it sounded like a second person in the room. I want to draw that breathing. I have no idea how.

Mom saw the Interbairros page and didn't say anything for two days. Today she sent a screenshot of Seu Ivo with 'this old man looks like your grandfather'. I saved the message. It's the closest thing to a compliment about drawing I've had from her.

Interbairros #30. Juca the parrot now has a tiny hat and a catchphrase: 'não falo com estranhos'. 1,200 followers. A classmate saw me drawing in the margin and said 'that's actually good'. I said 'thanks' and then thought about it for three days.

Rafa e eu vimos o jogo do Brasil numa televisão pequena no bar. Ele gritou tanto que o garçom trouxe água sem pedir. Eu desenhei o garçom de costas, servindo, sem saber que era a imagem mais bonita da noite. Às vezes é o que não participa que merece ser guardado.
Preparing a new strip about the RU line. Everyone in line looks like they're waiting for a bus to another life. Maybe that's just Monday.
I posted one bus drawing on Instagram. 12 likes. One was from a stranger. I stared at the notification like it was a marriage proposal.
Bia's birthday dinner. We didn't write on any wall this time, just ate cake and she told me to keep drawing. She says it like a doctor giving medicine. I'm taking it.
Pasta night in the república. We argued about whether water boils faster with the lid on. I drew the argument. Nobody agreed on pasta, but everyone agreed on the drawing. Progress.
Limonada is still only three leaves but she stands straighter now. I rotated the cup so she gets better light. She looks like she's posing for a portrait.
Bia, I drew you as a character in a bus comic today, standing at the bar in São Francisco. You look taller than in real life. Don't tell the others.
Money check: R$ 210 left until the 25th. Better than 2014. I bought a new blue pen, which is not a need, but the old one died and I need blue for the sea. This is not negotiable.

Mãe, hoje você viu a página do Interbairros e não disse nada por dois dias. Eu fiquei esperando. Agora entendi por que: você estava olhando as tirinhas. O velhinho do ônibus lembra o vovô. Eu não tinha visto isso até você dizer. Obrigada por não ter dito antes. Obrigada por ter dito agora.
Tio Beto's birthday. He played 'Asa Branca' and then handed me the violão mid-song. I froze. He took it back and said 'next year'. Again. Calendar keeps moving; I don't.
I keep drawing Vó Lúcia's stories in my head, the farm, the dog, the school gate. I haven't told her. I'm afraid if I say it out loud it becomes pressure.

Mom saw the Interbairros page. She didn't say anything for two days. Then she sent a screenshot of one strip with 'this old man looks like your grandfather.' It's the closest thing to a compliment I've ever had from her about drawing.

Rafa took me to São Paulo for the weekend. Too many buildings, too many noises, too many people walking fast. I drew the train and felt less lost. He held my hand and said 'see?' and I said 'I see a lot, that's the problem.' He laughed.

Mom saw the Interbairros page. She didn't say anything for two days. Then she sent a screenshot of one strip with 'this old man looks like your grandfather'. I'm counting it as a compliment. I'll take it to my grave.

Vó Lúcia called asking why I hadn't visited in three weeks. I said I was busy. She said 'busy drawing, I hope'. She doesn't know about the comics. I don't know how to explain them to her without sounding like I'm wasting time.
Vó Lúcia on the phone: 'menina do mar, you sound tired'. I said I'm fine. She said 'you don't call on Sundays to sound fine'. She's right. I'll call again Wednesday. She'll pretend to be annoyed.

Money check: R$ 180 e são dia 21. RU de segunda a sexta. Comi bolacha com margarina hoje e lembrei da mãe. Liguei para ela e ela disse 'compre carne, Marina'. Eu disse 'claro'. Não comprei. Mas senti que ela sabe.
Vó Lúcia asked about my drawings and I said 'just doodles'. She said 'doodles are just drawings that are ashamed of themselves'. I will never recover from that sentence.
Bia, you said 'draw what you know' and then told me to draw the university's RU omelette. So I did. It got 400 likes and one angry comment from a nutrition student. Worth it.
A girl at the faculty asked if I was 'the Interbairros girl'. I said maybe. She said her mom sends her the strips every Sunday. I had to leave before I cried in the hallway.
Tio Beto taught me two more chords. My fingers hurt and I can finally play the beginning of 'Asa Branca' without sounding like a cat on a piano. Small improvements. I will take them.
Rafa said São Paulo feels inevitable. I said the sea feels like home. We ate pastel in silence. Silence with someone is still company, I think.

I posted a strip about the parrot saying 'tchau, motorista' and people shared it 400 times. Someone commented 'I ride this bus and I know this man'. I feel like an anthropologist of my own city. I'm also tired, because making comics is work I don't get paid for, but it doesn't feel like work, which is suspicious.

Mom saw the Interbairros page. She didn't say anything for two days. Then she sent me a screenshot of one strip with the message 'this old man looks like your grandfather'. It's the closest thing to a compliment I've ever had from her about drawing.

Halloween não é nossa festa, mas as meninas da república fizeram abóbora com vela. Colocaram no corredor e assustou a vizinha, que bateu na porta com o rosto sério. Disse que não era halloween, era 'Abóbora Junina'. Acreditei. O Brasil sempre encontra jeito de improvisar.
November rain again. I worked on a new comic about Limonada: she's a tiny plant who thinks she's a tree. It's not autobiographical. Probably.
Cold morning. Bus windows fogged. I drew a little lemon tree on the glass with my finger and someone photographed it. I don't know who, but I hope they liked it.

Finados. Vó Lúcia took me to Irati and told the dog Coronel story again. This time Coronel waited nine years and ten. The numbers grow like the tree. I wrote it down in the sketchbook, not under the mattress.
Bia, we found a bar in São Francisco with live music and a terrible bathroom. We wrote our names on the wall again. This time I added a tiny parrot.
It rained during the whole bus ride and the window fogged up. I drew a fish on the glass with my finger. The man next to me drew a parrot. We didn't speak.

I passed Cálculo 2. Barely. I'm writing this in the RU so next year I remember it wasn't the end of the world. Again. Rafa bought me a pastel. Again. I think he thinks pastel fixes everything. It kind of does.
Rain in Curitiba and the bus was late. Seu Ivo held the parrot under his coat. I drew them like that: one small green eye looking out.

Dona Cida (71, from the swimming pool, still better than me) called to tell me there's a beginner class at 6am now. I said I can't wake up at 5. She said 'you'll learn'. She's right. I hate that she's right. I'm writing this so I remember she's always right about the water.

Tio Beto me mandou foto da Festa Junina do ano passado. Estou tocando violão com cara de concentração, como se resolvesse equação. Respondi que ano que vem toco inteiro. Ele mandou 'certeza'. Adoro que ele acredite. Preciso merecer.
Tio Beto, I played Asa Branca for you in my head today. I got through the second verse before my fingers forgot. Next year I'll use real fingers, I promise.

The bus was so full today that I ended up pressed against the window drawing with my elbow. Drew Seu Ivo's parrot with its beak open, mid-'bom dia.' The man beside me said 'that bird talks too much.' Everyone on the bus is a critic.

Rafa and I had our first real fight about São Paulo. Not dramatic. Just two people realizing they want different versions of far away. We ate pastel afterward and didn't resolve it. The pastel was good, at least.
11/11, 11:11. I wished for two things: learn to swim and keep drawing. Same wishes as 2014. I'm tired of making the same wishes. Next year I want new ones.
Swimming attempt number two of the year. I floated for nine seconds this time before panicking about my hair. A kid in the next lane floated the whole time. Children are unfair.
Limonada is almost as tall as the yogurt cup now. No lemons, no flowers, just stubborn leaves. Bia calls her decorative. I call her potential.
Bus broke down near the terminal. Everyone complained except Seu Ivo, who fed Juca a piece of bread and said 'motorista is resting'. I drew them in the delay. The best part of the day was the delay.

Dia da República. A república (a casa) comemorou com churrasco no quintal e uma menina tocou violão mal. Eu toquei 'Asa Branca' até o segundo verso e parei. Ninguém reclamou. Um rapaz disse 'não desista'. Não desisti, ainda não. Mas não avancei também.
Mom printed one of my comics at work. She says it's 'for the fridge'. She hasn't said she likes it. The fridge says enough.
Swimming: no. But I stood in the shallow end of the pool for five minutes without holding the wall. Dona Cida wasn't there, this was my own tiny brave thing. I counted it as a lap.

I can float now, barely, for maybe six seconds. Dona Cida says floating is about trust, not technique. I said that's very poetic for 6am. She splashed me. I love her. The lemon has eight leaves and I moved her to a real pot, the one Rafa brought from the feira. It's ugly. She deserves better. I'm keeping it.
Rain again. The bus smelled like wet coats and someone's orange. I drew the orange. It was the only bright thing in the whole drawing.

Rafa and I argued about São Paulo vs Curitiba, then made up over a pastel. We always make up over pastels. This is not a healthy pattern but it's ours. He said I'd love it there. I said I'd love the sea more. We changed the subject.

Mom saw the Interbairros page and didn't say anything for two days. Then she sent a screenshot of one strip with 'this old man looks like your grandfather.' It is the closest thing to a compliment she has given me about drawing. I zoomed in on her message for ten minutes.
The RU pastel today had no cheese. None. I wrote a complaint in my notebook like it was a legal document. The cook didn't care.
Tio Beto, I practiced 'Asa Branca' with the capo and it finally sounds less like a dying cat. Not good yet, but less dying. You would be proud and also probably laughing.

Ônibus 7am. Seu Ivo (o papagaio) disse 'bom dia, motorista' e eu desenhei isso. Hoje eu sei o nome do senhor? Ainda não. Mas sei o nome do papagaio na minha cabeça: Juca. Às vezes a mentira é carinhosa. Pergunto-me se isso conta como ficção ou afeto.
The república fridge has a new yogurt with my name on it, and Limonada has a new leaf. Good week. I'm learning that small things can be the whole news.

Rafa and I went to the cinema and he fell asleep during the second half. I drew him sleeping in the dark, on a napkin, by the light of my phone. It came out soft, the way he looks when he's not talking about São Paulo. I kept the napkin. That's two napkin drawings now. I have a napkin collection. This is who I am.
Rafa asked if I want to spend New Year in Matinhos again. I said yes before he finished the sentence. The sea is not negotiable, even in my relationships.
Money check: R$ 260 left, it's the 27th. I spent R$ 14 on a small pot for Limonada. Rafa said I'd regret it. I won't. She needed space.
Drew Vó Lúcia's story about Coronel from memory, the farm, the gate, the dog waiting. It's only one page and her hands are wrong. I'll fix them when I'm better. I will be better.
Rafa asked when I'm going to draw him. I said everyone on the bus is more interesting. He pretended to be offended and then asked for a parrot too.
Dream: sea again. But this time the water was warm and I was holding Limonada's pot. I wanted to set her down on the sand. I didn't. I woke up feeling like I'd almost done something.
December in Curitiba and my hands are cold. I keep drawing in bed until my fingers warm up. The sea is somewhere far away and still the first thing I think about.

Called Vó Lúcia on Sunday. She told me about the farm in Irati again, the jabuticabeira, Coronel buried under it. This time she added that he used to steal bread from the kitchen window. I wrote it down. Version five of Coronel. He gets braver and now he's a thief. I love him.
Sunday lunch at Vó Lúcia's. She told the Coronel story again and I wrote down every detail, including the part where the dog waited in the rain. I want to get it right one day.

Desenhei o portão da UTFPR na chuva, com pessoas correndo. A tinta da caneta borrrou e, em vez de ficar feio, ficou como se o próprio céu estivesse chorando. Guardarei como lição: erro às vezes é estilo.
Tio Beto sent a voice message playing Asa Branca and stopping at the same place I do. We're synchronized. That's family.

Limonada has seven leaves and no lemons, which feels like a metaphor I'm not ready to unpack. Bia says she is decorative. I refuse to accept this. She is a lemon tree in progress. I am also a lemon tree in progress.
300 people follow the bus drawings now, or at least that's what the number says. I don't know any of them. That feels both terrifying and like the beginning of something.
Limonada has nine leaves now and no flowers. Bia said she's 'decorative'. I told her to stop bullying my child. Bia laughed. Limonada stood there, leafy and unbothered.

Vó Lúcia sent me home with bolo de fubá and a bag of lemons from a neighbor's tree. I planted one seed, just in case Limonada needs company. Now I have two yogurt cups on the windowsill. The fridge rules are expanding.
End of the year. The sea dream is still there but the water looks warmer. I don't know if that means progress or just December. Both, maybe.
Mãe, if you're reading this: I'm drawing every week. Even when no one asks. Especially when no one asks.

Money check: first salary is still far, but R$ 600 from Mom for the dentist in 2015 is paid off. I paid her back with a drawing of her hands. She didn't ask for money, she asked for the drawing. I didn't expect that. The bus comics have 300 followers now.

Cálculo final went okay. I think. The professor smiled at me during the exam, which could mean I'm doing well or that he pities me. Either way, I left the room and drew the board full of equations like a crime scene.
Limonada has five leaves. I counted twice because I thought I was imagining it. The yogurt cup is starting to look too small for her ambitions.

One year of the lemon. Limonada now has six leaves and a small bud that might be a flower or might be nothing. I put her in a bigger cup. The yogurt cup is retired, taped to my desk with 'MARINA' still visible. I kept it. I keep everything.

Encontrei um limão caído na calçada perto da faculdade. Cheirei. Coloquei no bolso como se fosse tesouro. Em casa, coloquei ao lado de Limonada. A planta não deu fruto, mas trouxe um limão para ela. Simbólico, bizarro e um pouco triste. Guardo assim mesmo.
End of semester. I'm tired and proud and still carrying a sketchbook like contraband. Next year I want to post more comics and learn the third verse. Small goals, Marina.
Money check: R$ 400 left, it's the 14th, and I still bought a sketchbook because the old one is full. Priorities are questionable but my hands are happy. That counts for something.

Bia, it's almost New Year and I'm going to Matinhos with you again. Vó Lúcia is coming too, she said she won't travel but she will. I'm writing this so I remember: last year I stood with my feet in the water at midnight. This year I want to go a little further. Not all the way. Just a little.
I finished a sketchbook page every week this semester. Not because someone checked. Because 18-year-old me asked and I hate breaking promises to her.
Limonada survived a cold night on the windowsill. I wrapped her in my scarf. She has eight leaves and zero complaints. I wish I were that resilient and that quiet.
