Tio Beto, I played Asa Branca through the second verse today before forgetting. You said one more year. I'm counting it as progress and not cheating.

Last RU meal before break. They served 'surpresa de carne,' which was mostly surprise. I drew it as a mystery box. The cook looked at the drawing and asked if I wanted seconds. I said yes. Art has power.
End of year, the república smells like old wood and fried onion. Limonada is on the windowsill, 12 leaves, no lemons, still undefeated. If 2016 was the year of the lemon seed, I'm okay with that.
Mom, I bought you a small sketchbook for Christmas. Don't say drawing isn't a job until you've tried drawing your own kitchen. I love you.

Last bus of the year. Seu Ivo got off at the same stop as me and said 'feliz Natal, menina'. I said 'feliz Natal, Seu Ivo' and only realized afterwards that I said his name out loud for the first time. He looked surprised and pleased. Juca said nothing, which is unlike Juca.
Bia, if you're reading this at Christmas, save me a piece of bolo de fubá. I'll be late because the bus. Also, thank you for being the person who always asks 'are you drawing?'. Yes. Still yes.

Véspera de Natal na casa da Vó Lúcia. Ela me deu um desenho da minha infância, feito por mim, guardado numa caixa de sapato. Era um navio. Ela disse 'você sempre foi menina do mar'. Eu disse 'eu sei'. Ela disse 'então não esqueça'. Não esqueci. Não esquecerei.
Packed for Matinhos. Limonada stays with the girls and I left instructions like she is a baby: 'water, but not too much, talk to her if you want, she is a listener.' They said I'm insane. Accurate.

Christmas at Mom's. She made bolo de fubá, Vó Lúcia's recipe, and it was perfect, or at least we all said so. Tio Beto brought the violão and played 'Asa Branca' without being asked. I sang the first verse. Everyone went quiet. I think it was good. I think it was okay.

Christmas Eve at Tio Beto's. Mom made farofa and forgot the salt. Nobody said anything until Tio Beto added half the salt shaker and pretended it was always like that. Limonada stayed home, safe on the windowsill.
After Christmas, the república fridge is full of leftovers with no names. Anarchy. Beautiful, edible anarchy.

Matinhos. Stood with my feet in the water at midnight again because going further turned out to be harder than wanting to. But I went in to my ankles and stayed ten seconds longer than last year. Bia counted. She said 'that's progress'. I believe her. The lemon tree is on the windowsill at the república, waiting for me, eight leaves, ugly pot.
Rafa gave me a drawing tablet for Christmas. I said it was too much. He said I draw on every surface I meet, so it's practical. He's right and I hate that. Limonada approved by dropping a leaf on it.

Matinhos. Vó Lúcia fell asleep on the couch at 11 and woke up furious that she missed nothing important. I stood with my feet in the water at midnight again. Still as far as I go. The water was cold and the sky was ridiculous.

Christmas at Mom's. She made bolo de fubá and it was good this time. Nobody said anything, which is how we praise things in this family. I drew Vó Lúcia holding the cake and she said 'my nose isn't that big'. It is. I love it.

Christmas at Mom's. Vó Lúcia fell asleep at 11:30 and woke up claiming she saw a star. I believed her. We ate bolo de fubá and I drew everyone at the table. Vó's hands were the hardest part. They always are.
Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' after lunch and asked if I wanted to try. I played the first few bars and got stuck. He didn't say 'one more year' this time. He just nodded. Somehow that was harder.

Última semana do ano. Fiz uma lista de pequenas coisas: 43 desenhos de ônibus, 12 nados, 5 acordes, 1 planta viva, 0 finais de 'Asa Branca'. Não é pouco. Também não é suficiente. Mas é o que tenho. Futura eu, não despreze o que foi pequeno. Foi de verdade.
Bia and I wrote our names on a beach kiosk table with a pen. Not the bar wall this time, a kiosk table. We are expanding our graffiti empire. The waiter didn't care. I drew him anyway.

Last day of 2016. Limonada has eight leaves and a tiny crack in her pot. The Interbairros album has 310 followers. I passed Cálculo 1. Rafa is still asking about São Paulo. I still don't know. But I have a lemon plant and a drawing of a man with a parrot, and I think that's enough for now. One more year.

Last day of 2016. Limonada has five leaves, the comic has 300 followers, and I still can't swim properly. That's three things, two good. Not bad for a year. Tomorrow I go to Matinhos with everyone and I'll stand with my feet in the water again. For now. Just for now.

Last day of 2016. I am 20. I have a plant that has never produced a lemon, a bus comic with a parrot called Juca, a boyfriend who loves São Paulo, and a notebook full of drawings my mother pretended not to see. I have not learned to swim. I have not published anything. But I drew every week. Promise kept. Next year: the same, plus one more brave thing.

New Year's Eve. Writing to future me: did the lemon tree make it to 2026? Did you keep drawing, even one page a week? Did you learn to swim? I'm asking the 2014 questions again because they still feel true. I'm 20. I'm scared and I'm drawing. That's where I am. Happy new year, future me. I hope you're by the sea.

New Year's Eve at home, not Matinhos this year. Vó Lúcia fell asleep before midnight again and still swore she saw fireworks. I stood with my feet in a bucket of water because the beach was too far. It counts if I'm honest about it.

New year energy lasted exactly until the first alarm. I’m still on holiday in Matinhos but mentally already back at the bus at 7am. The sea was gray all week, which feels rude when I only get it twice a year. Drew Vó Lúcia’s hands from memory and got the second joint wrong again. She’ll correct me Sunday.

Bus was late again, Interbairros II, and I drew Seu Ivo from memory instead of waiting with my phone out. The parrot looked greener in my head than in real life. I miss the comics already, but the notebook is still here. Limonada has three new leaves and one of them is doing something weird and heroic.
First day back at the república and Limonada has three new leaves. Someone left a care label on her yogurt cup that just says 'Kiss me'. I suspect Bia.

First day back at the república after the holidays. The lemon seedling on the windowsill has three real leaves now. I moved it closer to the sun and it seems suspiciously happy. Vó Lúcia asked on Sunday if I was eating enough; I said yes. I had two pastéis and a café.

Bus 7am again. No new parrot man strip ideas today, just rain on the window. I drew the droplets instead. It looked like the sea if you squinted, which I did, because that's what I do now: see water everywhere and call it research.
Limonada has six leaves now and leans toward the window like she's trying to escape. I rotated the yogurt cup and she leaned back. Stubborn plant. Like me, I guess.
Rafa let me practice on the hill behind his building. I stalled six times and a dog watched every single one. He said 'third time's the charm' and I stalled on the third. I think I need a new hill.

Limonada grew two new leaves overnight and I checked her twice before leaving for the bus. The Interbairros was late, the parrot man said bom dia to the motorista first, and I missed my stop because I was drawing them instead of watching the street.

Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He made feijoada and played violão with food on his fingers. I still can't play past the first verse of 'Asa Branca', but I brought my sketchbook this time and drew his hands. He said 'finally you draw something useful'. Mom heard and pretended not to laugh.

Cold bus this morning, the windows fogged so fast I drew a little fish on it with my finger and a guy in a suit didn't even blink. Limonada has three new leaves. I'm counting them like a tiny victory.
Ten years from now, if you're reading this: are you still drawing? Did the bus comics become something? Did Limonada survive? Please say yes to at least two.

Interbairros Bus 7am. Seu Ivo wasn't there and the parrot silence felt louder than the engine. I drew a strip anyway, Juca alone on the seat. Maybe people only like the happy version. I'll post it later.

Limonada got a new leaf and I celebrated like she did something brave. The república fridge now has a magnet holding our names, a tiny sea drawing from Bia. She says it looks like a blue potato. She’s not wrong.
Found the yogurt cup from last year with 'MARINA' written on it. Limonada is still here. I'm still here. That's enough for today.
Pastel de queijo at the feira, the good one near the terminal, R$ 4 and worth every centavo. Rafa put ketchup on his and I pretended to be offended. I was offended.

On the bus today a teenager gave up his seat for Seu Ivo without being asked. Juca said 'obrigado' in a voice that sounded almost human. I drew it in the Álgebra notebook I still carry, even though Álgebra is long over.

The república fridge has a new rule: yogurt without a name goes to whoever asks first. I lost mine today. The lemon seedling, Limonada, got a new yogurt cup because the old one cracked. She is surviving with 3 leaves and a lot of optimism.

R$ 420 left, day 15. The math is not mathing. RU feijão with extra rice, bolacha from Mom, and a very serious discussion with the girls about whether yogurt counts as dinner. It does if you add granola and denial.
The 7am bus was late again. The driver apologized twice and nobody cared except me, because I was already late for Cálculo. I drew the people waiting in my notebook instead of studying.
Mom sent a voice message asking if I've 'decided to be normal yet'. I replied with a photo of Limonada's new leaf. She didn't reply. I'm choosing to read that as interest.
Bia, you forgot your scarf at the bar again. I have it. It smells like your perfume and beer. I'll return it next week or I'll keep it forever, no promises.
Failed the driving test. Stalled the car on the hill in front of the Detran examiner. He wrote something and didn't look at me. Second try in March.
Sunday call with Vó Lúcia. She told me the lemon tree at the farm used to flower every other year, 'como quisesse pensar'. I wrote it down because I don't want to forget that sentence.
O ônibus atrasou de novo. Desenhei o motorista e o cobrador enquanto esperava. Acho que desenhar me acalma mais que rezar.
Enrolment at Detran. I practiced hill starts in the parking lot until the instructor looked tired. My left foot refuses to cooperate. If I fail again I'm blaming the car, not me.
Mom sent bolachas in a box with 'MARINA' in huge letters. The fridge already has four names on it, so I wrote mine on the box too. Roommate Ana ate one and left a apology note shaped like a heart.
Money check: R$ 210 left until internship starts. I’m living on RU, bolachas, and spite. Bought a pastel de feira anyway because Rafa said I looked sad. He was right, which is annoying.
Limonada has five leaves now. The yogurt cup is cracking, so I'm looking for a real pot. The fridge rules still apply: everything must be labeled, even my daughter.
Failed the driving test again today? No—this is for March. The hill is still personal. In the meantime I drew the examiner’s face from memory. He looked like a motor with no vibration, just noise.

I tried to restart the bus comics tonight and stared at the blank page for forty minutes. Seu Ivo would say something funny now, but I don't know what. Missing them feels embarrassing, like missing a TV show that got cancelled.
Vó Lúcia is home from the hospital and already bossing Mom around. I called and she said, 'you don't have to worry, menina,' in the exact tone that means she knows I'm worrying. I worry.

Bia, the lemon tree now has six leaves and one of them is pointing at the wall like it's judging me. Mom sent bolo de fubá in the post and it survived the trip in one piece. Almost. We ate the crumbs with coffee.
Bia, thanks for the pastel after the driving test. I know you were late on purpose so I'd be less nervous. It didn't work, but the pastel was excellent and so are you.

PT: O ônibus Interbairros hoje veio com cheiro de bolo de milho. Ninguém assumiu. Desenhei o motorista segurando um pedaço e escondendo no painel. Seu Ivo e Juca não apareceram, então o quadrinho hoje foi só tristeza e milho.
Bus 7am, Interbairros II. Seu Ivo wasn't there but Juca was? No, just the driver in a parrot green jacket. Drew it anyway.
Rain all day. I measured vibrations at the factory in my head even while watching TV. Rafa says I smell like machine oil. He's not wrong.

Bus 7am. Seu Ivo (or whoever he is) wasn't there again. The parrot was missing too. I worried all the way to university and drew the empty shoulder space in my notebook. Sometimes absence is the whole scene.
Vó Lúcia called at 6am to say she's feeling better. She talked for forty minutes about the dog at the bakery. I was late for class and didn't mind.
Vó called at 7am to say she's better and then talked for an hour about the neighbor's dog. I wrote down the dog's name: Totó. She says he has 'olhos de gente'. I believe her.
Rafa bought me a pastel and said 'you're too smart to fail twice'. I didn't fail anything today, but I ate the pastel and felt loved in the annoying way he always manages to achieve.
Vó Lúcia's pneumonia news. I called and she said she was 'fine, just a cough', then coughed for so long I wrote my name on the steam on the window. She is home now. I'm calling Wednesdays too.
Bia, if you're reading this, thank you for laughing at my driving-test story instead of comforting me. Comfort would have made me cry. You know that. Also thank you for the pastel.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was drawing it from a boat, very professional, very calm, while a lemon fell from the sky. I think my dreams are merging into one long very stupid metaphor.

Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He made churrasco and forgot the pão de alho until the very end. I helped him play the second verse of Asa Branca again. Still can't get past it. One more year, apparently.
Bia, I still can't believe we're 21 and acting like adults. You owe me a pastel from the last time you won at cards. I'm writing it down so you can't deny it later.
Chamada com a Vó Lúcia: ela falou do Coronel de novo, e eu anotei a versão em que ele late pra afastar a chuva. Acho que ela inventa um pouco, mas eu prefiro assim. A cada semana ele fica mais herói.

Vó Lúcia got pneumonia in February, according to the later capsule, but today she called to complain that the hospital soup had no salt. She sounded stronger than my mom, who was crying in the background. I stayed on the phone for an hour while she described every doctor's tie.
Mom, I know I said drawing is just for fun now. It probably is. But I drew a motor cross-section during a meeting today and Cláudio asked to keep it, so maybe 'just for fun' is doing a lot of work.

Rafa brought me a single red flower from the vendedor at the terminal. I asked why not a whole bouquet and he said ‘because you’d complain about the vase’. Fair. Put it in the yogurt cup next to Limonada.
Valentine's at the factory cafeteria. Rafa bought me a pastel de feira after work and we ate it sitting on the curb. Very romantic, very grease stains.
Bia, today the parrot man's bandage was gone and Juca said 'bom dia, motorista' in the exact same voice. I drew him from memory later and his beak looked wrong. Tomorrow I'll try again.
Mãe, I know you think drawing is a hobby. I stopped the bus comics this month because of work, and I miss them more than I expected. That's all. Also I ate well today. Promise.
Limonada grew one new leaf this week. The girls clapped. I know it's a plant. Still, I clapped too. The windowsill is getting crowded with sketchbooks and yogurt cups.
Tio Beto, toquei 'Asa Branca' até a segunda parte e esqueci tudo. Você bateu palma do mesmo jeito. Um ano a mais.

Bus Interbairros at 7am, no parrot today. I sat in Seu Ivo's usual seat by accident and felt like an imposter. A woman with a basket of pão de queijo sat next to me and offered one without talking. I accepted. The commute was perfect for four minutes.

Bia, you stole my hoodie again and left a cookie wrapper in the pocket. I'm keeping the wrapper as evidence. Also thank you for the pastel today. If you're reading this in the future, yes, I still remember the wrapper.

Swimming lesson #? I lost count. I still swallow water when I turn my head. Dona Cida says I’m trying to win a fight with the pool. Maybe I am. The sea dreams are still there, but in the last one I got my feet wet on purpose.

I planted another seed in a new yogurt cup, just in case Limonada needs a friend. It has no name yet. The fridge already has five names on it, so this cup says 'MARINA 2'. That's not confusing at all.

PT: A república está com cheiro de mofo de chuva e eu estou feliz. Limonada gosta do úmido, eu gosto da desculpa para ficar dentro desenhando. O desenho de hoje: Seu Ivo com o papagaio e uma cadeira de rodas. Não mostrei para ninguém.

Português: Liguei pra Bia pra contar do estágio que começa em março e ela disse 'finalmente alguém vai me pagar pra medir motor'. Acho que sim. Estou tentando sentir orgulho em vez de medo. Ainda não consigo.
RU lunch: rice, beans, chicken that tasted like the plate. I sat with two civil engineering girls and we complained about calculus for forty minutes. Felt like 2014 again. Nice.
Practiced driving with Dad's car in the empty parking lot. I stalled three times. A pigeon watched me from a fence and I felt judged.
Chamada da Vó Lúcia on Sunday: she told me the story of Coronel again, but this time he had a blue collar. Wrote it down. She also said I'm too skinny and I should eat more rice.

Money check: R$ 280 until payday, internship hasn't started yet, and I spent R$ 18 on colored pencils I 'needed'. I ate RU rice with sardine three days in a row and didn't hate it. This is what growth looks like, apparently.
I packed a pastel in my bag for the bus and it leaked. My Álgebra notebook from 2014 would have been offended. Some things don't change.

Money check: R$ 210 until the end of the month. The bus pass ate most of it. I ate RU twice and once I ate instant noodles with egg, which felt both adult and sad. I am writing this so future me remembers the dignity of cheap food.

PT: Estudei para a prova de Física 2 com café e culpa. A bateria do notebook morreu no meio da lista de exercícios e eu quase chorei. Rafa me mandou áudio dizendo que eu não sou burra, só desorganizada. Eu sou os dois.
Vó Lúcia on the phone said the farm in Irati had frost and Coronel's grave under the jabuticabeira looked 'all white'. She didn't cry this time. I drew it later from memory and it wasn't enough.

First week at the factory. Cláudio showed me how to hold the vibration meter and said 'don't worry, nobody understands the first week.' I understood enough to be tired. Bought a pastel on the way home and ate it standing.
First day at the factory tomorrow. I laid out my clothes like it's a first day of school. Rafa took a photo and sent it to the group chat. Bia replied with a bus emoji. Thanks, friends.
Detran practice on the same hill that hates me. The instructor said 'relax your shoulders' and I told him my shoulders live in a state of permanent alarm. He didn't laugh.
Second driving lesson. The instructor said 'relax your shoulders' like that helps. My hands are glued to the wheel. The hill at Detran is waiting for me and I can feel it.
Driving lesson today. The instructor said 'relax your shoulders' seventeen times. I stalled once and apologized to the car. The car did not answer, which I take as forgiveness.
First week at the factory. The coffee machine makes a sound like a small dying animal. Nobody else seems to hear it. I think I'm going to like it here.

First day at the factory in CIC. The badge has my full name and I look like someone who knows about vibrations. I do, technically. The canteen has free coffee and I understand why engineers are intense now.

Cláudio showed me how to use the caliper at the factory and said ‘careful, this is the part engineers break most’. I broke it five minutes later. He laughed and gave me another one. I think I like factories more than I expected.
Internship paperwork signed. The factory smells like oil and instant coffee. I have a badge with my photo on it and I look startled, like someone woke me up. Accurate.
Rain all day, bus late, arrived at work with one wet shoe. Cláudio said engineers should be prepared for everything including weather. I said I was prepared for coffee, which I also forgot.
Internship starts next week at CIC. I bought safety shoes that are too big and a clipboard because I thought engineers carried clipboards. They don't. I kept it anyway.
Vó Lúcia perguntou se 'esse emprego de homens' não cansa. Eu disse que gosto de medir coisas. Ela riu e disse que medir é só adiar. Não entendi se foi conselho ou ironia.

International Women's Day. Mom called and asked if I was 'still doing that bus thing'. I said no. The lie was easier than explaining that I stopped because the factory took my time, not because I stopped caring.
A Limonada ganhou uma folha nova. Pequena, quase transparente. Acho que ela sabe que foi desenhada mais do que todos os motores da fábrica.

Bia, I measured vibrations in a motor today and thought of you because it was loud and pointless and someone still paid me. Are you still at that bar? Send me a photo of the wall if the paint is still there.
Dreamed of the sea again, but this time I was drawing it instead of standing at the edge. My hands were full of graphite. When I woke up, my fingers were curled like I was still holding a pencil.

Internship at a factory in CIC. I measure vibrations in motors. It's fine. The engineers are kind and I'm good at it, which is the scary part, because being good at something you don't love is a trap. I stopped the bus comics in January, there's no time. Vó Lúcia got sick in February, pneumonia, she's better now. I called every Sunday and some Wednesdays too.

Vó Lúcia is better. She scolded me for calling on a Wednesday and then talked for forty minutes about the farm dog. I didn't interrupt. I drew Coronel in the margin of my notebook again, third version this year.

Rafa got the interview in São Paulo. He didn't tell me for two days because he 'didn't want to make it a thing'. It's a thing. I'm proud of him and I'm scared and I put both feelings in the same drawer as the sketchbook.

Internship meeting with Cláudio. He speaks softly and knows every machine by sound. He asked me to check a vibration report, then looked at my notebook doodles and said 'you have steady hands'. I almost said 'thank you' like he'd given me a diploma.

PT: Limonada sobreviveu ao esquecimento de sexta. Cheguei em casa e ela estava murchinha, quase pedindo socorro. Reguei e contei como se pedisse desculpa. Ela abriu uma folhinha nova no domingo, o que achei generoso.

First week at the factory in CIC. The coffee is terrible and free, which is the correct combination. Cláudio showed me where the old motors are kept and let me sketch one during lunch. Nobody said anything. That felt like permission.
Failed the driving theory notes. Not the test, just my nerves. I made a cheat sheet for parallel parking using a lemon as a cone. Limonada judged me.

Second driving test attempt. Same hill. I stalled again. The examiner wrote something and didn't look at me. I sat in the car afterward and ate a pastel from the café across the street. It helped one percent.
I said I'd take a break from cars. I meant it. The bus is fine. Seu Ivo wasn't there today and I noticed more than I should.

Primeiro dia no estágio em CIC. Medir vibração de motor o dia inteiro. Cláudio parece um tio que sabe tudo, mas fala pouco. Vim de ônibus, e Seu Ivo me perguntou onde eu ia. Disse 'trabalhar'. Ele disse 'boa'. Gostei que fosse só isso.
Failed the driving test again. The hill. I'm taking a break from cars and from hills and from the Detran examiner's face. Limonada doesn't need driving. She is perfectly rooted.
Failed the driving test again, same hill, same examiner energy. I am convinced the hill has a grudge. Taking a break from cars before I start naming the hill.
Second driving test. Same hill. Same result. I said the hill is personal. Rafa said I should practice on a hill. I said I should move to a flat city. He laughed. I did not.

Vó Lúcia sent a voice message saying she’s proud I’m working, even if it’s vibrations and motors. She called me ‘engenheira’. I listened to it four times. I’m keeping the recording, even if it’s just her breathing between words.
Failed the driving test again. Same hill. I'm convinced the hill is personal. I'm taking a break from cars.
Tio Beto, I didn't practice Asa Branca this month. Work starts at 7 now and by the time I'm home the violão is sleeping. I'm not giving up. I'm just late, as usual, like every cousin you ever met.

The bus was late 25 minutes and I missed the first hour of vibration readings. Cláudio didn’t ask why, just said ‘seu café é aqui’. I drew him in the margin of the calibration sheet. He looked at it and said ‘I’m thinner than that’. He is not.
Vó Lúcia called to say she's better and then listed everything Mom is doing wrong in the kitchen. I wrote it down. The list is eleven items long and very precise.
Mom, I lied again. I am drawing, at lunch, in the factory break room. The engineers think it's funny. You would too, if you saw the sun with sunglasses I put on the diagram.

Portuguese: Hoje choveu o dia todo em Curitiba e eu fiquei no laboratório até as 19h medindo motor. O café era ruim, o chão molhado, e mesmo assim eu desenhei um girassol na margem do relatório. Cláudio viu e não disse nada, o que é a forma dele de dizer 'gostei'.
Domingo de feijoada at Tio Beto's. He asked if I practiced 'Asa Branca' and I said 'a little' which is a lie. He smiled like he knew. Played it himself, of course perfectly.
Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He let me play three chords and then took the violão back gently, like it was a sleeping animal. 'Asa Branca' is still in pieces inside my hands.

Rain all day in Curitiba. I walked from the bus stop without an umbrella and arrived looking like a wet cat. Rafa gave me his jacket and then complained about the smell of wet wool. He is impossible and I am keeping him.

First week measuring vibrations in motors. I understand the numbers but not why they matter yet. Cláudio said the trick is to listen before measuring. I think that's a metaphor but I'm too tired to check.
Mom, I know you think the factory is serious and drawing is cute. I'm keeping both. One pays, one doesn't, and I'm not choosing yet.
Lunch at the factory is 11:30 sharp, which means I eat rice and beans while thinking about drawing. A coworker asked why I always have a notebook. I said 'notes'. It's comics.

Rain all day. Bus was full, I stood the whole way home with Limonada's pot in my bag so she wouldn't get cold on the windowsill. A woman asked if it was a gift. I said 'it's my daughter.' She moved seats.
At the factory, a motor made a sound like a cat. I told Cláudio. He said 'every machine has a personality.' I believe him. I also drew the cat-motor during lunch.
Limonada has five leaves now and one of them is slightly yellow. I read that it means too much water. I am overmothering a lemon tree. This is my personality, apparently.
Drew a strip about the bus driver who sings 'tchau, passageiro' to nobody. Posted it to Interbairros. It got 47 likes, which is not fame, but I checked the number six times.

Vó Lúcia called on a Wednesday, which never happens. She said she was fine, then asked if I was eating. I said yes. She told me to eat rice and beans, not ‘essas coisas de estudante’. We talked about Coronel for twenty minutes. Same story, slightly braver dog.

Bia, I'm writing this to you because you asked why I'm always drawing motors at lunch. It's because they're round and honest. Also because Cláudio said I'm good at it and I don't know what to do with that compliment.
Limonada moved to a bigger yogurt cup because the roots were escaping. Bia says she's 'ambitious'. I am choosing not to take it personally.
Ate lunch at the RU and spilled feijão on my drawing of a motor. Now it looks like an accident report. Maybe that's more honest.
Sunday call. Vó Lúcia asked if I'm eating. I said yes. She asked what. I said rice and beans. She said 'that's not food, that's survival.' She's not wrong.
Rafa sent me a playlist for studying. It has three songs about São Paulo and one about the sea. I listened to the sea one six times.
I opened a capsule one year early by accident and it was about a yogurt cup. I'm going to pretend I didn't. Opens should stay mysterious.

Mom, if you're reading this later, yes, I still draw. No, it's not a job yet. But today the internship supervisor asked me to make a quick diagram by hand because the CAD was slow, and I didn't hate it. That's all. Don't make a big deal.
Mom sent a package with bolachas and a note that said only 'eat more.' I ate four in five minutes. The drawings under the mattress are still there; I just don't call them that in front of anyone.

Vó Lúcia called on a Wednesday just to say the jabuticabeira is blooming again. She said it in that voice she uses when she's pretending not to be sentimental. I drew a branch in the margin of my vibration report.
PT: Paguei a conta de luz com R$ 4,80 a mais do que eu tinha e tive que pedir emprestado para a Bia. Ela não fez piada, só transferiu e disse ‘quando tiver’. Isso me deixou pior do que a piada.
Bia, Rafa got the offer in São Paulo. He told me after dinner and then asked if I wanted dessert. I said no. He still ordered two. I ate half. We are not talking about the part where I didn't follow.
Rain all week in Curitiba. The república kitchen leaks in the same spot every year. We put a yogurt bucket under it. The fridge rules continue to make sense only to us.
Choveu forte e o teto da república pingou no meu quarto. Coloquei pote embaixo e desenhei o gotejar. Ficou bonito, desgraça.

Drew the factory floor during lunch, just the machines and the light. A coworker said it looked 'sad', and I said 'industrial'. We were both right. I like being the person who draws the place everyone works.
Dreamed about the sea again, but this time I was wearing steel-toed boots. The water didn't mind. I woke up and laughed, which is new.

Sunday call with Vó Lúcia. She told me the same Coronel story again, but this time the dog walked her to school in the rain and 'knew every puddle'. I wrote it down. The versions are getting better, like a myth improving with age.
Money check: R$ 580 left on the 28th. Better than 2014, still not great. Living on RU and the bolachas Mom sends, plus one emergency pastel.
Vó Lúcia got better. She told me the pneumonia was 'nothing, just a cold with ambitions'. I drew her sitting up in bed, hands folded, looking offended. That's her resting face.
Bus rain. The 7am Interbairros smelled like wet umbrella and bread. I sketched Seu Ivo from memory in the margin of a vibration report. Cláudio asked what it was. I said 'a dog'. He believed me.
Worker's Day. Slept until 10, which felt illegal. Drew Limonada in her new pot with sunlight. She has eight leaves now. No lemon, but very good leaf composition.

Work holiday. I slept until 10, then drew for three hours without checking the phone. It felt illegal. The bus comics are dead but my hands still want to draw motion: a woman chasing a hat, a man with a parrot. Juca lives on, at least.
Workers' day. Stayed home with Limonada and a sketchbook. Drew the lemon tree from three angles. None of them look like a lemon tree yet.
May Day off. Rafa and I made pastel at his parents' kitchen and burned half of them. His mom said mine were worse. She's right.
Dia do Trabalho. No beach, no Festa Junina, just a clean apartment and a lemon tree on the windowsill. Limonada has seven leaves and no opinions about labor rights.

Limonada has five leaves now and one of them is slightly yellow. I moved her to a sunnier part of the windowsill and whispered 'come on, girl'. The girls in the república think I'm strange. They are correct.

Português: Estágio no CIC, medição de vibração, planilha, gráfico, reunião. Fico boa nisso, e é isso que assusta. Durante o almoço desenhei o Cláudio lendo o jornal e quase senti falta do ônibus Interbairros. Quase.
A woman on the bus said Juca the parrot is 'muito educado'. I don't have the heart to explain he doesn't exist outside my notebook.
Tio Beto, I still can't play 'Asa Branca' past the second verse. I practiced on Rafa's guitar and his string cut my finger. The violão is waiting at your house, I know. One more year.

Rafa and I walked through Passeio Público after the pastel and he talked about São Paulo apartments for twenty minutes. I told him I like Curitiba because the trees are close. He said I'm romantic. I said 'you're moving anyway'. We laughed, but not all the way.
Bia's birthday dinner. We wrote our names on a napkin this time because the bar wall from 2014 got painted. She said the napkin is more portable. I folded it and put it in my wallet.
Money check: R$ 310 left and it's the 8th. I am becoming an expert in rice. The Interbairros page is still there, just sleeping. I miss Seu Ivo and Juca, even though Juca never existed.
PT: Aula de natação às 7h. Engoli metade da piscina e Dona Cida disse que flutuar é confiança, não técnica. Respondi que é muito poético para às sete da manhã. Ela me molhou. Gosto dela.
The factory has a coffee machine that makes a sound like a small dying animal. Every afternoon at 3pm. I've started drawing it during lunch: a metal bird screaming into a cup.
Limonada has eight leaves now and one of them is bent like it's waving. The girls at the república want to put her in the fridge rules. I said no.
Money check: R$ 280 left and it's the 13th. I'm living on RU rice and the bolachas Mom sends. The factory internship pays, but not much.
Mãe, I know you asked if I gave up on the drawings. I said yes again. There is a second sketchbook now, this one hidden behind the calculus books. Progress?
Bia and I walked in the Passeio Público. She said I talk about the sea like other people talk about boyfriends. I said the sea doesn't ask me to move to São Paulo. She said fair.

Vó told me the story of Coronel again, but this time she added that he stole a chicken once and she never told her father. 'Menina, todo cão tem um segredo.' I wrote it down. I want to draw a dog with a chicken under his arm.

At the factory, the machines smell like oil and warm metal. I like that smell, which surprises me. I measure vibrations and fill spreadsheets, but at lunch I sketch gears. Cláudio saw and said 'that's the right way to look at a machine'. I don't know what that means but I liked it.
PT: Mãe me perguntou se eu ainda estou ‘nessa história de desenhos’. Eu disse que não, de novo. Ela respondeu ‘então por que tem carvão na mão?’. Era marcador de desenho. Mentira ruim, Marina.
Rafa mentioned São Paulo again, casually, like it's weather. I changed the subject to the parrot man's bandage. He asked who Seu Ivo is. I said 'nobody important', which is a lie.
Rafa's apartment hunt for São Paulo has begun. He shows me listings and says 'imagine us there' in a voice that makes me love him and want to put my head under a pillow at the same time.
Money check: R$ 210 for eleven days. I am eating RU and the bolachas Mom sends. I'm also good at turning instant noodles into something that feels like food. Growth.
Bia disse que eu devo ter nascido com um lápis na mão. Eu disse que nasci com medo de água. Ela disse 'um dia'. Eu disse 'um dia'.
Tio Beto, I haven't practiced 'Asa Branca' this month. The factory eats evenings. I'll bring the violão to Festa Junina anyway, even if it's just to hold it.
I dreamed I was measuring vibrations inside a lemon. Cláudio would say it has a personality. I woke up hungry for pastel.
Tio, I tried 'Asa Branca' again last night and got to the second verse before the violão went out of tune. I think the violão is plotting against me. Or I am. Probably me.

Pastel de feira with Rafa. He talked about São Paulo again and I talked about the sea again. At least we are consistent. The pastel was good, the conversation was familiar, and somehow that is comforting.

Rafa’s mom invited us to dinner and asked about marriage again. He joked. I laughed. In the car later I said I’m tired of being the punchline and he said he didn’t realize it was a joke. I believe him, which is the problem.
Money check: R$ 900 left, it's the 24th, and the factory lunch is R$ 12. I am living on bolachas and optimism. Please, future me, laugh at this, not cry.
Swimming lesson #1: adult beginners, 7am. I swallowed half the pool and a child told me I was doing it 'all wrong'. She was right.
Dreamed of the sea again. I stood at the edge and the water came up to my ankles. Not warm, not cold. I woke up with sand in my shoes, which is impossible. I checked twice.
Bia, thank you for not asking why I stopped posting comics. You just asked if I was drawing. I said 'sometimes.' You said 'good enough.' It was good enough.
Bia, the parrot man wasn't on the bus all week. I drew a strip where Juca waits at the stop alone. It got 40 likes. I cried a little at the bus stop.
Portuguese: Festa Junina ainda não chegou e eu já estou com saudade do bolo de fubá da Vó. Ela fez no telefone, explicando cada passo, e eu escrevi tudo num guardanapo que provavelmente vou perder.
Money check: R$ 210 left and it's the 28th. Progress since 2014? I have a job, at least. But the job has less leftover than calculus stress did.

I stopped posting bus comics in January because of the internship. Today I opened the account and saw someone asking 'where is Seu Ivo?'. I didn't answer. I don't know the answer. That bothers me more than I expected.

Tio Beto, I still haven't learned 'Asa Branca' all the way through. I can get to the first chorus and then my fingers forget. But I played it for Limonada and she didn't judge. One more year, like always.

PT: Choveu no caminho para o estágio e cheguei com a calça molhada até o joelho. Cláudio me emprestou uma blusa velha do CIC que cheirava a café e oficina. Desenhei a blusa depois, com as manchas. Ele disse que virou arte. Eu disse ‘virou evidência’.
Failed the driving test. Same hill. I stalled and the examiner wrote something and didn't look at me. I cried on the bus home and Seu Ivo's parrot said 'bom dia' to me anyway. Thank you, Juca.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was holding a drawing of it, and the wind tried to take it. I woke up holding the sketchbook to my chest, which is dramatic but true.
Dia dos Namorados is coming. Rafa asked what I want. I said a walk, like always. He's already talking about São Paulo again.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's is next week. I am not trying 'Asa Branca'. I am bringing brigadeiro because that's the least I can do. He will ask anyway and I will pretend to be surprised.
It rained all day and the bus fogged up so much Seu Ivo's parrot became a green smudge on the window. I drew the smudge. It looks like a cloud with a beak.

Rain again. The bus was late and I stood under the shelter with five strangers and nobody spoke. I drew them from memory later: the woman with the red umbrella, the boy with the backpack bigger than him, the man checking his watch. It was a good page.
At the factory, Cláudio found my sketch of the motor and said it was clearer than the technical drawing. I said I was just doodling. He said 'keep doodling.' I will try.

Cláudio brought me a proper pencil from his old drafting desk. He said 'engineers who draw are dangerous'. I said 'engineers who sing are worse' and he laughed so hard coffee came out of his nose. I think I found my people.
Rafa talked about São Paulo again today. Buildings, subway, opportunities. I listened and thought about Limonada on the windowsill. Neither of us is wrong.
Rafa said São Paulo is where things happen. I said things happen on the bus too. He laughed. I didn't. The old man with the parrot is more reliable than any city.
Dia dos Namorados is tomorrow and I wrote the capsule to Rafa but I don't know if I'll send it. I am proud of him and tired of pretending I want São Paulo. Both can be true. I think.

Dia dos Namorados tomorrow. Rafa got the São Paulo offer and I am proud of him and tired of pretending I want to follow. I bought him a card that says 'parabéns' instead of 'te amo' because I panicked at the stationery store. Growth is not linear.
The bus comics have a name still, but my hand doesn't have time. I looked at the old strip of Seu Ivo e o Papagaio and thought: at least he's still on the fridge in my head.

Dia dos Namorados. Rafa, I'm writing this one to you but I don't know if I'll ever let it arrive. You got the offer in São Paulo. You're going. I'm proud of you and I'm so tired of pretending I want to follow.
Second driving test. Same hill. I stalled again, but only once. The examiner said 'again' and I said 'no' and he looked surprised. I'm taking a break from cars.
Rua XV smells like wet wood after the rain. Same as 2014. Some things don't change, which is comforting in a very small, very damp way.

Drew the assembly line during lunch. A motor, a hand, a coffee cup. Cláudio watched over my shoulder and asked if I could make the diagram ‘less technical, more friendly’. I said sure, and put a tiny sun with sunglasses in the corner. He kept it.
Rafa got the offer in São Paulo. I said I'm proud. I am. I also want to put my feet in the sea and stay there.

We went to Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I didn't play 'Asa Branca', I didn't even hold the violão. Tio Beto looked at me once and said 'next year'. I nodded. I'm tired of 'next year', but I wrote it down anyway.
Rafa's going-away lunch. I brought a comic strip of him as a building with legs. He laughed too loud. I didn't cry until the bus home, which counts as improvement.
Father's Day lunch at Tio Beto's. He asked if I still draw. I said sometimes. He said 'sometimes is better than never', which is the nicest thing he's said about it.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I didn't even try 'Asa Branca'. Tio Beto didn't ask. That silence sat at the table with us. I ate too much canjica to compensate.
Rafa and I made dinner in the república kitchen: pasta, no sauce, just garlic and hope. The girls said it was edible. I drew the pan afterwards, greasy handle and all.
Dia dos Namorados leftovers. Rafa made dinner and I did the dishes. He said 'we work well like this' and I agreed. The São Paulo thing sits between us on the couch like a third person.
The factory air conditioning broke and I measured vibrations in a pool of sweat. At lunch I sketched the motor fan blade and Cláudio stood behind me for a full minute without saying anything.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I didn't play Asa Branca. Tio Beto didn't mention it, which felt worse than the second driving test. I ate two bolos and left early.

Bia and I found the parrot man again on the 7am bus. He had a bandage on his hand and the parrot said ‘bom dia, motorista’ to everyone, then turned to me. I’m counting it. Drew them in the margin of a calibration sheet.
Rafa falou de São Paulo por vinte minutos no almoço. Eu falei do mar por cinco. Acho que ninguém percebeu. Eu percebi.

Money check: R$ 340 for ten days, which is better than 2014 but I still ate arroz com feijão four times. I bought a watercolor set on impulse and hid it under the bed. Some habits are inherited from the sketchbook under the mattress.

Limonada survived being forgotten on the windowsill during the weekend trip. The leaves looked dramatic, like small green flags of surrender. One hour of water and she forgave me. More than I deserve.

Limonada has eight leaves and no lemons, obviously. I moved her to a real pot today because the yogurt cup looked ridiculous and she was getting tall. I named the pot 'Curitiba' because it's sturdy and cold sometimes.
Rain in Curitiba, of course. Walked home with a broken umbrella and bought a pão de queijo to compensate. It worked for exactly four minutes.
At the factory I measured a motor that vibrates at exactly the frequency of my alarm clock. I told Cláudio and he said 'that's why you look tired'. He's not wrong.
Passeio Público with Bia. She asked if I'd follow Rafa to São Paulo. I said 'I don't know' and she said 'yes you do'. We sat on the same bench and ate pastel de feira. She was right.
Winter cold in Curitiba and the factory floor is even colder. I draw motors in my notebook during lunch because my hands need something warm to do.
Three years since the dream about standing at the edge. Still standing. But my feet moved a little this week, in the bath, which counts as research.

PT: Festa Junina na casa do Tio Beto. Toquei três acordes de ‘Asa Branca’ e parei por vergonha. Tio Beto não pediu mais, só disse ‘ano que vem’. Toda vez que ele diz isso meu estômago vira. Um dia eu vou tocar até o fim.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time the water was warm and someone was swimming next to me, but I couldn't see who. I woke up with my calves tight.

Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was at the edge and the water was warm, but instead of moving I just stood there talking to a fish. The fish said 'you're late'. I woke up and wrote it down because it felt important, though it probably isn't.

Money check: first salary from the internship, R$ 950. I bought a better sketchbook and felt guilty, then bought Mom a small printer she didn't ask for. She will use it to print things she won't admit she likes.
Limonada has eight leaves. I took a photo with my hand for scale and she looks like a tiny tree pretending to be brave. I relate.

Domingo na casa do Tio Beto. Viola na varanda, café forte, calor de julho. Ele perguntou quando eu voltaria a tocar e eu disse 'quando conseguir parar de esquecer a música'. Ele riu e disse 'essa é a única parte que importa'.
Swimming? No. But I watched a tutorial and nearly drowned in my own confidence. Dona Cida would laugh. I don't know Dona Cida yet, but I'm sure she would.

Português: Limonada passou da janela para um vaso de verdade. Oito folhas. Brought her inside wrapped in my scarf last winter and she survived, which is more than I can say for my calculus grade in 2015.
Rafa's mom asked about marriage again at lunch. I said 'when I learn to swim', which made everyone laugh. Rafa's hand was under the table and didn't squeeze mine. I noticed.
At the factory the motors sound like they're arguing. I hummed 'Asa Branca' while measuring one and Cláudio tapped his pen to the rhythm. He didn't say anything. I think we're friends.

Dreamed of the sea again. This time the water was warm and I was standing with one foot in. I woke up with my right foot cold and my left foot warm, which makes no sense but felt symbolic enough to write down.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's was rained out, so we ate canjica in the living room. He still asked if I practiced 'Asa Branca'. I said 'next year', which is becoming a tradition.
Mãe, hoje Limonada estava tão bonita na janela que até tirei foto. Seu Ivo perguntou se ela dá limão. Disse 'um dia'. Ele disse 'boa'. As pessoas gostam de promessas, né?
Mom called and asked if the internship is 'serious work.' I said yes. She said 'good, and the drawings?' I said 'also yes.' Silence. Then she asked what I was drawing. Progress.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I played 'Asa Branca' until the second verse and then forgot everything. He clapped anyway. One more year.
Vó asked if I still talk to Bia every day. I said yes. She said 'good, women need a witness'. I don't know what she meant exactly, but I wrote it down.
Went swimming with Bia at the public pool. I lasted twelve seconds floating. A child applauded. Bia said 'that's patronizing' and I said 'I'll take it'.

Cláudio asked me to redraw an assembly diagram by hand for the new line. It took two hours and I enjoyed every minute. He looked at it and said 'finally someone who sees the machine'. I have decided that is my compliment of the year.

Money check: first paycheck from the factory, R$ 1.350. I paid Mom back nothing because she refused again, bought Vó Lúcia a new phone card, and saved the rest. The ‘MAR’ fund is just a jar right now, but it exists.
At the factory I drew the assembly line from memory during lunch. Cláudio looked at it and said 'you missed a bolt'. He was right. Then he said it was good. I didn't know what to do with that either.
Bia's birthday bar. We didn't write on the wall this year; the bar changed owners and the wall is painted. We were still there.
Português: Bia tentou me ensinar a boiar de novo. Durou seis segundos. Uma criança de uns oito anos boiou ao lado com cara de desafio. Eu não vou desistir. Eu vou. Talvez.
At the factory, I found a stray lemon seed in my pocket from lunch. No idea how. Planted it in a coffee cup labeled MARINA because apparently I only plant things in labeled containers now.
A Vó contou a história do Coronel de novo. Cada vez ele fica mais corajoso. Escrevi as duas versões. Um dia desenho todas.
Bia, Rafa showed me apartments in São Paulo on his phone today. I smiled and said 'nice light'. The light was actually nice. That's the problem.
Mom asked if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said yes. I lied. The sketchbook is on the windowsill now, next to Limonada, like a couple of quiet conspirators.

Bia, you moved to Florianópolis and I am already jealous of your window. Thank you for being the only person who still asks 'are you drawing?' without making it sound like a joke. I promise I am, badly, but yes.
Passed the first theory test for the license. The clerk stamped my paper with the energy of a man who has seen a thousand nervous people and has decided to feel nothing about any of them.
Swimming pool at the club. Still can't float for more than ten seconds. A boy of maybe seven stayed next to me and floated like a cork. I hate him a little.
Vó Lúcia called to ask if I was eating. I said yes. I was eating bolachas. She knows.
Called Vó Lúcia on Sunday. She told me the farm dog Coronel could smell storms. I asked if she made that up. She said 'all good dogs can'. Fair enough.
Rafa and I walked along the canal. He talked about São Paulo again. I talked about the sea again. We are very consistent people. I drew the bridge instead of choosing a side.
Swimming still scares me. I watched a kid float at the pool and felt jealous. One day I'll do it. Not today.

Portuguese: Estou desenhando o diagrama de montagem do novo motor e descobri que gosto de precisão quando ela tem curvas. Retas puras me entediam. Talvez seja por isso que prefiro ônibus a carro: mais gente, mais detalhes, mais vida no meio do trajeto.

Sunday call with Vó Lúcia. She told me about the jabuticabeira at the farm and how Coronel is buried under it. She has told me this five times. I wrote down every version. The dog gets braver each retelling, which is probably how memory works.
PT: Dinheiro no fim do mês e ainda fiz café da máquina do estágio para economizar. O café é ruim. O motor que consertei vibra certo agora. Pequenas vitórias para um julho úmido.
At the pool, Dona Cida from the 7am class yelled 'a engenheira!' across three lanes. I swallowed pool water and waved. She is 71 and better than me at everything.
Limonada is too big for the yogurt cup now but I can't move her because she looks good there, and I'm weak. The roots are trying to escape the bottom like little white fingers.
PT: Sonhei com o mar. Dessa vez entrei até a cintura e fiquei lá, sem pânico, só observando o fundo. Acordei com vontade de desenhar e desenhei um quarto de página antes do alarme. Pequeno, mas foi.
Bus man with the green parrot was back after a week. He nodded at me like we share a secret. We do. His name is still Ivo in my head.
Work lunch sketching. I drew the motor from memory and Cláudio asked if I could draw assembly diagrams for the new line. Turns out drawing is useful. Mom would not be surprised.
Vó Lúcia's voice on Sunday: 'menina, você está trabalhando muito.' I said 'vovó, estou desenhando motores.' She said 'então você está desenhando, e isso é bom.' I needed that.
The bus was late and I missed the 7am. The 7:20 had a man with a green umbrella shaped like a frog. He noticed me drawing it and bowed. Curitiba is kind to people who look up.
Seu Ivo smiled at me on the bus today. I don't know if he recognizes me or if he's just polite. I drew his hat anyway. Juca was quiet, which worried me until he said 'tchau, motorista' at the end.

Swimming is not going well. I went to the pool with Rafa and lasted maybe four seconds before panicking. A kid of maybe six floated next to me the whole time, out of pure spite I think. I am 21 and being defeated by water.
Bia's birthday. We wrote our names on the wall of the bar in São Francisco again. The old marker was still there under the new one. We laughed for ten minutes.
Vó Lúcia told me the Coronel story again on Wednesday. In this version he walked her to school and waited at the gate even on Saturdays. I wrote down the difference. He gets braver every time.

The parrot man is still on the 7am bus. The parrot said 'bom dia, motorista' and nobody reacted, except me, as always. I drew them in the margin of my vibration notes. Cláudio asked if it was a machine. I said no.
Domingo na casa da Vó. Bolo de fubá quente e violão desafinado. Ela disse que eu engordei e depois perguntou se eu ainda desenhava. Disse que sim.
Limonada is taller than the yogurt cup now and I moved her to a real pot. The girls said I'm 'nesting'. I said 'it's a plant'. They said 'sure'. They might be right.
I tried to swim at the gym pool. Lasted two seconds, one more than 2015. Progress is embarrassing but it's progress.
Bus 7am. Seu Ivo was back with a bandage on his hand. The parrot said 'bom dia' to me specifically. I am counting it as a personal victory, small as it is.
Bia's birthday is coming. The bar wall in São Francisco is probably painted over now, but I drew our names in my sketchbook anyway, on a brick wall with a crack through the M.
Rafa's mom asked about the wedding again. He said 'when she agrees to São Paulo.' Everyone laughed. I smiled. The smile was not real, but it was polite.
Bia's birthday. We wrote our names on a new wall in São Francisco, because the old one really was painted over. She said 'second time's the charm'. I drew a tiny parrot next to our names.
Swimming lesson attempt number one. I paid for a month, stood at the pool edge for five minutes, then got in and remembered I hate getting water in my nose. The instructor was patient. I was not.

Bia and I ate pastel in the Passeio Público and she told me she’s thinking about Florianópolis. I said ‘when?’ and she said ‘not yet’. I understood. I also understood that I want to go with her and won’t say it yet.
Bia, Limonada has nine leaves and one of them is split down the middle like a heart. I'm not saying it's a sign. I'm saying I took a photo and sent it to Mom anyway.
Money check: R$ 580 left, day 20. I am rich by 2014 standards. This is the saddest victory lap. Bought a pastel and felt like a CEO.
I swam twice at the public pool with a floatie disguised as a noodle. A kid asked if I was 'learning'. I said 'practicing'. There is a difference and I am clinging to it.
Cláudio showed me how to measure vibrations on a motor. I drew the machine in my notebook and he said 'you should be in design'. I pretended not to care.
I stayed late at the factory to finish a diagram and the lights went out. Sat in the dark for ten minutes, drawing by phone light. The diagram looked better scared.
Bus 7am. Seu Ivo was back with a bandage on his hand and Juca said 'bom dia, motorista' very clearly. I drew them both on a napkin. Nobody reacted except me and, I think, the driver's mirror.
Limonada has ten leaves now. The coffee-cup seed did nothing, which is fine. Not every seed has to work. Some are just practice for hoping.
PT: Limonada ganhou um vaso de verdade porque a raiz atravessou o fundo do copo de iogurte. As meninas da república fizeram uma pequena cerimônia de mudança. Bia filmou. Não foi irônico, foi fofo.

Portuguese: Hoje Vó me ligou e disse que o Totó 'virou político', porque agora fica na porta do mercado. Ela ri de própria piada. Eu ri também, mas fiquei pensando que ela enxerga história em tudo, até num cachorro.
Mom saw me sketching at lunch and said 'you always liked paper more than numbers'. She said it like a diagnosis. I'm choosing to take it as permission.
The bus comics are dead but I still draw the bus. Today an old lady brought a cat in a shoebox. She opened it slightly so it could see out. I drew the eye looking through the flap.

Português: Frost on the windowsill. Limonada survived. Trouxe ela pra dentro enrolada no meu cachecol. Oito folhas. Mais alta que o pote de iogurte agora. Se ela vira árvore de verdade eu juro que desenho ela toda semana.
September, cold morning. Limonada is still on the windowsill with eight leaves now. She survived the week without sun by being stubborn.

Frost scare on the windowsill. I wrapped Limonada in my scarf and brought her inside. Eight leaves now. She's taller than the yogurt cup, so I moved her to a real pot and felt like a very small landlord.
Frost on the windowsill last night. I brought Limonada inside wrapped in my scarf. Eight leaves? No, ten. She is taller than the yogurt cup now, and she knows it. Moved her to a real pot.
The parrot man wasn't on the bus for three days. I was genuinely worried. When he returned, Juca said 'bom dia, motorista' and then, I swear, looked at me. I counted it as a personal greeting.
Limonada survived a frost on the windowsill. I brought her inside wrapped in my scarf. Eight leaves. She's taller than the yogurt cup now, moved her to a real pot.
First month of the internship felt like a year. The engineers are kind, the work is fine, and that is exactly the danger. I don't want fine to become forever.
Limonada survived the frost on the windowsill. I brought her inside wrapped in my scarf and put her next to the violão. Eight leaves. She looks stubborn. I respect her.
Sunday call with Vó. She said the jabuticabeira at the farm is full this year and asked if I was eating fruit. I said yes. I had one banana. She pretended not to notice the pause.
Frost on the windowsill last night. Limonada got wrapped in my scarf and brought inside. Eight leaves now, all still there. She survived. So did I.

Seu Ivo was back on the bus today after a week away. Juca said ‘bom dia, motorista’ and then looked at me. I’m pretending it was for me again. Drew them both before I got off. It’s the first bus drawing in months.
Rafa and I watched the Olympics reruns at his parents' house. His mom asked about São Paulo. He said 'soon.' I heard 'soon' like a door closing softly.
Rafa talked about São Paulo again, the apartments with elevators, the noise. I said the sea doesn't have elevators. He laughed and then didn't.
Mãe, vi a receita do bolo de fubá no grupo da família e pensei em Vó. Não comentei. Você também não comentou. É engraçado como silêncio pode ser uma receita.

Limonada survived a frost on the windowsill. I brought her inside wrapped in my scarf. Eight leaves. She's taller than the yogurt cup now and I have moved her to a real pot. I talked to her the whole time. She said nothing back but seemed grateful.
Sunday call with Vó Lúcia. She told me the Coronel story again. He gets braver every time. I wrote down this version: he barked at a snake. Next month he'll probably fight a dinosaur.
Frost on the windowsill tonight. I brought Limonada inside wrapped in my scarf. Her leaves are still green. I'm calling it a victory.

Cláudio saw me sketching a motor during lunch and asked if I could draw assembly diagrams for the new line. I said yes before he finished the sentence. Then I went to the bathroom and smiled at the mirror like an idiot.
Tio Beto, I didn't try 'Asa Branca' at Festa Junina and you didn't ask. That was harder than failing. I'm practicing the second verse now. Quietly. So nobody hears me mess up.
Bus home from the factory, late shift. The sky in CIC looked like someone spilled orange paint over the warehouses. I drew it on a receipt. Receipt drawing #47. I'm counting.
Bia, you said moving to Floripa was 'maybe someday'. I'm writing it down so you can't pretend you didn't say it. I'm holding you to someday.

At the factory today, a motor vibration report matched my hand-drawn sketch almost exactly. Cláudio looked at both and said 'you drew what it sounds like'. I have never been more proud of a sentence about a motor.
I started posting one tiny drawing a week again. Not the bus comics, just things: a bolt, a rain cloud, Vó's hands. Nobody asked. It feels like breathing.
Drew the assembly diagrams for Cláudio's new line. He said I draw better than the CAD. I put it on my fridge, not my tombstone yet. Too dramatic, even for me.

Mom, you'll hate this: I drew the farm in Irati from Vó's stories. Coronel is there, under the jabuticabeira, looking guilty about the chicken. It's not finished, but I think she would know which tree it is.
Money check: R$ 340 left and it's the 24th. Living on RU and Mom's bolachas. I'm writing it down so in a few years I can laugh at it. Or cry. Depends on the lemon tree.

PT: Vó Lúcia me ligou e me contou do Coronel de novo. Dessa vez ele esperou ela na porta da escola e latiu para um estranho. A cada versão ele fica mais corajoso. Guardei as diferenças num caderninho, não sei por quê.
Cláudio caught me drawing a motor during lunch again. This time he said 'you should show the diagrams department'. I pretended not to hear him. I heard him.
Money check: R$ 340 left for the month and it's the 26th. Living on RU and the bolachas Mom sends. I'm writing this so next year I can laugh at it. Or cry. Depends.
Rain all day. The bus leaked a little near the back seat. I drew the rain on the window and the woman next to me asked if I was an artist. I said 'sometimes'.
Cláudio showed me how to read a vibration graph and I understood it. The scary part is how satisfying the numbers are. I still prefer the drawings in the margins.
Rafa asked if I'd visit São Paulo with him. I said maybe. I meant no. I drew the train station instead and didn't show him. Cowardly? Perhaps. Artistic? Also perhaps.
Rafa said São Paulo is 'where things happen'. I said Curitiba has things. He asked what kind. I said 'trees and buses and a woman with a frog umbrella'. He laughed and I didn't.

Started drawing the motor diagrams for Cláudio at lunch. Small lines, correct angles, and a tiny sun in the corner that I erased twice and kept once. The assembly team said they were 'clear'. I'll take it.
Mom sent a photo of the printer I gave her. She printed one of my small drawings and taped it to the fridge. She didn't comment. The tape is crooked.

Mom saw the Interbairros page somehow. She didn't say anything for two days. Then she sent a screenshot of one strip with the message 'this old man looks like your grandfather'. It is the closest thing to a compliment I've ever had from her about drawing.
Mom asked on the phone if the 'little drawings' were still happening. I said 'sometimes.' She said 'hmm.' That hmm was bigger than a compliment.
Rafa's mom asked about wedding plans again. I said I'm learning to drive first. She laughed. I didn't.
Bus home from the factory. The driver let me off one stop early because it was raining. The parrot man waved. I waved back like an idiot. It was nice.

Mom printed something at home for the first time and showed me. It was a list of groceries. She said the printer ‘makes a lot of noise’. I laughed and she didn’t understand why. She also didn’t ask about drawings, which is progress.
Mom sent a screenshot of one of my old bus strips. She wrote 'this old man looks like your grandfather'. It's the closest thing to a compliment.

I started a small drawing of Mom's printer, because she uses it to print my comics now. She hasn't said she prints them. Bia's mom told me. I want to believe this is her way of clapping without clapping.
Bia and I wrote our names on the wall of the bar in São Francisco again. If they paint over it, we were still there. The marker bled a little. Good enough.
Money check: R$ 280 left, it's the 9th, and the fridge has names on every yogurt including one labeled 'DO NOT TOUCH, SERIOUSLY'. That's Ana. She's serious.

Drawing little comics again, this time about the factory. A strip about Cláudio and the singing bus driver got 200 likes. Strangers recognize the machines from my sketches, which is either flattering or worrying.
Called Vó Lúcia on a Wednesday because Sunday felt too far away. She told me the same story about Coronel but added that he once stole a chicken. I believe him completely.
Mom printed one of my old Interbairros strips. She didn't say anything. Bia's mom told me she has it on the fridge. I am choosing to believe this is a compliment.

Mom asked if I’m ‘still keeping up with the drawing thing’. I said yes this time. She went quiet for two seconds, then asked if I could draw her mother’s house in Irati. I said I’d try. That felt like a door opening a crack.
Limonada está com dez folhas e quase do tamanho do pote de iogurte. Nenhum limão, mas flor bonita. Bia chama de 'limão decorativo'. Eu me recuso.

Portuguese: Hoje na fábrica o café acabou às 15h e o engenheiro sênior disse que isso era 'crise de abastecimento'. Desenhei uma xícara triste e colei no quadro. Todo mundo riu. Foi o melhor momento do dia.
Vó Lúcia's hands were cold on the phone, or maybe that's just how I remember them. She told me about the farm dog and how he waited at the gate. I want to draw this one day and get the waiting right.
I stopped posting bus comics in January. Sometimes I see a scene on the bus and my hand reaches for a phone that isn't drawing. Missing something is a sign it mattered.
I tried to float at the pool again. Lasted six seconds. The kid next to me, maybe six, floated the entire time like he was bored. Spite is a strong motivator.
Sketched the Interbairros stop from memory during a meeting. Cláudio asked if it was a real stop. I said yes. He said 'good shading.' That's the best feedback I've had in months.

Called Vó Lúcia. She told me about the farm in Irati and the dog called Coronel again. She says he waited at the gate for nine years. I think she's adding a year every time. I'm keeping all versions. They're hers.
At the factory someone asked if I was 'the engineer who draws'. I said yes before thinking. It came out proud. I'm keeping that.
At the factory, I sketched a little sun with sunglasses on a diagram. Cláudio said 'not for the investor deck.' It went in the investor deck. I am very professional.

PT: Nadar ainda é um desastre organizado. Consegui três braçadas seguidas hoje e Dona Cida bateu palma como se eu tivesse ganhado medalha. Eu quase vomitei cloro, mas fiquei feliz. Dezoito anos pedindo isso.
Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He asked about the comics. I said I stopped. He didn't say anything, just handed me the violão. I played badly. He clapped.

Vó called on a Wednesday instead of Sunday and I panicked for half a second. She just wanted to say she saw a lemon tree in the neighbor's yard and thought of me. 'Agora você tem concorrente.' I love her so much it embarrasses me.
Bus comics might come back. I have three strips in a folder: Seu Ivo, Juca, and one about a woman who always carries two umbrellas. I don't know her name yet. Maybe I never will.
Vó, you told the Coronel story again today and this time he walked you to school in the rain. I wrote it down. I don't know when, but one day I'll draw it right.
Bia's birthday in São Francisco. We checked the wall where we wrote our names in 2014. It's still there, faded, under a poster. Bia said we're basically archaeology now.

Rafa got the offer. He tried to sound casual over the phone, like São Paulo is just a city and not a door closing between us. I said congratulations and meant it. Then I sat on my bed with Limonada and didn't say anything for an hour.

Rafa bought me a pastel and said I'm too smart to fail twice. He was talking about Cálculo, but it felt bigger. He is annoying and I think I love him. Also, I haven't drawn in two weeks. I know. I know.
Dreamed of Vó Lúcia on the farm, Coronel at her feet. She didn't say anything, just held my hand. I woke up and drew her hands before I forgot the way they looked.
I swam one length at the pool and swallowed water in the middle. Dona Cida wasn't there, but a retired man clapped and said 'bom trabalho'. I chose to believe him.
Halloween party at the república. I went as a motor. Cardboard, foil, and one lemon as a dial. People liked it more than my costume in 2016, which was 'tired engineering student'.
Halloween at the república: we dressed Limonada as a ghost with a napkin. She looked dignified. The fridge voted her best costume.
Halloween at the república. We didn't have costumes, so Ana drew mustaches on everyone with eyeliner. The delivery guy thought we were five very serious men. I was the only one who laughed.

Mom saw a strip I posted months ago, Seu Ivo e o Papagaio, and sent a screenshot with no comment for two days. Then: 'this old man looks like your grandfather'. It's the closest thing to a compliment about drawing I've had from her.
At the factory, a motor vibrated wrong and I found the problem before Cláudio. He said ‘engenheira’ with respect, not as a joke. I almost didn’t want to leave. Almost. The sea is still the sea.

Português: Limonada sobreviveu à geada na janela. Trouxe ela pra dentro enrolada no cachecol. Oito folhas. Mais alta que o pote de iogurte agora, passei pro vaso real. Ela parece mais séria nesse vaso.
Limonada survived a small frost on the windowsill. I brought her inside wrapped in my scarf. She now lives next to the sketchbook and the calculus book, which is a good neighborhood.

Cláudio saw me sketching a motor during lunch and asked if I could draw the assembly diagrams for the new line. Turns out drawing is useful. Who knew. (Mom.) I accepted before he finished the sentence.
Sunday call. Vó Lúcia said her hands were cold. I told her to wear gloves. She said 'who will hold your hand then?' I didn't answer. I just held the phone tighter.
Factory lunch. Cláudio saw me sketching a motor and asked if I could draw the assembly diagrams for the new line. Drawing is useful. Who knew. Mom, probably.

Rafa's offer got more concrete. He talks about São Paulo like a person he's in love with, and I'm tired of pretending I don't hear it. I drew the pastel stand at the feira from memory and it looked lonely. I don't know if that's about the pastel.
Cláudio saw me sketching a motor during lunch and asked if I could draw the assembly diagrams for the new line. Turns out drawing is useful. Who knew. (Mom.) I erased the sun before showing him.
Cláudio saw me sketching a motor at lunch and asked if I could draw assembly diagrams. I said maybe. My heart did something it doesn't do over vibration graphs.

Sunday call with Vó. She told me about the farm dog Coronel and how he waited at the gate. I've heard it before, but today she said 'he was loyal the way you are to your drawing, even when nobody watches'. I wrote it down twice.

Português: Cláudio viu meu desenho de motor no almoço e perguntou se eu poderia fazer os diagramas da nova linha de montagem. Desenho servindo pra alguma coisa. (Mãe, você tinha razão. Não vou te contar isso.)
Bia and I watched the sunset from the bus stop because the bus was late. She said I should draw faster. I said the light changes too fast. We stayed anyway.

PT: Dinheiro: R$ 340 sobraram e é dia 11. Vivi de RU e bolachas da mãe, de novo. Escrevo isso para rir ou chorar em dois anos. Se a Marina do futuro estiver rica, agradeço a paciência. Se não, pelo menos rimos juntas.
Limonada is in her real pot now and looks like a very small, very optimistic tree. No flowers, no lemons. Just stubbornness. We have that in common.
Bia, I haven't drawn the bus in months and I miss it. The parrot man probably has a whole life we don't know about. I want to know.

Portuguese: Eu desenhei o Seu Ivo de memória hoje, com Juca no ombro, e percebi que já não sei se ele existe assim ou se inventei a versão dele que preciso. Talvez seja assim com todas as pessoas que amamos no ônibus: elas viram personagem porque vão embora.
Swimming lesson before work. I swallowed half the pool and Dona Cida called me 'a engenheira'. I am not a swimmer yet. I am, apparently, a loud one.
A Sunday call with Vó Lúcia turned into Wednesday too. She complained about too many calls and then told me three stories. I think she waits by the phone.
At the factory the senior engineer, Cláudio, saw me sketching a motor during lunch and asked if I could draw the assembly diagrams for the new line. Turns out drawing is useful. Who knew. (Mom.)
Factory party for Cláudio's birthday. He gave a speech about machines and then, quietly, said 'and Marina draws them better than they are.' I went home and cried into a pastel.

Limonada survived the first frost on the windowsill. I wrapped her in my scarf at 2am like she was a baby. Eight leaves. She's taller than the yogurt cup now, so I moved her to a real pot and apologized to the cup.
Thanksgiving doesn't exist here but I made mashed potatoes anyway. Ate them with Rafa while reviewing calculus. Romantic? No. Comforting? Yes.

Rafa and I watched a storm from the república window. The lemon tree shook and I ran out in my socks to bring her inside. He called me dramatic. I called him dry. Limonada is fine, eight leaves, very proud of herself.
Rafa got the offer in São Paulo. He told me at dinner and I said 'that's amazing' and I meant it. We finished the meal. I did the dishes. The kitchen felt very large.
Rain again. The leak in the kitchen is back. We put the yogurt bucket under it again. Same bucket, same spot, same girls. The fridge still has names on every yogurt. Some rituals survive.
Called Vó Lúcia on Sunday and Wednesday this week. She complained I call too much and then talked for an hour about Coronel.
Money check: R$ 1.900 from the internship, R$ 400 saved, one watercolor set unopened under the bed. I feel rich and guilty at the same time, which is a new combination.
Limonada moved to a real pot today. She's taller than the yogurt cup now. I wrote 'MARINA' on the old cup anyway and kept it on the shelf.

PT: Limonada está com nove folhas e uma inclinação dramática para a janela. Acho que ela também quer o mar. Desenhei ela no caderno com o pote de iogurte ainda visível. Futura Marina, se ela tiver limão um dia, não esqueça de me avisar.
Factory holiday party. Cláudio told a story about a motor that exploded in 1998 and everyone laughed except me, because I was drawing the motor from his description. He saw. He didn't mind.
I signed up for swimming again after stopping in March. Dona Cida is 71 and still swims better than me. She called me 'a engenheira' and I floated for five whole seconds.
PT: Tio Beto me ensinou a trocar a corda do violão e disse que ‘Asa Branca’ está melhor, só falta coragem. Ele tem razão. Coragem é o acorde que não sei tocar.
Bia and I watched a movie and missed half of it talking about Curitiba versus everywhere else. She said I could go anywhere. I said I want the sea. She said 'then go.' I said 'soon.'
Decorated the república's tiny tree with a lemon ornament made from Limonada's old yogurt cup. The girls laughed. I think it's perfect.
We made bolo de fubá over video call with Vó. Mine came out too dry and she said 'menina, vai dar bolo é no chão'. We both laughed. I ate it anyway with tea and it was better than any store cake.
New Year planning. Mom wants Matinhos, Bia wants fireworks, Vó Lúcia says she'll stay awake this time. I stood with my feet in the water last year and that's still as far as I go. For now.
Rafa got the São Paulo offer. He told me at a café and smiled like someone introducing me to a new city. I smiled back. I'm proud and tired in the same breath.

Cláudio saw my lunch sketch again, this time of a bracket assembly, and asked if I could redraw the assembly diagrams for the new line. I said yes before thinking. Drawing for money. Mom was right, eventually.
Mom, I know you're reading this later. Thank you for the bolachas and for pretending not to notice the sketchbook. I know you noticed. I love you. Please don't ask me to stop drawing.
Money check: bought Mom a printer ink cartridge instead of a gift. She said 'finally, someone who understands priorities'. I think that's love.
Tio Beto sent a voice message trying to teach me the second verse of Asa Branca. I played it three times and still only have the first. I will try again. One more year. Again.

At Sunday lunch Vó Lúcia said my hands look like hers when she was young. She’s never said that before. I drew her holding the colher de pau and got the fingers right this time. She looked at it and said ‘too pretty’. That’s her highest praise.
Tio Beto at Sunday lunch asked if I'd play Asa Branca at Festa Junina. I said maybe. He said 'maybe means no.' He's right, but I didn't say that.
Faltam quinze dias pro Natal. Fiz um desenho da Vó com o chapéu grande da formatura dela. Ela disse que está velha. Eu disse que está perfeita.

Bia, I think Rafa and I are becoming two people at two bus stops. I'm not ready to say it, so I drew us as two figures on a platform, not facing each other. Tell me if it looks dramatic. It probably does.
New Year is coming and I want to make a list of promises, but I only have one that matters: keep drawing, even if it has to hide in lunch breaks and margins.
Bia, I'm scared that if Rafa goes to São Paulo I'll be alone with the bus and the factory and Limonada. Then I remember you'd tell me I'm being dramatic and also correct. Come visit before Christmas?
End of year at the república. The fridge has names on every yogurt again and Limonada has a tiny string of Christmas lights around her pot. She looks festive and confused. I feel the same.

Tio, I'm writing to you because you said one more year. I practiced twice this week. Both times I forgot the second verse. But I remembered the first one without looking, which is new. Don't tell anyone.
Last week before Christmas. I drew Vó Lúcia's bolo de fubá from memory and got the shape wrong. She said it looked like a hat. She laughed like stairs. I drew the laugh instead.
Year almost over. I still can't drive, still can't swim, but Limonada is alive and I drew every week, even if only on napkins.

Portuguese: Faltam duas semanas pro fim do ano e eu ainda não aprendi a nadar direito, ainda não toquei 'Asa Branca' até o fim e ainda desenho motors às 19h. Mas a Limonada está viva e a Vó está bem e eu tenho uma tinta nova embaixo da cama. Acho que conta.
Rafa, you said capsules are cheesy. Here: thanks for the playlist, for the pastéis, and for not making me choose yet. I know the question is coming.

PT: Viagem de fim de ano para Matinhos com a Bia e a família. Fiz pé na água à meia-noite, como sempre. Dessa vez olhei para o horizonte e pensei ‘um dia eu vou nadar até lá’. Vó Lúcia ficou acordada até 11:40 e jurou que viu os fogos.
Last bus before Christmas. Seu Ivo wasn't there, but the driver said 'bom dia' in the parrot's voice. I don't know if that's worse or better. I drew it anyway.
Failed the driving test again. Same hill. The examiner wrote something and didn't look at me. I told Limonada the hill is personal. She gave me no comfort, but she didn't contradict me either.
