End of year at the factory. Cláudio gave me a drawing pen. I gave him a drawing of him drinking coffee. He said 'I look better in real life'. He doesn't.

Bia wrote our names on the wall of a bar in São Francisco again, next to the old ones. The marker was green this time. I said it looked like a tiny fish. She said ‘that’s the point’. I don’t know the point, but I like it.
Christmas Eve at Mom's. Bolo de fubá, correct shape this time. Vó Lúcia fell asleep on the couch and still swore she saw the fireworks. Some things don't change. I hope they don't.
Christmas at Mom's. Bolo de fubá, too dry, nobody said anything. Tio Beto played Asa Branca without being asked. I didn't sing but I hummed the second verse under my breath.
Christmas at Vó's. She stayed awake until midnight just to prove she could. Her hands were cold when she held mine.
Christmas Eve at Mom's. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' without being asked and I didn't sing, but I hummed the second verse under my breath. He looked at me and nodded. I think that counts as a lesson.
Christmas at Mom's. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' without being asked and I didn't even try. He didn't ask. That's its own kind of kindness.
Christmas Eve at home. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' without being asked, and I didn't sing, but I hummed the second verse under my breath. Nobody heard. That counts, right?
Vó Lúcia fell asleep at 11:40 on Christmas Eve and still swore she saw fireworks. I held her cold hand and didn’t let go. I want to remember that: her hands were cold and she held on.
Limonada is taller than the yogurt cup now. Moved her to a real pot with a face I painted on it. She looks like she's judging my calculus notes. Fair.

PT: Último dia do ano e Limonada está no parapeito da janela, firme, com oito folhas e nenhuma lição. Rafa me mandou mensagem dizendo ‘ano que vem São Paulo’. Eu respondi com um emoji de onda. Ele não entendeu. Acho que não precisa.
New Year's Eve in Matinhos tomorrow. Vó Lúcia says she'll stay awake this time. She won't. I'll put my feet in the water at midnight again, as far as I go. Next year, maybe further.
I made a list of things I'm bad at: driving, swimming, playing 'Asa Branca', saying no to pastels. The sea is on the list of things I haven't done yet. I'm working on all of them.

New Year's Eve tomorrow. I'll stand with my feet in the water at midnight again, because that's as far as I go. Limonada is staying on the windowsill. Next year maybe I'll go farther. Maybe not. Either way, I'll write it down.
New Year at home, not the beach. I stood with my feet in the bathtub at midnight because that's as far as I go. Next year maybe more. I drew the water and called it a promise.

New Year's Eve in Curitiba, not Matinhos. Rafa came. We stood on the balcony at midnight and he talked about São Paulo again. I didn't stay with my feet in water because there was no water. I stood with my hands in my pockets and wanted the sea. I don't know if that's about the year or about him. Both, maybe.

New Year at Vó Lúcia's because Matinhos was too far. She stayed awake until midnight to prove she could and fell asleep at 11:43 again. I stood at the gate with my feet in the wet grass because that's as close as I get to the sea tonight.
One more for the year: I called Bia at midnight, then Mom, then sat with Vó Lúcia's hand in mine. Her hands were warm this time. I drew them quickly before I forgot the shape.
New Year's Eve with feet in the water, as usual, because that's as far as I go. Bia stood next to me and said 'one day you'll swim'. I said 'maybe'. I meant it this time.

Bus was late again and the parrot man waved at me like we're old friends. I drew Juca with a tiny scarf because it's January and Curitiba is doing its usual impression of a freezer. Rafa bought me a coffee at the station without saying anything, which is his whole language.

New year, same lemon tree on the windowsill. Limonada has eleven leaves now and a new neighbor: a cactus from Bia, with a post-it saying 'like you, but quieter'. The fridge in the república has a new yogurt with my name on it, which means someone finally noticed the old one expired in November.

Primeira semana do ano e já perdi a carteirinha da UTFPR no ônibus. Tive que contar uma história ridícula ao cobrador para pagar meia. Funcionou. Estou colocando um adesivo de gatinho na próxima, por segurança.

First week back at the factory and Cláudio already asked me to fix the same vibration report I fixed in December. I redrew the diagram on a napkin during lunch and he said it was better than the original. Small victories.
First Sunday of the year and no drawing done. Limonada has a new leaf though, so at least someone in this apartment is producing.

Monday rain in Curitiba, the kind that makes the república bathroom smell like wet wood. I took the Interbairros bus and the parrot man wasn't there, so I drew an empty seat with a green feather on it. Nobody asked who it was for. I like that.
Monday. The Interbairros was late and I drew Seu Ivo's parrot on the back of an old printout, just for practice. It didn't come out right, but the driver saw it and smiled. That was enough.

Portuguese diary entry: Hoje o céu de Curitiba estava cor de café com leite e eu pensei que isso é um clichê que eu aceito. O ônibus atrasou, desenhei duas pessoas conversando sem áudio, como sempre. Limonada tem uma folha nova. Pequenas coisas. Acho que é isso que importa.
The bus driver braked so hard my Álgebra notes flew into the seat behind me. The woman there handed them back without looking up. Monday.

First Monday of the year and I already forgot my umbrella on the bus. The woman next to me loaned hers and said 'guarda que eu sei onde você mora', which is either kind or threatening. I walked home with it dripping on my hair. Returned it to the company's lost and found tomorrow. Maybe.
Bia, you moved to Florianópolis in my head three years early and I'm already jealous of your future window. If you're reading this in 2020, save me the room facing the sea. I'm serious.

Cold Curitiba morning. Limonada is on the windowsill with twelve leaves now and a slight lean toward the glass, like she's trying to overhear the street. I watered her with the last sip of my coffee. The drawing above my bed is still the sea. Future me, if it's not, please put it back.
The old man with the parrot wasn't on the bus today and I stared at his empty seat like it owed me something. I drew him from memory and missed a stop.

Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He tuned the violão and handed it to me without saying anything. I played the first three chords of 'Asa Branca' and stopped, embarrassed. He said 'one more year'. It has been one more year for four years now.
I tried to read calculus notes on the bus and fell asleep on page three. The parrot man looked concerned.
Found an old notebook from UTFPR with a drawing of the sea in the margin. I still can't swim but I can draw waves better now. Progress is lopsided. Life is lopsided.
Limonada lost a leaf in the cold and I panicked like a parent. She has seven again already. Rafa says I talk to the plant more than to him. He's not wrong.
Cláudio asked me to redraw the motor assembly diagram by hand again. My handwriting in engineering notation is still terrible, but he says it looks 'less dead' than CAD.

First week back at the factory. Cláudio asked me to redraw the assembly diagram because the lines were 'too emotional'. I didn't know lines could be emotional. He's right though. I traced them straighter and felt mildly insulted on behalf of the crooked ones.
Bus was late again, so I drew three strangers' shoes from memory while waiting. One was a pink croc with a sock. I liked it too much.
Bia, we should make a pact: whoever finds a job by the sea first has to send the other a photo every morning. I'm calling the photo 'prova de vida marítima'. Also you owe me a pastel from 2016 still.
Limonada has survived another winter on the windowsill. Seven leaves, very serious expression. I water her with the same mug I use for coffee, which feels illegal but she doesn't complain.
Rain all day. Limonada on the windowsill got too much water and looked dramatic about it. I dried the soil with paper towels like a worried mother. She survived. I did not get to the factory on time.

Got rained on halfway home from the factory and arrived with my shirt glued to my back. Dona Sandra from the canteen gave me a comadre-sized towel and refused to take it back. I owe her two pães de queijo.
Mãe, se você estiver lendo isso, obrigada pelos bolachas. As da marca nova estão melhores que as da antiga, mas não conte que eu disse isso.
Desenhei a mão do Cláudio segurando o parafuso hoje, só pra prática. Ficou parecendo um polvo simpático. Ele viu e não disse nada. Acho que ele acha que sou esquisita. Talvez seja verdade.

Portuguese diary entry: Rafa me ligou da Paulista. Ouvir a voz dele still dói um pouco, mas menos do que em outubro. Ele falou de trabalho e esqueceu de perguntar como eu estava. Anotei isso. Não por rancor. Por registro.

Bus 7am, Interbairros II. Seu Ivo's parrot said 'bom dia, Marina' today, or at least I choose to believe it was Marina. Drew them in my engineering notebook again. The professor saw and asked if it was a motor. I said yes. It was not.

Bus 7am. Saw an old man with a green parrot for the first time in a while and thought of Seu Ivo. Wrong parrot, wrong man, same feeling. Drew them in the notebook I keep in my bag now instead of my lap.
I counted the days since the breakup and stopped counting. That feels like progress.

Mom, if you're reading this: I found a drawing of the farm in my old sketchbook, the one from 2015. I didn't finish it because I didn't know what Coronel looked like. I still don't. That's the part that makes it yours, not mine.

Rafa called from São Paulo. He sounded tired in a way I recognize: too many buildings, not enough sky. We talked about nothing for an hour. I still haven't told him about the breakup capsule I wrote for 2019. Probably never will.
Rafa left a mug at my flat. I washed it and put it in the cupboard instead of giving it back. Small stupid thing. It says 'I love SP' and I might keep it as a warning sign.
Rain all afternoon and the república roof made that ticking sound. I missed class and finished a sketchbook page about the parrot man instead. Priorities.
Rain all week, the RU was serving that suspicious lasanha, and Cálculo exercises until my hand cramped. I drew Cláudio's motor during lunch anyway. It's the only time the factory feels like mine.
R$ 2.900 left after rent and the bus card. Not bad. Not good either. The lemon tree needs a bigger pot and I'm pretending that's the reason I'm not buying it yet.
Rafa brought pastel de palmito and we ate it on the bus bench at Passeio Público. He talked about São Paulo again. I talked about lemons. We are very good at talking past each other.
Bia me mandou áudio de cinco minutos chorando porque uma formiga morreu na comida dela. Eu ri e depois senti culpa. Mandei uma figurinha de formiga. Está tudo bem.
It rained all day and Limonada’s soil turned to mud. I moved her to the dry side of the windowsill and talked to her about it. She did not answer.

Rafa made pasta with the wrong pan and pretended it was intentional. I laughed so hard the neighbor knocked on the wall. We ate it with cheap wine and both agreed it was the best meal of the year. I'm writing this so I don't forget the quiet ones.
Went swimming at the indoor pool for the first time since 2015. Lasted six seconds floating. The lifeguard pretended not to notice. I'm counting that as progress.

Portuguese diary entry: Sonhei com o mar de novo, mas dessa vez o pé esquerdo entrou. Acordei com a panturrilha apertada e pensei: pelo menos mudou alguma coisa. Ainda não contei para ninguém. Alguns sonhos são privados até não serem mais.
Tomei chuva até a parada de ônibus e cheguei na fábrica pingando. O vigilante disse 'senhora, você quer um saco plástico?' e eu disse sim como se fosse a solução para tudo.

Rafa and I broke up last week. Nobody did anything wrong, we just want different cities: he wants São Paulo, I want the sea. I'm writing this so in a year you remember it was the right call even though it hurts now. I kept the playlist. I'm not ready to delete it.
Mãe, thank you for the printer, for the bolachas, for asking about the drawings even when you're pretending not to. I bought you another ream of paper. Don't tell me you don't use it.
Post-breakup Sunday. I cleaned the whole república, reorganized the fridge labels, and cried into a pão de queijo. Bia came over with chocolate and didn't try to fix anything. Good friend.
Post-breakup week. I keep opening the fridge and seeing his yogurt brand. I didn't buy it. I moved it to the back shelf and now I avoid the back shelf. Growth, apparently, has stages.
Bia, I found the old marker wall photo from São Francisco. We were so young. I'm keeping it in the sketchbook now, not on my phone.

Went to the pool with Bia because she said swimming is like riding a bike, and I said I don't know how to ride a bike either. She laughed so hard the lifeguard looked over. I did my usual four seconds of floating, panic, apology.
Tio Beto called to ask if I'm 'still dating the São Paulo boy'. I said I don't know yet. He said 'menina, you sound like someone deciding between two cities' and I hate that he was right.
Four years in the república today. The fridge still has names on the yogurt, but now one of them is Limonada's pot. Progress.
One month until the sea dream check-in. I keep forgetting to ask myself how I'm doing. The answer, I think, is: okay, but in a quieter way than before. Like a room with one less chair.
Bia, thanks for letting me cry on your shoulder and then stealing my fries. You are the worst best friend. Come over Saturday and bring the good vinho, I promise we will not talk about him.
I drew the factory gate while waiting for the bus after work. It looked less sad on paper. Maybe everything does.
A fábrica inventou um novo formulário de manutenção que ninguém entende. Desenhei um fluxograma com um peixinho no canto e a turma começou a usar o meu em vez do oficial. Pequena vitória.
Ate at the RU and drew the tray line in my notebook. Someone asked if I was an architecture student. I said 'sort of'.
Mãe, I finished the drawing of Vó Lúcia's kitchen and it's on my desk. If you read this later, I kept the bolo de fubá recipe taped to the back. I haven't dared to make it yet.

Portuguese diary entry: Na fábrica, Cláudio me chamou de 'engenheira que desenha'. Não sei se é elogio ou diagnóstico. Aceito os dois. Limonada tem quinze folhas e está mais alta que o pote. Mudança é devagar, mas é real.
Pastel de feira after work with Bia. We sat on the curb because the tables were full. Grease on my fingers, sun going down. For ten minutes I forgot about everything else. Small miracles.
Rafa's playlist still exists on my phone. I opened it, listened to one song, then closed it. Not yet.
Bia, thank you for not asking 'are you okay' every hour and for asking 'did you eat' instead. I ate. Twice. The second time was just bolacha with doce de leite standing up. That still counts.
Fev em Curitiba: o ônibus atrasou, choveu dentro do casaco, e o senhor do papagaio estava lá com uma bandagem nova. O papagaio não disse nada. Eu desenhei os dois assim mesmo, quietos.
Dreamed of the sea again. I put one foot in and the sand was cold. Woke up with my calves tight, but I think the dream is changing.
I tried to learn three chords on Tio Beto's violão and got two. The third sounds like a cat falling down stairs. I'll practice when nobody is home. So never.

Bus Interbairros, 7am. The parrot man wasn't there, but a woman in the back was knitting a tiny scarf, green, for what looked like a very small dog. I drew her hands. Felt like being back in the Interbairros strips, except real and therefore harder.
Therapy-ish: I bought a sketchbook with a blue cover and wrote 'not under the mattress anymore' on the first page. Small rebellions.
Went to Vó's on Sunday and she made bolo de fubá twice because the first one sank. She said the oven is to blame, not her. I believe her. We ate both.
Choveu a semana toda. Limonada está no meu quarto porque a janela do apê vaza. Ela não parece gostar de Curitiba, mas também ninguém pediu a opinião dela.
Bia, I know you already know, but here it is in writing: the breakup was not a failure. It was two people being honest in a kitchen. Please remember that if I forget.

Dreamed of the sea again. This time the water was warm and I put both feet in, but I stayed at the edge. There was a parrot on the fence behind me. I woke up and the taste in my mouth was salt, which is impossible and also very dramatic of my brain.
Money check: R$ 820 left, rent due tomorrow, I ate pasta with ketchup twice this week. It's fine. It's fine.
Sea dream again. This time I was waist-deep and the water was cold, not warm. Strange. I woke up missing Vó Lúcia's bolo de fubá more than anything else.
Limonada perdeu uma folha e eu entrei em pânico por vinte minutos até lembrar que planta faz isso. Ela tem seis folhas agora. Estou escrevendo para que eu não me esqueça de que seis é suficiente.
Tio, I still owe you 'Asa Branca'. I know. I'm not promising a date anymore, just that I'm still trying. The violão is in the corner and I look at it every morning.

Portuguese diary entry: quatro anos do meu pedido em 2014 sobre desenhar uma página por semana e aprender a nadar. Nadar ainda não. Desenhar sim, mas não toda semana. Acho que vou refazer a promessa. Só ajustar o prazo, não desistir.
Called Vó Lúcia and she told me about Coronel again, but this time she added that he used to steal eggs from the neighbor. Details accumulate. I'm writing them all down.
Vó Lúcia asked if I was eating enough. I said yes. I had eaten a pastel and three bolachas. Technically.
Seu Ivo e o Papagaio are still my favorite invented people. Juca would say something rude today. I wrote it and didn't post it.

The factory bathroom has a mirror that makes everyone look tired. I washed my face and thought about Rafa's playlist, then took it out of my phone and put it back in the same minute. Progress is ugly.

Mom called to ask if I'm 'eating properly'. I said yes. She said 'you always say yes'. She's right. I had rice and egg for lunch, which is proper enough. I also had three cookies before dinner, which I will not mention.
Money check: R$ 120 for the rest of March after bus, RU, and one emergency pastel. I'm very good at emergency pastéis. Need to stop being good at it.
Mom sent bolachas again. The box arrived crushed and I ate the broken ones first because they felt like they needed rescuing. I know. I know.

Mom, I know you think the factory is the safe choice. You're probably right. I just keep thinking about Cláudio asking for drawings during lunch. I wish you could see my face when someone asks me to draw.

Bia, if you're reading this, thank you for the voice message yesterday that was just you screaming 'MENINA DO MAR' for forty seconds. I played it four times. It helped more than I can explain. Also please stop calling me brave; I'm not, I just show up tired.

Bus was so full I had to hold onto the strap with two hands like a flag. A man offered me his seat and I almost cried, not from gratitude, from back pain. I accepted and then felt thirty years old at twenty-one.
Tried floating in the pool for thirty seconds. Panicked at twenty-nine, as usual. The lifeguard clapped anyway.
Mom called to ask if I'm eating enough. I said yes and then ate an entire package of bolacha Maria standing over the sink. The sink is not a table, Marina.
O Limonada soltou uma folha nova depois daquela noite fria. Trouxe ela para perto da mesa enquanto eu desenhava. Ela é teimosa, e isso me deixa feliz.
At the factory, Cláudio caught me sketching a motor during lunch again. He said 'at least this one has the right number of bolts'. Progress.
Same sea dream, but this time I put one foot in. Probably because of the breakup. The therapist I don't have yet would have something to say about that.
Failed the driving test again? No, I didn't even try. The Detran hill can live without me this semester. I walked home in the rain and felt oddly triumphant.

Bia, thank you for not making the breakup a thing. You just brought bolachas and said 'we're going to the sea this weekend, even if it's just to look at it'. We looked at it. I didn't go in. You didn't push.
April Fools: Cláudio asked me to redraw the assembly diagram 'funnier'. I gave the motor a smile. He left it in the file. I love this factory a little bit.
Dreamed of the sea again, but this time I only saw the edge from far away. No panic, just a far feeling. I wrote it down before breakfast.
Ate lunch at the RU with the girls from the república. We talked about Física 2 like it was a person who wronged us. I drew caricatures on napkins and Bia asked for the one of me panicking.
Money check: R$ 900 left and rent due in five days. I ate RU for lunch and dinner and called it a day of character building. The bolachas from Mom are gone. Again.
Vó Lúcia sent a voice message that was just her laughing at something on TV. Three minutes long. I listened twice.
Paguei o cartão de crédito com três dias de atraso e levei um susto que pensei ser ataque cardíaco. Era só culpa. Culpa também faz o coração bater rápido.
Tio Beto, I haven't practiced 'Asa Branca' this year yet, but I thought about it twice, which is more than last year. Next Sunday. I'm saying it out loud so it counts.

Limonada has nine leaves now and one of them is bent like a tiny ear. I moved her away from the window because the afternoon sun was too strong. She looks offended. Plants can look offended. I'm sure of it.
Money check: R$ 1.100 left, it's the 6th. The factory pays on the 5th but I forgot to move the money, so now I'm that person. Lunch was RU and an apple. Still, cheaper than crying in a restaurant.
Found the Álgebra notebook from 2014 with the parrot drawings in the margins. I'm better now, but they're sweeter.
Bia and I walked in the Passeio Público and talked about nothing important for two hours. The turtles were still there. I drew one badly and we laughed.
At lunch Cláudio explained gears with a napkin and a pen. I sketched it so well he kept it. He said 'you draw like someone who misses it'. I said I don't. We both knew I lied.
Mom, I printed one of the Interbairros strips on your printer today and put it on the fridge. You didn't say anything, but you didn't take it down either.
Trabalhei sábado na fábrica. Cláudio trouxe bolo de fubá e disse que era da mulher dele, mas tinha gosto de padaria. Eu comi dois pedaços e desenhei a forma. Pequenas alegrias, Marina.
Rain all day. The Interbairros was late and I missed my stop because I was drawing a wet dog on the sidewalk. I walked three blocks in the rain and didn't even mind.

Portuguese diary entry: Domingo na casa da Vó. Ela fez bolo de fubá e esqueceu o açúcar, ninguém disse nada até ela mesma falar. Depois ela riu e disse que o bolo era 'dieta de viúva'. Desenhei sua mão segurando a xícara. Mãos são difíceis, mas as dela são mais.
Found an old comic strip of Seu Ivo e o Papagaio in my drawer. I drew him with a mustache he didn't have. I think he'd have liked it. I hope he's okay in Ponta Grossa, if that's where he went.
Tio, I still haven't learned 'Asa Branca'. But I played the chorus today for Seu Ivo's parrot and Juca tilted his head. I'm counting it as progress.

Bia, você vai ler isso no futuro e lembrar que eu te liguei hoje às 2h da manhã dizendo que sonhei com um cachorro laranja que me pedia informações no centro. Você disse 'isso é seu cérebro pedindo férias'. Tinha razão.
Tio Beto, I practiced Asa Branca three times this week. Got to the second verse. Your turn to clap when I see you in June.

Vó Lúcia told me the Coronel story again, with a new detail: he used to bark at the rain before it started. I wrote it down. I'm going to draw the farm fence exactly crooked, the way she always says it was.
Tio Beto called just to ask if I had practiced Asa Branca. I said yes. I played the first three chords and stopped. He said 'one more year' without waiting to see if I'd continue. Automatic now.
Dream: sea again, but this time I had a swimsuit on and was just sitting at the edge with my feet in. Progress? I'll take it.
Painted a little lemon on the yogurt cup before I moved Limonada to the terracotta pot. Kept the cup. It has one water stain and my bad handwriting and I can't throw it away.

Tio Beto sent a voice message playing 'Asa Branca' on the violão with a wrong chord on purpose, I think, just to make me reply. I replied with a voice message of me humming the missing chord. He sent back seven laughing emojis. That's the whole conversation.
The factory coffee machine broke and everyone looked at me like I could fix it with engineering. I could not.
Bia dormiu no meu sofá e roncou alto o suficiente para acordar meu vizinho. Ofereci café no outro dia e ele aceitou. Amizade construída sobre ronco.
Called Vó Lúcia on Sunday. She told me the same story about Coronel, except this time the dog waits under a different tree. I wrote down both versions. I think the story is growing its own bark.
Limonada got a new leaf and it's brighter than the others, almost lemon yellow. I keep staring at it like it's a sign. It's probably just a leaf. But I'm keeping the optimism.
Money check: R$ 210 left, it's the 28th. Living on RU and Mom's bolachas again. Some things do not change. I wrote down the same panic in 2014 and it still sounds identical.
Money check: R$ 120 left and it's the 28th again. The universe is recycling jokes.
Limonada got a new pot today, terracotta, from the feira. She looks like she owns the place. I almost named her after Vó Lúcia but that felt like too much pressure for a plant.
I tried to cook feijão tropeiro from memory and it became a kind of soup. Ate it anyway. The kitchen looked like a crime scene but I didn't take a photo, so future me only has my word.
Found an old pastel de feira receipt in my jacket from when Rafa and I walked in Passeio Público. I almost threw it away. I didn't.

Holiday. The república is empty and too quiet. I cleaned the kitchen, which counts as a personality transplant. Limonada got a drop of water on one leaf and looked instantly happier. Maybe I should try that.
Bia, I dreamed of the sea again and put one foot in. I didn't wake up sad. I think that's new.
Bia, I found a lemon in the república kitchen and almost cried. It wasn't even mine. I miss you. Let's go to Matinhos soon, even if it's just for one weekend.
Went to the feira on Sunday and bought a cactus for R$ 8. Named it Curitiba. It looks tough and needs almost nothing, which is not me but I admire it.
Money check: rent paid, R$ 180 left, and the bus driver gave me change with a parrot sticker on the coin. I kept it in my wallet next to the photo of Limonada's first leaf.

Portuguese diary entry: Fui à feira e comprei limão. Plantei três sementes em copo de iogurte de novo, por nostalgia. As outras duas da turma não germinaram. Limonada é a única sobrevivente, a diva. Se alguma germinar, vou chamar de Sobrinha.
I saved 200 reais this month by not buying coffee outside. Then I spent it on a sketchbook with nice paper. Money is a river and I am a fish with poor impulse control.
Money check: R$ 280 left and it's the 9th. The RU queue was long so I ate a pão com mortadela on the bus. Two people looked at me. The parrot looked at me. Everyone judges, even birds.
Drew a motor assembly diagram at lunch and Cláudio said 'this is almost art'. Almost. I'm taking the almost.
Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He asked if I still play 'Asa Branca' and I said 'em partes'. He said parts are better than nothing. I believe him.
Desenhei o Seu Ivo de novo, dessa vez com o chapéu. O motorista da linha 402 me disse que o desenho ficou parecido. Fiquei feliz demais por isso.
Mother's Day lunch at Tio Beto's. Mom asked if I'm 'still with the factory thing'. I said yes. She said 'good, stable'. I said nothing. Growth, maybe.
Mother's Day. Mom pretended she didn't want flowers and then put them in the printer room where she could see them while printing my comics. I didn't say anything. She didn't either.
Domingo em Matinhos na casa da Vó. Ela me deu um casaco velho porque disse que eu estava com cara de quem sente frio. Eu estava com cara de quem dormiu quatro horas. Os dois não se excluem.

It rained so hard today that the street in front of the república turned into a small river. We threw paper boats from the window. One of them got stuck on a tire. A man fished it out and waved. Perfect afternoon.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time the water touched my ankles and stayed. I woke up with wet feet that were probably sweat, but I'm choosing to believe otherwise.
Four years since Bia's birthday wall. I walked past the bar in São Francisco today. The wall might have been painted, I couldn't tell. We were there anyway.

Fourth anniversary of seeing the parrot man. I thought about drawing him but didn't. Some days the drawing wants to happen and some days it doesn't; today it didn't. I let it not happen without making it a crisis. That might be progress.
Bia's birthday. We wrote our names on the bar wall again, next to the old marker. The paint is coming up. We are still here. That's the whole point.
Tio, hoje toquei a introdução de 'Asa Branca' sem errar. Só a introdução. Prometo não sumir com a promessa de novo.
Rafa texted to ask if I still have the playlist. I said yes. He said 'good'. That was the whole conversation and it didn't ruin my day. Noted.
Dreamed of the sea and this time the water was warm and I was already in it. I couldn't see anyone next to me, but I wasn't alone. Woke up happy, which is new.
Mom sent a voice message saying 'você viu o email da faculdade sobre o alumni?' I didn't. I never see emails. Sou arquiteta de planos e inimiga de inboxes.
Limonada is still a meter tall and still hasn't given a lemon. I talked to her while watering. Bia says she heard me. She's right, I was talking.
Sonhei com o mar de novo. Dessa vez eu estava sentada na areia com Vó Lúcia e ela me chamou de menina do mar. Acordei achando que ela tinha dito isso de verdade. Talvez tenha dito.
At the RU today the dessert was goiabada com queijo and I ate two. No regrets. Engineering remains the excuse.
Bus driver let Seu Ivo off at a different stop today because his knee was bad. Juca said 'obrigado'. I cried a little behind my notebook, normal.
Bia and I walked in São Francisco and found our names still on the bar wall, faded but there. She traced them with her finger. I didn't want to write over them.
Limonada has ten leaves now. I moved her closer to the window because the light changed with the cold. She leans toward the sun like she's listening to it.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time I didn't even try to enter, just sat on the sand with Vó Lúcia and ate goiaba. Progress? Maybe.
On the bus today a little girl drew on my notebook while I wasn't looking. A purple dog with wings. I didn't erase it. It lives in the margin of page 47 now and I like it more than anything I draw.
Mom sent a box with bolo de fubá and a note saying 'don't skip dinner'. There was also a new sketchbook. She didn't mention it, but I know her handwriting. I started drawing the farm dog on page one.
Tio Beto, I haven't practiced 'Asa Branca' since January. I'm writing this so you don't have to ask at Festa Junina. Please don't ask. I'll try to show up with bread at least.
The factory cafeteria changed the feijoada day and I felt personally attacked. Drew Cláudio's face at lunch. He didn't notice.
Cold enough for socks in the república. Limonada is inside again, wrapped in my old scarf. She has eight leaves and a lot of attitude.
Dreamed of Coronel, Vó Lúcia's dog. Not even my dog. He was waiting at a gate that wasn't ours. I woke up feeling like I had been somewhere very far away.
I spent an hour drawing motors instead of reviewing for the exam. I regret nothing except maybe the exam.
Bia, I wore the yellow dress today and it didn't feel like a costume. I walked to the bakery and back. That's the whole report. It was enough.
At the pool a child told me my freestyle looked like 'a fish having a problem'. She's not wrong. I laughed and she asked if I was okay. Crianças são juízes rigorosos.
Mom called to ask if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said yes. I lied. The sketchbook is no longer under the mattress; it lives in my backpack now, which is its own kind of bravery. I think.
Cálculo never came back, but the fear did in small ways. Today it was the job offer email. I stared at it for twenty minutes.
Rain all week in Curitiba. The lemon tree's leaves went glossy and ridiculous, like she's showing off. I repotted her with soil from the little garden by the building. She deserves nice dirt.
Started drawing tiny comics again after months. Not for posting, just for me. The first one is a motor with legs going to the bus. It made me laugh out loud on the 7am bus.
Worked late at the factory to finish the assembly diagrams. Cláudio brought me a pastel from the bar nearby and said 'engineers who draw should be paid double'. I said I'd settle for the pastel.
Bus comics people still message me asking for new strips. I tell them I'm busy with the factory. It's true. It's also not the whole truth. I don't know how to explain the rest.
The lemon tree has eight leaves and an attitude. I repotted her and she leaned to the left like she's judging me.
Rafa mandou mensagem perguntando se eu ainda tenho o mesmo número. Respondi sim. Ele mandou um emoji de coração. Fingi que não vi. Mentira, vi na hora.
Ate a pastel de feira alone in the Passeio Público and remembered the first date with Rafa. The pastel was better. That's not a nice thing to write, but it's true, and I'm not sorry.
Vó Lúcia called to say she saw a dog that looked like Coronel. She sounded happy. I drew it from her description and she corrected the ears three times.

Tio, estou escrevendo isso porque a Festa Junina está chegando e eu já sei que não vou tentar 'Asa Branca' este ano. Não quero fingir. Mas quero que você saiba que ainda treino em casa, às vezes, sem violão, só cantando. Promessa não morreu. Só atrasou. Um beijo.

Festa Junina isn't for two weeks but the whole neighborhood already smells like popcorn and wood smoke. Tio Beto texted 'violão waiting'. I didn't reply. I'm going. I'll probably not play. But I'm going.
Swimming lesson: I floated for eight whole seconds. Dona Cida wasn't there, it was a substitute, but I'm claiming the record anyway.
Factory barbecue. Cláudio told a story about a motor that screamed in the night and everyone laughed. I drew it later: the motor with a mouth. He wants it framed.
Cláudio asked for another assembly diagram. I drew the motor and then, in the corner, a tiny parrot. He didn't mention it. Good. That one is for me.

Mãe, thanks for the printer. I used it to print comics at 2am and the whole república now knows I draw. You still haven't said you like them, but I saw the one about Seu Ivo on your fridge. That's enough for today.
I burned rice for the first time in months and immediately called Vó Lúcia for instructions. She said 'fogo baixo, menina' as if I hadn't heard it a hundred times. Ela tem razão sempre.
It was cold enough for a scarf and I wrapped Limonada in it for the night. In the morning she had a new leaf. I'm taking credit.

Tio Beto, não toquei 'Asa Branca' e você nem perguntou. Isso foi pior. Prometo que no ano que vem eu pelo menos tento o primeiro verso sem parar. Se for mentira de novo, pode me cobrar na frente de todo mundo.
Curitiba cold in June. Limonada's leaves curled a little and I wrapped the pot in a scarf again, like last year. She survived a frost once, so I'm trusting her.
Festa Junina. Didn't even try 'Asa Branca'. Tio Beto didn't ask. That's worse than him asking.
Festa Junina was warm and loud and Tio Beto didn't ask me to play. He just handed me a plate of paçoca and sat next to me. Sometimes not asking is the kindest thing.
I bought a pair of swimming goggles and wore them around the apartment to 'get used to the feeling'. Bia called and I forgot I had them on. She said I looked like an accountant from the future.

Day after Festa Junina. Tio Beto didn't ask about 'Asa Branca'. The violão stayed in the corner. I helped wash dishes and cried a little into the towel, which is dramatic for someone who wasn't even asked.
It's winter and Curitiba is doing its usual grey. I wore two scarves and still my nose ran on the bus. The driver said 'boa noite' at 6pm, which made me laugh. Small city, big night.
Limonada survived a week without water because I forgot. Her leaves drooped and then came back after I apologized out loud. I am not joking. I apologized out loud to a lemon tree.
It's cold enough that Limonada stays inside wrapped in my scarf again. She doesn't fit the yogurt cup, but the habit remains.
World Cup in Russia. Brazil lost and I drew the living room faces instead of watching the second half. Tio Beto's frown is now immortalized in my sketchbook.
Festa Junina leftovers for three days. I ate bolo de milho for breakfast like it was a responsible choice. Tio Beto's violão is on the couch and nobody touched it. I don't want to ask why.
Went to the bookstore and spent 40 minutes touching covers without buying anything. The cashier looked at me like I was planning a heist. I bought a postcard of the sea instead.
Same sea dream, but the water smelled like lemon. I don't know what that means and I'm not going to overthink it.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I didn't touch the violão. He didn't ask. He just put extra feijão tropeiro on my plate, which is his version of saying something. I miss the asking anyway.

Cold snap. Limonada is inside, wrapped in my scarf again. She has twenty leaves now and a stubborn little branch that grows sideways, like she's trying to escape the cup. Eight leaves felt like a lot last year. Now it's a whole plant with opinions.
At the factory, a motor failed and I found the vibration issue before Cláudio did. He said 'engenheira' and I pretended not to be proud. I was very proud.
I found my old 'Interbairros' account on my phone and scrolled for twenty minutes. People still comment on Seu Ivo sometimes. I didn't post anything. I didn't delete it either.

Mãe, escrevi esta cápsula em português porque é você. Ví que você imprime meus quadrinhos. Não falamos disso. Mas eu vi. Obrigada. Também quero dizer que você tinha razão sobre o RU ser barato, mas errada sobre desenho ser hobby. Um dia vamos rir disso. Ou não. Tanto faz. Te amo.

Limonada got moved to a bigger pot by the girls at the república, who called it a 'ceremony'. She looked proud. Eight leaves. I drew her in the margin of a vibration report, which Cláudio didn't notice.
Bia, thank you for the birthday drawing of a lemon tree with a tiny swimmer underneath. It's on my wall next to the sea drawing from Vó Lúcia. Best wall in Curitiba.
Sunday. Called Vó Lúcia and she complained about the heat and then talked for forty minutes. I drew her feet in slippers while she talked. The drawing is bad but the slippers are right.
Vó Lúcia called and said the jabuticabeira is full this year. She described each branch like it was a person. I wrote it down because one day I want to draw all of them.

Drew a comic about the factory during lunch: a motor that sings when no one is looking. Cláudio saw it, didn't say anything, then left a drawing of a coffee cup on my desk with 'bom trabalho' written on it. I kept it.
A swimming pool at the club smelled like chlorine and regret. I did three laps badly and one decent one. The lifeguard gave me a thumbs up. I'm choosing to believe it wasn't pity.
On the Interbairros bus the parrot man waved at me like we were old friends. I waved back and almost missed my stop. A pequena comunidade do transporte público.
Bia, você não estava no churrasco mas sua mãe trouxe a maionese que você faz. Comemos e choramos um pouco. Saudade sua sem motivo.
Started drawing on the bus again, just quick little hands and umbrellas. Nobody looks twice. I missed this.
Factory lunch: I drew a diagram for the new line in five minutes and Cláudio said 'faster than CAD'. I'll take it. My hand hurts. CAD doesn't hurt. CAD also doesn't know what a motor sounds like.
I made bolo de fubá from Vó's recipe and it was a little dry. I ate three slices anyway. The next one will be better.
Went to Matinhos for the weekend with the girls from the república. I stood at the edge and didn't go in. The water was cold, that's my excuse. It's not the whole reason.
Drew Vó Lúcia's hands from memory while she talked on the phone. I think I got the way she holds the receiver too tight. She said 'you're quiet, menina, are you drawing again?' and I said no.
Tried to cook risoto for the girls and burned the bottom. They ate around the black part and said it was 'smoky'. I am keeping them. The pan is another story.
Bia sent a voice note that was just waves in the background and no words. I saved it.
Fui ao mar com a Bia. Não entrei. Fiquei com os pés na água e desenhei a linha do horizonte três vezes, porque a primeira não saiu direito. A terceira foi a que gostei.

Went to Matinhos with Mom for the weekend. I stood with my feet in the water at night and thought about 18-year-old me, who wanted the same thing and was too scared to go further. I'm still too scared. But the water was cold and I stayed.
Money check: paid the rent, bought groceries, and still have R$ 400. For 22-year-old me this is a festival. I'm not saying I'm rich, I'm saying I'm less panicked.
Sunday. Called Vó Lúcia. She pretended she wasn't waiting by the phone and then talked for forty minutes about a neighbor's cat. I love her.

Sunday. No Rafa text this morning, which is fine, but my phone felt heavy anyway. I called Vó Lúcia instead. She told me about the farm dog again. I listened like it was new. It mostly was, in the way she told it.
Hot day in Curitiba, which feels illegal. Bought an ice cream and walked to the bus stop. The parrot man's old seat is still empty. I ate the whole thing before the bus came. Productive afternoon.
Cláudio asked me to redraw a motor housing because mine was 'too artistic'. I removed one line and he said perfect. Art.
Dreamed I was in the bus and Seu Ivo's parrot turned into a tiny old man with a green coat. He said 'tchau, Marina'. I woke up and couldn't decide if that was sad or funny. Both, probably.
Comi um pastel de queijo tão bom na feira que esqueci de reclamar do preço. Isso é crescimento emocional ou fome? Ambos.
Ate a whole bolo de fubá alone because Mom sent it and it was too good to share. Escrevo isso para o futuro arrependimento, que virá em formato de estômago.
Vó called to tell me Coronel's story again. The dog walked ahead this time, not beside her, and waited at the gate 'with his tail like a flag'. New detail. I wrote it down.
Rafa sent a song on the playlist we used to share. I listened once, from the hallway, with the phone face down. It sounded like a window opening.
Vó Lúcia called me 'menina do mar' on the phone again. I still don't know if she means I belong by the sea or that I'm a dreamer. Maybe both.
Someone at the factory asked if I had a portfolio. I said no, then went home and opened the old Interbairros folder. Juca the parrot is still funny. I miss him a lot more than I admit.
Money check: R$ 1.200 left and it's the 5th. Living on RU again and pretending I'm not. The lemon tree got water first, which I think says everything.
It rained in Curitiba the way it only rains here, like the sky forgot something. I drew the street from the factory window while the machines were loud. The drawings looked angry. Maybe they were.

Portuguese diary entry: R$ 3.200 é o salário que vou receber se passar na entrevista da fábrica pós-formatura. Não sei se quero. Mas é dinheiro e dinheiro vira tempo e tempo vira desenho. A conta é feia, mas funciona.
Rain again. Limonada is inside, I am inside, everything is inside. Except the bus, which is late.
First day back at the factory after vacation. The machines sound louder than I remember. Or maybe I'm quieter. Drew a little sun on the corner of my notebook during a meeting. Nobody noticed. Good.
Limonada has thirteen leaves and a stem that leans toward the window like she's listening to something outside. I rotated the pot and she leaned back the same way. Stubborn. I respect her.
Tio Beto sent me a video of himself playing Asa Branca with a caption 'força, sobrinha'. I watched it five times. Didn't practice once. Working on it.
Bus 7am. The parrot man wasn't there again and I worried all day. He came back on Wednesday with a bandage and the parrot said 'bom dia' to the driver first, then to me. I'm counting it.
Mom, if you're reading this, yes I am eating vegetables, but I define 'vegetable' generously. Batata frita tem origem vegetal. Não me julgue.
I bought a second pot for Limonada and felt like I was expanding a kingdom.

Na fábrica, o café da máquina saiu aguado e eu desenhei a xícara como se ela estivesse triste. Cláudio viu e disse que minha xícara tem mais personalidade que o relatório. Eu vou tomar isso como elogio.
Bia called to say she saw a man with a parrot in São Francisco and thought of me. She didn't even ask if it was Seu Ivo. She just said 'your people are everywhere'. I liked that.
Interbairros II, 7am. No parrot man. I still look for him even now. A teenager with a headphones had a parrot keychain and I stared too long. He moved seats.
Money check: got paid a little extra for helping with a motor diagram. Bought myself an iced coffee and felt rich for ten minutes.
Interbairros is back online, just one strip. 'Seu Ivo e o Papagaio' waiting for the bus. 40 likes, all from people I know. That's fine. It's mine again.
Passed a weekend in Matinhos with Bia's family. Stood with my feet in the water at night. Didn't go in. One foot though, one foot was enough for now.
Money check: first salary month, sort of. R$ 1.200 from the internship stipend, minus rent, minus bus, minus the pastel I bought for Rafa because I missed him. Still not enough. Still here.
I tried to swim 10 meters and stopped at 8. The pool man said 'good'. I said 'almost'. He said 'almost is also a number'. Ele deve ser poeta.

Bus 7am, Interbairros II. A woman got on with a caged canário and sat where the parrot man used to sit. The canário didn't say bom dia. I drew them anyway, because some mornings you just need to draw something leaving a cage.
Money check: first salary of R$ 3.800 went to rent, food, and a printer for Mom. She called to say it prints crooked. I said 'that's character'. She said 'that's a defect'. We both laughed.
Rafa got the São Paulo offer. He called to tell me. I said 'congratulations' and meant it. Then I drew the bus stop alone and it looked a little empty. Normal.
I tried to learn one more verse of Asa Branca tonight. Got stuck on 'longe vai o meu sertão'. It's a sad song when you're already sad. I closed the violão.
Mom called and asked if I had 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said no. She went quiet. Then she said 'good'. I almost dropped the phone.
Cláudio asked why I always draw people's hands. I said they're hard. He said 'you like hard things, that's why you're an engineer'. He thinks he's a philosopher. Ele não é. Mas gostei da resposta.
Drew Vó Lúcia from memory and got her glasses wrong. She doesn't wear glasses. My memory is a liar with good intentions.
Mom called to say she saw my old bus comic saved on her phone. She didn't comment. She just sent it again, as if checking it still existed.

First salary month minus rent minus bus minus food equals R$ 240. I wrote it down to remember being dramatic about it later. The RU pastel is still R$ 4,50 and still the best investment I make weekly.
Limonada got a new leaf after I moved her to a bigger pot. She looks taller than me in the right light.
At the factory, a motor vibrated wrong and I knew before the instruments confirmed it. Cláudio said 'you have an ear'. I said 'I have a pencil'. He laughed, then asked if I could draw the fault.
Mom asked if I'm 'still at that factory'. I said yes. She said 'for how long'. I said 'two years'. She laughed. I don't know if she believed me.

Started keeping a small notebook in my work bag, not for reports. Just drawings of things that happen at the factory: gloves, coffee cups, Cláudio's hands. Mom says I should stop 'wasting paper'. I think she means the opposite.
Hot afternoon. I drew Limonada on the windowsill with the sun behind her and the shadow of the leaves on the wall looked like the sea. I'm keeping the sketch. Some days the apartment is enough ocean.
O Papagaio Juca disse 'bom dia, motorista' e depois, eu juro, olhou pra mim. Seu Ivo riu sem som. Desenhei tudo.
Bia, you said the sea would fix everything. I don't think it fixes, but it helps me forget to check his Instagram for whole hours.
Graduation planning: bought a cheap hat bigger than my head by accident. Mom said it makes me look like Vó Lúcia. I'm keeping it.
Read about Florianópolis at lunch and didn't tell anyone. Just saved three photos of balconies facing the sea and closed the tab before anyone could see.

Portuguese diary entry: Menina do mar não é apelido que eu escolhi, mas é um que vou guardar. A Vó não disse isso hoje, mas disse 'você tem cara de quem fica olhando a janela'. Ela conhece mais de mim do que eu aceito às vezes.
Vó Lúcia asked on the phone if I still draw. I said ' às vezes'. She said 'menina do mar desenha'. Não sei se ela sabe que isso virou meu apelido favorito.

Walking home from the bus, I saw a lemon tree on a sidewalk in Bigorrilho, loaded. I stood there for five minutes. Nobody asks a woman why she's staring at a lemon tree, but I'm sure I looked like I was having a moment.
Drew Vó Lúcia's hands while she was talking on the phone. She noticed and said 'at least draw them younger'. I love that woman. I will draw her hands old forever.

At Vó Lúcia's, she made me drive her to the pharmacy and back. She held the dashboard the whole time and said nothing. At the door she said 'you drive like a maniac' and then 'thank you'. I'm framing the thank you.
Called Vó and she told me the farm dog story again. Coronel gets braver every time. I wrote down version four.
The swimming pool smelled like chlorine and someone's shampoo. I stayed for twenty minutes and didn't drown. Growth.
Worked late at the factory and drew a comic on a napkin about a motor that wants to be a boat. Thaís would say it's 'less technical'. I liked it.
The factory hired a new intern who asked if I was an artist or an engineer. I said 'both, badly'. He laughed. I went home and drew a panel about it for no reason.
I visited Vó Lúcia in Irati. She made bolo de fubá and told the Coronel story again. I didn't interrupt. Some stories are better when you let them choose their own shape.
Cláudio brought me a drawing compass and said 'you'll need it someday'. He's retiring next year, or so he says. I don't believe him. Ele parece imortal.
The senior engineer retired and left his old compass on my desk with a note: 'for the drafts you actually like'. I use it for drawings of Limonada. He doesn't know that. Or maybe he does.
Seu Ivo brought a tiny umbrella for Juca. The parrot refused to use it. I respect that.
Dreamed of the sea again. I put both feet in this time. The water was warm and there was no one else. I woke up with my calves tight, but also with a strange calm. Maybe that counts.
Cláudio saw me sketching during lunch and said I should put my drawings next to the technical ones. I said I'd think about it. I'm thinking.
Mom, I used the printer today to print two Interbairros strips for the fridge. You'll probably say nothing and then quietly move them to the better side. I see you. Thank you for seeing me first.
Bia me mandou mensagem: 'desenhou hoje?' Respondi que não. Ela mandou um emoji de peixe. Eu entendi. Desenhei um peixe depois, às 23h, em cima do relatório de vibração.
Bia and I tried to cook bolo de fubá from Vó's recipe. It came out dense and yellow and wrong. We ate it all anyway. Next time.
Called Vó Lúcia on Sunday and she told the Coronel story again, the farm dog in Irati who waited at the gate. I wrote it down this time. She said 'why are you writing it?' and I said 'for practice'.

Bia, I paid Mom back the R$ 600 from the dentist. She refused, so I bought her a printer. She uses it to print my old comics. She hasn't said that, your mom told me. I'm writing this down before I forget it.
Rain all weekend, so I stayed in and drew six pages of nonsense. One of them is a lemon with a face. I named him Limão. Limonada vai ficar com ciúmes.
Applied for a minor drawing elective at UTFPR even though I'm almost done. The professor looked at my comics and said 'you should have done this from the start'. I nodded like an idiot.

Tomorrow is my first salary. I already know I'm paying Mom back the dentist money and buying her something she'll pretend to hate. I'm writing this tonight because future me should remember how nervous spending money on love makes me.

Money check: first salary. R$ 3.800. I paid Mom back the R$ 600 from the dentist in 2015 and she refused, so I bought her a printer. She uses it to print my comics. She hasn't said that, Bia's mom told me.
First salary arrived and I stared at the bank app for five minutes like it was a magic trick. Then I paid the phone bill.
Vó got a cold and called me three times to say she was dying. Then she made coffee and forgot to call back. I went anyway. She was fine. I was not.

Bus 7am. Seu Ivo had a bandage on his hand again. Juca said 'bom dia' to the whole bus. The woman beside me smiled. I drew it in five seconds, which is not art, but it is evidence that the morning happened.
The therapist I don't have yet would say I'm doing too much. I agree. The factory, the drawings, the calls, the bus comics in my head. But most of it feels like breathing, so I don't stop.
First salary month feels strange and good. Paid Mom back the dentist money; she said no. I bought her a printer because she prints everything, including my comics, apparently.
Printed the assembly diagrams on the office printer and one came out with a tiny sun in the corner. Nobody noticed except me. I kept it.
Sea dream. I put both feet in. The water was warm and my calves didn't tighten. I woke up and checked my legs like an idiot. They were fine.
Went to Bia's birthday dinner. Her cousin asked what I do and I said 'engineer' because it's shorter than 'engineer who secretly draws comics about buses'. Nobody asked for the long version. Good.
Ate a lemon from the market and remembered the yogurt cup in the república. I'm not planting seeds this time. Okay, maybe one.
Bought Mom a printer. She printed an Interbairros strip and put it on the fridge. I found out because Bia's mom sent me a photo. Mom said 'it was just to test the machine'. The machine works.

Limonada is taller than the windowsill now. I had to move her to the floor. She leans toward the window like she's listening for the sea. We have that in common, which is ridiculous, because she's a plant.
Swimming: floated for twelve seconds and didn't panic. Then panicked immediately after. The pool guy said 'muito bom'. I'll take it.
Money check: first month with a little left over. Not savings, not yet, but enough that I didn't eat RU all week. I bought a sketchbook instead of dinner one night and I'm not sorry.
Drew the assembly diagram all afternoon. By dinner, my hand hurt and I didn't care. It's the best feeling I've had in months.

Portuguese diary entry: Nadei hoje? Não. Mas comprei uma touca de piscina na promoção e isso já é intenção. A moça da loja perguntou se eu era atleta. Disse que era engenheira. Ela não entendeu. Nem eu.
Mãe, comprei a impressora. Ela imprime melhor que a do Tio Beto. Não diga que eu disse isso pra ele.
Money check: depois do salário, paguei a mãe, comprei a impressora, e ainda sobrou o suficiente para um pastel e um caderno novo. O caderno é para desenhos, não para cálculo. Crescimento.
Chamei a Vó no domingo como sempre. Ela falou do Coronel, do jabuticabeiro, do frio em Irati. Disse que estou desenhando bem. Ela não vê, mas eu desenhei o que ela disse.
The lemon tree got one new leaf this month. Just one. Very modest. I respect her pace. Sometimes I wish I had her confidence about growing slowly.

Vó Lúcia told me she used to swim in the river near Irati with Coronel sitting on the bank, 'like a very serious lifeguard'. I drew it immediately. She said I made Coronel too fat. I said 'he was happy'. She didn't argue.
Drew Limonada with a tiny smiley face in the pot. She still has no lemons but she has character. Mom said the drawing looks like a real lemon tree. Best compliment week.
Rafa texted to ask if I still have the playlist. I said yes before I could think about it. Then I put the phone down and drew for an hour, which felt like cheating but also like surviving.
A woman at the bus stop asked if I was the one who drew Interbairros. I said I used to. She said 'my son loved Seu Ivo'. I didn't correct her about the name.
I tried to float for forty seconds today. Panic came at thirty-five, but I stayed. Dona Cida, wherever you are, thank you.
Achei uma foto minha com Rafa de 2015 no armário. Ele estava sorrindo muito. Guardei de novo. Não por amor, por registro histórico. Sou arqueóloga da minha própria vida.
Payday. R$ 3.800 felt enormous and then I paid rent, bought Vó a printer ink, and ate a good pastel. Still felt enormous. I'm keeping the receipt. Proof I survived.
Called Vó Lúcia and she told me about the farm again. This time Coronel was 'the color of jabuticaba'. I don't know if that's a color. I want to draw it before I forget how she said it.
The bus driver said good morning to me by name today. I'm not sure if that's comforting or alarming.
Bia's birthday. We wrote our names on a bar wall again, this time in Santa Felicidade. Smaller bar, worse marker. We were there anyway. I drew us before the ink dried.
Tio Beto said 'one more year' again at Sunday lunch, out of nowhere, about 'Asa Branca'. I said 'one more year' back. We both knew what it meant.
Rain again. I stayed in the república and sketched Limonada leaf by leaf. She is patient. I am not, but drawing her makes me slower.
I drew Vó Lúcia's hands from memory while waiting for the bus. They were wrong. I kept the drawing anyway.
At the factory, Cláudio retired? No, not yet, but he brought bolo and said 'one more year'. I ate two slices and drew the cake on a napkin. Some things are worth recording badly.
First Halloween party at the república. I drew everyone's costumes instead of dancing. Someone asked for a portrait and I charged R$ 5. I'm an entrepreneur now.
Cláudio asked me to redraw a diagram 'less ugly'. I asked if that was a professional term. He said yes. I redrew it. It is now less ugly. Career milestone.
It's getting warmer and the lemon tree has buds. I don't know if that's normal for November, but I'm treating it like a holiday. Bia says I talk about Limonada like a pet. She's not wrong.
Sunday call with Vó Lúcia: she told me about the jabuticabeira and Coronel one more time. I wrote down that he had one floppy ear. New detail. I'm keeping a list now.
Sunday dinner at Tio Beto's. He didn't hand me the violão and didn't ask. I sat next to him and peeled potatoes, which is a different kind of music but still counts.
Money check: R$ 400 before rent. Ate RU and pretended it was a choice. Bought lemons anyway. Some expenses are not expenses.

Portuguese diary entry: Domingo sem ligação da Vó porque ela foi viajar com a igreja. Liguei duas vezes mesmo assim. A segunda ela atendeu e disse 'você é insistente, menina'. Ri sozinha no ônibus. O papagaio também disse bom dia.
Mãe, a impressora já imprimiu três tiras dos quadrinhos. Você disse que foi 'sem querer'. Eu sei.
Limonada dropped one leaf and I panicked like it was a family emergency. Bia reminded me she is a plant and plants do that. I put her closer to the window and whispered 'sorry'.

I tried to float in the bathtub again. Lasted six seconds. The water was cold and my knees betrayed me. Still, six is more than four. I'm keeping count. Dona Cida doesn't exist yet, but I think she'd be proud.
Bad day at the factory. The motor made a sound nobody could fix and I sat in the car afterward drawing the sound as a monster. It helped.

Bia and I shared a pizza and talked about São Paulo, Floripa, Curitiba, as if choosing a city were choosing a person. She said Floripa smells like vacation. I said Curitiba smells like rain. We both ordered another slice.
Put a little note in Limonada's pot: 'two years by the sea'. Not sure if plant or promise. Both, maybe.
Drew Limonada from below, looking up at her leaves. She's taller than the windowsill now. Eight leaves, no lemons, still mine.
The lemon tree on the windowsill has a new leaf, small and pale. I put a little stick next to it for support. It didn't ask for one, but neither did I.

Parrot man was on the bus today with a new bandage and the parrot said 'bom dia' to the whole bus. I drew it in the margin of my notebook, which is getting crowded. Engineering has become a sketchbook with math in it.
Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He didn't mention 'Asa Branca'. Neither did I. We ate rice and beans in suspicious silence.
Drew a small comic about the factory, the motor as a grumpy animal. Cláudio laughed and said keep it.
Started sketching on the bus again. Not comics, just faces and hands. A woman noticed and asked if I was an artist. I said 'engineer'. She looked disappointed. I understood her.
Dreamed I was swimming with Vó Lúcia. She was faster than me, which is absurd, because she can't swim. In the dream she laughed like stairs. I woke up happy, which is rare for a dream about water.
Limonada has ten leaves now and still no lemons. I tell her she's taking her time. She doesn't answer, which is probably for the best.
Sunday. I called Vó Lúcia and she asked if I was eating enough. I said yes. We both knew I was lying. She mailed me pão de queijo without saying anything. It arrived still warm, somehow.
I finished a drawing of the parrot man and didn't post it anywhere. Some things are just for me now. Growing up, I guess.

Bia, you asked if I still draw. I showed you the notebook and you got quiet, which is your version of a hug. Then you said 'Marina, this is real'. I didn't know what to do with that, so I drew you looking serious with a cookie.
Mom, I fixed your printer today. You printed a comic about Seu Ivo and the parrot. You said nothing. The fridge has it now.
Bia and I ate pastel at the feira and talked about nothing important. She said my drawing of the parrot man should be in a book. I laughed. She didn't. I'm writing it down in case she was right.
Graduation countdown: four weeks. I'm not nervous about the ceremony, I'm nervous about the part after, when everyone asks 'and now?'
A Limonada deu flor. Minúscula, quase invisível. Eu fiquei dez minutos olhando para ela no parapeito, como se estivesse esperando por isso a vida toda. Talvez estivesse.
Dreamed about the república's bathroom queue. Four girls, one mirror, someone knocking. I woke up and missed them, which is strange because I did not miss them at the time.
Mom sent a screenshot of one of my bus comics to the family group with no comment. Tio Beto replied with a thumbs up. That's the family review. I'm counting it as four stars.

Therapy is not happening yet, but I bought a notebook and wrote 'coisas que não digo' on the cover. First entry: I don't want to work in a factory forever. Second: I still check if Rafa's playlist is there. It is.
It was so hot the bus windows stuck. Juca fanned himself with one wing. Seu Ivo looked proud.
Another late night at the factory. I ate RU leftovers at my desk and drew a motor that looked like a tired cat. My supervisor walked by, said 'nice cat', and kept going. Best review of the year.
Money check: R$ 1.200 saved. I named the account 'MAR' in the bank app. It's small, but it's the first thing I've saved for myself instead of paying back someone else. Feels like a tiny boat.
Graduation photos today. I wore the wrong shoes and smiled with my whole face. Vó Lúcia approved on the phone, which is rare.
Cold outside, warm inside the república. I made a terrible instant soup and ate it watching the frost on the window. Limonada survived by being inside. I survived by being stubborn. Same strategy.
Bia, if I cry at my own graduation, tell everyone it's allergies. Also, if Vó wears the big hat, take a photo from behind so she thinks it's a normal picture. I want to draw it later.
Bus 7am, Seu Ivo had a new parrot? No, same Juca, new tiny hat. I drew it immediately. The Interbairros page got 120 likes. Small universe, mine.

Bia's mom told me my mom prints my comics and keeps them in a folder. I asked my mom about it and she said 'the printer came with paper, what else was I supposed to do'. I cried in the bathroom for three minutes.
Graduation is close. I bought a dress that Mom says makes me look 'responsible'. I think she means old. Vó Lúcia is coming. She already bought a hat.
Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He asked if I still play. I said 'não'. He said 'one more year' anyway, automatic, like a prayer. Eu ri e joguei a colher na salada sem querer.
Bia, if you ever read this: I walked past the bar in São Francisco and our names are still on the wall. Faded, but there.
The sea dream changed a little: I was already in the water, not at the edge. I didn't swim, I just stood there, and it was warm. I woke up and my calves weren't tight. First time.
Graduation is in two weeks. I tried on the hat and it made my ears stick out. Vó Lúcia said I look like a bishop. I don't know if that's a compliment, but I'm keeping it.

Portuguese diary entry: Faltam doze dias para a formatura. A Vó já comprou chapéu. A Mom já comprou vestido. Eu comprei só coragem, e olha, foi barato. Escrevo aqui para lembrar que mesmo tendo medo, fui. Sempre fui.
I swam one lap at the pool and panicked halfway, but I kept going. Not elegant. Still counts, I think.
Bia and I wrapped presents at her house. She said 'you'll live by the sea, Marina, I know it'. I said 'shut up and pass the tape'. I didn't shut up, but I thought about it for days.

First cold morning of December. Limonada came inside wearing my scarf again. I made coffee and drew her silhouette against the window. The drawing looks like a person standing alone, which is probably not about the plant.
Limonada survived another cold week. Eight leaves, maybe nine. I wrapped the pot in my scarf and felt ridiculous and right.
Final exam week. I studied with a pastel in one hand and a highlighter in the other. The pastel won. I think I passed. I think.
Limonada got a tiny white flower and I took a photo like a proud mother. No lemons yet, but she's trying.
Vó Lúcia asked if I still dream of the sea. I said yes. She said 'um dia você entra'. I wrote that down too.
Packed my room at the república. The drawing of the sea Vó Lúcia framed for me is still above the bed. I took it down carefully. My room smells like old wood again, which means it remembers me.
Vó Lúcia will come to graduation with that hat. I can already see it. I'm drawing it now so I don't forget.
Limonada has flowers! Small, white, smell incredible. No lemons yet, but flowers count. I put her closer to the window and told her she's doing great. Yes, I talk to my plant. No, I won't stop.

Two weeks until graduation. My hands smell like pencil all the time now. I keep thinking about Vó Lúcia saying 'menina do mar', which I don't think she ever said to me, but Mom might have heard it differently. I'm holding onto it anyway.
Vó said she's buying a hat for graduation. I asked which color. She said 'the biggest one'. No further questions.
Mom, I kept the sketchbook out in the open today. You saw it. Neither of us said anything. That's fine.
Final week of classes. The república fridge has my name on a yogurt and a drawing of a lemon. Limonada is on the windowsill, eight leaves, one bud I refuse to jinx.
Limonada is coming with me to the new place, obviously. The girls gave her a goodbye party with bolachas. She looked indifferent, as she should.
Graduation in four days and I'm terrified. Vó Lúcia is coming with a hat bigger than her. I hope she claps at my name. Even if she doesn't, I hope she's there.
Tio Beto asked if I would play Asa Branca at the family Christmas. I said maybe. He said 'maybe is better than no'. I think he's lowering the bar on purpose.
Graduation ceremony rehearsal. My cap kept sliding over my eyes. Vó Lúcia will find this hilarious.

Last day before the holidays and I stayed late fixing a report nobody will read. At least the graphs are beautiful. I am becoming the kind of person who makes beautiful graphs. Isso é triste ou admirável?
Mom, I said yes to the factory offer. I know you wanted me to say yes. I know I said two years. I'm writing it down again so you can hold me to it, and so I can't quietly pretend I didn't.

Mom, I'm graduating on Thursday and I'm scared. Not of the ceremony. Of the part after. You said drawing wasn't a job, and now I have a job drawing diagrams. I think we're both surprised. I love you. Bring tissues.
Tomorrow I graduate. Tonight I ironed my shirt and tried to draw the sea dream. It came out wrong, as always. The water looks like curtains. Still, I kept it. Twenty-two-year-old me made it this far.

Graduated! Vó Lúcia came to the ceremony with a hat bigger than her and clapped at the wrong name twice. Got a job offer from the same factory. I said yes. I keep telling myself it's for two years, then I go somewhere by the sea. Writing it here so it becomes a promise: two years, Marina.
Graduated. Vó Lúcia clapped at the wrong name twice and didn't care. She held my hand after and her hands were warm this time. I want to remember that too.
Graduation day. Vó Lúcia clapped at the wrong name twice and I loved her more for it. I kept her hand in mine while we walked out. Her hands were warm.
Mom, thank you for the printer. I know you said it was for documents. I saw the comics in the tray. You don't have to say it.

Véspera de Natal na casa da Vó. Ela fez bolo de fubá e me chamou de menina do mar na frente de todo mundo. Eu não sabia que ela dizia isso para os outros também. Guardei a frase como se fosse uma chave.

Portuguese diary entry: Natal na república com as meninas. Cada uma trouxe um prato que falhou de um jeito diferente. Rimos. Limonada ganhou uma bolinha de Natal improvisada com papel aluminio. Ela não reclamou. Boa menina.
Christmas at Vó's. She asked about Rafa and I said we broke up. She said 'menina do mar doesn't stay inland'. I didn't know what to do with that, so I drew her hands instead.
Vó Lúcia stayed awake until midnight and held my hand. Her hands were warm this time. I wrote down the exact sound of her laugh: high, then falling like stairs. I don't want to forget how it starts.
Tio Beto played Asa Branca after dinner without asking anyone. I didn't sing. I watched his hands instead. One day I'll have hands like that.
Tio Beto, I tried 'Asa Branca' alone in my room today and got to the second verse before collapsing into laughter. One more year. I know, I know. But I think this is the year I mean it.

Money check: first real salary at the factory. R$ 3.800. I paid Mom back the dentist money from 2015 and she refused, so I bought her a printer. She uses it for my comics. Bia's mom told me. I'm keeping the secret.
I opened the 2014 capsule about the sea dream today, the one asking if it changed. It changed a little. I put both feet in now. Future me, keep going.

Portuguese diary entry: Últimos dias de 2018. Resumo: trabalhei, desenhei pouco, chorei um pouco, ri muito. Limonada cresceu. A Vó ligou. A Mom imprimiu. Rafa foi. Tudo segue. Não é pouco. É só humano.
Bia, if you're reading this in 2020, I still haven't gone to Floripa and I'm still jealous of your window. I'll visit soon. I promise I'll draw your kitchen and not just look at the sea.
Bia, I know 2019 is going to be weird and good and hard. I can feel it. Come to Curitiba before February. I want to show you Limonada's new leaf.

Last day of the year. The república is quiet and Limonada is by the window with her white flowers. I stood with my feet in the cold water of the shower and pretended it was the sea. It wasn't. But it was close enough for tonight.

First workday of the year at the factory. The coffee machine still makes a noise like a small animal in pain. I drew it during lunch and labeled it 'trabalhador temporário'. Cláudio laughed and asked if I could draw the new motor too. Small victories.

January in Curitiba: sun at 7am, rain at 10, sun again at 3. I wore three different outfits and still carried an umbrella. Limonada got a few drops on her leaves and looked offended. The bus was late, as always, and I drew a man holding a bag of pão de queijo like it was a baby.

Found a pastel de feira cart at the 8am stop near the factory and ate it standing in the rain. The dough tasted exactly like the one Rafa bought me after I failed Cálculo. I almost texted him about it. Didn't. The rain was enough.

Curitiba woke up grey again and the kitchen window had that little drip I keep forgetting to report to the landlord. I drew it as a sad watercolor drop on my napkin before work. Cláudio saw it and said 'is that a metaphor?' I said it's a leak. It was both.

Monday at CIC, the machine vibration was off by 0.3 and Cláudio looked at me like I had personally insulted the motor. I fixed it, then drew the waveform in my notebook because it looked like a little storm. The men on the floor pretend they don't know I draw. One of them asked if the storm was for sale. I said maybe. He said 'quanto?'. I don't know what a machine storm costs.

Limão (Limonada) has 11 leaves today and one bent like it's looking at the street. I watered her, checked the soil like Vó taught me, and then remembered Vó's hands smelled like earth even after she washed them. Small thought for a Monday.

First Monday back at the factory after the holidays. The motor on line 3 makes a sound like a cat arguing, and Cláudio says that's normal. I believe him because he's 58 and never wrong about motors. I brought a sandwich and ate it on the loading dock. It started raining and I didn't move. Good afternoon, future me.

First salary of the year and I already bought a new sketchbook. It's thinner than the old one, so maybe I'll actually finish it. Limonada has nine leaves now and one is growing in a weird direction, like she's reaching for the window. I moved her two inches closer to the light. I don't know if plants count as having moods, but she looks offended when I forget.

Back at the factory after holidays. The coffee machine still makes that sad noise before heating up. I drew a tiny steam cloud in my notebook during the 7am stand-up. Cláudio didn't notice. Two years, Marina. The clock is ticking, but the coffee is terrible.

First Monday back at the factory after New Year. Cláudio brought back caju juice for the whole team and I spilled a little on the assembly report. He said a report with a juice stain is 'sincere'. I'm framing that as a compliment.
Sexta-feira à noite, cozinha da república. Cozinhei arroz com feijão e tostei pão velho no forno. Comi vendo a chuva. Pequeno, bobo, suficiente.

Morning fog, the kind that makes the city look like a pencil sketch with no lines. I drew it on the bus with a blue pen and the driver said 'artista?' I said 'engenheira.' He said 'same thing.' Maybe.
Limonada is three years old, has eleven leaves, and still zero lemons. I don't care. She survived a frost, a move, and my watering schedule. She's the bravest thing in this apartment.

Portuguese? No, this is English. Just checking: Vó Lúcia's hands were warm today when she held mine. Wait, that's in the future. No. Today she held my hand and said 'you're too skinny, menina'. I am not too skinny. But I drew her hands anyway, with the rings she wears even to wash dishes. Warm.

Domingo de chuva e eu desenhei três quadrinhos sobre o busão 7h. A Juca apareceu de guarda-chuva e isso me pareceu verdade, mesmo que invenção. Vó Lúcia ligou e falou por uma hora sobre o Coronel, como sempre. Prometi desenhar o cachorro um dia. Ainda não consegui. Mas prometi.
Rain all day, the bus fogged up and everyone drew little faces on the windows. I drew Juca on mine and wiped it before anyone could see. Seu Ivo would have laughed.

Rain all day, the bus was late and I got to the factory with my hair stuck to my face. The parrot man wasn't there either, which made the morning feel incomplete. I ate my RU rice cold at 11 and drew a bird on the napkin. Juca, not the real parrot. Or maybe both.
O ônibus das 7h veio cheio e eu desenhei a mão de uma senhora segurando o corrimão. Ela nem viu. Ficou parecendo uma árvore. Gostei tanto que não vou corrigir.
Bus 7am, Interbairros II. Seu Ivo's parrot said 'bom dia' to the driver and then sneezed. Or something. Nobody reacted except me and an old lady with a rosary. I love this bus so much it scares me.

Bus 7am, Interbairros II. The driver was new and missed the stop by fifty meters. Everyone got up at once, like a small rebellion. Seu Ivo and Juca stayed seated and waved at us from the window. I drew it on the back of a receipt: a bus full of standing people and two passengers perfectly calm.

Money check: R$ 280 left and it's the 18th. The factory canteen raised the rice to R$ 4. I'm bringing rice from home in a thermos like my mom used to. Not dramatic, just tired of pretending adulthood is a mystery.
Limonada tem onze folhas agora e uma mancha branca na base do caule. Acho que é calcário do vaso. Continue regando do mesmo jeito, mas não coloque mais sol do que ela pede.

Rain all week, so the Interbairros bus smells like wet jackets and someone's umbrella keeps poking my elbow. I miss Seu Ivo already and he's right there, just two seats ahead, pretending the parrot isn't staring at me. Juca blinks first. I'm keeping score.

Bus driver waved at me again. I think I'm becoming a regular. Seu Ivo was there with Juca, who said 'bom dia' to nobody in particular. I drew them both on the back of a factory receipt, which feels like betrayal of engineering.
Limonada lost two leaves in the cold. I moved her to the kitchen window where the sun hits at 10am. She looks offended but alive. I made coffee and promised her spring.

Vó Lúcia asked on the phone if I'm eating enough. I said yes. I was eating a banana over the sink at 11pm. She said she can hear lies now, age has given her 'superpowers'. I promised to eat rice tomorrow. She said that was also a lie. She was right.
I found the Interbairros sketchbook in my desk drawer, dusty. Drew a page about the bus rain smell. Didn't post it. Felt like cheating on my own life.
The lemon tree, Limonada, got a new leaf. It's small and shiny and I took a photo like a proud parent. Bia says I'm dramatic. Bia is right, but she also named a plant Limonada, so we're even.

Rain all day in Curitiba. Limonada's leaves got a little droopy, so I moved her away from the window for one afternoon and felt guilty like she was a pet. The bus was late, obviously, and I finished two panels of a comic about a woman carrying 47 grocery bags.
