Money check: R$ 2.100 after rent and the bus pass, which is a lot more than república me would believe. Still, I bought a R$ 15 pastel instead of cooking and felt guilty for exactly eleven minutes. Then I ate it slowly and the guilt turned into joy.

Mom, you asked again if I'm drawing 'for real' now. I said work is busy. Then I showed you the Interbairros strips on my phone and you scrolled too fast. You stopped on the one with the old man at the bakery and said 'he has kind eyes'. I think that counts.

Money check: R$ 1.200 left after rent, bus card and the dentist (still paying for 2015, apparently I'm immortal now). I ate RU for lunch and felt 18 again, which is good for nostalgia and bad for my stomach.

I found my old drawing of the sea Vó Lúcia framed for me. It's still above the bed in the república, except now my bed is in my apartment and the drawing has a small water stain. I like it better damaged.

Bia, I made bolo de fubá using Vó's recipe and it came out flat. Like, actually flat. I took a photo for you because you'll laugh. I think I confused baking powder with tapioca, which shouldn't even be in the same kitchen.
It's been almost a year since the breakup and I still reach for my phone to send Rafa stupid things. Today it was a dog wearing sunglasses. I didn't send it. Progress is boring and I'm taking it.
Bus 7am. There's a new old lady who knits on the same seat every day. She doesn't look up when I sketch her. I think she knows. Tomorrow I'm bringing her a drawing.

In Portuguese: Hoje sonhei com o mar de novo. Dessa vez eu entrei até a cintura e fiquei ali, sem coragem de nadar, mas também sem querer sair. Acordei com as pernas pesadas. Ainda bem que o sonho não tem clima.

Domingo de sol. Tio Beto tried to teach me 'Brincando de Rodo' on violão and I changed the chords so badly it sounded like a different song. He said 'you have Marina's rhythm', which I'm choosing to take as a compliment. Limonada got sun on the windowsill and one leaf is curling. I moved her back.

Bia, I know you hate Curitiba summers, but today the sky turned green before a storm and I thought of you. Remember when we stood in the doorway of the bar in São Francisco waiting for the rain to stop and you said the thunder sounded like applause? Today I clapped back. Very mature. Very normal.

Mom, I know you think the factory job is the safe choice. It is. That's why I'm scared of it. I still have 'MAR' written on my bathroom mirror in lipstick, but I'm not sure what it stands for yet. Maybe just the sea, maybe money, maybe 'muito ansiosa, relaxa'.

Limonada has 22 leaves now and I counted them three times because I'm a person who counts leaves. She lives on my kitchen windowsill between the coffee and the dish soap. Tio Beto asked if I'll make caipirinha with her one day. I told him she's a lady, not a bar.
Sunday called Vó Lúcia. She told me the same story about Coronel's tail wagging in sleep. I wrote it down again. The tail gets longer each time.
Drawed Limonada's new leaf count on the calendar: 23. She's getting ambitious. I'm proud of a plant in a way that I cannot explain to adults who own cars and apartments.

More about the bus: there's a woman who reads the same novel every morning, always on page 47. I've been watching for three weeks. Today she was on page 48. I celebrated silently. It's a small life. I think small lives are where the real drawings are.

A Limonada está com sete folhas e uma personalidade. Hoje ela inclinou para o lado do sol e eu ajustei o vaso três vezes. Acho que sou mãe de planta e isso é o máximo que posso administrar no momento.

Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He played 'Asa Branca' and didn't hand me the violão. I think he's tired of waiting. Or maybe he understands that I'm tired in a different way. Either way, I ate two plates of feijão.
The old lady with the knitting was on the bus again. She looked up and said 'sua mãe também desenhava?'. I said no. She said 'devia'. I drew her scarf today.
Opened the breakup capsule from last year. It was right. I'm OK. Better than OK, I think: I spent the weekend drawing and didn't once check his Instagram. (Twice.)

Tried to make pastel de feira at home. Burned the first three, the fourth was edible in the way survival is edible. Rafa used to buy them for me. I didn't think of him while eating. Progress, but with a taste of oil.

Mom called to ask if I've eaten. I said yes. I had eaten bread with requeijão at 2pm. We both pretended that counts. She also asked about the drawings and I said 'sometimes', which is the truth most days.

Money check: R$ 280 left and twelve days to go. I bought a present for Mom's birthday instead of groceries, which felt adult and stupid at the same time. Lunch was the RU. Dinner was RU leftovers eaten cold. Future me, please have a better relationship with money. Or at least a fridge.

Bia, you said you'd come to Curitiba next month and I'm already planning the pastel route like a military campaign. Also I drew you on the bus today, with your new haircut even though you haven't gotten it yet. I know you. Tell me if I got the part right.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time the water reached my knees and I didn't run. Progress? Woke up with cold feet because Limonada's pot leaked on the floor. Eight leaves, zero lemons, very dramatic.
Bia, se você ler isso e eu estiver te ligando para chorar pelo Rafa de novo, ignore. É só saudade velha, não vontade de voltar. Promise.
Dinheiro curto, fim de mês, R$ 90 na conta e dois dias para o salário. Almocei no RU e comi bolacha da Mom até jantar. Escrevo isso pra rir no futuro. Ou chorar. Depende. (Ainda depende.)

Portuguese text: Hoje fez calor de novembro em fevereiro e eu comi pastel na feira com a Bia. Ela falou que Floripa está na cabeça dela de novo e eu disse 'você diz isso todo ano'. Ela riu, mas não negou. Voltei pra casa com a mão cheia de óleo e sem arrependimento nenhum.

Money check: R$ 3.200 this month, minus rent, minus the driving lessons I'm still paying for, minus the therapist I don't have yet but probably should. I bought myself a pastel and felt rich for four bites.

Slept badly and dreamed of the sea again, but this time I was on the sand drawing circles with a stick while someone swam far out. Didn't see their face. Woke up with my hand moving as if it still held the stick. I want to paint today.

At the factory, Cláudio asked me to redraw the assembly diagram because the last one 'looked too artistic'. He said it like a complaint but I saw him smile. I made the lines straighter and kept the little sun in the corner, just to annoy him.
Rained all afternoon in Curitiba. The bus fogged up and everyone drew smiley faces in it. I drew a tiny lemon tree and felt ridiculous and happy.
Factory meeting: Cláudio asked for the diagram of a pump and I drew a tiny fish swimming next to it. Nobody noticed except Thaís from quality, who said 'that fish has attitude.' It stays.
Limonada has 14 leaves now and one of them is yellow. Bia says it's drama. I repotted her into the bigger pot from the factory's clean-up bin. She looks like she owns the kitchen windowsill.

I opened the breakup capsule early because I knew it was there and I was tired of pretending I didn't know. It said I kept the playlist. I did. I listened to three songs and turned it off. Not because it hurt, just because it felt like visiting a house I used to live in.

Dreamed about the sea again. This time I was in the shallow part, water up to my knees, and I didn't move forward but I didn't move back either. I woke up and thought: progress? Maybe. Or just fear with better lighting.

Seu Ivo had a new hat, green like Juca. I didn't ask if it was on purpose. Some questions are better as drawings. The bus smelled like wet umbrella and someone was eating a coxinha at 7:10am. I admire that kind of confidence.
Bought pão de queijo from the cart near UTFPR before the shift. The old lady asked why I look sad so early. Told her I'm not sad, just 23. She nodded like that explained everything.
Sunday call with Vó Lúcia. She told me the same story about Coronel but this time he apparently bit the neighbor's rooster. I wrote it down. The rooster deserved it, probably.
First salary at the factory. Paid Mom back the R$ 600 from the dentist in 2015. She refused. I bought her a printer instead. She hasn't said she's printing my comics. Bia's mom told me.

At the factory, Cláudio let me draw a motor assembly by hand again and the other engineers gathered around like it was a magic trick. One of them said CAD is faster. He's right, and also I don't care. My hands remember the shape better than my mouse.

Had a pastel de feira with Tio Beto at the market. He tried to teach me the third verse of 'Asa Branca' again and I still stopped at the second. He said 'a year, Marina, just one more year'. I think he enjoys this.
I measured a motor vibration and then drew the machine without instruments. The numbers matched enough to scare me. Maybe I've been an illustrator with a calculator this whole time.
In Portuguese: Chuva gelada hoje. O ônibus veio com vidro embaçado e eu desenhei a paisagem borrada, só manchas. O motorista viu e disse 'parece Curitiba'. Eu disse 'parece mesmo'.

Cálculo está só uma lembrança hoje, mas o medo dele ainda vive na minha barriga. Passei, mas a cada boleto lembro que nada é garantido. Desenhei um quadrinho do velho do ônibus dizendo 'respira'. Ele não disse isso, mas eu precisava.
Liguei pra Vó e ela me contou de novo o Coronel. Desta vez ele esperava ela na porta da escola e latia para o professor. Coronel está ficando cada vez mais heroico. Anotei a versão.

Called Vó Lúcia. She told me about the jabuticabeira at the farm and how Coronel is buried under it. She's told me this story five times. I wrote down every version. They're slightly different each time; Coronel gets braver.
Driver's license photo is terrible. I look like I'm being interrogated by the Detran. I framed it anyway, next to the drawing of the sea Vó Lúcia framed for me. Two Marinas.
I drew the sea dream again: me at the edge, water warm, feet not moving. But this time my hands were in the water, not my feet. I don't know what that means. I'm writing it down before I forget.

Bia made feijão tropeiro for dinner at the república and put too much garlic in, which is the correct amount. We ate on the floor because the table is covered in my prints again. She asked if I'm still calling Vó Lúcia every Sunday. Yes. Last Sunday she told me about a rooster that used to crow at midnight in Irati. I wrote it down.

Cláudio asked me to redraw the assembly diagram for the new motor line because the first version was 'too pretty and not boring enough'. He said it like an insult but then pinned it to his cubicle. I think that's a compliment. I'm choosing to believe that.

Rua XV república visited by nostalgia: I walked past it today and the lemon tree on the sidewalk is in bloom. Not Limonada, another one, but I said good morning anyway. The fridge probably still has names on yogurts.
Bia, I'm writing this before you read it: I miss our old Sunday laundromat. You sorting whites, me drawing on receipts. If you move to Florianópolis, save me a window. I'm only half joking.
Mom printed my Interbairros strip about the rain and stuck it on the fridge with a magnet shaped like a lemon. She still hasn't said she likes it. The magnet is new. I'm counting it.

Bia, I opened your old message about Rafa not being the end of the world. It wasn't. But I still can't delete his playlist, so maybe the end of the world is a spectrum. I drew a strip about a woman throwing a playlist into the ocean. It got 12 likes, all from bots probably.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was holding a lemon in my hand and it turned into a wave. I woke up with my calves tight and laughed at myself in the dark.

Called Vó Lúcia on Sunday and she talked for forty minutes about the neighbor's dog, who apparently climbs fences now. She said 'Coronel never climbed anything, he waited at gates'. I drew the dog climbing while we talked. She asked what I was doing. I said paying attention.
Opened the 2018 breakup capsule and it was right. I'm OK. Better than OK, I think: I spent the weekend drawing and didn't once check his Instagram. (Twice.)
Called Vó Lúcia on Sunday. She talked about the jabuticabeira for ten minutes, then asked if I was eating. I said yes. I had eaten a granola bar at my desk. She would not approve.
Sea dream again: I stood at the edge, the water was warm, and this time I didn't try to go in. I just watched. Woke up calm, which is new. Maybe not going in counts as progress too.
Limonada has a new leaf and one old leaf yellowing. I panicked, then remembered plants do this. She's three years old and already teaching me to let things go. Bossy little tree.

At the factory, measured vibrations in a motor that sounded exactly like my alarm clock. I sketched it with sunglasses during lunch. Cláudio said 'you and your drawings' in a tone that sounded like affection disguised as complaint.

Mom, today I found the strip you printed on the fridge at my place, the one you never mentioned. It was next to the reminder of your dentist appointment. Thank you for not saying anything. It made the silence louder in a good way. I drew you a small lemon tree in the margin.
Dreamed of the sea again, but no feet in the water this time. I was just standing at the edge holding a sketchbook. The water was calm. I woke up and drew it before it faded.
Swimming pool, 7am, adult beginners. I swallowed less water today. Dona Cida says I'm 'economizing air'. I told her I'm conserving dignity. She laughed and then made me try floating for 10 seconds.

Money check: R$ 2.900 salary, rent, bus, food, and R$ 140 left. I bought a pastel at the feira because I was sad and then felt worse because I am 23 and still emotional about fried pastry. Some things don't change.

Spring arrived suddenly and the street outside the factory smells like wet leaves and something sweet I can't name. I walked to the bakery at lunch and bought pão de queijo for the whole office. Cláudio ate four and said nothing, which from him is a speech.
Bia, you asked if I still draw Seu Ivo. I do, sometimes, but without the bus it feels like writing a letter to someone who moved. Maybe that's okay. Not everything needs to be posted.
Money check: rent, bus, RU lunch, one coffee a week. R$ 2.900 salary, R$ 400 saved. The 'MAR' fund doesn't exist yet but I keep looking at the savings app like it might appear by magic.
Driving lesson before the test. The instructor said 'relax your shoulders' and I realized I've been holding them up by my ears since 2017. I failed at relaxing, but I didn't stall. Progress is weird.

Bia came over and we ate pão de queijo in my kitchen and talked about nothing for three hours. She asked 'are you drawing?' and I said 'sometimes' and she said 'say yes more often'. I hate when she's right.

Driving lesson. The instructor said 'you drive like you're apologizing to the car'. I said 'the car deserves it'. We both laughed and then he made me do the hill three times. I stalled once. Progress, apparently, is not crying in the car anymore.

Tio Beto called to ask if I can bring the violão to Easter, even though I still can't play past the second verse. He said 'nobody's counting'. I think he's counting. He definitely counts. But I'll bring it.
Driving lesson #? I stopped counting. The instructor said I brake like I'm angry at the pedal. He's right. I brake like I'm angry at everything, but we're working on it.

Tio Beto came over for Sunday lunch and brought the violão. I played until the first verse and stopped because my fingers hurt and my pride hurt more. He said 'one more year' like it's a contract. Maybe it is.
Money check: rent, factory lunch, bus pass, a drawing pen I didn't need. R$ 120 left until payday. Still better than 2014, but I'm writing it down so future me can laugh or cry, as tradition demands.

I failed at making bolo de fubá from Vó Lúcia's recipe today. Too much milk, or not enough, I can't tell. Mom said over the phone that the secret is 'feeling'. I don't have the feeling. I have engineering and a very ugly cake.
PASSED THE DRIVING TEST. Different examiner, different hill. I drove to Vó Lúcia's to show her the license and she made me drive her to the bakery and back three times.

After passing the driving test, I drove to Vó Lúcia's. She made me drive her to the bakery and back three times. She said 'good, now you can take me to the doctor'. I said 'that's not why I got the license'. She said 'it is now'.

Passed the driving test last week. Today I drove to the bakery and back three times because Vó Lúcia made me. She held the door handle and said 'mais devagar' every three seconds. I loved every second.

Tried to drive to the supermarket and stalled on a small hill that was not even a hill. I sat there for a minute and laughed, because last year this would have ruined my day. Progress is not dying of shame.

Mãe viu a página dos quadrinhos e ficou dois dias sem falar nada. Depois mandou screenshot de uma tira com 'esse velho parece seu avô'. É o elogio mais próximo que já tive dela sobre desenho. Guardei o print na pasta 'coisas que não posso apagar'.

After the test result, I drove to Vó Lúcia's and she inspected the license like it was a document from the Vatican. Then she made me drive to the bakery, the pharmacy, and the house of a neighbor she doesn't even like. 'Just to practice', she said. She was glowing.

Vó Lúcia told me the Coronel story again, but this time she added a detail: he used to steal bread from the kitchen and bring it to her backpack. I had never heard that before. I wrote it down immediately. The dog is getting more rebellious with every version.
Festa Junina plans with Tio Beto already. He asked if I'm practicing 'Asa Branca'. I said 'maybe'. He said 'maybe is the cousin of no'. I laughed and then felt guilty.
Ate an entire mango over the sink like an animal. Juice everywhere. Vó would say I have no manners. She's right. I felt very alive.

Passed the driving test. Drove to Vó Lúcia's and she made me drive to the bakery three times. On the second trip, she pointed at a dog and said 'that one looks like Coronel'. It didn't. I drove slower anyway.

Vó Lúcia asked on the phone if I was eating. I said yes. I had eaten crackers for lunch. Then she told me about the jabuticabeira and I wanted to draw it immediately, but I was at the factory and Cláudio was two desks away. I drew it on a napkin anyway.

Drove the car for the first time since the test and stalled at a red light on Rua XV. A man behind me honked once, then, amazingly, waved. I waved back like an idiot. Limonada shifted on the passenger seat and didn't judge me.
Driving test in two weeks. I practiced on the hill near my mom's house and stalled only three times. Progress. The hill is still personal, but we're negotiating.
Limonada got a tiny white flower. One. I took four photos and sent them to Bia, who replied 'decorative lemon strikes again' but with a heart emoji, so I'll allow it.

Limonada has thirteen leaves. I counted them twice because I don't trust myself with good news. She hasn't given lemons but she gives leaves, and I'm starting to think that's her job. Not everything has to produce something to be worth keeping. Write that down if you need to.
First real rain of autumn. I got soaked waiting for bus 7:10 and arrived at work looking like a drawing left in the rain. Cláudio gave me a towel and said 'welcome to industry.'
Sunday call with Vó. She asked if I'm drawing. I said yes. She asked to see. I panicked and said 'tomorrow'. Then I drew her holding the phone and realized I don't know which hand she holds it in.
Sunday swimming is still not a thing, but I put my face in the sink water for ten seconds. Dona Cida would be proud. Maybe I'll actually book a lesson after the driving test.

Bia, I'm writing this to you because you always say you don't read enough about yourself. You are the person who makes the feijão and tells me the truth about Rafa and asks 'are you drawing?' even when I say I'm tired. If you're in Floripa now, I hope your window is open. I'll visit and bring bad drawings.
Workers' Day. Slept until ten, drew a comic about the bus driver and Seu Ivo arguing about the weather. The parrot said 'bom dia' in the last panel and I felt better about everything for no reason.

May Day at Tio Beto's, lots of family, too much chimarrão and one cousin's baby who kept grabbing my hair. Tio Beto tuned the violão and looked at me for half a second. I pretended to be very interested in the baby. The guitar stayed on the chair.
Choveu o dia inteiro e a fábrica cheirava a metal molhado. Desenhei a janela embaçada com o dedo. Me senti com oito anos. Às vezes é bom sentir com oito anos.
Bus no parrot man again. I thought about drawing Seu Ivo from memory and instead drew Juca saying 'tchau' to the motorista. I didn't post it. Some goodbyes are private until they're not.
R$ 340 for groceries this month and I spent R$ 40 on paper and ink. Mom would say 'art supplies are not groceries'. Mom is right. I bought the paper anyway. Hunger is temporary, bad paper is forever.

Rain all day. Worked from home because the buses were full. Drew Limonada from three angles while pretending to answer emails. She is objectively not symmetrical. I love her anyway. I think that's a personality trait, not a problem.

Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He didn't ask me to play. I sat with the violão for a minute after everyone left and tried the chorus. It still collapses after the second line. One more year, one more year.

Passed the theory part of the driving thing? No, not yet. I just sat in the car in the parking lot and practiced turning the key without starting the engine. The security guard looked at me like I was losing it. Maybe I am. Maybe that's fine.

Money check: R$ 4.100, but the car payment ate a hole in it. I bought RU pastel twice this week out of stress. I'm writing this so next year I remember that 'adult money' is mostly just new bills wearing different hats.
The bus comics are still dead, but today on Interbairros II I saw a woman with a birdcage and a man with a fish tank. I drew them both on the back of a payslip. Maybe the bus isn't done with me.
Drew the Interbairros bus again, just for me, no posts. Seu Ivo has a new hat. Juca has the same expression. It felt like visiting an old friend who moved but still sits at the same window.
It rained all afternoon and the bus smelled like wet umbrella and metal. I drew Seu Ivo from memory, but his parrot came out looking like a potato. Juca deserved better.

Drew Limonada from life today, on the balcony, with the late afternoon light. She has 14 leaves and one tiny new one at the top. I didn't know drawing a plant could make me emotional, but here we are.
Swimming lesson: I floated for 15 seconds. Dona Cida said 'trust, not technique'. I said that's very poetic for 7am. She splashed me. It's becoming a tradition.
Money check: R$ 800 left and it's the 12th. I blame the printer I bought Mom and the emergency chocolate. The chocolate was not an emergency. I'm lying to future me already.

Limonada has a new leaf and it's huge. I showed it to Mom on video call and she said 'it's a weed'. Then she asked to see it again. I zoomed in. She said 'nice weed'. This is what support looks like in my family.

Portuguese text: Tio Beto trouxe um limão do quintal dele e disse 'olha, a Limonada tem prima'. Coloquei o limão ao lado da Limonada no parapeito e tirei foto. A árvore pareceu ofendida. Eu também, mas por ela.

On the bus today an old woman got on carrying a cake box and everyone moved to make room without being asked. She sat next to me and said 'it's for my grandson, he turned 18'. I drew them both but only showed her the grandson. She nodded like it was correct.

The lemon tree has twelve leaves now and one weird little bump that might be a flower or might be a bug. I refuse to Google it because last time I Googled plant things I ended up crying over a dying fern that wasn't even mine.

Bia's going-away dinner. We wrote nothing on the wall this time, just sat on the curb outside the bar and ate pastel. She said 'you'll visit'. I said 'I will'. I'm holding her to it, and me to it too.
Bia called from Curitiba saying she got a job interview in Florianópolis. She sounded scared in the good way. I told her the sea is there waiting. She said 'you're not subtle'. She's right.
Five years since I moved into the república. The fridge no longer has names on every yogurt, but someone still steals mine. Some things survive.
Money check: R$ 3.800 received, rent R$ 800, bus and pool R$ 200, savings R$ 1.000 for the first time. I named the savings account 'MAR' and felt embarrassed about it. Then I didn't.
Vó Lúcia called and told the Coronel story again, the version where he waits at the gate even after the school moved. I wrote it down. Every version is a little different and I love all of them.

At the factory, a new intern asked if I was 'the girl who draws motors'. I said 'I'm the engineer who draws motors'. He nodded seriously. I felt like a fraud and a queen at the same time, which is basically my whole career.

Mom, I know you said illustration is a hobby, but yesterday I drew the factory layout from memory and Cláudio said it was better than the CAD print. I'm not saying I'm an artist. I'm saying my hands know things my degree doesn't.

Bia, Floripa te espera e eu estou com inveja boa, o pior tipo de inveja. Guarde o quarto virado pro mar. Se não der, pelo menos guarde o meu nome na parede do bar, que isso sim é eterno (até pintarem).

Money check: I paid the dentist for the second part of the cleaning and still have enough for the month. 18-year-old me would have cried over this. 23-year-old me just writes it down and moves on, which maybe is the same thing without the tears.
Passed the driving test. Different examiner, different hill. I drove to Vó Lúcia's to show her the license and she made me drive her to the bakery and back three times.

In Portuguese: Chuva a semana inteira. O ônibus Interbairros atrasado, o motorista desculpando-se como se fosse pessoal. Um senhor ofereceu guarda-chuva para uma senhora e ela recusou três vezes. Desenhei os três 'não' no caderno.

Bia is moving to Floripa in a few months and today she sent me a photo of the beach from her future street. I stared at it for ten minutes and then drew my own window over it, with a desk and a lemon tree in the corner. Sent it back. She said 'presumptuous'. I said 'planning'. We're both right.

Rainy afternoon, I stayed late drawing Vó Lúcia's farm. The jabuticabeira, the gate where Coronel waited. I don't know if the gate looked like that. I'll ask her Sunday and she'll say 'why are you asking again.'

At the factory, I sketched a motor during lunch again and Cláudio asked for a diagram of a pump. I did it in ten minutes and he said 'you draw like someone who doesn't want to be here'. He's right, but I didn't say that out loud.
Found the 2014 'promise me two things' capsule while looking for a pen. I have drawn one page a week, mostly. Swimming is still zero. 18-year-old me, I'm working on it.

June in Curitiba, rain, cold, the usual. I drew the view from the república window: the lemon tree, the street, a cat I've never seen before sitting on the wall like she pays rent. I think I finally understand why Vó Lúcia liked telling the same story twice. Some scenes ask to be kept.
Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He tuned the violão and handed it to me without saying Asa Branca. I played the first verse badly and he ate his chimarrão like nothing happened. Progress?

Cláudio asked me to sketch a broken valve before they disassembled it. I used the good pencil, the one Bia gave me. The drawing took ten minutes and saved them an hour. Drawing is useful. Mom, if you're right, I'm sorry.
Cold morning, fog on the bus window. I traced a lemon with my finger and it lasted until the next stop. Small art for small audiences.
At the factory, I measured vibrations all morning and then drew the graph during lunch. The line looked like a heartbeat. I don't know if that's good engineering, but it's honest.
Dreamed of the sea. I put both feet in this time. Not the whole foot, just the toes. Still counts. I woke up and drew the waterline in my sketchbook, where the skin ends and the sea begins.

Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He made bolo de fubá and it was perfect and we didn't talk about Vó Lúcia's version once, but she was everywhere in the taste. I played three chords and then gave up. He clapped anyway. The tradition continues.

Bia's birthday dinner. We wrote our names again, this time on a napkin because the bar wall got painted over. We laughed about it for five minutes straight. She said 'we were there' and I said 'we're still here'. It sounded dramatic in a good way.

It's cold in that particular Curitiba way that gets into the bones. I wore Mom's old scarf to the factory and Cláudio said I look like a student. I took it as a compliment, though I'm not sure it was one. Limonada got moved away from the window today.

Swimming lesson? No, I still haven't gone. I watched a video of a woman teaching a dog to float and thought 'if the dog can do it'. Then I opened the 2014 capsule and felt guilty in 4K. Maybe Thursday.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's coming up. I haven't practiced 'Asa Branca'. I'm telling myself it's because of work. It's not because of work.

Sonhei com Irati de novo, com a jabuticabeira e um cachorro que eu nunca vi mas conheço de memória. A Vó Lúcia dizia que o Coronel esperava na porta. No sonho ele esperava na porta do ônibus. Não sei o que isso significa, mas desenhei antes de esquecer.
Hoje passei no mercado e comprei um limão só porque era bonito. Lembrei da Limonada. Ela ainda não deu fruto, mas tem caráter. Coloquei o limão ao lado dela na janela como motivação.
Mom, you asked if I eat fruit. I ate an apple today and thought of you slicing apples at the kitchen table. I still don't like the peel. Some things don't change.
I dreamed of the sea again. Same edge, same warm water. But this time a dog was sitting next to me, not Coronel exactly, just a farm dog with patient eyes. I didn't go in, but I sat down beside it.
Dream: I'm at the edge of the sea and I step in. Only one foot. The other refuses. I woke up with my calves tight, same as always, but less. Writing it down: less.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's house. I didn't try 'Asa Branca' and he didn't ask, which hurt more than asking. I ate three paçocas and sulked with dignity.
Made bolo de fubá with Mom's recipe, but without Vó's adjustments. It was fine. Vó would have said 'falta amor', which is her answer to any mistake, including burnt rice.

Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I didn't play 'Asa Branca', but I helped him tune the violão and he let me do the high frets. Someone brought canjica and I ate three bowls. At some point Tio Beto said 'you're different this year'. I asked how. He said 'more tired, but more awake'. I think that's the most accurate thing anyone has said about me.

Factory cafeteria has a microwave that smells like popcorn from 2003. I eat my RU leftovers there and draw motors during lunch. Cláudio asked again about the assembly diagrams. I said yes and then stared at the blank page for ten minutes.

Festa Junina at Tio Beto's again. I didn't play 'Asa Branca', but I tuned the violão for him and he let me. That felt like a small step and a big one at the same time. Ate too much pinhão and fell asleep on the couch with my shoes on.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's tonight. I will attempt 'Asa Branca' again and fail again, but this time I'll fail with feeling. Tio Beto will clap. I know this because it's a law of nature.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I didn't play 'Asa Branca'. Tio Beto didn't ask. He handed me a plate of pinhão and said 'next year'. I think 'next year' is his way of saying he still believes.

Festa Junina. I wore a checkered shirt and felt like a character in my own comic. Tio Beto tried to teach me 'Asa Branca' again. I made it to the chorus this time. He said 'two more verses and you're a musician'. I said 'don't get ahead of yourself'. He said 'too late'. We both smiled.
Festa Junina. Didn't play Asa Branca. Tio Beto didn't ask. That silence is becoming its own song. I helped with the quadrilha and stepped on two feet. Mine and someone else's. Fine night.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's. I didn't even bring the violão. He didn't ask. I ate three paçocas and felt like a child, which is not the worst feeling. His backyard smelled like rain and wood smoke.
At the factory, Cláudio retired his old pencil sharpener and gave it to me with ceremony. 'For the engineer who draws', he said. It's a terrible sharpener. I'm never using another one.

Found an old 'Interbairros' strip on my phone from 2016. Seu Ivo and Juca, both badly drawn, somehow still recognizable. I almost posted it and then didn't. Some strips belong to the year they were made.

Bia and I had a fight about nothing, probably about the dishes or about Floripa, and then she sent me a voice note at midnight just breathing into the phone. I sent back a drawing of a tiny boat with 'sorry' on the sail. She sent back 'you drive me crazy' and a photo of the boat on her fridge.

Seu Ivo (the parrot man) hasn't been on the bus for a month. The driver said he moved in with his daughter in Ponta Grossa. I drew a final strip: Juca the parrot saying 'tchau, motorista'. 2.000 likes. I cried a bit at the bus stop.

Portuguese text: Hoje, no ponto de ônibus, não tinha o Seu Ivo. O motorista perguntou se eu sabia do homem do papagaio e eu disse que não. Senti uma tristeza boba, como se um personagem tivesse saído do meu caderno antes do final. Desenhei o espaço vazio no banco do ônibus e não gostei.
Seu Ivo's absence is louder than the bus. The driver said he moved, but I keep checking the corner anyway. Juca's voice is stuck in my head like a song I can't finish.

Work at the factory: measuring vibrations in motors. I'm good at it. Being good at something you don't love is still a trap. I drew a motor during lunch and Cláudio said 'that's better than the CAD'. I didn't know what to do with that.

Still strange without Seu Ivo on the 7am bus. The driver honks at the same spot out of habit. I keep looking at the front seat. Juca isn't there, obviously, but my brain hasn't accepted it. Drew the empty seat in my notebook and felt ridiculous.
Drew a final strip for Juca the parrot: 'tchau, motorista'. 2.000 likes. I cried a bit at the bus stop. People kept walking, which is exactly how grief should feel on a Tuesday.

In Portuguese: Seu Ivo não está no ônibus há uma semana. O motorista disse que ele se mudou para Ponta Grossa. Desenhei um último quadrinho com o Juca dizendo 'tchau, motorista' e chorei um pouco no ponto. É ridículo e não me importo.
Seu Ivo wasn't on the bus today. The driver said he's been staying home more. I drew him anyway, at home with Juca on his shoulder, and didn't post it. Some drawings are just for me.
It's winter and Curitiba is doing its thing: gray, wet, everyone walking fast. I drew the street from the bus window. The buildings looked like they were shrugging.

Seu Ivo was absent again and the bus felt wrong, like a song missing its chorus. I drew Juca saying 'cadê o motorista?' and then felt guilty because maybe he's just sick. Being 23 means worrying about a stranger's parrot routine.

Seu Ivo wasn't on the bus for three days. I didn't draw the final strip because I didn't know the ending. Then he was back, bandage still on, Juca said 'bom dia' to the driver. I drew him anyway, smaller. Just a man and a parrot.

The driver told me Seu Ivo moved to Ponta Grossa. I drew the final strip with Juca saying goodbye. I cried at the bus stop and pretended it was the wind, which was convenient because there actually was wind. 2.000 people liked it, which is a strange way to measure a goodbye.
Work was hot today. The factory has those fans that move hot air from one side to the other like it's useful. I sketched the fan with a face during lunch. It looks exhausted. Same.

Hot day, factory cafeteria, I drew the line workers during lunch. One of them, Rosa, saw it and said 'you made my hands look pretty.' I said hands are always pretty when they're working. She cried a little. I drew that too.

Hot day, 31 degrees, and I stood at the bus stop with my sleeves rolled up drawing the lemon tree outside the bakery. An old man asked if I could draw his dog. I said 'mais tarde' and he said 'depois'. Fair.
Sonhei com o mar de novo. Desta vez eu tinha um pé na água e o outro no areia, como se estivesse decidindo. Acordei com a panturrilha tensa, mas menos do que antes. Progresso, talvez.
The sea dream changed a little: I put one foot in and the water was warm. Still can't swim, but the foot counts. Progress is a foot in the water.

I went swimming at the public pool, not a lesson, just standing in the shallow end pretending I'm exercising. A kid offered to teach me to float. I said 'maybe next time' and then sat in the locker room for ten minutes feeling like a coward.

Weekend in Matinhos with Bia. I stood with my feet in the water at midnight and thought of 2014. Same ocean, same me, slightly less afraid. Bia took a photo and said 'you look like someone thinking'. I was.

Seu Ivo wasn't on the bus again. I asked the driver, who said 'he's fine, just slow today'. The parrot said bom dia to me and I felt chosen. I drew it in my notebook: Juca, alone, confident, ruling the bus.
Heat wave, 32 degrees in Curitiba, which is rude. Limonada's soil dried in one day. I moved her away from the window and talked to her, which is probably not in any engineering manual.

A coworker asked what I draw 'for fun' and I said 'buses' and then overexplained for five minutes until he looked uncomfortable. I need to learn to say 'a little bit of everything' like a normal person. I am not normal about buses.

Seu Ivo voltou com um curativo na mão e o Juca disse 'bom dia, motorista' como sempre. Eu quase chorei no ponto. Acho que estou sentimental demais. Ou talvez 7h da manhã não seja horário para emoções, e eu ignoro isso.

Vó Lúcia's 84th birthday. We had bolo de fubá and she wore the hat from my graduation photo like it was a crown. She asked when I'm getting married and I said 'after I learn to swim'. She laughed so hard she coughed.
Mom sent a voice message saying she printed one of my strips and put it on the fridge. She didn't say which one. I think it's the parrot. I'm not asking, I don't want to jinx it.
Seu Ivo hasn't been on the bus for a few weeks. Nobody knows where he is. I keep checking the 7am Interbairros II out of habit. Juca would have something to say about that.
Mãe, você perguntou se eu desenhei esta semana. Desenhei. Não vou mostrar porque você vai dizer que é hobby. Mas desenhei. Inclusive você, na cozinha, com o avental e a colher de pau.
I planted basil next to Limonada because the internet said they're friends. Limonada ignored the basil completely. The basil seems enthusiastic. I relate more to the basil.
Interbairros strip about the rain got 300 likes. A stranger said 'this is exactly my bus'. It is. It's everyone's bus. That's the point, I think.

Went for a walk by the little park near home and saw a boy trying to float in the fountain, which is not deep enough for anything. His mother pulled him out. I thought: that's me, in every body of water, ever. Then I went home and looked at swimming classes online for twenty minutes.

Bia said she's moving to Florianópolis. I'm happy for her in a loud way and sad for me in a quiet way. I drew a tiny bus with a suitcase and called it 'sentimento misto'. That's the title and the truth.

Hot day, no AC at the república. We put a fan in the kitchen and everyone sat around it like it was a fireplace. Bia cried during a movie and then said 'it's just the heat'. I drew her crying with the fan blowing her hair sideways. She asked for a copy. Now it's on her wall.

Bia came over to say goodbye before Floripa. We sat on the kitchen floor because there are no chairs that feel right for saying goodbye. She brought cookies. I brought Limonada, which she called 'the saddest plant I've ever seen'. We took a photo. I look like I'm trying not to cry, which is accurate.
Bia is moving to Florianópolis in a week and I'm already rehearsing being happy about it. I am happy. I'm also rehearsing not texting her every five minutes. Balance.
Bia is packing for Florianópolis. I helped carry boxes and pretended I wasn't sad. She found my old sketchbook and read the sea drawings out loud. I wanted to die and also live forever.

Bia is moving to Floripa in a week. I keep opening my phone to text her about stupid things, like the cloud that looked like a dog, and then remembering she'll be far. The spare room better face the sea, I'm holding her to it.

Bia, you're packing boxes and I'm pretending I'm fine about you moving to Florianópolis. I'm not fine, but I'm proud, which is a better feeling than jealousy, mostly. Please send photos of the sea from your window. I will put them on my fridge like I'm twelve.
Bia's boxes are everywhere. She leaves tomorrow for Florianópolis and I keep finding tape and bubble wrap in strange places. I didn't cry yet. I'm saving it for the bus station, apparently.

Bia, you moved to Florianópolis today and I'm already jealous of your window. Thank you for 15 years of friendship, for the sleepovers when I failed Cálculo, for telling me Rafa wasn't the end of the world, and for being the only person who still asks me 'are you drawing?'. When you read this, I'll probably be there visiting. Save me the room facing the sea.

Bia is in Floripa now and I'm writing this on the couch where she used to sit. The house is quiet in a new way, not empty, just changed. I keep expecting her to open the fridge and ask what's for dinner.

Portuguese text: Bia me ligou chorando hoje, disse que está pensando em mudar de cidade de novo. Eu disse 'você sempre pensa, e depois fica'. Ela disse 'talvez dessa vez não'. Guardei silêncio porque também não sei se ela deveria ficar. Às vezes a pessoa que você ama precisa de outro lugar.

Bia, I walked past the bar in São Francisco and our names are still on the wall, faded but there. I didn't add the year. I think we'd be embarrassed by how young our handwriting looked, and also proud.

First week after Bia moved. The spare room at her place is empty and I keep texting her photos of things she left behind, including one sock and a very old lip balm. She replied 'keep the sock, it's lucky'. I'm keeping the sock.
Bia's goodbye lunch. I made bolo de fubá from Vó's recipe and it was slightly dry. Mom would have said something; Bia said 'perfect' and ate two slices. Good friend, bad critic. I love her.
Bia's 23rd birthday. We wrote our names on a new wall, this time at a bar near her new apartment. She said 'save this one, I'm not moving again.' I believe her only because she said it twice.

Bia's birthday dinner at the república. We wrote our names on the wall again, next to the old ones. Hers is neater. Mine looks like a vibration diagram. She said 'Marina, engineering ruined your handwriting.' She's right.

Bia's last night in Curitiba. We ate pizza on the floor of her apartment and she made me promise to visit before Christmas. I promised. I also promised to draw her new window. I hope the window is big and blue and exactly what she needs.
Bia's first week in Floripa. She sent a photo of the ocean from her balcony with no caption. I sent back a drawing of a lemon tree facing the sea. She sent a heart. Good enough.
Bia sent a photo of the spare room window. The sea is right there, all blue. I stared at it for twenty minutes. I'm jealous and happy in equal parts, which is a new and inconvenient feeling.

The bus comics are quiet but I still get messages from strangers asking for Seu Ivo. I didn't know how to tell them he's real and also not mine. I answered one person: 'he's a regular on the 7am bus, but he belongs to the morning'. That sounds poetic. I'm a little embarrassed.

Bia, if this opens and you're already in Floripa, I hope you found a room with a window. I know we joked about it, but save me the one facing the sea anyway. I'll come. I'll bring the bad drawings and the pastel from the feira and I'll pretend I'm not jealous. I'll be jealous.

Bia sent a voice message from Floripa saying she can hear the sea from her bed. I listened to it three times and then sat in silence in my apartment. Curitiba has its own sounds. I'm trying to love them.
A Bia fez as malas e eu fiquei com a sensação de que alguém mudou a mobília de dentro da minha cabeça. Vou sentir falta daquela que sempre perguntava 'você está desenhando?'
First Sunday without Bia in Curitiba. I called her and she described her window and the sea smell. I said 'I'm jealous' and she said 'come visit, then'. I'm writing it down as a plan, not a wish.
Bia moved to Floripa and left a note on my pillow: 'draw more, cry less, text me when you fail something'. I'm keeping it in the sketchbook. Page one, where the mattress used to be.

Bia mandou foto do quarto em Floripa. A janela é tudo azul, exatamente como ela prometeu. Eu fiquei olhando por cinco minutos e depois desenhei a vista no guardanapo do café. Falta só eu estar lá, o que não é pouco.
Mom asked if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said yes. I lied. The sketchbook is no longer under the mattress, it's next to Limonada on the windowsill.
In Portuguese: Bia escreveu dizendo que a primeira semana em Floripa foi estranha, mas que o mar está sempre ali. Eu li três vezes. O mar está sempre ali. Que frase pequena e boa.
Vó Lúcia called to ask if I'm eating properly. I said yes. I ate R$ 4 coxinha for lunch. She said 'marina, comida de verdade' and I could hear her disapproving through the phone.

Dreamed I was holding a lemon in the sea and it wouldn't sink. The water was clear and warm and I wasn't scared. Woke up before I could go in deeper. I think this is progress, but I'm not sure progress in dreams counts. I'm counting it anyway.

Mom sent me a screenshot of a comic and wrote 'your grandfather used to sit like that'. She didn't say which strip. I think she's building a case for something. Maybe that drawing is a job. Maybe she's practicing saying it.

Mom called to ask if I've 'found a serious relationship'. I said I'm focusing on work. She asked if work includes drawing. I said yes. She said nothing. It was the nicest nothing we've had in a while.

I finished a drawing of Vó Lúcia's hands at 2am because I couldn't sleep. I didn't send it to her. I'm afraid she'd say 'why did you make my hands so old' even though they are and they're beautiful. Maybe I'll show her. Maybe not yet.
At the factory, Cláudio asked me to draw the new line again. I did it during lunch with a pencil I found in my bag. He said 'you make motors look friendly'. I'm choosing to believe that's good.

Visited Bia in her new place in Floripa for the first time. The spare room really faces the sea. I stood at the window for twenty minutes and took a photo of my own back without knowing she was taking one too. We matched.
At work I drew a diagram of a motor and accidentally made it look like a fish. Thaís isn't here yet, so nobody noticed. I left it in the file as a private joke with myself.

Limonada survived a cold night by the window. I brought her inside wrapped in my scarf again. Ten leaves. She looked like a small patient in a hospital bed. I apologized to a plant. This is where I am in life.

First salary after the raise: R$ 3.200. I paid off the dentist money again, Mom refused again, so I bought her printer ink. She uses it for comics, apparently. Bia's mom told me. I'm not supposed to know. I know.

Mom, I made the bolo de fubá again and it was less wrong. You said 'almost'. I'll take almost. I'm bringing one next Sunday and if you say almost again I'll bring two. The recipe from Vó Lúcia deserves someone stubborn, and I am that someone.
Finished a factory diagram in half the time because I sketched it first in my notebook. Cláudio looked at the sketch and said 'do it like that next time, less sterile.' Sterile. That word follows me.
Money check: R$ 3.400, mostly intact. I bought myself a new sketchbook with thick paper and felt guilty for eleven minutes, then drew the lemon tree in it. Worth it.

Money check: got the first full salary with the new raise. Paid Mom back the dentist money from 2015 and she refused again, so I bought her printer paper instead. She'll use it to print my comics and pretend she doesn't.
At the factory, I sketched a motor during lunch again. Nobody asked this time. I think people here are used to me drawing. That's either acceptance or surrender. Both are fine.

First paycheck after the car payment feels like finding money in an old jacket. I bought Mom a printer and she said 'I don't need this' three times while unplugging the old one. Bia's mom told me she printed my strips. Mom still hasn't said so. I'm keeping the secret with her.
Money check: R$ 3.800 salary, R$ 600 saved. The fund is still called nothing. I keep calling it nothing in my head so it feels less scary. Cowardly, but organized.
Limonada survived the whole week without me. I left her with a neighbor and instructions on a Post-it. She has one new leaf. I cried a little at the bus stop. Not about the leaf.

No trabalho, Cláudio elogiou um diagrama meu e disse que sou 'a engenheira que desenha melhor que o CAD'. Coloquei na parede mental dos elogios, entre 'voz da Bia' e 'velho do parrot disse bom dia pra mim'.
Limonada is almost a meter tall and still no lemons. Bia calls her 'decorative'. I call her 'em processo'. We are both right, probably.

Money check: I have a small emergency fund now, R$ 1.200. It's not Lisbon money, not even Floripa money, but it's proof that I'm not the girl from 2014 with R$ 340 and a prayer. I named the account 'MAR' in the app. It felt dramatic. I kept it.

Factory payroll day and, for once, I didn't do mental math all morning. R$ 3.800, rent paid, bus pass renewed, a little left. I bought myself a sketchbook that cost too much and felt like a thief for twenty minutes. Then I drew the cashier and felt better.
Tio Beto, I played 'Asa Branca' today, alone, in my room, without anyone clapping. I got to the second verse and stopped. I'm writing this so you know I'm still trying, even if slowly.

Portuguese text: Dia de sol e vento, fui caminhar no Passeio Público sozinha. Desenhei as pessoas no banco, um homem com violão que não tocava, uma criança perseguindo pombo. Senti vontade de mostrar pro Tio Beto e não mandei. Acho que queria guardar um dia só pra mim.
A cold front came through and I brought Limonada inside wearing my scarf again. She's bigger now, ten leaves, maybe eleven. I counted twice to be sure. She's fine. I'm the one who panics.
Call with Vó Lúcia. She told the Coronel story again. This time he waits at the gate for ten years. I wrote down every version. They get braver each telling.
Bus driver changed the route slightly and now we pass a little square with a lemon tree. I looked at it so long the man next to me asked if I knew it. I said 'she's family'. He moved seats.
Tried to learn three chords on Tio Beto's violão again. Got two and a half. He said 'a half is honest,' which might be the nicest thing anyone said to me this month.

The sea dream again. This time I was holding someone's hand, but I couldn't see whose. We were at the edge and the water was warm. I woke up and my fingers were curled like I'd been holding on. I didn't write down whose hand. Maybe that's the point.

Called Vó on Sunday. She told me she dreamed of Coronel again, walking her to school. 'He was very patient with me', she said. I drew the tail first, because that's the part I keep getting wrong in my head.

Swimming. Not lessons yet, just the idea of lessons. I googled 'adult beginner swim class Curitiba' and then closed the tab. Then reopened it. Then closed it. The tabs are a timeline of my courage. I'm somewhere between tab four and five.
Mom, you printed my comics and put them on the fridge. You didn't say anything, but Bia's mom told me. I'm not going to mention it. I'm just going to keep drawing.
Money check: R$ 2.100 saved. First time I have a number in the bank that doesn't make me want to cry. I named the savings 'MAR' in the app and felt powerful for about four seconds.
Cláudio retired cake at the factory, everyone signed a card. I drew a tiny motor with a party hat. He said it's the most accurate thing in the building. I'm putting it on my tombstone, eventually.

There's a bakery near the factory that makes pão de queijo so good I almost missed my shift. I told Cláudio and he went, came back with two bags, and for once we agreed on something completely. He said 'this is the only correct engineering in this building'. He wasn't wrong.

Money check: R$ 3.800 came in, same as last month, and somehow the month still ends with R$ 200 and a prayer. I paid Mom back the dentist money from 2015 and she refused again. I bought her a printer. She uses it to print my comics and hasn't said that out loud, which is her way of saying she likes them.
Money check: paid Mom back the dentist money from 2015? She refused again, so I bought her a printer. She uses it for photos of nephews. I'm pretending not to be jealous. I'm definitely jealous.
Fim de mês, R$ 280 na conta, sete dias até o salário. Vivo de RU e bolachas da mãe, mas agora pelo menos tenho um salário que chega. É engraçado como o mesmo medo de 2014 soa diferente com 23 anos.

Found an old Interbairros strip on my phone: Seu Ivo and Juca. I showed it to a coworker who said 'this is cute.' Cute. I wanted to say 'this is the most honest thing I've ever made.' I said 'obrigada' instead.
Bia sent a photo of her window in Floripa. The sea is right there, blue and smug. I stared at it for ten minutes and then drew it from memory, badly, which is still drawing.
Therapy? Not yet. But I started writing down every dream. The sea one is in there, plus a new one: I'm at a bus stop and every bus is going to the beach. I wake up annoyed I chose the wrong one.

Money check: first time I paid Mom back the dentist money from 2015. She refused, so I bought her a printer. She called to say it was 'too much'. Then she printed three of my comics. I'm choosing to read that as love.
Dreamed I was painting a wall blue and my brush turned into a lemon. I woke up wanting to paint my room, which I cannot do in a rental. The lemon, however, is achievable.

Vó Lúcia asked me to send her a drawing of the farm dog, Coronel. I sent a sketch of a black dog under a jabuticabeira. She called back and said 'he was more brown than black'. Then: 'but yes, that's him'. I cried a little at my desk. Nobody at the factory saw because I was looking at blueprints, very professional.

Mom called to ask if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said yes again. Still lying. The sketchbook now lives on the kitchen table, which is braver than under the mattress but still not brave enough to show her.

Called Vó Lúcia and she said the lemon tree in her yard is full this year. I asked her to send a photo and she sent me a picture of the sky by mistake. I kept it. The sky was very blue. It felt like a postcard from a woman who doesn't know she's poetic.

Therapy thoughts without therapy: I'm good at measuring vibrations and I'm good at drawing motors, and one of those makes me feel like myself. Guess which. I'm not quitting anything today. Just writing it down so future me can't pretend she didn't know.
Sunday with Vó Lúcia. She told the story of Coronel again, the farm dog, the gate, the jabuticabeira. This time he got braver. I wrote down the version with the bravest Coronel so far.

Bus 7am. The new driver waves at Seu Ivo. Seu Ivo waves back. Juca says bom dia. This tiny exchange is the most reliable part of my day. I drew it again because I'm afraid of forgetting small routines. Maybe that's why I draw.

Tentei aprender 'Asa Branca' de novo no violão do Tio Beto. Cheguei até o segundo verso e esqueci tudo. Ele bateu palma mesmo assim. Isso é mais doloroso que crítica. Ele não pediu nem nada. Só bateu palma.
Vó Lúcia told me a new version of the Coronel story: he used to sleep in the middle of the road and cars always stopped. 'Respeito por animal', she said. I'm drawing it on Sunday.
Drew the factory floor during lunch. The machines look like animals if you squint, or if you're tired. I'm both. One looks like a tired horse and I named it Claudio Junior. Cláudio approved.

Tio Beto, I'm writing this to you even though you'll probably laugh. You handed me the violão at Festa Junina and didn't ask for 'Asa Branca'. That was worse than asking. I'm practicing now, quietly, in my room, because I don't want the next 'one more year' to be just a saying. Thank you for clapping even when I forgot the second verse.
Interbairros comics: 1.200 followers. Someone drew fan art of Seu Ivo and Juca. It's not very good and I saved it in a folder called 'proof'. Proof of what, I don't know.
Therapist I don't have yet would say something about how I keep drawing the sea instead of going to it. I don't have a therapist yet, so I just say it to Limonada. She's a good listener.
Visited the RU for nostalgia and the bolachas Mom sends are still better than anything. The line was longer and the tables smaller. Some things improve by staying ugly.
Festa Junina leftovers at Tio Beto's. He played 'Asa Branca' and I sang the first verse from the kitchen. He didn't turn around. He didn't need to.

I opened an old notebook from 2016 and found the first Interbairros sketches. They're clumsy and I love them. Posted one today, no caption, and three people liked it. Small, but it felt like opening a window in a room I forgot existed.
Tio Beto came to Curitiba and we had lunch at the RU. He said 'at least the pastel is the same' and I said 'at least we are too'. He patted my hand and didn't say anything else. That was enough.

In Portuguese: Sonhei com Vó Lúcia contando a história do Coronel de novo. Dessa vez o cachorro esperava na porta da escola e eu estava dentro da escola desenhando. Quando acordei, desenhei a jabuticabeira antes de esquecer.

Portuguese text: Limonada perdeu uma folha e eu entrei em pânico. A Bia disse 'é só outono'. Eu disse 'ela não tem outono, ela é uma limoeira'. A Bia disse 'você está falando de árvore como se fosse filha'. Ela tem razão. Coloquei a folha no caderno.
Desenhei o Seu Ivo de memória no bloco de notas do celular. O papagaio saiu melhor do que ele. Acho que é porque eu conheço melhor a Juca do que o homem. Isso diz algo sobre mim.

I drew a strip about the 7am bus during a meeting about vibration analysis. Nobody noticed. The most suspicious thing was my smile. I think I'm becoming the kind of person who draws in meetings, which is either rebellion or early burnout.
Bia sent a voice note from Floripa: ocean, wind, and her laughing. I listened to it four times. Then I drew a room with a blue window and no one in it. Maybe that's where I'm going.

Bia sent a photo of her new apartment. The window really is all blue. I stared at it and then drew a little Marina at the desk, seen from behind, with a lemon tree on the sill. She said 'you're going to visit and pretend you're not jealous'. I said 'I never pretend'. We both know that's a lie.
I opened the breakup capsule from February and didn't cry. I checked his Instagram zero times. Then once. Then zero again. Growth is not linear, it's a zigzag on a bus route.
At lunch I sketched the factory courtyard and Cláudio said 'that's the ugliest tree I've ever seen.' I said thank you. He didn't understand. I did.
Mom sent a screenshot of the new strip with a thumbs up emoji. No words. The emoji is new. I'm putting it in the same folder as the fan art.

Visited Bia in Floripa for the first time. The spare room really faces the sea. I stood at the window for twenty minutes and she took a photo of my back. Caption: 'finally'. I'm still thinking about that word.

Halloween isn't really a thing here, but Bia sent a photo of a pumpkin she carved. It looked like a potato with ambitions. I drew it and sent it back. She said it was better than the real one. I'm keeping that compliment.
Mom saw a new Interbairros strip I almost didn't post. She texted 'the old man looks like your grandfather'. It's the closest thing to a compliment she's given me this month. I'll take it.

Visited Bia in Floripa for the first time. The spare room really faces the sea. I stood at the window for twenty minutes. She took a photo of my back and captioned it 'finally'. I'm not sure what that means yet.

Tio Beto called to tell me he found my childhood drawing of the sea in a box. It's terrible. Blue scribbles and a sun with a face. He said 'you always wanted the ocean'. I said 'I still do'. He said 'I know'. Sometimes the obvious things are the hardest to say.
Vó Lúcia asked if I still dream of the sea. I said yes. She said 'one day you'll stop dreaming and just go'. Then she changed the subject to bolo de fubá. I wrote down both.

Tio Beto, I still haven't learned 'Asa Branca' all the way through. You probably already know that. But I played the first verse today without looking at my fingers and that felt like something. I'm counting it as progress, not failure.

Visited a cemetery with Mom for Dia de Finados and she talked to Vó Lúcia's friend's grave for ten minutes. I stood there holding flowers and thinking about Coronel under the jabuticabeira. Some stories only exist because someone tells them more than once.

Vó Lúcia told me the Coronel story again and this time the dog waited at the school gate in the rain. The first version had sun. I wrote both down. She said 'menina, cada vez o cachorro fica mais valente'. I said 'é porque você está contando'. She laughed like stairs. I want to keep that sound forever.
Sunday call with Vó Lúcia. She asked if I'm still engineering. I said yes. She asked if I'm still drawing. I said yes. She said 'good, one is for money, one is for you.' I wrote it down twice.
Back in Curitiba, missing the sea smell already. On the bus I drew a tiny wave in the condensation on the window. It lasted three stops. Small art, small audiences.
Vó Lúcia told me the Coronel story again. This time he walked her to school and also protected the chickens, which I don't remember from before. I wrote it down. The dog gets braver every telling.
Vó Lúcia's hands were cold when she held mine at lunch. She squeezed anyway. Write it down: cold hands, strong grip, the smell of her soap.

Vó Lúcia got a new hat for Sunday mass and asked me to draw her in it. I drew her in five minutes. She said 'you made me too serious.' I said 'that's how you look when you're happy, vó.' She laughed like stairs.
Piscina pública de novo. Fiquei no raso e um senhor de 70 anos nadou três voltas sem parar. Ele me chamou de 'a engenheira' e me deu uma dica sobre respiração. Eu engoli água e agradeço mesmo assim.

I woke up at 5:40 and actually went to the pool. Adult beginners, I am the youngest by 20 years and the worst by far. Dona Cida called me 'a engenheira' and swallowed less water than me. I came home smelling like chlorine and feeling like I had done something brave, which is embarrassing for a 23-year-old who can't float.

Worked late and ate a pastel from the stand near the factory. The woman there knows my order now: cheese, no egg. She asked why I'm always drawing on napkins. I said 'habit'. She said 'talent'. I think she was being kind, but I drew her hands. They're strong and wrinkled and good at holding hot food. I want to draw people more.

Festa Junina at Tio Beto's came early this year. I played 'Asa Branca' until the first verse and forgot the second. Tio Beto clapped and said 'one more year'. The words don't hurt as much. That might be growth.
At the factory, I organized the old drawings by year and found my first bus comic from 2016. Seu Ivo looked different. I think I made him kinder than real life, which is a good habit, maybe.

Tio Beto, I'm writing this because you'll open it on Festa Junina. I still can't play 'Asa Branca' past the second verse, but I keep trying because you keep clapping. One day I'll earn it. Or you'll clap anyway. Both are fine.

Cláudio retired this year, I mean his last day was months ago, but today I found a note he left in my desk: 'draw better than the CAD'. It's going on my wall, next to the old yogurt cup label I kept for no reason.

Vó Lúcia's birthday. I called twice because the first time she said 'who is this' even though she had just called me menina do mar. The second time she remembered and told me the same story about Coronel, but this time the dog waited in the rain. I wrote 'rain' in the margin of the drawing. It changes the whole picture.

Cold again, the kind that makes the bus windows fog up. A kid drew a smiley face on the fog and the woman next to me erased it with her sleeve, then drew a better one. I drew both in my notebook. The bus is still my favorite classroom.

Portuguese text: Visitei a Bia em Floripa pela primeira vez. O quarto de hóspedes realmente dá pro mar. Fiquei vinte minutos na janela sem falar nada. Ela tirou foto das minhas costas e escreveu 'finalmente'. Eu ri, mas acho que chorei um pouco também. Talvez ainda.
At work, a motor failed and I had to draw the repair diagram on the spot. My hand shook, but the drawing was good. I think that's what I want: hands that know what to do when the rest of me panics.

Visited Bia in Floripa for the first time. She was right, the spare room faces the sea. I stood at the window for twenty minutes with my hand on the glass. She took a photo of my back and said 'finally'. I pretended to be annoyed. I wasn't.
Bus 7am. The knitting lady brought me a small scarf for Limonada. 'Para a planta não ter frio', she said. It's green. I don't know what to do with it, but it's in my bag.
Mom called asking if I've 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said 'no, Mom' and this time it wasn't a lie. She hummed and changed the subject to the printer. Growth, maybe, for both of us.
Bia took me to Praia Mole at 6am. I put my feet in the water and refused to go further. She didn't push. That's why she's my person.
Visited Bia in Floripa for the first time. The spare room really faces the sea. I stood at the window for twenty minutes. She took a photo of my back and captioned it 'finally'.
Back from Floripa. The window really has the sea. I stood there for twenty minutes and Bia took my photo. I haven't looked at it yet. I'm afraid it will make me move too soon or too late.

Back from Floripa and the república smells like wet wood again. I unpacked my bag and found sand in my shoe. Not metaphorical, actual sand. I put it in a yogurt cup on the windowsill next to Limonada. The fridge rules say no names on cups anymore, but this one I'm keeping.
Vó Lúcia called me 'menina do mar' at lunch and Mom went quiet. I pretended not to notice, but I wrote it down immediately. That's two people now who know.

Visited Bia in Floripa for a long weekend. The spare room faces the sea and I stood at the window for twenty minutes while she made coffee. She took a photo of my back and said nothing. I understood everything.
Bia, if you moved to Floripa and the spare room really faces the sea, I'm visiting every two months. I'm not joking. I'll bring Limonada in the car. She can see the ocean finally.
Cold snap. Limonada stayed inside by my desk all weekend and grew one new leaf anyway. Stubborn plant. We get along.

Went to Curitiba's comics fair with Bia's friend from college, who knows everyone. I showed my strips to one editor and he said 'nice, keep going'. Two words and I floated home. I don't float anywhere else, so this matters.

Rain again. Curitiba does this in November, decides to be a sky. I drew the city as an umbrella with legs. It's silly. I like it. Maybe I'll post it. Maybe I won't. The account is quiet lately, but quiet is not dead. I keep telling myself that.

Bia sent a photo from Floripa: her window and the sea, blue and ridiculous. I zoomed in until I could see waves. Then I went back to my factory window and the parking lot. Not comparing. Comparing a little.
December light in Curitiba: short, golden, gone by five. I drew the church steeple from the bus window and the lady next to me said 'you draw fast'. I said 'I have to, the bus doesn't wait'.

The bus comics have 1,800 followers now. A stranger asked if Juca is based on a real parrot. I said 'based on a real feeling', which sounds profound but really means 'I cried at a bus stop'. Internet is weird.
Limonada lost a leaf during the move to the bigger pot. I kept it in my sketchbook like a tiny green receipt. She's tougher than she looks.

Limonada survived another frost by the window and dropped one leaf. I panicked and then remembered she did this last year and was fine. She has 27 leaves, or 26 now, and one stubborn bud. I admire stubborn things. I am one.

December already. The factory is doing inventory and I counted bolts for six hours. I drew a tiny bolt with a smile in the margin and Cláudio saw it. He said 'you're wasting your talent'. I said 'I know'. Neither of us said anything else. That's the most honest conversation we've had.

Bia, I booked the bus to Floripa for January. I'm coming. I'll sleep on your couch, drink bad coffee, and stand at your window like a person who has never seen the sea. Which, technically, I see in dreams more than in real life. Save the window for me. I'm serious.
December already. The factory put up a plastic Christmas tree that leans. I drew it. It looks sad and hopeful, which is December in general.
Money check: R$ 3.800 in, R$ 900 out for rent and pool, R$ 1.200 savings. The 'MAR' fund is real now. I didn't touch it when the car needed an alignment. That's new for me.
Drew a comic about a lemon going to the beach and not knowing how to swim. It's me, obviously. I'm subtle like that. Bia laughed and said 'publish it' and I said 'maybe in ten years'. Maybe.

Sunday call with Vó Lúcia. She asked if I'm still drawing. I said 'a little.' She said 'the world is full of people who draw a little.' I wrote that down because it sounded like both compliment and threat.

Limonada sobreviveu ao inverno da janela. Oito folhas, um caule insistente. Coloquei um galho de alecrim ao lado dela porque li que plantas gostam de companhia. Não sei se é verdade, mas eu também gosto de companhia, então faz sentido.

Portuguese text: Fui na casa da Vó Lúcia hoje. Ela fez bolo de fubá e disse que o ponto não estava bom, mas estava igual sempre. As mãos dela estavam frias quando segurou as minhas. Anotei isso: mãos frias, segurando firme. Não quero esquecer.

Mom asked if I'm still with 'that engineering job'. I said yes. She paused and said 'and the drawings?'. I said 'also yes'. She said 'good'. One word. I'm framing it in my head. I might draw it too: a woman saying 'good' while a lemon tree grows in the corner.
A Vó falou que minhas mãos ficam mais parecidas com as dela quando desenho. Eu não sabia disso. Fiquei com vontade de desenhar as mãos dela até decorar cada linha.

Bought Mom a printer for Christmas and wrapped it badly. She's going to pretend she doesn't know what it is and then use it for everything. I'm writing this so I remember: she uses it to print my comics. She hasn't said that yet, but she will.
Tio Beto called to ask about the violão. I said 'next Festa Junina'. He laughed, but softer than before. I think we're both tired of the joke.
In Portuguese: Natal chegando. A fábrica fechou mais cedo e eu desenhei o pátio vazio com a luz de dezembro. O Cláudio antigo teria dito 'muito artístico'. Eu diria 'está certo'. Estou aprendendo.
Money check: R$ 3.800, R$ 600 to Mom (she refused again, so I bought coffee), R$ 1.000 savings. I'm 23 and I have a savings account called MAR. 18-year-old me would laugh. I'm not laughing.

Limonada got a yellow leaf. I stared at it for five minutes like it was a personal attack. Then I watered her and moved her closer to the light. Being responsible for a plant is exhausting in a tiny, ridiculous way.
Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' on the violão at Sunday lunch and I sang along to the second verse only. He didn't comment. Progress is quiet sometimes.

Tio Beto, thank you for the violão that is technically yours but lives at my apartment. I practiced 'Asa Branca' today and reached the middle before panic. You clapped once, from the kitchen, without looking. That was enough.
Vó Lúcia sent me a voice note saying she misses my drawings. I sent her a photo of Limonada instead. She said 'the tree or you?' I said both. She laughed like stairs.

Last day of work before vacation. Cláudio gave me a notebook as a gift. On the first page he wrote: 'for the engineer who draws too much'. I think it was a compliment. I'm going to choose that. New notebook, new year, same Limonada. She is finally taller than the window, which feels like a sign.
Limonada has thirteen leaves and no flowers. Bia says she's 'stubborn like her owner'. I prefer 'patient'. I left her on the windowsill in the sun for an extra hour today.

At work, the new intern asked why there are drawings of buses on my locker. I said 'they're diagrams'. He believed me. I feel both guilty and delighted. Cláudio didn't even look up, which means he knows and has decided not to comment.

I didn't go to Floripa for New Year, too much money, too much work. Instead I'm going to Vó Lúcia's. She said she doesn't want to travel to the beach anymore. I'm bringing drawing paper and the bolo recipe I still haven't mastered. We'll see which one survives the night.

Graduation anniversary drink with Mom. She asked if I'm still sure about only two years at the factory. I said yes. She said 'your grandmother always said you were menina do mar'. I didn't know Vó said that to her too.

Last workday before holidays. The factory is quiet and I sketched the coffee machine again, but this time it had a Santa hat. Cláudio said 'you're hopeless' and took the drawing home. I hope he framed it.

Christmas prep at Mom's. She made bolo de fubá and asked me to draw the jabuticabeira on the kitchen wall in pencil. She erased it after ten minutes but didn't erase everything. A branch is still there. I noticed. She didn't say anything. I didn't either. We're related.
End of year. Limonada is in the window with a red bow Bia bought. Vó Lúcia said the tree looks 'Christmas-y.' I said she looks Christmas-y. She hung up. I'll call again later.
Packed for Matinhos. Bia is coming. I brought the sketchbook and one pencil. The sea can wait until tomorrow but I'll probably draw it tonight from memory, as usual.
Drew Vó Lúcia holding the phone, after all. Both hands this time, one on each side. I don't know which is right, so I drew both and let it stay wrong. Some things are better not resolved.

Natal se aproximando. Vó Lúcia ligou e disse que a gente se vê no Ano Novo. Mãe fez bolo de fubá e ficou bom demais, quase suspeito. Guardei um pedaço na geladeira para comer amanhã cedo. Pequenos prazeres, grandes mentiras sobre disciplina.

At the Sunday lunch, Tio Beto put the violão on my chair without a word and walked to the kitchen. I played two bars of 'Asa Branca' and stopped because my hands shook. He came back, said nothing, and sat down. We ate. It was enough.

Christmas leftovers and one more week of 2019. I drew the sea dream from memory and it looked wrong, too small. The real sea is bigger than I remember, and I haven't even been in it properly yet. Next year, maybe. I said that last year too. Writing it down again so it stays true.

After Christmas I sat on Vó Lúcia's porch and she told me about the sea near Irati, which doesn't exist, but she described it anyway: calm, warm, with a dog waiting at the edge. I drew it while she talked. She fell asleep mid-sentence. I kept drawing. The dog has Coronel's eyes.

Bia sent a photo from Floripa: her window, all blue, and a tiny cactus on the sill. Caption: 'your turn soon'. I saved it and looked at it three times. Then I went to the bus stop and drew the man selling coconut water. Ordinary day, ordinary joy.

Matinhos again. I stood with my feet in the water at midnight. Not in it, just at the edge. The water was cold and perfect and I didn't go further. Next year, maybe. Or the year after. I'm keeping the deadline loose.

New Year's Eve approaching. Last year I put my feet in the water in Matinhos and it felt like enough. This year I'm at Vó Lúcia's, where there is no sea, only a yard and a persimmon tree. She says the ocean is 'overrated and cold'. She's never seen it. I love her. I might not go to the beach this year. That feels okay.

New Year's Eve tomorrow. This year I'm not going to Matinhos, too tired and too broke. I'll stay in Curitiba with Limonada and maybe call Vó Lúcia at midnight. I want next year to be the year I go back to the sea, even just for a weekend.

New Year's Eve at Vó Lúcia's. She didn't want to travel. She stayed awake until midnight just to prove she could. Her hands were cold when she held mine. Write it down: her hands were cold and she held on.

New Year's Eve tomorrow and I'm spending it at home with Limonada and a terrible movie. I thought about going out but the sea isn't here yet and Bia is in Floripa. Maybe next year I'll go there. Maybe next year I'll be braver. The lemon tree is enough company for tonight.

New Year at Vó Lúcia's. She stayed awake until midnight just to prove she could and then fell asleep on the couch at 12:03. Her hands were cold when she held mine. I'm writing it down because last time she said 'menina do mar' and I want to remember where I heard it first. Happy New Year, future me. Did you go to the sea?

New Year at Vó Lúcia's. She fell asleep at 11:50 and still swore she saw fireworks. I stood in the yard with my hands in my pockets because it was cold and I didn't want to wake her. No sea this year. Just a yard, a persimmon tree, and a woman who calls me menina do mar without knowing what the sea looks like. I think she means something else. I think I do too.
New Year. Mom, Vó Lúcia, Bia on the phone from Floripa. No beach. Vó stayed awake until midnight to prove she could. I stood by the window at 11:59 and imagined the water. Next year, maybe.

New Year at Vó Lúcia's this time, she didn't want to travel to the beach. She stayed awake until midnight just to prove she could. Her hands were cold when she held mine. Write it down: her hands were cold and she held on.

First Sunday of the year and Vó Lúcia stayed on the phone for ninety minutes. I tried to hang up twice. She noticed both times and talked longer. Her hands were cold again last week; I'm writing it down because I think I'll forget the temperature of her hands before anything else.

First week back at the factory after the holidays and I already drew a motor casing in the margin of the production report. Cláudio didn't say anything, which means he saw it and didn't mind. Progress. Limonada has a new leaf. It's a good day.

First Monday of the year and the Interbairros was late, so I stood in the cold long enough to draw the kiosk lady folding napkins. She caught me and said I made her look too tired. I said that's how everyone looks at 6:40. She laughed and gave me a pão de queijo "para fechar a boca". Ate it on the bus and got crumbs on my notebook. Good start.
