Bus 7am, still Interbairros II, but no parrot. I keep looking for Seu Ivo in the crowd and then remembering Ponta Grossa. Drew Juca on my notebook margin anyway, because habits are stubborn. The old lady across the aisle asked if I was drawing her; I said 'no, a parrot', and she looked offended and pleased at the same time.

Bus 7am again. No parrot man anymore but a new guy boards every day with a plastic bag of laranjas and eats them one by one. By the end of the line the bag is empty and the bus smells like citrus. Drew him. Might be Seu Laranja.

Bus 7am, Interbairros II, sem o Seu Ivo já nem me cai. O motorista hoje falou 'bom dia, motorista' no lugar do papagaio. Acho que ele sentiu falta também. Desenhei a cena no caderno de reuniões e o Cláudio achou que era esboço de peça.

Curitiba is doing that thing where it rains for twenty minutes, stops, and everyone pretends it didn't. The bus was late anyway. I drew a man on the 7am line whose tie looked like a snake; he caught me and asked if the snake was friendly. I said, depends on the day.

Slept badly because of the heat and woke up with the fan pointing at the wall, as usual. Made coffee too strong and drank it reading about engineering stress tests, which felt like a metaphor I'm too tired to write down. The lemon tree has seven new leaves. I counted them like they're going to be graded.

I opened the 2016 yogurt-cup capsule early by accident last week and read 'do you still have a lemon tree?' Limonada is five now and still no lemons, but she is alive, which is the part I'm keeping. I didn't write an answer. I'm writing one now: yes.

Hoje choveu a manhã inteira e o ônibus Interbairros veio atrasado vinte minutos. Desenhei três pessoas sem olhar para o papel, só sentindo o movimento do ônibus. Saíram tortas, mas vivas. Acho que estou aprendendo a desenhar sem medo de errar.

It's hot enough that the asphalt smells like tar. I walked to the bakery at 6am and the bread was still warm. Ate three pães de queijo on the street like someone who doesn't pay rent. I pay rent. I'm aware.

Bia, você disse que Florianópolis tem cheiro de maresia. Hoje choveu em Curitiba e o arco-íris saiu do meu prédio até a Pedreira. Quase tirei foto, mas sabia que não ia ficar igual. Guardo em desenho, que é onde coisas grandes cabem melhor.

Bia texted me a photo of the sea from her window at 6am, with the caption 'still saving the room'. I stared at it through my entire lunch break. Curitiba looked very gray today, but I'm not complaining to the weather, it's not its fault.

Vó Lúcia called to say she made bolo de fubá and it's 'a little burnt on one side, the way you like it'. I don't remember liking it burnt. I told her I'd come Sunday. The bus driver was the same one from the parrot days; he honked at me. I waved like an idiot.
Bia sent a voice note complaining that the sea outside her window is 'always doing something'. I replied that my window faces a building with a pigeon problem. Solidarity.

Bus 7am again. Interbairros II. The parrot man wasn't there, but the driver had a sticker of a green parrot on his windshield. I think he misses him too. I drew the bus with steam on the windows and it looked like I drew a tiny ocean inside it.

Vó Lúcia called at 9pm to ask if I had eaten and then, when I said yes, to tell me about the woman at the market who tried to sell her a "limão orgânico" for R$ 4. "Limão is limão, menina." She is right. I drew her hand holding a lemon. The fingers are hard to get right.

Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. Vó brought pão de queijo and critiqued my posture at the table. Tio Beto taught me a fourth chord. He says I sound like someone stepping on a cat, which is fair. He then played 'Asa Branca' himself to show me how it's done and I had to pretend not to be emotional about it.

Factory lunch: Cláudio brought brigadeiros because it's his birthday, and I ate three before realizing the meeting was in five minutes. I spent the whole meeting thinking my shirt had chocolate on it. It didn't. I checked twice in the bathroom. The motor drawings I made after lunch were better than any I've done at 9am. Notes for future me: sugar as methodology.

Choveu o dia inteiro e Limonada ficou brilhante na janela. Desenhei uma casinha com árvore de limão e uma menina olhando da cozinha. Não é eu. Ou é um pouco eu. Ainda não sei desenhar poemas, então desenho casas.

Bia, I miss you in Curitiba. Floripa is lucky. I keep your old mug in the cupboard facing the one I use at breakfast, like a tiny conversation. Today I drank coffee out of it by mistake and felt like I'd stolen something. Write back soon, even if it's just 'saudade'.
Bia sent a voice note complaining that the sea in Floripa is too loud at 5am. I replied with a 40-second recording of my neighbor's dog barking. Friendship is competitive misery.

Money check: R$ 1.100 left, 29th of the month. I spent too much on art supplies again. The paper I bought is beautiful and I'm afraid to use it, which defeats the purpose. I'll use it tomorrow. Or next week. Definitely this month.

Água fria de fevereiro, janela aberta, e Limonada com três folhas novas na ponta dos galhos. A Bia disse que a árvore está me imitando: cresce aos poucos e reclama do clima. Talvez seja o melhor elogio que a Bia já me deu.

Bia, you moved to Floripa months ago and I still send you voice notes as if you were in the next room. Today I found your old hoodie in my closet and wore it to work. It smells like the bus. That might be the laundry's fault. Miss you. Save me the side of the bed that isn't facing the sea.

Bus 7am, Interbairros II, still. No parrot man anymore, but there's a new woman who knits on every ride and once offered me a tiny red sock without explanation. I said obrigada and put it in my bag. It's on my desk now.

Money check: paid the IPVA today and felt like an adult, then bought a pastel de palmito to celebrate and undid the feeling. R$ 2.800 left until the 15th. Living on rice, beans and stubbornness. Limonada got watered, at least.

Money check: R$ 1.240 left, it's the 3rd, and I just realized I have been buying coffee every day. Not even good coffee. Tomorrow I'll take the thermos. (I said this in 2014 too. I am consistent in the wrong things.)

Limonada has three new leaves and a brown tip on one. I moved her 10 centimeters away from the window because I read that drafts are bad, then moved her back because she looked sad. Plants are dramatic. I am a person who says a plant looks sad, and I accept this.
Tio Beto sent a voice note singing 'Asa Branca' slightly off-key. I played it twice. He asked if I was still practicing. I said 'working on it'. That's technically true and emotionally a lie.
Found an old sketchbook page from 2016, Seu Ivo and Juca, with a coffee stain over the parrot. I almost threw it away and then put it back in the drawer. Some stains are architecture.

Vó Lúcia me ligou para dizer que hoje fez sol em Irati e ela pendurou lençóis no varal. Parece simples, mas ela falou como quem avisasse que o mundo continuava funcionando. Eu anotei na margem do caderno: 'lençóis no sol'. Quero desenhar isso.

Fevereiro e já choveu três dias seguidos. Limonada está na janela e parece grato. Eu também estou grata, menos pelo mofo no banheiro. Marquei 'ir ao dentista' na agenda pela terceira vez e não fui. Um dia.

Money check: R$ 2.100 left after rent, and it's the 9th, which is not terrible and not great. I bought a new sketchbook instead of a proper lunch. RU was closed, so I had a pastel and called it dinner. Still drawing, still tired.

Mom, if you're reading this, I'm sorry I forgot to call Sunday. I spent the afternoon drawing the farm from Vó's stories and lost track. The jabuticabeira has too many branches and I keep wanting to add more fruit.
Valentine's Day in Curitiba, no one to send it to. I drew a small heart in the margin of a factory report and felt ridiculous. Then I drew another one. The second was better. I'm keeping both.

Opened the old breakup capsule from 2018 early by accident. I'm fine. Better than fine. I spent Valentine's at the factory cafeteria eating a coxinha and drawing a motor. Nobody asked. It was a good day.

Bia, you sent me a photo of the sea from your balcony at 6:40am and I stared at it for ten minutes on the bus. Seu Ivo would have liked your view. Juca too. I miss both of them, even though I invented one of the names.

Vó Lúcia ligou dizendo que Coronel, o cachorro da fazenda, esperou o pai dela na porteira mesmo com chuva. Ela disse: 'não era chuva, menina, ele só esperava'. Gostei mais dessa versão. O cachorro fica maior a cada história. Eu também.

Rain all day. The factory smells like oil and wet shoes. Cláudio brought cake for no reason and we ate it at 10am. I drew a diagram of a motor, then in the margin a motor with legs running away from the rain. The second one felt more useful. I'm keeping both.
Mãe, I made the bolo de fubá from your instructions and it cracked right down the middle. It still tasted like home, so I'm counting it as a win. Save me a slice of the next one?
Limonada está soltando uma folha nova por dia, exatamente como se tivesse agenda. Ainda sem limão. Bia diz que é 'lemon tree em fase de autoconhecimento'. Anotei isso para desenhar depois.

Bia, today I saw a lemon for sale at the feira that looked exactly like the ones Vó used for bolo de fubá and I bought it and smelled it at the bus stop like a weirdo. When this opens, I hope you still laugh at me for that. Also: Floripa sounds impossible right now, but your window keeps showing up in my dreams.
Dreamed of the sea again. Same beach, but this time there was a lemon tree growing in the sand. I woke up and checked on Limonada. Four leaves, no lemons. She's trying. I'm trying.

Limonada has exactly fourteen leaves today. I counted while pretending to water the other plants. She is turning into a small tree with attitude and absolutely no fruit, like a tiny stubborn engineer.

Limonada got a new leaf after I moved her closer to the bathroom window. She's dramatic about light. Bia says I'm projecting, but I think the lemon tree and I have the same personality: we both need sun and complain when we don't get it.

Money check before everything changed: R$ 2.100 left after rent and bills, which is not brave-fund territory but enough for a few pastéis. I wanted to visit Matinhos in March. I wanted to, and then I didn't.

Dreamed about the sea again. Same beach, same warmth, same feet that won't move. But this time I was holding someone's hand. Couldn't see whose. Woke up and drew it fast before it left. Vó Lúcia says hands in dreams are never random. She may be right about most things, but this one I'm not sure.

Money check: R$ 1.900 left on the 28th, which is better than the R$ 340 of 2014 but still not the 'courage fund' I keep talking about. I spent R$ 40 on pens last week. I'm not apologizing. The old me would have apologized.

Bus ride in Curitiba with no parrot man. I still look for him every time, which is ridiculous because he moved. The new passenger on the 7am route is a woman with a plastic bag full of lemons. I'm choosing to see it as a sign and not ask questions.

Leap day. I almost forgot. Nothing happened, which feels like the point of a day that only exists every four years: it doesn't have to be special, it just has to be there. I drew the lemon tree. It has a leaf that looks like a little flag. I named it nothing. Some things can just be leaves.

Mãe, I know you think I should focus on engineering. But today I drew the clouds from the bus window and a man asked if it was for sale. I said no. I don't know why I said no. Maybe because it's the first thing I've drawn that felt mine. I'll bring it to Sunday lunch.

A vizinha from 402 left a chocolate on my doormat with a note: 'para a menina da planta'. It was Limonada's fame, not mine. I ate the chocolate and moved Limonada two centimeters closer to the window. She deserves applause.

Thermos coffee improved my morning by 30%. The rest of the day continues to be engineering. Cláudio brought bolo de fubá da esposa e eu comi dois pedaços porque lembrava o da Vó. Não disse isso para ninguém.
Tio, I practiced 'Asa Branca' twice this week and only forgot the second verse once. Progress. I still want to play it at Festa Junina without you clapping out of pity. Okay, a little pity is fine.

Mom asked me, again, if I am "still doing those drawings". I said sometimes. She said "hmm" in the way that means she has opinions. Then she sent a photo of the bolo de fubá she made, and in the background, on the fridge, one of my Interbairros strips. She didn't mention it. I didn't either. Progress.

Women's Day. Mom sent a message saying 'você desenha tão bem'. I stared at it for ten minutes. She has never said that before. I didn't reply with anything clever, just 'obrigada, mãe'. It was enough.

Dia das mulheres e minha mãe mandou mensagem com um 'orgulho de você' que me fez chorar no onibus, sozinha, com o senhor ao lado perguntando se eu estava bem. Eu disse que estava bem. Era verdade e mentira ao mesmo tempo.

Mãe, as bolachas chegaram e a geladeira virou prateleira de padaria. Desenhei as embalagens porque tem sua letra nos rótulos. Você vai dizer que é desperdício. Não é. É arquivo. Guardei até os papéis.

PT: Hoje meu feed tinha um desenho antigo dos Interbairros, o Seu Ivo e o Papagaio. Uma pessoa comentou 'eu conheço esse senhor'. Eu não conheço, mas inventei o nome. Às vezes me sinto fraudadora. Outras vezes me sinto arqueóloga de ônibus.

Weather: rain all week, the kind that makes the república smell like wet dog. I stepped in a puddle on the way to the factory and my shoe squeaked the whole shift. Cláudio asked why I was walking like a cartoon. I said I'm making art. He believed me.
Working from my bedroom now. The factory sent a laptop and a chair with no lumbar support. I drew a little stick figure in the corner of a vibration report today. Nobody noticed. That's good and sad.

Working from home now. My desk is the kitchen table and my chair is a stool. I measured vibrations all morning, then drew Seu Ivo from memory at lunch. His parrot had a red mark on one wing that I never put in the comics. I don't know why I remember that.

Vó Lúcia called to say the lemon tree in her courtyard is blooming. She said, 'yours still hasn't given you a lemon?' and I said 'no, avó'. She said, 'patience, menina do mar, patience'. I wrote it down because her voice sounded like a secret.

A Sunday with nowhere to go. I cleaned the kitchen, called Vó Lúcia, and then drew the lemon tree from memory because Limonada looked offended on the windowsill. The drawing came out more patient than I am.
Home office day one. My desk is the kitchen table and my chair is a dining chair that hates me. I drew a tiny dinosaur on my meeting notes. Thaís didn't notice. I think.

Limonada has a new leaf, the first in months. I talk to her while I make coffee. The girls think I'm crazy but they also talk to the fridge, so we're even. She's small and stubborn, like Vó says about me, except in a nice way.
Bus driver today said 'bom dia, motorista' to himself, I'm sure of it. The bus was empty except for us. I drew it and sent to Bia. She replied 'era o papagaio?' I replied 'não, era pior: era eu'.

We're being told to work from home starting Monday. I brought home my monitor, my notebook and three pens. The office plant stayed. I hope someone waters it. I hope the plant survives this, like the rest of us.

Started a tiny sketchbook just for the lemon tree. Page one: Limonada in the sun. Page two: Limonada in the rain. Page three: Limonada ignoring my expectations, again. It's the most reliable relationship of my life.

Domingo na fábrica é mais silencioso do que pensei. Trabalho remoto, café ruim, Limonada na janela. Desenhei o teclado e o monitor e achei estranho: um desenho de tela dentro de uma tela. Cláudio riria disso.

Tio Beto texted me a voice note that is just him humming 'Asa Branca' and then saying "calma, estou aprendendo outra coisa". He is 67 and learning accordion. I told him he is my hero. He said "menina, não exagera". I did not exaggerate.
Mãe, estou bem, não estou saindo de casa, estou comendo, estou desenhando. A Limonada está bem. Prometo que ligo para a vó todo dia. Obrigada por ter mandado os bolachas, chegaram hoje. Beijos.

Fiz um quadrinho sobre um ônibus que vira aquário quando chove. Ninguém vai ler, mas eu gostei. O velho do papagaio não está mais na linha, e isso ainda dói um pouco. Desenhei um motorista sozinho dizendo bom dia para ninguém. Parece triste, mas é carinhoso.

Work asked me to review vibration reports from home starting next week. I made a tiny desk in my bedroom with a lamp and three mugs. The first mug is coffee, the second tea, the third 'emotional support water'.

Factory: Cláudio asked me to redraw the assembly diagram for the new line because the official one 'looks like a crime scene'. I did it in one afternoon and he stuck it on the wall. It's the most seen drawing I've ever made and nobody knows it's mine. Good enough for now.

Mom, I know you're going to ask if I'm working, eating, and if I've given up on the drawings yet. Yes, yes, and no. I have a sketchbook on the desk and I'm using it again. Please don't ask for proof. Love, Marina.
Day 12 of lockdown. I cleaned the whole apartment, including behind the fridge, which I didn't know had a behind. Then I drew the fridge with a face. It looks tired. Same.

Working from home started. My bedroom is now also a factory, which means the bed is technically a desk and the desk is technically a clothes rack. I've drawn three motors from the kitchen table. The coffee is better than the RU. The loneliness is worse, but I won't write that in the office log.

Vó Lúcia told me over the phone that the dog Coronel used to carry her lunch in a cloth bag. She said 'he never dropped it, not once'. I wrote that down. I'm going to draw Coronel with a lunch bag even though she didn't ask for it.

Bia, your voice note made me laugh on the bus, except I wasn't on the bus, I was in my bedroom, which is worse. Thank you for sending me the photo of the sea from your window again. I looked at it for too long and burned the rice. Calling it 'Marina's risotto now'.

Called Vó. She told me about Coronel again, the dog who walked her to school in Irati. This time he also supposedly caught a chicken thief. The story grows every call. I wrote down this version. Coronel is becoming a legend.

Vó Lúcia told me the Coronel story again, but this time she said he was 'um cachorro de verdade, não desses de hoje'. I asked what that meant. She said he had patience. I think she was talking about more than the dog.

Video call with Bia. She made me laugh so hard I spilled water on the keyboard. She's painting the spare room walls blue, 'for when you come'. I cried after hanging up, which is ridiculous because she's in Floripa and I'm in Curitiba and nothing changed except the walls.

The lemon tree has eight new leaves and no lemons, as usual. I moved it closer to the window and told it, out loud, "você está atrasada, mas eu entendo". The girls heard me and now call me "a mãe do limão". I am accepting the title.
Bia, if you read this later: I dreamed you were standing on my balcony and the sea was outside the window, but it was actually just your towel drying. My brain misses you and is bad at metaphors.

Called Vó, she told the Coronel story again. This time he was so brave he walked her to school in the rain with a broken umbrella in his mouth. I don't think that part is true. I wrote it down exactly anyway.

Called Vó Lúcia. She talked for one hour about Coronel again, the dog from Irati, and I wrote down that this time he waited at the gate even in the rain. She corrected me: 'not even rain, Marina, he just waited.' I like that she remembers it differently each time. It makes the story bigger, not smaller.

Called Vó Lúcia at 8pm and she said she had already eaten dinner, which is a lie because I could hear the pot. She talked for 47 minutes about a cat on her street that she calls Coronel II, because of course she does. I didn't correct her. Coronel II is apparently very brave.
Rain all day. No bus, no factory, no Cláudio. I drew Vó Lúcia's hands from memory and they came out wrong three times. I kept the third one anyway. She'll say I made them too thin. She's right.

Pandemic. Working from my bedroom. I can't visit Vó Lúcia, so I call her every day now and she complains that it's too much and then talks for an hour. I started drawing again because there's nothing else to do: small drawings of her stories, the farm in Irati, the dog called Coronel. She doesn't know. I want to give her a little book when this is over.
Five years since Vó told me the Coronel story. I'm drawing the whole thing now, frame by frame, from every version she told me. Coronel is very brave in the last frame. He deserves it.

Five years today since Vó told me the Coronel story. I asked her again on the phone and she added that he once barked at the teacher for giving her too much homework. Every version gets better. I'm keeping them all in a folder called 'Coronel V1-V7'.

Video call with Vó Lúcia. She put the phone so far away I could see her whole kitchen and a calendar from 2018. She talked for an hour about the dog who used to follow her to school. I could listen for ten hours.
Sonhei que o mar era feito de bolachas do RU e eu tentava nadar com uma colher. Vó Lúcia diria que preciso comer mais. Ela provavelmente tem razão. Tomei café e banana no jantar ontem.

Rain all day in Curitiba, the kind that makes the bus stop smell like wet bread. I drew the woman next to me at the supermarket, from memory, in the car while waiting. She had a purple umbrella and a very serious expression about bananas. I think I'm getting better at hands.

Home office day 3. The kitchen table is my office now. Bia and I video called over lunch and ate the same feijoada from two cities, which felt like a trick. I drew her laugh in the margin of a meeting note. The drawing is better than the note.

Bia called and said she could hear birds outside her window, and that the air smelled like salt. I went to my window and heard a bus and smelled someone's barbecue. We are in the same country. It doesn't feel like it.

Home office day one. My desk is the kitchen table, my coworker is a bag of farinha, and the wifi dies every time someone in the building showers. I miss the Interbairros but not the 6:30 alarm. Drew Vó Lúcia's farm from memory. The jabuticabeira is too big. It should be too big.

PT: Fiz bolo de fubá da receita do caderno da Vó, mas ficou baixo. Acho que bati pouco. Comi metade ainda quente, com manteiga, olhando pela janela. A mesa ficou com farinha por toda parte e eu não limpei de propósito porque me pareceu um bom sinal.

Tried to cook feijão from scratch. Soaked beans overnight, forgot them in the morning, remembered at lunch, panicked. Final result: edible but spiritually tired. Bia would say 'at least it's not burned'. Bia is generous.

I started drawing Vó's stories on loose sheets: the farm, the gate, the dog under the jabuticabeira. She doesn't know. They are clumsy and too small but I think her hands are the hardest part. I keep getting the knuckles wrong.
Started a new notebook just for Vó Lúcia's stories. The first page is Coronel under the jabuticabeira, but I drew him too dignified. Real dogs have crooked ears. I'll fix it tomorrow.

Hoje Vó me contou que Coronel tinha medo de fogos de artifício. Ela disse que ele ia para baixo da cama e ela ia junto, porque 'cachorro também precisa de companhia no escuro'. Escrevi isso três vezes para não perder.

Português: Chama Vó de novo e ela me contou da jabuticabeira no sítio dos avós, como comia jabuticaba até a barriga doer. Ela ri alto ao contar. Anotei tudo. Quero desenhar essa árvore cheia de frutinha colada no tronco, parece milagre.

Called Vó for an hour. She talked about the weather in Irati, which is apparently colder than she'd like, and about a neighbor's cat that keeps stealing her laundry. No sea stories today. I drew the cat instead.

Pandemic dreams are weird. Last night I dreamed the sea was made of RU bolachas and I tried to swim in it with a spoon. Vó Lúcia would say I need to eat more. She's probably right. I had coffee and a banana for dinner yesterday.

Home office day 20-something. My desk is the kitchen table, so every email is replied with the fridge humming in the background. Limonada got a new leaf directly over the laptop camera. She is now part of my professional image.

Dia do Trabalho em casa. I ate a pastel de queijo straight from the pan at 11am and felt no shame. Then I drew the pan. Then I felt some shame. Then I ate another. The drawings are getting better at food than at motors, which is either a problem or a sign.
Tio Beto sent a voice note playing 'Asa Branca' badly and laughing. I played it three times. He asked if I was still practicing; I said yes. I am not practicing. I feel terrible about this.

Meu vizinho do lado toca violão toda noite às 21h, sempre a mesma música que eu não conheço. Hoje bati na parede três vezes no ritmo. Ele bateu de volta. Foi a interação social mais próxima que tive em semanas.

First mask with a little sun drawn on it in permanent marker. Thaís, my future manager (we haven't met yet, but I know she exists), would probably approve. The security guard at the factory asked if I made it myself. I said yes. He said 'ficou bonito'. Best review of 2020 so far.
Rain all day. I ate the last RU bolacha from Mom's stash and felt dramatic about it. Then I drew the bolacha. Art is sometimes just grief with crumbs.

Limonada deu mais uma folha depois que mudei para a janela da tarde. Ela é dramática com luz. A Bia diz que estou projetando, mas acho que a limoeira e eu temos a mesma personalidade: precisamos de sol e reclamamos quando não tem.

Money check, pandemic edition: I'm saving on bus fare and losing on snacks. The R$ 340/month girl from 2014 would not believe I now have a savings fund. She would also ask why I still eat like a student. Fair.

Rainy Monday. Worked in pajamas until 3pm then realized I hadn't eaten. Made instant noodles and felt like 18 again. Limonada got moved closer to the window for more light. She looked hopeful about it, or I'm projecting, which is fine.

Mother's Day. I sent Mom a drawing of Vó's hands, not the cake, just the hands. She didn't say anything for two days. Then she called and said 'you got the knuckles right'. I cried after hanging up. I'm putting this here so I don't forget.

Video call with Bia. She showed me her window in Floripa and the sea behind it. I put my phone on the pillow and just listened to the waves for five minutes while she typed. She said 'you're weird'. I said 'I know'. It was the best five minutes of the week.

I tried to learn 'Asa Branca' again, with the violão Tio Beto lent me and forgot to take back. Got as far as the first chorus. My fingertips hurt. Tio Beto would say 'one more year' and he'd be right again.

Started a small drawing of Vó Lúcia's farm from the phone description she gave me. The jabuticabeira is bigger in my head than any real tree. I put a little dog under it but I haven't decided if it's Coronel yet. I don't want to get it wrong.
Mãe, today I almost called you to say the bolo de fubá is on fire. It wasn't. But I thought of you. I know you'd say 'menina, coloca a tampa'. So I did. Worked.

Dinheiro: R$ 2.100 na conta e uma conta de luz que eu achei que ia ser mais barata. Comprei um caderno melhor e um café que custava caro demais. Me sinto rica por uma hora, depois me sinto adulta. Acho que é assim para todo mundo.
Vó asked if I was 'still hiding the drawings'. I said no, I'm making a small book for her. She went quiet and then asked if Coronel could be brown. He can. He will be.

Dreamed of the sea again. Same beach, same warm water, but this time there was a small dog running along the shore, not Coronel, just a dog. I didn't go in. I woke up with my calves tight and the feeling that I was close to something. I drew the dog before breakfast.

Bia, your voice note about the Floripa sunset was 47 seconds long and I listened to it four times. I drew the balcony railing from memory and added you as a tiny silhouette. It's not accurate, but the feeling is right. Miss you.

Vó Lúcia contou a história de Coronel pela quinta vez e eu anotei tudo. Desta vez o cachorro esperou mesmo com chuva. Ela corrigiu: 'não era chuva, menina, ele só esperava'. A memória dela muda e, strangely, fica mais certa.

Money check: the savings account has R$ 1.200 and I'm weirdly proud. Started calling it 'MAR' again in the app, like in 2022, except that's the future, so I'm calling it that in advance. Time travel banking.

Vó told me the Coronel story again, this time with a detail she'd never said before: he used to wait for her at the gate even on Sundays, when she didn't go to school. I asked why she never mentioned that. She said, 'nobody asks the right questions the first time'. I'm writing them down now.
Bia, your video call yesterday had you standing in front of the window so long I thought you were a screensaver. I miss you. Tell the sea I'm working on getting closer.

Six years since I wrote about the parrot man on the bus. Today I found the old Álgebra notebook in the drawer. The drawing of him is still good. The algebra is not. Some things improve with time, some don't.
A neighbor fixed my bicycle tire in exchange for a drawing of his cat. The cat is orange and enormous and looks suspiciously like a bread loaf. Fair trade.
Ran out of instant coffee and had to drink plain hot water like a person in a survival documentary. Limonada looked at me with judgment. I apologized to a plant. This is where I am.

Money check: R$ 2.400 left because there's nowhere to spend it. I bought pencils instead. And a small cactus. Limonada now has a roommate on the windowsill. I named him Carrinho because he's round. Limonada didn't react.

Mãe, you said on the phone that you're 'managing'. You used that word twice. I know you're not managing. I can't visit yet. I drew you the kitchen in Irati from memory, the one with the yellow tiles, and I'm sending it by mail. It's not enough. It's what I have.

Dreamed of the sea again. This time the water reached my knees and it was warm. I didn't go in, but I didn't panic either. Just stood there like a post. Woke up and ate cereal with the weird happiness of someone who has accepted her own slowness.

Mãe, I found the old photo of Vó Lúcia at the farm, the one with the hat too big for her face. I drew it twice: once careful and once fast. The fast one looks more like her. I think she would prefer the fast one. She never liked people standing still for too long.

Called Vó and she complained I call too much, then talked for an hour about the jabuticabeira and how the fruit tasted better when she was twelve. I asked if Coronel ate jabuticaba. She said 'claro que comia, besta'. I miss her already and she's on the phone.
Swam in the bathtub today, technically. Sat in warm water and practiced floating while holding the edge. Dona Cida would be appalled and then supportive. I can almost float for five seconds.

Mãe, you sent the bolachas again. There are so many that the fridge looks like a bakery shelf. I'm drawing the packages because they have her handwriting on the labels. You probably think I'm wasting food. I'm not. I'm keeping the wrappers.

Mom, today I showed you the page with Coronel's grave under the jabuticabeira and you said 'she cried every time she told this'. I know. I think I'm drawing it because I want to stay inside her voice a little longer. Thank you for letting me take your time.

Português: Último dia de maio e eu ainda em casa. Trabalho, desenho, ligo pra Vó. A rotina é monótona de um jeito quase confortável. Vó disse que Coronel, o cachorro, tinha medo de trovão e dormia debaixo da cama com ela. Adicionei mais um desenho à pasta.
June. Still working from home. The factory sent an email about 'returning to normal'. Normal isn't a place anymore, I think, it's a person. I'm trying to be mine.

Called Vó again. She told me the farm's jabuticabeira story with a new detail: Coronel once stole a slipper and carried it home like a trophy. In every version he gets braver, as promised. I wrote it down three times.
Drew a strip about a parrot wearing a mask on the bus. It got three likes, one from my mother. Still counts. Limonada dropped a leaf and I took it personally.
Limonada has nine leaves now and still no lemons. I moved her closer to the window and talked to her about patience. Bia would say I'm losing it. I think I'm practicing for something.

Bia, sua mensagem de áudio me fez rir no ônibus, só que eu não estava no ônibus, estava no quarto, o que é pior. Obrigada pela foto do mar na janela. Olhei demais e queimei o arroz. Agora é 'risoto da Marina'.

Bia sent a photo of her window in Floripa. The sea is very blue and very far from Curitiba. I zoomed in until it was pixels and then put the phone down. Today I drew my own window, with the lemon tree instead of the sea. It is not the same. It is still a window.

Dreamed I was at the farm in Irati with Vó, but I was my adult self and she was young, maybe thirty. She was planting a lemon tree. I asked her why. She said 'para a menina do mar'. I woke up and Limonada had one new leaf. I'm counting coincidences as signs now.

The factory asked me to draw assembly diagrams again. I did them on the kitchen table between a cold coffee and a pile of laundry. Cláudio said they were better than the CAD versions. I'm keeping that sentence in a drawer, physical drawer, like evidence.

Vó asked me to explain Zoom again. I said it's like telephone with picture. She said 'então é televisão'. Fair enough. She then told me a 20-minute story about the farm and fell asleep with the phone on her chest. I stayed on the line until her breathing got even.
Bia, if you read this next year: the sea is still there. I know because you send me photos. One day I'll be in the photo. I'm saving for it. The fund is called MAR and it's patient.

The Interbairros notebook is back on the desk. I'm not posting, just drawing the old 7am characters from memory: the driver, the school kids, Seu Ivo. Juca the parrot is still the star. Some things don't need an audience.

Called Vó, she told me about the jabuticabeira at the farm and how Coronel is buried under it. She's told me this story five times. I wrote down every version. They're slightly different each time; Coronel gets braver.

Dia dos Namorados sem namorado e sem festa. Tio Beto ligou para perguntar se eu estava sozinha e eu disse que não, porque a Limonada estava comigo. Ele riu e disse 'planta não conta'. Eu disse 'conta sim'. Fomos os dois em silêncio um pouco. Foi bom.

Bia, your voice note saying 'the sea is too loud today' made me laugh and then miss you in the same breath. I'm drawing your window from description. It keeps turning into mine, which is unfair to both of us.

Limonada got a new leaf after I moved her to a bigger pot. Bia says I'm a plant mother now. I am not ready for that title. I watered her at midnight because I couldn't sleep and talking to a lemon tree at midnight felt less ridiculous than talking to myself.

Pastel de feira disappeared, so I made one at home. The dough tore, the oil was too hot, and the kitchen smelled like a mistake. I ate it standing up and it tasted exactly like 2015. I'm not sure if that's comforting.

Limonada has grown another 3 centimeters since I last measured, which isn't much but I'm proud. I moved her to the window with the good afternoon sun and whispered 'don't you dare die, I already lost enough this year.' She didn't answer. Trees are rude like that.

Winter. The apartment is cold and the lemon tree is dropping leaves like it is personally offended. I wrapped the pot in a scarf and moved it away from the window. We are both dramatic about temperature. I drank three cups of tea and sketched the scarf on the pot. It looks like a patient.

Vó told me the jabuticabeira story again. Coronel is now brave enough to fight a boar. I wrote down version number six. The versions are diverging like rivers. I love all of them. The book of drawings is at 9 pages now.
Vó asked me to sing 'Asa Branca' on the phone. I did, badly. She clapped and said 'one more year'. I said 'Vó, I've been saying one more year for five'. She said 'and?' Point taken.

Chamada com a Vó. Ela contou de novo sobre a jabuticabeira e o Coronel. Escrevi cada versão. Elas são um pouco diferentes; o cachorro fica mais corajoso. Gosto disso. A memória dela não é exata, é generosa.

Rain all day. The kind that makes the apartment smell like wet cement. I cleaned the kitchen and then ruined it cooking feijão. Tio Beto called to say his violão has a loose string. I told him I still owe him 'Asa Branca' all the way through. He laughed and said he knows.

Mom printed one of the Interbairros strips on her printer, the one with the parrot, and put it on the fridge. She said it was because the fridge looked empty. It did not look empty. I'm counting this as a compliment.
Limonada tem sete folhas novas. Nenhuma limão. Bia disse que ela é 'decorativa'. Eu disse que ela é resiliente. Acho que estamos falando da planta e de mim. Tudo bem. Resiliência vira limão um dia.

Tio Beto, I still haven't learned 'Asa Branca' all the way through. But I hummed the first verse today while doing dishes and didn't get lost. Small victory. Please don't clap yet. I'll embarrass myself.

Drawing small pictures of Vó's stories every evening now. Coronel keeps getting braver in my drawings than in her telling. Today he escorted a whole parade of chickens. I know that's not right. I think I'm trying to give him a better life on paper.
Limonada has a new leaf and I have a new gray hair. We are growing in different directions but with the same stubbornness. I gave her extra water and myself extra coffee. Balance.

Na ceia de junho, Bia e eu comemos milho na sacada, longe uma da outra, de máscara. Ela trouxe o milho e eu o violão, sem saber tocar. Cantamos 'Asa Branca' mal e comemos tudo. Tio Beto ligou e disse que ouviu dizer que estávamos tentando música. Desliguei rindo.

Cláudio sent a photo of the factory floor, empty. "Saudade do barulho", he wrote. I miss the coffee machine more than the motors. Drew the coffee machine from memory. It came out looking like a small friendly robot. I think that's fair.

PT: Tentei desenhar a Vó ontem e desisti na segunda tentativa porque ela tem um jeito de segurar a xícara que não encaixa no papel. Vou tentar de novo hoje. Talvez o segredo seja desenhar a mão primeiro e o resto depois.

Dreamed of the sea again. Still standing at the edge. But this time I was holding a drawing of Vó Lúcia's hands, and the paper got wet before I could show her. Woke up and sketched the hands from memory. They're not perfect, but the rings are right.

Limonada is about 60cm now and looks like a real plant instead of a yogurt cup accident. No flowers, no lemons. Bia calls her 'decorative lemon' and I refuse to accept it. I watered her with leftover café today. Probably wrong. She'll survive.

I cooked arroz e feijão three times this week and all three times the rice stuck. Vó Lúcia, over the phone: 'você tá mexendo demais, deixa quieto'. She's right. I never leave things quiet. Not rice, not myself.

Tentei desenhar a receita de bolo de fubá da Vó, com as manchas de gordura no papel. Ficou bonito, mas triste. Vou guardar no caderno. Talvez ela vire a última página do livro, se eu conseguir terminar.

Therapy is still once a month and I'm bad at it in a very specific way: I prepare sentences beforehand like homework. Today she asked what I'd do if not afraid. I said 'publish the comics'. Then I changed to 'swim in the sea'. She wrote both down. I felt exposed.

Factory remote: Cláudio emailed to say the new diagrams are 'almost artistic, don't tell anyone'. I told everyone. Mom said 'finally'. She always waits for the finally. I'm writing this so I remember to be proud of the small official wins, not just the big scary ones.

Tio, no Festa Junina this year, obviously. I lit a candle and played 'Asa Branca' until the second verse, then stopped, because some traditions are allowed to be incomplete during strange years. Next year we try again.

Festa Junina at home, alone, with popcorn and a forró playlist. Danced in the kitchen. Not quite the same as Tio Beto's, but the violão in the song was close enough. I didn't cry. I almost did. That's progress.
A chuva de julho e eu desenhei a vista da janela: telhados, uma antena, um pedaço de céu. Parece Curitiba, parece vida normal, parece quase nada. Gosto de desenhar o quase nada. É onde eu moro mesmo.

São João on the balcony with Bia, just the two of us, far apart and masked. She brought corn on the cob and I brought the violão without knowing how to play. We sang 'Asa Branca' badly and ate all the corn. Tio Beto called and said he heard we were attempting music. I hung up on him, laughing.

Dreamed of the sea again. Same dream, but this time I was holding Vó's hand and we were both at the edge, not going in. She was laughing like stairs even in the dream. I woke up and drew it before it faded. It's a bad drawing. I kept it.

Sunday lunch is now a video call. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' with his phone propped badly, so we only saw his chin. Mom asked when I'm learning guitar. I said 'one more year'. He laughed, but it was a tired laugh. I don't like that laugh on him.

Tio Beto called to say he tuned his violão and it stayed in tune for three whole days. He called it "um milagre de julho". I recorded him saying it and played it three times. Some people make you feel like the world is still good. He is one.

Português: Liguei pra Vó e ela reclamou que eu ligo demais e depois falou uma hora seguida. Contou que o vizinho tem um papagaio. O papagaio diz 'bom dia, dona Iracema'. Rindo até agora. Desenhei Vó com o telefone e o papagaio.

Walked to the mercadinho with a mask and sunglasses, came back with eggs, milk, and a plant I didn't plan to buy. It's small, purple, and called by the cashier 'a sortuda'. Now Limonada has company. She looks unimpressed.

Limonada tem quatro anos, um metro, e nunca deu um limão. A Bia diz que é 'limão decorativo'. Eu me recuso a aceitar isso. Hoje medii ela e escrevi o número num papel. Se eu desenhar bem, talvez ela dê fruto por gratidão.
Sunday, no Festa Junina this year. I played 'Asa Branca' from memory on the air-violão, which is just my hands on the table. Tio Beto would say one more year. I'm starting to understand that phrase.

Mom video-called and showed me the comics printed from her printer. She doesn't know I saw her smile. She said 'your grandmother would say this looks like her farm', which is the strangest and best review I've ever had.
Dreamed of the sea. I was standing at the edge again, but this time I had a towel over my arm like a very organized ghost. No swimming. Woke up annoyed with myself.

Bia, I miss the bar in São Francisco where we wrote our names on the wall. The marker is probably painted over by now. But I keep thinking: if I go back and the wall is gone, does the writing still count? I think yes. We were there. That's the whole point of these capsules too, right.
Bia sent a voice note of the waves outside her apartment. I played it three times on the bus to nowhere, which is how I think of going to the pharmacy now. The waves sounded close. Maybe they are.

Rain all day. The lemon tree leaves are shiny and I think I understand why people write poems about rain. I still can't write poems, but I drew one: a small house with a lemon tree and a girl looking at it from the kitchen window. It's not me. It's not not me either.
Money check: I spent R$ 120 on paper and ink, zero on clothes, zero on going out. This is the most honest version of my life. The bank app called it 'diversos'. I'd like to call it 'becoming'.

I tried to float in the bathtub today. Lasted six seconds, then water in my nose. Dona Cida is not here to splash me because I do not have a Dona Cida yet. I made a note: swimming later, when the world opens. For now, the bathtub is honest about my limits.
Made a playlist called 'Curitiba waiting'. It has the song Rafa sent me in 2015 and also a song about pigeons. I'm not overthinking it. I'm just listening while doing dishes.

No ônibus vi um homem com uma sacola de limões. Pensei em Vó na hora, sem querer. Fiquei desenhando a sacola até ela sumir no ponto. Desenhei também o ponto. Estou virando gente que desenha coisas que já passaram.

Weather: cold snap, and I wrapped Limonada in a scarf and brought her inside like in 2017. She has more leaves now, twelve, and I counted them twice to be sure. Vó said on the phone 'you're going to kill her with too much love'. She might be right.

Cláudio asked me to draw the new motor assembly again. I did it in 20 minutes and then added a tiny parrot in the corner of the diagram. He didn't notice until the meeting. Someone laughed. Cláudio said 'keep it'. I kept it.
Limonada is blooming? Tiny white flowers, smells like soap. Bia says 'decorative lemon'. I refuse to accept this. I watered her with more optimism than usual.

Vó told me about the jabuticabeira again and how Coronel is buried under it. She's told me this story five times. I wrote down every version. They're slightly different each time; Coronel gets braver. I don't correct her. I think she's editing him into the dog she needed.
Tentei boiar na banheira hoje, como a Bia me ensinou aos 18. Durei seis segundos e água no nariz. Acho que o mar lembra que tenho medo dele. Ou preciso de uma banheira maior.

Money check: R$ 3.400, paid Vó back R$ 200 for the bolo ingredients she sent by bus last month. She refused three times on the phone and then accepted because I threatened to stop calling. She called back in ten minutes to say thank you.
Limonada has 14 leaves now and I counted them twice because I'm a person who counts leaves during a pandemic. She's the only one in this apartment growing on schedule. I admire her.

Cláudio is retiring-ish next year but won't say it. Today he fixed my chair with a screwdriver and said 'this chair deserves respect'. I think he was talking about me too. I'm choosing to believe that.

Vó Lúcia told me the story of Coronel again, but this time she added that he used to sleep at the foot of her bed and kick in his sleep "como se estivesse correndo atrás de alguma coisa". I wrote it down exactly. I want the book to have his sleep in it.

Bia, I tried to teach myself to float in the bathtub today like you taught me at 18. I lasted six seconds and got water up my nose. I think the sea remembers I'm afraid of it. Or maybe I just need a bigger bathtub.

Found an old 'Interbairros' strip in a drawer, Seu Ivo and Juca at the bus stop. I pinned it above my desk. The desk is in my bedroom, so technically the desk is next to the bed, which is next to the laundry. The pin is crooked. Nothing is where it should be and still it's fine.

Bia, happy birthday, six years since we wrote our names on the wall in São Francisco. I don't know if the wall survived. I know we did. I'm making you a tiny drawing of the parrot saying bom dia. It's not much, but it's Tuesday and I'm in Curitiba.

Worked from the kitchen today because my bedroom desk felt like a cage. Vó called and said, 'You sound like you're in a cave.' She's right. I moved back to the desk with the three mugs. The cave has a better lamp.

Português: Primeiro dia que senti a falta de desenhar por desenhar, não por trabalho. Abri o caderno e fiz um quadrinho do ônibus. Sem personagem, sem nome. Só o ônibus vazio às 7h. Ficou triste e bonito. Postei e ninguém viu, mas eu vi.

PT: Hoje a Vó me contou que o Coronel, quando chovia, não entrava em casa porque tinha medo de escorregar no piso. Ela colocava um cobertor na varanda para ele. Eu desenhei isso antes de dormir e não sei por quê chorei.
Sonhei que eu estava no mar e não tinha medo. Acordei antes de entrar. Mesmo assim, por um segundo, me senti corajosa. Vou guardar esse segundo em algum lugar e usá-lo quando precisar.

Mãe, a Vó disse que o bolo de fubá ficou certo dessa vez e eu acredito nela mas não em você, desculpa. Mandei as fotos do desenho da mão dela. Você vai dizer 'ficou parecido' e eu vou fingir que não estou esperando isso. Te amo.

Money check: the factory pays, the rent takes, and the courage fund called MAR is at R$ 800 and not moving. I opened the bank app and stared at it for longer than a sane person should. It's not about the number. It's about the name.

Vó Lúcia told me about the time Coronel followed her father to the field and came back alone with a chicken. She laughed so hard she coughed. I asked if the chicken was okay. She said 'menina, the dog was fine, the chicken was the problem.' I'm drawing this one for sure.

Vó and I talked for an hour and forty minutes today. She told me her father's farm had a lemon tree too, near the gate. I asked if Coronel ever ate a lemon. She said 'that dog ate everything, Marina'. New page in the book.
Limonada is one meter tall and still has never given a single lemon. Bia says she's a 'decorative lemon'. I refuse to accept this diagnosis. We are in a long-term negotiation, she and I.

Bia and I had a video call wine night. She showed me her Floripa window with the lights off. I showed her my window with the curtains open. Both views were just dark. We talked like we were in the same room and that was enough.

Swimming goal update: still zero. But I can now float in the bathtub for twelve seconds without panicking. Progress is progress. The bathtub is not the sea, but neither was the panic, and I defeated that.

Vó Lúcia asked what I was drawing these days. I said 'motors and old people's hands'. She said, 'that sounds like a sad exhibition'. I said it might be. She laughed the high-to-low laugh. I'm trying to keep that sound in the lines of my drawings.

Bia, you asked if I am drawing. Yes. Every night, between work and calling Vó. I haven't shown anyone. The drawings of her farm are getting a folder on my computer called "nao mostrar". Maybe that's where the good ones go. Maybe that's where the brave ones go. Same folder.
Limonada is four years old, a meter tall, and has never given a single lemon. Bia says it's because she's a 'decorative lemon'. I refuse.

Attempted to learn three chords on a borrowed violão from a neighbor's son. The neighbor's son is 14 and much better. I managed 'Asa Branca' badly enough to scare Limonada. Limonada cannot hear, but I'm blaming the vibrations. Some day, Tio Beto. Some day.

Vó asked on the phone what I was drawing lately. I said work diagrams. She said 'desenho de verdade, menina'. I changed the subject and then cried in the bathroom for two minutes. I'm writing this because I want to stop doing that.
I stood on my balcony and watched a cloud shaped like a dog for about four minutes. Then I drew it from memory and it turned into a cat. Memory is unreliable. Clouds too.

Dreamed of the sea again. Same edge, same warm water, but this time I was holding Vó Lúcia's hand and she was saying 'menina do mar' without moving her lips. Woke up and drew it before breakfast. It's not good, but it's true.

Sábado. I made feijão and burned the bottom, which is apparently my specialty now. I scraped it and ate it anyway. The lemon tree dropped one more leaf and I put it in the pot like a blanket. We are both surviving September. It is not glamorous.
Attempted a swim in the inflatable pool on the balcony. It is not the sea. It is not even a pool. Dona Cida from the lessons I don't have would be disappointed. I swallowed water and dignity.

Independence Day at home alone. I made feijoada for one and ate it on the balcony. The radio played 'Asa Branca' and I almost cried into the beans. Tio Beto would have said 'one more year'. I texted him a photo of the plate. He sent back a thumbs up and a violão emoji.

Money check: I paid the rent, bought Vó's favorite cookies, and still have R$ 400. I wrote 'MAR' in the bank app next to the savings number, then changed it to 'LIMONADA', then changed it back. Future me, don't read too much into that.

Independence Day with no parade. Made brigadeiro at 11am because I could. Ate three and saved the rest for later. Later came at 11:15. Rinsed the pan immediately because guilt is more productive than the dishes.

Bia, I watched the sunset from the window today and it was orange-pink like that one day in Matinhos in 2014. I took a photo but sent you the drawing instead. You said 'this is better'. You're biased and correct.
I realized today that I can't remember if Vó's laugh starts high or low. It does both, somehow. I'm going to call her tomorrow just to hear it and I won't tell her why. If I write it here, it's real.
Fiz café de tarde e desenhei Limonada do lado errado da luz. A sombra ficou exagerada e parece que ela está escondendo alguma coisa. Talvez seja eu. Às vezes o desenho sabe antes da gente.
Dinheiro: paguei aluguel, comprei bolachas favoritas da Vó e ainda sobraram R$ 400. Escrevi 'MAR' no app do banco, mudei para 'LIMONADA', depois voltei. Futura eu, não interprete demais.

Português: Vó perguntou se eu ainda desenhava. Eu disse que sim. Ela disse 'bom', num tom que pareceu aprovação disfarçada de indiferença. É o tom dela. Aprendi a ler. Desenhei ela com esse tom, meio sorrindo, meio não.

Video call with Tio Beto. He showed me the violão with a new string he put on himself. He played 'Asa Branca' while I held the phone and cried a little, which I'm writing down because he can't see it and it's okay to cry at an old man playing guitar badly.

Bia, I tried to float in the bathtub again. Four seconds. Still better than 2015, when I lasted four seconds in an actual pool and a six-year-old outspite me. Growth is measured in seconds, apparently.

Cláudio from the factory sent a voice note saying he misses seeing me sketch at lunch. I miss his terrible coffee. Work is fine. The drawings on the side are getting better, which makes the job feel smaller, not better.

Called Bia to complain about the factory and ended up talking about her move to Floripa next year. She described the spare room window and I got quiet. She said, 'you're picturing it, aren't you?' I was. I am now. It's very blue.
The bus route changed and now I don't pass the old stop where Seu Ivo used to wait. I noticed this like noticing an absent tooth. The city rearranged itself without asking me.

Called Vó and she was annoyed because I called "muito cedo", at 10am. Then she talked for 52 minutes. I timed it. She told me about the jabuticabeira and about how the fruit used to stain her hands purple. I drew her hands purple after. Small detail, big meaning, or something.

Limonada is taller than me when I sit on the floor next to her. Still no lemons, still no flowers. Bia says she's a 'decorative lemon'. I refuse. Some things take time and are not decorative, they are just late.

Desenho de hoje: a Vó sentada, mãos no colo, olhando a jabuticabeira. Não ficou perfeito. As mãos estão um pouco grandes. Mas ela segurava meus desenhos assim quando eu era criança, e acho que por isso desenho mãos grandes. Acho que está certo.

Vó told me a new version of the Coronel story: he apparently waited at the gate even when it rained, and once refused to go home without her. I don't know how much is true. I don't care. The dog in my drawings gets braver every week.
Dreamed of the sea again. The water was warm and I was already in it, floating. Someone was next to me but I couldn't see who. Woke up calm, which is new. Wrote it down before it faded, like a rule.

Vó told me the story of Coronel for the fifth time. This time he waited at the school gate in the rain. I believe every version. Memory is a dog that keeps fetching the same stick and making it bigger.

The Interbairros page has 1.200 followers now and someone asked for a new Seu Ivo strip. I don't know what to say. He moved away and the story ended. Maybe that's the point. I drew a little Juca on my notebook margin saying 'tchau' again. Just for me.

Vó said today that she used to walk to school with Coronel and he waited at the gate until the bell rang. Then she said 'mas você já sabe disso, né'. I said yes. She said 'então por que pergunta?'. I didn't have an answer. I just wanted to hear it again.
Português: Money check: R$ 410 no fim do mês. RU fechado, então arroz com ovo e bolacha da mãe. Escrevendo pra poder rir no ano que vem. Ou chorar. Depende. (Igual 2014, mas agora com mais anos.)

September. The sea dream came back. This time I was standing on the edge and my feet moved. Just one step. I woke up with my calves fine for once. I think that's the version 18-year-old me would have wanted.

Money check: R$ 860 left, it's the 28th, and I have finally accepted that I will always be broke around the 28th. At least I'm consistent. The coffee thermos broke, so I'm back to bad coffee. Full circle.

Ate pastel de feira alone on a bench near work and drew the man frying them. He caught me and held up the pastel like a trophy. I gave him the drawing. He taped it to the stall with masking tape. Best gallery in Curitiba, probably.

Cost of living check. Rent, groceries, internet. I have enough for six months if I'm careful. Careful is not my natural state. But the savings fund is named MAR and I'm treating it like a person I don't want to disappoint.

Vó sounded tired on the phone today, but she still complained about the neighbors and then laughed. I wrote down the laugh. High at the start, falling like stairs. I don't want to forget the shape of it.

I cleaned the apartment and found three old Interbairros strips under the mattress, from 2016. Seu Ivo and Juca. I am not the same person who drew them, but I recognize the hand. The parrot's expression is too serious. I should fix that one day. Or not.

Vó Lúcia died on Tuesday. Covid. We couldn't be in the room. I didn't finish the book in time. I'm writing this because in ten years I want to remember her laugh exactly, not just that she laughed: it started high and fell like stairs. She called me 'menina do mar'. I will finish the book. I promise you I will finish it.

Writing this on the floor next to Limonada. Vó Lúcia died on Tuesday. I keep thinking she'll call to complain about too many calls. I haven't finished the book. I'm going to finish it anyway, because promises don't have deadlines, I hope.

Sunday. I stood at the window and looked at the lemon tree for a long time. It is alive and stupid and perfect. No lemons. No sign of lemons. I drew it with a tiny flag on one leaf. It deserves a flag. I deserve a flag. We are both still here.

Português: Vó morreu na terça. Covid. Não pudemos entrar no quarto. Não terminei o livro. Escrevendo isso porque em dez anos quero lembrar do riso dela exatamente, não só que ela ria: começava alto e caía como escada. Ela me chamava de 'menina do mar'. Vou terminar o livro. Prometo.
Vó Lúcia died on Tuesday. I can't write more than this today. I'm putting the pen down and going to bed. Maybe tomorrow I'll draw something. Maybe not.

The book folder has 11 drawings now. Today I drew Vó's hands holding the phone, knuckles a little swollen, nails unpainted, same as always. It took me an hour because I kept stopping to look at my own hand and compare. I think I got the fingers right.

PT: Hoje não tenho cápsula engraçada. A Vó foi. Escrevo só para registrar: a cozinha ainda cheira a café forte e o telefone ainda toca no horário em que ela ligava. Não vou atender. Mas vou continuar contando as horas.

Called Vó's number today. It rang four times and then nothing. I hung up before the voicemail. I don't know what I expected. I think I expected her voice saying it was too much and then talking for an hour.

I found the sketchbook with the drawings of her stories, the 14 of them. I looked at the one of Coronel under the jabuticabeira for a long time. Vó told me five versions and now there's no one to ask which one is true. They're all true. That's what I'll go with.
Called Vó and talked about the book. I didn't tell her I haven't finished it. I said, 'It's coming along.' She said, 'Things usually do.' I am keeping that sentence in my pocket forever.

The drawing of the jabuticabeira is finished. Coronel is under it, small and brave. I didn't show Vó yet. I want to give her a whole little book, not one page, and I don't have one yet. Today I just looked at the page and thought: I can do this. That's something.

Money check: R$ 1.200 left for the month and it's the 11th. Better than 2014, worse than I'd like. The factory pays on time, at least. I bought a new sketchbook and pretended it was a work expense. It was not. It will be used for Vó's stories.

Português: Choro em hora marcada agora. 18h, quando era hora de ligar pra ela. O telefone toca e meu corpo ainda espera. A planta da Vó, um esquecimento que ela me deu, está na janela. Reguei demais. Ela não vai morrer também.
Mãe, I know you're worried. I'm okay. Some days I draw Vó's stories and then need a walk around the block, but the walking helps. I'm not disappearing. I'm just being quiet in a different direction.

Six drawings for the Vó book now. Today I drew the farm in Irati from her description: the jabuticabeira, the dirt road, Coronel at the gate. I've never been there, but her voice is a good reference. Every detail she says twice is the one I trust.

PT: Ainda estou desenhando as histórias da Vó. São 14 páginas. A Coronel fica mais valente a cada versão que a Vó contou. Acho que isso era o ponto: ela não lembrava do jeito certo, lembrava do jeito que queria.

Couldn't draw for a week. Today I drew Coronel, only his head, on a napkin. It looked like a dog and not like a dog at the same time. I put the napkin in the sketchbook. It's the worst drawing I've ever made and I'm keeping it forever.

Mom made the bolo de fubá today and it was wrong, too dry. She said it before anyone else. We laughed and then cried. I drew the cake on a napkin and Mom said 'you got the cracks right'. I didn't know I had.

A página Interbairros tem 1.200 seguidores e alguém pediu um novo quadrinho do Seu Ivo. Não sei o que responder. Ele se mudou e a história acabou. Talvez seja o ponto. Desenhei um Juca pequeno na margem dizendo 'tchau'. Só para mim.

Vó Lúcia's voice on the phone today was thinner, like someone turned the volume down one step. She still complained about the limão orgânico woman. I drew her hands. I think I got the knuckles right. I don't know why that makes me feel useful.

Tio Beto, obrigada por tocar 'Asa Branca' no velório. Não pedi. Você tocou mesmo assim. Eu não consegui cantar. Mas ouvi. Escrevendo pra você porque sei que você não vai ler isso até 2022, e então talvez seja menos pesado. Talvez.

I bought a new sketchbook with the salary from the freelance diagrams. It's bigger than the old ones. I drew 'Interbairros' on the first page just to see if it still felt like mine. It does. Strange, like meeting an old friend at the bakery.

Mom came to Curitiba for the weekend and we didn't talk about Vó once, which means we talked about her the whole time. She found the 14 drawings and held the one of the farm for so long I thought she'd fallen asleep. She hadn't.

Mom, I know you're not ready for this. I'm not either. I'm writing anyway because if I wait until I'm ready I'll never write it. She called me menina do mar. I'm going to draw her stories. Please don't ask to see them yet.

Não consigo ouvir 'Asa Branca' sem pensar no Tio Beto e na Vó ao mesmo tempo. Hoje coloquei a música baixinho enquanto desenhava o rosto dela. A mão tremia, mas o desenho ficou parecido. Acho que ela iria reclamar do nariz.

Tio Beto, I didn't sing 'Asa Branca' at Christmas because I couldn't get through the first verse without stopping. You played it without being asked. I heard it from the other room and drew your hands on the violão. Thank you for not asking me to sing.

I couldn't be in the room. I keep writing that sentence and it still doesn't make sense. I'm putting down everything I remember: the farm, the dog, the hands. If the book isn't finished yet, that is not a failure. It is unfinished love.

I painted the lemon tree's pot blue. Just blue, no reason. Now it looks like it lives by the sea. The tree did not react. I think it approves. Bia said the photo looked like a postcard. I am taking that as encouragement.
Português: Tentei desenhar Vó hoje e não consegui passar do nariz. As mãos, esqueci. O caderno ficou aberto na mesa a tarde inteira. Amanhã tento de novo. Não desistir, mesmo sem conseguir.

Mom sent me a photo of Vó's bolo de fubá recipe in her handwriting, which is just ingredients and no instructions. I stood in the kitchen and tried to remember the smell. Limonada watched from the window, as if she could help. She could not.

I don't know what to write here. She is gone. I keep thinking I will call her on Sunday and then remember. The sea dream hasn't come yet. When it does, I hope she is there. I'm drawing her hands again tonight, from memory, and they are wrong and right at the same time.

Halloween isn't really our thing but I carved a face into a lemon from the fruit market and it's the most cheerful thing in the apartment. Limonada doesn't seem jealous. Carrinho is indifferent as always.
Português: Domingo. Ninguém pra ligar. A frase mais triste que escrevi. Fiz café, liguei pra mãe e fingi que era normal. Ela também fingiu. Nós duas fingindo juntas é a versão familiar do luto, acho.

Finados. I called Vó instead of visiting her, promised I'd go soon. She said she made arroz doce for me and froze it. I believe her. She could be making arroz doce and freezing it for me right now, like a tradition with a fridge.

Tio Beto, today I played the first verse of 'Asa Branca' without looking at the sheet. Only the first verse. Don't tell anyone yet. I want to bring it to the next Festa Junina, whenever that is, and let you hear the whole thing before I show off. You were right: one more year. Several, actually.

November. I made a list of Vó Lúcia's stories on a piece of paper taped to the fridge: Coronel, the jabuticabeira, the limão orgânico, the hat, the purple hands. Eight items. I will add more. The book is not a plan yet. It is a list and a promise.

Bia called and said, 'You don't have to be okay.' I cried so hard the phone screen fogged up. Then she sent a photo of the sea being 'too blue today' and I laughed again. Friendship is a very strange lifeboat.
Tio Beto, I keep wanting to call Vó on Sunday and then remembering. You played 'Asa Branca' at Christmas last year without being asked and I couldn't sing. This year I might try. Don't make it weird.

Bia called and I talked about Vó for an hour without planning to. Bia listened the way she does, which is to say: completely, without fixing anything. I think that's what I'll miss most about friendship when I'm old. Not the fixing. The listening.

Mom made bolo de fubá today, the first one without Vó's recipe. It was too dry and she said it herself before anyone else could. We laughed and then nobody talked for a while. I drew the cake with cracks on top. It looked like a map of something.
Chamada com a Vó cancelada porque ela tinha visita. Fiquei sem saber o que fazer com a hora extra. Desenhei a parede do quarto. Parece pior do que é, mas é o que tenho hoje. Amanhã ligo de novo.

I started a little book about Vó Lúcia today. Twelve drawings of the farm and the dog and the gate. I don't know if I can finish it. I don't know if I'm supposed to. I'm doing it anyway, on Sundays, at the time I used to call her.
I found a lemon on the kitchen counter and for one second thought Limonada did it. It was from the supermarket. I apologized to the lemon for doubting its origin. Then ate it. Life is strange.

Português: Desenhei a jabuticabeira da fazenda sem olhar referência. Saíram frutinhas coladas no tronco, como milagre. É a primeira página do livro que eu gosto. Vó teria dito 'ficou bonitinho' no tom dela. 'Bonitinho' era o máximo de elogio.
First Sunday without calling Vó. The phone stayed in my hand for twenty minutes before I put it down. I drew instead, a small dog under a tree, no face yet. Maybe faces come later.

Found a lemon on the supermarket floor and put it in my pocket like a child. It rolled around all day. When I got home I drew it. Limonada still has no lemons. I'm building an archive of lemons that are not hers.

I drew Vó Lúcia's laugh from memory, the way it started high and fell like stairs. It took me four attempts and then I got it, or close enough that I looked at it and felt like she was in the room. I left it on the table overnight. In the morning it was still good. I don't always trust that.

Bia, today I tried to float in the bathtub again and lasted nine seconds. Progress. I also sent you a drawing of your window in Floripa based on your photo, with the sea a little bluer than reality. You said "perfeito". Reality is overrated anyway.

Therapy hasn't started yet, but I made the appointment. The receptionist asked if it was urgent and I said no, which was a lie and also the truth. I'm going to draw in the waiting room. At least I'll know what to do with my hands.
Money check: I have R$ 3.200 saved, the most ever, and I don't even know what it's for yet. Not a car, not São Paulo. Maybe a window somewhere. Maybe just proof that I can be brave slowly.

Bia, você disse pra não desistir do livro. Eu não desisti. Mas é mais difícil do que pensei porque toda página é uma conversa com ela e depois preciso de uma caminhada. Estou desenhando aos domingos, na hora que ligava pra Vó. Parece certo.

Money check: finally paid the phone bill on time. The cashier at the lottery house asked if I wanted to try my luck. I said I already have a lemon tree that doesn't fruit, that's enough suspense for one person.

Started a folder on my computer called 'Vó'. It has 47 files: photos, voice notes, drawings of the farm, a scan of her bolo de fubá recipe with a coffee stain on it. The coffee stain is not accidental. I'm preserving it.

Bia, thank you for sending me the voice note of the sea from your window. I listened to it three times while drawing. I don't know if I'm drawing the sea or drawing myself wanting the sea. Maybe both. I miss you, not just the ocean.

Mês de novembro, dia frio. Fiz bolo de fubá sozinha e ficou seco, como o da mãe no Natal que ainda nem chegou. Comi mesmo assim com café. Vó teria dito 'coloca mais leite'. Anotei isso para não esquecer.

Bia sent me a voice note from her balcony in Floripa, just the sea for thirty seconds. I drew the window and the sound of it, which is impossible. The drawing is bad. It's the truest thing I've made this year.

Mom asked for the drawings of Vó's stories. I showed her the fourteen I have. She went quiet, then said, 'You got her hands right.' I didn't know I had. I went to the bathroom and cried with the door open because it felt honest.

Português: Visitei Bia em Floripa pela primeira vez. O quarto de hóspedes de frente pro mar. Fiquei vinte minutos na janela. Ela tirou foto das minhas costas e escreveu 'finalmente'. Meu coração doeu de um jeito bom.

A drawing da jabuticabeira terminou. O Coronel está embaixo, pequeno e corajoso. Ainda não mostrei para a Vó. Quero dar um livrinho inteiro, não uma página, e não tenho ainda. Hoje só olhei para a folha e pensei: consigo. Já é algo.

Bia, você me perguntou se eu estava desenhando. Estou, todos os dias, as histórias da vó. São 16 agora. Eu queria te mandar todas mas não consigo ainda. Um dia eu mando a pasta inteira. Obrigada por sempre perguntar.

Tio Beto sent a photo of his violão with a new string. He wrote "as velhas também quebram". I laughed and then felt sad, then laughed again. I drew the violão with one missing string. It looks like it is singing anyway.

Money check: I didn't do one in October and I'm sorry, past me. R$ 1.600 left, rent due, nothing dramatic. I bought a new sketchbook with the last of the MAR fund. The fund is now at R$ 0 and I'm choosing to find that symbolic rather than reckless.
Bia, obrigada pela mensagem de voz cantando 'Asa Branca' errada de propósito. Tocou três vezes. A vizinha bateu na parede. Acho que ela não entende arte.

Swimming: I still can't. I watched a woman float at the clube pool through the fence today while waiting for Bia to finish a call. She stayed still for ten seconds. I timed it. Ten seconds of doing nothing on water. I want that so badly it feels stupid.

Money check: R$ 3.800 salary, savings almost gone after months of quiet, and a fridge with names on yogurts again, old habits. Still, I drew something this week that felt like mine. The bank doesn't measure that, but I do.

PT: Tentei aprender 'Asa Branca' no violão do Tio Beto, que está aqui emprestado. Consegui os primeiros acordes. Meus dedos doem. O violão cheira a casa da Vó e eu não sei se isso é real ou saudade inventando cheiro.

Vó told me she used to swim in the river in Irati when she was young, before she was afraid of it. She said 'medo chega depois, menina do mar'. I didn't ask more. Some things you just write down and keep.

December. The lemon tree has two flowers now, small and white, and I am choosing to believe they are not imaginary. I drew them life-size. They smell like nothing from here but I remember. Maybe that's enough for a drawing.
Limonada has three new leaves and zero lemons. I measured her with a ruler today: 1.02m. She's taller than some children in the building. I'm not comparing, just noting facts.
Worked all week on the investor deck and the only part people commented on was the sun with sunglasses. Thaís asked if I could do more. I said yes too fast. I'm happy and terrified in equal measure.

I found the drawing of the sea Vó Lúcia framed for me, the one from before I moved to the república. It's still above my bed. I took it down for a moment to clean it and the wall looked wrong without it. I put it back. Some things stay.

Found the 2016 yogurt-cup capsule in my drawer and laughed at my own promise about the lemon tree. Limonada is in the next room, four years old, a meter tall, and still lemonless. But she is here, and so am I.

Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' on the violão over the phone for me. It was out of tune and perfect. He said 'one more year' and I said 'you always say that'. He said 'and one day it will be true'. I think he meant the song, but maybe not only the song.

First Sunday without calling Vó and I picked up the phone twice before remembering. The silence where her voice should be is a specific shape. I drew it. It looks like an empty chair. That's probably too literal. I'm keeping it anyway.

The sea dream, again: I stood at the edge, but Vó Lúcia was behind me, holding my shoulders and saying nothing. The water was still. I woke up with my calves tight and my hands cold. I drew the shoulders first, then the sea. The drawing is small and I'm putting it in the book.

I tried to learn 'Asa Branca' on Tio Beto's old chords from 2014. My fingers hurt and the neighbors probably hate me. I got to the first line and then stopped. He said one more year. I am six years late and still counting.

Português: Limonada completa quatro anos, um metro de altura, e nunca deu um limão sequer. Bia diz que ela é 'limão decorativo'. Me recuso. Reguei com café de novo. Se for errado, que seja com boas intenções.

Christmas tree is up. It's small and leans slightly to the left, like me at parties. Mom called to ask if I was coming to Curitiba. I said yes. She said 'bring the drawings'. I said 'which ones'. She said 'all of them'. I didn't cry. I cleaned the kitchen.

Primeiro Natal sem ela já está pesando, e ainda não chegou. Fiz uma lista de coisas que quero desenhar dela antes de esquecer: as mãos, a voz, o jeito de segurar a xícara. Se eu guardar isso, guardo ela também.

Home office fatigue. I found myself drawing the bus driver's hands during a meeting about vibration reports. His hands were kind. I don't even remember which driver. Memory improves when I don't need it and betrays me when I do.
Bia sent a photo of her window at midnight. The sea was black and there were three lights on boats. I zoomed in until it was just pixels. Still felt like looking at it through her eyes.

I stood on the balcony and tried to see the sea in my head, the way Bia describes it. Curitiba gave me clouds, a pigeon, and a very determined laundry line. I drew the pigeon. It has Vó's eyes, accidentally, and now I can't unsee it.

Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' on the violão at Sunday lunch, unasked, and nobody sang. I drew his hands again, the same hands as Christmas. They are easier to draw than Vó's. I don't know what that means.

I drew a small comic about a lemon tree on a balcony that grows one leaf at a time. Nobody will read it but me. Limonada has seven new leaves. I counted them like I count the days since March. Both numbers are too small to be happy about and too real to ignore.

Tio Beto ligou e disse 'você está bem?' e eu disse 'estou', e ele não perguntou de novo, o que significa que ele ouviu que eu não estava. Ele falou por meia hora sobre o violão e sobre a festa junina de 2021 que 'vai acontecer'. Eu quero acreditar.

Mãe, fiz o bolo de fubá da Vó hoje. Saiu seco, todo errado. Não disse nada. Você disse por nós duas. Aí rimos e choramos. Tio Beto tocou 'Asa Branca' no violão sem ninguém pedir. Eu não cantei. Mas ouvi até o fim.

Limonada is 84cm today according to the ruler. She has 47 leaves, I counted because I'm like this now. No lemons. But she survived my learning curve, which is more than most plants can say. I'm proud of us both.

Money check: bought Mom a printer last year and she uses it for my comics. This year I bought her ink. She said I spend too much. Then she sent me a screenshot of a strip with 'menina do mar' in the caption. I'm not crying at work. I'm hydrating.
O desenho da árvore ficou pronto e parece mais com a história dela do que com a fazenda. Isso deve ser bom. A Vó diria que memória não é fotografia. Ela diria isso com bolo na mão, provavelmente.

Vó asked if I've been drawing her stories. I said 'um pouco'. She said 'menina do mar, me desenha bonita, não velha'. I said she is bonita. She laughed like stairs. I wrote that down before I forgot the sound.

I bought a small frame for the drawing of the sea Vó gave me in 2014. It's above the bed again, where it's been the whole time, but now it's framed. She would have said it looks expensive. It was R$ 25. I'm not telling her that.
Mom is making bolo de fubá for Christmas. She texted, 'Too dry?' I answered, 'Always.' She sent back a laughing emoji and a photo of the oven. I think this is our love language: dry cake and honesty.

Christmas preparations: Mom is making the bolo de fubá. I'm not helping because last time I forgot the salt and she still mentions it. I drew the mixing bowl instead. It's the closest I can get to being useful in a kitchen.

Mom, I know you're reading this in two years. I'm okay. I'm drawing again, not every day, but enough to not hide the sketchbook under the mattress. You said drawing wasn't a job. You were right then. I'm not asking you to be wrong now. I'm just asking you to keep printing the strips.

PT: Fiz lista de compras para o Natal: farinha, açúcar, leite. Esqueci que a Vó não vai estar lá para dizer que coloquei pouco sal. Comprei sal mesmo assim. Coloquei pouco, do jeito que ela não gostava. Vai ser uma piada só minha.
