Mãe, comprei um caderno novo e escrevi seu nome na primeira página. Não porque não vou usar, mas porque quando você abrir daqui dois anos vai saber que pensei em você. O caderno é para desenhos da Vó. A senhora aparece no fundo, lavando prato.

Limonada has a new leaf for Christmas. I put a tiny red ribbon on the pot, which is ridiculous, but so is everything else this year. If she could talk she'd say 'menina do mar, calm down'. Maybe that's Vó's voice. Maybe it's mine. I'm learning to hear both.
PT: Falta quatro dias para o Natal e eu ainda não comprei presente para a Bia. Vou desenhar algo, como sempre. Desta vez vai ser o mar. O mar dela. O mar que um dia vai ser meu também.

Português: Um homem no ônibus viu meu caderno e disse 'essa menina desenha que é uma beleza'. Não era ninguém. Foi o melhor elogio do ano, depois do 'finally' da Bia. Guardo elogios de estranhos como se fossem moedas.

Packed a small bag for Mom's house for Christmas. Included: one drawing of Coronel, one of the farm, and a lemon from the market to pretend Limonada produced something this year. She didn't. But hope is free and lemons are cheap.
Limonada está perto da janela, com um laço vermelho ridículo no vaso. O céu de Curitiba está cinza, mas dentro de casa tem café e papel e a sensação de que, mesmo cansada, alguma coisa está brotando.

Tio, tomorrow you'll play 'Asa Branca' and I won't sing, not this year. But I'll be listening, and when the chorus comes I'll hold the violão with you for a second, just to say: we're still here. One more year.

First Christmas without Vó. Mom made the bolo de fubá and it was wrong, too dry, and nobody said anything. Then Mom said it herself and we all laughed and then cried. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' on the violão without being asked. I didn't sing.

First Christmas without Vó. I didn't sing. But I drew her place at the table, empty, with the napkin folded the way she folded it. Tio Beto said it looked like her. I said I know. He said 'então tá bom'. It was.

After Christmas. The bolo was dry and Mom said so herself. We laughed, then cried, then Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' and I didn't sing, which is not a resolution, just a fact. On the bus home I fell asleep and dreamed of nothing. That was enough.
Português: Última semana do ano. No Natal sem Vó. Amanhã Réveillon em casa, só nós. Limonada com um botãozinho verde nas pontas. Pode ser flor. Pode ser imaginação. Não vou jogar.
Português: Terminando 2020. O desenho da Vó parou no nariz, mas o livro tem 14 páginas. O bolo saiu seco. A Limonada não deu limão. O ônibus continua. Eu continuo. That's enough for this year.

Last capsule of the year. Limonada is still leafless in the lemon department, I still can't swim, and Vó Lúcia is still gone. But I drew 18 drawings of her stories and I think that counts as something. Tomorrow: new year. I want to stand in the water up to my ankles and call it a start.

New Year at home, just me and Limonada and the sound of neighbors counting down through the wall. I stood with my feet in the shower at midnight, because that's as far as I go this year. Next year, maybe the sea. I'm keeping the promise, one small tide at a time.

The first week back at the factory after the holidays and everyone acts like nothing happened. I drew a tiny lemon on my notebook margin during a meeting and Cláudio almost caught me. Almost is enough.

First week back at the factory. The coffee machine still makes a noise like a small animal dying. Cláudio said good morning and then immediately asked if I brought any new drawings. I said no. I brought two in my bag. I'm not ready to show work people my Vó drawings yet, so for now they live in the notebook between motor specs.

The lemon tree has dust on its leaves. I wiped them one by one with a damp cloth, which is the most grandmother thing I have ever done. Vó would have approved. She liked clean plants and clean people.
Work was quiet today. Fixed a vibration diagram and ate lunch at my desk. Cláudio would have drawn on the margin of my notebook. I miss him already, even though he hasn't retired yet.

First Saturday of the year. I cleaned the apartment and found a ticket stub from Interbairros in my coat pocket. The bus smelled like diesel and someone's mandioca. I sat on the floor and almost cried, which is dramatic for a piece of paper. Keeping it.

Saturday with too much rain. Limonada didn't get any sun and looked offended. I wiped her leaves with a damp cloth and felt ridiculous. The bus was late so I walked to the padaria and ate a coxinha standing under the awning. Small victories.
First Saturday without calling Vó. I picked up the phone at 9am anyway and put it down. Made coffee, burned it, drank it. The kitchen smelled like her bolo de fubá for a second and then didn't.

Saturday and the whole city smelled like rain before it actually rained. I stayed in bed drawing Vó's farm from memory until the thunder started. Limonada's leaves were trembling on the balcony. I moved her inside and she looked offended about it.

Hoje choveu em Curitiba e o ônibus pingava no teto. Todo mundo fingiu que estava normal. Sentei com jornal no colo e mesmo assim voltei com o joelho molhado. Pelo menos a Limonada parecia contente. Ganhou uma folha nova, verde de um jeito quase agressivo.
Bus 7am still dark. The new driver doesn't wait for the old lady who runs from the corner and it makes me unreasonably angry. I drew her silhouette in the notebook and now I'm late for the factory.
Rain all day in Curitiba, the kind that makes the bus windows look like watercolor. I brought Limonada inside again, just in case. She has fourteen leaves now and I am unreasonably proud.

Cold morning, I walked to the padaria and the man with the green parrot wasn't there, of course he's been gone since 2019, but for one second I looked for him. Bought pão de queijo anyway. The sea dream came back last night, but I put both feet in. Progress, maybe.

Summer in Curitiba and the lemon tree has exactly seven leaves left, which is fewer than I have houseplants and I have zero houseplants. I moved her away from the window last night because the cold coming in felt like a hand on the glass. Me too, Limonada. Me too.
It rained all afternoon and the bus fogged up so much I could only see the parrot man's reflection. I don't know if he's still on the line. I hope he is.

Em português hoje porque às vezes inglês não cabe. Passei a manhã desenhando a Vó no caderno novo, do jeito que ela ria, com a mão na boca. Minha mão não obedece direito. Mas a risada ficou parecida. Espero.
Hoje choveu o dia todo e eu desenhei a mesma janela três vezes com a luz mudando. A terceira ficou melhor porque eu parei de tentar acertar e só fiz.
Money check: R$ 210 left on the 17th. Lived on rice and egg for three days and still bought paper for the sketchbook. Mom sent bolachas again. I ate four before dinner. Growth is not linear.
Hoje o ônibus atrasou 40 minutos e eu desenhei todo mundo. O motorista me viu e perguntou se eu era artista. Eu disse engenheira. Ele disse 'mesma coisa'. Gostei dele.

Mom sent a box with feijão tropeiro in plastic containers and a handwritten note saying 'eat well, engenheira'. I ate two portions standing at the kitchen counter while watching Limonada's leaves move in the window draft.

Rain all week in Curitiba. The bus leaked and everyone pretended it was fine. I sat with a newspaper on my lap and still went home with wet knees. At least the lemon tree looked happy. It has a new leaf that's almost aggressively green.
Video call with Bia. She held her phone out the window so I could hear the sea. It sounded like a radio between stations. I pretended I could. She knew I was pretending.
Bia sent voice note from Floripa. She said the window was making a sound like a flute at night. I asked her to record it. It sounded like a kettle. We laughed for five minutes on the phone.
Found a seed in a lemon at the market and planted it in a yogurt cup, because apparently I am a person who does this now. Wrote 'MARINA 2' on the cup. The fridge rules live on.
Money check: R$ 420 left, it's the 27th, and I have three days until payday. I made arroz com feijão e ovo and pretended it was a choice. RU pastel would have been cheaper and probably better.

Bus 7am, Interbairros II. Sem Seu Ivo. O motorista novo fala com o rádio ligado. Ninguém diz bom dia pra ninguém. Desenhei um quadrinho no caderno e senti culpa por isso, como se estivesse traindo a série. Talvez o Interbairros acabou com o Juca.
Dona Cida at the pool asked if I had ever been to the sea. I said yes, from the sand. She said 'next time go in'. I told her I was working on it and swallowed some water as proof.
Bia, I made bolo de fubá again. It was better than Mom's Christmas one, which feels illegal to say out loud. I ate two slices standing at the sink.
Therapy homework: write down one thing I did well today. I wrote 'made coffee without spilling'. It counts. Tomorrow maybe 'didn't cry on the bus'.
Day off, cold. Stayed in bed drawing Vó's kitchen from memory. The stove had a blue flame that nobody believed. I drew it blue anyway. Memory is allowed to be wrong.

Portuguese practice: Hoje choveu a tarde toda e eu fiquei desenhando a Vó no caderno. Desenhei a mão dela, com os anéis que ela nunca tirava. Acho que acertei os anéis e errei o sorriso. Mas é um começo.

Bia called to say Floripa is too hot and she misses me. I said Curitiba is too cold and I miss her. We compromised by complaining together for forty minutes. She asked if I'm drawing. I said yes. The truth is I'm drawing more than I tell anyone.
Mom, if you read this someday, I left the laundry in the machine again. I'm sorry. Also the bolo de fubá was perfect last week. I didn't say it because I was crying and didn't want to make it weird.
Therapy day. She asked me to describe the sea dream without using the word sad. I couldn't. I'm working on it.
Rain all day. Limonada got a new leaf even though it's January. I'm keeping a notebook of her leaves like a sad, proud mother.
I drew a motor today for the factory and accidentally drew a tiny sea in the corner of the diagram. Nobody noticed. I left it. It felt like a secret I was allowed to keep.

O ônibus atrasou vinte minutos e eu fiquei em pé do lado do ponto olhando a chuva fina. Um moço me ofereceu guarda-chuva e eu disse não, obrigada, mas acabei aceitando. Foi a única conversa de verdade que tive essa semana.
Dreamed of Vó again. She was in the kitchen making bolo de fubá and the oven kept beeping. I woke up and the apartment was quiet, which was worse. Drew her hands from memory before they faded.

Bia, I had a dream that Limonada gave lemons and you were the one who picked the first one. Woke up happy and then sad that it wasn't real. Come visit when you can. Bring your window with you, somehow.

Mom sent a voice note to say the printer works again and she printed a drawing of a lemon for the fridge. She said 'não tem limão, mas pelo menos tem desenho'. I saved it. I'm not deleting that audio.

Bia, hoje comi pastel de feira sozinha e pareceu 2015. O homem da barraca ainda tem o mesmo rádio. Quase mandei mensagem pro Rafa dizendo isso. Em vez disso escrevi aqui. Você tem permissão de me lembrar de não fazer isso.
A terapeuta perguntou o que eu faria sem medo e eu respondi desenhar. Ela olhou pra mim esperando mais. Eu olhei pra ela esperando elogio. Ambas ficamos decepcionadas.
A natação foi horrível hoje, engoli água e saí tonta. Mas flutuei por três segundos. Três segundos é mais do que ontem. Contando.

Bia, your voice note from Floripa made me pause the drawing I was doing. You said you can see the sea from your kitchen sink now. I stared at my bathroom window, which faces a wall, and drew a tiny fish in the margin. Not fair.

Valentine's Day. I bought myself a pastel de feira and ate it on a bench near the factory. The filling was too hot and I did that thing where you blow on it and then burn your tongue anyway. No romance, just cheese.
Bia, I bought myself a pastel today and ate it alone on a bench in the Bosque. Not sad, just strange. I thought of Rafa for about thirty seconds and then thought of the parrot man. Life is funny.
Dia dos Namorados e ninguém. Comi pastel sozinha na feira e desenhei a mão da mulher que fritava. Ela tinha um anel de ouro velho. Desenhei o anel também.

Valentine's Day. No chocolate this year, but I drew Vó Lúcia's hands from memory. They came out right on the third try. I taped the first two to the fridge, because mistakes are also evidence of caring.

Bia, today I ate pastel de feira alone and it tasted like 2015. The man at the stall still has the same radio. I almost texted Rafa to say that. Instead I'm writing it here. You are allowed to remind me not to do that.

Mom, I'm leaving this here because I won't say it to your face. Thank you for the printer. I know you print my comics. You never say you do, which is how I know. One day I'll make you something worth framing, and this time I won't pretend it's just a hobby.
Factory meeting ran late. Cláudio showed me a diagram and asked if I could redraw it 'like a human'. I said yes and made the gears look like little suns. He didn't say it was wrong.

Bia, your voice note about Floripa rain made me laugh in the middle of the open office. Cláudio looked at me like I had broken a machine. I think I miss your laugh more than I miss the sea, and that's saying a lot.
Limonada dropped one leaf in the cold and I panicked, then remembered she did this last year too. Eight leaves again. We're both dramatic.

One year since I moved out of the república and I still wash the yogurt cup before using it. Four girls, one bathroom, a fridge with names. I can still smell the old wood sometimes when I'm falling asleep.
Seven years since I moved into the república. I still think about the yogurt with names on it sometimes. Mine was 'MARINA' and someone kept moving it. I never found out who. I miss that fridge.
I had the sea dream again, but this time someone was swimming next to me. I couldn't see who. I woke up and wasn't sad, just confused in a good way. Wrote it down before it turned into the old one.
Ate feijoada at Tio Beto's and fell asleep on the couch. Woke up to him playing violão softly. For a second I thought it was Vó humming. It wasn't. It was enough.
A man on the bus had a cat in a cardboard box and the cat was calmer than me most weekdays. I drew them both. Nobody talked about it, which is how you know Curitiba has decided it's normal.

Money check: I bought a new sketchbook with my own salary and felt absurdly proud. It's the A4 one with the blue cover, the expensive one. I will not spill tea on it. I will absolutely spill tea on it.

Money check: R$ 2.900 salary, rent, therapy, and a suspicious amount spent on colored pencils. I'm 25 and I still buy them like they're illegal. Mom would say I'm acting like Vó with her fabric. Maybe that's where it comes from.

Hoje foi o aniversário do Coronel, na minha cabeça. Vó contava que ele esperava na porta da escola todos os dias, rain or shine. Desenhei ele esperando. Demorei duas horas para a orelha. Ainda não está certa. Tudo bem.

Em português. Acordei com vontade de mar e fui de ônibus até o terminal. Não tem mar em Curitiba, mas tem o cheiro do terminal velho e o homem do suco de laranja. Desenhei ele. Acho que ele reparou, porque riu.

Bia, I dreamed about Vó again. She was showing me a lemon tree that had no lemons and saying 'paciência, menina do mar'. I woke up and called you and you were already awake. Thank you for being awake at 6am for me.
Therapy homework: write down one thing I did this week that was only for me. I drew Vó's farm dog for twenty minutes during lunch. Cláudio asked if it was a new motor. I said yes. It was not.

I stopped calling anyone on Sundays because there's no one to call on Sundays anymore, and that sentence is the saddest thing I've written. Therapy started. The therapist asked what I would do if I weren't afraid. I said: draw for a living and live near the sea. She asked what I was afraid of. I'm still thinking.
International Women's Day. The factory put flowers on the women's desks. Mine is already wilting next to my sketches. I think the flower and I have the same energy.
Dia da Mulher no trabalho e ganhei um chocolate do RH. Cláudio deu parabéns e depois perguntou se eu podia medir uma bomba. Desenhei o chocolate comendo o bomba. Ninguém viu.
Therapy week two. The therapist asked me to name one thing I did for pleasure last week. I said swimming. She asked why I said it like an apology. I didn't have an answer. I'm going back Thursday.
I drew the factory parking lot during lunch. Nobody asked why. I think people are used to me being strange now.
A lemon tree update: Limonada survived winter inside, lost three leaves, gained one. Bia says she's 'stubborn like her owner'. I choose to take that as love.

Therapy homework this week: write down one thing I'm afraid of without explaining it. I wrote 'the factory becoming forever'. Then I crossed it out and wrote 'Vó's voice fading'. I don't know which one is true, so I left both.

Therapy homework: list three things I did this week that were mine. I wrote swimming, the drawing of the lemon tree, and refusing the extra shift on Saturday. The third one felt like cheating but my therapist said no.
Fiz feijão e esqueci de temperar. Comi assim mesmo porque joguei comida fora ontem e me senti mal. Aprendi que tempero é importante e que sou dramática com feijão.
Sunday call with Bia. She says Floripa is windy and beautiful. I say Curitiba is cold and I drew a motor today. We both pretend this is a fair exchange. It isn't, but I love her.
Therapy homework: write three things I'm good at. I wrote 'drawing hands', 'measuring vibrations' and 'pretending I'm not sad'. She said the last one doesn't count. I'm keeping it.

Cheque financeiro: salário de R$ 2.900, aluguel, terapia e uma quantia suspeita em lápis de cor. Tenho 25 anos e ainda compro como se fosse ilegal. A mamãe diria que eu estou agindo como a Vó com os tecidos. Talvez seja de lá que vem isso.

Therapy week two. She asked about the sea dream. I said I still can't go in. She didn't push. She just nodded like the sea was a person I haven't spoken to in a while. Left feeling lighter and annoyed about it.

Therapy. She asked me to bring one drawing next time. I brought the Coronel one, the dog walking Vó to school. She looked at it for a long time and said 'you're not avoiding the grief, you're keeping her in lines'. I cried in the car for twenty minutes.
Mom called to ask if I had eaten. I said yes. I had coffee and a banana. She knows. She always knows.

Went to the factory by bus because the car wouldn't start and I refuse to panic about it. Fell asleep on the Interbairros and missed my stop by two neighborhoods. The driver recognized me and woke me up. Some things stay.
Therapy homework: list things I'm afraid of. I wrote 'the factory forever' and then drew a little exit sign next to it. Progress is probably not this literal, but I'll take it.

Rain all day. The lemon tree on the balcony is getting yellow leaves, which is not supposed to happen. I moved it away from the cold wind and apologized out loud. Bia heard me and said 'she's a tree, Marina'. She's not wrong, but she's not right either.
Chamei a Bia no WhatsApp e ficamos duas horas em call sem falar quase nada. Ela limpando a cozinha, eu desenhando. Às vezes amizade é isso: presença sem necessidade de frases.
Em português. Paguei a conta de luz e ainda sobrou R$ 80. É pouco, mas é meu. Vou guardar no fundo 'MAR' no app do banco. Tem nome, tem meta, tem coragem escondida aí dentro.

Money check: R$ 1.200 left, fridge empty, and it's the 22nd. I made arroz com ovo and thought of the RU. The difference is now I'm paying for the rice and the therapy and the sadness is the same price.
Found one of Vó's old voice messages on my phone. It's just her saying 'menina do mar' and laughing. I backed it up three times.
A lemon tree branch knocked against the glass at 3am and I woke up certain it was someone at the door. Limonada is growing crooked again. I staked her with a chopstick and felt absurdly maternal.
Worked late on a motor assembly diagram. Cláudio said it looked like a drawing, not a diagram. I said thank you and he said that wasn't a compliment. It felt like one anyway.
Bia, you told me on the phone that Floripa smelled like salt today. I sat in my bedroom afterward and imagined it so hard I could almost taste it. Don't tell anyone I did that.

Sunday without calling anyone. I made coffee and stared at Limonada for a while. She has eight leaves and zero lemons, same as last year. I talked to her anyway. She didn't answer, which is probably good.

Cláudio is retiring soon. At lunch he asked to see the motor sketch I did. He nodded once, very slowly, like a man inspecting a bridge. Then he said 'you should be drawing full time.' I laughed because if I didn't I'd have to take him seriously.
Mom, I made the bolo de fubá using Vó's recipe from memory. It was a little dry, again. I ate two slices standing up and thought of you saying 'this one is almost right'. Almost is progress.
Rain all week. Limonada has seven new leaves and zero lemons. I told Bia I was giving up on lemons and she said I say that every year. She's right.
Tio Beto called to ask if I was still playing Asa Branca. I said no. He said 'pelo menos você não mente mais'. We both laughed. I practiced until my fingers hurt anyway.
Money check: R$ 2.100 left after rent and groceries. Not terrible. I put R$ 300 into the 'MAR' fund and bought a cheaper brand of coffee, which I am pretending tastes the same. It does not.
Swam ten meters today without stopping. It wasn't pretty. Dona Cida clapped from the edge like I had won something. I almost believed her.
Tried making Vó's bolo de fubá from memory. It came out too sweet and too flat. I ate two slices standing at the counter anyway. I think the secret was her hands, which is not helpful.
Bus Interbairros II, 7am. Still no parrot man. I drew the new driver's hands on the ticket machine. He has a tattoo of a butterfly. I named him Seu Marcelo in my head.
Drew Vó Lúcia's hands again. Mom said I got the right one. I looked at the photo for twenty minutes and still think the thumb is wrong. I'm not fixing it yet. Sometimes wrong is true.
Passei o sábado inteiro desenhando a história do Coronel para o caderninho da Vó. Acabei não almoçando, o que ela chamaria de bobagem. Acho que ela teria gostado dos pelos dele.
Found an old bus ticket in my wallet. Interbairros II, 7am. I don't take that bus anymore, but I keep it in the sketchbook. Seu Ivo would say 'bom dia, motorista' even if nobody answered.

Mom, I'm not sending this yet, but I want you to know: the drawings of Vó's hands are the hardest thing I've ever done. Not technically. Emotionally, which sounds dramatic, but it's true. You keep not asking about them. Thank you for that.
Mom, I know you meant 'desenho não paga conta' as protection. I need you to know I'm not angry anymore, just persistent. Also your bolo de fubá improved. Not there yet, but closer.
Sunday call with nobody. I called Mom anyway and she talked about the neighbor's cat for forty minutes. I drew the cat in the margin of my engineering notebook and it looked like a small angry cloud.

Em português. Dona Cida me chamou de 'a engenheira' de novo no banho, e eu achei graça. Ela nada como se fosse brincadeira. Quando eu crescer, quero ser assim. (Já tenho 25, então já sou assim, só falta a técnica.)
Rain again. The lemon tree is inside now, next to my sketchbook. I sat by the window and drew the rain on the glass. It looks like static. I kind of love it.
Picked up the car from the mechanic and drove home with the windows down. The city smelled like rain and fried pastel. I thought: one day the sea will smell like this. I don't know what that means.
Sonhei que Vó me chamava de menina do mar de longe e eu não conseguia nadar até ela. Acordei com a sensação de perna cansada. Ainda assim, bom sonho.
Called Bia on Sunday. We talked for an hour about nothing important: a stray cat she feeds, a bad haircut, the smell of her building's elevator. It was the best hour of my week.

Domingo. Liguei para o Tio Beto. Ele disse que o violão está desafinado e não tem coragem de tocar. Eu disse que não precisa tocar, só segurar. Ele ficou em silêncio e depois disse 'saudade, menina'. Eu também.

Pandemic still. I called Vó Lúcia's number by mistake today, old habit, then sat on the bed for ten minutes. Nobody answered. Of course nobody answered. I drew her hands again. They came out wrong and I cried. Then I drew them again.
Bia, your balcony plant is alive? Mine is a meter tall and still stubborn. I talked to her today because the therapist said it's okay to talk to things. She didn't respond, which felt mature.

Vó told me the Coronel story on this day in 2015, and I wrote down every version. Five years later, the farm dog gets braver each time. Today I drew him with a bandana because why not. The dead don't care about accuracy.
The lemon tree has tiny buds. Not lemons, just buds. I checked three times before bed. Bia says I'm obsessed. She's right.

Dreamed of the farm in Irati again. Not the sea this time. Vó was hanging clothes and Coronel was under the jabuticabeira, but younger, like the story she told. I woke up smelling fruit that doesn't exist in my bedroom.
Mom, I used your old iron to press the pages of the drawing book flat and the steam made the ink run on one corner. It looks like fog now. I'm keeping it. Sometimes mistakes become weather.
The lemon tree has a new leaf. I know that's nothing. I'm writing it down anyway because tiny things have been keeping me alive this year.
Earth Day at the factory. I planted a small seedling near the gate and Cláudio said it would die. I watered it anyway. It is not a lemon tree, but it is something.

Dreamed about the sea again, but this time I was just standing at the edge with Vó Lúcia. She didn't say anything, just held my hand. Her hand was warm this time. I woke up crying and not sad, which is a confusing combination.
Tio Beto sent a voice note playing 'Asa Branca' very badly and very proudly. I listened three times. I still can't play the second verse. He is patient and I am stubborn. Someday.

Chuva em Curitiba, o tipo que parece que o céu desistiu de ser céu. Desenhei o ônibus da cozinha, a janela embasada, e uma xícara de café que esfriou. Gosto de dias assim. Me dão permissão para não produzir.

Tio Beto, I still haven't played Asa Branca all the way through. But I played the first eight bars today and remembered the exact wrong chord at Festa Junina 2018. I'm writing this so someday you can laugh at me from the future.

Bia, I miss you. I keep wanting to send you a photo of the sky and then remembering you're in Floripa and the sky there is a different color. Is that possible? Write me back. I'll call Sunday, not because there's someone else to call on Sunday, but because you're there.
At the RU I sat alone and drew the tray of beans as if it were an archaeological artifact. The lunch lady asked to see. She approved.

At the factory I measured vibrations in a motor for three hours and thought about how nothing in engineering is as quiet as drawing. Came home and drew a lemon tree that doesn't exist, with too many leaves. It looked like Limonada's cousin.
Comprei papel novo para desenho. Caro. Mas quando abri o pacote senti cheiro de escola, de caderno novo. Acho que valeu.

Mom came for lunch and didn't mention the therapy or the drawings, which is its own kind of kindness. She brought bolo de fubá, less dry this time. We ate in silence and I think that was the best conversation we've had in years.

Dreamed of the sea again, but I was on a bus next to Seu Ivo and Juca. The parrot said 'tchau, motorista' and then we were at the beach. I woke up and wanted to draw it immediately. I didn't. I'm writing it here so I don't forget.

Rain stopped, Curitiba turned golden for twenty minutes and then went back to gray. I drew it from the bus window. The old man in front of me was reading a newspaper and the headline was about rain. I wanted to tell him I was drawing his weather.
Walked past the RU today. The line was the same. I considered joining it out of nostalgia and then remembered I have a salary and also dignity, probably.
Rain all weekend. I cleaned the apartment, including the space under the bed where the old sketchbook used to live. Found a dried lemon seed in a yogurt cup. I don't know why I kept it. I kept it.
Money check: R$ 2.100 left, rent due in five days. I ate arroz com feijão for lunch and dinner and called it a budget. The drawing account has R$ 40 in it. Small but real.
Money check: enough for the month but no extras. I chose the good coffee anyway and felt both proud and guilty. The receipt is in my pocket like evidence of a crime.
Limonada got new leaves this week. Four of them, bright and arrogant. She has never given me a lemon and still acts like she's doing me a favor just by existing. I relate to her.
Therapy homework: list five things I like about myself. I got to three and stared at the ceiling for twenty minutes. Progress.

Mom asked about the drawings again. I showed her only three this time. She pointed at the one of the farm and said 'the fence was lower'. I corrected it. She didn't say thank you, but she stayed ten more minutes.
Mother's Day. I drew Mom's hands holding a cup of coffee, the way she holds it with both hands even when it's not cold. I didn't give it to her. I'm not ready for her to know I see her like that.

Sonhei com a fazenda em Irati de novo. Não foi o mar dessa vez. A Vó estava estendendo roupa e o Coronel estava debaixo da jabuticabeira, mas mais jovem, como a história que ela contava. Acordei cheirando fruta que não existe no meu quarto.
At the factory today I measured a motor that vibrated at exactly the frequency of Vó's old sewing machine. Nobody asked. I wrote it in my notebook like a secret.
Mãe das Mães day at Vó's grave. We took flowers and Mom talked to her like she was late. Tio Beto played violão standing up. I drew them from behind and didn't show anyone.
A Limonada deu uma flor nova e eu fiquei olhando por dez minutos antes de ir trabalhar. Ela não deve nada a ninguém. Eu também não, talvez.
Mom asked to see the drawings of Vó's stories. I showed her the 14 I have. She went quiet and said 'you got her hands right'. I didn't know I had.
Mom asked to see the drawings and I showed her 14. She went quiet for so long I thought she didn't like them. Then she said I got Vó's hands right. I have been smiling like an idiot since.
At the factory, Cláudio asked me to draw the new assembly diagram again. I spent lunch on it and didn't mind. The drawing paid for my pastel, which counts as a job, technically.
Mãe, you asked if I was eating properly. I said yes. I had rice and egg today, which is technically food, and an apple that was more intention than fruit. I love you. Please don't worry.

Mom saw the drawings of Vó's stories and said I got her hands right. I didn't know that. I'm putting it on the fridge next to the printer she bought, which she still uses to print my comics even though she says they're 'just little cartoons'.

Em português. Desenhei o Seu Ivo de memória, sem foto. O papagaio Juca ficou maior do que lembrava. Acho que é porque na memória tudo o que importa cresce. Ele disse 'bom dia, motorista' e eu quase chorei no café.
Money check: R$ 2.100 for the month, rent due on the 5th, no panic yet. I made soup from the carrots Mom sent and felt very grown up. Called her to say so; she asked if I had eaten breakfast.

Swimming lesson #4. Dona Cida told me to stop holding my breath like it's an argument. I said I don't know how else to hold it. She said 'like a secret you're about to share'. I went home and cried in the shower. Good cry.
Mom came over and saw the drawings pinned above my desk. She touched one of Vó's hands in charcoal and said nothing. That's a lot, from her.
Domingo de chuva. Fiz café forte, sentei perto da janela e desenhei a Limonada. Ela tem oito folhas novas. Desenhei cada uma. Fiquei com a mão dolorida e feliz, o que é uma combinação boa.
Bia sent a photo of her window in Floripa, all blue and angry storm sea. I stared at it for five minutes and then drew a tiny person standing in front of it. That person is me, probably.
Drew Vó's farm from the story about Coronel. The jabuticabeira has too many leaves and I can't fix it. Maybe that's right. Farms are messy.

Tio Beto sent a voice message playing 'Asa Branca' halfway through and stopping at the second verse, like a joke only we understand. I replied with a voice message of me laughing. I didn't try to play it. Next year.

Tio Beto called and asked if I could plant lemons for him too. I said I don't even have lemons for me. He laughed. Then he played 'Asa Branca' on the phone and hung up. I stood in the kitchen holding the phone like an idiot.
Limonada has a new leaf and I am disproportionately proud. Watered her carefully and whispered 'not today' when she seemed to lean. She is a plant. I know. Still.

Finished drawing number 14 of Vó's stories. This one is the farm in Irati with the jabuticabeira. I gave Coronel a slightly crooked tail because she said he was 'torto but bonito'. I think that's all of us.
Tio Beto, ontem toquei Asa Branca até a segunda estrofe e pensei em você. Não era perfeito, mas não parei. Acho que você ia bater palma mesmo assim.

Therapy notes: I want to draw for a living and live near the sea. I said it out loud twice this week. The second time it sounded less like a joke. Writing it here makes it real, or at least harder to pretend I didn't say it.
Bus was so crowded I had to stand the whole way. Someone's umbrella poked my sketchbook and ruined a drawing of Dona Cida. I'm pretending it's abstract now.
It's Festa Junina month and I haven't practiced Asa Branca enough. Tio Beto will not ask. That silence is getting heavier than the violão.
Work from home: I made an assembly diagram and a tiny sun with sunglasses in the corner. Thaís didn't notice. I left it. The drawing pays half the happiness and none of the bills yet.
At the factory someone asked what I'd do if I left engineering. I said 'draw'. They laughed. I went back to my desk and drew a tiny lemon tree on the corner of a vibration report.
Domingo frio, fiz sopa de abóbora e desenhei até a mão doer. Limonada tem um novo broto no topo, pequenininho. É ridículo como eu comemoro broto.
Swallowed half the pool again. Dona Cida says I'm 'fighting the water like it owes me money'. I think that's fair. I owe it a lot of years.
Bia sent a voice note from the beach: just wind and waves for forty seconds, no words. I listened three times and then put my phone face down like it was a wild animal.
Drew for two hours on the living room floor because the desk felt too serious. My back hurts. The drawing is just of my coffee cup, but it looks like morning feels. I want to remember that.
Pool at 7am. I floated for ten whole seconds today. Dona Cida clapped like I had won something. A man in the next lane asked if I was okay. I was. Progress.
The lemon tree is in full summer mode. Still no lemons, but the leaves are bigger and it smells like something I can't name when I water it. Bia says I'm projecting. I think I am. I don't mind.

Dia dos Namorados. Não é mais difícil, mas é diferente. Lembrei do Rafa me dando pastel no dia em que eu reprovei. Não senti falta dele. Senti falta de quem eu era com ele: mais leve, talvez. Ainda estou aprendendo a ser leve sozinha.
Dia dos Namorados. Ate pastel alone again, but this time I brought a sketchbook and drew the couple at the next table. They noticed and posed. I felt like a fraud and also like myself.
Dia dos Namorados. I bought myself a pastel at the feira and ate it on a bench. Rafa's name didn't cross my mind for a whole minute. Progress. The pastel was cold.
Dia dos Namorados com Limonada na janela. Comi brigadeiro de colher e vi um episódio antigo. Acho que estou bem. Não sei ainda, mas acho.

Festa Junina at Tio Beto's, still no 'Asa Branca' from me. He didn't hand me the violão this year either. We both pretended to be fine. The bolo was good. I went home and drew the fairy lights until 2am.
I dreamed of the sea again. This time I was sitting on the sand, not standing at the edge. Small victory. Woke up with sand between my toes, which is impossible and comforting.
Money check: the savings account has R$ 1.200. It's not the six months I want, but it's not R$ 340 on the 28th either. I bought a better eraser. Small victories.
Em português. Money check em português porque dói mais: R$ 1.800, aluguel daqui a três dias, e um suco de uva na geladeira que eu comprei como prêmio. O prêmio se chamou 'eu sobrevivi à segunda'.
Tio Beto mandou áudio tocando Asa Branca errado de propósito e rindo. Respondi com outro áudio cantando alto e desafinando. Meu vizinho bateu na parede. Valeu.
Bia sent a photo of the spare room with the window open. The sea is right there, like it's showing off. I saved it as my phone wallpaper and then felt ridiculous about being so jealous of a window.

Money check: saved R$ 300 this month by eating at home every day. The pasta was terrible but the numbers were good. I'm calling it the 'MAR' fund in my head, even though it's currently just R$ 300 and instant noodles.
The lemon tree grew three new leaves this month. No lemons. Bia says it's decorative. I say it's patient. These are different things and I'm choosing mine.

Cheque financeiro: R$ 1.800 sobrando no dia 18. Não é ótimo, não é terrível. Os lápis de cor venceram. Os lápis de cor sempre vencem. Estou me dizendo que é investimento em uma carreira futura que ainda não existe.

Festa Junina season. I bought a quentão from the corner and stood there holding it until it stopped steaming. Tio Beto asked about the violão. I said I was busy. He said 'one more year' again. He still does that.

Saturday market. Bought too many jabuticabas and ate them on the walk home, purple fingers and all. I thought about Vó under the tree at Irati. I didn't cry. I just stood there with sticky hands and let it be what it was.
Fiz uma sobremesa de banana que não deu certo e ainda assim comi inteira. Aprendi que orgulho também se come com colher.
At the pool today I floated for ten seconds. Dona Cida said, 'now you just need to trust the water'. I trust soup more, but I'm trying. Small victories.
Money check: I treated myself to a bakery pastel and felt guilty for four hours. Old habits die slowly, and expensively.
Festa Junina virtual na família. Tio Beto tocou Asa Branca no celular, meio cortado. Todos cantamos fora de tempo. Vó teria rido. A gente riu por ela.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's, small this year. He didn't bring out the violão. I think he was waiting for me to ask. I didn't. We ate canjica and talked about the weather. I regret not asking.
Tio, I practiced 'Asa Branca' until the second verse. Again. I stopped because my fingers hurt and because it makes me miss Vó too much. One day I'll play it for you all the way through. Not yet.

Mãe, the bolo de fubá you sent turned out wrong too dry, but I ate it anyway and said it was good. Next time I'll ask for the recipe properly. Thank you for trying. I know it's the hardest recipe because it was hers.

Dream anniversary. Seven years ago I wrote about the same dream. Today I floated for six seconds in the pool before panicking. The dream didn't come back tonight. I don't know if that's because of the swimming or the therapy, but I'll take it.

Cold morning, bus at 6:40. No parrot man anymore, but an older woman got on with a basket of mandioca and said 'bom dia' to everyone like she was conducting a choir. I drew her hands. They were good hands.
It was cold enough to need a scarf in July and I thought of Limonada's frost night. I brought her inside just in case. She didn't need it. I did.

Saturday. Made pastel de feira at home because I missed it. Burned the first one. The second one was acceptable. Rafa's recipe, approximately. I didn't cry. I ate it with tea and felt like a person who has moved on, mostly.
The factory air conditioning broke and the motor I was measuring vibrated so hard my notebook danced across the table. Cláudio said it was 'character'. I drew it vibrating and felt better.
Cold front in Curitiba. I wore two socks and still couldn't feel my toes. Limonada is inside again, wrapped in my scarf. She looks ridiculous and regal at the same time.

Went to Matinhos for the weekend with Bia. I swam in the sea up to my waist, which is my line, and she swam circles around me. The water was warm. I stood there and thought of the dream and didn't panic. Small victories.

Cold morning, 7am, the bus heater didn't work. I sat next to a woman with a cat in a carrier. The cat looked at me like it knew my whole personality. I drew it in the margin of my notebook. Nobody asks for that anymore, which is maybe why I keep doing it.
Watched the fireworks from the balcony alone. They were small and far away. Limonada didn't flinch. I held her pot with one hand. Some nights that's company enough.
Choveu a tarde inteira e eu fiquei desenhando a Vó no caderno. Senti saudade do jeito que dói, mas também do jeito que esquenta. As duas ao mesmo tempo.

Dreamed of the sea again. I was standing at the edge, water warm, feet still. But this time I was holding Vó Lúcia's hand. She didn't say anything. I woke up with my calves tight and a feeling like gratitude.
Levei o caderno de desenhos da Vó para o trabalho. Na pausa, Cláudio folheou em silêncio. No final disse 'isso aqui não é hobby, Marina.' Saí da sala antes de chorar.
Read three pages of the Coronel stories to Mom over the phone. She corrected two details. Vó's version had the dog bigger. Mom's version has the jabuticabeira older. I wrote both down.
Festa Junina na casa do Tio Beto. Não tentei Asa Branca. Ele não pediu. Isso é pior do que pedir.

Therapy: she asked what I'd do if I weren't afraid. I said draw for a living and live near the sea. She asked what I was afraid of. I said: of being wrong about what I want. She didn't answer. I appreciated that.

Ônibus, 7h. Uma mulher sentou com um gato numa caixinha de transporte. O gato me olhou como se conhecesse minha personalidade inteira. Desenhei ele na margem do caderno. Ninguém pede isso mais, talvez seja por isso que eu continuo fazendo.
Rain again. I made a small drawing of the bus from memory: the seats, the handrails, the fog on the windows. No parrot man. I left a green dot on a shoulder anyway, just in case.
I drew Tio Beto's violão from memory and got the crack in the wood wrong. I'll ask Mom for a photo. He'll never admit he cares.
Vi um homem no ponto de ônibus carregando um limão gigante como se fosse um bebê. Desenhei sem pensar. Acho que Limonada ia se sentir representada.
Swimming lesson was canceled because of rain. I went anyway and sat by the pool like a sad person. Dona Cida waved from the window and shouted 'a engenheira descansa hoje'. I rested. It was hard.
Dreamed of the bus, not the sea. Seu Ivo was there with Juca. The parrot said 'menina do mar' and I woke up annoyed because a parrot from my own comic should not have better material than me.

Bus 7am, Interbairros II. Desenhei um homem com uma sacola de laranjas e um cachorro sem coleira. O motorista freou e as laranjas rolaram. Todo mundo riu. Desenhei assim mesmo. O ônibus é um estúdio que se move.

Money check: R$ 1.800 left on the 18th. Not great, not terrible. The colored pencils won. The colored pencils always win. I'm telling myself it's an investment in a future career that doesn't exist yet.

Worked late at the factory measuring a motor that wouldn't stop vibrating. Cláudio said 'the machine is just nervous'. I laughed and then sat in the car for five minutes before driving home. I think I am also just nervous.

Hot enough to fry an egg on the sidewalk. The fan in my room sounds like a helicopter. I drew the ice cream cart guy and he gave me a churro for free because he said I made him look handsome. I didn't, but I accepted.
Swimming lesson today. I swallowed water, coughed for five minutes, and Dona Cida said 'the pool is not a beverage'. Fair.
Swimming still hasn't started officially, but I put my face in the shower stream for ten seconds and didn't panic. Bia would laugh. I'm counting it as practice.
Lição #3: Dona Cida disse para parar de lutar contra a água. Eu disse que é fácil falar. Ela flutuou por um minuto sem se mexer e eu quase chorei no canto raso.

Drew Vó's hands from the 14 drawings and this time added her ring. I didn't remember the ring until I looked at the photo. Memory is strange: it keeps the hands and forgets the gold. I'm writing this so I don't forget the gold.
Called Mom on Sunday instead of Vó and the silence on the other end was the loudest thing. She said 'menina, você devia vir no domingo'. I said 'eu sei'. We both did.
I made bolo de fubá using Vó's recipe and forgot the salt. It was sweet in a suspicious way. Mom said 'ta bom' and I knew it wasn't. I ate two slices anyway because I made it and that matters.

Factory day: I drew a diagram for Cláudio and he said 'finally, someone who draws like a human'. I pretended not to be pleased. I was extremely pleased. Then I went home and drew Vó's kitchen from memory, which is less flattering and more important.
Bia, em português porque é da gente. Limonada deu flor. Minúscula, branca, cheiro de limão mesmo sem limão. Fotografei e mandei. Você respondeu 'a menina do mar e a árvore teimosa'. Acertei você.
Money check: R$ 2.900 salary, R$ 800 therapy, R$ 400 drawing supplies I told myself were for work. They are for work. They are also for me. I'm learning the difference is smaller than I thought.

Found the Interbairros old strips on my laptop. I read three of them and felt like visiting someone I used to be. Seu Ivo looks exactly like my grandfather in my head, which is impossible, but there it is.
Therapy. I said out loud that I'm afraid of being a bad engineer if I leave the factory. She asked what 'bad' means. I said 'ungrateful.' She wrote something. I hate when she writes things.
Bia, I tried to float and sank like a stone. But I also ate the best pastel of my life at the feira and that counts as balance, right? Send photo of your window, I need blue.
I called Bia and we talked for two hours about nothing. She said my voice sounded lighter. Maybe it is. Maybe it's just the phone connection.

Went to the pool on a Wednesday and there was an old man doing laps with a snorkel and a radio waterproofed in a bag. I want to be him when I grow up. Also I swallowed less water today, which is progress.

Em português. Terminei o 14º desenho da Vó. Ela era menina em Irati, de vestido curto, com o Coronel do lado. Pinte limpo a mão dela ao redor da orelha do cachorro. A mãe disse que acertei as mãos. Eu não sabia que tinha.
Swimming lesson #20. I can float now. Dona Cida says floating is about trust, not technique. I said that's very poetic for 7am. She splashed me.
Therapy today. I said I'm afraid that if I leave the factory I'll disappoint everyone who said I was good at it. She asked who 'everyone' is. I couldn't name one person. That was uncomfortable.
Aula de natação número 15. Floatiei por trinta segundos. Dona Cida disse que flutuar é confiar. Eu disse que é muito poético para sete da manhã. Ela me jogou água. Justo.
Hot day, no air conditioning at the apartment. Limonada got a new bigger pot because she looked cramped. She has nine leaves now. Still no lemons. We are both stubborn.

Found an old 'Interbairros' sketchbook in the closet. Seu Ivo e o Papagaio. I didn't delete anything, contrary to 2016 me's fear. I looked at them for an hour and thought: I was funny once. Maybe still am.

Drew Seu Ivo and Juca from memory. It took fifteen minutes and I still cried at the bus stop, which is embarrassing because I'm 25 and not 18. But it's a good crying. The kind that means you cared about something real.
Swimming lesson #16. Dona Cida says I'm almost there. I asked 'there' to where. She pointed at the deep end. I said 'no'. She said 'next week'. I believe her, which is new.
Went to the feira and bought jabuticabas. Ate them on the way home and thought of Vó. They were too sour. I ate them anyway.

Bia's birthday again. We video-called and she wore a paper crown she made herself. I wore one too, off camera, which is the most honest version of that sentence. She asked if I'd come to Floripa soon. I said yes. I'm starting to think 'soon' is a place I keep visiting.
Bia, lembrei de 2014, bar em São Francisco, nossos nomes na parede. Acho que pintaram por cima. Mas nós estávamos lá e isso é o que importa.
Aniversário da Bia. Mandei mensagem e ela respondeu com uma foto do mar e 'você aqui'. Eu salvei. Um dia vou responder com a mesma foto, mas de dentro do mar.

I drew Vó Lúcia's hands today from memory. They were smaller than I remembered and more wrinkled. I erased the whole thing twice and started over. The third version made me cry in the kitchen, which is not ideal because Cláudio was on a video call.

Sun today, finally. Walked home instead of taking the bus and drew the route in my head: bakery, pharmacy, the tree with the weird split trunk. I want to draw it for real tomorrow if I wake up early enough.
Swam zero meters again. But I put my feet in the pool at the academy and stayed there for ten minutes. A lady asked if I was okay. I said yes. I meant it.

Therapist asked what I'm afraid of and I said 'being average'. She didn't laugh. She asked what 'average' would look like. I said 'a job I don't hate and a life that doesn't scare me'. She wrote something down. I hate that.
Desenho de Vó Lúcia contando a história do Coronel, versão em que ele rouba um pão da padaria. Acho que inventei isso, mas soa verdade. Algumas memórias são melhor desenhadas do que lembradas.

Aula de natação doze. A Dona Cida diz que estou 'progredindo' e não sei se é elogio ou aviso. Engoli menos água hoje. Conto isso como sucesso. Minhas panturrilhas ainda doem, o que parece prova de que algo está acontecendo.
Sunday lunch at home. Tio Beto brought the violão but didn't play. He just held it. Nobody asked. Sometimes not playing is its own sentence.
Sunday. No one to call. Called Mom anyway and she read me a recipe for bolo de fubá from a magazine. It was wrong. We both knew. We made it anyway over the phone, talking like nothing was missing.
I sketched the view from the factory window during sunset. Cláudio said it looked like a postcard. I said it looked like Tuesday. Both can be true.

Swimming lesson twelve. Dona Cida says I'm 'progressing' and I don't know if that's a compliment or a warning. I swallowed less water today. I count that as success. My calves still hurt, which feels like proof that something is happening.
Therapy today: the therapist asked about the sea dream. I said it's always the same. She asked what I'm standing on. I said sand. She wrote something down. I hate when she writes things down.

Mom came over. She looked at the 14 drawings for a long time and said 'you got her hands right'. I didn't know I had. She took one photo with her phone and sent it to nobody. That's her version of keeping it.
Fez sol a manhã inteira e eu desenhei Limonada no caderno, não o prédio, ela. As folhas estão mais largas que a semana passada. Cláudio me chamou de nerd e eu assenti.
Bia sent a postcard from Floripa. She wrote 'your window is waiting'. I put it on the fridge. It's next to Mom's bolo recipe and a bad drawing of a lemon. Good wall.
Started drawing little comics again, just for me, no posting. The parrot man became a character called Seu Ivo again. I don't know if I'll ever publish. For now it feels safe in the notebook.

Thaís asked for 'something less technical' on a diagram and I drew a tiny sun with sunglasses. She laughed and said 'this is going to the investor deck'. I nearly fell off my chair. The sun has sunglasses. I have a career.
Swimming lesson #14. I went under the water with my eyes open for the first time. The pool is blue and noisy and nothing like the sea. But I wasn't afraid, which is something.

Therapy: she asked what I'd do if I weren't afraid. I said draw for a living and live near the sea. She asked what I'm afraid of. I said I'd tell her next session. I'm writing this so I don't forget that I promised.
Planted basil next to Limonada. She ignored it. The basil is thriving out of spite, which I respect.
Therapy. She asked what I would do if I weren't afraid. I said: draw for a living and live near the sea. She asked what I was afraid of. I'm still thinking.
Saw a kid floating in the pool, out of pure spite, like the kid in Matinhos years ago. I laughed underwater and swallowed half the pool. Dona Cida pretended not to notice.
Therapy again. She asked what I would do if I weren't afraid. I said draw for a living and live near the sea. Then I cried in the car for ten minutes and drove home.
Independence Day, no parade for me. I stayed home and drew 14 little panels of Vó's stories. Her hands are the hardest part. I keep erasing them and starting over.

Sonhei com o mar de novo. Dessa vez eu não estava na beira. Estava numa cozinha, ouvindo barulho de onda pela janela, e alguém fazia bolo de fubá. Não vi quem era. Acordei com cheiro de milho, que é impossível. Mas acordei bem.
Bia, your mom told me she found an old 'Interbairros' strip printed and taped to her fridge. Seu Ivo. She said the parrot looks like your uncle. It does, a little. I laughed for ten minutes.
Em português. Domingo. Acordei cedo, fiz café, desenhei por uma hora sem pensar. É o mesmo horário da chamada de domingo. Desenhar virou o lugar onde a chamada mora agora. Acho que está tudo bem.
No ônibus vi um menino dormindo com a cabeça no ombro do pai. Desenhei rápido e depois achei invasivo. Mas guardei o desenho porque o rosto do pai parecia tão cansado e gentil.

Bia video-called from Floripa and showed me the sea through the window. I said 'save me the room'. She said 'it's yours whenever'. I closed the laptop and sat on the floor for a minute because my chest felt too small.

Therapist asked me to name one thing I'm not afraid of. I said 'drawing badly'. She asked if I meant 'drawing'. I said no, I'm terrified of drawing well, because then I'd have to take it seriously. She smiled. I hate her a little.

Mom called and asked if I was 'still going to those psychology meetings'. I said therapy, Mom, and yes. She was quiet and then asked if the therapist was 'at least Catholic'. I said no. She said 'fine' in a tone that meant not fine.
Limonada is covered in small white flowers. No lemons yet, but the smell in the kitchen is enough. I keep the window open just for that.
Domingo de sol e eu não fiz nada produtivo. Desenhei a Limonada, tomei café, olhei o céu. Às vezes isso conta como viver.
Found an old Interbairros strip saved on my hard drive. Seu Ivo and Juca. I didn't delete it. I don't know if that's loyalty or stubbornness. Maybe it's the same muscle.

The parrot on the bus isn't there anymore, but a woman got on with a cat in a stroller today. The driver said 'bom dia' to the cat. I drew the whole thing. Some days Curitiba is a small, ridiculous gift.
A kid at the bakery asked if I was drawing a 'real person' from Vó's stories. I said yes. He asked if she was famous. I said 'in my family, yes.' He seemed satisfied. So am I.
Dream: standing at the edge of the sea, warm water, feet in the sand. I didn't go in. But I stayed longer than usual. Woke up and drew the shoreline before it faded.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's, but smaller this year. He played 'Asa Branca' without being asked. I didn't sing, again. But I stayed in the kitchen the whole time, which felt like enough.
Started a new sketchbook. On the first page I wrote 'for Vó's hands'. On the second page I drew the coffee cup again, because practice is less romantic than feelings but more useful.
Sunday dinner at Tio Beto's. He played 'Asa Branca' and I hummed along for the first time without him asking. He looked at me and didn't say a word. That was better than applause.
Tio, I practiced Asa Branca for 40 minutes tonight and got through the first verse without stopping. My fingers hurt and I'm ridiculously proud. Don't tell anyone I'm practicing in secret.
The bus was late and I almost missed my stop. An old lady grabbed my sleeve and said 'desce aqui, menina'. She didn't know my name. She called me menina anyway. It felt like a small Vó moment.
Limonada está quase um metro e meio agora. Três galhos novos. Nenhuma flor, nenhum limão. Olho pra ela e penso: você também não sabe o que está virando, né.

Sunday. I tried to play 'Asa Branca' on the violão Tio Beto lent me. Got through the first line and stopped. The strings hurt my fingers and my pride. I put the violão back in its case like it was sleeping.
Money check: R$ 1.900 after rent and the car battery. Not bad. I put R$ 100 in the 'MAR' fund and felt very brave for exactly two minutes.
Money check: paid all bills on time and still had R$ 200 left. I put it in the 'MAR' fund and felt like a millionaire for about an hour.
The RU pastel price went up. R$ 8.50. I complained out loud and the girl behind the counter said 'inflation'. We both laughed. I miss when things were cheap and I was too.

One year since Vó died. I didn't go to Irati because of work and because I wasn't ready. I drew her today instead: the hat from graduation, the hands, the laugh. I put it on the fridge next to her bolo recipe. Mom hasn't said anything. That's enough.
Um ano sem a Vó. Liguei para a Mom e ela não atendeu, depois mandou mensagem só com um coração. Desenhei a jabuticabeira que ela descreveu, mas não tenho foto, então é só imaginação.
One year without Vó. I went to her grave in Irati with Tio Beto. He played 'Asa Branca' quietly and I sat on the grass and drew the trees. The birds there were loud and exactly right.

Um ano desde que a Vó morreu. Não fui a Irati. Desenhei as mãos dela em vez disso, devagar, pela foto em que ela segura uma xícara de café. Errei o polegar duas vezes. Guardo as duas versões porque ela tinha bons polegares.
Found my old calculus notebook while organizing the shelf. The margin still has the parrot drawing from 2014. He looks small and brave. I kept the notebook. Some failures are worth keeping.

Bus home at 6pm, crowded. A woman was reading a children's book out loud to her daughter and everyone pretended not to listen. I listened. Drew them both on the ticket. The daughter looked like Vó as a girl, maybe.
One year without Vó. I went to the cemetery with red flowers because she said yellow looked 'doente'. There was a cat sitting on her stone. I think she would have liked that. I drew it on the spot.
Pago a conta de luz e ainda sobrou o suficiente pra um pastel. Pequenas vitórias, Marina. Escreve isso porque você esquece rápido.
Desenhei o motor da fábrica de memória, sem referência. Cláudio reconheceu. Disse 'você desenha o que ama, não o que vê'. Saí pensando nisso o resto do dia.
Dona Cida faltou e eu nadei sozinha por 15 minutos. Não foi bonito, mas foi. Saí do mar cloro com as pernas tremendo e me senti incrivelmente viva.

Therapy: I said 'I stopped calling anyone on Sundays because there's no one to call'. She asked who I'd call if I could. I said Vó. She asked who next. I said Bia. Then I said I do call Bia. She said 'then Sundays aren't empty'. I hated that she was right.
I visited Vó's grave in Irati with Mom and Tio Beto. Mom brought flowers. Tio Beto didn't play the violão, but he hummed 'Asa Branca' by the gate. I drew the scene later, from memory.

One year since Vó died. I didn't go to Irati. I drew her hands instead, slow, from the photo where she's holding a coffee cup. I got the thumb wrong twice. I'm keeping both versions because she had good thumbs.

Money check: paid all the bills and still have R$ 80 for the rest of the month. I'm calling that a victory, not a disaster. The notebook with the budget smells like the sea for no reason and I love it.

Festa Junina memory: Tio Beto didn't hand me the violão this year and I was relieved and sad in equal parts. I helped in the kitchen instead. The canjica was good. I sang under my breath and nobody heard.
I reread the 2016 capsule about the lemon seeds. 'Do you still have a lemon tree?' I do. She's on the windowsill, stubborn and leafy and fruitless. We are similar, I think.
Bia, I had a dream that you texted me a photo of the sea with no caption. I woke up and checked my phone. There was no message, just a newsletter about kitchen appliances. Rude.
Passei o domingo inteiro desenhando o Coronel. Deixei as orelhas grandes demais. A Vó teria corrigido. Faz parte.

Worked all Saturday on technical diagrams. My hand hurt, but in the good way. I sketched a motor in the margin and Cláudio wrote 'nice' on it. One word. I'm putting it on the fridge next to RU receipts.
Raining all week. The factory smelled like wet concrete and everyone was irritated. I stayed after my shift to finish a diagram and ate a pão de queijo frio. Good day, actually.
Money check: R$ 4.200, rent paid, two pastéis de feira justified. I bought myself a new pencil set and felt guilty for six hours, then drew something with it and stopped feeling guilty.
Made pastel de feira for dinner because I missed 2015. Ate it on the balcony. It rained a little. I drew the view with the rain on the glass and it looked like the sea if you squinted. I squinted.
Pasta for dinner, again. I drew the pot while it boiled and the drawing is better than the pasta. This may be a metaphor. I'm not exploring it.
I tried to swim in the condominium pool after work. Lasted one lap and swallowed water. The lifeguard asked if I was okay. I said yes and then cried in the locker room. Normal day.
Bia perguntou por que eu nunca desenho ela. Desenhei ela ontem, de costas na janela de Floripa. Mandei. Ela respondeu com um emoji de sol e nada mais. Foi perfeito.
I started the little drawings of Vó's stories again. Coronel gets braver every version, just like she told it. I think that's how memory works.

Factory lunch: Cláudio told me about his granddaughter's drawings and then asked to see mine. I showed him one Vó drawing. He looked at it for a long time and said 'you should do this all day'. I laughed and changed the subject.

Bia, Floripa window report: is it still loud? Mine is quiet and I'm not sure I like it. Quiet sounds too much like Sunday phone calls that don't happen. Send me a voice note with the flute/kettle noise.
Listened to Rafa's old playlist while drawing Vó's hands. Halfway through I realized I wasn't listening for him, just for the songs. That felt like something. Not closure, but close to the door.

Tio Beto, I played 'Asa Branca' in my room today and only forgot the second verse. I'm getting closer. Next year at the party I'll play it for you, even if my hands shake. Thank you for the three chords that started everything.
Limonada has a tiny new branch near the bottom, growing out at an angle like she's reaching for something. I moved her a little closer to the window. Maybe she'll find it.
Um ano do falecimento da Vó. Fiz sopa de legumes e comi sozinha. Desenhei a mão dela segurando a colher. Ainda não consigo desenhar o rosto. Um dia.
Mom saw the drawings of Vó's stories again. This time she said 'she would have complained about the nose'. Then she asked for copies. I pretended not to be emotional. I was.
Halloween isn't our thing but Bia sent a photo of herself in a sheet ghost costume with the caption 'remember 2014'. I laughed so hard on the bus I missed my stop.
Mom sent a photo of Vó's old tablecloth being used for lunch. She didn't mention Vó. I didn't either. We are both experts at talking around the hole.

Halloween no escritório, Thaís de sol de óculos escuros. Ela disse que era em homenagem à mim. Eu disse que o sol era meu. Ela disse 'então é homenagem ao seu desenho'. Éramos quatro pessoas e um cachorro.
Sunday. No call to make. I drew instead, at the time I used to call her. It felt like a conversation, just slower.
Finados. I went to the cemetery in Curitiba even though Vó is in Irati. Lit a candle for a stranger's grave because it had no flowers. It felt less wrong than doing nothing.

Mom, I know you think therapy is for people with bigger problems. I think it's for people who are tired of pretending they're fine. I'm fine, mostly. But I'm tired. The lemon tree needs water and so do I.
Dona Cida told me her secret is not to fight the water. I said 'that's very philosophical for 7am'. She said 'you're very difficult for 7am'. Fair.
Voltei da natação encharcada porque esqueci a toalha. Dona Cida disse que é 'coisa de engenheira' e me emprestou a dela. Eu notei que ela tem um peixe bordado no canto.

Swimming lesson #19. I floated for ten seconds without panic. Dona Cida clapped from the edge. I swallowed water and didn't care. This is the most embarrassing good thing that has ever happened to me.
Sunday with no phone call to make. I sat at the kitchen table and drew for two hours. At the end I realized I had drawn the sea, not Vó. She was probably in it somewhere anyway.
Bus to the bakery. The old man with the bandaged hand wasn't there, nobody was. I sat in his spot and felt like an imposter. Some seats belong to stories, not people.

First real swimming lesson tomorrow at 7am. Adult beginners. I packed my bag three times and still forgot the towel. Bia sent a voice note cheering. I feel like I'm going to a final exam I didn't study for.
Sunday. I didn't call anyone. I made bolo de fubá from Mom's recipe and it was too dry. I ate a slice anyway and said 'Vó would have said something'. She would have. That's the point.

Sunday. No one to call on Sunday. I called Bia anyway and she answered on the second ring. We talked about nothing for an hour. She said 'menina do mar' by accident and went quiet. I said it's okay. It was.
Comecei a desenhar as histórias da Vó em caderno separado. São 14 desenhos e nenhum está 'certo', mas ela aparece. Acho que é isso que importa.

Signed up for swimming lessons. Adult beginners, 7am, I'm the youngest by 20 years. Dona Cida, 71, swims better than me and calls me 'a engenheira'. I swallowed half the pool today. I'm going back Thursday.

Bus 7am, Interbairros II. Uma senhora com um gato numa caixa de sapatos disse bom dia pro motorista. O motorista respondeu. Desenhei os dois e senti que o ônibus ainda é o meu estúdio, só mudou o elenco.

Swimming lesson, the first one after signing up. I'm the youngest by twenty years and Dona Cida calls me 'a engenheira'. I swallowed half the pool. My nose still smells like chlorine. I'm going back Thursday because I said I would.

R$ 4.200 this month, minus rent, minus the car repair I didn't plan for. Money check: I survived. I also ate bolacha for dinner twice, which Mom would have opinions about. The 'MAR' fund got R$ 200. Better than nothing.

Signed up for swimming lessons. Adult beginners, 7am. I'm the youngest by 20 years. Dona Cida, 71, swims better than me and calls me 'a engenheira'. I swallowed half the pool today. I'm going back Thursday.
Há um ano Rafa era só nome distante. Hoje nem procurei o Instagram. Acho que é progresso. Comi pizza sozinha e desenhei o gato do prédio vizinho, que se chama Nuvem segundo o porteiro.
Five years since Rafa. I didn't plan anything about it, but I made pastel at home and it was good. That's enough. The playlist stayed deleted this time, which I'm counting as grown-up behavior.

Five years since the capsule to Rafa. I reread it and didn't feel anything dramatic, just a small warmth in the chest. The playlist is still in a folder called 'não apagar'. I haven't pressed play in months.
Money check: R$ 3.800 salary, first time I have leftovers that aren't an accident. I moved R$ 300 to 'MAR'. The app asked me to name the fund. I typed 'MAR' and meant it.
Swimming lesson ten. I can put my face in the water now without holding my breath like I'm hiding from someone. Dona Cida said 'good' in a way that meant 'finally.' I'll take it.
Swimming lesson #3. Dona Cida floated next to me like it was nothing and said 'the water wants to hold you, Marina'. I said 'tell that to my lungs'. She laughed so hard she swallowed water too.
Money check: R$ 3.600, first paycheck after the raise. I bought a sketchbook with better paper and didn't feel guilty. I did feel a little guilty. Then I drew in it for an hour, which fixed it.
Limonada lost a leaf and I panicked for no reason. Bia said leaves fall, it's not a metaphor. She's right. I'm writing this so future me remembers that not every leaf is a sign.
Swimming lesson. Dona Cida said floating is about trust, not technique. I said that's very poetic for 7am. She splashed me. I floated for three seconds and panicked. Progress-ish.

Thanksgiving isn't ours but Bia declared it ours and made turkey. I brought lemon pie from a recipe that didn't work. Mom ate two slices and said 'está diferente, mas bom'. Diferente is my favorite compliment from her.
The parrot man's absence still bothers me. I drew him one more time, from the back, with Juca on his shoulder. I hope they're both fine in Ponta Grossa.
Primeira aula oficial de natação, nível adulto iniciante. A Dona Cida, 71 anos, nada melhor que eu e me chama de 'a engenheira'. Engoli metade da piscina. Volto na quinta. Promessa.
Tio Beto, I practiced 'Asa Branca' today and only forgot the third verse. Progress, maybe. Thank you for not asking about Festa Junina. I know you're waiting. I'm working on it.
Em português. Aula de natação 7. Flutuei quatro segundos antes de afundar. Dona Cida disse 'confiança, engenheira'. Saí da piscina molhada e feliz. 18 anos eu pedi isso. Demora, mas chega.
Primeira aula de natação para adultos. Sou a mais nova por vinte anos e engoli metade da piscina. A Dona Cida me chamou de a engenheira. Volto quinta.

December already. I keep thinking last Christmas was the first without Vó and this one will be the second. The first one still feels like the only one. I don't know when it becomes normal. Maybe it doesn't.
First cold night of December. I wrapped Limonada in a scarf and brought her inside. She looks ridiculous. I look ridiculous. We match.

Mãe, I painted your kitchen from memory and hung it on my wall. The stove is wrong and the window is too big, but you're in it, and you're smiling. Thank you for still sending food even when I say I'm fine.
Decorated the apartment with a tiny fake tree. Limonada got a red ribbon. Mom said it's tacky. Bia said it's perfect. Both are right, probably.
Limonada has a new leaf. Just one. I took a photo and sent it to Bia. She said 'decorateive lemon, not decorative'. I'm not sure what that means but I'll take it.
Mom made bolo de fubá again and this time it was good, almost right. She said 'your grandmother's hands were magic, mine are just hands'. I told her hers are fine. She didn't answer but smiled.
Frio em Curitiba, Limonada dentro de casa enrolada numa echarpe. Ela tem 18 folhas agora. Conte. Não conte os galhos. Os galhos ainda estão aprendendo a ser galhos.
Therapy: she asked what I'd do if I weren't afraid. I said draw for a living and live near the sea. She asked what I'm afraid of. I'm still thinking. But I'm thinking out loud now, which is new.
Mom came for lunch. She saw the drawing of Vó's hands on the table and said nothing for a long time. Then 'she had those lines, the ones by the thumb.' She was right. I fixed them later.
First proper summer-ish day. I took Limonada outside and she looked like a small queen surveying her kingdom of concrete and laundry. Still no lemons. The audacity.

Bia texted me a photo of the sea from her window. I stared at it for a full minute, then drew it badly and sent it back. She said it was better than the photo. It wasn't, but I kept the compliment in my pocket.

Tio Beto, I still haven't played 'Asa Branca' all the way through. I know. But last night I played the first verse for myself in the kitchen and didn't mess up the chords. Small promise, small keeping. Obrigada pelo violão que não é meu mas mora na minha cabeça.
Limonada tem sete folhas novas e nenhuma flor. Bia diz que é decorativa. Eu recuso. Reguei ela e li em voz alta um trecho da história do Coronel. Ela não reagiu, mas creio que ouviu.

Tio Beto mandou um áudio tocando 'Asa Branca' até o segundo verso e parando. Escreveu: 'um dia'. Eu respondi com um desenho do violão dele. Ele não respondeu. Respondeu com um emoji de coração. Tio Beto não usa emoji. Foi real.

Mom is making bolo de fubá again for Christmas. She asked me if it was too dry last year. I said a little. She said 'good, I'll add more butter'. I don't know if that's how baking works but I said okay.

First December without Christmas plans beyond Mom's bolo de fubá. I'm practicing 'Asa Branca' in secret. Tio Beto sent another voice message, this time playing the whole song. I'm not ready, but I'm closer.
Christmas tree small. Put a drawing of Vó next to it, not a photo. Photos freeze. Drawings breathe a little. Tio Beto saw it and said nothing. That was enough.
First Christmas shopping. Bought Mom a printer ink cartridge because she prints my comics and pretends she doesn't. She'll say it's unnecessary. She'll use it tomorrow.
Therapy. I told her about the dream: sea, warm water, Vó holding my hand. She asked if I felt afraid in the dream. I didn't. She said 'that's new'. I said 'I know'.
Decorei a árvore com uma bola verde que encontrei no mercado. A Limonada ficou ao lado e parecia aprovada. Natal sem Vó ainda doi, mas doi diferente de antes.
Bia sent a photo of her window in Floripa. The sea is gray today. I zoomed in until it was pixels. Still counts.

Money check: I have R$ 3.200 saved, which is the most I've ever had and still not enough to change my life. But it has a name in the bank app now: 'MAR'. Small steps. The lemon tree gets the first lemon someday, I'm convinced.
Wrote Vó's name on a little tag and hung it on the tree. Mom saw it and didn't say anything for a while. Then she hung a tag with 'Coronel' written on it. We didn't talk about it. We didn't need to.
Comprei um caderno novo para desenhar as histórias da Vó e tive medo de estragar a primeira página. Desenhei um pássaro. Ficou meio torto. Aceito.
Bia called and talked about the sea for twenty minutes straight. I listened and drew waves in the notebook margins. She asked what I was drawing. I said 'nothing'. She knew.
Last Sunday call of the year. Bia and I talked until her phone died. I sat with the silence after and didn't reach for anyone else. That's new. I think it might be okay.
Christmas prep: Mom made bolo de fubá again. Less dry. She didn't say anything, just put it on the table. Tio Beto didn't play 'Asa Branca'. I think next year I will ask him to.

Christmas prep at Mom's. She made bolo de fubá and said it was wrong before anyone tasted it. We laughed, then cried, then ate it. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' without being asked. I didn't sing. But I hummed. Barely.

End of the year. I'm tired in a way that sleep doesn't fix. But Dona Cida says I floated for fifteen seconds today, and Limonada has a new leaf, and Bia texted me a photo of a stray cat wearing a tiny scarf. So. Here I am.
New Year plans: Bia invited me to Floripa but I'm staying in Curitiba with Mom. I'm making bolo de fubá. It will be wrong. We will eat it anyway. That's the whole plan.

Christmas Eve at Mom's. She made the bolo de fubá again and it was still too dry. This time we said it out loud, laughed, then cried, then ate it anyway. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' without being asked. I didn't sing, but I hummed, which is something.
First Christmas at home without going to Matinhos. Mom made the bolo de fubá. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' after dinner and I hummed. That counts. I think that counts.
Primeiro Natal sem a Vó. A Mom fez o bolo de fubá e ficou seco demais, ninguém falou nada. Depois ela mesma falou e a gente riu e chorou. Tio Beto tocou Asa Branca sem pedir. Eu não cantei.

First Christmas without Vó was last year; this one is just the second. Mom made the bolo again, a little less dry. Tio Beto played without being asked. I sang this time, quietly, and my voice cracked on 'Asa Branca'. Nobody mentioned it.

Boxing Day leftovers and a drawing of Vó's hands holding a lemon. No lemon came from Limonada this year, but the drawing has one. Future me, keep the tree alive. It's the only thing I've grown from a seed.
Christmas leftovers for three days. Mom's bolo was better this time, less dry. Nobody said anything. Then Tio Beto said 'almost'. We laughed. That's enough.

Boxing Day, sozinha em casa. Fiz lista de metas para 2022: nadar 25 metros, terminar o livro da Vó, juntar dinheiro. Olhei para a lista e pensei 'e se eu não conseguir?' Depois pensei 'e se conseguir?' Vou ficar com a segunda.
Ano acabando. Fiz 14 desenhos da Vó, não terminei o livro, aprendi a flutuar, não aprendi Asa Branca inteira. Ainda assim, 2021 me pareceu mais meu. Acho que é isso.

Ano novo sem praia. Comi lentilha com a mãe pelo vídeo, e o Tio Beto tocou violão no grupo de WhatsApp. À meia-noite desenhei o ceu da janela. Não é o mar, mas os fogos refletiram no vidro e, por um segundo, parecia água. Feliz 2022, Marina.

New Year on the balcony. Mom called at midnight and talked over the fireworks. I held the phone out so she could hear them. She said 'next year, the beach'. I said 'next year'. I hope we both mean it.
Woke up and wrote down the sea dream before it faded: I was already in the water, and no one was watching. I didn't wake up sad. I think this is what people mean by progress.

Primeira segunda do ano. Ônibus 7:08, Interbairros II. Não tem mais Seu Ivo nem Juca, mas o motorista novo toca rádio alto e canta sem vergonha. Desenhei a mão dele no volante no caderninho. Ainda parece estranho, depois de dois anos de home office, voltar a contar o dia em ônibus.
Portuguese: Hoje o mar apareceu no meu sonho de novo, mas eu entrei sem medo e não acordei com a panturrilha apertada. Acordei com gosto de sal. Não sei se é bom ou só estranho.

First week back after holidays. The factory feels smaller. I measured a motor housing and thought of Vó's hands measuring flour. Same gesture, different flour. I wrote that down because it made me sad and useful.

Primeiro desenho do ano: o velho do ônibus que sempre carrega uma maleta azul. Ele desceu ontem sem a maleta e eu pensei que tinha esquecido. Hoje estava lá, com a maleta de novo. Desenhei as duas versões na mesma página. A verdade é que não sei qual é a certa.
Primeiro domingo do ano. Fiz bolo de fubá com a receita da Vó e ficou seco, igual o da mãe. Ninguém reclamou, mas eu soube. Guardei um pedaço para o café da manhã e comi pensando nela.

A cold morning, the kind where the bus heater smells like burning dust. I drew the woman in front of me, with her wool hat pulled down to her eyebrows. She turned around and smiled. I pretended I was doing calculus. Old habits.
Bus was late, so I sketched the clock at the stop. It said 7:43 for the whole ten minutes, which felt personal.
The sea dream changed. I went in. The water was warm and someone was swimming next to me but I couldn't see who. Woke up and wasn't sad.

Bus was late today and I drew the same old man three times in my notebook waiting. He was not the parrot man. He was just an old man with a very serious umbrella. I missed my stop because of him. Worth it. Still at the factory, still measuring vibrations, still drawing in the margins.
