Bus was late and the driver apologized to everyone by name. I love this city sometimes. Drew him in my notebook, hat too big, smile too wide. Not for the comics, just for me.

Rain all week in Curitiba and Limonada got moved to the top of the shelf because the window leaked. She now has 14 leaves and the same stubborn expression. Bia says plants don't have expressions. Bia has never lived with Limonada.

Bus Interbairros again, 7am. There's a new regular, a woman with a cat in a backpack. The cat and I made eye contact for so long I missed my stop by one. Drew them both before the next one came. Same route, different passengers, still my little museum.

The factory heating is broken and everyone is wearing three layers. Cláudio brought a thermos of coffee and a second thermos of more coffee. I drew him like a survival guide character: 'HOMEM DO INVERNO, NÍVEL 9'. He laughed for ten minutes. Nice to hear that laugh in a room that usually only smells like oil.
Dona Cida me chamou de 'a engenheira' de novo e ainda não decidi se é elogio ou aviso. Ela nadou 40 metros enquanto eu tentava não engolir água. Hoje não chorei no vestiário. Progresso.

Sunday call with Mom. She talked about the neighbor's cat for eleven minutes. I didn't tell her I was drawing Vó's farm while she spoke. The cat somehow got into the kitchen. I think she just wanted someone to talk to.
New year, same balcony in Curitiba, no sea window yet. But I made coffee, drew one ugly small boat in the corner of my planner, and didn't check the time. Progress is a weird animal.
Rain all morning. The bus window was fogged up, so I drew a tiny sea in the condensation and then wiped it away before anyone saw. Felt like a secret.

It rained so hard the street became a river and Bus 23 was 40 minutes late. I drew the window of the bakery across the road because I couldn't see anything else. The baker waved, even though he probably couldn't see me either.

I dreamed of the sea and this time I could see the person swimming next to me. It was not anyone I know. It was just a shape, friendly, like a seal. I woke up and drew it before breakfast. The drawing is better than the dream.

Sunday walk to the bakery near Vó's old street. I bought sonhos and ate two standing outside. The street smelled like rain and wet dust. I wanted to call her about the weather and then remembered the new version of Sundays.
Bia texted me a photo of the sea with just the caption 'your future'. I saved it in a folder called 'MAR' because naming things makes them more real, and I'm very serious about it.
Sunday at Mom's. She made bolo de fubá and asked three times if it was dry. It wasn't. Tio Beto brought the violão but didn't play, just tuned it and put it back. I think that's his version of a hug.
Limonada's leaves looked droopy, so I gave her water and moved her two centimeters away from the cold glass. She already has opinions, like her owner.
Drew Vó Lúcia's hands again, from the photo of her holding the bolo de fubá. I still don't know how I got them right the first time. Maybe I didn't; maybe Mom was being kind.
Factory cafeteria: the feijão is the same color as the badge they gave me. Cláudio said that out loud and then ate it anyway. I drew a tiny spoon holding its breath.

Paguei o aluguel e ainda sobrou R$ 1.200 no 'MAR'. Nao e luxo, e e a primeira vez que respiro. Comi pao com manteiga no cafe e achei que era festa. Curitiba faz isso com a gente: um dia de sol e ja parece feriado.

It's 7am and the pool is empty except for Dona Cida, who is already doing laps like it's normal at her age. I asked if she ever gets tired. She said 'yes, every day, and then I swim anyway'. I wrote that on my hand so I wouldn't forget and then washed my hand in the shower.
Dreamed of the sea again, but this time I was swimming next to someone I couldn't see. Woke up calm. Maybe that's what progress looks like: not the water, just not being afraid of it.
Portuguese: hoje é aniversário da Vó e eu não tinha para quem ligar no domingo. Fui até a lagoa e desenhei a água por uma hora. Não ficou parecido com o mar, mas a cor tentou.
Sunday. Called Mom and she talked for an hour about the neighbor's cat. I drew the cat while she talked. It has a very opinionated face. I think Vó would have liked it.

Bia, your voice note about the sea being 'too loud today' made me laugh and then stand on my balcony pretending I could hear it. I can't. But the wind here smells like someone else's barbecue, so we're equal.
Swimming at 7am. Dona Cida brought me a banana again. I still don't know where she keeps them. I swallowed less water today, which feels like progress and humiliation at the same time.

Bia, I found the old Interbairros notebook in the drawer. The parrot sketches are crooked and I love them. I'm sending you a photo of the one where Juca is yelling at the rain. You're the only person who understands why that's funny.
Aula de natação: Dona Cida disse que eu nado como se estivesse fugindo de alguma coisa. Ela não está errada. Engoli metade da piscina e ainda assim fiquei um pouco mais longe do fundo.

Cláudio me perguntou se eu já pensei em ir para outra área. Eu disse que estava só medindo vibração. Ele riu e falou 'é, Marina, só isso'. Fiquei pensando o dia inteiro e desenhei um motor com asas, besteira, mas gostei.
Bus 7am, Interbairros II. There is a new passenger with a cat in a backpack. The cat does not say bom dia. I drew them anyway. Seu Ivo's ghost is everywhere on this line.
Limonada got a new leaf this week, dark green and shiny like it knows something I don't. Still no lemons. Bia says I should talk to her. I told her I do, mostly complaints about the factory.

Swimming class at 7am. I still swallow water when I panic, but less. Dona Cida says I hold my breath like I'm preparing for a sinkhole. She is not wrong. The pool was cold and my goggles fogged. I came home and drew her hands.

Bia, I finished a strip at 2am and sent it to you because you're the only person who won't ask why it's 2am. It's Seu Ivo, older now, walking slower, no parrot. I don't know if it works. Tell me if it's sad in a good way.
Limonada dropped three leaves and I panicked like she was dying. Bia said all plants do that and I said 'not MY plant'. She did not ask for clarification.

The bus driver today was the one who used to be quiet, but he said 'bom dia' to everyone as they got on. No parrot, no commentary, just that. I drew his reflection in the window because the light was nice. He didn't notice, which made it better.

I made arroz com feijao and it was almost right. Almost. The rice was a little wet, like my confidence. I ate it anyway, standing at the counter, looking at Limonada. She judged me silently, as a plant should.

Valentine's Day. Nobody special, but I bought myself a pastel de feira and walked in Passeio Público alone. The parrot woman was not there. I ate the pastel in peace. That is a good day, even if it doesn't look like one.

Valentine's at the factory. Someone left heart-shaped brigadeiros in the break room and Cláudio ate three. I drew a little heart on a vibration log sheet and then erased it. Being discreet is a profession too.
Feb 14th. No Rafa, obviously, but I bought myself a pastel de feira and ate it on the curb outside the factory. A stray cat watched me the whole time. We had a good evening.
No Valentine. I bought myself a pão de queijo and a new sketchbook. The cashier said 'nice treat' and I said 'I'm the treat'. She laughed. I didn't, but it sounded good.
Valentine's Day without anyone to text. I bought a pastel de feira and sat on the Passeio Público bench. A man feeding pigeons asked if I was okay. I said yes and meant it mostly.
Bus home, rained the whole way. There was a man eating a coxinha with terrifying confidence. I drew his hands. They were beautiful and slightly greasy.

In Portuguese: Choveu a tarde inteira e a Limonada ficou toda molhada na varanda. Trouxe ela para dentro e ela pingou no chão da sala por vinte minutos. Achei que ela estava brava, mas era so agua. Prometo que vou tratar melhor da minha planta.

Bia, I tried your voice message recipe for bolo de fubá and it came out dense like a brick. I ate two slices anyway. Mom would say it needs more corn. She would also eat two slices. Sending you the photo of the crime.
Therapy today. She asked what I would miss most if I left Curitiba. I said the bus, then felt silly, then didn't. Some things are just home-shaped.
Chuva em Curitiba e o ônibus atrasado. Desenhei o motorista e o cobrador no caderno, como se ainda fosse 2014. A diferença é que agora sei que isso também é trabalho, mesmo que ninguém pague.
Rain all weekend. I cleaned the apartment and found the yogurt cup from 2016 behind a book, empty, with 'MARINA' still on it. I kept it. It's now a pencil holder. The circle of life for yogurt cups.
Money check: R$ 2.100 left after rent and the bus pass. Not broke, not comfortable. I bought a new sketchbook instead of fixing my phone screen and I regret nothing until I have to type a message.
Found a lemon seed in the fruit bowl. I almost planted it. Then I remembered Limonada. One impossible tree is enough. I ate the lemon instead. It was terrible and funny.
In Portuguese: Limonada sobreviveu ao verão. Está maior que o vaso. Mudei ela para um vaso de verdade, de barro, comprado no mercado. Ela ficou linda. Ainda sem limão. Mas linda.
Bia, thanks for sending the voice note of the sea from your window at 6am. I listened to it on the factory floor, between motor tests, like a secret.

Limonada has new leaves and one branch that points exactly at my window. I turned the pot so she gets morning sun. Eight leaves? No, more now. She still hasn't given a lemon, but she's stubborn in the way I recognize.

Portuguese: A Bia me mandou mensagem perguntando se eu ainda desenhava. Respondi 'sim' e senti vergonha de demorar tanto para responder. A pergunta dela é sempre a mesma e a minha resposta também, mas a vergonha muda de tamanho.
Chuva a tarde toda em Curitiba. Fiquei desenhando no sofá com uma xícara de mate e a Limonada na janela. Parecia que a cidade inteira tinha desacelerado comigo. Gostei desse ritmo.

Bia, hoje a Limonada colocou duas folhas novas e eu tirei foto para você. Ainda sem limão, mas acho que ela está tentando. Como está o mar da sua janela hoje? Aqui choveu e o ônibus atrasou quarenta minutos. Te mando o desenho da chuva pelo WhatsApp.
Bia, você falou de onda de inverno e eu fiquei com saudade do mar sem nunca ter morado nele. Um dia. Enquanto isso, desenho ondas no caderno da fábrica.

Acordei cedo, fiz café e desenhei a limonada na sacada antes do trânsito começar. Ela ainda não deu limão, mas as folhas brilhavam. Parecia que ela estava fingindo não saber que era oito de março de manhã.

Portuguese: Dona Cida me chamou de a engenheira de novo e depois perguntou se eu já tinha desenhado ela. Disse que sim, de memória, ela com touca cor-de-rosa. Ela disse que era vermelha. Ainda vou corrigir o desenho.

Swimming lesson at 7am, I swallowed water three times and still left happy. Dona Cida says my kick is improving, which is nice because my breathing is still a negotiation. Ate a pão de queijo at the bakery after and felt like an athlete.

Cláudio asked me to redraw the assembly diagrams again, but neater this time. I stayed late at the factory with a ruler and a black pen. The motor looks like a small ugly house. I like it more than the CAD version, which is probably why Cláudio sighs.
At the factory today I measured a motor that vibrates exactly like my phone on silent. I wanted to write that down somewhere so it wouldn't disappear.
Money check: R$ 2.900 left, car insurance due, dentist still pending. I opened the MAR fund to look at it and felt braver for 30 seconds. Then closed it.

Today at swimming Dona Cida made me float while she walked away to talk to the lifeguard. I held it for twelve seconds and then panicked because I couldn't see her. She came back and said 'you were fine, you just didn't believe it'. Fine.

Swimming lesson. Dona Cida made me float for a full minute while she talked about her granddaughter's wedding. I only swallowed water once. She called me 'a engenheira corajosa', which is a lot of words for not drowning.
I called Mom and she told me she found my old sketchbook from 2014 in the closet. She didn't say 'I was wrong'. She said 'you drew a lot of buses'. She is right. I drew a lot of buses.
Mãe, I printed one of the Vó drawings and put it on the fridge. You didn't say anything, but you adjusted it twice so it was straight. That counts. I'm counting it.
Went to Tio Beto's for Sunday lunch. He put the violão on the table and then didn't ask me to play. I almost did anyway. Almost. The feijoada was perfect, which is its own kind of pressure.

Worked all day on vibration reports. By 6pm my eyes hurt and my hand was shaking. I drew one small line drawing of a motor and felt better. It is strange that the thing I am paid to do drains me and the thing I do for free fixes me.
Aula de natação. Dona Cida disse que flutuar é confiar, não técnica. Eu disse que isso é poesia demais para sete da manhã. Ela me jogou água na cara. Aprendi a técnica e a poesia.
Mom, I showed you the drawings of Vó Lúcia's stories and you said 'you got her hands right'. I have thought about that sentence every day since.

Tio, I practiced Asa Branca tonight and got to the third verse before everything fell apart. One day I'll play it all for you without stopping. You told me one more year in 2015. I'm counting on that.
On the bus today a little boy pointed at my sketchbook and said 'desenha o papagaio'. I drew Juca in two minutes. He smiled. His mom said thank you. I didn't correct them about Juca being fictional.
Ten years since the internship started. I looked up the old factory photo: younger, more hair, same hands. I drew my hands now next to it. They have more lines and fewer doubts. Mostly.

Swimming lesson #? Dona Cida made me repeat 'not sinking is enough' until I believed it. I swallowed less water today. She says I'm 'almost elegant'. In the water, at least. On land I still trip over my own flip-flops.

At the RU I overheard two students talking about 'following your passion' like it's obvious. I almost laughed. Then I remembered I used to draw in the margin of my Álgebra notebook and that was the same thing, just smaller.
Mom, I used the printer you gave me to print a drawing of Limonada. She is now hanging on the fridge next to my old comics. Thank you.
Money check: bought a new pen for R$ 42 and felt guilty for three hours. Then drew a page with it and felt zero guilt. The pen is good. My guilt is old.

Domingo ligou pro Tio Beto. Ele falou da horta e de que o limoeiro da casa deu fruto esse ano. Eu contei da Limonada, quatro anos e zero limoes. Ele riu e disse que arvore da Marina demora porque herda da dona. Nao sei se e elogio.

Money check: R$ 2.100 left after rent, bus, food, and one coffee I didn't need. I bought the coffee anyway. It was raining and the café had a plastic plant. I stayed ten minutes longer than I should have and finished a sketch of a woman with a green umbrella.

Mom, I know you think I should stay at the factory because it's stable. I'm not quitting tomorrow. But I wanted to write down that stable is not the same as alive. I'll say it to you when I'm ready. Maybe soon.
Swimming lesson. Dona Cida made me practice breathing on land. I looked ridiculous. She said all progress looks ridiculous from the outside.

At work, a new drawing request: vibration sensor housing. I made the sketch a little too elegant and Cláudio said 'engineering is not an art contest'. He then asked for a copy. I'm keeping this private victory.

Walked past the Passeio Público and thought of Rafa and the pastel and the first date. Not sad, just strange, like remembering a song you used to know all the words to. I bought a pastel anyway. Solo. It was good.

Money check: paid all bills on time and still had R$ 400 left. I saved R$ 200 and spent R$ 200 on a book about sea creatures. The book is heavy and beautiful. The savings are light and invisible. Both make me feel safer in different ways.
Money check: R$ 4.200 salary, rent, food, savings. I opened a separate account and named it MAR. It has R$ 800. Not impressive, but it exists, like a tiny door in my chest.
Sunday lunch at Tio Beto's. He made feijoada and forgot the orange slices. We ate anyway and he played half of Asa Branca while we did the dishes. Nobody corrected him.
Found an old printed 'Interbairros' strip in my bag from 2016. Seu Ivo and Juca, still funny. I don't know why I kept it folded like that.

Mom, I put a drawing of your kitchen on the fridge at the factory. The one with the window and the clock that's always five minutes slow. Someone asked who painted it and I said my mother. That's a lie, but it's the right kind.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was swimming, badly, but swimming. The person next to me was blurred. I woke up with my hair damp, which is impossible.
April Fool's. Nobody fooled me. I drew a fake resignation letter and almost left it on Cláudio's desk, then remembered I need the factory salary. Almost brave.

April Fool's: I told Mom I was considering a master's in São Paulo and she went quiet in a way that lasted three minutes. Then she said 'Curitiba tem mestrado também'. She is very efficient with fear. I was only joking, but the joke felt like a test I didn't pass.
Bus 7am. No parrot man, of course. But there is a new woman who knits a blue scarf every day and never looks up. She didn't notice me drawing her. Maybe Seu Ivo had a secret knitter rival.

Ate a terrible lemon from the market today and thought of Limonada. She is eight years old and has never given me anything but leaves. I admire the commitment. I also watered her twice because I felt guilty for eating her cousin.
Bia, I drew you on the phone, laughing, with your hair up. I didn't send it because it looked too much like love and I didn't want to be weird. But it's true, so I'm writing it here instead.

Dreamed of the sea again, but this time I was walking on the beach with my work shoes on. The sea didn't ask me to go in. I just watched. Woke up calm, which is new. I think the swimming lessons are changing the dream, slowly.
Bia called from Floripa. She opened the window so I could hear the sea through the phone. It sounded like someone shuffling papers. I said it was beautiful anyway, and it was true.
Money check: R$ 1.900 left, ten days to go. I am not crying this time. I am simply eating rice with a feeling.
At the factory Cláudio asked why I was sketching during a vibration test. I said stress. He said 'drawing is never stress'. He is annoyingly right.

Dreamed of Vó Lúcia in the kitchen, cutting jabuticaba with a knife that was too big for her hands. She told me Coronel was waiting at the gate. I woke up and drew her hands before they left. Got them right, I think.

Money check: R$ 2.100 after rent and the swimming fee. Not as dramatic as 2014, but still the kind of number that makes you stare at the fridge. Mom sent bolachas by mail again. I am 26 and the mailman knows me by name.

Domingo liguei pra mae. Ela falou vinte minutos sobre o novo liquidificador e depois disse, no final, 'voce esta desenhando ainda?'. Eu disse sim. Ela disse 'bom'. Desliguei e fiquei parada na cozinha por um minuto inteiro.

Rained all day. The bus was late, the engine sounded like a tired animal, and I drew three passengers from memory. One woman had a lemon in her bag. I wanted to ask for a recipe. I didn't, because I'm not insane, just hungry.

In Portuguese: Sonhei com a Vó de novo, ela estava cozinhando e nao dizia nada, so sorria. Acendei a cozinha, fiz arroz doce e coloquei canela demais. Comi mesmo assim. Fez a cozinha cheirar igual a casa dela, mais ou menos.

In therapy today I said 'I'm afraid of wanting things'. She didn't say anything for a while, which is her trick. Then she asked what I would draw if I weren't afraid. I said 'the sea, but with me in it'. She said 'then maybe start there'. I haven't started yet.
Mom called to ask if I was eating. I said yes. I had eaten crackers at 11pm. That counts as food in the broad, generous sense of the word.

Money check: R$ 80 left before payday and I still bought a pastel at the RU. It had cheese and disappointment in equal parts. I ate it on the bus. The driver said 'boa tarde' like he knew. He did not know.

Factory lunch: rice, beans, fried egg, farofa. Cláudio told me about the time he drew the whole plant by hand in 1989. He still has the notebook. Some people keep their lives in paper and that makes me feel less alone.
Mãe, I showed you the drawings of Vó's stories again. You said 'the kitchen has the right smell' and I wanted to ask how a drawing has a smell, but I didn't. Thank you.
Money check: R$ 1.200 left and it's only the 18th. I ate RU all week and didn't draw. The sketchbook sat there like a patient dog. Tomorrow I draw the RU tray. Today it wins.

In Portuguese: Vi uma foto antiga da Vó com o cachorro Coronel. Ela era jovem e rindo. Rindo como escadas, do grave para o agudo. Guardei a foto e desenhei a mão dela no cachorro. A mão estava certa dessa vez.
Sea dream again. I went in up to my knees and someone far away waved. I woke up and my feet were cold.

Swimming lesson. I floated for ten seconds without touching the wall. Dona Cida said 'that's the part where you stop fighting'. I said 'I wasn't fighting, I was surviving'. She splashed me anyway. I laughed all the way home.
Cláudio from the factory retired. At the party he said 'you were the only engineer who drew better than the CAD'. I'm putting it on my tombstone.
On the bus, a woman asked me for directions to the hospital. I gave them, then drew her hat while she was getting off. It was a very ordinary hat. Ordinary things deserve witnesses.
Portuguese: no ônibus, um homem tocava violão e cantava 'Asa Branca'. Era ruim, mas cantou até o fim. Aplaudi na cabeça. O motorista olhou para mim pelo retrovisor. Não expliquei.
Cláudio retired last week and I still haven't processed it. The new engineer is 24 and very confident. I want to tell him it's a trap, but he'll learn. Or not. Maybe he'll be happy. I hope so.
Visitei a Bia em Floripa por dois dias. A janela do quarto dela realmente dá para o mar. Fiquei vinte minutos olhando e ela tirou foto das minhas costas. A legenda foi 'quase'. Eu também acho.

Cláudio's retirement party. There was a cake with 'boa sorte' written twice because someone miscounted. He gave a speech about torque and then about kindness. I cried in the bathroom and came back pretending it was the cake.
At the factory a motor made a sound like a cat purring. Cláudio said it was 'normal'. I wrote a tiny comic about a purring motor and it made lunch better. Nobody asked, but I'm keeping it anyway.
Dreamed I could swim but only backward, like a crab. Woke up laughing, which is rare and deserves to be recorded.

Tio, I practiced Asa Branca today for twenty minutes and got to the bridge before my fingers forgot. I know, I know. One more year. But my fingers are improving, which is more than I can say for my guitar case, which is full of old bus sketches.

Bia, you asked if I'm drawing. Yes. Small things: the bus, the pool, Limonada, a motor at work. I didn't show you the drawings of Vó's stories yet because they make me cry and I don't want to cry on video call. Soon.

Mae, passei na frente da casa hoje e o limoeiro do quintal esta cheio de flor. Pensei em voce antes de pensar em limao. Vou te levar um desenho na proxima visita. Nao prometo que esteja bom, mas prometo que estara honesto.
May 1st with family at Tio Beto's. He asked about the violão and I said 'still learning', which is the most honest sentence I have ever said.
Limonada has 19 leaves now. Still no flowers, no lemons, no sign of ambition. I respect her.
Therapy: she asked where I feel the sea dream in my body. I said 'shoulders'. She nodded. I wanted to draw her nodding but that felt like cheating.
Money check: not broke, not rich. The savings account has R$ 800 in it and I named it 'MAR' even though it's not much. It feels nicer to say I'm saving for the sea than for an emergency.
Mother's Day. I called Mom and we talked about nothing for an hour. She said the printer still works and she still prints my comics. I didn't know that. I'm keeping that sentence forever.
Mother's Day. Mom said my drawing of her at the kitchen table made her look 'tired'. I said 'that's the point, you're real'. She cried and then told me to eat. She always finds the exit.

Mother's Day. Mom made bolo de fubá and it was better than last year but still not Vó's. Nobody compared. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' outside and the neighbor clapped from the window. I almost sang. Almost.
Ate a lemon from the market and thought: one day Limonada. Not today. Not this year maybe. But one day. I'm patient. I've been patient for six years. A little more won't kill me.
Found an old Interbairros printout in my backpack. Seu Ivo and Juca, smiling. I don't even remember printing it. I put it back. Some days the past is just a passenger.
Went to Matinhos for the weekend with Bia's family. I floated for thirty seconds and cried into the water, which is either progress or salt. Both, probably. The sand was warm and nobody asked me why.

I found an old 'Interbairros' strip saved on my phone, the one with Seu Ivo and Juca. 2.000 likes feels like another person's life. I almost reposted it and then didn't. Maybe next month. Or maybe I let it rest like Seu Ivo in Ponta Grossa.

Festa Junina plans with Tio Beto over the phone. He asked if I was practicing 'Asa Branca' and I said 'a little'. The truth is I played it twice this month and forgot the middle again. He said 'one more year' without me asking, which is either encouragement or a curse.
The lemon tree still has no lemons. It has flowers now, small white ones, and they smell like something I can't name. I'm calling that enough until it isn't.
Drew Vó Lúcia's hands again. I think I finally got the wrist right, the way she held the coffee cup with both hands. Mom says I got it right. I put the drawing in the folder with the other fourteen.
Limonada has nine leaves now. I counted them twice because the number felt important, and then felt silly for feeling that.
Bia sent a photo of a man at the market carrying a green parrot. I stared at it for five minutes. It wasn't Seu Ivo. Grief is so strange, it makes you scan the world for ghosts.
Bia, your window in Floripa still lives in my head like a lighthouse. I'm not moving yet. But I opened the 'MAR' fund today and almost booked a ticket. Almost counts as courage, right?
Dreamed about the sea again. This time I was already inside, but I kept turning around to check if anyone was watching. Nobody was. I think that's the part I need to keep.
Limonada tem uma folha nova e uma mancha de sol no vaso. Ela segue sem dar limão, mas segue viva. Se isso não for lição de paciência, não sei o que é.

The pool was crowded today. I swam next to a man who was clearly showing off and I, predictably, swallowed water. Dona Cida said 'you can't compete with a peacock'. I laughed so hard I almost drowned. Again. Progress is not linear.
Swimming lesson #40-something. Floated for 20 seconds. Dona Cida said 'the sea is just a bigger pool'. I said 'that's terrifying'. She said 'yes'. We both laughed and then she made me do it again.
Swimming lesson #? I lost count. Dona Cida says I'm not allowed to count anymore, just swim. I swallowed water, recovered, and kept going. She clapped once, like a very serious seal.
Fui ao mercadão com Bia no telefone na orelha. Comprei limão, coentro e um bloco de desenho. A moça da fruta disse que esses limões não vão dar pé. Eu disse que ela não conhece a Limonada.
At Sunday lunch I played three chords very badly and Tio Beto clapped like it was Carnegie Hall. I am keeping him.

Aos domingos, quando não chama ninguém, desenho a janela da cozinha. Hoje tinha um passarinho na antena da vizinha e eu fiquei mais tempo desenhando do que vendo. Isso é um tipo de felicidade, eu acho. Pequena, mas real.
Rain all day. Limonada got a little bath on the balcony. I moved her under the awning and she looked offended. Plants can have opinions; I've decided.
Bia, I miss you in a specific way today: no one is texting me bad puns at 7am. Send puns. I will judge them silently and love them.
Drawing night: finished two pages of Vó's stories and a small comic about a lemon tree that refuses to give lemons. I think Limonada is becoming a character. She deserves a spin-off.
Sunday. No one to call on Sundays still. I drew instead, for two hours, Vó's hands again. It helped more than it should have.

Swimming lesson. I floated for thirty seconds and then heard Dona Cida say 'finally'. I didn't know she was still watching. Some people stay in the corner of your life and make it warmer without asking for credit.

Limonada has nine leaves now, all new since March. I measured her with a ruler like a real engineer. Bia says I treat a plant like a project. She is correct. The pot is too small again. I need a bigger one and less attachment.
Therapy homework: write down one thing I did this week just because I wanted to. I drew a lemon with a face during a work meeting. Does that count?

Bia, I still have the photo of my back at your window in Floripa. It's my phone wallpaper when I need courage. The sea looks like a promise in it. I'm not moving yet, but I'm keeping the promise alive.

Mãe, hoje o desenho do motor que fiz no almoço saiu quase bonito. O Cláudio enquadrou numa parede do laboratório sem me avisar. Quando eu vi, fiquei com vontade de ligar para a senhora e dizer 'olha'. Mas a senhora não ligou, então estou escrevendo aqui. Obrigada por não ter dito isso em voz alta.
Passed the motor vibration report with no corrections. Cláudio said I should be proud. I felt nothing, then guilt for feeling nothing. Good day at work, bad day at being a person.

Tio Beto, I still can't play 'Asa Branca' all the way through. I played the first verse at Festa Junina and stopped before the second, on purpose this time, because I wanted to know how that felt. It felt like waiting. Next year.
Tio Beto called to say 'June is coming' like a warning. I said I practice in secret now. He laughed, then coughed, then laughed again. I love that man's stubborn lungs.

In Portuguese: Festa Junina no Tio Beto em julho. Ja estou treinando Asa Branca no banheiro porque nao consigo passar do segundo verso. Limonada esta no banheiro comigo, porque a varanda estava fria. Ela e uma boa plateia.

Rain all week. The bus windows fog up and I write little faces in the condensation with my finger, then feel guilty because someone will clean it. I am that kind of person now. A small, guilty artist on public transport.

June in Curitiba means fog on the bus window and everyone pretending it's not cold. I sat in the last seat and drew the reflection of the passenger next to me. He noticed and smiled. Small victories count even when they're not mine.

At the factory Cláudio asked me to redraw an assembly diagram because the CAD looked 'like a robot with a fever'. I spent lunch on it and he pinned it above his desk. I pretended not to see him do it.
Tio Beto, I heard you playing 'Asa Branca' through the open window and I stopped on the sidewalk for ten minutes. One day I'll play it back to you without stopping.
At swimming, a child asked if I was 'the lady who can't swim yet'. I said 'not yet'. Dona Cida almost drowned laughing. I came home and drew the whole thing in four panels.

Bia sent a voice note from Floripa saying the sea was 'ridiculously blue' today. I listened to it three times on the bus. The parrot man was not there, of course, but for a second I imagined Juca saying 'bom dia' to the ocean.
Dia dos Namorados with no boyfriend and a lot of lemon tree. I made limonada from store lemons and pretended it was from Limonada. She is four years old and owes me nothing.
Rained all day and the bus leaked above my seat. An old lady shared her umbrella with me at the stop and called me 'moça' like I'm still young. I think I like being called moça.

Swimming lesson: Dona Cida said I am 'stubborn in a good way'. I told her that's the nicest thing anyone has said to me since Vó called me menina do mar. She didn't ask what that meant. She just nodded.
Mom came to visit and brought a printer cartridge. She saw the Vó drawings on the table and said 'you got her hands right' again, then quickly changed the subject to laundry. I let her.

Limonada lost a leaf in the frost scare and I panicked for five minutes. Then I saw the others were fine. She is stubborn, like me. I moved her closer to the window and told her 'stay'. Plants don't understand Portuguese, but it helped me.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's is next week. I have not practiced 'Asa Branca' at all. I plan to hold the violao and look thoughtful. That has worked for seven years. Not proud. Just honest.
Festa Junina at Tio Beto's next week. I practiced 'Asa Branca' in my room and forgot the second verse again. Some traditions are stronger than me.

Father's Day with Mom at her house. She made bolo de fubá and it was better, still not Vó's. We didn't say that. We talked about the garden instead. The lemon tree in her yard also gives nothing. Apparently it's genetic.

Sunday lunch at Mom's. Tio Beto brought the violão but didn't take it out of the case. I think he's waiting. I think I'm waiting too. We talked about the lemon tree instead and he said 'give it time, everything does'.
June bugs in the window screen. Drawn one. It looked like a tiny armored spaceship. Universe is ridiculous and I mean that affectionately.
Swimming lesson #44, if I'm counting right. Dona Cida says I float when I stop trying so hard. I said that's also true out of the water.
Swimming lesson: floated for thirty seconds without panicking. Dona Cida said 'see, trust' and I said 'I trust the pool, I don't trust my lungs'. She laughed. I did not swallow water. Almost.

Festa Junina at work, surprisingly. Someone brought a violão and played badly. I ate four espetinhos and didn't think about Vó until I got home. Grief is a elevator: sometimes you're on a different floor before you notice.
Tio Beto, I saw your message that you bought a new violão. I hope this one stays in tune better than the old one. I still owe you a full song. I haven't forgotten.
Tio, toquei Asa Branca até o segundo verso hoje e depois esqueci tudo, de novo. Mas toquei sozinha, sem você clamar. Um dia chego no fim. Prometo que não vai ser em doze anos.

In Portuguese: Chuva forte e a luz acabou. Fiquei no escuro desenhando no caderno com a lanterna do celular. Desenhei a Vó cozinhando. Saiu bem. Talvez a luz apagada ajude. Ou talvez eu esteja ficando boa. Espero que seja a segunda.
Portuguese: Festa Junina na casa do Tio Beto. Ele me deu o violão sem dizer nada e eu toquei só até o segundo verso. Ele disse 'um ano mais'. Eu disse que isso já virou religião. Ele riu.

Portuguese: Acordei com vontade de desenhar a Vó Lúcia rindo. Fiz três tentativas e nenhuma ficou certa, mas as mãos saíram boas. Talvez seja isso que fica quando alguém vai embora: as mãos, o jeito de rir, e o resto a gente inventa.
Almoço de domingo na casa da mamãe: arroz, feijão, linguiça e aquele silêncio bom que só existe em cozinha de domingo. Desenhei o prato antes de comer.

Dreamed of the sea again, but this time I was on the bus, not at the shore. The bus went into the water and kept going, like a boat. Nobody panicked. I woke up with my feet warm, which never happened before. Wrote it down because the change feels small and I don't want to lose it.
Festa Junina no Tio Beto. Eu ainda não toquei 'Asa Branca' toda. Mas comi dois bolos e dancei descalça com a prima Lívia. Ele disse 'um ano a mais', sem pressa. Estou começando a gostar desse prazo.
Worked all Saturday on a vibration report nobody will read carefully. Made a tiny doodle of the motor in the margin. If anyone asks, it's a diagram. It is not a diagram.

At the factory, Cláudio retired and someone brought a cake with too much cream. I ate a slice standing near the motor assembly diagrams and thought: I am good at this and I am tired. Both things can be true. I wrote it on a Post-it.

One year since I stopped the bus comics, according to no calendar except mine. I opened the old folder and the drawings are rougher than I remembered. The parrot looks wrong in every frame. But Seu Ivo's hand on the railing is right. I might keep that hand.
Swimming lesson. Floating for 12 seconds today. Dona Cida said trust, I said fear, she splashed me again. Progress is wet.
Sea dream again. I was swimming, not floating, and the water was warm. Woke up with my hand on my chest, like checking if it was still there. I'm keeping this one.

Hot day in Curitiba, which is rare and suspicious. I ate pastel de feira at the market and drew the man frying them. He asked if I was from the newspaper. I said no. He said 'shame, I have a good face'. He did.

Limonada has new leaves after the cold week. Small, bright, almost rude in their determination. I moved her closer to the window and talked to her while watering, which I used to think was crazy and now think is polite.
At the factory someone asked why I still draw in my notebook. I said 'old habit'. It's not. It's the only part of the day that feels like mine.
Na piscina hoje pensei em Vó. Ela odiava água fria, dizia que era castigo de Deus. Hoje a água estava morna e eu nadei pensando: castigo nenhum, vó. Só estranho.

After the swimming lesson I bought pão de queijo on the way home and ate it on the bus. A teenager next to me looked at the crumbs and moved one seat. Fair. I drew him anyway, with headphones almost bigger than his head.

I drew Vó Lúcia's laugh again, from memory. The falling-stairs part is hard. I keep making it too elegant. It wasn't elegant. It was loud and a little too high and it filled the room. I'll try again tomorrow.
Dona Cida arrived with a swim cap that has a fish on it. She says it's 'for morale'. I wore it. I swam 10 meters without stopping and felt like I was 18 and 28 at the same time.
Dona Cida put me on the fast lane today. I didn't think I had a fast lane. The pool is still half water, half panic, but the ratio improved.

In Portuguese: Limonada tem oito anos e ainda nenhum limão. Mas tem folhas novas, então estou perdoando ela de novo. Coloquei ela no sol da manhã e ela parece mais viva. Ou parece que quer sol, não sei distinguir.
Money check: the 'MAR' savings fund has R$ 4.200. I stared at it for a long time. It looks small and huge at the same time.
Cláudio's retirement party. He hugged me and said 'don't let the drawings stop, engineer'. I cried in the bathroom for three minutes, which I consider reasonable. Then I ate cake.
Made bolo de fubá from Vó's recipe. Too dry. Mom's version. I ate two slices anyway and forgave myself.
Swimming today was bad. Swallowed water, panicked at the wall, Dona Cida called it 'a very dramatic reunion with the pool'. I laughed and then cried in the shower. Both counts as practice.

Factory day. A motor broke down at 2pm and I spent the afternoon measuring vibrations while thinking about a drawing I hadn't started. I'm good at this, and being good at this is still a little scary. But today it felt less like a trap and more like a season.

I SWAM 25 METERS WITHOUT STOPPING. Dona Cida cried. I cried. 18-year-old me asked for this in 2014 and it took eight years, but it happened. Writing it down so it's official: promise kept. Next one is harder: the factory. It's been almost four years, not two.
Bia sent photos from Floripa. The sea was blue and angry and beautiful. She wrote 'your future window is waiting'. I saved the message in a folder called 'not yet'. One day I'll rename it.

I swam 25 meters. I already know I'm going to write a capsule about it because 2014 me asked for this. But today, privately, I just want to say: my calves didn't hurt this morning. The dream is changing too.
25 meters. OK, not today. 12 and a half, then I touched the wall and acted like that was the plan. Dona Cida nodded in a way that said 'nice try'. Back Thursday.

Nadei 15 metros hoje, parando no meio. Dona Cida nao aplaudiu, so disse 'respira, menina'. Eu respirei. Fiquei tão orgulhosa que desenhei a raia da piscina inteira em casa, com ela no fundo, pequena e exigente.
Curitiba cold enough to see my breath. I walked to the bakery just to warm my hands on the bag of pão de queijo.
Money check: R$ 3.100 after rent. I did not touch the MAR fund. I did look at it twice. It is starting to feel like a person I am dating.

Portuguese: sonhei que Vó Lúcia estava na cozinha cortando jabuticaba. Ela disse 'menina do mar, essa fruta não é do mar, mas você insiste'. Acordei rindo e triste ao mesmo tempo, que é o pior jeito de acordar.
Drawn the kitchen from memory: Vó's bolo de fubá on the table, Mom's hands, Tio Beto's violão on the chair. It took two hours and I feel lighter and heavier at the same time.
Tio Beto, I practiced Asa Branca twice today and got through the third verse before forgetting. This is progress. I'm writing this so you can't say I didn't try. One more year, as promised.
Sonho do mar de novo. Dessa vez eu já estava dentro, nadando. Quando acordei, minha mão estava no peito, como se estivesse conferindo se ainda estava tudo lá.

Bia called from Floripa to say she found an apartment with a balcony bigger than her bed. She talked about the light, not the price. I could hear the sea in the background and pretended it was the washing machine. It wasn't.
Dreamed of sea again. This time I was already in it, not entering. No fear, just salt in my eyes. Woke up and smiled before I was fully awake. Good sign.
The sea dream changed again. I was already in the water, and it was warm, and I didn't need to know who was next to me.
Hoje o ônibus estava vazio e eu sentei na frente, do lado do motorista. Ele dirigia cantarolando. Desenhei a mão dele no volante e a estrada como uma linha que some.

The bus parrot man is gone for good now, but sometimes I still hear 'bom dia, motorista' in my head when the bus stops. I drew it in my sketchbook this morning, from memory. Juca's beak was too big. I left it.
Bus with a new parrot man? No, just a kid with a plastic parrot on a stick. He waved it at the driver and said 'bom dia'. I almost asked for its name. Didn't. Some jokes belong to the bus.

Cláudio retired and came back to visit on a Tuesday. He brought cake and said 'the vibration readings are worse without you'. It was a joke, maybe. I chose to believe it. Then he asked if I was still drawing motors and I said 'only the ones with personality'.
Bia visited Curitiba for the weekend. We went to Passeio Público and sat where I went on my first date with Rafa. Neither of us mentioned it. We talked about her window instead.
Cold Curitiba morning. Limonada got a little flower, white, tiny, smells like nothing and everything. No lemons. I'm choosing optimism over botany.

At the pharmacy the cashier asked if I wanted a bag for one lemon. I said yes. She put the lemon in a bag the size of a shirt. I carried it home like a baby. Limonada still has not produced anything. I'm starting to take it personally.
Mom called to ask if I have 'given up on the drawings yet'. Same question, eight years later. I said no this time. She was quiet, then said 'good'. It may have been nothing. It felt like everything.
Swimming lesson. I did 15 meters without stopping and Dona Cida said 'you're arguing with the water less'. That might be the nicest thing anyone has said to me in a pool. Or anywhere.

At the factory I drew the new assembly diagram and hid a tiny sun in the corner, like in the old comics. Nobody noticed. Thaís hasn't hired me yet. I don't know if she ever will. The sun is there anyway.
Na fábrica, o Cláudio viu um desenho de motor que fiz no intervalo e disse que não era ruim. Do Cláudio, isso é praticamente um prêmio. Guardei o desenho no caderno, não no lixo.

Rain, mud, bus delayed by 40 minutes. I read 'Cem Anos de Solidão' for the third time and still don't understand who is who. But the rain on the window made me draw a small house with a lemon tree. Some days that's enough.

Cláudio's retirement party is still three months away, but he already talks like a man with one foot out. He asked if I ever thought of drawing for a living. I said 'not out loud'. He said 'that's the same as yes'. He's too old to be right.
A colleague at the factory asked if I ever thought about leaving engineering. I said 'every day, quietly'. He nodded like that was a normal answer. Maybe it is.
Bia came from Floripa for a weekend. We sat on my bed and she asked if I was still drawing Vó Lúcia's stories. I said 'slowly'. She said 'slow is still doing'. I wrote that on my wall.
I swam 20 meters today, not 25, and I'm not going to pretend that doesn't count. Dona Cida pretended not to notice I was out of breath.

Dream last night: I was standing at the edge again, but the sea was very small, like a bucket. I put my hand in. Woke up thirsty. Drawed the bucket before forgetting. It looked like a tiny ocean in a cup.

Limonada has a new leaf and a tiny flower bud? Maybe. It might be a leaf with ambition. I asked Bia to confirm by photo and she said 'Marina, it's a plant, not a child, you can't name every bud'. She is wrong, I already named it Coragem.
In Portuguese: Sonhei que estava nadando, mas dessa vez eu estava com uma pessoa do lado, não sabia quem. Acordou feliz. Acho que é progresso. Não quero analisar demais porque estraga.
Dreamed of Vó Lúcia in the kitchen, singing 'Asa Branca' while stirring. I couldn't see her face, only her hands. I drew them from memory at 3am. The drawing is shaky but true.

Mãe, you asked if the drawings could 'become something'. I said I'm working on it. You nodded, which is your version of a parade. I wanted to tell you they already are something, but I like when you believe it first.
Checked my savings app. The 'MAR' fund has R$ 8.000. I stared at it like it was a small brave animal. I didn't add anything today. Some months are for surviving, not saving.

I stood on the balcony and watched a lemon tree in the building across the street. It has real lemons, fat ones. I felt competitive and then embarrassed. Limonada is still a decorative lemon, as Bia says. I refuse, but with less confidence.
Mom asked if I still think about the sea. I said 'every day'. She said 'then you should go'. She said it like ordering someone to take medicine. I laughed and she didn't. I think she meant it.

Mom, you asked again if drawing will 'turn into something'. It already turned into diagrams, comics, and a small book I'm not showing anyone yet. I'm not arguing this time. I just wanted to write that down somewhere.
Portuguese: Chuva em Curitiba, ônibus atrasado, e mesmo assim o homem do cachorro na mochila estava lá. Desenhei os dois. O cachorro tinha cara de quem também não gosta de segunda-feira.

Visited Bia in Florianópolis for the weekend. The spare room still faces the sea. I stood at the window for ten minutes and she took a photo of my back without asking. She captioned it 'again'. Some things don't need to change to be good.
Interbairros II 7am. The parrot man is gone, but a woman got on with a birdcage and a small radio playing sertanejo. The bus did not react. I did.
Money check: paid all bills, saved a little. The savings account is still called 'MAR'. Every deposit feels like dropping a coin into a secret drawer.
Called Bia and she told me about a man on her bus in Florianópolis who reads aloud to a plant. I said I miss having bus characters.

Mom called to say she printed one of my old Interbairros strips and put it on the fridge. She didn't say 'nice'. She said 'the parrot has your grandfather's eyes'. I don't know what that means but I cried in the bathroom at work.

At the factory, Thaís from marketing asked if I could draw a small sun for a solar project sticker. I drew one with sunglasses and she laughed so hard she choked on coffee. It might actually be used. I feel like I'm cheating by having fun at work.
Mom asked if I'm seeing anyone. I said 'the pool'. She said 'Marina, that's not what I asked'. I said 'I know'. She laughed. I think we both needed that.
Therapy. I told the therapist I still feel like a fraud in engineering. She asked 'what would you draw today if no one paid you?' I said 'the sea, obviously'. She smiled. I hate when she's right.

Saturday. I cleaned the apartment, which means I moved piles from one surface to another and called it progress. Then I drew Vó Lúcia's hands from memory. They came out better than the ones from 2020. Practice sneaks up on you.

At the pool I swam 15 meters without stopping. Nobody cried, including me, but I stood in the shallow end for a while afterward pretending to adjust my goggles. Dona Cida pretended not to notice, which is her version of kindness.
Rain all week. I drew in the bus margins again, like 2014, except now the passengers are different and my drawing is less terrible. Progress is sneaky like that.
Portuguese: A Limonada deu flor de novo. Sem limão, mas com flor. A Bia diz que é limão ornamental e eu ainda me recuso a aceitar isso.
Bia, I saw a parrot on a shoulder today, not green, red. I almost followed the man home. You would have understood.
I tried to cook bolo de fubá from Vó's recipe. It came out dry, like Mom's at Christmas. I ate two slices anyway and texted Bia that I missed her. She sent back a sea photo and no words. Correct.

Had lunch with a former classmate who works in São Paulo now. She talked about the city like it's a person. I listened and thought: I still want the sea. Some things don't change. That's not a failure.
Cláudio retired this year and I miss him more than I expected. The new engineer is efficient and does not draw. I eat lunch alone now. It is fine.

Portuguese: hoje o café da padaria estava muito forte e eu desenhei o copo, a mesa, o homem do jornal. Ele percebeu e disse 'moça, desenha meu cachorro também'. Desenhei. O cachorro chamava-se Pitoco. Pequena glória.
Limonada dropped one leaf today. I panicked and then remembered that's what trees do. She is fine. I am slightly not fine.

Bus 7am. No parrot man, obviously, but a man had a small dog in a backpack and the dog barked at every red light. I drew them. It's not Seu Ivo, but the bus still has people in it who deserve to be kept.
Money check: spent R$ 180 on art supplies I technically don't need. I need them emotionally. The pencil case has a sticker of a parrot that I bought in 2016 and it is peeling. I will not replace it.
A draughtsman at work asked me to sign one of my assembly diagrams. I signed it 'Marina' and a tiny sun. He looked confused. I looked proud. We were both correct.

In Portuguese: O terapeuta perguntou o que eu faria se não tivesse medo. Respondi desenhar para viver e morar perto do mar. Depois perguntou do que eu tenho medo. Respondi 'de estar errada'. Ele sorriu. Ainda não sei se era um sorriso bom.
Money check: savings at R$ 1.500. I renamed the account from MAR to SEEDS, because lemons and courage apparently grow at the same speed. Slowly, then all at once if you're lucky.
Called Tio Beto and he played 'Asa Branca' on the phone, badly, with a dog barking in the background. I laughed so hard I cried. He said 'see, one year'. It has been many years. He is eternal.

Bia, your new apartment in Floripa looks too beautiful in photos. I am jealous in a loving way, which is still jealousy. Tell the window I said hi. Also, did you eat the brigadeiro or save it? Be honest. I will know.
Therapy: she asked if I was drawing for myself or for Vó now. I said both. Then I cried. She handed me tissues and didn't ruin it by talking.
Therapy: she asked what 'ordinary' means. I said 'a life with no big decisions'. She said that's rare and maybe enough. I drew an ordinary cup of coffee. It was the best drawing of the month.
Bia called from Floripa and said she saw a parrot in a tree near the beach. No owner, just a parrot. I told her the name would be Juca, obviously. She agreed without hesitation. Good friend.
At work I drew the assembly line as a little procession of tired robots. Cláudio looked over my shoulder and said nothing. In factory language, that means 'good'. I'm fluent now.

At the factory, I sketched a motor during lunch and Cláudio's replacement asked if it was 'for a presentation'. I said no, it's just for me. He looked confused. I felt like a secret agent with a sketchbook instead of a gun.

Tio Beto, toquei 'Asa Branca' até o segundo verso hoje e não esqueci. Esqueci no terceiro. Mas por um momento inteiro eu toquei sem olhar para a mão. A senhora ia dizer 'quase'. Eu sei. Um dia eu vou tocar até o fim e a senhora vai ter que achar outra coisa para dizer.

Mom, I showed you the drawings of Vó's stories again. You said 'you got her hands right' and then looked away, which means you didn't want me to see you crying. I saw. I didn't say anything. We're getting better at this.
Drew the lemon tree today, every leaf. It took two hours and I missed my bus. Worth it. There's something about drawing something you love that makes time behave differently.
Café da manhã na padaria perto da fábrica: pão francês, manteiga, café com leite. Desenhei o balcão enquanto esperava. O padeiro viu e disse 'ficou bom'. Sem mais.
Therapy homework: write three things I'm afraid of. I wrote: quitting, money, and being ordinary. She said the last one was interesting. I drew it as a small gray cloud with a face.

Cold morning, 7am pool. Dona Cida made me swim with a board and said trust is a muscle too. I wanted to argue but I was too busy not drowning. She is annoying and right, which is a terrible combination.
Limonada has 23 leaves. She is 6 years old and has never given a lemon, a flower, or any sign of gratitude. I love her unconditionally and I am starting to suspect she knows it.

Two years since Vó died. I lit a candle and drew her hands holding a lemon. The drawing is small and imperfect and I taped it above my desk, next to her photo. My room smells like candle wax and old wood.
Money check: I have six months of savings for the first time. That's my courage fund. It has a name in the bank app: 'MAR'.

Therapy. She asked what 'enough' looks like. I said: a window, a drawing table, and not being afraid of my own plans. She asked me to write the plans down. I haven't yet, but the list exists in my head like a stubborn lemon seed.
Limonada grew 3 cm, I measured with a ruler like a mother. She is eight years old with no lemons. Bia says 'decorative lemon' and I am choosing optimism over evidence.

Money check: six months of savings. The bank app says 'MAR'. I stare at it more than I should. It's not a number, it's proof that I can leave when I decide to. That's a strange and good kind of power.
Six months savings. I stared at the number in the app for five minutes like it might change if I looked away. It didn't. It feels like courage with a decimal point.

In Portuguese: Chamei a Bia e ela me contou que o mar em Floripa estava calmo hoje. Disse que sentiu minha falta no café da manhã. Menti que não chorei. Chorou um pouco. Estou guardando dinheiro para visitar ela.

Money check: 'MAR' has seven months now. I stared at it like it might disappear if I looked away. I did not buy the shoes. I bought a new pen and a pastel. Priorities. The pen was cheap and writes like it knows I'm broke.

The 7am pool is cold and I keep going. Dona Cida says the water remembers fear. I think she means the person in the water. I floated today while thinking about Vó Lúcia's farm and did not swallow the pool. Small victory, still victory.
Wrote down another version of the Coronel story from a notebook Vó sent years ago. In this one he waited at the gate in the rain. He gets braver every time. Memory is a kindness.
Wrote a list titled 'things I'm afraid of' and then crossed out half of it because it was just 'talking to people'. Therapy is making me suspicious of my own lists.
Money check, the good kind: paid all bills on the 5th without checking twice. I celebrated with a pastel de feira and felt 18 again, except with money and slightly worse knees.
Último trecho da natação. Vinte metros sem parar. Dona Cida chorou e eu também, mas disfarçamos como cloro. Promessa de 2014 cumprida, com oito anos de atraso e muito engolindo água.

Visited Vó Lúcia's grave in Irati with Mom. The jabuticabeira is small now, but alive. Mom put a candle down and said 'your grandmother would complain about the smoke'. We stayed ten minutes and left.

Money check: I paid all bills on time and even bought a lemon. A real one, from the market. It sat on the counter next to Limonada like a message. I did not eat it. I just wanted her to see what success looks like.

Money check: I bought myself a proper drawing tablet with part of the savings. It felt like spending on a secret identity. The box is still on the floor because I can't throw away something that made me this happy.
Money check: paid the credit card without sweating. This feels like a superpower and I will not get used to it.

Bia sent a voice note saying she saw my old Interbairros strip printed on someone's fridge in Floripa. She sent a photo. It's Seu Ivo e o Papagaio. The parrot has the wrong number of tail feathers. Nobody cared. I cared a little, then let it go.
At the factory, Cláudio's old chair still has his jacket on it. Nobody moves it. I think it's grief, but also laziness. Probably grief.

Dona Cida, thank you for calling me 'a engenheira' even on days I swim badly. I drew you today, with your pink cap and your stern face. You are not old, you are just decisive. I hope I look like you at 71.

Factory party. Cláudio gave a speech about 'the young engineer who draws' and I almost cried into the feijoada. Someone took a photo of me holding a plate and smiling like a person who might actually be happy.
Rua XV in my memory today. Four girls, one bathroom, fridge rules. I still write my name on yogurt out of habit. Old habits are just love letters to who we were.

Sunday calling ritual: I called Mom at 10am. She asked about the car and I said 'still parked'. She laughed. I didn't ask what she was doing, and she didn't tell me, but I could hear Tio Beto's violão in the background. That helps.
On the bus today a woman asked if I was an artist because of my sketchbook. I said 'engineer' first, then 'also artist', then 'mostly tired'. She nodded like that was a complete answer. Maybe it is.
Money check: six months of savings now. I named it MAR in the bank app and felt ridiculous and proud at the same time, which is probably my natural state.
Dreamed of Vó Lúcia's farm again. The jabuticabeira was full and Coronel was waiting at the gate, tail going. I woke up wanting bolo de fubá.
Limonada tem uma folha nova e amarela. Pensei que fosse doença. Tio Beto disse que é como gente: às vezes muda de cor e continua viva. Anotei a frase no caderno.
Swimming: swam 15 meters without stopping. Not 25 yet. Dona Cida said 'halfway is still forward'. I wanted to hug her but I was wet and she's 71 and doesn't hug wet people. Respect.
Halloween-ish. Bia sent me a photo of a pumpkin with a parrot drawn on it. I didn't ask. She just knew. Long-distance friendship is mostly sending each other proof that you're still thinking.

Bia, a senhora da piscina, a Dona Cida, completou 72 anos ontem. Trouxe bolo de fubá para a aula de hoje. Eu comi antes de nadar e quase morri, mas foi bom. Ela disse que 'quem faz 72 pode comer o que quiser'. Concordo. Vou tentar lembrar disso quando chegar lá.

Halloween at the factory office. Someone brought brigadeiros. Cláudio wore a motor as a hat. I drew the whole thing in three minutes during a meeting no one noticed. This is either useful or the beginning of trouble.
Swam 20 meters today, not 25. Five meters missing felt like a planet. Dona Cida said 'the water will be there Thursday'. She is annoyingly right about most things.
In Portuguese: Dia dos Finados. Fui na casa da Vó mentalmente, porque ela está em Irati e eu não fui. Acendi uma vela na cozinha e pensei nela lavando o café. A vela apagou sozinha. Achei bonito.
Swimming. I swam 10 meters without stopping. Dona Cida said 'engineer, that is not 10, that is the beginning of 25'. She is not allowed to be right twice in one day.
Limonada got a second flower. Still no lemon. I said 'take your time' to a plant and meant it. Some things can't be rushed, including me.
Swimming at 7am and the sun came through the pool windows. Dona Cida said 'today you look like you trust the water'. I said 'don't push it'. She splashed me again. Ritual.

Limonada got a tiny new leaf, bright green, almost yellow. I took a photo and sent it to Bia with the caption 'she's trying'. Bia replied 'like mother like daughter'. I am not sure if that's about me or the plant.
Six months of savings now. I opened the bank app three times just to look at the name 'MAR'. It feels like a small, real door.

Today I noticed I haven't checked Rafa's Instagram in months. Not because I'm brave, just because I forgot. The playlist still exists somewhere in my phone. I didn't delete it. I also didn't listen to it. It can stay where it is.
Dona Cida said floating is about trust, not technique. I said that's very poetic for 7am. She splashed me again. I'm keeping the tradition alive, in case future me forgets the small stupid joys.

Portuguese: Limonada perdeu duas folhas e eu quase chorei. Bia disse que isso é normal no frio. Ainda assim fiquei falando com ela enquanto regava, o que prova que falei demais ou que ela realmente é uma pessoa na minha cabeça.
Money check: R$ 2.100 left on the 12th. Not good, not terrible. I drew my bank app balance as a person with a tired smile. It made the number less sharp.
Money check: six months of savings. Not much, but I can see it growing. I opened the account and stared at the number for a minute. It's not the sea yet, but it's a boat.

Portuguese: hoje fez frio e Limonada perdeu mais uma folha. Reguei ela, falei com ela e desenhei o vaso. Bia disse que eu cuido mais da árvore do que de mim. Talvez seja verdade, talvez seja mais fácil.

Mom, I made your bolo de fubá today using the recipe you sent. It was too dry. I called you and you laughed and said 'your grandmother's was worse'. We both knew that was a lie. Thank you for the lie.
Passei na feira de domingo e comprei um limão cheiroso só porque cheirava a Vó Lúcia. É estranho como um cheiro pode abrir uma porta tão rápido. Eu desenhei na mão antes que fosse embora.
Swimming lesson: I did a full lap without stopping and then immediately forgot how to breathe normally. Dona Cida said 'progresso'.
Bia asked if I was still drawing the Interbairros strips. I said no, no time. She said 'you always have time for what matters, you're just afraid of it being yours'. I hate that she is accurate.
Swimming lesson #? I can do 20 meters now and Dona Cida has started calling me 'menina do mar', which is either a compliment or a challenge. I choose to take it as both.

A storm knocked out the power at the factory for two hours. We sat in the dark break room and Cláudio told the story of how he once welded a spoon to a robot arm by accident. I drew it on a napkin. Everyone asked for a copy. I felt ten years old in the best way.
Curitiba cold. I wrapped Limonada in a scarf like 2017. She survived then and I think she knows. I also know. Some rituals are just love with a costume.

Swimming at 7am. I swam 20 meters without stopping and then immediately forgot how to breathe on land. Dona Cida patted my back and said 'you're not drowning, relax'. I relaxed. I did not fully relax.
The factory feels heavier now that Cláudio is gone. Not bad, just slower. I sketch during lunch again, little motors with faces. Nobody stops me. I think that's progress.

Bia, obrigada por perguntar 'você está desenhando?' mesmo quando eu respondo 'mais ou menos'. Isso é o suficiente para eu voltar à mesa. Um dia você vai ler isso e dizer 'obviamente'. E vai estar certa.
Fiquei pensando na Vó Lúcia hoje, no jeito que ela falava 'menina do mar' como se fosse um nome próprio. Desenhei ela do meu jeito, com a mão segurando o telefone.

In Portuguese: Limonada deu uma flor pequena hoje. Branca, cheirando bem. Nenhum limão, mas uma flor. Acho que ela está aprendendo comigo a fazer pouco e bonito. Ou estou projetando. Provavelmente estou projetando.

Bus ride home, a woman was carrying a tiny lemon tree in a supermarket bag. It had one flower. I wanted to ask where she bought it, but she got off first. I wrote 'lemon woman' in the margin and felt like Seu Ivo.

Bia, thank you for the voice note about your new balcony plants. I listened to it while watering Limonada and for a second it sounded like you were here, talking over my shoulder. Plant people understand each other.
Swimming lesson. I floated for ten seconds. Dona Cida said floating is trust, not technique. I said that sounds like therapy. She splashed me. We are friends now, I think. Older friends count double.
Bia sent a voice note of the sea. I listened to it three times while washing dishes. The plates dried in circles. I drew the circles later. Nothing is wasted if I draw it.
I opened the old Interbairros files. Seu Ivo e o Papagaio still makes me smile. Juca was the best parrot I ever invented. Maybe I'll draw them again someday, just for me.
The lemon tree has three new leaves and no lemons. Bia says 'decorative lemon' again. I refuse again. I bought a small stake for support because the pot leans and I am projecting.
Bia, your voice note from Floripa today had the sea in the background. I played it three times. I am not ready for you to be living there, but I am ready for you to keep sending me the water.
Money check: R$ 2.900 this month, plus a small freelance diagram for a friend. I put it in the 'MAR' fund. It is growing slowly, like Limonada, but it is growing.
Bia, I keep your message 'finally' from 2019 as my phone wallpaper. Not because I'm sentimental. Because it's true. I'm finally getting closer to something. I don't know what yet.
Mom asked if the factory job was 'still good'. I said yes. She said 'good, but good like you or good like a trap?' I didn't answer. She didn't push. Growth, maybe.

Tio Beto asked if I was going to Festa Junina next year. I said yes. He said 'then bring the violão'. I said I don't own one. He said 'you will'. I don't know if that's a gift or a prophecy, but I wrote it down.

Tio Beto called to say he played 'Asa Branca' at a bar and nobody listened. He said it like a joke, but I could hear he wanted someone to listen. I told him I would listen next time. I mean it. I need to learn it.
First swim of December, indoor pool, everything echoey. Dona Cida brought panetone. We ate it in swim caps, which I think is the definition of adulthood.

Wrote 'MAR' on the savings app and stared at it for a while. Six months is a number, not a courage. But it's the first number I've ever had that feels like permission. I don't know what I'm permitted to do yet, but the app says I can.
First Sunday of December. I made bolo de fubá using Vó's recipe. Too dry, like Mom's. I added more oil next time and it improved. I think recipes are just grief with measurements.
Finished a drawing of Coronel under the jabuticabeira. His ears are wrong. I'll redo them. Vó would say the dog is handsome anyway, and she would be doing me a kindness.

Money check: I bought a new sketchbook and felt guilty for four hours, then drew Vó Lúcia's farm in it and stopped feeling guilty. Priorities are strange. The sketchbook cost R$ 45, the farm cost nothing, and the farm won.
Mom said 'finally, a drawing with a sea in it' like she had been waiting. I said 'I've been drawing the sea for years'. She said 'not for me'. That landed somewhere important.

Tio Beto asked if I'm playing Asa Branca at Christmas. I said maybe. He said 'maybe is progress'. He's right. I practiced the fourth verse and got through it once. Then cried a little. Not from sadness. From the sound of it.
The sea dream changed again. I was swimming with someone and I could see their feet in the water. Not the face. Just feet and bubbles. I woke up and drew the bubbles before they disappeared.
First cold weekend of December. Limonada came inside by the heater. She looked offended, as if I had insulted her constitution. She is from a yogurt cup. She can handle it.

Mae, comprei um violao emprestado do Tio Beto por um mes. Nao sei tocar 'Asa Branca', mas estou aprendendo os tres acordes que ele me ensinou em 2014. Meus dedos doem. Se voce me ouvir tocando, nao ria. Ou ria, tanto faz.

I made a list of things I want to do before 30. It has seven items, and three of them are about swimming, two about drawing, one about the sea, one about money. I didn't write 'quit the factory' because that would make it too real. But it's there between the lines.
Bus home in the rain. The window fogged and I wrote 'menina do mar' on it with my finger, then erased it before anyone could see. Some things are between me and the glass.
Portuguese: Natal chegando e eu ainda não decidi se vou para Curitiba ou se fico sozinha desenhando. Às vezes sozinha não é solidão, é só um silêncio com café e papel.
Tio Beto at lunch. He asked if I still have the violão's three chords. I played one chord and forgot the rest. He clapped as if I had played a symphony. The man is a saint with bad timing.

In Portuguese: Natal se aproximando e a casa da Vó não está mais lá para ir. Fiz bolo de fubá usando a receita dela. Saiu errado, como sempre. Comi com café e pensei que ela estaria rindo do meu bolo. Rindo e comendo.
Factory almost empty for the holidays. The machines were off and the silence was strange. I sketched the room with no people in it. It looked like a shipwreck. I kind of liked it.
Drew Vó Lúcia at the farm, the way she looked when she told the Coronel story. I got the hands right again. Her hands were always the hardest part, and now they're the part I miss most.

Christmas is coming and the city smells like rain and grilled meat. I bought wrapping paper with little suns on it because it was on sale. Mom will say it's too cheerful. I will wrap her gift in it anyway.

Christmas shopping list: a book of sea stories for Bia, a printer cartridge for Mom even though she won't admit she needs it, and nothing for myself because I already have the pencil that is almost too short to use. I love that pencil and I will not throw it away.
Drew 12 pages of Vó's stories this year. Not a book yet. Not even close. But 12 pages that didn't exist before, and her hands in every one. Counting it as something.
Bia, I listened to the playlist today, the one from Rafa. I didn't cry, which is progress. Then I cried a little because I didn't cry. I'm telling you this so you can laugh at me later.
Mom made bolo de fubá and it was right this time. She didn't say anything, just cut a bigger slice for me. I think Vó Lúcia would have approved. I think that's enough.
Money check: end of year, no panic. That is new. I bought a small frame for Vó Lúcia's bolo de fubá recipe and hung it in the kitchen. Mom saw it and touched the paper with her finger.
End of year feeling. The factory is fine and I am not fine with fine. I cleaned my desk and left a small drawing of a sun with sunglasses in the drawer for whoever sits there next.
Mom brought bolo de fubá. Better than last Christmas, still not Vó's. Nobody said that out loud. We all knew. Tio Beto played Asa Branca and I hummed, which counts as progress.

End of the year. Factory still pays the bills. Swimming still scares me. Drawing still feels like a secret. Limonada still has no lemon. I'm writing this so 2023 me remembers: nothing is finished, and that's okay.
At the factory party I drew caricatures of coworkers on napkins. The new engineer asked if I do commissions. I said no. Then I thought about it all night. Maybe yes.
Christmas Eve. Mom's bolo de fubá was better this year. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' and I almost sang. Almost counts as something.

Christmas Eve. Mom made the bolo de fubá and it was wrong, too dry, and nobody said anything. Then Mom said it herself and we all laughed and then cried. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' without being asked. I still didn't sing. Next year, maybe.
Christmas at Mom's. Dry bolo de fubá again, but this time we said it first and laughed before crying. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' without being asked. I sang two lines. Small, but real.

Christmas Eve. Mom's bolo de fubá was almost right this year, only slightly dry. Nobody said anything until she did. Then we laughed. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' without being asked. I didn't sing, but I listened. That's something.
Went to Vó's grave in Irati with Mom. Brought the notebook with the Coronel versions. Read one out loud at the gate. Mom held my hand and didn't say anything. We didn't need anything else.
Sat on the balcony with Limonada. No lemons yet, but she has buds. I drew one bud with a magnifying glass. The page took forty minutes and felt like five. That's how I know I'm in the right place.
Year-end. I swam, I drew, I didn't quit, I didn't move. The 'MAR' fund exists. Vó's book doesn't yet. That's the gap I'm carrying into 2023. I can carry it. It's heavy, but it's mine.

In Portuguese: Última semana do ano. Fui na piscina sozinha, sem aula, e flutuei olhando o céu. Pensei na Marina de 2014 que não sabia nadar. Pensei na de 2026, espero que ela esteja vendo o mar. Escrevendo aqui para ela saber que estou tentando.
After Christmas I drew the table: Mom's bolo de fubá, Tio Beto's violão, the empty chair. The empty chair I drew bigger than the rest, on purpose.

Portuguese: jantar com Tio Beto e Mom. Ele tocou violão depois do café, não Asa Branca, outra música que ninguém conhecia. Mom disse 'isso é muito triste'. Ele disse 'mas bonito'. Os dois estavam certos.
Bia sent a voice note from Floripa: waves in the background, just 'oi, saudade'. I listened three times. One day I'll answer from a balcony with the same sound, and it won't be a recording.
Tio Beto, I practiced 'Asa Branca' again for New Year's and only forgot the last verse. That's progress by any reasonable standard. Please don't tell me 'one more year' this time.
Year-end money check: I have more than I started with and less than I want. The usual. The MAR fund is intact. I am intact. Close enough.
I made a list of fears: the factory, the sea, the book, the phone ringing on Sundays. I didn't resolve any of them. I just wrote them down neatly, like grocery items. Less scary in ink.
New Year tomorrow. No big plan. Coffee, maybe a drawing, maybe a call. I think that's enough for a year that didn't break me. I'm keeping that as the standard.

New Year in Curitiba, not Matinhos. Bia sent a video of the fireworks over her window and I watched it on my phone in bed. Next year maybe I go. The sea was in the video, small and bright. I am learning that small and bright is enough.
A meia-noite fiquei na varanda, não na água. Limonada tinha uma vela de Natal presa com barbante e eu pensei: não é o mar, mas é meu. Começo 2023 desse jeito.

First day of the new year and Limonada has a single new leaf, pale and stubborn. I gave her a little water and told her she's keeping the family together while I figure out my own roots. She didn't answer, which is fair.

First week without the factory badge and I keep reaching for it in the morning, like a phantom limb. The remote job is quieter than a motor room: just my laptop, the cursor, and the lemon tree watching me from the window like a small green supervisor. I drew the sun with sunglasses during a break and it made me laugh for the first time in days. Maybe this is what starting over feels like before you know it's starting over.

Curitiba is doing that thing where it rains sideways and my umbrella becomes a decoration. The bus was late by twelve minutes, which I used to draw the old man selling umbrellas at the stop. He looks like he knows something about the weather nobody else does. The technical drawing at the factory today was a ventilation shaft; I added a tiny cloud in the corner and Cláudio pretended not to see it. I ate my lunch at my desk and it was exactly the kind of day that makes me grateful for the notebook under my bag. Nothing happened. Everything happened.
First week working from the solar startup office. Thaís brought lemon cake on Monday and said it was 'for motivation'. It was. I ate two slices and then drew the team as solar panels with sunglasses.
Limonada got a new leaf this week. It's the small, stubborn kind of growth that doesn't look like anything yet. I'm choosing to take it as a sign.

Rain since Tuesday. The bus Interbairros II at 7am smelled like wet dog and someone's nescau. I drew three commuters in my notebook with the sun from my phone as a lamp. None of them noticed. The drawing of the man with the umbrella turned out better than the one of the woman with the kid, which is typical: I can never get children's hands right. Future me, please keep a pencil in your coat. You always forget.

First week after quitting the factory. My old engineering badge is still in my bag; I haven't thrown it away, but I also haven't worn it. The solar startup pays less and my panic attacks have halved. I think that's a good trade. Future me, if you're reading this from somewhere with a sea view, please don't pretend you forgot.

Limonada dropped four leaves on the floor overnight and I nearly called a plant doctor before realizing it's January. She's fine. I'm the anxious one. Drew her leaves on the back of a solar diagram before sending it to Thaís.

Sunday morning coffee and Limonada is already getting a little new leaf. The factory feels far away now, but my hands still smell like solder in dreams. I drew the bus from my window and sent it to Bia, who replied 'still the parrot lady' like it was obvious. It is, somehow.

Portuguese capsule test: hoje acordei com vontade de desenhar a Curitiba do inverno, aquele cinza que parece filtro de filme. Fiz três esboços do ponto de ônibus perto de casa e um do Limonada sem folhas novas, só galhos. Acho que ela está guardando energia, como eu. Se em 2024 você tiver folhas novas, eu também.

Money check: last month at the factory, and the bank account says R$ 4.100, which is the most I've ever had and also the most scared I've ever been. Courage fund 'MAR' at R$ 2.300 now. I'm quitting in 18 days and I keep opening the banking app to look at the number like it's a flu shot.
Bus 7am again, first time in months. Still no parrot man, which I know, but I looked anyway. A woman had a little dog in a shopping bag. The dog looked like it had been to more places than me.

Dona Cida sent a voice note saying she swam 50 meters today and that I should stop making excuses. I am not making excuses. I am working. I also have not been to the pool since December, which is a different thing. I drew her standing at the pool edge, arms up like a referee. She looks magnificent. I will go Thursday. (I say this every week.)

Mom, I quit the factory. I know, I know: 'drawing isn't a job'. But my new job is drawing, technically. Less money, more sleeping. You'll probably say 'see, I told you'. I hope you're right about the job, not the money.

Domigo de chuva e café. Fiquei duas horas desenhando a janela da cozinha, com a torneira pingando e o som do tanque. O risco da torneira virou um personagem novo: Torneirinho, que reclama de tudo. Me divirto fácil.
