First week at the solar startup and my manager Thaís asked for 'something less technical' on a diagram. I drew a little sun with sunglasses and now it lives in the investor deck. I am choosing to see that as a good sign.

Bus to the factory for the last month. The driver today had a radio playing 'Lamento Sertanejo' and everyone pretended not to sing along. I sang along. Professional dignity is a ladder I keep forgetting I own.

Money check: still six months in 'MAR', but half of that is now mentally labeled 'book' even though the book is still 12 pages of Vó's stories and one very bad cover idea. I keep thinking I should wait until I'm 'ready'. Future me, if you are reading this and haven't started page 13, start today. Ready is a scam.
First day without the factory badge. My desk at home is just the kitchen table and a second monitor, but I can see the sky from here and I keep drawing little suns in the margins of spreadsheets.
Sunday call with Bia. She asked if I'm drawing. I said yes, then sent a photo of a terrible sketch of a solar panel. She said it was 'emotional'. I'll take it.

Wrote 'menina do mar' on the first page of a new sketchbook today. Not the project, not yet. Just the phrase. I am not ready to start the book about Vó Lúcia. Every time I think about it I hear her laugh, the one that started high and fell like stairs, and I need to sit down. But the phrase is there now, on page one, waiting. That counts.

Bia, I'm quitting the factory. I haven't told Mom yet. You're the first. Come here for the weekend and I'll make you bolo de fubá (wrong, like Mom's, but mine). Bring the photo of Vó laughing that you have on your phone, I need to draw it again, I never got the teeth right.
Money check: first paycheck at the new job is smaller and somehow my table is happier. I bought a proper sketchbook with the difference. Don't tell Mom, she'll say I told you so in 2014.

Bia, today I tried to make Vó Lúcia's bolo de fubá and it came out too dry, exactly like Mom's. I ate two slices standing at the counter and understood something small: recipes are just love with measurements missing. Please keep teaching me.

Rainy morning, bus ride to the factory one of the last ones. A woman across the aisle was knitting something yellow and smiling at her phone. I drew her hands and the yellow thing. It looked like a lemon. Probably coincidence. Probably not.
Bia, I quit. Not the idea of it—the actual job. I'll tell you properly when I get there, but I needed to leave this here first so future me remembers the day I stopped negotiating with myself.

Tomorrow I quit the factory officially. Tonight I packed my desk: one badge, one mug, one drawing of a motor. I kept the drawing. The badge can stay in the drawer; I don't need to carry old definitions forever.

Quit the factory. Took a remote job doing technical drawings and diagrams for a solar energy startup, half the salary of being a 'real engineer', twice the happiness. Mom said 'finally something with drawing in it' as if she hadn't told me drawing wasn't a job. I laughed instead of arguing. Growth?

On the bus to nowhere, just to draw. An old woman had a bag of bergamota peels and the whole back smelled like Christmas. I didn't draw her face, only her hands and the peels. Some things are better left half-seen.

Thaís asked for a diagram of a solar panel array and I gave her one that looked professional and, in the corner, a tiny parrot. She didn't mention it. I checked the draft three times in case I had imagined it. It stayed. I think I'm allowed to be a person at work now.
First paycheck from the solar job came in smaller than I expected and somehow I wasn't scared. I think that's new. The 'MAR' fund still has six months in it and I'm guarding it like a dragon.

Bia, it is February and I have eaten pastel de queijo three times this week because the RU is gone from my life but not from my habits. The solar startup office smells like coffee and new carpet and nobody asks me to measure vibrations in motors. I keep waiting for someone to tell me I am doing it wrong. Nobody does. I think that means it is okay. Also your voice note made me laugh so hard I spilled tea on the keyboard. The Z key is now sticky. Congratulations.

First week at the solar startup. The office is a coworking space with a plant that someone named Cláudio, which is confusing because Cláudio is my old mentor. Thaís brought brigadeiro on my first day. I don't trust jobs where people are this nice yet, but I'm drawing suns with sunglasses for a living, so I'll risk it.
Chuva forte o dia inteiro. Fiquei em casa desenhando o Limonada da janela porque ela parecia brava com o vento. Ela não é brava, eu sei, mas desenho melhor quando finjo que sim.

PT: Hoje choveu em Curitiba o dia inteiro e o Limonada ficou na varanda com aquela cara de planta ofendida. Desenhei ele com uma sombrinha. A Thaís curtiu a imagem no grupo e disse 'coloca no deck'. Eu achei que ela estava brincando. Não estava.

Mom, this capsule arrives two years from now and I want to say thank you for the printer, even if you never say you use it for my comics. Bia's mom is a snitch. I love you. Please don't reprint this part.
Rain all weekend, so I stayed in and drew the farm in Irati from memory. Coronel got slightly braver again. Vó would have corrected the dog's ears and then hugged me.
Dreamed of the sea again, but it was Curitiba rain pretending to be ocean. I was standing in a puddle on Rua XV and thought, close enough. Woke up wanting pastel. Very sophisticated subconscious.

Dona Cida's swimming pool lesson today: she made us float while holding a plastic cup of water on our stomachs. Mine fell in immediately. She said, 'Marina, you are fighting the water again.' She's right. She usually is.

Chuva o dia todo e o app do trabalho caiu três vezes. Desenhei um sol com óculos para a Thaís e ela riu tão alto que meu vizinho bateu na parede. Pequena vitória do dia: the sunglasses sun is now our unofficial logo.

Sunday morning. No one to call on Sundays anymore and I am saying this again because it is still true and still sad. But I drew for two hours instead of calling, and the drawing is of a kitchen I do not recognize, with a woman at the stove whose hands I drew before her face. I think it is Vó. I think it is me. It might be both.

Valentine's Day. No plans, which is fine. I drew a heart on the bathroom mirror with lipstick and immediately washed it off because it looked like a crime scene. Ate a coxinha at the bus stop. The parrot man's old stop still has the bench where I sat. I miss Juca.
Ate feijão tropeiro at the RU and thought of Vó's version, which had more bacon and less certainty. I drew her hands while eating and got sauce on the paper. Future restorers, I'm sorry.
Valentine's Day without Rafa has been normal for years, but today I saw a couple sharing pastel in São Francisco and missed someone, not him specifically. Just the pastel.
Dona Cida asked if I was 'still an engineer' while I was doing my warm-up laps. I said yes, but smaller. She said that's the best kind. I swallowed less water today, which I'm counting as progress.

Bia, I'm sending this because you always ask. No, I haven't moved yet. Yes, I'm still looking at windows in Floripa listings like a woman on a diet looking at cake. The sea is still there, apparently. It has been patient with me longer than I deserve. Tell Júlia I said hi if she's reading over your shoulder, which she is.
Bia, I tried your lemon cake recipe for the first time and it tasted like your apartment. Too sweet. I added extra zest and it became mine. Save me a slice if you visit, I'll pretend it's yours.

Limonada has twelve leaves and one tiny flower that might be a bug bite. I refuse to investigate further because I need the hope. The pot is getting small but every time I think about repotting her I get nervous, like moving her will break the spell. She has never given a lemon. Bia says decorative lemon. I say patience. The afternoon light in the kitchen was the kind of gold that makes me want to draw furniture. I drew the chair instead. The chair deserved it.
Nine years since I moved into the república. I still can't believe four girls fit one bathroom. Today I miss that fridge with all the names on the yogurts. Mine was always gone first.
Swimming at 7am before work. Dona Cida wasn't there, but a man in lane three did the backstroke like a very calm frog. I tried to copy him and got water in my ear for the rest of the day.
PT: Acordei às 5h40 para nadar e o céu ainda estava escuro. No caminho, pensei em desistir. Não desisti. A Dona Cida já estava na piscina, acenando como se fosse uma reunião de trabalho. Talvez seja.

Swimming lane this morning: Dona Cida was not there, so I swam 25 meters and immediately told a stranger who did not care. He said 'nice' in the exact tone people use when a dog does a trick. Fair. I still felt like a champion for an hour.
Bia, sent you a photo of my coffee next to the tram poster and you replied 'still menina do mar, but with a Lisbon accent'. I am taking that as a compliment and a warning.

Swimming at 6:40 because 7:00 means the lane is full of overachievers. Dona Cida wasn't there. I swam 30 meters and argued with myself the whole time about whether counting meters makes me less poetic. It doesn't.

Limonada got her first real repotting today. She's in a red ceramic pot from the feira at Largo da Ordem, cost me R$ 18. She lost two leaves in the move and I stared at them on the floor like they were a diagnosis. She'll be fine. Plants lose leaves. I keep telling myself that.
Last week at the factory. Cláudio's desk is empty and someone put a plant on it that nobody waters. I watered it. If it dies, that's on all of us.

Thaís asked me to 'make it less technical' and I added a sun with sunglasses to a solar panel diagram. She approved it. It is now in the investor deck. I am 27 and a sun with sunglasses is in an investor deck. I want 18-year-old me to know this.

Primeiro dia no home office. Minha cadeira é a mesma, mas a mesa tem vista para o quintal e para Limonada, que hoje parece um pouco mais verde depois da chuva. Ainda não sei se isso é liberdade ou só solidão com Wi-Fi.

Money check: the MAR fund is smaller now because my salary is smaller, but I didn't touch it for rent. I'm eating more RU-adjacent food: arroz, feijão, an egg when I'm fancy. Future me, I hope you're not still doing the 'courage fund' spreadsheet in 2026.
Thaís asked for 'something less technical' and I drew a sun with sunglasses. Now I'm the person who put sunglasses on a diagram. Mom would say this proves drawing is a job. I'm not telling her yet.
Lunch at the RU: rice, beans, chicken that gave up. R$ 3,80. I sat alone and drew a tiny sun with sunglasses in the margin of my notes. Thaís would approve.

Sunday. Called Mom. She asked if I'm eating. I said yes. I was eating instant noodles. We both knew. She didn't say anything, which is her way of saying everything. Drew Limonada from the window instead. Her leaves look like small hands waving.

Hoje tomei chuva no caminho da natação e cheguei atrasada. Dona Cida não reclamou, só disse que a piscina já estava molhada. Consegui nadar 200 metros sem parar, mas decidi não contar para ninguém porque quero que seja meu segredo por um dia.

Mãe, escrevi isso pra te dizer que não, não esqueci de jantar, sim, o arroz queimou um pouco, e não, não precisa mandar mais bolo. Mas se você mandar, eu como. A Limonada está bem. A Thaís disse que o sol de óculos foi 'divertido', que é a palavra que você usou quando viu meu desenho do motor em 2017. Gênios pensam igual.
International Women's Day. Mom sent me an audio saying she's proud of me 'even though engineering was a weird detour'. I listened to it three times while drawing the sun with sunglasses.
Remote work, day nine. I ate lunch on the balcony with Limonada and realized silence has a flavor. Today it tasted like arroz e feijão and possibility.

Mom, you asked if I am eating properly and the answer is that I had rice and beans for lunch and an apple for dinner, which technically counts as a meal if you are generous. I am learning. The remote work is strange: I miss the factory noise for about five minutes every morning and then I do not. I draw during lunch breaks now, small things, the coffee cup, the window, my own hand. You once said drawing was not a job. I am trying not to be petty about it. I am failing.

Bia, today the sea dream changed again. I was swimming and the water was warm, and this time I could see it was just me, no one else. Woke up peaceful and slightly annoyed at my subconscious for being so literal.
Mom, I bought a printer cartridge and thought of you. No, I'm not printing comics again. Yes, I am. But better ones. You'll see.
Swimming lesson in the evening for once. The pool lights were on and everything looked like a very blue dream. I floated for thirty seconds and thought about Vó's hands, which were cold and held on.

Bus Interbairros still runs at 7am, no parrot now, but there's a teenager drawing on the window with his finger. I wanted to tap him on the shoulder and tell him to keep a notebook. I didn't. I'm old enough now to let people be.

Ate a last lemon from the bag Mom sent and thought about 2016, the yogurt cup, the three seeds, the name in capital letters. Limonada has not given me a single lemon in seven years, but she gave me a reason to water something every day, which might be the same thing.

Thaís asked for 'something warmer' on the diagrams and I drew a sun with a little scarf. She sent it to the whole team on Slack with three sun emojis. I closed the laptop and sat there for a minute. It's a small thing. It's not a small thing.

Bia, if you're reading this: I bought a plant for my desk and it's already leaning toward the window like it's homesick. I think it wants the sea too. Save me the spare room, even though it's still 2023 and I haven't moved yet.
Thaís pediu um diagrama de string de painel e eu mandei três versões. Na terceira coloquei um sol de óculos escuros no canto, sem pensar. Ela disse 'gostei'. Eu disse 'era teste'. Mentira.
First month at the solar startup. My manager, Thaís, asked for 'something less technical' on a diagram and I drew a little sun with sunglasses. It's now in the investor deck.

Thaís introduced me in a meeting as 'our engineer-illustrator' and I nearly choked on my water. At the factory, drawing was tolerated like a hobby in the corner. Here it is in the deck, next to the numbers. I keep waiting for someone to take it away. Nobody does.

Swimming lesson with Dona Cida. She made me float on my back for a full minute and I did not panic. She said 'the water wants to hold you, Marina, you just have to let it'. I told her that was very poetic for 7am and she splashed me. Some things are constants. Some things should be.
Remote work means I can eat lunch at home, which means I eat too much rice and beans and then draw like a raccoon. Thaís has not noticed. Productivity remains suspiciously high.
Money check: rent paid, solar invoice paid, and I still have money for a pastel at the feira. I count this as wealth. Vó Lúcia would say it is. She was right about most things.

Tio, I want to record 'Asa Branca' on my phone, just you and the violão, one Sunday at the farm. Not for a video. For me. I'll bring the phone and you bring the hat you always complain about. The hat stays in the story.
Drawing at a café in São Francisco. The waiter asked if I was drawing him. I was drawing the lemon tart, but now I'm drawing him too. He added extra whipped cream. Art has value.
Limonada tem uma folha amarela na ponta. Fiquei ansiosa como se fosse febre em criança. Bia disse que é normal, o vaso é pequeno. Amanhã compro um maior e prometo não exagerar, como sempre exagero.
April Fool's Day and nobody pranked me, which is a prank of its own. I drew a fake announcement that Limonada produced her first lemon. Thaís almost congratulated me. I deleted it quickly.

PT: Passou um ônibus com o mesmo cheiro de ferro velho que eu lembrava do Interbairros II. Quase desenhei um senhor com papagaio só de saudade. Depois lembrei que Seu Ivo não está mais no ponto, e fiquei um pouco triste no ponto de ônibus, como se isso fosse normal.

Sunday: cleaned the apartment, watered Limonada, sketched Vó's farm from memory. The jabuticabeira keeps moving in my drawings, like she is correcting me. I think that's the problem with memory: it edits. I prefer the edits to the facts.

Mom, I know you're reading this later and probably pretending you don't remember saying drawing wasn't a job. I'm not angry. I'm just happy you print my comics. The printer you refused to let me pay for is doing more for me than either of us expected.

I dreamed about the sea again but it was not the old dream. I was already in the water and it was calm and I could see the bottom. There was no one swimming next to me this time. I woke up and thought about Vó Lúcia, who used to say the sea was the only honest thing. I do not know what that means but I wrote it down before I forgot. The notebook by the bed is becoming a graveyard of sentences that sound profound at 3am.
PT: A Thaís me chamou de 'desenhista' pela primeira vez. Não 'engenheira que desenha'. Desenhista. Fingi que não era nada, mas guardei a palavra no bolso como se fosse moeda.

I swam 30 minutes without stopping today, no breaks, just me and the lane. Dona Cida was in the next lane and yelled 'a engenheira!' across the water and three people turned around. I waved like it was normal. It was normal. That's the miracle.

Bia, se isso abrir no seu aniversário (ou perto), quero lembrar que em 2023 você me ligou chorando porque um pombo entrou no seu apartamento e saiu pela janela em duas horas. Isso é amizade de 19 anos. O pombo também.
Domingo na casa da mãe. Tio Beto tentou ensinar 'Asa Branca' para o vizinho de novo. O vizinho é simpático, mas o violão merece mais respeito. Limonada ganhou vaso novo e ficou esnobe.
Mom, I finally stopped arguing when you ask if drawing pays. It does not pay all the bills yet, but it pays enough to make me less angry. Thank you for not saying I told you so. I know you want to.

Rain all week in Curitiba, the kind that makes the lemon tree shake. I worked from the couch and drew the rain hitting the window like it was a diagram. Thaís said 'less poetic, more scale' and I almost replied 'scale is a kind of poetry'. Almost. Growth?
Drew at lunch today for the first time in a week. Just the lemon tree, because it finally has a flower bud and I was afraid to look away in case it changed its mind.

I passed a man on the street today carrying a green parrot on his shoulder and for one second I thought it was Seu Ivo. It was not. But the parrot said 'bom dia' to no one in particular and I drew them from memory standing on the sidewalk. I am 27 and I still draw parrots on the margins of things. Some habits are not phases.

Mom, this opens in 2027. If you're reading it, I probably moved or didn't, and either way you'll say 'I told you so' in your own way. Thank you for the printer. Thank you for printing my comics. Thank you for the dry bolo years too.
Money check: R$ 2.400 left after rent, plus R$ 800 in the MAR fund. I opened the banking app three times to look at it like a pet. It still doesn't buy courage, but it buys pastel.

Bia called and asked if I was drawing. I said yes, which was true for once. She didn't ask what. That's the best question anyone can ask me. I still don't know how to answer it, but I like being asked.

Rain all afternoon. I worked with the window open because the sound helps and because the smell of wet earth makes me feel like I'm 18 again, living in the república with a sketchbook under the mattress.

Limonada's leaves are a little yellow at the edges. I moved her closer to the window and talked to her about persistence, which is absurd but also free therapy. She has one new leaf. I'm choosing to take it personally.

Tiradentes holiday. I finished three pages of technical drawings and one page of Vó Lúcia stories, the one where Coronel waits at the school gate. The dog's ears are getting better. I still don't have a plan for the book.

Earth Day. Thaís gave everyone a small solar charger. Mine has a sticker of a cat that I don't remember putting there. I drew a cat on the charger at lunch, just because. It's a good cat. I named her Juca.

The bus smelled like wet earth after a storm. A kid was pressing his nose to the glass and his mother kept pulling him back. I wanted to tell her some windows are worth the nose print. I drew them instead.
Swimming at 7am again. Dona Cida said I 'swim like I'm apologizing to the water'. She's right. I apologized out loud and she laughed so hard she choked on her own goggles.
Limonada's pot finally has a drainage hole. I drilled it myself and felt like an engineer for five minutes. She did not react, which I interpret as approval.

Portuguese capsule: cozinhei o bolo de fubá da Vó hoje. Ficou bom, não excelente, bom. Coloquei menos açúcar sem querer e a massa ficou mais alta. Acho que ela teria dito 'ficou diferente', que era o elogio dela para coisas que ela não queria admitir que gostou. Comi duas fatias e senti ela na cozinha, o que é ridículo, mas não vou apagar isso.

First month at the solar startup is done. Thaís says my diagrams are 'beautiful and slightly too charming', which I am choosing to take as a compliment and not a performance review. I made a spreadsheet of my income and expenses and named the savings column 'MAR' again. It has R$ 400 in it. That is not a courage fund yet. That is a courage puddle. But puddles become rivers if you are patient, which is what I keep telling myself about Limonada too.
Mom, I bought a printer. Not for you this time. For me. I print my drawings and hang them on the wall, like you did with my comics without telling me. We're both pretending not to care.
Dreamed of the sea again. I wasn't at the edge this time. I was already swimming and the water was warm. I woke up hungry, which feels unfair for a dream.

Found a bus seat by the window and sketched the Interbairros line from memory. The parrot man is gone, but the route is still the same curva near Praça Rui Barbosa. I miss the city in a way I did not expect.

Dia do Trabalho, nothing to work. Cleaned the apartment, watered Limonada, listened to the Rafa playlist by accident and kept it on for two songs then switched to Chico. Progress. Drew a small comic about a girl and a lemon tree. Might become something.

Labour Day. I worked a little because the solar diagram had a deadline, but also because I like the little sun with sunglasses too much to stop drawing it. Mom said 'you found a job where your hobby wears sunglasses'. Fair.

Rode the bus just to see if the parrot man's route still exists without him. The driver is different, the seats are the same, and nobody says 'bom dia, motorista' now. I said it for him. The driver looked startled, which means the tradition is broken. I may need to become a regular.

Money check: I have R$ 3.400 in the MAR fund. Thaís gave me a raise and did not tell me until I noticed it on the payslip. I bought Limonada a new pot. She looks ridiculous in it, too big, like a child in an adult's coat. She has fourteen leaves now and I am counting them like a maniac. Still no lemon. Still no giving up.

Tio, I still haven't learned the third verse of 'Asa Branca'. I can play the first two without crying now, which I think counts. Please don't ask me at Festa Junina if I'm ready. I'll bring the violão anyway.
Money check: the startup pays less, but I bought myself a real sketchbook with hard cover and didn't feel guilty. I'm counting that as financial planning with personality.
Mother's Day weekend at home. Mom made bolo de fubá, but it was too dry and she said it herself before anyone else. We laughed and then cried. I drew her hands holding a spoon.
Tio Beto sent a voice message just saying 'menina, quando você vem tocar?' I have not practiced enough. I will practice enough. I say this every year and mean it for about three days.

Fiz brigadeiro para ninguém, porque tinha leite condensado e paciência. Acabei comendo a panela com a colher e sentindo falta do barulho da cozinha da Vó. Guardei um brigadeiro em um pote pequeno, como se fosse lanche escolar.

Limonada has new leaves, finally. Small ones, pale, stubborn. I stood there for five minutes like a proud parent at a school play. She still has no lemons, but she has attitude, and I respect that. Mom would say 'decorative lemon', and I would defend her with my life.

Tio, I practiced 'Asa Branca' today and got through the second verse without stopping. This is not a victory, you would say, because the third verse is where it falls apart. You are right. But I am closer than last year. I will not play it at Festa Junina unless you ask. If you ask, I will probably play it badly. If you do not ask, I will be quietly offended. This is the arrangement and we both know it.
Mãe, você achou o desenho do bolo de fubá na minha mesa e não disse nada. Eu sei que você viu porque você virou a folha de ponta-cabeça antes de ir embora. O bolo está quase certo. Quase.
PT: Hoje o ônibus atrasou 40 minutos e eu desenhei três pessoas e um cachorro. Nenhuma delas sabia que eu estava fazendo isso. Me senti um pouco espiã, mas pelo menos espiã artística.

Mother's Day. I sent Mom a drawing of her hands holding a printer. She said 'you made my hands old'. I said 'they're beautiful hands'. She changed the subject to the casserole. I'm counting it as a compliment, like the printer years ago.
Mother's Day drawing: Mom's hands holding a printer. I know. It's not poetic. But she cried, so I'm keeping it as evidence that art works sometimes.

Mother's Day without Vó. Mom cried once in the kitchen, then pretended it was the onions. I drew her hands holding a spoon because they looked exactly like Vó's and I wanted to keep that ordinary moment forever.
Bia called and talked for forty minutes about her new balcony plant, and I listened to all of it because someday I will miss this version of her, the one who treats a fern like a roommate.

Nine years since Bia's 18th birthday and the wall in São Francisco. I don't know if the wall still has our names. I don't want to check. Some things survive better as a maybe. I texted Bia 'remember?' and she sent back a marker emoji and no other words, which was perfect.

PT: Achei um desenho antigo do Coronel debaixo de um bloco de notas. Ele está com a boca aberta, parecendo que está latindo. Vó contava que ele latia para o carteiro e depois pedia desculpa. Eu não sei se isso é verdade, mas eu desenhei assim.
Drew Tio Beto's violão from memory and got the scratch on the wood wrong. Corrected it, then left the wrong version in the sketchbook. Memory is allowed to be inaccurate, Marina. You're not a camera.
Dreamed of the sea again, but this time there was a lemon tree growing right on the sand. It made no botanical sense. I drew it before breakfast and it looked like a very confident plant.
Ate the last pastel de feira with extra cheese and felt no guilt. Progress. At 28, this is the kind of freedom I actually wanted at 20.

Thaís asked if I'd illustrate the investor deck's cover. I said I'd try. 'Try' is my word for 'I'm already sketching it at 2am'. The sun with sunglasses is there, plus a panel array that looks like a field. I hope investors like suns. Everyone likes suns.

Money check: R$ 2.100 this month after rent. The 'MAR' fund has grown to R$ 1.800. I am not rich. I am not even comfortable. But I am not the 18-year-old crying in the RU with R$ 340 left, and that is something. I bought myself a decent pencil today, the 4B, and it felt like luxury. The drawing I made with it was of the coffee cup. It looks like a coffee cup. Progress.
Bus in the rain. I drew the condensation on the window and a little face in it. The old lady next to me said 'parece você'. I think she meant the bad mood, not the drawing.

Bus broke down on the Interbairros II, 20 minutes stopped under a tree. A man in the back played samba on his phone out loud. Nobody complained. I drew the driver's hands on the wheel, resting. He looked tired in a dignified way. I want to be like that when I'm tired.

Ate a pastel de queijo at the feira near work and remembered the first date with Rafa. No sadness, just the taste of mint tea after. He was right about some things, wrong about others, and I am finally okay with that.

Thaís asked for 'less technical' again on a diagram, and I added a sun with sunglasses. She laughed, then said to send it to the investor deck. I'm 27 and my career is now partly based on a cartoon sun. Cláudio would be proud.

Swimming lesson #something. My goggles leaked and I swam half blind, which felt like the metaphor for this whole year. Still, 40 meters without panic. Dona Cida said 'agora tu vai' and I pretended not to care.

Heat in Curitiba is a betrayal because everyone says it is a cold city and then June arrives and I am lying on the floor at 2pm with a fan pointed at me. I drew the fan. It has a face now, in my head, and a bad attitude. The lemon tree on the windowsill looks like it is suffering. I moved her inside and now my room smells faintly of dirt and hope. I am not complaining. This is what I asked for.

Saturday. Ate feijoada at Tio Beto's, Limonada got three new leaves this week and I told everyone at the table. They smiled politely. Tio Beto asked if she has lemons yet. She doesn't. He said 'one more year' and I threw a bean at him.

Festa Junina approaching. Tio Beto hasn't texted about 'Asa Branca', which is either mercy or forgetfulness. I've been practicing the chords quietly at night, and Limonada is not a good audience because she doesn't have ears, but she doesn't complain either. That's enough for now.
Practicing 'Asa Branca' with the violão on my knees. My left hand hurts in the old way. Tio Beto would say that means I'm doing it right and I'm choosing to believe him.
Tio Beto, se você abrir isso em 2027, saiba que ainda não sei tocar 'Asa Branca' até o fim, mas prometo que este ano tento. O violão está no canto, empoeirado, com vergonha. Ou eu estou.

Swimming lesson with Dona Cida. She said floating is about trust and then made me float while she held my head with one finger. I stayed up for ten seconds. She said I looked like a very serious starfish.
Tio, I practiced 'Asa Branca' again and my fingers hurt in the good way. If I can play it at Festa Junina this year, I will cry and pretend it is the fireworks. Please save me the violão.
Tio Beto, practised Asa Branca with the metronome app and nearly gave up at the bridge. I recorded myself and it sounded like a cat stepping on piano keys. I'm sending this early so you can laugh.

Swimming at 7am in June in Curitiba is an act of faith. The pool was cold enough to make me question my choices and Dona Cida's sanity. I did 15 meters without stopping, then 20. I did not cry this time, but only because my goggles were foggy.
Made bolo de fubá from Vó Lúcia's recipe. It was too dry again. I ate two slices anyway and wrote 'almost' on the recipe card, which is the nicest word I can give myself today.

I practiced 'Asa Branca' for an hour and my left hand hurts in a way that feels earned. Tio Beto sent a voice note asking if I was still coming to Festa Junina. I said yes. He said 'good, I left the violão tuned'. He has never left the violão tuned before. This means something. I do not know what yet.
Curitiba weather doing its usual dramatic thing: sol, chuva, sol de novo em vinte minutos. Limonada adora chuva, eu não. Desenhei as duas reações em um guardanapo do café.
Sunday at Vó Lúcia's old house, now Mom's. I sat in the garden and drew the jabuticabeira from memory. It's too big in my drawing, but maybe that's how memory works.
Festa Junina practice in the living room. I played 'Asa Branca' until the second verse and then forgot everything. This time I did not panic. I just started again. Tio Beto would clap either way.

Tio Beto, I know you're reading this in the future and already know what happened on the 24th, so this is me before the courage. I practiced until my fingers hurt. If I mess up, clap anyway. If I get through it, please say 'I told you, one more year' again, because I want to hear it one more time while it's true.

Dia dos Namorados alone for the fifth year in a row. I bought myself a pastel de feira and a sketchbook. The pastel was better. Ate it on the bus home, grease on the cover of the new sketchbook. First page. I drew the pastel. It looks like a small angry moon.

Festa Junina is in a week and Tio Beto has not mentioned the violão yet. Neither have I. We are both waiting. This is our whole relationship: two people waiting for the other one to speak first, then pretending it was obvious. I practiced until my fingers hurt. I think I can make it to the end this time. I am not saying it out loud because saying it might curse it. I am only writing it here.
Lisbon plans on hold, but I bought a small poster of a yellow tram and hung it above my desk. Curitiba is wet and familiar and I love it in a tired way. Sometimes that is enough.
I swam 25 meters again, this time without stopping to question my life choices midway. Dona Cida said 'now you're swimming like you mean it'. I said 'I always meant it'. She splashed me anyway.

Curitiba winter: I put on two sweaters and still feel the cold in the bones. The apartment heater is a lie. I drew Vó's farm with snow on it, which never happened, but it felt honest. Memory doesn't care about weather reports. Neither do I, at this point.
Thaís asked if I'd do a small illustration for the company's birthday card. I drew the whole team as plants. She laughed so hard she had to leave the call. This is my favorite kind of work.
Festa Junina is next week and I haven't decided my dress. Last year I wore sneakers and regretted nothing. This year I might wear the blue one Mom thinks is too much. That's exactly why.
Festa Junina coming up. I practiced 'Asa Branca' twice and both times forgot the second verse again. My fingers know the chords better than my memory knows the words. Strange kind of body, this.
Pre-Festa Junina week. I practiced 'Asa Branca' in secret in the laundry room so nobody would hear me fail. Limonada heard everything and did not judge. She has no ears, but still.
Festa Junina. Tio Beto handed me the violão without a word. I played 'Asa Branca' until the end. ALL of it. Nine years late. He said 'I told you, one more year' as if it had been one.
End of June, end of first half at the startup. I drew 47 diagrams and one very unserious sun. I'm tired in a way that feels chosen, not trapped. That's new.
Festa Junina is over. I played until the end. I haven't told anyone how much my hands shook, but Tio Beto said 'one more year' as if it had been one, and I let him have that version.

PT: Festa Junina ontem na casa do Tio Beto. Comi dois pasteis, joguei três balloons e não toquei violão, porque já sabia que ia errar o terceiro verso. Mas fiquei com o violão no colo por uma hora. Tio Beto fez de conta que não viu.

Swimming lesson went badly today. I swallowed water, coughed, and Dona Cida said 'the sea will not drown you, Marina, but you are trying to drown yourself'. She has no filter at 7am. She is right, though. I went back Thursday anyway. That's the whole victory.
Cold morning, three blankets, Limonada shivering on the sill. I brought her closer to the bed and apologized for climate and metaphors. She looked fine. I looked like a scene.

Nine years since the sea dream started. Tonight I dreamed of the sea again, but I was already in it, swimming slowly, and someone was floating next to me, just a shape. Woke up calm. The sheets were warm. Drew it before breakfast: two small shapes in a blue rectangle.
Sunday drawing session. Tried to draw Vó's laugh as stairs and failed twice. Third attempt, I added a small lemon at the bottom of the stairs. Don't know why. It worked.
Winter morning. The lemon tree has four new leaves and zero lemons, same as always. Bia says decorative lemons are a lifestyle. I'm starting to suspect she's right and it hurts.
Dreamed about the sea again, but this time I was drawing it from a bus window. The water stayed water. That feels like progress even if I cannot explain why.
Limonada has three flowers now. Small, white, smelling like nothing I can compare. I drew them before work because I was afraid of forgetting how they looked in the morning light.

Curitiba winter is doing its usual performance: fog until 11am, sun for twenty minutes, then fog again. The solar startup is quiet on weekends so I used Saturday to draw Vó Lúcia's farm from memory. The jabuticabeira is bigger in my head than it probably was. Coronel is running in every version. I know I cannot trust the details but I trust the feeling. The feeling is accurate.

Money check: six months still, untouched, plus a small freelance diagram for a neighbor who is building a shed. He paid me in cake and gratitude. Best invoice of my life. I drew the shed plans with a sun in the corner. He didn't notice. I did.

Dreamed of the sea again. I was already in it, floating, not afraid. But the water was too quiet and I couldn't hear anyone. Woke up and drew the silence instead of the sea. Strange drawing, good one.

Vó Lúcia would have been 84 this week. I made the bolo de fubá from her recipe and it was almost right, almost. Mom said it was good and I believed her because she does not lie about food. I lit a candle and put it on the windowsill next to Limonada. The flame went out twice from the draft. The third time it stayed. Small victories.
Dreamed about the sea again. Not the old dream. I was swimming, and the person next to me was wearing sunglasses. Probably the sun from the investor deck. Therapist would love this.

I made bolo de fubá using Vó Lúcia's recipe. It was not wrong, but it was not hers. Mom texted 'looks good' and didn't mention the crack on top. I think that's her way of saying it was acceptable. I'll take acceptable.
Swam 20 laps today, badly and with pauses, but I counted them and Dona Cida said, 'you are not fighting today.' I think she meant the water. Maybe also everything else.

Winter in Curitiba. The sky is that gray that looks like a bruise. I wore the scarf Mom gave me and bought a hot chocolate at the place near UTFPR. The student in line looked exactly like 18-year-old me. I wanted to tell her to keep drawing. I didn't. Maybe I should have.
Bia texted at midnight: 'are you drawing?' I said yes. I was actually watching a video about pasteles de feira in São Paulo, but the answer still counts spiritually.
Ate a lemon at the kitchen table and thought of the yogurt cup from 2016. Limonada has never given a lemon, but she gives leaves, and leaves are honest enough.

Portuguese: sonhei com a Vó hoje. Ela estava na cozinha, sem avental, rindo de escadas, e disse 'menina do mar, você ainda não nadou no mar?' Eu respondi que ainda não. Ela disse 'então para de desenhar o mar e entra nele'. Acordei com o coração acelerado e a vontade de ligar pra ela, que é a parte que dói. Mas o conselho era bom.

Dona Cida, I went back to the pool today after two months away and I did not die, which is my new standard for success. You were not there, of course, because you are 71 and have a life, but I imagined you at the edge calling me 'a engenheira'. I floated for forty seconds. It is not 50 meters but it is more than four seconds, which was 2015 Marina's entire career. I am sending this to you in 2025 and by then I hope we have swum together again.
PT: Tio Beto me mandou áudio tocando 'Asa Branca' no violão, errando o mesmo acorde que eu erro. Achei que fosse zoeira. Era carinho. Às vezes não sei a diferença, mas este era carinho.
Swam 30 meters without stopping today. Dona Cida didn't cry this time, just nodded like it was obvious. I prefer that. It felt like being trusted.
Thaís asked me to illustrate a whole investor deck in one weekend. I said yes, then panic-drew six suns with sunglasses. They liked them. My body said no, but my wallet said thank you.

Bia sent a photo of her balcony in Floripa: sea, sky, no caption. I stared at it for a minute and then opened a new tab to look at rentals. Closed it. Opened it again. This is my personality now: a woman with one tab open to the future and one to the fear.
Money check: I have five months of savings now, not six. I bought myself a better chair and I'm not apologizing for it. The 'MAR' fund is now called 'MAR and chair' in my head.
Money check: the 'MAR' fund is still growing. I opened the app and just looked at the name for a minute. It's stupid that a bank account makes me emotional, but here we are.

Ate a pastel de queijo at the feira and cried a little, not because of the pastel. The vendor called me 'querida' and it was too close to Vó's voice. I ate another one to recover. It didn't help, but it was good.

Thaís approved my first full diagram set without changes. I printed it and taped it to the fridge next to Limonada. It looks ridiculous and proud. Took a photo and sent to Mom. She sent back a sun emoji. I'll take it.

Thaís gave me feedback that the diagrams are 'clean and human', which I will put on my tombstone next to Cláudio's line about drawing better than CAD. I'm collecting compliments like stickers. At 18 I would have said that's sad. At 27 I say it's inventory.
Mom called to ask if the solar job is 'still drawing'. I said yes and she went quiet in the proud way. I wish I had learned to translate that silence earlier. It took me years.

Called Bia and she was at the beach at 10am on a Tuesday. I was at my desk drawing solar panels. I'm happy for her and also briefly, shamefully, jealous. Then I remembered I chose this. The jealousy left. The happiness stayed.
There is a construction site across the street and every morning at 6:50 a man yells 'bom dia' to nobody. I answer from the window now. He waves. We have a routine without names.

Bia sent a photo of her window in Florianópolis and the sea is right there, as always, mocking me from three states away. I sent back a photo of my windowsill and Limonada. She replied 'your sea'. I replied 'she has never given a lemon'. Bia replied 'neither has the sea'. This is the kind of friendship that survives everything.

I called Vó Lúcia in my head on Sunday. Not out loud, just the habit. Then I sat at the table with the sketchbook and drew her face from memory. The teeth are wrong again. Her laugh is the hardest thing I've ever drawn, because it was never a face, it was a sound that moved.
Thaís usou o sol de óculos no investor deck e ninguém pediu para tirar. Estou chamando isso de 'soft launch de Marina artista'. Faltam apenas 15 anos de coragem.
Frio hoje. Fiz bolo de fubá na cozinha da mãe e acertei a mão, ou quase. Ela comeu duas fatias sem comentar e depois disse 'você pegou o ponto da Vó'. Fingi que não era nada demais.
A woman at the feira recognized my sun-with-sunglasses from the investor deck and asked if I was the artist. I said 'sometimes.' That word felt honest and insufficient.

I drew Coronel again, the farm dog, because I keep losing the exact shape of his ears. Every version gets softer. Vó's stories do that: they wear down the sharp parts until only the love is left. Maybe that's not accuracy. Maybe that's the point.
Bia sent a photo of her window and the sea was gray. I said it was beautiful anyway. She said, 'you always say that.' She's right. I always do.

I swam 25 meters again today, alone, without Dona Cida. It took me eight years to do it the first time and three months to do it the second. The difference is that the second time I was not proving anything. I was just swimming. I think that is what 27 feels like: doing things without the performance of doing them.

Sunday. I called no one, because Sundays are still a little empty. But I drew Vó's farm for two hours and the emptiness became a room I could sit in. Therapy words. They're starting to feel like mine.
Money check: the 'MAR' fund is still alive, and for the first time I added illustration money to it. It is not a fortune, but it is a door. I keep the door unlocked, just in case.

Mãe, hoje eu ia te ligar pra pedir a receita do bolo de fubá outra vez, mas lembrei que você me mandou por áudio em 2021 e eu ainda tenho. Ouvi de novo. Sua voz ficou mais baixa no final, quando você disse 'não deixa queimar'. Eu não queimei. Quase. Obrigada por ensinar sem perceber.
Drew the old man with the parrot from memory. I don't know his real name and I never will. I hope he's somewhere warm, with Juca on his shoulder, saying 'bom dia' to whoever will listen.

PT: Tive um sonho estranho: estava num ônibus noturno e o motorista era Vó Lúcia, jovem, com o chapéu da formatura. Ela disse 'menina do mar, desce no próximo ponto'. Acordei e desenhei o ônibus antes de esquecer. Ainda não sei o que significa.
Limonada grew a new branch at the top, like she's showing off. Still no lemons. I talked to her while watering and then felt silly, so I kept talking. She deserves to know she's doing well.

I found the old 'Interbairros' folder on my hard drive. 40 strips. Seu Ivo and Juca and the bus and the 7am light. I do not post them anymore but I still love them. The parrot man moved to Ponta Grossa years ago and I still think about him when I see a green parrot anywhere, which in Curitiba is never. I drew him again today, older, softer. Some characters do not leave.

Visited Bia in Floripa for the weekend. The spare room faces the sea and she left a towel with my name embroidered on it. I stood at the window and drew the horizon line for twenty minutes. She took a photo of my back again and captioned it 'still'.
A lemon, very small, grew on Limonada and then fell off before ripening. I kept it on the windowsill because it tried. That's enough for me today.
Comics fair in Curitiba. Nobody knew my face without the sunglasses sun. A kid asked me to draw his dog. I drew it with sunglasses too. His mom laughed, so I count it as a success.

The lemon tree got a new pot today because she was root-bound and leaning. I sat on the floor and repotted her like a small surgery, talking the whole time. 'You're okay, you're okay.' I don't know who I was reassuring. We are both leaning toward the window.
Called Tio Beto and he made me play 'Asa Branca' over the phone. He clapped at the wrong time and I loved him for it. I'm getting better at loving people without correcting them.
I printed a small drawing of Vó Lúcia's hands and put it above my desk. Not above the bed, like the sea drawing from 2014, but close enough to look at when the solar diagrams get too straight.

Bia, your voice note about the sunset made me stand at my own window for ten minutes. No sea here, just rooftops and a dog on someone's roof. I drew the dog. It looked like you were right about the light.

Came back from Floripa and cried at the Curitiba bus terminal. Not sad, exactly. Just the contrast between a window full of sea and a terminal full of coffee smell. Drew the crying in the sketchbook. My nose is enormous in drawings when I cry. Physics of it.

Bia, you sent me a photo of the sea from your window at 6:40am and I stared at it until my coffee got cold. I'm not moving yet, but I am looking at apartments in Floripa with windows facing east. Just looking. Mostly.
Money check: six months of savings still. The 'MAR' fund is officially for the book now. I renamed it and felt ridiculous, but also serious, which is a good combination.
Bia, you sent a voice note laughing about Júlia burning rice and I listened to it four times at the bus stop. I miss your kitchen chaos already. Save me a chair.

Booked three weeks in Lisbon for September, working remotely. I told Thaís it was 'inspiration gathering' and she said 'just don't fall in love with the city and quit'. Too late, possibly. I haven't even gone yet. This is how my life works: I pre-fall in love with things and then worry about the falling.

Packed for Lisbon with one sketchbook and too many socks. Decided against the violin strings Tio Beto gave me. Then took them out and put them back in twice. They're in the side pocket now, just in case.

Thaís left a note on my desk that said 'your diagrams are the reason clients say yes'. I put it in the drawer because I do not know what to do with compliments from people who are not my mother. Mom would say 'finally something with drawing in it' and I would laugh. I am laughing now. It is becoming a habit, laughing instead of arguing. I think this is what growth looks like from the inside.

Money check: I have five months of savings again, not six, because I bought a better chair for drawing. My back stopped hurting, so I'm filing this under 'investment' and not 'weakness'. Future me, please don't audit me.
Packed a bag for Lisbon with more sketchbooks than clothes. Thaís said I could work from anywhere and I chose to believe her. The sea is still far, but it's getting closer.

Money check: salary from the startup is R$ 2.900, less than the factory but the 'MAR' fund grew to R$ 3.100 because I stopped buying lunches out. Eating sandwiches at the desk. The sandwich budget drawing is a real genre now. I should publish a book called 'Marina's sad sandwiches'.
Packing for Lisbon with one suitcase and the postcard of the parrot man, which I bought before even going. I'm aware this is ridiculous. I'm also aware I'm very excited.
Lisbon is in three weeks. I keep opening the map app and measuring how far I am from the Tejo. It's not the sea, but it smells like it, according to strangers on the internet who know everything.
Bought a new sketchbook and wrote 'Menina do Mar' on the first page. Nothing else yet. I am giving myself permission to be slow, which is the hardest permission I have ever given.

Lisbon is one week away and I have not finished packing. I have finished three drawings of Curitiba from memory: the bus stop, the RU, the factory gate. I am not sad to leave. I am not thrilled. I am somewhere in the middle, which is where most good decisions live. I will write from there. I will write from everywhere from now on.

Packed for Lisbon: laptop, sketchbook, one sweater, too many chargers, and a small drawing of Limonada for the hotel room because I am sentimental and I don't care. Bia said 'take a photo of the sea for me' and I said 'I will if the sea is nice'. She said 'it's always nice'. She's right. I'm the problem.
Airport. Mom cried at the gate and then said 'go before I change my mind'. Tio Beto sent a voice note playing 'Asa Branca' badly and told me to 'send fotos do mar'. I will.

PT: Céu azul em Curitiba, o que eu sempre trato como evento raro. Levei o Limonada para a varanda e ele parecia feliz, se uma planta pode parecer feliz. Tirei uma foto para Bia. Ela respondeu 'parece que ele está tomando sol'. É isso.
Aeroporto de Curitiba. I ate a pastel at 5am and it tasted like goodbye and also like breakfast. I'm carrying the old 'Interbairros' notebook with me, just in case I meet someone worth drawing.

Packing for Lisbon. I have packed the postcard of the man with the parrot, three sketchbooks, one toothbrush, and too many charging cables. I did not pack the violão because I only know one song and that song needs a room with people in it. I am excited and scared in equal amounts, which is how I know it is the right thing to do. 18-year-old me wanted the sea. I am going toward it.

One week until Lisbon. I packed a pencil case instead of extra clothes. Thaís said I can work from anywhere. I keep looking at Limonada and thinking 'who waters you'. Bia's cousin will. I wrote instructions on a sticky note. They are very bossy. Like Vó.
Lisbon, café in Alfama, 10:12. The coffee is too strong and I love it. A pigeon walked across my table and looked at my drawing. I chose to take it as approval.
Thaís asked if I'd be okay working remotely from Portugal for a month. I said yes before she finished the sentence. Then I spent twenty minutes drawing a tiny airplane with a sun inside it.

Lisbon! I'm writing this from a café in Alfama, three weeks of working remotely here. I can see the Tejo, which isn't technically the sea but it smells like it. I keep thinking I could live here. Then I think of Bia and Mom and the RU pastel and I'm not sure. Future me: did you move? Don't lie.
Mom, the laundry here dries in two hours and I understand now why you always complained about Curitiba's humidity. I also understand why you stayed. I'm thinking about both things at once.

Lisbon, day 4. I found a miradouro near my rental and drew the rooftops. An old man sat next to me and said 'bom dia' without looking. I said 'bom dia' back. He left. I missed the parrot man for a second. Then I drew him from memory, on the same page, next to the rooftops.
Lisbon, day four. The café owner called me 'menina' and my whole body went still. I drew him a small sun with sunglasses as a tip. He taped it to the espresso machine.
Lisbon day one, technically just landed and I am sitting in a café in Alfama staring at the Tejo like it owes me something. It smells like sea and coffee. I am already homesick and already in love.

Portuguese: dia 6 em Lisboa. Acordei cedo e fui até o Tejo. Não é o mar, eu sei, mas tem cheiro de sal e gaivotas e isso já é mais mar do que eu tive em anos. Desenhei um homem com chapéu e um casal discutindo no tram. A cidade fala alto, como a Curitiba que eu invento na cabeça. Gosto daqui. Isso me assusta.
Lisbon, day 6. The Tejo smells like the sea and I keep walking toward it. I drew a tram full of people and nobody looked like anyone I know, which is both lonely and freeing.
Found a shop with a cat sleeping on the postcards. Bought the parrot one and almost cried at the cashier, not because of the postcard. She asked if I was okay. I said 'sim, só vento'.

Lisbon, day 8. Ate a pastel de nata that made me understand why people move cities for pastry. I drew it too. The custard looks like a small sun with sunglasses. Thaís would approve. I'm drawing signs on everything now. Lisbon is a city of small signs.
Found a tiny bookshop in Alfama with old Portuguese editions. Bought one about the ocean that I can't fully read yet. Future me, if you read this and know Portuguese properly, smile.

Lisbon, a café in Alfama. The owner heard me ask for 'um café' and switched to perfect Portuguese-accent English, which is flattering and slightly insulting. The coffee is small and strong and I love it.
Found a tiny postcard of a man with a parrot on his shoulder in a shop in Alfama. The shop owner said it was old stock from the 1950s. I bought it for the price of a coffee and put it on my laptop.

Lisbon, day nine. The light here is different, thinner, and it makes everything look like it is about to become a painting. I drew the tram today, the yellow one, and an old woman with a bag of fish. She caught me drawing and waved. I waved back. The Tejo is not the sea but it smells like it and I will take it. The solar startup does not mind where I work. Thaís said 'send photos'. I sent photos.
PT: Um cliente pediu para redesenhar um diagrama 'mais sério'. Eu fiz mais sério e adicionei um solzinho minúsculo no canto. Ninguém notou. Eu notei. Isso é o suficiente.
Lisbon, day 12. In a tiny shop in Alfama I found a postcard of a man with a parrot on his shoulder, from the 1950s. Bought it for R$ 2 worth of euros. It's on my laptop now.

Found the parrot postcard in Alfama and cried in a tiny shop over two euros. The man's parrot looked like Juca, and Seu Ivo, and every bird I've ever invented to feel less alone. The shopkeeper asked if I was okay and I said 'I'm an illustrator', as if that explained everything. It did, somehow.
Found the postcard with the man and the parrot in Alfama. I bought it and put it inside the notebook like a bookmark. Some things don't need a reason. They just need to be kept.

Last day in Lisbon. I sat by the Tejo and tried to draw the light on the water and couldn't. Light on water is impossible, it's always moving. I drew my own hand holding the pencil instead. It's a good hand. Vó would say I got the knuckles right. I think I did.
Back in Curitiba and the air smells like damp leaves. I unpacked everything except the parrot postcard, which stayed on my desk like a guest who refused to leave.
Lisbon, day fourteen. I walked to the river before work and sketched the water until my hand hurt. The Tejo is not the sea, but it listens like one.

Started drawing one page a week again, like 18-year-old me asked. This week it's a small comic about a man and a parrot on a bus, except now the man is old and the parrot says 'tchau, motorista'. I don't know why I keep returning to them. Maybe because they were the first thing I drew that felt like mine.
Worked from the café again today. Thaís thinks I'm 'inspired'. The truth is I'm just close enough to the Tejo to pretend the river is the sea, and that's working fine.
Lisbon, day 19. Walked to the Tejo in the rain and drew the boats. A man with a parrot was not there, because I'm not allowed to have everything, but I checked.

Back in Curitiba. Limonada survived, barely: one leaf yellow, Bia's cousin apologized in a voice note that lasted four minutes. I watered her and talked to her for ten minutes. Mom said I treat the plant like a child. She's not wrong. I'll take it.

Back in Curitiba, and the apartment feels smaller after Lisbon. Limonada looked exactly the same, which is either reassuring or rude. I watered her and apologized for leaving. She didn't answer, but she didn't drop leaves either, so I'm taking it as forgiveness.
Back home. The lemon tree survived my absence, which feels like a small vote of confidence from the universe. Limonada and I are both stubborn in the same language.

Lisbon, day 23. I bought bread every morning from the same bakery and the owner now recognizes me and adds an extra roll without being asked. I drew him too. The city is full of people who are easy to draw because they have been shaped by wind and salt. I think about Vó Lúcia here more than at home, which is strange. Maybe because she never came to Portugal but she talked about it like she had.

PT: Hoje choveu tanto que o ponto de ônibus parecia um aquário. Desenhei um peixe dentro do ponto, só para mim. Amanhã provavelmente vou ter que explicar por que desenhei um peixe num ponto de ônibus. Ou não explico. Também é opção.
Drew a comic about a lemon tree that travels to Portugal in a suitcase. It's silly and I love it. Limonada is in the third panel, looking suspiciously taller than real life.
Back home and the lemon tree has two new leaves. The apartment smells like cold coffee and wet laundry. I watered Limonada first, before unpacking. Priorities, apparently.

Thaís asked how Lisbon was. I said 'I could live there'. She said 'you could live anywhere, Marina, you work remote'. This sentence is sitting in my chest like a stone. I know she meant it kindly. I also know it's true, and true things are the heaviest ones.

Thaís said my drawings are 'the reason clients remember us'. I said thanks and then panicked internally for twenty minutes because if I'm good at this, then I have fewer excuses to stay safe. Growth is annoying.
Thaís said the sunglasses sun is 'brand identity now'. I stared at the message for a while. Six years ago I was hiding a sketchbook under a mattress. Time is strange and kind.

In Lisbon I met a man who painted tiles for forty years and his hands were covered in blue. I drew his hands. He looked at the drawing and said 'you got the calluses right'. I wanted to cry. I did not. I bought a tile from him and put it in my bag. It is heavy and fragile and I do not know why I bought it. I think I know why.
Autumn in Curitiba means the bus is always late and everyone has a cough. I sat next to a man reading a book upside down. I didn't correct him. Some days are better left upside down.

A Sunday with no plans. I drew the whole afternoon: Curitiba rooftops, the view from my window, Limonada in three angles. The third angle is the best, she looks like she's about to say something. I think she's planning lemons. I'll wait.
Sunday call with Mom. She asked if Lisbon is forever. I said I don't know. She said Vó used to call me 'menina do mar'. I'm writing it here because I didn't know that and I need proof.
Back in Curitiba. The apartment felt smaller and quieter. Limonada had grown one new leaf while I was gone, which feels like revenge for leaving her.
Back in Curitiba and the bus was late, which felt like a welcome home. I drew a small parrot in the corner of my notebook and did not apologize to anyone for it.

Bia and I spent an hour on video call comparing windows. Hers faces the sea, mine faces Limonada. We agreed that both count as blue, technically. I believe this more than I believe most things. Friendship is a window comparison, if you think about it, which I do.

Bia, Lisbon has the same quality of light as your window in Floripa and I am taking that as a sign. I sat by the Tejo and drew the cranes in the port and thought about how your spare room is still the room I want most. I am here now but I keep checking if the sea is the same ocean. It is. It is the same ocean. I miss you and Limonada and the specific sound of your balcony door.
I dreamed of the sea again and this time I was floating, not swimming, just floating. It felt like the pool, but bigger and warmer. Woke up with my shoulders relaxed, which is rare and worth noting.
Dona Cida brought me a swimming cap with little lemons on it. I wore it immediately and swallowed less water, which may be unrelated but I'm choosing to believe in the lemons.

Swam 30 meters today. Not gracefully, not pretty, but 30. Dona Cida said 'you're not swimming, you're arguing with the water and losing less'. I'm choosing to take it as progress. The water and I have a complicated relationship, but we are talking again.
Halloween here is not Halloween, but a bakery sold pumpkin cake and I took it as a sign. Ate it on the balcony with Limonada. We looked at each other like two old women who had earned the afternoon.

Halloween isn't a thing here but the kids in the building knocked anyway. I gave them brigadeiro and they looked disappointed. Drew a small ghost for them on a sticky note. The ghost has a parrot on its shoulder. They said 'who is that'. I said 'nobody'. I lied.
Bia, your spare room still faces the sea and I'm jealous from another continent. Also, please water Limonada if Mom forgets. She forgets. She says she doesn't. She forgets.
Domingo de chuva. Desenhei o Limonada e depois desenhei o mar, tentando juntar os dois na mesma página. A planta ficou pequena e o mar ficou imenso, o que é justo.
Worked all Sunday on a solar diagram and then drew Dona Cida from memory. She would not be impressed, but she would say something kind and then splash me. I miss 7am swimming.
Mom asked if I'm 'going to Lisbon forever'. I said I don't know. She said Vó said I was menina do mar, not menina de Curitiba. I didn't know that. I'm sitting with it.

Finados. I went to the cemetery with Mom. We didn't say much. I drew the flowers on Vó's grave while Mom sat on a bench. She said 'you got the color of the lilies wrong'. Then she said 'but it's pretty'. I'm keeping both.
Day of the Dead, not Mexican, but I thought about Vó Lúcia anyway. I drew her hands holding mine from the 2020 memory. They're still cold in the drawing. I don't know how to warm them up on paper.

The investor deck with the sun is going out. I checked the file seventeen times. Thaís said 'stop refreshing, you're making the cursor nervous'. I refreshed once more after that. The cursor is fine. I am not, but in a good way.

Tio, I fixed the bridge in 'Asa Branca' finally, with a YouTube video and a lot of swearing. I still can't play it in front of people. Next Festa Junina I'll try. Don't clap before the end; it makes me forget the third verse.

Back in Curitiba. The apartment is cold and the windowsill has dust on it. Limonada survived three weeks without me, which is more than I expected. She looks the same. I look different, I think, but nobody says so. I made coffee and drew the cup and it looked better than the Lisbon coffee cups. Maybe that is what being home feels like: the same objects, drawn better.
Money check: MAR fund at R$ 1.900. Lisbon took a bite, but not the whole apple. I named the withdrawal 'postcard' and felt fancy about it.
Rain in Lisbon, real rain, not Curitiba's dramatic fifteen-minute tantrum. I walked with no umbrella because it smelled like Vó's farm after a storm. I don't know how. It just did.
Mom, I cooked bolo de fubá again and this time it was right. Not perfect, but right. You said 'melhorou' and I almost cried into the pan. I think that was your compliment.

Started page 13 of Vó's book. Drew her hands first, because that's what Mom said I got right. Her fingers are hard to draw because they were small and strong and full of opinions. I keep erasing and starting over. She would have said 'deixa assim, menina'. I'm leaving it.
Dreamed of Vó Lúcia's hands. Not her face, just her hands holding mine, cold and strong. I woke up and drew them before coffee. They came out right, which made me cry a little.
Tio Beto, I played Asa Branca at the family lunch today and only messed up the bridge once. You clapped before the end. I pretended not to notice, but I noticed.
Drew Seu Ivo e o Papagaio again, from memory, for the first time in years. Juca looked wrong without a bus behind him. I added one anyway. Some things belong to the background.
Tio Beto, se você está lendo isso, eu toquei 'Asa Branca' inteira em junho e você disse que parecia uma música. Eu ainda estou ofendida. Também estou tocando toda semana agora, e cada vez melhor.
Sunday drawing instead of calling Vó, which is still strange. I drew her laugh falling like stairs and then took a walk because every page is a conversation.
PT: Chamei a Dona Cida de 'professora' por engano hoje. Ela disse 'eu sou engenheira como você, só que da água'. Aí ela me venceu por 50 metros de novo. Justo.

Mom, I told you Lisbon was not forever and you said 'your grandmother always said you were menina do mar, not menina de Curitiba'. I did not know she said that to you. I have been saying it about myself for years like it was mine. It was always hers. I am drawing her again tonight, not from memory, from the sentence. It looks like her. I think it does.

Portuguese: choveu a tarde inteira e eu desenhei o ponto de ônibus do Interbairros de memória, com o velho do papagaio. Não sei se ele ainda está vivo, não sei se Juca ainda fala 'bom dia, motorista'. Mas no meu caderno eles existem, e isso é o suficiente. Às vezes a memória é o único lugar onde as pessoas não morrem.

A guy at the coworking saw my sketchbook and asked if I take commissions. I said maybe. He wants a portrait of his dog. I said yes before I could think. Dog portraits are a slippery slope. Vó would have loved this. She'd have asked for Coronel.
Money check: three weeks of Lisbon and I've spent too much on pastries and not enough on courage. The 'MAR' fund is still there. I haven't touched it. I'm proud of both things, in different ways.
Tio Beto sent a video of himself playing 'Asa Branca' and I watched it three times. My fingers are still learning the second verse, but I am stubborn in the best way.
Sunday call to no one. I still pick up the phone at 9am and then put it down. Today I called Mom instead and she talked for an hour. I think that's the new Sunday.
Called Bia and told her about Lisbon and Curitiba and the sea. She listened, then said, 'you can visit my window anytime.' That sentence is the safest place I know.

The apartment is too quiet after Lisbon. I turned on the radio and drew the radio. It looks like a small angry animal. I am not good at drawing radios. Limonada is fine. The coffee is fine. Everything is fine and I am restless in a way that feels like the beginning of something, not the end.

Bia, I drew your window from Floripa from memory tonight. The sea part is wrong, I know, but the curtains are right. You hung them crooked. I miss them. Send me a photo of the sunset this week, I want to draw it before I forget the exact pink.
PT: Domingo de chuva, sem chamada de Vó, mas com café e caderno. Desenhei a mão dela com a aliança torta. Tentei lembrar se a aliança era de ouro ou de bronze. Não lembrei. Desenhei bronze mesmo.
Thaís asked if I want to stay in Portugal longer. I said maybe. She said 'send me a drawing of the decision'. I sent a drawing of a suitcase with a lemon on it. She understood too well.
First cold swim of the season indoors. Dona Cida said I complain less now. I told her I'm just saving energy for the complaining I'll do later. She splashed me anyway.

Mom asked if Lisbon would be 'forever'. I said I don't know, which is the most honest thing I've said in months. She said Vó called me 'menina do mar', not 'menina de Curitiba'. I didn't know she said that to Mom too. I stood in the kitchen holding the phone and pretending I wasn't crying, which is a talent I've perfected since 2020.

It rained all day and I did not leave the apartment. This is not depression, this is Curitiba in November. I drew the rain on the window and then I drew the window and then I drew my own reflection in the window. That is three drawings in one day, which is more than I have done in months. The drawings are not good. The act of making them is the point. I am learning this slowly.

First December without the factory for the first time in years. I'm less tired, more uncertain, and somehow both of those feel like progress. I drew a small reindeer on the invoice by mistake and left it.
December and the lemon tree has tiny white flowers again. No lemons, but flowers are a promise with good manners. I took a photo for Bia and she replied with seventeen heart emojis.

Thaís asked where I want to be in a year and I said 'somewhere by the sea'. She did not flinch. She said 'we can work with that'. I do not know if she meant remote work or something larger. I am choosing to believe she meant something larger because I need that today. The 'MAR' fund has R$ 4.200 now. That is not a move. That is a start.
Advent calendar chocolate, day two. Limonada looks the same, which is the point of a tree, I think. I drew the first page of the book and it is ugly and alive and I am keeping it.
Limonada has seven new leaves and zero lemons. Bia calls her 'a planta mais bonita que não produz nada'. I defend her honor. She's trying. I respect that in a plant and in myself.

The courage fund is still named 'MAR' and I stare at it like it's a door. Half my income is still from solar diagrams, half from drawings that pay less and matter more. Thaís said I can work four days a week starting January. I said yes before she finished the sentence. The fifth day is for Vó.

Mom asked if Lisbon would be 'forever'. I said I do not know. She said 'your grandmother always said you were menina do mar, not menina de Curitiba'. I did not know she said that to you. I have been claiming that phrase for years like it was mine. It was always hers. It is mine now too. I think that is allowed.

First December at the startup. Thaís brought a small pine tree for the office and decorated it with solar-panel ornaments she made. I drew a sun with a scarf on top of the tree. It's now the official star. I'm putting this on my CV under 'achievements'.
Walked by the Tejo at night and thought: this isn't Curitiba, but it isn't the sea either. It's a very polite river pretending. I forgave it.
Mom asked if Lisbon would be 'forever'. I said I don't know. She said Vó Lúcia always called me menina do mar, not menina de Curitiba. I didn't know she said that to Mom too.

Bia, Mom asked if Lisbon would be 'forever' on the phone today. I said I don't know. She said Vó always called me menina do mar, not menina de Curitiba. I didn't know Vó said that to her too. I'm still thinking about it.

Mom asked about Lisbon again, this time while folding laundry. She didn't look at me when she asked. I said I don't know yet and folded a towel wrong on purpose so we'd both have something to do with our hands.
Advent calendar chocolate, day nine. Limonada has a tiny green thing in her branches. Could be a lemon, could be my imagination. I am not jinxing it.
Mom asked if Lisbon would be 'forever'. I said I don't know. She said 'your grandmother always said you were menina do mar, not menina de Curitiba'. I didn't know Vó said that to her too.

PT: Fiz compras de Natal sozinha no supermercado e fiquei olhando as jabuticabas por dez minutos. Não comprei. Mas pensei na Vó, como sempre. A caixa de som do mercado tocava 'Asa Branca'. Ignorei como pude.
I drew Vó Lúcia from the photo where she's holding the hat at graduation. Her hands look bigger than I remembered. Maybe hands grow in memory. I hope so.

Thaís said I could take ten days off at the end of the year and I said yes before she finished the sentence. I am going to Bia's in Floripa. I will sleep in the room facing the sea. I will draw the window. I will not swim because it is December and I am still working up to that. But I will stand at the edge. I will put my feet in. That is the 2014 promise, kept in parts.

Christmas shopping. Bought Mom a new printer, she'll pretend to hate it. Bought Tio Beto strings for the violão. Bought Limonada a bigger pot for January, her birthday, if plants have birthdays. I say they do. Drew a small card for Bia: a window with the sea behind it, and 'wait for me' under it.
Last Sunday in Lisbon this trip. I drew the river from the same chair all three weeks and now the chair knows my name. Or at least my coffee order.
Sunday drawing session. Fourteen pages of Vó's stories now. I didn't show Mom this time; I'm not ready for 'you got her hands right' again, because I might cry in front of her.
Mom asked if Lisbon would be forever. I said I do not know. She said Vó always called me 'menina do mar, not menina de Curitiba.' I did not know Vó said that to her too.

New Year approaching and I don't know if I'm celebrating in Curitiba or running to the sea. Bia invited me to Floripa. Mom said 'go, I'll make the bolo here'. I'm making lists: what to pack, what to draw, what to let go of. The list of things to let go of is longer, which is probably good.
Money check: the 'MAR' fund is intact and I bought Mom a printer cartridge without being asked. Small, ordinary generosity is the kind I want to be known for.

Christmas Eve tomorrow. Mom is making bolo de fubá and I'm pretending not to watch the oven. Tio Beto already tuned the violão. I wrapped a small gift for Limonada, which is absurd, and I'm not sorry.

PT: Natal com Mom e Tio Beto. O bolo de fubá não ficou seco dessa vez; ninguém comentou, o que eu considero vitória. Tio Beto tocou 'Asa Branca' sem ninguém pedir. Eu cantei baixinho, quase inaudível. Ele fingiu não ouvir. Foi perfeito.

Christmas Eve at Mom's. The bolo de fubá was better this year, still not Vó's but better. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' without being asked and I sang the first verse under my breath. Mom heard. She did not say anything. She put her hand on my shoulder for three seconds and then went back to the kitchen. That was enough. That was the whole evening.

Christmas Eve at Mom's. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' without being asked, and this time I sang the first verse. Mom cried. Tio Beto pretended not to see. I drew the table after everyone left: five plates, one chair empty where Vó would sit. The empty chair is the hardest thing I drew this year.

Christmas. Mom made bolo de fubá and it was good this time, and nobody mentioned the dry years. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' without being asked. I sang half and cried at the chorus, which is progress.

Christmas Eve. Mom made bolo de fubá and this time it was right. Nobody said anything for a whole minute. Then Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' without being asked and I sang the first verse. Only the first.
Boxing Day with leftovers and rain. I ate rice with bolo de fubá at 11am and called it research. Drew the plate before washing it. The fork was the most interesting part.
Christmas leftovers and a quiet balcony. I finished one page of the book and it is still ugly and alive. That is enough for today.

Last capsule of 2023. I'm sitting with Limonada, the laptop, and the parrot postcard taped above my desk. The sea is still a window I don't have yet, but I have a fund named after it, a friend who saved me the room, a grandmother's sentence, and 13 pages of a book. That's not nothing. I'm learning that not-nothing is a lot.
End of the year. Limonada is still leafy, my hands still smell like ink, and the sea is still out there. Not answers, just facts. I'm learning to let facts be enough.

Last drawing of the year. I drew my hands holding a lemon that does not exist yet, from Limonada, from the tree that has never given a lemon. The drawing is optimistic and slightly absurd. I am keeping it. I am keeping all of them. The notebook is full and I am buying another one tomorrow. The new one will start with 'menina do mar' on page one and this time I mean it.

Year-end check. I swam, I drew, I worked from another country, and I played a song all the way through. 18-year-old me would think I became a different person. I'm still the same, just less afraid of the water.
Last day of 2023 with my feet on the floor, not in the water. I'm okay with that. New Year can wait one more minute while I finish this drawing of the lemon flowers.

New Year's Eve at home, alone, which is fine. Limonada has a new leaf and the sky over Curitiba did its usual gray. I drew the fireworks from memory, not the real ones, the ones from Matinhos 2014 when Vó fell asleep at 11:40 and swore she saw them. I'm 27. I wanted to be further by now. But I'm drawing, and I'm here, and the courage fund exists. Tomorrow the sea, maybe. Or just the window. Either way I'll draw it.

January in Curitiba doing that thing where the morning is warm and by 4pm you need a jacket. The bus was late again. I drew the lady with the umbrella on the back of my grocery list. Limonada has new leaves but still no lemons, which I am choosing not to take personally.

Curitiba is doing that thing where it rains for five minutes and then the sun comes out like nothing happened. I drew the puddles on Rua XV during lunch and got water on my sketchbook. Still counts as drawing. Still counts as lunch.
Sunday drawing at the kitchen table. The lemon tree has exactly 14 leaves today and Limonada is already asking for water, somehow. Drew a tiny boat that looked like a shoe. Keeping it anyway.

Monday, 6:40 bus, Curitiba still dark. The old man at the stop is not Seu Ivo but he also says good morning to the driver, which feels like a small inheritance. I drew him in the margin of my solar diagrams. Thaís will think it's a wiring error. Fair.

First week of January in Curitiba and the bus still smells like wet wool. Drew a man sleeping with his mouth open, very wrong to do. The driver took a corner too fast and my sketchbook slid under the seat. A teenager handed it back without looking at it. Small mercy.

First Monday of the year, rain, bus late, I drew the driver holding his coffee with two hands like a relic. Worked for 9 hours and then I was too tired to draw my own thing. Tomorrow, I said. Tomorrow, probably.
First Monday of the year and the bus was late enough to make me miss my coffee. I drew the man sleeping on my shoulder instead of being annoyed about it. Small mercy: he didn't snore.
