Monday, remote work, rain all day. Thaís asked for a diagram with 'less jargon' and I sent her a sun wearing sunglasses again. She replied with a laughing emoji and then used it. I think that means I'm on the right track. It's the small things. Drew Limonada from memory while waiting for a file to upload; she looked taller than she is.
Thaís asked for a new diagram style today and I drew a tiny sun with sunglasses in the corner. She didn't ask me to remove it. I'm taking that as permission to be ridiculous at work.
January bus to work in Curitiba, rain so heavy the windows looked like aquariums. I drew the condensed drip patterns on my sleeve. Thaís asked if it was a solar panel diagram; I said yes, from space.

Chuva em Curitiba e o ônibus atrasou. Sentei no fundo e desenhei o homem com a sombrinha verde, igual aos velhos cadernos. Não sei se ele era o mesmo do parrot man, mas eu quis que fosse. Às vezes desenhar é só querer de volta o que foi.

Curitiba winter morning, coffee too hot, fingers numb. I wrote 'menina do mar' on the foggy window of the solar startup office and Thaís said it looked like a motivational poster. Maybe it is. I need motivation that isn't just spite.
Worked until 9pm on a diagram and then drew for 20 minutes just to remember who I am. The drawing was ugly and honest, which is more than I can say for some of my technical work.

I found a postcard in a drawer from Lisbon, the man with the parrot. It made me smile and then feel strangely homesick for a place I don't live in anymore. Curitiba is still the city of the 7am bus in my head.
Money check: R$ 410 left, it's the 14th, and I already bought a cafajeste pastel. Thaís approved a diagram with the sun with sunglasses again. Small victories.
Drew Limonada from above, on the kitchen table, with a cup of coffee next to her. The coffee got cold while I worked. Worth it. The leaves look like little hands.
Portuguese practice: Hoje o céu em Curitiba estava tão cinza que parecia desenho a grafite. Nem desenho bem assim. Fiz uma caneca de chá e trabalhei de pijama até as três.
It's January and the sea sounds like applause at night. I keep the window open a crack and the salt gets on the drawings. I think Vó Lúcia would have liked this window.
Bia, I tried your mother's bolo de fubá recipe again. Too dry again. I think the secret is that she underbakes it and lies about the time. I miss Vó's version every time I open the oven.

It rained all afternoon and Limonada got a new leaf, which is not connected to the rain but I'm choosing to believe it is. Money check: R$ 4.200 in the account, R$ 900 earmarked for nothing yet. I'm calling it 'maybe money'.
Rua XV today, just passing by. The república still has the same blue door. I wanted to knock but I didn't want to be the weird woman talking about a lemon tree from 2016. Progress.

Rain in Curitiba, the kind that turns the street into a river. Bus was late, I missed my stop by two and had to walk back under an umbrella that gave up after three minutes. My shoes are drying on the radiator and I am eating pão de queijo for dinner.

I made bolo de fubá using Vó's recipe and it turned out edible. Not right, but edible. Mom said 'it's better than mine', which is both true and suspicious. I think she's being kind. Keeping the recipe card anyway.
Thaís asked me to make the inverter diagram 'less aggressive'. I toned down the arrows. Then I gave the sun one eyebrow by accident and now the whole team calls it 'Marina's sun'. I'm not fixing it.

Money check: R$ 1.200 left, rent paid, the 'MAR' fund still has enough for two months. I bought a pastel de feira at the bus stop and ate it too fast, like 2015. Some things don't change. I'm not as broke as I was at 18, just as greedy for warm food on a cold day.
Sunday coffee with Mom. She tried to show me a TikTok recipe and accidentally liked a post from 2018. We both pretended it didn't happen.
Bia, I miss your balcony before I even have it. Today I stood at my kitchen window and saw a parking lot. You win. Save me the room anyway.
Limonada lost three leaves in the cold and I moved her closer to the heater. She looks offended. I told her it's temporary. She doesn't believe me either.

Slept with the window open and dreamed of the sea, but this time I was already in it. No panic, no feet stuck. Just water and a small lemon floating nearby, which is probably Limonada asserting herself in my subconscious.
Portuguese: Hoje choveu em Curitiba e eu fiquei em casa desenhando o motor do projeto solar. Thaís disse que 'ficou elegante'. Elegante é a palavra menos provável para um motor. Aceitei com orgulho.
Choveu o dia inteiro em Curitiba e o ônibus embaçou por dentro. Desenhei um dragão na janela com o dedo e um adolescente tirou foto sem dizer nada. Foi a única conversa do dia. Mesmo assim, valeu.
Sunday at the pool. I did 20 meters without stopping and then pretended it was normal. Dona Cida winked. My legs felt like two opinions disagreeing.

Cooked Mom's bolo de fubá in the new kitchen and it came out too dry, like Christmas 2020. I ate two slices anyway and texted her the photo. She replied 'needs more milk' and nothing else. That's love, I think. Also, I need more milk.
Mom, if you're reading this I probably owe you another apology about the printer. You still use it for my comics, don't you? I know because Bia's mom tells me everything.
Terminou janeiro e eu jurei que não ia contar dinheiro todos os meses. Ainda contei. O app ainda chama o fundo de 'MAR', o que me fez sorrir na fila do mercado.
Thaís asked for a diagram of the solar panel mount and I gave her a tiny sun with sunglasses again. She didn't use it but she laughed. That's enough.
Swimming lesson #? I stopped counting. Dona Cida says my kick is still 'elegant but useless', which is the nicest insult I've received. I ate a coxinha on the way home and felt like a champion.
Mom, se você estiver lendo isso, não se preocupe: o trabalho está bem. Comi verdura ontem, tirei foto pra provar, mas a foto ficou feia. A Limonada também está bem. Beijos.
Limonada's branches touched the ceiling of my apartment bedroom. I tied the top one with kitchen string so she wouldn't scrape the paint. She looked offended.

Bia, I know you're in Floripa and I'm still in Curitiba, but I bought tickets for March. Save me the room again, the one with the blue window. I promise I won't rearrange your kitchen. I will rearrange your kitchen.

Sunday money check: the 'MAR' fund still exists, still small, still named dramatically for a savings account. R$ 1.200 this month after rent. I bought paper and ignored the inner voice that calls it unnecessary. The voice sounds suspiciously like 2014 me.
Limonada got a new leaf today. One. Just one, right at the top, like she's raising her hand in class. She has never given a lemon but I'm proud of her anyway.
Bus to the market, woman with a basket of jabuticaba. I didn't ask if they were from Irati. I wanted the version in my head to stay clean. Some facts are better as drawings.

Limonada has buds. No, I'm not sure they're buds. They might be just leaf tips being dramatic. Bia says I stare at that tree the way other people stare at their phones. She's right. I'm okay with that.

Mom, I know you think I moved to Floripa because of the sea. That's true, but also because you once said Vó called me 'menina do mar'. I didn't know she said it to you too. Thank you for telling me in December. I'm still carrying it.

Tio Beto mandou áudio dizendo que o violão está com uma corda quebrada e que eu deveria ter aprendido a trocar cordas também. Ele tem razão. Vou aprender antes da próxima festa junina, ou pelo menos antes de comprar outro pastel para ele.

Febre em pleno verão, fiquei em casa desenhando da cama. Um desenho da Vó com as mãos na cintura, do jeito que ela fazia quando estava certa de alguma coisa. Ficou bom. Acho que ela estaria certa de mim também.

Found my old Interbairros notebook in a box. Seu Ivo e o Papagaio, Juca, all of it. I didn't post anything, just sat on the floor reading it. The bus still doesn't have a parrot man, but the drawings remember.
Called Tio Beto and he played three chords of 'Asa Branca' before the call dropped. He called back to say he meant it. He didn't mean it. We laughed.
Domingo de sol em Curitiba, o que é milagre. Fui no Parque Barigui caminhar e desenhei os patos. Tio Beto mandou áudio tocando 'Asa Branca' fora do ritmo. Respondi com um coração e ele mandou três.
Money check: savings still alive, no drama. I bought a proper sketchbook instead of another technical notebook and felt like I was stealing something.
Valentine's Day and I spent it drawing Limonada for the book. No drama. Just lemons and branches. Dona Cida texted me 'happy couples day' and I said happy independence day. She liked that.
Made bolo de fubá from Vó's recipe today. Too dry again, but I ate two slices standing at the counter and called it data collection. I miss her hands more than the recipe.

Ran into someone from university at the supermarket. He asked if I still draw and I said 'professionally, sometimes'. He looked surprised. I wanted to say 'you should have seen my calculus grades', but I just bought my milk and left. Growth.

Valentine's Day and I am alone with a bag of pipoca and a drawing of a motor. This is not sad, this is research. Also the motor drawing got approved by Thaís with only one 'less technical' comment, so we are growing.

Mom, I know you read these when they arrive. The lemon tree has buds again and I put a little stake beside it so it won't lean into the radiator. You said I overwater everything. You're right. I'm learning to wait.
Tio Beto, se você estiver lendo isso eu ainda não aprendi a tocar a terceira parte de 'Asa Branca' direito, mas toco até o fim mesmo errando. Você disse one more year e eu ainda conto.

Swimming at 7am, different pool now, closer to work. Dona Cida isn't there, but I still hear her voice when I panic: 'float is trust, not technique'. I floated for a minute today. A full minute. It felt like a secret.
Money check: R$ 1.900 in the MAR fund and one unexpected electricity bill. Made lunch from what was left in the fridge: rice, egg, a sad tomato. It was good. I'm counting it as a win.
Dona Cida sent a postcard from Ubatuba: 'a engenheira, o mar está te esperando.' I put it on the fridge next to the Lisbon parrot card.
Tio Beto's birthday audio: he said he was proud I moved, then immediately asked if I brought the violão. I did not. I feel like a cousin who failed a tradition. One more year, as usual.

Cooked for Bia on video call and burned the garlic. She gave instructions calmly, like a flight attendant. The pasta was edible. We counted it as a victory. She asked if I'm drawing. I lied and said yes. Then I actually drew the burned garlic. It looked like a tiny planet.

Desenhei o limoeiro hoje porque estava com saudade da janela antiga, mesmo estando ainda aqui. A Limonada tem cinco folhas novas e não me deu nem um limão, mas tem cara de quem está tramando. Prometo: quando você ler isso, conta se ela finalmente deu.
Swimming at 7am. Dona Cida said my kick is still angry. I told her my kick has always been angry. She said good, keep it, just aim it forward.

Swimming class this morning. Dona Cida asked why I was smiling and I said 'no reason', which was a lie, since I'd just realized I was swimming for fun and not for proving something. She splashed me anyway.
Wrote in my sketchbook: 'maybe the sea dream is not about swimming.' Then crossed it out. Then wrote it again. Drawing is easier than this kind of honesty.
Money check: MAR fund is at R$ 4.200. It's not the sea, but it's a boat. I keep checking it like other people check horoscopes.
Tio Beto, I played Asa Branca on your violão again last Sunday without being asked. You pretended not to care. I know you were listening from the kitchen.

Thaís asked me to make a diagram less serious. I drew a solar panel wearing sunglasses. She put it in the deck without telling me. I found out when a client asked if the sunglasses were sold separately.

Portuguese capsule test: Hoje o céu de Curitiba estava daquele cinza que parece tinta aguada e eu gostei. Desenhei três nuvens na margem do relatório. A Limonada recebeu sol na janela e fez cara de quem não aprova nada. Alguns dias são assim e tudo bem.

Decision: Florianópolis, not Lisbon. Closer to Mom, Bia already there, and the sea is the same ocean, technically. Limonada comes with me in the back seat of the car, which I can drive, which is still a miracle.
Packed Limonada into the car with a towel around the pot and talked to her for the whole trip: 'hold on, almost there, you're dramatic, same as me'. She lost two leaves and gained a story.

International Women's Day and I spent it drawing a diagram of a solar panel while eating instant noodles. Very glamorous. But Thaís sent a voice note saying my work makes the company look human, and I kept it. It's my new 'tombstone quote', after Cláudio's.

International Women's Day and I spent it drawing technical diagrams for a man who called me 'a engenheira' without irony. Progress is strange. I drew a tiny sun with sunglasses on his invoice. Nobody noticed.

A Thaís pediu 'algo menos técnico' em um diagrama e eu desenhei um sol de óculos escuros. Agora está no deck dos investidores e eu sou oficialmente a pessoa do sol na empresa de energia solar. Acho que minha carreira está indo bem.

Tenth anniversary of starting engineering and I am sitting in a sunny kitchen making diagrams with a sun wearing sunglasses. Younger me would be confused. Younger me would also be relieved. I think that counts.
Mom, I planted lemon seeds today in a yogurt cup, because apparently I'm 18 again. If even one sprouts I'm keeping it forever. Wait, I already said that once. I'm saying it again.

I didn't post about the move decision anywhere. It feels too big and too ordinary at the same time. Floripa in June. Lisbon later maybe. Mom said I could keep her printer if I promised to draw more. I promised.
Portuguese practice: decidi que vou escrever uma cápsula por semana, mesmo que seja só uma frase. Hoje: a chuva está lavando Curitiba e eu estou lavando louça. Glamouroso.
Went to look at an apartment near Bia. The window faces a wall. Came home grumpy and drank an entire chimarrão by myself. The lemon tree is not impressed by my standards.
Feijão, arroz, ovo frito, limão no arroz porque sim. Comi sozinha na mesa da cozinha olhando para Limonada na janela. Ela continua sem dar limão, mas está brilhante. A gente se parece.
Packed three boxes labeled 'drawings' and realized two of them are actually kitchen things. I'm not reorganizing. Future me can deal with the plates in the sketchbook box.

Thaís loved the tiny sun with sunglasses so much she asked for a second diagram with a sun in a hard hat. I have accidentally become the solar sun person at the solar company. Mom would say this is a very Marina career path.

Bia called to say the spare room window still faces the sea. I haven't moved yet and she's already saving it for me. I told her not to, she said 'too late'. I cried in the bathroom for two minutes and then went back to drawing arrows for the solar startup.

Primeira natação do ano em piscina aquecida. Dona Cida não estava lá, então não havia ninguém para me xingar carinhosamente. Boiei três minutos e pensei em Vó Lúcia dizendo 'menina do mar'. Saí da piscina com vontade de ligar para alguém que não existe mais.

Mom, you asked if the remote job is 'real work'. Today I spent six hours drawing solar diagrams and one hour explaining to a client why the sun with sunglasses is staying in the deck. Thaís agrees with me. Tell Tio Beto I still haven't learned all of 'Asa Branca' on the violão, but I'm closer.
Mom, I know you think the solar startup is a phase. But Thaís let me draw a diagram with a little sunglasses sun and it is now in the investor deck. I am 28 and professionally silly. Love you.
Rain again. Bia and I stayed inside and played cards for three hours. She cheated with the face of an angel. I let her win once because the sea was noisy and I was happy.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was swimming and Limonada was floating next to me, which makes no botanical sense. Woke up smiling.
Bia, your voice note about the Floripa wind made me miss the sea so much I drew it from memory. It looked like a bus route map. Progress.
At the solar startup stand-up I said 'drawings' and everyone looked at me like I'd said 'magic'. Thaís smiled. I'm learning that being the art person is not an accident.
Portuguese: Hoje desenhei a Limonada no caderno e ela ainda não deu limão. Oito anos. Bia disse que é 'decorativa'. Eu disse que é 'resistente'. São palavras diferentes para o mesmo orgulho.
Thaís asked for a diagram of a solar inverter and I gave her one plus a tiny bird on the wire. She didn't say anything, but she used it. I think that's the compliment.
Rain all week. Worked from bed with Limonada by my feet. Made a small comic about a woman trying to parallel park in the rain. It is me. I did not parallel park.
Bia, your voice note saying 'come before the lemon flowers' made me laugh and then cry in the supermarket. I am working on it. Please don't move the spare room bed.
Tio Beto, I played Asa Branca twice today, just for practice. The second time was better. I'm not telling you when it happens, I'm just telling you it's coming.

Sonhei com o mar de novo, mas desta vez eu estava desenhando na areia, não nadando. A onda apagava tudo e eu começava de novo. Acordada, pensei que isso talvez seja o trabalho todo: desenhar, perder, desenhar de novo. Tô bem com isso.
Thaís said my diagrams are 'the prettiest technical documents in the company'. I am choosing to believe this is a compliment and not pity.

I moved a succulent to the windowsill and accidentally killed it in eight days. Limonada looked at me like she knew. She is eight years old and still lemonless. We are both stubborn, but at least I can buy groceries.

Bus 7am, Interbairros II, still. Different driver, same route. A woman offered me half her bisnaguinha and I accepted because I was raised right. Drew them both in my notebook and felt, for a second, like 2014.

It rained all week and the bus fogged up from the inside. I drew the condensation dragon on the window with my finger and a teenager took a photo of it. We didn't say anything. That's the whole interaction. It made my day anyway.
Mom called to ask if I'd 'given up on the drawings yet' again. This time I laughed and said yes. She laughed too. We are both liars and we know it.

First full week in Floripa and I already have a regular at the padaria who calls me 'menina do mar' without knowing Vó. I said thank you and didn't correct him. Some names fit whether you planned them or not.

Tried to draw Coronel again, this time from Vó Lúcia's story about the farm gate. His ears are too big, but she never said they weren't. I like the idea of a dog with enormous ears waiting for a girl who will eventually become my grandmother.

Bia, I'm writing this on a Tuesday because I saw a cat that looked exactly like your old one, Juju, and I miss you even though we talked Sunday. Come to Curitiba soon. I'll make pastel and you can complain about the hills.

Mãe, a impressora que a senhora disse que não precisava já imprimiu 30 tiras do Interbairros. O Seu Ivo com o papagaio virou magnet na geladeira da Bia. A senhora não vai dizer nada sobre isso e eu vou fingir que não percebi.
Portuguese: Bia said 'saudade' is untranslatable and I said 'so is the smell of Matinhos at midnight.' We were both right and slightly dramatic.
Money check: the 'MAR' fund is small but existing. I keep opening the bank app to look at the number like it's a pet. It doesn't do anything, but it sits there. That's enough for now.

Tio Beto ligou perguntando se eu já tinha tocado 'Asa Branca' para alguém em Curitiba. Eu disse que toco só para a Limonada no domingo. Ele riu e disse que a árvore tem bom gosto. Eu disse que ela é exigente. Boa conversa de tio e sobrinha.
Portuguese practice: Limonada fez uma folha nova today e eu celebrei como se fosse promoção. Oito anos sem dar um limão e ela me surpreende com uma folha. Amor incondicional.

I opened the 2014 capsule about swimming and cried a little, not because I'm sad but because 18-year-old me wrote 'promise me' like it was a contract. I can swim now. Not well. But the promise is kept and that matters more than style.
Rain all morning. The Interbairros bus was late and I drew the woman with the red umbrella who was furious about it. She looked like she was arguing with the sky. Fair.

Swimming lesson, different pool, same panic at first. I floated for forty seconds and then laughed so hard I swallowed water. The instructor asked if I was okay. I said 'yes, I just remembered I used to be afraid of this'. She said 'and now?' I said 'still a little'. Honest answer.
Dreamed of the sea again, but this time the water was full of bus tickets. I have no idea what that means. Going to swim tomorrow anyway.
Bus Interbairros II, 7am. There is a new driver who brakes like he is braking for a cat. Nobody said anything. I miss Seu Ivo, but buses still have characters if you look.
Dreamed about the sea again, but this time I was on a bus and the bus drove straight into the water. Nobody panicked. The driver said 'bom dia, motorista' to himself. I woke up smiling for no reason.
Found a lemon seed in my jacket pocket from the republica era. No idea how. I planted it in a yogurt cup and wrote MARINA on it anyway, in case history wants to repeat itself.

Money check: finally paid off the last credit card installment from Lisbon. The 'maybe money' has a name now: 'MAR' again, because I'm sentimental and apparently also a one-trick pony with savings folders.

Bia, I tried to float on my back in the bathtub tonight and panicked at the exact same second as always. The ceiling is very interesting when you're pretending not to drown in four inches of water. Still not giving up.
Rain all day in Curitiba. I drew the lemon tree with a tiny umbrella over it, even though it lives indoors. Limonada has new leaves, which feels like the universe paying rent late but paying.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was swimming with someone whose face I couldn't see, and when I turned around it was nobody. I woke up and wanted toast, which I think is progress.

The bus today smelled like rain and someone's thermos of coffee. I drew the woman with the red umbrella in the margin of my notebook, like 2014, except now it's a digital file that nobody will ever see. I miss paper a little. Maybe that's why I still have sketchbooks.
Mom printed one of my comics on the old printer I bought her in 2018. It still works. So does she, apparently, in her own way.
First warm day. Ate feijão tropeiro at the RU with the girls and we pretended nothing changed since 2014. The fridge still has names on every yogurt. Some things survive.
Tio Beto, encontrei o violão em cima do armário e toquei o refrão duas vezes sem errar. A Limonada não aplaudiu, mas também não caiu. Conto como sucesso.
Tentei desenhar o mar por dez minutos e não consegui. Ficou uma faixa azul e uma linha de espuma. Entendi por que 18-year-old me só desenhava ônibus: eles são mais obedientes.
Found a tiny shell in my coat pocket from Lisbon and put it on the desk. No reason. Just to remember I was brave once, which means I can be again, probably, after coffee.

Dessas noites em que o mar parece mais perto do que está. Abri a janela e o cheiro entrou antes da vista. Desenhei o contorno do prédio vizinho como se fosse uma onda. Vai virar uma página do livro, tenho certeza.
Drew Vó Lúcia's hands again from memory. I keep thinking I'm forgetting the exact curve of her knuckles, but my hand remembers better than my eyes. Strange and comforting.
Portuguese practice: Domingo de sol, liguei para Dona Cida. Ela disse que estou nadando melhor do que meu orgulho deixa aparente. Ela está certa.
Bia, I bought a tiny succulent for your balcony and then realized it might die in your care, so I'm keeping it and giving you the drawing instead. Less murder, more art.
Swimming today. Dona Cida says my freestyle improved but my breathing still sounds like a broken motor. She is kind about it in the way only someone who swims better than me can be.

Tio Beto, I played 'Asa Branca' three times this month, alone, in my apartment, and only messed up the bridge twice. If you ask me next Festa Junina, I might survive it. Do not tell Mom I practiced, she'll expect a concert.
Labor Day. Took the day off and drew nothing. Best decision I made all month.

Little drawing of Coronel on a farm gate, the way Vó described it: ears up, tail straight, looking down the road. I don't know if that's accurate. It feels accurate. I'm keeping it even if it's wrong.

Fez um dia de sol estranho em Curitiba, daqueles que parecem pedir perdão. Comi uma coxinha do posto da esquina e desenhei o céu aberto por vinte minutos. Thaís quer o diagrama amanhã. Ele vai ter um céu pequeno no canto, sem avisar.

The bus in Floripa is different: no parrot, no Seu Ivo, no romance. Just people and heat. I miss the Interbairros line in a way that feels embarrassing for a 28-year-old. Maybe I'll draw it anyway, from memory.
I am 28 and still cannot parallel park. This is not a capsule about achievement. It is a capsule about acceptance.

Mother's Day preparation: I drew Mom holding a printer, which she will either find funny or not understand. Bia says go with a lemon tree drawing instead. I drew both and will decide tomorrow, which is also how I make all important decisions.
Bia, I packed one box labeled 'DRAWINGS + LIMONADA' and then panicked because you cannot pack a lemon tree like books. She is coming in the car. I will strap her in like a child.
Tio Beto called to ask if I was still practicing the violão. I played three chords over the phone and he said 'está melhor' with the tone of a man lying kindly. I accepted the lie.
Ate pastel de feira for lunch and thought about Rafa for half a second. Half a second is still progress from 2018.
Swimming lesson at 7am. Dona Cida made me float for two whole minutes while she described her breakfast in detail. I did not sink. Progress tastes like tapioca.

Tio Beto voice note, five minutes long, about the jabuticabeira and how Vó used to pick the fruit before sunrise. I listened twice. He didn't cry. I did. I'm drawing the tree today, with a small dog under it, even though Coronel wasn't under that one. He should have been.
Portuguese: Hoje desenhei um caranguejo no caderno porque estava pensando no mar. Não sei desenhar caranguejo. Parece um sapato bravo. Vou mostrar para Bia e ela vai rir. Rir é bom também.
Mom sent a voice message asking if Floripa 'has enough engineers'. I replied with a photo of Limonada's flowers. She replied 'bonita'. One word, but I felt it.
Bia's girlfriend Júlia made coffee and then corrected my pronunciation of 'chimarrão' with terrifying gentleness. I let her. Love is sometimes a woman teaching you to say a word correctly.
Drew the lemon tree from memory and got the leaves wrong. Opened the photo and counted them, then felt silly. It has 23 leaves. I drew 17. Art is not journalism, but still.
Thaís asked for a less technical diagram and I gave her a little sun with sunglasses again. She said 'you're doing it on purpose now.' I said 'yes.'
Swimming without goggles today because I forgot them. The sea looked like a watercolor when I opened my eyes. Dona Cida would say that's not an excuse.
Bia, your window sounds incredible over the phone. I can hear the waves in the background and it makes me both happy and furious. Save me the room.

Mom asked, over the phone, if I'd 'found a nice boy in Curitiba yet'. I said I'm 27 and busy. She said Vó Lúcia found Tio Beto at 28. I said Vó Lúcia also adopted a dog at 29, and Mom laughed, so I think we're fine.

Tio Beto, I played 'Asa Branca' twice this week, once for practice and once because Limonada looked tilted, which I know is not a reason to play guitar. I think I'm just lonely for Sunday lunch. Call me if you're free, I'll bring pastel.
Bia sent a photo of her window and I put it as my wallpaper. My screen now shows the sea but my room smells like Curitiba rain.

Bia, I found your old drawing of my back at the window in Floripa. I look like someone who hadn't arrived yet. I'm still arriving. Tell Júlia the burned rice was not her fault, but I will be bringing my own rice next time.

Sonhei com o mar de novo. Desta vez eu estava nadando, mas a água era grossa, quase como gelatina, e eu não conseguia avançar. Acordei com o coração acelerado e desenhei antes de tomar café. O desenho ficou bonito e triste, que é basicamente o meu gênero.
Money check: the 'MAR' fund has enough for gas to Floripa, one dinner, and probably a parking ticket. I'm calling that a budget, not a dream.
Swimming lesson before work. Dona Cida says I glide now. I said I mostly sink with style. She didn't laugh. She should have.

Swimming practice today: 50 meters, nonstop. Dona Cida wasn't there, but I sent her a text and she replied with three exclamation marks and a fish emoji. I am collecting evidence that 18-year-old me would be insufferable about this.

A drawing of Vó Lúcia from the photo with the big hat. Her hands took me all afternoon. I kept erasing the fingers and starting again because they looked too young and I wanted them right: tired and warm.

Checked the 'MAR' fund at 11pm, which is a terrible time to check money. R$ 1.450. Not enough to move, enough to keep believing I will. I renamed it 'LIMONADA' for one minute, then renamed it back. No need to tempt fate.
Ate pastel de feira alone and watched the same man feed pigeons for fifteen minutes. Drew him in my notebook. One pigeon looked directly at me, as if filing a complaint.
Portuguese practice: desenhei o Tio Beto na cozinha, com o violão e a camisa xadrez. Ele disse que está mais bonito do que na vida real. Falei que é o que ele pensa.

Bia, I'll be there soon, I hope. Your spare room is becoming a character in my head: the room that faces the sea. I haven't even seen it this month and I already miss it. Don't paint the walls blue, I'll bring the color myself, probably on paper first.

Tio Beto, this one is for you because Sunday lunch is coming and I know you'll hand me the violão. I practiced 'Asa Branca' twice this week and messed up the same verse. One day I won't. Until then, obrigada por não desistir de mim.
I swam longer than I meant to today, not far by anyone's standards, but past the point where my brain usually says stop. Dona Cida would say I trusted the water. I say I got distracted counting fish.

Packing starts. The apartment looks like a tornado with opinions. I found the old Interbairros notebook behind the bookshelf and spent twenty minutes reading it instead of packing. Limonada is in the corner, watching me like a tiny supervisor.
Packing boxes. Limonada is in her pot on the windowsill, pretending nothing is happening. I counted every leaf again so I notice if one falls on the road. She has 24 now. Progress.

Packed one box of drawings today and cried for no reason. Then I cried because I cried for no reason. The box is labeled 'IMPORTANT (not money)'. Limonada has been staring at me from the windowsill like she knows.
Lisbon is still in my head like a song stuck on repeat. But Mom's voice on Sunday was louder. I wrote both things down and chose the one that let me sleep.
Boxes started. I keep opening things and finding drawings I forgot, like a 2015 sketch of Vó's kitchen. The lemon tree is the last thing I'll pack and I'm already nervous about the back seat plan.

Last week in Curitiba before the move. I found the bus comics folder on my old laptop and almost opened it. Decided not to. Not because it hurts, but because I'm not done being the person who made them. I just want to arrive in Floripa first.
Limonada has three new leaves. I am moving a lemon tree to the beach in a few weeks and I feel like a nervous parent on a school trip.
Limonada got too wide for the car door. Bia and I turned her sideways and said sorry for ten minutes. She arrived with one leaf in the armrest and dignity intact.

Last Friday in Curitiba. I walked past the república building on Rua XV and it looked smaller. I didn't go in. I just stood there and remembered the fridge with names on the yogurts. Mine said 'MARINA' in red marker. I wonder if it's still there. I didn't check.
The move list had 47 items and I crossed out 3 by noon. Limonada was item 1. The violão tuning fork was item 47. Everything else is negotiable.

Organized the move in three boxes: drawings, kitchen things, and 'things I'm not ready to sort'. The third box is the heaviest. It contains two sweaters, a playlist printed on paper, and a postcard of a man with a parrot.

Packed two boxes for Floripa and immediately unpacked the sketchbook to draw how stressed I looked. The irony was not lost on me. Limonada is already in the back seat mentally, like a passenger with opinions.
Last night in Curitiba. I walked past the república on Rua XV and didn't knock. The window had a light on. Someone else is living the smell of old wood now. I hope they have a plant.
Packed the first box. Limonada's pot is in the back of the car, wrapped in my old scarf. She's eight years old and has never been to the sea. Poor thing.
Mom, I'm leaving Curitiba soon and I didn't know packing books would make me this emotional. Your bolo de fubá recipe is in the same box as Vó's stories.
Limonada survived the move prep so far. I wrapped the pot in a towel and she looks like a small kidnapped tree. She has three new flowers, which I'm choosing to read as encouragement and not panic.

Bia, I am bringing Limonada in the back seat. She is taller than the car ceiling if we don't tilt her. I have a blanket for the pot and a playlist for the road. If we arrive with one leaf missing, I am not speaking to you or Júlia for a week.

Last week in Curitiba. I went to the bus stop at 7am just to stand there. No parrot. No old man. Just the hill and the exhaust smell. I drew it anyway, badly, because some places deserve a bad drawing.

A storm came through Floripa and Limonada's pot almost tipped on the balcony. I brought her inside, wrapped in my scarf, just like 2017. She has more leaves now. So do I, technically, if leaves means gray hairs.

Packed the car. Limonada on the back seat wrapped in a scarf, like 2017, except now she's taller than me. I checked the rearview mirror six times. She didn't move. She looks bored. That's probably a good sign.
Last week in Curitiba. Ate pastel at the feira where Rafa and I had our first date. Just the pastel. It was good. Some things stay good without the person.
Packed the last box and found the yogurt cup from 2016, empty now, with 'MARINA' still written on it. I kept it. Some things are too small to throw away and too important to explain.
Tio Beto, obrigada por ter tocado violão na minha casa quando eu tinha medo da mudança. Acordei hoje cantando 'Asa Branca' sem querer. Você venceu.
First morning in Bia's flat. The window is all blue and I stood there with my toothbrush in my hand for a full minute. The tea got cold. Worth it.
Portuguese practice: empacotei tudo e deixei o quarto da república vazio. A parede ficou com uma marca retangular onde ficava o desenho do mar da Vó Lúcia. Levei ele comigo.

Moved to Florianópolis. Not Lisbon, not yet. Bia's spare room really does face the sea, she saved it, like I asked in 2019. I wake up and the window is all blue. I'm 28. 18-year-old me wanted exactly this window. I opened her capsule from New Year's 2014 early by accident and the answer to both of her questions is yes.
First night in Floripa and the sea is actually visible from Bia's balcony. I stood there until my feet went cold. 18-year-old me would not believe me.

Portuguese: Primeira semana morando em Floripa e a janela é toda azul. Ainda não acredito. A Limonada está na varanda, com vento de mar, e eu tenho medo que ela goste demais e esqueça Curitiba. Eu também.

Curitiba me, meet Florianópolis me: same person, more sunscreen, less coat. Limonada survived the back seat and only lost two leaves. I cried at the bridge, not from sadness, from the fact that the water was actually blue.

Curitiba is still warm somehow and I packed my scarf anyway because I am who I am. Floripa next month. I keep opening the 2014 capsule early, which is cheating, but it makes me feel 18 again and that's worth it.
Bia made pão de queijo at 7am and the kitchen smelled like every good morning I ever had. I ate three and then apologized to no one. The sea through the window is so blue it looks fake. It isn't.

First morning waking up with the window all blue. Bia was right: it's not a view, it's a mood. I stood there for a long time and then burned the omelette. The sea wins. The eggs lost. Acceptable trade.
Bia, your spare room is even better than the 2019 photo. The window is all blue and my heart is doing something undignified.
First week in Floripa. The window really is blue. Bia left a mug of coffee on my desk with a note that said 'seu'. I slept with the window open and the sea sounded like someone breathing slowly.
Bia's neighborhood has a bakery that opens at 5:30. I haven't seen 5:30 since the bus years. The bread is warm and I forgive it for the hour.

Limonada is on the balcony now and she looks offended by the wind. Eight years old, no lemons, but flowers. Small white ones that smell like something I can't name. I drew them before breakfast. Thaís is going to ask why the diagram smells like jasmine and I'll say 'it doesn't, it's a PDF'.
Limonada survived the car ride to Floripa wrapped in a scarf, like in 2017. She looks confused by the ocean wind but she is alive and so am I.

First week in Floripa and the weather is showing off. Bia's balcony smells like salt and detergent. Limonada got flowers today, small white things that smell better than anything I own. No lemons. I am not asking for lemons anymore. Okay, I am asking a little.
Bia's balcony smells like sea and laundry detergent. Limonada is getting more sun than she's ever had and I'm suspicious. The spare room really does face the sea and 18-year-old me would scream.
I drew Vó Lúcia's hands again, this time from memory, not the photo. They came out less accurate and more real. I think that's what memory is for: forgiving the details until only the love remains.
Bia made coffee so strong it could fix asphalt. I drank it and saw through time. She calls this 'carioca strength'; I call it 'a cry for help.'
Limonada lives on Bia's balcony now, facing the sea. Eight years old. She got her first flowers. Small, white, smell incredible. No lemons yet but flowers count.
Limonada got her first flowers on the balcony. Small, white, smelling like something I can't name. No lemons yet, but flowers count. We're both settling in.
Swam at Praia Mole with Bia watching from the sand. Not far, but far enough to feel like a different person. She clapped from the towel. I pretended to be embarrassed. I was not embarrassed.
First dinner on Bia's balcony. We had grilled fish and talked about nothing. The sea did most of the talking. I drew a fish with a sunglasses face because apparently I cannot stop.
Limonada's balcony has wind and she hates it. I tied her to the railing with a scarf and felt like a person who talks to plants. Bia caught me. She did not comment. She made coffee. Good friend.

First swim in Floripa, shallow, with Bia yelling instructions from the sand. I swallowed less water than usual and considered that progress. The sea was cold and then not cold and then I forgot to care.

Bia, if you're reading this, your spare room really does face the sea and you really did save it. I stood there for twenty minutes again, like Floripa 2019. You took another photo of my back, didn't you? I'm not mad. I look good in silhouette.
Portuguese practice: acordei com a janela toda azul hoje. Fiquei olhando vinte minutos antes de ligar o computador. Bia tirou foto das minhas costas, disse 'finalmente'.

Work from the balcony now. Thaís asked why the new diagram has a tiny wave in the corner. I said it was an accident. It was not an accident. The client liked it. We are unstoppable and also mildly unprofessional.
Walked to Praia Mole before sunrise. The sand was cold and my towel got wet. I didn't swim yet. I just needed to know the sea was really there.

Bia's balcony, sunset, Limonada throwing a tiny shadow on the wall. I drew it in three minutes, which is the fastest I've ever drawn anything that mattered. Some days the hand knows before the head. I'm keeping the sketchbook open on the kitchen table now, not hidden anywhere.
Limonada's balcony now faces the sea. She leaned toward the water all afternoon like she was listening. Or she needs water. I gave her both.

Bia and I walked on the beach at dusk and she said, 'you finally live near the sea' and I said, 'yes', and then neither of us said anything for a while, which was the best conversation we've had in months.
Limonada is on Bia's balcony. She got two new leaves this week and I choose to believe it is happiness, not sunlight. Bia's cat stared at the pot for ten minutes. Nobody won.

Bia, your spare room really does face the sea. I stood there for twenty minutes and you took a photo of my back and captioned it 'finally' again, like a sequel. I'm keeping both photos. The first one is from 2019 and I look scared. This one I look tired and happy, which is better.

I swam twenty meters in the sea today and stopped because I got scared of a fish. A small fish. Dona Cida would be disappointed, but the sea is not a pool and the fish did not ask for my opinion. I'll try again Thursday.
First full week working from Bia's table. Thaís asked if the new view is distracting. I said no. The waves are not distracting, they're the point.

Money check in Floripa: rent is higher, groceries are higher, the sea is free. I'm adjusting the numbers. The 'MAR' fund is now called 'book' in my head even though there is no book yet. I have 12 pages of Vó's stories and a lot of fear about the 13th.

Money check: Floripa is more expensive than I admitted and the savings fund is blinking at me. I drew a diagram for Thaís while eating crackers, so at least the work continues. Crackers are not a meal, Marina.
First time drawing on the balcony. The wind took one page into the neighbour's yard. I knocked and a man returned it with 'nice turtle' written on the back. It was a lemon.
Limonada got her first flowers on the balcony and I cried in front of Bia's girlfriend, who kindly pretended it was allergies. Eight years for five small white flowers. Worth every stubborn year.
Bia's balcony has become my office. Limonada is next to my laptop and she looks like she approves of my productivity.

Portuguese: Hoje fui à feira e comprei limões de verdade para zombar da Limonada. Ela não tem nome mais, a árvore, mas ela venceu moralmente. Bia fez limonada com os limões e disse que era 'uma ofensa à árvore'. Rimos até doer a barriga.

Praia Mole at 7am, just walking. The sand was cold and my feet went numb, which is probably how a fish feels. I drew the lifeguard tower from memory and got the window wrong. Tomorrow I'll go back with the sketchbook.

First time making coffee in the new kitchen while Bia was still asleep and the window was all blue. I drew the light, not the sea, because the light is what makes the sea look like that. I'm learning.
Mom, I sent you a photo of the sea from the balcony. You replied with a lemon emoji. I think that's your way of saying you're proud. I'm keeping it.

Thaís asked for 'something less technical' again and I drew a little sun with sunglasses for the investor deck. Then I added a lemon in the corner, very small, because I could. She didn't mention it. Nobody did. I think that's how the best things enter a room: quietly.

Swam in the sea alone for the first time, early, before the surfers. Not far. Far enough. Nobody watched, which was the point. I came out shaking and laughing and drew the shape of my own footprints before the tide took them.
Bia and Júlia made feijoada and I ate too much and fell asleep on the couch. Woke up with Limonada's shadow on the wall moving like a slow animal. I drew her before I moved.
Made feijoada and forgot the bay leaf. Mom would be scandalized. It was still good. Bia's girlfriend Júlia ate three plates and said nothing, which I respect.

Ate pastel de feira alone at the market and thought of Rafa without pain, which felt like a weather report: clear, warm, no forecasted storms. I paid for two pastels anyway. One for the version of me who needed them in 2015.
Bia, I swam for ten minutes this morning and only panicked once. You sleeping through it was the kindest thing you've ever done.
Tio Beto, I found your violão tuning fork in my moving box. I'm keeping it on the desk. If you read this, play 'Asa Branca' for me on the phone, badly, as usual.

I tried to go to Praia Mole at sunset and took the wrong bus, ended up at a bakery with a view instead. Ate a coxinha and decided the day was still good. The sea can wait for a morning when I don't get lost.
Praia Mole early, before the surf crowd. I went in only up to my knees and then went farther than I planned, which is not the same as bravery but is close enough for a Saturday.
Drew the balcony today: Limonada, the sea, a bird on the railing. It took me ten minutes and felt like meditation. Maybe that's what work is supposed to feel like.
Dona Cida sent a postcard from Curitiba. It says 'a engenheira aprendeu a nadar?' and has a sticker of a duck. I put it on the fridge next to nothing else yet. The fridge is winning at minimalism.
Dreamed I was back in the república, four girls, one bathroom, but the sea was outside the window instead of the street. I woke up smiling, which is a new thing for a dream about the sea.

Festa Junina was in July, obviously, and I almost wrote 'I didn't try Asa Branca' out of habit. But I did play it last year, and I'm still allowed to be proud of that. This year Tio Beto sent a voice note playing it badly on purpose. I laughed so hard Bia thought something was wrong.
Swam at Praia Mole before work, just ten minutes. The water was cold enough to make me loud. Bia took a photo from the sand and I look like a small, surprised seal. I am keeping the photo.
Swam to the buoy at Praia Mole and back. A little kid cheered from the sand. I pretended not to hear and then waved when he wasn't looking.
Bia made dinner and Júlia brought wine. I drew them laughing in the margins of my notebook. They didn't notice. That's the best kind of drawing.
Found an old 'Interbairros' strip on my hard drive and posted it for old times' sake. Three people liked it. One of them was Mom, from the printer, which is not how Instagram works but I accepted it.
Portuguese practice: hoje o vento aqui é tão forte que Limonada curvou um pouco. Eu disse 'firme, amiga' e senti ridícula e sincera ao mesmo tempo.

Mom called and said the apartment in Curitiba looked 'too clean', which is her way of saying she misses me. I sent her a photo of Limonada's flowers. She said 'your grandmother would have watered it wrong'. We laughed. I think that counts as a compliment.

Worked all day, drew a little sun for the deck, ate pastel at the beach at sunset. Thaís asked if I was 'inspired by Floripa' and I said 'I'm inspired by finally being where I said I'd be'. She wrote back 'good'. One word. Enough.

Called Mom and she asked if I was eating. I said yes, which was true in the sense that coffee and biscoito count as a meal if you're 28 and optimistic. Then I made real lunch and sent her a photo. She replied 'melhor'. That's mother for 'I love you'.
Found a shell shaped like a tiny ear on Praia Mole. I put it on the desk and now every drawing sounds like the sea if I hold it close.

Limonada got her first flowers. White, tiny, smelling like something I can't name. I drew them four times and still couldn't get the petals right. Maybe lemons are next. Maybe not. I'm trying not to demand miracles from a ten-year-old plant.
Went swimming with Bia. She floats like a professional and then tells me not to compare. I compared anyway. She splashed me. We are 28.

Sonhei que estava nadando no mar e alguém dizia 'menina do mar' perto de mim, mas não era Vó Lúcia. Era eu mesma, mais velha. Acordada, desenhei a onda e escrevi 'olá' embaixo. Não sei por quê. Ficou bom.
Thaís asked for 'something less technical' on a solar diagram again. I drew a sun with sunglasses and a tiny umbrella. She said publish it. I said maybe.

Thaís asked if I'd illustrate the whole investor deck in a less technical style and I said yes before she finished the sentence. I am now drawing a sun with sunglasses and, apparently, a hard hat again. Full circle.
Limonada has small white flowers and no lemons yet. I keep checking every morning like a person waiting for an email that matters. The balcony wind is dramatic. She survives it. We are alike in that.
Money check: MAR fund now at R$ 5.100. Still a boat. Still not the sea. But the sea is outside the window now, so the boat can wait.
Money check: Floripa is more expensive, but I can see the sea from the kitchen. I'm counting that as rent payment.
A windy Sunday. Drew the sea from the balcony four times because the horizon kept changing its mind. One drawing is all waves, no sky. It might be my favorite.
Drew a comic about a bus in Florianópolis where the passenger is a lemon tree in a pot. Nobody recognized the reference except me and that was enough. Some jokes are private dividends.
Portuguese language check: I caught myself saying 'tu' at the bakery and the woman said 'aqui é você'. I said 'você' and felt like a tourist in my own country.

Mom came up for the week. We walked the beach and she said, very casually, that Vó called me 'menina do mar'. I said I know. She said 'she said it to me too, every time you visited'. I didn't know. I'm writing it down so I don't forget the way my stomach felt.

Mãe, I'm writing this because you said my drawings look 'more relaxed' now and I didn't know what to say. Thank you for noticing. I think I'm just closer to the sea, and maybe that makes my hands looser.

Swam thirty meters today without stopping. Not in the sea, in the pool, because the sea and I are still in the negotiation phase. Dona Cida would say 'float first'. I'm working up to floating with an audience.

Started a new notebook labeled 'Menina do Mar', page one, no plan, just a drawing of the sea from Bia's window. It looks ordinary. I think that's the point. The sea is ordinary if you let it be yours.

Portuguese: Hoje choveu tanto que a rua virou rio. Desenhei a janela embaçada e a Bia dormindo no sofá, com o cobertor velho. Foi um desenho pequeno, mas acho que ficou honesto. Desenhos honestos são os que eu mais gosto e menos consigo vender.
A dream: Vó Lúcia sitting at a table with the parrot man, both eating lemon cake. She called him 'menino do mar' too. I woke up and wrote it down before it vanished.
Portuguese practice: desenhei Dona Cida swimming como se fosse super-heroína. Ela vai rir e depois vai me corrigir a braçada.
Swam in the sea alone for the first time, early morning, Praia Mole. Not far. Far enough. Nobody watching. That's the part 18-year-old me wouldn't believe.
Swam in the sea alone for the first time, Praia Mole, early morning. Not far. Far enough. Nobody watching. That's the part 18-year-old me wouldn't believe.
Swam in the sea alone again, not far, early morning, a dog watched me from the sand with total contempt. I waved. He did not wave back. Still counts.
Opened the 2014 capsule early by accident, the one from New Year's in Matinhos. The answer to both of your questions is yes: I see the sea from the window, and Bia is still the first person I text.
There is a cat that lives behind the building and stares at me like I owe it money. I started leaving water. It has not forgiven me, but it has started looking at me like I owe it less.

Swam in the sea alone early morning, Praia Mole. Not far. Far enough. Nobody watching. Eighteen-year-old me wouldn't believe it, and that's the point of writing this: proof that she was wrong about what was possible for her.

Bia and Júlia went out and I had the apartment to myself for the first time. I played Rafa's old playlist very quietly and didn't cry. Then I played it louder and cried a little. The playlist is still good. That's not a betrayal.
Swam in the sea alone for the first time. Not far. Far enough. Nobody watching. That's the part 18-year-old me wouldn't believe.
Bia, thank you for saving the room. I know I said it already, but the morning light comes in at 7:12 and I have started waking up to see it. That is a sentence 18-year-old me would not have believed.

Swam in the sea alone at Praia Mole early this morning. Not far, but far enough. No audience, no performance. I kept thinking of the dream from 2014 where my feet wouldn't move. They moved. Slowly, but they moved.
Mom visited and inspected the balcony like a general. She approved Limonada, the view, and the fact that I own a proper mop. She did not approve my coffee. Fair.
Postcard from Lisbon pinned above my desk. A man with a parrot on his shoulder from the 1950s. I don't know why it makes me feel less alone, but it does.
Júlia taught me to make brigadeiro in a tiny pan. We burned the first batch and ate it anyway with spoons, standing up, laughing too much for a Tuesday.
Limonada has six flowers and one thing that might become a fruit or might be a leaf. I refuse to investigate. Hope is cheaper than botany.

Money check: six months of savings, still called 'book' in the bank app. I almost renamed it 'MAR' again and then decided no, let it be the book. The book is the sea now, in a way. Vó would have liked that sentence. She would have said 'menina do mar' and I would have said 'vó' and that would be enough.
Portuguese practice: almoço de peixe com Bia, Júlia e minha mãe. Minha mãe disse que eu estou menos tensa. Não sei se isso é um elogio ou observação médica.

I hung the old drawing of the sea that Vó Lúcia framed above my bed again. The frame is dented and the glass is foggy. It looks more like the actual sea now, honestly. Some things improve by being imperfect.

At the comics fair in Curitiba, a woman held an old Interbairros strip and said 'this is my grandfather'. I wasn't there this year, Bia sent me the photo. I stared at it for ten minutes. I invented 'Seu Ivo' and 'Juca' in 2016. Only one was wrong. I'm still thinking about which one mattered more.

Money check from Floripa: rent is higher, coffee is better, and I spend less on bus passes because I mostly walk. The 'MAR' fund became 'book' fund became 'new chair because my back' fund. Priorities.

Money check: illustration paid for the groceries this week and the technical drawings paid for the rest. I put R$ 200 in the 'MAR' fund and felt both rich and ridiculous, which is probably what growing up feels like.

Money check: first month in Floripa went over budget because of the moving truck and a emergency fan for the balcony. Still, the MAR fund survived. I named the new account 'MAR II' because I am not creative with bank apps.
Limonada lost a branch in the wind. I panicked, then realized she has many. She's eight years old and more resilient than me on most days.
A postcard from Lisbon is still on my laptop. I look at it when the drawings are going badly. It reminds me there are other places with sea smell.
Found an old 'Interbairros' sketch in a moving box. Seu Ivo and Juca, both smiling. I stuck it inside my passport so I'd stop losing things I love in cardboard.

Onze anos sem a Vó e eu ainda pego o telefone aos domingos. Hoje desenhei o coronel, o cachorro da fazenda, com o chapéu do avô dela, porque ela diria que ele usava. Não sei se é verdade. Vou acreditar porque é mais bonito.

Tio Beto, on Sunday I played 'Asa Branca' for Mom over video call and she said 'you still speed up at the end'. She is right. I speed up at the end of everything. Working on it, slowly, like swimming.

Tio, mando este para você: toquei 'Asa Branca' até o fim hoje, sozinha, na varanda, com Limonada assistindo. Não errei (muito). A senhora pode clamar os créditos que quiser no próximo almoço. Um ano atrasado de nove, mas chegou.
Portuguese practice: tentei desenhar o mar de memória e saiu um quadrinho do Interbairros. Seu Ivo apareceu no meu traço sem eu chamar. Sinto falta dele.
Technical drawing all day, then a small drawing of a wave for myself. The second one is better. I am learning not to feel guilty about that.
Bia, your girlfriend Júlia asked if I always draw at breakfast. Yes. I told her it's how I wake up. She said that's beautiful. I said it's also avoidance. She laughed. Fair.

Started the book about Vó Lúcia again. 'Menina do Mar'. Twelve pages done, not counting the ones I redid because her hands looked wrong. I draw on Sundays now, at the hour I used to call her. It feels like a conversation that moved to paper.

I tried to draw the sea from memory and it came out as a blue rectangle with waves like parentheses. Honest, if not beautiful. Bia looked at it and said 'that's exactly what it looked like when I moved here'. She meant it as a compliment.
Rain all weekend. I drew Vó Lúcia's farm from memory, the jabuticabeira too wide, Coronel too brave. I wasn't sad. Just careful with the hands.

Comics fair in Curitiba is next year and I'm already nervous about the table. Bia says I should bring Limonada illustrations but she's a plant, not a product. Then again, she has more personality than some characters.

Found the postcard from Alfama in a book, the man with the parrot on his shoulder. I put it on the fridge next to Mom's printed comic strips. The fridge is becoming a small museum of people I love and birds I invented.
Started a small sketch of Dona Cida from an old photo. Her hands look strong. I want to draw every person who taught me something and not tell them. It feels like a private thank-you list.

Money check: illustration paid for a third of the month. The solar job paid for the rest. The 'MAR' fund is now called 'LIMONADA' in the app because I renamed it during a phase. I am not ashamed. The plant is doing better than the fund.
Drew Vó Lúcia's laugh as stairs again, because I don't want to forget the shape of it. It starts high and falls. I put it in the corner of a solar diagram and Thaís didn't notice. Good.
Found an old Interbairros strip in a drawer from 2016. Seu Ivo e o Papagaio. I miss them. I miss the 7am bus. Not enough to go back, but enough to remember.

Bia and Júlia are on the balcony, Limonada is between them, and I'm pretending to work in my room so they have the moment. I can hear them laughing. This is the part of life that doesn't fit in a diagram and doesn't need to.
Thaís let me work four days a week and I spent the fifth drawing Vó Lúcia's hands from photos. I still don't know if I got them right.
I drew the view from Bia's window for the hundredth time. The sea is never the same blue twice. Vó Lúcia would have said that and meant it.

Thaís asked if I could work four days a week and I said I'd think about it, which is adult for 'yes, absolutely, please'. I drew a tiny calendar with a lemon on Friday and sent it to her. She replied with a sun wearing sunglasses. The team is learning my language.
Halloween, Bia handed out candy on the balcony and I drew her as a sea witch with an apron. Limonada had a tiny ghost made of tissue. Nobody saw the ghost. We did. That's enough.
Ate a pastel at the feira and drew the vendor without asking. He saw it and said 'I look tired'. I said 'artistic tired'. He laughed and gave me a second pastel. I'm a negotiator now.

Tio Beto mandou áudio no WhatsApp cantando 'Asa Branca' até a terceira estrofe, só para mostrar que não esqueceu. Respondi com um desenho do violão e ele disse 'essa viola está sem corda'. Ele está certo. Um dia conserto.
Mãe, hoje eu desenhei a Vó Lúcia sentada na varanda. Não ficou perfeita, mas a mão dela ficou certa. Lembrei do que você disse em 2021. Obrigada por ter dito.
Bia and I watched a terrible movie and paused it every five minutes to argue. Júlia joined and sided with me. Bia pretended to be offended. The popcorn burned. Good night.

Mom, I know you're proud of the drawings because you print them, but it would be nice if you said it out loud too. I'm practicing saying things out loud. This is me practicing. Hi. I love you. Also the bolo de fubá recipe is still wrong and we both know it.
Tio Beto, I played Asa Branca on the beach today, to no one. The waves kept time better than I did. I'll be ready by next Festa Junina. I think.
Portuguese: Hoje desenhei Dona Cida do WhatsApp, com óculos e touca de natação, mas de memória. Ela me chamou de 'a engenheira' de novo. Ainda gosto. Ainda dói um pouco, mas gosto.

Money check: half my income comes from illustration now, if you count the small commissions Thaís sends my way. The 'MAR' fund is the 'book' fund. I'm not telling Mom the numbers yet. She'd say 'finally' and I'd have to agree, and agreeing with Mom about drawing still feels like a trap I'm not ready to enter.
Portuguese practice: Mom came up for the week and immediately asked if eu estou comendo direito. Respondi que estou comendo o mar de vista, que conta.
Thaís let me draw a diagram with a little sun again and this time it stayed in the deck. I'm not saying I've made it. I'm saying I have a sun in an investor deck.

Mother called to say she printed a new comic and stuck it to her fridge. She didn't say 'good drawing'. She said 'this parrot has a lot of personality'. I'll take it. Personality is as close to love as my mother gets with ink.
A bus driver in Floripa said 'bom dia' to everyone by name. Nobody had a parrot, but I almost cried anyway. Drew him in the margin of a meeting note. Thaís did not notice, or pretended not to.

Bia made dinner and Júlia burned the rice. We ate it anyway and declared it 'textural'. Limonada's flowers are falling off now, which feels like a small funeral I am not ready for. I saved one in a book, which is very dramatic for a flower.
Thaís let me work four days a week starting January and I've already used the extra day to draw nothing and drink coffee. Rest is also work, I'm telling myself. My therapist would agree, probably.
Money check: rent plus Balneário groceries plus a birthday present for Dona Cida. The 'MAR' fund dipped below R$ 200. I considered panic and chose swimming instead.

Sunday drawing time. I tried the first page of the book about Vó again and got as far as her hands holding coffee. My own hands shook a little, which is not useful for ink. I went for a walk and came back. The hands calmed down. Page one exists.
Thaís said my inverter drawing 'has personality', which is engineer for 'too many curves, but I like it'. I am collecting compliments that don't sound like compliments and I am rich.

Limonada got her first flowers. Small, white, smell incredible. No lemons yet. Bia says flowers count. I agree. I've been agreeing with Bia a lot lately; it's a good habit. Drew the flowers before breakfast and they looked like tiny moons.
Bia's girlfriend Júlia watered Limonada while we were out and said she heard the leaves rustling. Limonada is now the third roommate in status.
Dreamed I was swimming with someone I couldn't see. Woke up and the room was full of blue light from the sea. Didn't want to move yet.
Bia, I found a lemon flower bud this morning and took six photos from different angles. You asked if I was OK. I am better than OK. Please don't move the pot while I'm at the pool.
Money check: a client paid late and I ate pastel de feira for three days. It wasn't hardship; it was research. Pastel is still the perfect food.

Sunday drawing time, balcony, Limonada, wind. I sketched Bia's coffee cup and she complained that I made it look too elegant. I said it's because I love her. She said 'draw my messy hair then'. So I did.
Portuguese practice: desenhei o Coronel, o cachorro da Vó Lúcia, pela enésima vez. Cada vez ele fica mais corajoso. É assim que ela contava.
Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was already swimming and the water was full of tiny lemons. Very on the nose, subconscious. I woke up hungry.
Bia and Júlia argued about curtains and I hid in my room pretending to work, which is becoming my superpower. The sea was very blue today. I drew the blue and nothing else.
First lemon tree flower? No. Still buds. I checked three times today. Limonada is teaching me patience, which is rude of a plant with no deadlines.

I started sketching Vó Lúcia's stories again, just small ones. Not a book, not yet. Just Coronel at the gate, and the jabuticabeira, and her hands. My hands are not hers, but they are learning. I need a walk after every page.
December in Floripa is loud. The neighbors have a dog that barks at the sea, which I understand. I drew the dog and the sea and Limonada on the same page, like they're family. Maybe they are.
Dona Cida sent a postcard from her granddaughter's school play. On the back: 'a engenheira, continue nadando'. It is now on the fridge, next to the parrot man. The fridge museum is expanding.
Mom, I made the bolo de fubá again. Better this time. I think the secret is stopping two minutes early. I'll never tell you that's what you did wrong.

Decorated the apartment with Bia and we put a tiny green ball on Limonada's branch because there's no tree small enough. She's nine, almost, and still no lemons. I love her anyway, which is how I feel about most things.

Thaís let me work four days a week now. The fifth day is for the book. I told her it's 'personal illustration work' and she said 'finally, less solar panels, more sun'. She's right that I draw better when I'm happy. Everyone is, probably. I just hadn't tested it before.
Thaís gave me Friday afternoons off for illustration. I celebrated by buying a new sketchbook and then being too scared to make the first mark. Very me.

The sunset tonight was absurd, pink and orange like someone spilled paint on the ocean. I drew it badly because the light kept changing. Some things are not meant to be captured, only witnessed. I am writing this so I don't forget that.
New Year plans already. Bia wants fireworks on the beach, Mom wants a hotel, I want to swim a little bit past the point where I usually stop. I wrote it down so I can't pretend I was too tired.
Mom found my drawings of Vó's stories on the balcony table and said nothing for five minutes. Then she said 'you got her laugh right'. I didn't know I had.
Ate bolo de fubá using Vó Lúcia's recipe. It was slightly dry. I laughed alone in the kitchen and then ate two slices. Some things are correct even when wrong.
One month until New Year. No plans yet except: sea, Bia, Limonada. That's enough. 18-year-old me wanted exactly this, minus the lemon tree, which she hadn't planted yet.
Mãe, I'm writing this early because I know you'll say Christmas is 'just another day' and then cry at the table. Bring the bolo de fubá. Wrong is fine. Wrong is ours now.

Mãe, você veio passar a semana em Floripa e eu cozinhei feijão igual o seu, mas coloquei limão sem querer. Você disse 'ficou bom' de um jeito que eu conheço: foi elogio e memória ao mesmo tempo. Obrigada por não corrigir.
Limonada produced one flower so small I thought it was dust. I took a photo and zoomed in until my phone battery died. It's a flower. It counts.

Mom called to ask if Lisbon would be 'forever'. I said I don't know, but I'm in Floripa now, and the sea here is the same ocean. She was quiet and then said Vó always said I was menina do mar, not menina de Curitiba. I didn't know she told Mom too. I'm glad she did.

Bia, thank you for not asking 'are you drawing?' every day. You ask it exactly often enough. The spare room is still blue. I keep opening the curtains even when it's raining, which is probably a metaphor I won't examine today.
Bia made a gingerbread house and it collapsed. Júlia said it was structural failure. I said it was a lemon tree without lemons. Nobody laughed except me. I'm fine with that.
Portuguese practice: hoje foi dia de sol em Floripa e eu fui nadar cedo. Ninguém assistindo. Isso ainda parece mentira de filme.
Year-end. Made a list of small things I want to keep: morning light, Bia's coffee, Limonada's leaves, Dona Cida's voice, the sea sounding like breathing. Nothing dramatic. Just this.
Decided to start the book about Vó Lúcia again. Not finished, just started. Twelve pages feels impossible and also like the only thing worth doing.

Money check: illustration is almost half my income now, not quite, but enough that the 'MAR' fund turned into 'book' in my head. I haven't started the book but I think about starting it every day, which is the pre-book phase.

Bia lit candles on the balcony and Limonada's flowers smelled stronger in the warm air. I drew the three of us from the kitchen doorway: Bia, Júlia, the sea. I left myself out of the frame. I was still there, just behind the line.
Final drawing of the year: Limonada with a single flower, the sea behind her, and a tiny parrot on the windowsill that I invented for luck. Happy 2025, if it arrives.
Packed for New Year's on the balcony. Tiny green ball in Limonada's branches. Could be a lemon. Could be my imagination. Not jinxing it.
Mom, I found your bolo de fubá recipe written in Vó's handwriting. I'm making it on Sunday. If it's too dry again, we'll laugh and cry like last time. I'll bring the printer paper.

Portuguese: Hoje é aniversário do dia em que graduei, seis anos atrás. Vó veio com um chapéu maior que ela. Ainda não sei o que fazer com essa data, mas fiz um desenho dela na cerimônia e coloquei na geladeira, ao lado do desenho de Seu Ivo e do papagaio.
Called Tio Beto and he played 'Asa Branca' on the phone. I sang the second verse and got it right. He went quiet for a moment and then said 'next year, the whole song'. We both know what that means.

New Year's is coming and I don't know what I'll do at midnight. Maybe stay with my feet in the water, like 2014. Maybe swim out a little. Bia says she'll scream either way. I believe her. Writing this so that when I read it later, I remember that not knowing was okay.
Bia, if you're reading this before New Year's, thank you for saving the room. You saved more than a room.
New Year approaches. I have a dress I like and a lemon tree with one real bud. If it opens before midnight, I will count it as a very small miracle and not tell anyone except you.
Christmas Eve without Vó, still. Mom brought the bolo. Nobody said it was dry this year. I think that's progress.
Christmas was loud and warm and Mom did cry at the table. Bia put the photo of Vó next to the bolo and nobody mentioned it and everyone saw it. I'm okay. I'm more than okay. I'm by the sea.
Portuguese practice: Tio Beto mandou áudio dizendo 'feliz ano novo, menina do mar'. Fiquei com o telefone na mão por três minutos.
Wrote 'Menina do Mar' on a notebook cover today, then erased it. Too soon, maybe. But the word is there now.
Last capsule of the year. The sea is outside the window and Limonada is on the balcony. Tomorrow I'm not staying with my feet in the water at midnight. That's all I'll say.
Portuguese practice: amanhã é réveillon. Vou nadar um pouco, não só ficar com os pés na água. Bia disse que grita. Eu sei.
Last work day of the year. Drew a tiny lemon on the corner of my last diagram. Thaís will pretend not to see it. I will also pretend.

Ten years since Matinhos. This year I didn't stay with my feet in the water at midnight, I swam out a little. Bia screamed. I want to write down the people at this New Year's: Bia, her girlfriend Júlia, Mom who came up for the week, Dona Cida's postcard on the fridge. Missing: Vó Lúcia, as always.

First swim of the year at Praia Mole, alone, 6:40am. The water was colder than I expected and I made a noise only dolphins could hear. Still counts. I came home with sand in my eyebrow and ate toast standing up.

It rained all afternoon and the whole balcony smelled like wet wood and basil. I tried to sketch the rain on the glass and gave up after three lines. Bia made popcorn and Júlia put on a song I don't know. I sat by Limonada and counted her buds again: seven. Not bad for January.

First swim of the year at Praia Mole before work. The water was cold enough to make me reconsider all my life choices, then fine, then wonderful. I counted twenty strokes before my brain woke up. I think that's a record for January.

Primeiro banho de mar do ano na Praia Mole, 6h30, ninguém por perto. A água não estava quente, mas estava mansa. Fiquei mais tempo do que planejei porque o sol apareceu de uma vez só. Esse ano começa leve.

Sunday drawing block again. I sat at the kitchen table with Limonada’s flowers smelling like something between jasmine and laundry. Drew Vó Lúcia’s hands three times because the knuckles kept coming out wrong. Bia walked by and said, “you’re doing the thing where you frown at the paper,” which is fair. The funniest part: Thaís messaged asking for the sun with sunglasses in vector format, and I sent it while humming a violão song. Halfway there, future me. Halfway on the bills, still all the way in love with the work.

First swim of the year at Praia Mole before work. The water was colder than I expected and I complained out loud to no one. My hair is still salt-stiff. Bia left coffee on the counter with a note that said 'brave nerd'. I'm keeping the note.
Limonada got a new leaf on the balcony and I acted like it was a baby announcement. Bia took a photo of me pointing at it. I'm keeping it for the book.
Rainy day in Floripa. Took the bus to the market and came back with three lemons, which felt like cheating, but Limonada needs company. Drew Bia sleeping on the balcony with a blanket over her head.

Worked four hours on the book and got one page that doesn't make me flinch. Then ate a whole bowl of pipoca watching the sea change color. Limonada's flowers are still there. Nobody needs to know that this counts as a productive day.
Found a yogurt cup in the fridge with 'MARINA' written on it, leftover from Bia's roommate years. I laughed so hard I woke everyone up.

First swim of the year at Praia Mole, 6:40am, water still cold and the sky not fully awake. I only went in to my waist, but I counted it. Limonada has two new leaves on the balcony and looks smug about it. Bia says I talk to the tree more than to Júlia. She might be right.

Went swimming before work, early enough that the sea looked like pewter. I only swam for maybe six minutes, but it was enough to make the whole day feel slower. A dog stole one of my flip-flops at the kiosk. I got it back by offering it a piece of pão de queijo, which feels like a negotiation I won and lost at the same time.
Mom, thanks for the printer. I know I said it was too much, but it's still printing the Interbairros strips you pretend you don't read. The ink keeps running out in suspiciously regular intervals.

Limonada dropped one tiny leaf on the balcony floor. Bia says that's normal; I'm treating it like a medical emergency. I moved her pot two centimeters away from the wind. No progress on lemons, but she looks very green and stubborn.
Primeiro domingo de janeiro em Floripa. Chuva grossa, janela aberta, cheiro de maresia. Desenhei o mar de memória e ficou parecendo Curitiba com ondas. Ainda não é o meu desenho ainda.

Portuguese: Hoje acordei com o cheiro do mar pela janela e levei uns segundos pra lembrar que não era sonho. Bia tinha feito café. A Limonada já tem duas flores novas. Pedi licença da vida e fiquei cinco minutos olhando a rua.
Portuguese: O supermercado tocou uma música de rádio de quando eu tinha 16 anos. Fiquei dois minutos parada no corredor das bolachas.
Bia and Júlia got engaged on the balcony, next to Limonada. I was hiding in my room pretending to work so they'd have the moment. I heard the scream through the wall. Wedding in 2026.

Desenhei o porto hoje, quinze minutos entre duas reuniões. Thaís perguntou se eu estava distraída. Disse que era pesquisa visual. Ela sorriu, então acredito que passou. Faz tempo que não desenho algo sem utilidade. Gostei do gosto disso.

Thaís asked for one more diagram for the solar project and I stayed up until midnight drawing little lightning bolts in the corners. She'll probably ask me to remove them. I won't remove the one that looks like a crooked smile.
Bia and Júlia keep leaving wedding magazines on the kitchen table. I keep moving them next to the lemon tree so at least Limonada gets to judge the flowers.
Bia e Júlia discutindo paleta de cores da cozinha nova. Eu desenhei três opções em guardanapo e uma virou "a oficial". Me sinto útil de uma forma que não sabia que queria.
Bia found a caterpillar on Limonada's balcony pot and named him Frederico. We spent ten minutes moving him to a safer leaf. He did not thank us.

Bia, thank you for leaving the sea window slightly open at night. It makes the room breathe. I know you think I’m dramatic about sounds, but the waves do a better job than my playlists. Also, yes, I heard Júlia laugh at 2am and no, I don’t need to know why. Save me some breakfast. I’m drawing the balcony chairs and one of them looks judgmental.
Bia, if I ever complain about the balcony wind again, remind me that I asked for a window facing the sea and got one. I'll shut up and take the wind.
Thaís asked for a diagram with 'a little warmth'. I added a sun with sunglasses again and she laughed, then said okay but maybe no sunglasses this time. Compromise: sunglasses off, still smiling.

Chuva o dia inteiro em Floripa. Fiquei em casa desenhando a Vó Lúcia nova, a versão com 30 anos que ela me contava. Tentei não chorar por causa das páginas molhadas. Consegui, mais ou menos. O caldo da Bia queimou no fundo e a cozinha inteira cheirava a tostado. A gente comeu assim mesmo e ninguém reclamou.
Portuguese: Hoje o céu estava daquele azul que eu desenho mal. Tentei três vezes. Acabei desenhando o poste da esquina e a antena da vizinha.
Read the 2014 capsule about the sea dream tonight. I put one foot in back then. Now I swim. Progress is annoyingly slow and then suddenly not.
Ate a lemon tart at the café near the office and thought of Limonada. No relation, of course. Still, I raised my fork to her. She's on the balcony, growing, ignoring me as usual.
A man on the bus was reading 'A Moreninha' and smiling at the same page for twenty minutes. I wanted to ask which part. I didn't. I drew him instead. Some conversations are better as drawings.
Bus in Curitiba for a weekend. An old man had a canary in a cage. Nobody reacted. I drew them in my notebook and felt 18 again, except now my back hurts.
PT: Hoje o vento fechou a janela da Bia e meu caderno de esboços voou para a cozinha. Três páginas de Vó Lúcia sumiram dentro do forno. Recuperei duas. A terceira virou arte abstrata com margarina.
Thaís asked for a less technical diagram again. I drew the sun with sunglasses, but this time I added a little lemon tree next to it. She said 'cute, keep it'. I am being paid to be cute, apparently.

Bus ride to the comics fair planning meeting. There’s a man with a caged canary and a woman carrying a ficus; nobody says anything. I miss Seu Ivo and Juca in a way that makes no sense because I never knew his real name. Drew them both on a napkin. The driver braked too hard and the canary didn’t react either. I think I’m the only one keeping score.
