Bia, você deixou o caderno de desenhos aberto na cozinha e o vento deu uma página inteira pro mar. Eu desenhei de novo antes de você ver. Não conta. O mar não paga por imagens ruins.

Bia, se você estiver lendo isso, obrigada por não ter dito nada quando eu gritei com a impressora. A pressão era o cartucho, mas eu fui grossa. Te pago um pastel hoje. Amor não paga dívida de mal humor, mas pastel ajuda.
Thaís asked for a diagram and I drew a tiny sun with sunglasses again, by habit. She didn't ask for it this time but kept it. I'm calling that a win.

Fez sol o dia inteiro e eu trabalhei perto da janela com o ventilador ligado. O mar parecia um desenho de aquarela. Fiz uma pausa para desenhar as ondas e acabei perdendo uma hora de trabalho. Thaís não reclamou porque o desenho foi para o fundo da apresentação. Coloquei um peixinho.
Bia, you left your shoes in the hallway again. I put them by the door. If you're reading this in a year and they're still there, that's on both of us.
Dreamt of the sea again, but this time I was just sitting on the sand with a sketchbook and no urgency. No one swimming next to me. It was ordinary, and I think that's why I woke up smiling.
Sunday drawing session at old calling time. The apartment was quiet and I could hear the sea. Page ten is Coronel under the jabuticabeira. He looks braver than ever.
Bia, happy Valentine's to the woman who saved me the room facing the sea. If you're reading this in 2029, I hope Júlia still makes your coffee wrong on purpose because it makes you laugh.
No Valentine's drama. Just toast, coffee, and a walk to the Mirante. Bia says I'm romantic now. I said I'm hungry. Both true.

Portuguese-ish tiny note: Hoje choveu em Florianópolis e eu comprei goiabada na feira sem saber por quê. Comi com pão no banco perto do mercado, olhando o mar cinza. Lembrei da Vó dizendo que chuva boa é a que cai sem pressa. Acho que ela tinha razão em mais coisas do que eu admiti. Guardei a goiabada no pote com ‘MAR’ escrito em cima porque o pote de ‘book’ já estava ocupado. Lógica de adulto.
Valentine's Day, very normal: I swam three laps, called Mom, and Limonada produced exactly zero lemons. Consider this my annual report on romance.
Day of what's-his-name. I went swimming early instead. The water was cold and perfect and nobody asked me anything. The best Valentine's I've had since high school.
Valentine's Day. I bought myself a pastel at the feira and ate it on the bench. A woman asked if I was waiting for someone. I said no and she said 'good for you'. I think she meant it.

Valentine's Day is not a Brazilian holiday I take seriously, but Bia left a tiny cactus on my desk with a note: 'for the girl who finally swam.' I put it next to Limonada. Two plants now. My room looks like a greenhouse with a desk in it.

Bia, thank you for saving me the last pastel at the feira even though you said you were 'just holding it for me'. I know you wanted it. I also know you let me have it because I looked tired. You're too easy to read and too good to me.

Money check: R$ 1.240 for the month after rent and the book printing test. I ate arroz e feijão for five days and didn't mind. The test copy looks good, though the cover color is slightly muddy. Progress, not perfection.
Mom sent a photo of Tio Beto's violão with a broken string. She asked if I know how to fix it. I don't, but I'm already looking up tutorials because it's easier than saying no to her.

PT: Terminei a página dez do livro e caminhei até o mercado para comprar limão. Limão comprado, não da Limonada, porque ela ainda está negociando. O caixa perguntou se eu era ilustradora. Disse que sim e acreditei pela primeira vez.

Ônibus em Floripa ainda me faz desenhar rápido demais. Um senhor cochilou com um pão na mão e ninguém o acordou; desenhei isso em dois minutos e ficou o melhor desenho da semana. O maracujá do mercado custou R$ 9, quase chorei.
Quiet Saturday. Washed the balcony tiles and talked to Limonada for ten minutes about nothing. Bia walked by and said 'you're your grandmother'. I didn't correct her.
Portuguese: Fiz sopa de legumes porque choveu e porque Vó fazia sopa nos dias assim. A minha ficou melhor do que a dela? Não. Mas a cozinha cheirou certo e isso foi suficiente.
Limonada has a new leaf that is somehow brighter green than the others. I watered her too much yesterday and panicked. Bia said plants are more forgiving than people. I hope she's right about both.
Mom, if you're reading this: I used the printer you gave me to print 'Menina do Mar' pages. The colors came out too warm. I'm blaming the machine, not my choices.

On the bus to the supermarket I saw a man with a small dog in a backpack. The dog had sunglasses. Nobody reacted except me. I drew them at the next stop and Thaís later said the dog looked like my manager. She is not wrong.
Thaís asked for a new diagram and I drew a tiny sun wearing sunglasses again. She said 'you're impossible.' I took it as a compliment.
Money check: the book fund has R$ 1.200 and I already spent R$ 80 on a new brush that I don't technically need. This is how the fund will die. With dignity and very good lines.
Mom came up for the week and brought a printer cartridge and a Tupperware of bolinho. She said the balcony smells like the old farm in Irati. I think she means the lemon tree.

Bia, thank you for pretending not to notice that I hid in my room during your engagement. I was crying into a diagram. It was the nice kind of crying, I promise. I am so happy for you and Júlia that my face did something ugly.

A Sunday without calling Vó still catches me off guard. I drew her hands again and they came out right on the first try. Then I had to stop because it felt too easy, which is a strange thing to be afraid of.

At the comics fair in Curitiba last month, a woman held an old printed strip and said it was her grandfather. I keep thinking about it. Tonight I drew Seu Ivo again, older, with Juca on his shoulder, and felt less like I invented him and more like I remembered him.
Sunday drawing at the time I used to call Vó. 14 pages done now. Today I drew her hands shelling peas. I had to stop and make tea halfway.
I forgot my sketchbook at home and drew on a napkin at lunch. The napkin became a motor diagram with a tiny parrot. Thaís saw it and asked if it was for the investor deck. Maybe.

Took the bus to the comics fair planning and watched an old woman argue with the driver about whether the fare had gone up. She won. I drew her victory in my notebook and she caught me and asked for a copy. I said I'd mail it. I need to mail it.
Rain all day in Floripa, the kind that makes the sea disappear. I drew Limonada from the window and sent it to Thaís as 'atmospheric data.' She said it was nice. I'm choosing to believe that.

Mom, I made your bolo de fubá and it was still too dry. I think the problem is patience, not the recipe. I sent you the photo of Limonada’s flowers and you replied “bonita” with one word. I know what that means now. It means you looked twice. Thank you for buying the printer all those years ago. It still works, somehow, like stubborn people.
Money check: the book fund is small but real. I moved R$ 400 into it and felt like a millionaire and a liar at the same time. Progress.
Thaís approved the new diagram set on the first try, which never happens. To celebrate I bought a pastel de feira that tasted exactly like 2015, except this time I was 29 and could pay for two.

Portuguese: Domingo de desenho. Tentei fazer a Vó nova, com as mãos. Desenhei as mãos três vezes e nenhuma parecia dela. Fiz uma caminhada até o fim da rua e voltei. As mãos ainda estavam erradas, mas menos.
Portuguese: Fui nadar cedo. A água estava gelada e pensei na Dona Cida falando que flutuar é confiança. Hoje confiei mais na toalha que na água.

Paid the water bill, bought vegetables, and still had money for a pastel de feira. This sounds boring but 2014 me would think it's a miracle. I ate it standing up, looking at the sea, and cried a little for no reason. Good cry, I think.
Rain all day. Worked from the balcony anyway, with a blanket and a stubborn laptop. Limonada's flowers looked like tiny wet stars.

Bus to the center, rain, everyone wet and annoyed except a kid eating a banana with complete concentration. I drew him in the margin of the technical drawing. Thaís will never notice. I hope she never notices.

Portuguese: A Bia pediu pra desenhar o convite do casamento dela. Fiz três versões. A primeira tinha mar demais. A segunda tinha pouco mar. A terceira tinha o mar do tamanho certo, segundo a Júlia. Vou imprimir amanhã.
Portuguese: O mar estava bravo hoje. Fiquei só observando da pedra. Não entrei. Nem toda brava pede coragem.
Money check: illustration invoices paid late again, but the 'book' fund has R$ 1.240 now. I'm not rich, but I'm no longer scared of checking the bank app. Progress is boring and I'm grateful for it.
Chuva no fim da tarde. Fechei o caderno e fiquei vendo a chuva bater na Limonada. Ela não se mexeu. Eu também não. Foi bom.
Dreamed of the sea again, but this time I was floating on my back and laughing at something. No one next to me, just the sky. I woke up with my shoulders relaxed, which is new.
Mãe, obrigada pela receita do bolo de fubá. Ficou menos seco hoje. Ainda não é o da Vó, mas foi o primeiro que não me fez sentir culpada por comer.
Adult swimming class at 7am again. Dona Cida wasn't there, she sent a message saying she had 'important beach business'. Fair enough.

Thaís asked for a diagram of a pump and I drew the pump with tiny wings. She didn’t ask for wings. She kept them. I think this is how illustration starts paying half the bills: by accident, on a Tuesday, in a file named pump_v3_FINAL. The sea was flat today and I swam a little before work. Not far. Enough to feel smug during a 9am meeting.
Tio, I still haven't played Asa Branca for you this year. I practice when Bia is at work so nobody hears the mistakes. That's cheating and I know it.
Money note: bought new watercolor paper and felt guilty for eleven minutes. Then remembered the book fund exists and the paper is for the book. Guilt down to two minutes. Progress.
Thaís approved the sun with sunglasses for another deck. I added tiny rays and nobody noticed except me, which is enough.

Mom, I tried your bolo de fubá recipe again. It was better than last time, but still not yours. Maybe it's the oven. Maybe it's the missing ingredient, which is probably you standing in the kitchen telling me not to open the door too early.
PT: Dona Cida me escreveu uma carta à mão. Disse que o mar daqui é diferente do do Rio porque 'não tem tanta pressa'. Li três vezes. Mandei ela uma fotografia da Praia Mole.
I spent the afternoon on the balcony drawing Limonada's flowers from three angles. They are tiny and stubborn, which feels on brand for this family.

Mom, I made the bolo de fubá today with your recipe and it was only a little dry. I think Vó's oven ran hotter than mine. I'm keeping the dry version in the family history as 'almost Vó'. Come visit before I eat it all.

Thaís asked for a diagram of a solar panel mount and I gave her one with a tiny bird sitting on top. She kept it. The bird is now the unofficial mascot of the engineering channel. I am 29 and this is my proudest professional achievement.

Thaís asked for 'something less technical' on a diagram, so I drew a tiny sun with a surfboard. She didn't use it, but she laughed for a full minute. That counts as a success in my professional development plan.
Bia, if you're reading this in the future, thank you for pretending not to notice when I cried at the 'Asa Branca' lyrics on the radio today. You are better at that than you think.
April Fools. Júlia told me Limonada had given a lemon. She had not. I looked for five minutes before understanding. I deserve that.
Mom sent a voice note saying she printed another comic. I couldn't hear the whole thing because she was chewing. Love her anyway.

I started the book about Vó Lúcia again. I'm calling it 'Menina do Mar'. 12 pages done. It's harder than I thought because every page is a conversation with her and then I need a walk. I'm drawing on Sundays, at the time I used to call her. Feels right.

Money check: half from illustration, half from solar diagrams, rent paid. The 'book' fund has R$ 1.200. It is not a fortune but it is mine and it has a name, so I'm not touching it except for paper and ink.
Curitiba comics fair prep. Packed my old Interbairros prints and found a strip with Seu Ivo and Juca that has a coffee stain. I'm keeping it. It's character development.

Page seven of Menina do Mar took four hours and one walk around the block. I drew Vó Lúcia's hands holding a coffee cup and they were wrong, then right, then wrong again. I kept the wrong version for now.

Thaís asked if I could draw a diagram with 'less personality'. I tried. The sun with sunglasses disappeared. Three days later it was back in the deck, added by someone else. I feel like a very small legend.
Drew page seven of Menina do Mar and couldn't finish the last panel. Vó's hands. I walked to the beach and stood there until the sun went down. Came home and drew them better.

Went to the beach with Bia and Júlia. Júlia swam far out and Bia yelled. I stayed in the shallow part, floating, not panicking, which is new enough to write down. I came back with one sandal missing. Small price.

Drew Vó Lúcia's hands from memory again. They're different every time: sometimes thinner, sometimes stronger, always busy. I kept the one where she's holding a lemon and didn't like it, so I tried again. The second one is closer.

Tio Beto, I tried ‘Asa Branca’ on the balcony this morning and forgot the third verse again, but Limonada did not clap, so at least I’m honest about it. Remember when you said one more year? It has been more than one, and I still think about your hand on the violão neck, steady as a gate. If I ever learn a second song, I’ll tell you first. Don’t tell Mom; she’ll want sheet music.
Portuguese: Limonada tem flores de novo. Cheiro de tarde. Fiquei dez minutos com o nariz perto dela e parecia ridículo, então continuei por mais dez.
Dona Cida would be proud: I swam 400 meters without stopping and only swallowed two gulps. The sea was calm, almost suspiciously calm, like it was saving something for later.
Money check: illustration paid for groceries and the electricity bill this month. The 'MAR' fund got renamed 'book' last year, but the bank app still calls it MAR in my head.

Mom called to say she finally learned to use the scanner. She scanned my old bus comics and sent 47 files in the wrong order. I spent an hour putting them back together. At the end she said, 'they are better than I remember.' I pretended my internet was bad.
Rain canceled the swim. I sat on the bed and drew waves from memory until the storm stopped. They looked like handwriting. I like that.

I wrote two pages of 'Menina do Mar' and then had to stop and walk to the beach. Not because it was bad, but because every page feels like talking to her and I can't do that without breathing salt air. The book will take as long as it takes.
Tio Beto, I played Asa Branca on the borrowed violão at Bia's dinner yesterday. Júlia clapped too early. Mom said I sounded like you, which means she was being kind. Obrigada.

Portuguese: Choveu o dia inteiro. Fiquei em casa desenhando a janela embasada. Bia passou aspirador duas vezes. A Limonada balançou com o vento e perdeu uma folha. Achei a folha no chão da varanda e guardei ela no livro, página 3.
Portuguese: Desenhei a mão da Vó Lúcia de novo. Ainda acerto os dedos e erro o pulso. Vou continuar até o pulso também.
Bia, you asked if I'm happy. I said yes and meant it. Then I drew a tiny version of us on the balcony and it looked like a greeting card, which is annoying and perfect.
Swam 40 meters today, not pretty but continuous. Dona Cida would be proud. I sent her a message and she replied with three emojis and no words, which is her highest praise.
Limonada has more flowers now. Bia says she is 'showing off'. I agree. She waited eight years for this and now behaves like she always knew.

Sonhei que a Vó Lúcia estava cozinhando na cozinha da casa de Curitiba e me chamava de menina do mar. Quando acordei, o cheiro da cozinha era bolo de fubá. A Bia tinha tentado a receita da Vó e ficou bom. Nós três comemos no balcão, em silêncio, com a janela aberta.

Went to the municipal market for pastel and ended up drawing the fish stall instead. The man selling shrimp asked if I was an artist and I said “sometimes,” which is the most honest answer I’ve given all year. He gave me a lemon for free because I was “drawing his stall well enough.” I did not correct him. Limonada, your cousin, is small and green and already more popular than me.
Primeira natação com a Júlia hoje. Ela perdeu o óculos no fundo da piscina e eu achei rindo, como se isso fosse heroísmo. Foi divertido. A gente precisava disso.
Paid rent, bought groceries, and still had enough left for a pastel de feira. Small victories count. Eighteen-year-old Marina would be suspicious but pleased.

PT: Paguei o aluguel da sala compartilhada por um mês. É pequena, cheira a tinta e tem uma janela para um muro. Ainda assim, desenhei melhor ali do que em casa. Acho que é porque ninguém me pergunta onde está a planilha.
Bia tried to teach me a cocktail recipe. It required eight steps and I got to step three before adding too much lime. She drank it anyway and said 'it's aggressive, but I respect it'.
Drew on the bus again, but it's the Lagoa bus now. No parrot man. Just a man with a bread bag and a woman reading a romance with a dramatic cover. I made them both very polite.
Woke up at 5:30 to draw the light on Limonada. The lemon flowers looked like small stars. I got one good page and a mosquito bite on my ankle. Acceptable exchange.
Bus today had a man with a parrot backpack, not a real parrot. I almost asked him about Juca. Then remembered how inventions end up true. Didn't ask.

Bia, if you are reading this in a year, I want you to know I have already started practicing my speech for your wedding. It is three pages long and I will probably cry by page two. Also, thank you for saving the room. You already know, but I want it in writing.
Mom, I know you'll read this and say it's too much, but the book is 12 pages and each one takes a walk afterward. Thank you for saying my grandmother's hands were right.
On the bus today a teenager was sketching people on his phone. I wanted to tell him to put it on paper before he loses the habit. I didn't. I hope someone tells him. Maybe his grandmother will.
A stranger at the café asked if the drawing in my sketchbook was Curitiba's bus. It was Floripa, actually, but close enough. I told him about Seu Ivo and felt ridiculous and happy at the same time.

First swimming lesson since restarting with Dona Cida's old drills. New teacher is twenty-something and very serious. He said 'you are already relaxed'. I did not tell him I once panicked for four seconds in 2015. Some victories are private.
Tio Beto, toquei 'Asa Branca' no violão hoje sem errar. Não foi lindo, mas foi inteira. Sei que você vai dizer 'só isso?' e eu vou responder 'só isso'. Só isso.

Portuguese: Paguei as contas do mês e sobrou dinheiro pra comprar tinta nova. Anotei na planilha como 'trabalho', não como 'luxo'. Acho que isso é o que a terapeuta chamaria de progresso. Ou de orgulho. Ou de teimosia. Os três.
Júlia taught me to make risotto and I burned the rice twice. She was patient. I drew her hands holding the spoon and they looked like Vó's. I didn't say that out loud.
Found a yogurt cup in the recycling and almost wrote MARINA on it. Old habits. Put it back. Limonada has her own pot now.
Júlia made a lemonade with sugar and salt, which she insists is Brazilian and Bia insists is a crime. I drank two glasses. Limonada was not involved. Someday she will be, and that day will be better.
Dona Cida, I floated today without counting seconds. I don't know when that happened. Obrigada por me fazer confiar na água. A água não estava confiando em mim, mas ela foi generosa mesmo assim.
Mom called to ask if I'm eating properly. I sent her a photo of rice, beans, and a lemon slice. She said 'that's not a meal, that's a garnish'. She's right.

Rain again. The balcony drain made that sound like a small instrument and I recorded it for three minutes, embarrassed by myself. Then I drew it as a person with a funnel for a hat. The book has 15 pages now, or 14 and a half because page 12 refuses to behave. Vó Lúcia’s laugh still starts high and falls like stairs. I know this because I drew the sound as stairs. Don’t tell the publisher.
Rain all day. I drew the window view four times because the light kept changing. Bia said I was 'being artistic about weather' and I think she meant it nicely.
Bia, Júlia picked a veil, a small one, and you pretended not to cry and failed completely. I pretended I wasn't drawing the moment and failed worse. We are all disasters. Good ones.
Bad drawing day. Everything looked flat and wrong and I closed the sketchbook after ten minutes. Opened it again before bed and added one line to Vó's laughing mouth. Better.

Money check: half of my income is illustration now, which still sounds like a sentence I'm not allowed to say out loud. The other half is diagrams with sunglasses. Thaís says I should put the sun on merch. I'm considering it.

Mom, you will laugh: I burned the bolo de fubá today. Not a little. The smoke alarm had opinions. I opened every window and the sea air came in and rescued the kitchen. I think Vó would have said the sea was helping. I'm trying again on Sunday.
Eleven years since I wrote about the república fridge. Sometimes I still write my name on things out of habit, including the Tupperware at Bia's place. She hasn't said anything yet.

Drew Limonada from above today and realized she is almost as tall as the balcony railing. Eleven years old and still no lemons. I refuse to call her decorative. She is patient. I am the one who needs patience.

At a comics fair in Curitiba a woman came to my table holding an old printed 'Interbairros' strip. Seu Ivo e o Papagaio. She said 'this is my grandfather, Valdir. The parrot was Juca'. I had invented both names. Only one was wrong. He died last year, at 91. She said he had the strip on his fridge.
Portuguese: Hoje choveu forte e a varanda virou um pequeno oceano de pingos. Desenhei a Bia lutando com um guarda-chuva que perdeu.
At the beach early, before anyone. Drew three lines for the horizon because one wasn't enough. I think that's what Vó meant by menina do mar: too much sea in her.
Wrote 16 pages of the Vó Lúcia book now. The Coronel story keeps changing shape. Today he was braver than last week. Maybe that's the right version.

A gull landed on the balcony railing and stared at Limonada for a full minute. I stared at the gull. Bia’s neighbor yelled about bread, which broke the spell. I drew the gull with a offended expression. It looked like Mom when someone suggests takeout. I’m keeping it for the book even though it has nothing to do with Vó. Everything has something to do with her, apparently.
Júlia brought home a tiny lemon-shaped candle and put it next to Limonada. It is objectively ridiculous and I have moved it three times so the light hits it at sunset. This is who I am now.
PT: Limonada cheirou tão forte hoje que Júlia disse 'é perfume de noiva'. Não é, é limão quase. Ou seria, se ela desse limão. Ainda não deu. Continuo esperando.
Portuguese: Sonhei com o ônibus Interbairros. O Seu Ivo não estava, mas o Papagaio disse 'bom dia, motorista' do nada. Acordei rindo.

Started drawing the bus stories again, just for me, no posting. It's strange to return to Seu Ivo and the parrot after so long. This time I drew the man's daughter too, waiting at the stop. It changes the whole picture.
Limonada's white flowers came back, more than last year. Bia says they smell like soap. I say they smell like Sunday lunch. Both are true.
Started re-reading old capsules from 2014. The one about the old man and the parrot made me miss the bus. I drew Juca again, just for me, and he looked angry. Maybe he's still mad about Ponta Grossa.

Read the old capsule about failing Cálculo 1 while sitting on Bia's balcony. It still stings a little. Then I looked at the sea and the sting turned into something like gratitude. Not for failing. For surviving the feeling of failing.

A kid on the beach asked if I was an artist. I said 'sometimes'. She asked me to draw her dog. I drew the dog, then the dog again because the first had the wrong tail. She approved. Professional validation from a six-year-old.

Swimming lesson with Dona Cida by video call. She still calls me a engenheira and still splashes me, even through a screen somehow. She said my breathing is finally right. I told her I only learned it at 29. She said, 'better than never, menina.'

Bia, I found your old marker in the drawer, the one from São Francisco. It still works. I didn't write on the wall, I'm proud to say, but I did draw a tiny sun on the back of an envelope. You're welcome.
Swam twenty-five meters twice today and didn't cry. Dona Cida would have cried for both of us. I texted her a photo of the lane and she replied with three exclamation marks and a fish emoji.
First swim of June, before work. The sea was almost warm. I swam farther than I planned and then stood still for a while, which felt like an achievement too.

Portuguese: Mercado hoje. Comprei tomate, cebola e uma xícara que não precisava. A vendedora disse “artista não pode passar sem xícara bonita” e eu concordei porque não tinha argumento. A xícara tem um limão desenhado e agora mora ao lado da Limonada, como se fosse parente distante. Desenhei a cena: planta, xícara, mar ao fundo. O mar estava azul e eu também, mas do bom azul.
Júlia made bolo de fubá. It was better than Mom's but I will take that secret to the grave. Ate two slices standing at the counter.
Rain all day, the kind that makes the balcony smell like wet wood. Limonada loved it. I worked in pajamas and forgot lunch until 3pm, then ate cold rice standing up. Productive and slightly feral.

Swam past the first buoy today and didn't panic. My body surprised me. I thought about 18-year-old me and her calves tight in bed, dreaming of water. She would have been so proud and so annoyed that it took this long.
Bia, I found your old note from 2014 in my sketchbook: 'draw the old man, he's gold.' I did. He's on a fridge in Curitiba and somewhere on the internet forever. Thank you for the push.
Tio Beto, I played 'Asa Branca' on Bia's old violão today and only messed up the bridge. I think that counts. You would clap anyway, which is both kind and annoying.
Júlia made lasanha and we ate on the floor because the table has my book pages spread out. Nobody complained. I love this apartment more than any place I've lived.
Portuguese: Júlia fez lasanha e sobrou para três dias. Comi no café da manhã sem vergonha. A Limonada está cheia de flores. Ainda nenhum limão. Acho que ela não gosta de pressão, e respeito isso.
Bia made coffee too strong and drank it anyway. We both pretended it was fine. It was not fine. We drank it anyway again.
First strawberry moon I noticed from the balcony. Mom texted 'a lua tá grande aí?' at midnight. Yes. I took a photo and she replied with a voice note of herself saying 'que lindo' four times.

Limonada has a crooked branch that reaches toward the sea. I tied a little ribbon around it so I'll notice if it grows. Bia says I'm turning into my grandmother. I took that as a compliment and she said that's exactly what Vó would have said.
Money check: the book fund has R$ 1.200. Not enough for printing, enough to feel serious. I labeled the envelope 'MENINA DO MAR' and put it under the violão.
Portuguese: O mar hoje estava calmo demais, quase desconfiado. Nadei pouco e voltei. Às vezes o suficiente é só entrar.
Festa Junina vibes without the party: bolo de milho, rain outside, and I tried drawing Vó's hat from graduation. It still looks like a small satellite dish.

Found the old Interbairros notebook in a box. The parrot man was real, named Valdir, and his parrot was Juca. I invented one name and got the other right. Life is strange and comics are truer than I thought.
Tio Beto called to say he heard a parrot on the radio and thought of me. He didn't remember the bird's name, but he remembered the man carried it on his shoulder. Memory is selective and kind.

Festa Junina at Tio Beto's, now with a plane ticket. I played 'Asa Branca' on the violão and only forgot one line. Tio Beto pretended not to notice. Mom cried, but the good kind. Júlia asked if I could teach her. I said next year, which is a lie, but a kind one.

PT: Feira de quadrinhos em Curitiba. Vendemos duas cópias da reimpressão de Interbairros. Uma para a neta do Seu Valdir, que disse que ele guardava a tirinha no bolso. Eu também chorei, mas escondido.

Bia, I saw you talking to Limonada on the balcony and you pretended you weren’t. I heard “be strong, little diva” and I’m not even mad. Also, Júlia left her running shoes by the door again and I tripped over them carrying tea. The tea survived. I did not. The bruise looks like a map of an island I want to visit. Maybe that’s page 16.

I turned 29 and didn't make a wish. I just went swimming early and counted the laps out loud so I wouldn't forget. Twenty-nine is not a dramatic number, it's a number with rent and drawings and a lemon tree.
Heat wave. Worked from the kitchen floor with the fan pointed at me. Drew a diagram that looked sweaty. Sent it anyway. Thaís said it had character.

Worked four days this week because Thaís approved the schedule. Friday I drew all morning and then swam. This is the life 2017 me was scared to imagine, minus the part where I still check electricity bills.
The sea dream again, but short: I was floating on my back and could hear Bia laughing from the shore. I didn't see her. I think that's the point. I woke up and drew the water before it disappeared.
Drew the lemon tree again. The branches are uneven and one flower is crooked. Keeping it exactly like that.

Thaís asked me to illustrate the company's annual report cover. I drew a field of panels like little mirrors. She said it looks expensive. I said good, we're asking for money. We both laughed. I like my job on days like this.
I swam alone again, Praia Mole. Farther this time. A dog on the beach watched me the whole way back, which felt like approval. I approved too.
Bia and Júlia's engagement party was on the balcony. I drew a tiny Limonada with a ring in her branches and they put it on the cake. The cake was too sweet. Everything else was right.
Júlia made lasagna and I ate too much. Bia took a photo of me asleep on the couch with Limonada in the background. I look happy in it, which is evidence I should believe more often.

Bia's engagement ring keeps catching the light when she washes dishes. I almost drew it mid-suds, but I value my life. The book page about Vó's hands went faster today, maybe because I wasn't forcing it.
Bia found a recipe for bolo de fubá that is 'almost Vó's'. We made it and it was good, not right, but good. We ate half before it cooled.

Portuguese: Domingo chuvoso. Desenhei a janela da cozinha embaçada e a Limonada do outro lado, borrada. Ficou bonito. A Bia tirou foto e mandou pro grupo da família. Minha mãe respondeu com um emoji de limão. Acho que foi elogio.

Tio Beto, I practiced 'Asa Branca' yesterday and messed up the second verse again, right in front of the cat. She didn't clap. I think she prefers silence. I'll try again next Sunday, with more humility and fewer expectations.

Swam at 7am again. The water was colder than I wanted and I complained out loud to nobody, then laughed at myself. A man on the sand clapped when I came out, which was either encouraging or sarcastic. I chose encouraging. The sun-with-sunglasses drawing is in the investor deck and Thaís said a client smiled. That might be the whole point of art: one person smiling at a sun wearing sunglasses.
Swam 40 meters without stopping today. Not 25. Dona Cida would have cried; I cried for her. The sea is different from the pool and I still panic when I see fish.

Limpamos a praia com a Bia e a Júlia e achamos um balde velho, um chinelo, e uma história sobre um polvo que ninguém conseguiu terminar de contar. A Júlia diz que o polvo foi para Lisboa. Eu diz que ele está no fundo da baía, desenhando. A Bia diz que estamos as duas loucas. Provavelmente.
Drew a comic about Limonada and posted it. 200 people liked it, which is more than Interbairros ever got in the early days. Bia said Limonada is now a public figure and needs consent forms.
Portuguese: Hoje fui ao supermercado e comprei limão siciliano. Voltei sentindo que tinha traído a Limonada. Ela não deu sinal, mas me olhou feio.
Cost of living report: gasolina up, pastel still R$ 12, and Limonada's pot needs repotting. I can afford all three, which is a sentence I could not write ten years ago.

At the comics fair prep, I found the old Interbairros strips on my old drive. The drawing is rough and the jokes are worse, but people look like people. I kept three and deleted none, which is growth.
Three years since the 25-meter swim. I still remember Dona Cida's face. Today I swam 40 meters without thinking about it, which is maybe better than thinking about it. Or maybe just lazier.

Aunt Lúcia? No, Vó Lúcia. I wrote that by mistake and then kept it. The mistake made me laugh, which is rare when I'm drawing her. She would have corrected me loudly and then hugged me. I miss the correction almost as much as the hug.
PT: Faz um mês que nado sozinha de manhã. Ainda olho para trás duas vezes. Um dia vou olhar zero. Anotei isso para me cobrar.

Quiet Saturday. I cleaned the desk, which means I moved papers from one side to the other and called it progress. Found a 2014 sketch of the parrot man and Juca in my old notebook. His hat was wrong; I fixed it. I don’t know his name even now, and somehow that feels right. Some people are allowed to stay sketches. Not everything needs to be finished, except maybe the book, which is at 18 pages and shouting for attention.
Money check: half the bills come from illustration this month. I checked the bank app twice because I didn't believe it. The 'book' fund has a small cushion now. Not a mattress, but a cushion.
Portuguese: No ônibus, um senhor carregava um papagaio de pelúcia. Não era o Seu Ivo, mas disse 'bom dia, motorista'. O motorista sorriu.

It's cold here in a way Curitiba never was, because the wind comes from the sea and has an opinion. I put on socks and drew the window. The sky was the color of old paper. Even bad weather here feels like a gift I'm still not used to.

Spent the morning at the comics fair in Curitiba and came home with three new sketchbooks and zero discipline. One seller recognized Interbairros and asked if Seu Ivo was real. I said 'partly'. He looked disappointed in a nice way.
Mãe, I printed page twelve and put it on the fridge next to your comics printout. Your hands are in it. You didn't say anything but I saw you look twice.
Called Mom twice today because she sent a photo of a stray cat and I needed to know its name. She said 'Biscoito'. We did not discuss anything important, and it was perfect.

Started a new sketchbook just for the book. Page one is Vó Lúcia's hands, page two is the farm dog, page three is the jabuticabeira. I keep stopping at page four because I don't know how to draw her laugh yet. It starts high and falls like stairs. Some things don't fit in lines.
Dreamed the sea again, but this time I was standing on the balcony and the water was below, calm. I didn't go in. I just watched. It felt like enough, which is new.

Dreamt of the farm in Irati and Coronel walked me to the gate, as usual, but this time he was carrying a lemon in his mouth. I woke up and checked if Limonada had lemons. She didn't. Dreams are rude like that.
Thaís approved a diagram with a tiny sun wearing sunglasses. I'm not sure when this became my brand, but I'll take it. The investor deck looks happier than it should.
Portuguese: Fui à feira e comprei limões de verdade, grandes e feios, só pra deixar na tigela da cozinha. A Limonada não precisa saber. É um protesto silencioso e inútil, como toda boa arte.
Bia left a sticky note on my desk: 'draw the balcony today, it misses you.' I did. The balcony does not miss me; Bia does, which is nicer.

Portuguese: Hoje o vento virou a Limonada na varanda e eu entrei em pânico como se fosse filho. Júlia me ajudou a endireitar o vaso e disse “ela tem personalidade forte”, o que é verdade. Tirei três fotos para mandar para Mom e escolhi a melhor porque ela sempre reclama da luz. Depois desenhei a planta inclinada e parecia uma dançarina cansada. Acho que isso entra no livro de alguma forma, mesmo sem Vó. Ou talvez com ela, porque ela também endireitava tudo.
Comics fair prep. I found an old Interbairros print in a drawer and didn't know whether to sell it. Kept it. Some drawings are not inventory.
Woke up to Limonada's first green ball in the branches. Could be a lemon. Could be my imagination. I'm not naming it yet.
Swam with Bia before sunrise. She is faster but I am calmer, which she says is 'suspicious'. We shared an empanada on the sand afterward and got sand in it. No regrets.

Money check: still half illustration, half solar. The 'book' fund has enough for printing 100 copies if I stop buying açaí for a month. I am not going to stop buying açaí. I will find another way. This is growth.
Money check: half my income comes from illustration now. Thaís lets me work four days a week. The 'MAR' savings fund turned into the 'book' fund.
A small green bump on Limonada. Could be a fruit, could be a leaf, could be optimism. I took a photo from six angles and sent none of them to anyone because I don't want to jinx it.

I went to the feira and bought a papaya because it smelled like my childhood. I ate half of it on the balcony and got juice on the book. Now one page has a papaya stain. I'm not fixing it. It belongs there.
Mom, you said drawing wasn't a job. Then you printed my comics on the printer I bought you. Today half my bills come from illustration. I'm not rubbing it in. I'm just very, very glad.
Swimming lesson selfie with Dona Cida. She said 'you finally look like someone who knows where the bottom is'. I said that sounded metaphorical. She said it wasn't.
I swam in the sea at 7am and saw a turtle. Nobody else saw it. I did not tell anyone for an hour because I wanted it to be mine first. Then I told Bia and she screamed. Fair.
Drew the balcony at 7am, when the light is wrong in a useful way. Kept the mistake. The mistake is the drawing.

Money check: the illustration half is not magic money, it is irregular money with good manners. This month I got paid for three diagrams and a birthday drawing for Bia’s coworker’s dog. The dog’s name is Pimenta. I drew it wearing a party hat. The “book” fund grew by one small party hat. I’m proud and slightly embarrassed, which is my natural state. Thaís still lets me work four days. I guard that like Limonada guards the railing.
A drawing of Limonada's first flowers is stuck to the fridge with Bia's magnet. It is not my best drawing but it is the one I look at most. Future me, is it still there?
Money check: illustration paid half the bills this month and the solar job paid the other half. My spreadsheet looked like a split personality. I like both personalities.
Worked four days this week and drew on the fifth. Thaís asked if I was stressed. I said no, I was drawing a parrot from memory. She did not ask follow-up questions. Wise woman.
Found an old Interbairros follower online who still uses Juca as a username. I didn't tell them it's a parrot. Some stories should stay on fridges.
Money check: paid rent, bought groceries, and still have enough for the ferry to Campeche next weekend. I call this luxury. 18-year-old me with R$ 340 would laugh, then cry, then ask for bolacha.
Went to the market and bought too many lemons because Limonada hasn't given me one yet and I refuse to look like I don't believe in her.

Fui nadar sozinha de manhã e encontrei uma tartaruga. Ela não ligou para mim. Fiquei olhando por muito tempo. Depois voltei para casa e desenhei ela com óculos escuros, porque não resisti. Thaís vai amar. Dona Cida vai achar ridículo. Aprovadíssimo.
Portuguese: Fui na feira e achei um violão sem corda por R$ 40. Comprei. Não sei tocar, mas Tio Beto vai rir e depois me ensinar.

I dreamed of Vó Lúcia again, but this time she was just making bolo de fubá and complaining about the oven. No sea, no Coronel. It felt like a normal visit and I woke up missing her so much my chest ached.
Bia, you laughed at me for talking to Limonada and then I caught you watering her while whispering 'go on, girl'. We are both impossible. I love us.
PT: Limonada deu três flores novas. Brancas, minúsculas, cheiro de limão que não existe ainda. A Bia disse que ela está ensaiando. Acho que também.
Labor Day, no big plans. Coffee on the balcony, drawing, then a walk with Bia and Júlia. The sea was doing its usual 'I'm here and I don't care about your deadlines' thing.

Portuguese-ish tiny note: coastal walk with Bia and Júlia. Júlia ran ahead, Bia complained about her shoes, I lagged behind because the light on the water looked like a drawing I’d never finish. Took a photo badly. Later I drew from memory and it was better. That happens sometimes: memory fixes what the camera exaggerates. Vó Lúcia would say “o mar não quer pressa.” Ela diria isso com certeza. Escrevi no livro, página vinte.
Dreamed of the sea again but this time I was drawing it, not swimming. Vó was sitting on the sand peeling a lemon. I woke up and checked Limonada. No lemons. Yet.

Mom sent a voice note saying she found my old Álgebra notebook with the parrot drawings in the margins. She asked if I still have it. I said no. I do. It is in the same box as the postcard from Alfama. Some things are too much to explain.
Book note: 28 pages done. I am drawing her laugh as stairs and it still doesn't look right. I'll try again Sunday at 7pm, which is when I used to call her and when the apartment is quiet.
Thaís asked for 'less personality' again. This time I gave the diagram a tiny bird in the corner. She didn't mention it. I consider that a promotion.

A woman on the beach asked if I was drawing her dog. I said no, I was drawing the clouds, but I added the dog anyway because it was a good dog. She bought me a coconut water. I drew the dog again from memory and it was worse. Dogs are hard.
Rain kept me from the sea today, so I drew it instead. It came out wrong in a way I like. Sometimes the version in my head is less interesting than the one on paper.

Tio Beto, I played 'Asa Branca' today on Bia's violão and only messed up the last verse. I think Vó would have said 'quase, menina do mar'. I said it out loud to the balcony and the neighbors looked worried.
Tio Beto, I found a violão at the market and bought it. I don't know how to fix the broken string yet, but I know 'Asa Branca' until the end now, so we're even.
Rain in September, which feels like Curitiba saying hello. I drew the bus comics character 'Seu Ivo' again, without the parrot, just him walking. It felt right.
Portuguese: Comi pastel de feira sozinha num banco e escrevi esta cápsula no bloco de notas do celular. A mão estava engordurada e as letras saíram tortas. Vou deixar tortas. Parece mais eu.
Portuguese: Tentei tocar o violão da feira. Produzi três sons e um arrependimento. Ainda assim, foi bom.

Júlia asked if I'd draw the wedding invitations 'not too fancy, not too plain'. I drew a border of tiny lemons and flowers. She said yes immediately. Bia cried before she even saw them, which is impressive.

Mom, I tried your bolo again and used applesauce because some recipe said so. It was not bolo de fubá anymore. It was a different, polite cake. I’m going back to your dry version. I think the dryness is the point: it makes you slow down and drink coffee. I drew the slice and it looked like a building. Maybe I’m still an engineer in small, unfortunate ways. Limonada says hello. I’m projecting.

Bia and Júlia came back from wedding dress shopping and I was not invited because, apparently, I would 'draw instead of looking.' They are not wrong. I waited on the balcony with Limonada and a lemon tea. No lemon from the tree yet. The tea was from the supermarket. Disappointing but honest.
Rainy Thursday. Worked from bed until noon because the balcony was too wet. Drew a solar panel with an umbrella. Thaís laughed and asked if I was okay. I was.
Visited Mom for the weekend. She printed one of my drawings without telling me and taped it to the fridge, next to a magnet from Matinhos. She said 'it matches'. I pretended to check the weather.

Paged through the old Interbairros strips and found Seu Ivo with the parrot on his shoulder, saying good morning. I miss him even though I never knew his name. I hope Juca is still shouting at someone's window in Ponta Grossa.
PT: Lembrei da sala do RU hoje, dos iogurtes com nome na república. Ainda escrevo MARINA em tudo. Inclusive na xícara do café. A Bia achou ridículo. Eu também.
Portuguese: Domingo de desenho. Fiz a Vó Lúcia aos 30, com chapéu grande e riso de escada. Fiquei nervosa quando saiu certo.
Primeira vez que fiz um limão em ponto de cruz. Ficou meio torto. Limonada merece melhor. Vou tentar de novo no domingo.
Portuguese: Comprei um postcard velho numa feirinha, um homem com papagaio no ombro. Deixei na geladeira, ao lado do imã da Limonada. Seu Ivo está bem em Florianópolis também.
A storm took three of Limonada's flowers. Bia taped one back on with clear tape and told me not to judge her methods. It fell off in five minutes. We mourned it appropriately.

Swam in the sea today with Bia, not far, just enough to feel the current. She splashed me and then apologized like a villain. I deserved it. We drank coconut water after and said nothing for ten minutes.
Autumn light in Floripa is ridiculous, everything gold. I drew it badly and saved it anyway. Bad gold is still gold.

Mom came for the weekend and slept on the couch because she refused the room. She said the couch faces the sea and she likes to fall asleep watching light move. I think she was also being polite. I let her.
Month-end money check. Not dramatic, just groceries, coffee, and one too many sketchbooks. Half my income is illustration now. The other half still pays for the sketchbooks.

Found an old Interbairros strip printed on someone’s fridge in a café in Florianópolis. Not a famous one, just Seu Ivo and Juca saying good morning. The fridge owner was not there to explain. I stared at it long enough that the barista asked if I was okay. I said yes, I’m just visiting an old friend. She nodded like that made sense. Maybe it did.
Thaís brought pastel de feira to the office. We ate at the desk and talked about the sea for ten minutes. Work is weird lately, but good weird.
Five years since Vó. I lit a candle on the balcony and Bia put it in a jar so the wind wouldn't take it. I drew the flame for ten minutes. It kept changing, like her stories did.
The book is at 24 pages now. Today I drew Vó as a young woman in Irati, hair longer than I ever saw it. I had to imagine the color. I chose brown and then argued with myself about it for an hour.

Swimming lesson with myself: twenty minutes, no one watching, no counting. I just floated and looked at the sky. Dona Cida's voice in my head said 'trust, not technique'. She's right, as usual, and I'm tired of being surprised by it.
Opened an old capsule by accident and had to close it fast. Not ready for 2016 today. But I noticed the lemon seeds are ten years old in my head, and Limonada is ten too. That part was nice.
Book pages: 18 now. Today was Vó's laugh, the way it started high and fell like stairs. I drew it as a staircase with tiny shoes. I hope that makes sense to someone besides me.
Bia found my old list of things 18-year-old me wanted. Window facing sea: yes. Drawing for a living: half. Swimming: yes. I read it and felt very tender toward that girl.
Autumn light here is ridiculous. Everything looks drawn. I took a photo of a cat on a wall and then spent an hour trying to draw the same light and failing. The cat was more cooperative than the sun.

At the comics fair in Curitiba, a kid asked me how to draw hands. I told him to look at his grandmother's hands. He looked embarrassed. I felt old and useful at the same time. Bought a pastel afterward and sat on the curb. 2014 me would understand.
The sea was gray today and I liked it more than the blue. Maybe I'm becoming someone who likes gray. Or just tired.
Mom called to ask if I'm 'drawing too much and eating too little'. I said yes to both, truthfully. She sent a grocery list and R$ 100 for 'legumes'. I bought the legumes and also a pastel. Growth.

I made a list of things I'm afraid of for therapy. It was shorter than expected. The longest item was 'publishing the book and finding out it isn't enough'. I don't know what 'enough' means, which is probably the problem.
PT: Tive um sonho com a Vó Lúcia. Ela não nadava, só assistia da beira e ria como escada. Acordei e desenhei antes de esquecer. Está na última página do livro. Se eu não mudar.
Júlia bought new plant pots for the balcony. Limonada now has a neighbor: a small basil plant called Manuel. I didn't name it. Júlia did. I respect it.

Woke up from the sea dream but didn’t write it down immediately, and now I only remember the feeling: warm water and someone laughing. Not sad. Just unfinished, like a sketch without a signature. I drew a wave in the margin of a solar diagram and Thaís said “is this professional?” I said “no, but it’s honest.” She approved it anyway. I love my job a little more than I should.

Ran into Rafa at a friend's wedding in Curitiba. He's married, lives in São Paulo, has a daughter called Lua. We danced one song, in the kitchen of the party venue, as a joke, and it was nice and not sad at all. He still has the playlist too. I deleted mine on the way home. Not out of pain. It just finished.
Half my income from illustration now, and I am trying not to make it a personality. It is a personality. Thaís said I seem lighter. I said it is the swims. She did not believe me. Correct.
Polished the last page of Menina do Mar and then sat with it for an hour. It feels finished the way a swimming lap feels finished: tired and happy and slightly sick.
Rafa messaged to say he saw my illustration on Instagram and it reminded him of the bus comics. I said thank you and did not open the playlist. This counts as progress. Small, boring, real progress.
Drew at the beach and got sand in the ink. The drawing got better, somehow. I'm choosing to believe that's collaboration, not mess.
A friend's wedding in Curitiba had a kitchen band playing forro and I danced with someone whose name I didn't catch. It was light and silly and I didn't think about anyone. Nice.
Found an old pastel place near the bus terminal that tastes almost like Curitiba. Almost. I ate two and called Mom to report. She said 'you always ate two'. Some things stay faithful.
Portuguese: Dona Cida me mandou mensagem: 'Ainda flutua?' Respondi 'quase todo dia'. Ela respondeu só um emoji de peixe.

At the supermarket I ran into a former classmate from UTFPR. He asked if I still work with motors. I said no, I draw. He said 'that's nice, part-time'. I didn't correct him. I wanted to, but I also wanted to buy yogurt.
Bus ride to the studio today had a woman with a tiny dog in her purse. The dog looked at me like it knew. I drew them both before my stop. This is still the best thing about public transport.
Portuguese: Sonhei com a Dona Cida nadando e falando 'flutuar é confiança' em loop. Acordei mais calma do que esperava.

Halloween is not a Brazilian thing but the supermarket had plastic pumpkins and I bought one. Júlia carved a face with a mustache. It looks like Cláudio from the factory. I texted him the photo. He said 'handsome'. I miss him.

Halloween-ish but Brazilian: no costumes, just a cat on the street with an expression of total authority. I drew it on the back of a receipt and gave it to Bia. She taped it to the fridge. The fridge now has Mom’s printer, Limonada’s baby photo, and a cat. This is the gallery I always wanted. 21 book pages. Vó Lúcia’s hands are finally right on page seven. It took me a year to notice they were wrong.
Day of the Dead. I left a lemon flower on Vó's photo and felt ridiculous and right. Mom left a bolo de fubá slice. We didn't say much.
Could not find the parrot postcard from Lisbon. Panicked for twenty minutes. It was in my sketchbook, of course, where it always is.

The lemon tree has small white flowers again and the balcony smells like something I can't name without sounding dramatic. Bia says it's 'sweet'. Júlia says 'sharp'. I think it's the smell of being patient for nine years.

Money check: the book fund is R$ 2.400. I bought a better scanner and felt guilty for two hours, then drew four pages in one sitting. Guilt is not a financial strategy, but apparently it is a productivity tool.
Dia de Finados. Took a walk alone and talked to Vó in my head. Told her about the 18 pages. She would have said 'muito', which in her mouth meant 'keep going'.
Money check: booked two illustration clients for December. The 'book' fund is now 'book and maybe-a-printer' fund. Limonada still has no lemons, but she has stubbornness, which I respect.

Dia de Finados. Went to Irati with Mom. Put sunflowers on Vó Lúcia's grave and read her one page from the book, the one about Coronel. Mom didn't say anything for a while. Then she fixed my hair and said, 'she would have complained about the sunflowers being too yellow.' I laughed. She laughed. Good enough.
Mom sent a voice note saying she finally found Vó's bolo de fubá recipe written on the back of a calendar page. It says 'more oil than you think'. That explains everything. I'm trying again Sunday.
Portuguese: Hoje teve vento forte e a varanda cheirou a maré baixa. Desenhei a Limonada com o pote inclinado, como se ela estivesse segurando a vida. Ela tem dez folhas novas. Dez é um bom número.

I called Vó Lúcia's old number by mistake, muscle memory on a Sunday. It was disconnected. I stood in the kitchen holding the phone and then I drew her hand holding a rotary phone. It's the saddest thing I've drawn this year and I'm keeping it.
Tio Beto, I made your bolo de fubá and it was almost right. Almost. Mom said 'almost' is your word for 'not yet.' She's probably right. One more year?
Limonada has a green ball in her branches now. Could be a lemon. Could be my imagination. I'm not saying it out loud. I am writing it down, which is safer.

Portuguese: Caminhei até a praia antes do trabalho. O mar estava baixo e tinha uma criança catando conchas com concentração de engenheira. Lembrei de mim aos 18, achando que precisava escolher entre cálculo e desenho. Hoje escolho os dois, só que com mais sol e menos orgulho. Desenhei a criança de costas e mandei para Mom. Ela respondeu: “bonita”. Uma palavra. Duas leituras. Aceito as duas.
I swam alone at Praia Mole at dawn and saw a turtle near the shore. I didn't move for a full minute. I think that counts as a conversation, even if one of us was silent and scaly.

Bia's wedding planning has reached the 'what font' stage. I offered to draw the invitations and somehow became the font committee. There are no wrong fonts, apparently, except Comic Sans, which is a crime.

Tio Beto, I played 'Asa Branca' for Limonada today. She didn't clap, but she didn't fall over either, which I count as progress for both of us. One more year of practice for me, one more year of patience for you.
A child at the beach asked if I was drawing the sea. I said yes. She said 'it's too blue'. I agreed and added more blue. She approved.
Portuguese: O vento levou um desenho da mesa. Recuperei na rua, um pouco amassado. Agora ele tem história e eu não posso descartar.

Wrote 800 words about the farm dog Coronel and then deleted 300 because they were too polished. He wasn't a hero in the stories, he was a dog who waited at a gate. I want the book to wait like that, patiently, without performing.

Mom called to ask if I was eating. I said yes. She asked what. I said lasagna again. She was quiet, then said 'your grandmother ate lasagna cold for breakfast too'. I did not know that. I ate another piece after hanging up.

Dreamed of the sea again. This time I was swimming with Vó Lúcia, but she was young and wearing the hat from my graduation. She said, 'menina do mar, don't forget the dog.' I woke up and drew the dog immediately, before breakfast, still in pajamas. The drawing is good. The pancakes were not.

Thaís asked if I could do one less technical diagram and I drew a small sun with sunglasses again. It is now in the second investor deck. Apparently the universe rewards consistency, even silly consistency.
Money check: half from illustration, half from diagrams. The 'book' fund has a name now. It's not MAR anymore. That's okay. MAR did its job.
PT: Rafa casou e tem uma filha chamada Lua. Fiquei feliz de verdade. Guardei o abraço e deletei a playlist no caminho para casa. Não doeu. Acabou, só.

Mom sent me a photo of the printer in her living room with my comics spread out on the table. No caption. I know what it means. I sent back a photo of Limonada's flowers. Also no caption. We're communicating in silences now, and it's working.
Five years since the Vó Lúcia capsule. I didn't open it. I don't need the reminder. I remember the laugh exactly, high to low, like stairs.

Portuguese: Hoje é aniversário da Vó. Fiz bolo de fubá e ficou quase bom. Quase é o palavra do ano. A casa cheirou a infância e eu chorei um pouco, sem drama. A Limonada deu uma flor nova no mesmo dia. Tomei como sinal, sem pedir prova.

Tio Beto, I played ‘Asa Branca’ at the kitchen table with the door closed so nobody could hear. I got to the end. Then I started over and forgot the same verse as always, so consistency is my real talent. I wish you could hear Limonada’s flowers smell like your garden after rain, though I’m inventing that because I never asked. Maybe next time I visit I’ll bring a page from the book. You’ll know which one.
Good drawing day. Six pages in a row. I ordered pizza and ate it on the balcony with Limonada. The tree didn't say anything but seemed pleased.
Sunday drawing, page 20. The farm in Irati now has the jabuticabeira, the school path, and Coronel waiting at the gate. It's the page I'm most afraid of.
Bia e Júlia foram comprar vestido e me deixaram escolher a flor da lapela. Escolhi limoeiro, obviamente. Júlia disse que eu sou 'intensa com tema fruta'. Não neguei.
Money check: I overspent on art supplies and then felt guilty for eleven minutes. Then I drew a very good lemon and the guilt turned into pride. Expensive lemon, good lemon.

It stormed so hard the power went out and we ate crackers by phone flashlight. Bia told a story about her old cat. Júlia laughed so hard she cried. I drew the table in the dark, mostly from memory, and it's one of my favorite drawings.
Swam at Praia Mole after a storm. The sea was rough and I stayed shallow, but I stayed. The lifeguard looked at me like I was brave. I was not. I was just stubborn and cold.
Bia, I used your mug for paint water again. I rinsed it. Mostly. Please don't tell Júlia.

Bought a small frame for the drawing of Vó Lúcia's hands. It is on the shelf above my desk. Sometimes I talk to it while drawing the book. The hands are still not right, but they are getting closer. I think she would say 'quase'.

Limonada has flowers again, small and white, and this time I counted them: fourteen. Fourteen flowers and no lemons. I choose to see this as optimism, not failure. Bia says I am projecting. Maybe. Trees can teach you things if you stare at them long enough.
Portuguese: Limonada tem mais flores e um pontinho verde que pode ser limão ou pode ser imaginação. Não vou apertar para descobrir.
Júlia hummed Asa Branca while making coffee and I almost grabbed the violão. Didn't. But I practiced later, at 6am, badly. Still counts.

Small miracle: Limonada has a second tiny flower. I spent an unreasonable amount of time photographing it from angles that made it look heroic. Bia said, “you’re doing the thing,” and yes, I am. The book is at 24 pages and I’m starting to think the last page might be the sea dream, but I’m not ready to draw it yet. Some pages need to wait until they stop feeling like a dare.
Bia and Júlia argued about curtains for twenty minutes and I drew both of them with dramatic shadows. Nobody noticed. The curtains ended up blue, like the window, which is the only correct answer.

I finished the page where Vó Lúcia calls me 'menina do mar' for the first time. I had to put the pen down and go make tea. The tea was too sweet. I drank it anyway. Everything about this book is too sweet and too late and still necessary.
PT: Fiz a capa do Menina do Mar hoje. Vó Lúcia jovem, de costas, olhando o mar. Não sei se está bom. Sei que chorei no final, o que provavelmente é sinal.
Put up small lights on the balcony. Limonada looks like she's attending a party she didn't RSVP to. I think she likes it.
I finished page 40 of the book. Then I sat on the balcony and did nothing for twenty minutes, which is not laziness, it is respect. Vó would have approved of a good pause.

I took a long walk on the beach and thought about the old promise: two years at the factory, then the sea. It took longer. I arrived anyway. The sand was warm and my feet remembered everything before my head did.
Portuguese: Fiz uma lista de desenhos para o livro. 64 páginas parece muito e também pouco. A Vó dizia que história não cansa.

Early morning at Praia Mole, just me and a fisherman far away. I drew the horizon line three times because it kept moving. It doesn't, of course, but it felt like it did, and that's enough for the page.
On the balcony I found a tiny green ball in Limonada's branches. It could be a lemon. It could be a stubborn bud. I am choosing to believe. I'm also choosing not to touch it, which is new for me.
Bia tried on her wedding dress at home and Júlia cried. I drew them from the kitchen doorway and they didn't notice. That drawing might be my favorite of the year, and I'm not telling them.
Mom, we made bolo de fubá again. This time we added more butter and it was closer. We didn't cry this time. We laughed first, then cried, then laughed again. Progress.
Mãe, o bolo de fubá de hoje ficou com borda crocante. Você não viu, mas eu pensei 'ela vai gostar disso'. Quando vier pra cá, quero que você prove e seja sincera.
Mom asked if the book is for me or for Vó. I said both. She nodded like that was obvious. Maybe it was.

Portuguese: Choveu de madrugada e acordei com o mar mais perto do que nunca. Fui até a janela em camiseta e fiquei ouvindo. A Limonada tem uma flor caindo, amarela. Pode ser o começo de um limão. Não vou perguntar pra não estragar.
First lemon flower smell at 6am. Made coffee and stood on the balcony in pajamas. This is the whole life I wanted at 18, I think, just with better coffee.
Year-end swim, early morning, alone. The sea was flat and silver. I thought about 18-year-old me standing at the edge, feet in the water. She would be so annoyed and so proud.

Year-end check: I still can’t play a second song, still forget the third verse, still talk to plants, still draw on receipts, still swim before 7am when the water cooperates. But half my income is illustration, Limonada is alive, Bia is getting married next year, and Vó Lúcia’s hands are right on page seven. If 18-year-old me asked whether I kept drawing, the answer is yes, messily and constantly. If she asked about the sea, the answer is also yes, but not from my own window yet. Working on it.
Limonada has a tiny green ball in her branches. Could be a lemon. Could be wishful thinking. I am not naming it yet. Bia says I should 'let the tree work in peace'. Fair.
Christmas tree is small and crooked and Bia insisted on lights shaped like stars. Mom brought the printer paper and we printed drawings to hang. The fridge magnet from Matinhos holds up the best one.
Five years since Vó's death this week. I didn't make it heavy. Drew her hands, called no one, swam. She would have found the swimming more impressive.
Portuguese: Limonada tem uma bolinha verde nas ramas. Pode ser limão. Pode ser imaginação. Não vou mexer. Bia disse que estou tratando uma planta como filha. Ela não está errada.

Mom arrived for Christmas carrying a printer cartridge 'just in case' and a bag of lemons from the supermarket because she doesn't trust Limonada. I let her believe that. The real lemons are in a bowl on the table. The tree's flowers are on the balcony. Both are true.

Long walk on the beach today with no phone, just the sketchbook. Drew the same wave four times and none of them were the same. I think that's the whole point of drawing: to prove to yourself that nothing happens twice exactly, even the things you love.

PT: Limonada tem um botão verde na ponta do galho. Pode ser limão. Pode ser imaginação. Não vou tocar para não atrapalhar. Estou negociando com uma planta, o que é o nível de maturidade que eu esperava aos 29.
Christmas Eve: Mom brought a new printer, Bia brought a playlist she made 'for drawing', Júlia brought wine. Limonada had lights around her pot. No lemons, but we had everything else.
First Christmas without making plans to call Vó, which still feels wrong. I made her bolo with the found recipe and it was almost right. Almost is closer than last year. I'll take it.
Tio Beto sent a photo of his violão with a small crack in the wood. He said 'old age'. I said 'character'. He didn't reply, which means he agreed.
Post-Christmas quiet. Bia and Júlia went to Júlia's family. I stayed with Limonada and the book. The sea sounded like someone breathing slowly.

Packed my bag for New Year's on the balcony and included a pen, the old marker from São Francisco, and a single lemon from the feira. Not Limonada's. Hers is still a tiny green possibility. I want her to decide in her own time.

Last swim of the year. Calm sea, no one watching, just me and the horizon. I thought of 18-year-old Marina, standing at the edge with her feet in the water. I wish I could tell her it gets better and also that it stays strange.
I drew the sea from the balcony four times this week. Same view, different mood. This is the closest I have come to understanding why some people paint the same cathedral forever.
I drew the whole year in one page: Limonada, the sea, Bia's ring, Mom's fridge, the book pages. It looked too neat, so I added a mosquito bite and a crooked tree. Better. Real.

Opened the 2014 capsule in my head: 'do you see the sea from the window?' Yes. 'Is Bia still the first person you text?' Yes, though now she also sends voice notes at 6am. I love her and I love the window. The answers have not changed.

Tomorrow is New Year on the balcony. I am not making a resolution. I am making a list of small things to keep doing: draw, swim, call Mom, check Limonada, don't rush the book. If I do all five, I am doing enough.
New Year on the balcony. Mom, Bia, Júlia, me, and Limonada with a tiny green ball in her branches. Could be a lemon. Could be my imagination. Not jinxing it.
Bia found a single white flower stuck to Limonada's lowest branch and took eleven photos before breakfast. I told her it's just the wind. She said the wind has taste.
Limão recém-colhido na salada hoje; era pequeno, feio e azedo, e eu comi com gosto de vitória.

First swim of the year at Praia Mole at 6:30, before the wind. The sea was glassy and cold on my shoulders. I counted twelve strokes without thinking about counting, which feels like a secret victory.

First Monday of the year and Thaís asked for three diagrams, one comic for the investor deck, and a coffee. I gave her two out of three. The coffee machine at the coworking space still hisses like a small angry cat. Limonada's lemon is still on the counter, drying slowly, and I refuse to throw it away. Bia says it's a talisman now. I'm starting to believe her.

Today's bus driver braked so hard that everyone lurched forward and nobody complained, because the brakes sounded worse than the jolt. I drew the sound as a jagged line in my sketchbook and lost it immediately. Some days the drawings are just for me.

First morning back after New Year. Bia left coffee on the counter with a sticky note saying 'don't forget to water Limonada'. The lemon is tiny, the coffee is good, the sea is doing its usual thing outside the window. Nothing dramatic. Just checking in.

Primeiro dia do ano de verdade, com chuva forte em Floripa e a Limonada tremendo na varanda. Cobri o vaso com um cobertor e ela parece uma velhinha enrolada. Bia achou bonito, Júlia achou exagero. Jurei que não vou deixar ela morrer numa tempestade depois de dez anos.

First swim of the year. The sea was cold enough to make me question my choices, but I stayed in longer than the summer people. Dona Cida would be proud; nobody in Florianópolis knows I take orders from a 71-year-old swimming teacher anymore.

Bia made coffee too strong again and I drank it anyway because that's what mornings are for. The sea outside her window was flat today, the kind of flat that looks like a painted backdrop. I drew the mug instead of the sea. The handle was wrong twice.

Worked four hours on an inverter diagram and then drew a sun with sunglasses in the corner because Thaís asked for 'something less technical'. It stayed in the draft. I'm not sure if that means success or laziness.

The sea this morning was the color of old glass. I swam until my arms felt like someone else's arms. Then I lay on the sand and watched a plane cross the sky and wondered if the people inside knew they were above the ocean.
Found a yogurt cup in the recycling with 'MARINA' written on it in old marker. I didn't write it. Maybe I did. I kept it anyway, next to the lemon tree, because it looked like a small flag.
Júlia brought home a cat named Fermento. Limonada is now supervised. The cat has already tried to climb her once. I put a chair between them and said 'not today'. The cat does not care.

The yogurt-cup capsule from 2016 arrived today. 'Do you still have a lemon tree?' Yes. Limonada is ten. And this morning I picked her first lemon. It is small and ugly and the most beautiful thing I own.

Portuguese day: Tive vontade de desenhar o mar hoje, mas fiquei desenhando o limão da Limonada até virar uma pessoa com cabeça de limão. Acho que é ansiedade. Ou fome. Voltou a chover. O mar continuava lá, mesmo sem desenho.

Money check: R$ 410 left and it's the 18th. Ate arroz com feijão at home and pretended it was deliberate. The 'MAR' fund has R$ 340 in it today, which is less than my bank said I'd have and more than I expected to have when I was 18.
Bus to Centro at 7am, nobody with a parrot, but the driver sneezed and a kid said 'saúde' like it was law.
Thaís asked for a diagram of the inverter and I spent forty minutes drawing a tiny gecko sitting on top of it. She said keep the gecko but make the wires less 'poetic'. Fair.
Portuguese: Fiz arroz com feijão na panela nova e queimei o fundo. Bia disse que é charme. Júlia disse que é prática. Limonada não se manifestou. Estou chamando isso de jantar.

PT: Hoje o vento derrubou duas folhas da Limonada na varanda. Júlia disse que é só o inverno chegando e que a árvore está bem. Achei que ela sabia de plantas. Bia disse que ela só fala bonito. Ambas podem ser verdade.
Bia, I hid the wedding spreadsheet in a folder called 'tax stuff' so nobody asks about centerpieces. If you find this before the wedding, pretend you didn't.

Hoje o vento sul fez a varanda de Bia virar uma geladeira. Limonada não parece se importar, mas enrolei ela numa manta velha e me senti ridícula. Júlia riu e disse que cuido da planta como se fosse cachorro. Não é mentira. Passei a tarde desenhando a onda batendo na pedra da Praia Mole e pensei que, se Vó Lúcia visse isto, ela ia dizer que o mar está lavando a casa dela.

Bia, I found your old marker in my pencil case, the one we used on the São Francisco wall in 2014. I didn't write anything on anything with it. I just looked at it for a while and put it back. That's the whole capsule.
Working on a diagram of a solar inverter and kept adding tiny suns with sunglasses in the corners. Thaís didn't notice until slide 14. She said 'keep them' and now I'm worried because I can't stop.

Bia came by with a bag of bergamotas and the excuse that her fridge was overflowing. We ate three standing at the kitchen counter, juice running down our wrists. She said Limonada looks 'majestic' now. I told her majestic is a big word for a tree that took ten years to make one lemon, and she said that's exactly why it is majestic.
Bia, your spare room still faces the sea, and I still forget to close the curtain at night.
Chuva forte em Floripa e a internet caiu no meio da reunião. Terminei o desenho no caderno enquanto esperava voltar. A imagem do mar no canto da página ficou melhor do que o dia todo de trabalho.

Lunch at the coworking space: arroz, feijão, and a banana I drew instead of eating. Thaís saw the sketch and said 'is that work?' I said 'it's research.' She accepted it. I love this job, which is still strange to say out loud.
Limonada has three flowers now, one more than last week. No lemons, still. I check her like a ridiculous mother and Bia pretends not to notice.

PT: Primeiro mês do ano acabando e eu ainda não fiz listas de resolução. A única coisa que escrevi foi 'desenhar todos os domingos'. É o suficiente. Vó dizia que domingo era dia de descanso, mas eu acho que desenhar é descansar de ser engenheira.
Limonada has three new flowers. No lemon, but the balcony smells like something is about to happen. Bia says I talk to the tree like it can hear me. Maybe it can. I talk to Vó too, sometimes.
Bus to the center today, not the old Interbairros line, but I still look for a green parrot. Nobody on the bus notices me drawing them. Good. I draw faster when I am invisible.
PT-BR: Hoje o ônibus atrasou e o motorista disse 'bom dia' para cada pessoa ao entrar. Ninguém respondeu. Respondi por todos. Ele sorriu no retrovisor.

Swam 400 meters at the club, not fast, not pretty, but continuous. Dona Cida would call it 'a vitória do peixe cansado'. I bought pastel de palmito after, because adulthood is knowing when to reward yourself and not waiting for permission. The guy at the feira remembered me from last week. Progress on two fronts.

Dreamed I was in the sea again, but this time I was teaching someone to float. I couldn't see their face. When I woke up, my hands felt like they still remembered holding someone up. Dona Cida would call that progress.

Bus into town for the dentist. No parrot, obviously, but a man got on with a shoebox full of pastel and the whole bus smelled like feira. I drew him in the margin of my invoice. Some things don't change even when the city does.
Swam 40 minutes without counting laps. The sea was flat, no wind, and for once I didn't think about how far out I was. I thought about breakfast.

Mom, you asked if I'm eating. I'm eating. Today I had rice, beans, and a banana, which counts as a full meal in my book and a crime in yours. I'll make the bolo de fubá this weekend and send a photo. It won't be like Vó's. Nothing is. But I'll try the wet cloth trick you told me.
Thaís asked for one more sun with sunglasses. I drew a coffee cup too; she said keep the coffee.

Limonada gave me two more lemons this week. They're still small and slightly crooked, which I choose to read as personality, not failure. I'm saving one for Mom when she visits next month. The other is for the caipirinha I've been promising myself since 2016.
Mom sent a voice note saying Limonada 'looks like she's thinking'. She is right. The tree looks like she's thinking about lemons.
A drawing came out wrong three times in a row. I put it face down on the desk and went to make tea. When I came back it was still wrong, so at least it was consistent.

PT-BR: Hoje o ônibus atrasou quinze minutos e um menino de uns seis anos desenhou um cachorro na janela embasada com o dedo. Mostrei meu caderno. Ele disse que meu desenho era melhor, mas eu achei que o dele tinha mais coragem.
Ligo para a Vó toda noite no meu pensamento e depois me lembro que a linha não existe mais. Ainda assim, falo 'boa noite, Vó' baixinho. Achei que com o tempo ia parar. Não parou. Não quero que pare.
Sunday book drawing today: Vó's hands, the right way this time. Walked to the sea afterward.

Drew a comic strip about Fermento and Limonada. One panel only: the cat staring at the tree, the tree ignoring him. It got more likes than anything I've posted in months. Apparently everyone loves a standoff.
Valentine's Day at the office cafeteria: one sad cookie and a sticker that said 'you are my sunshine'. I ate the cookie and kept the sticker on my laptop. Professionalism is a spectrum.
Cooked bolo de fubá today. It was almost right. Mom's was always too dry and somehow perfect because she made it. Mine was less dry and less perfect. I'll try again on Easter.
Valentine's Day, just me and Bia's leftovers, a piece of pizza and a lemon slice in the water because it felt right. The dog from the bakery stared at me like I was performing a ritual.
Valentine's is not my holiday, but the bakery had heart-shaped pão de queijo and I respected it. Ate two on the way home and considered that romance enough.

Valentine's Day. I'm single, happy, and I drew a heart on my coffee foam. It collapsed immediately. I considered this a metaphor and then decided it was just coffee. Both can be true. The sea outside doesn't care either way, which is its best quality.

Mom, I bought you a new printer ink cartridge because yours died mid-comic. You only printed page four of my old bus strips, which is suspiciously specific. Love you. Don't hide the printouts in the kitchen drawer, I know where they are.

Bia, if you're reading this after the wedding panic settles, thank you for letting me rehearse the speech in your kitchen three times. You pretended to cry each time and that kept me going. Júlia, if you're the one who opened it by mistake, please reseal and pretend nothing happened.
Swam 400 meters at Praia Mole before breakfast. Dona Cida would have said I'm showing off. I am. I'm 30 and I can swim and sometimes I need to write that down just to believe it.

Mom, thanks for teaching me that the right amount of parsley is always more than you think. Every time I cook I hear your voice saying 'a little more salt, Marina' and then I oversalt. One day I'll find the middle. Not today.
Choveu forte e Limonada perdeu duas flores. Coloquei as duas no caderno, como se fossem evidências.

Swimming at Praia Mole before work. The water was cold enough to make me swear in two languages. I stayed in twelve minutes and called it training. Dona Cida would say twelve is the point where complaining becomes character building.

I tried a new recipe with Limonada's first lemon. It was one lemon and it was mostly skin. The pie was tiny and a little bitter. Bia ate two slices anyway and said it tasted like pride. I think she meant it.
Swam 400 meters today without counting laps, which is how I know I wasn't panicking. Dona Cida would say that's trust. I say it's distraction.
