Made bolo de fubá from Vó Lúcia's recipe today. It was closer than Christmas. I put it next to Limonada on the balcony and ate a slice talking to her like a sane person.

Portuguese day: A Bia me mandou mensagem dizendo que sonhou com a Vó Lúcia ontem. No sonho, a Vó estava regando uma planta e disse 'menina do mar, não esquece de regar a sua'. Acordei e reguei a Limonada antes de tomar café.
Mom, I bought a printer for your birthday but I think you'll use it to print my drawings again.
A man on the bus had a small dog in a backpack with its head sticking out. Nobody reacted except me. I drew it on a napkin. Bia said it looked like Juca if Juca had been a dog. She's not wrong.
Mom, if you read this in 2029: yes, I still eat lunch at odd hours. No, I have not become a 'real engineer'. But I sleep better, and the drawings pay rent. That's the deal.
Mom, if you're reading this and I never said it properly: thank you for the printed comics you kept pretending not to like. They're in a folder labeled 'work'. I know.

Opened the capsule from March 2021 today, the one about the therapist asking what I'd do if I weren't afraid. I do both now. Not perfectly: the drawings pay half the bills and the sea is Bia's window, not mine. But I'm not afraid of the answer anymore. Next fear to look at: whether I'm brave enough to publish the book.
The bus to downtown still has that one seat with the broken window and I sat there on purpose. The driver had a parrot sticker on the dashboard. Almost cried. Didn't. Mostly.

Cold snap in Floripa, which Bia says isn't real but I'm wearing two socks. Limonada's flowers bent a little; I moved her closer to the wall. She survived a frost in 2017 and a person in 2026. She's tougher than both of us.
Rain all day, so I drew Vó Lúcia's hands again, the ones Mom said I got right. They're still hard. One finger always ends up crooked and I leave it.
Dream: I was walking through the farm in Irati and Coronel was there, old and grey, waiting by the gate. No sea, no water. Just grass and his tail. Woke up peaceful.
Swam only ten minutes before work, but Dona Cida's postcard on the fridge watched me go.
Thaís asked for a diagram of a battery rack and I drew a tiny sun with sunglasses in the corner again. She didn't remove it this time. Progress, or exhaustion. Either works.

Thaís asked for a diagram with 'a sun that doesn't look like it's judging anyone'. I drew it smiling sideways, like it's trying to be polite. It's in the new deck. Sometimes I can't believe my job is this.

Bia, your wedding invitations are done. I drew the lemon tree on the corner because it felt like it belonged there. If you hate it, I'll redo them, but I think you won't. You never hate things I draw, even when you should.

Rained all day in Floripa and the power flickered twice. Worked from bed with Limonada watching me like a tiny lemon tree judge. Drew a page of 'Menina do Mar' that turned out too sad, so I walked to the padaria and ate a pão de queijo standing up. Sometimes the fix is simple and warm and costs R$ 4,50.
Desenhei um gato cinza que apareceu na varanda. Ele não assinou contrato.
Portuguese: Domingo, 7 da manhã, hora de desenhar Vó Lúcia. Hoje ela tem chapéu grande demais, como na formatura. A mão ainda é difícil. Toda vez é difícil, de um jeito diferente.
Mãe, se você ler isso, eu não achei o bolo de fubá seco, eu achei 'com personalidade'. Guardei a receita da vó no mesmo caderno dos desenhos. Prometo tentar no domingo.

Portuguese day: Tio Beto me mandou um áudio de três segundos, só o violão tocando 'Asa Branca' até a segunda estrofe. Respondi com um áudio tocando até o fim, tentando. Ele respondeu só com 'kkk'. Entendi como aprovação.

Thaís asked me to mentor the new intern, who is 19 and terrified. I told her being good at something you don't love is a trap, and then realized I was quoting my 2017 self. She asked if I was okay. I said yes, and meant it this time.
Money check: illustration is half my income. The 'book' fund has R$ 4.200. I'm not spending it on anything except paper and those expensive pens I pretend are unnecessary.

Bia and Júlia are arguing about curtain colors. I am Switzerland, drawing in my room, pretending to work. This is the best use of my architecture-adjacent degree: staying out of domestic disputes while looking productive.
Money check: R$ 4.200 this month, R$ 2.100 from illustration. The book fund has R$ 3.800 and I haven't spent any of it on pastries, which deserves a medal.
Thaís asked for a less technical diagram again. I drew a tiny sun with sunglasses again. It is now on a mug, not just in the investor deck. Capitalism is strange and sometimes wears sunglasses.
A sketch I made of Bia's balcony lemon tree got 1.200 likes. Nobody asked if it was technical. I think this is what peace feels like, or at least a smaller version of it.
Money check: rent, groceries, one pastel from the bakery, and R$ 40 left for the week. Progress.

Read the old capsule from 2016 about the bus comics. The account still exists, barely, with 400 followers and one very loyal stranger. I thought about deleting it and didn't. Some unfinished things are just resting.
Mom, the bolo de fubá came out right this time. I used Vó's recipe and didn't rush. I ate two slices and called you, but you were in the market. Consider this the call, in capsule form. It was right.

Went swimming at 6:30 before work. The sea was flat and cold and I kept going longer than usual because the water felt like permission. Came back to the apartment with salt in my hair and did not shower before the meeting. Nobody mentioned it. Progress.

Thaís asked if I could 'draw something less technical' one more time. I drew a motor with sunglasses. She put it in the client presentation. Nobody said anything about the sunglasses, which is somehow better than praise.

It rained all afternoon and the balcony smelled like wet wood. I opened the window for Limonada, because she likes drama, and drew the rain hitting the sea. The drawing was better than the rain, which is rare.

Tio Beto, I practiced 'Asa Branca' on Thursday night and messed up the second verse again. The neighbors didn't complain, which either means they like it or they've given up. I'll bring the violão to the wedding and you can tune it, because I still don't know how.
Bus in Florianópolis, not Interbairros, but there was an old man with a canary in a little cage. Nobody reacted. I drew him in the margin of my solar diagram and felt 18 again.
Limonada has three tiny lemons now. None edible. All precious.

PT-BR: Chuva fina o dia inteiro. Trabalhei quatro horas de pijama, desenhei duas páginas do livro na pausa do café e fui tomar um banho de mar às 17h porque o céu abriu. O mar estava morno. Fiquei com sal no cabelo até de noite.

April Fool's Day. Thaís sent a fake email saying the solar startup was switching to a font called 'Comic Sans Forever'. I almost believed it for three seconds. The sun with sunglasses from 2023 is still in the investor deck, I checked.
It rained so hard the balcony drain flooded and Limonada's pot sat in a puddle for two hours. She looks unbothered, which is more emotional stability than I have.

Mãe, hoje te liguei só para dizer que a impressora nova funciona e que imprimi uma página do livro. Você disse 'não está torto não?' e eu entendi o elogio. Guardo este capsule para um dia em que eu sentir falta de ser entendida pela metade.
Bia, Júlia ate the whole bolo de fubá and said it was perfect. Mom would be suspicious.
A limonada da Limonada deu seis flores pequenas hoje. Ainda não é limão, mas Bia disse que 'conta como vitória parcial'. Fiz bolo de fubá para comemorar e ele não ficou seco como o da mãe.
Opened the 2014 capsule about moving into the república. The drawing is still above my bed, just now it's in Bia's spare room and the bed is closer to the sea. Yes, future me. It's still there.
Worked four days this week, as planned. The fifth day became drawing day, except I spent half of it cleaning the desk, which I am counting as part of the creative process.

PT: Choveu a tarde inteira e a varanda virou um pequeno lago. Limonada parece uma rainha desabrigada. Fiquei desenhando a chuva caindo no telhado da casa vizinha, que tem uma telha solta e faz barulho de castanholas. Curitiba também chovia assim, mas aqui o mar fica cinza-azul.

Drew the bus this morning from memory: Interbairros II, seven a.m., the window seat with the crack. No parrot man anymore, but the drawing still feels like him. I think some characters outlive the people they're based on and that's allowed.
Swam 400 meters today at Praia Mole in calm water. Not fast. Not pretty. But I didn't panic, and that was the whole fight in 2014, wasn't it? The fight was never with the water.

Drove to Vó Lúcia's grave in Irati alone, with the lemon tree in the back seat because Limonada fits there now. I read her one page of the book. The wind took the page. I took it back. She would have laughed at that.
Dreamed of the sea again, but this time I was on a bus that drove straight into it. The driver said 'bom dia, motorista' and I woke up laughing.

Tio Beto, I practiced 'Asa Branca' this afternoon and got through all three verses but the bridge still sounds like a question mark. Next Festa Junina, I'm bringing the violão. Save me a spot near the caipira.

Portuguese day: Hoje o mar estava tão calmo que parecia pintura. Nadei devagar, sem ninguém, e lembrei dos pés parados na beira quando eu tinha 14. Eles não estão mais parados. Ainda estranho quando algo velho muda por dentro.
Noite de domingo, desenho de Interbairros por nostalgia: um ônibus atrasado e um cachorro esperando.

Dreamed of the república in Curitiba again. Four girls, one bathroom, names on yogurt. Nobody was angry, everyone was just washing cups. Woke up wanting to text them and then remembered it's 2026 and I'm 30 and the fridge is only mine.

I dreamed about the farm in Irati. The jabuticabeira was full and Coronel was under it, but older, gray muzzle, sleeping. Nobody spoke in the dream. When I woke up I drew it from memory and it looked like Vó's hands.
Found an old pastel de feira wrapper in my bag from Curitiba and didn't throw it away. Kept it in the book fund jar. Financial planning is storytelling.
Tio Beto, toquei Asa Branca ontem para a Bia e quase cheguei ao fim sem errar.
Bia, when you read this I hope the apartment still smells like coffee and Júlia's shoes are still in the wrong place. Thank you for letting the sea be the first thing I see every morning.

Bia, I found your old marker from 2014 in the kitchen drawer, the one that wrote our names on the bar wall in São Francisco. It still writes. I didn't use it. It felt like opening a time capsule inside a time capsule. We're nesting capsules now. Very responsible.
Bia left a note on my desk: 'draw something today, even if it's ugly'. I drew her coffee mug. It is ugly. But I drew it, and that's the deal.

Bus from downtown to the island in the rain. A man carried a small dog in a backpack and the dog had a raincoat. Nobody reacted except me, so I drew them in the margin of my notebook and felt 22 again. The drawing is bad. The feeling is good.
Mom, I showed you the drawings of Vó's stories again and you went quiet in the same place you always go quiet. You said 'her hands'. I think that is enough for both of us. Thank you for saying it.
Bia tried to teach Júlia to float in the condo pool. Júlia lasted two seconds and then argued with the water. I timed it. Love is patient, apparently, and also hilarious.
Met a dog named Coronel at the park and laughed until my face hurt.
Tio Beto called to ask if I 'still have the hands for Asa Branca'. I played it over the phone, badly, and he said the timing was wrong. He's right. I'll practice.
Bia, if you read this, the seating chart is fine. We are not assigning 'the table with the most drama'. That is not a real category. Stop inventing it.
Bia and Júlia adopted a second cat, Pão de Queijo. The balcony now has two cats, one lemon tree, and zero peace. Limonada has started producing more leaves, possibly out of spite.

PT: Tio Beto ligou para dizer que as goiabas da árvore do fundo estão maduras. Ele mandou uma caixa pelo correio. Chegaram amassadas e perfeitas. Comi três em pé na cozinha e liguei pra ele contar. Ele disse 'menina, você sempre comeu goiaba como se fosse a última'. Tem razão.
Portuguese: Limonada deu outra flor, menor que a primeira, quase invisível. Sei que é bobagem, mas fiquei orgulhosa como se fosse filha.

Money check: the book fund has enough for printing one more test copy. The 'MAR' fund is still in the app, empty, stubborn. I like that it's still there. Some names are worth keeping even when the number is zero.
Dia do Trabalho, trabalhei das 8 às 9 desenhando e depois dormi até o meio-dia. Luxo.
PT-BR: Dona Cida mandou um cartão dizendo que a piscina do clube trocou o horário das aulas de adultos para 6h. Ela escreveu 'a engenheira vai chegar atrasada, como sempre'. Mandei flores para ela.

The book is at page 52. I drew Vó Lúcia's hands holding a bolo de fubá and had to stop for a walk. The walk turned into a swim. The swim turned into me floating on my back and talking to her out loud. A man on the shore waved at me. I waved back. Nobody wins, nobody loses.
Money check: illustration is now 58% of income, engineering 42%, which is the opposite of what I said at 19. I still call myself an engineer when strangers ask because it's faster. Working on it.
Tio Beto ligou pra testar se eu lembrava a segunda estrofe de 'Asa Branca'. Lembrei. Ele desligou sem comentar, que é a versão dele de elogio.
Found an old Álgebra notebook with the parrot man in the margin. The drawing is terrible. I kept it anyway. It is the first time I ever drew someone because I was afraid of forgetting them.

It rained all day and the bus smelled like wet umbrellas. I sat in the back with my sketchbook open and drew the condensation on the window. None of the drawings looked like rain. They looked like something I couldn't name yet.

Bia and Júlia's wedding in the garden. I gave the speech and drew the invitations. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' and handed me the violão halfway through. I finished it. Bia cried at the wrong part, as usual.
Wedding leftovers in the fridge. Tio Beto's violão still on our couch, tuned to G.

Market day. Bought jabuticabas and thought of Vó Lúcia, obviously. Ate them on the balcony and Limonada dropped one small, ugly lemon into my lap while I was eating. I think she was showing off. Fair enough.

Bia and Júlia's wedding was three days ago and the house is too quiet. I keep finding little green balls from the decorations in odd places: behind the toothbrush, in my shoe, in the sugar bowl. Limonada gave us her first lemon in the middle of all that. I'm calling it the wedding lemon even though nobody asked.

At the comics fair in Curitiba, a teenager asked how I draw hands. I said 'badly, for years, until one day my mother said I got them right.' The teenager wrote it down. I hope she keeps drawing badly for years.
Bia, obrigada por casar com a Júlia e ainda assim me deixar morar na casa com vista para o mar. Eu prometo não roubar o quarto da varanda quando vocês voltarem de lua de mel.
Bought a tiny watering can shaped like a fish because it was next to the register. Limonada does not care. I care deeply.
The sea dream again, but I was teaching someone to float. Don't know who.
Worked on page 41 of the book. Vó Lúcia's laugh is impossible to draw without making her look startled. I ruined two sheets and kept the third because her hands looked right.
Money check: the book fund has enough for paper and ink, not enough for confidence. Confidence still on backorder.
At the market I found bergamotas shaped like tiny lemons. I bought all of them and put one next to Limonada's lemon on the windowsill. They look like cousins who haven't met yet.

Bia and Júlia came over for dinner. Júlia brought a lemon pie made with store lemons because Limonada's first lemon is still too small and I threatened to write a capsule about it. I'm writing the capsule anyway.

Portuguese day: Achei um desenho velho do ônibus na minha gaveta, o senhor do papagaio e tudo. Escrevi 'Seu Ivo' embaixo, depois 'Valdir' por cima, depois risquei os dois. Alguns nomes não precisam de nome.

Post-wedding apartment: confetti still in the grout. Helped clean Júlia and Bia's place and found a printed invitation I drew, signed by me, tucked behind the fridge. I think that's where important things live in this family.

At the market I saw a man carrying a green parrot on his shoulder. It said 'bom dia, motorista' to no one in particular. I didn't draw him. Some things are better as memories, I think. Or maybe I just forgot my pen.
A woman at the comics fair remembered Seu Ivo and Juca and showed me a photo on her phone. The parrot had a little blue band. I didn't remember the blue band. Now I can't forget it.
Ate feijão tropeiro on Sunday and thought about Vó Lúcia's kitchen, the way the steam fogged the window. Drew it from memory later and the steam looked wrong but the window was right.

Bia came home with a wedding planning notebook that she says is 'just a notebook' and is clearly not just a notebook. Júlia is letting her think she's in charge. I recognized the look from 2015, the one where she pretends not to be dreaming.
Comics fair table in Florianópolis: one woman remembered Seu Ivo. I gave her a drawing for free.
Rain all day. Limonada got the full south wind and lost two leaves. I moved her closer to the wall and apologized out loud. Bia heard and said 'you're talking to the tree again'. I said 'and?'.

The wedding photos arrived. There's one of me giving the speech where I look terrified and happy at the same time, which is apparently my natural state. Tio Beto is mid-clap in the background. I'm printing it for the fridge. The fridge is becoming a museum.
Tio Beto, if you're reading this with the violão: I played 'Asa Branca' again last week, alone, and didn't stop at the second verse. I think that's what you were waiting for all those years.
PT-BR: Comi um pastel de queijo na feira e lembrei do primeiro encontro com Rafa. Não senti nada de pesado, só o queijo derretendo. Achei que isso já era uma vitória.
Limonada's first real lemon is still on the branch, green and stubborn.

PT: Comprei um caderno novo só para os sonhos. O primeiro desenho do livro está quase pronto: Vó na Festa Junina, com o chapéu maior que ela. Ainda não desenhei o Coronel porque não sei se ele deve aparecer como cachorro ou como sombra. Os dois, talvez.
First lemon still on the tree. It is greener than I expected and smaller than my thumb. I look at it every time I pass the balcony, which is every ten minutes.

Passei pela Festa Junina e não tentei tocar 'Asa Branca'. Tocar no casamento da Bia em maio foi suficiente por um tempo. Tio Beto disse que estou 'guardando o violão para ocasiões importantes'. Ele tem razão e eu não vou admitir.

Festa Junina season. Tio Beto sent a voice note of himself tuning the violão and saying nothing else. I listened twice. I haven't played 'Asa Branca' in months. Maybe this weekend. Or maybe next year. We've both said that before.
Swam forty meters without stopping today. Not a race, just me and the line and the hum of the pool. Eight years ago twenty-five felt like the moon. I keep moving the moon.
Mom, your bolo de fubá this year was not dry. We cried anyway, but the good kind.
Went to Praia Mole at 6am and swam while the lifeguards were still setting up. Nobody saw me. I counted 30 strokes and then stopped counting, which felt like the point.

Winter swim today. The pool was cold enough to make me question my choices, but 18-year-old me wanted this, so I did ten laps and came out with blue lips and a ridiculous smile. Thaís asked why I was glowing. I said vitamin D. It's the swimming.

Bia, thank you for saving the room facing the sea. Thank you for the lemon pie with store lemons. Thank you for asking 'are you drawing?' even when the answer is no. You are the only person who asks like it matters.
Swam twenty laps at the pool. Nobody clapped. Dona Cida wasn't there, so I clapped for myself in the shower, quietly, like a person who has learned to be her own audience.

Tio Beto called to say he finally learned a second song and wouldn't tell me which one. He hummed four notes and hung up. I'm 70% sure it's 'Garçom' and 100% sure he'll make me guess at the next Festa Junina.
Ocean smelled like the dream this morning, warm and not dramatic. I stood with my feet in the water for one minute and then got in. Progress is sometimes just staying.

Rain on the balcony and Limonada's leaves are dark and heavy. I drew her with a tiny umbrella and felt guilty, because she's a tree and doesn't need props. Then I kept the drawing. It's cute. She deserves props.
Thaís asked for 'less personality' on a diagram. I gave her less personality. It hurt. The sun with sunglasses remains in the drawer as a secret.
Sunday drawing with Vó's farm stories; today she was twelve and Coronel stole a chicken.
Started page 40 of the book. Stopped because the dog Coronel should be braver in the last version, like he got in Vó's stories. I think she was right to make him braver each time.

Money check: illustration is now 52% of income, diagrams the rest. The 'book' fund has enough for printing fifty copies and one very good lunch. I'm keeping the lunch for the day I actually hold the finished book. Or for a bad Tuesday. Whichever comes first.
Weather turned cold suddenly. I brought Limonada inside and she sits in the corner of the room like a guest who doesn't want to impose. I keep talking to her anyway.

Money check: half my income is from illustration and the rest is from solar diagrams. The 'book' fund is growing. It is not a fortune. It is a door held open a few inches, and I'm trying not to let it close.

Rain all day. Worked from the kitchen table and drew a little comic about a lemon tree that refuses to behave. Posted it nowhere. Some drawings are just for me and Limonada, who doesn't seem impressed.
Limonada has four green balls on her branches. They could be lemons or they could be my imagination, as established. I took a photo and refused to zoom in.

Portuguese: Sonhei com Vó Lúcia de novo, mas dessa vez ela me ensinava a fazer bolo de fubá e eu dizia que estava ruim. Ela riu e disse: 'menina, é carinho que falta'. Acordei com a cozinha cheirando a algo que não existe.
One year in Floripa. Bia says I still talk about Curitiba like a person, not a city. She's right. I miss the RU pastel and the hill I never learned to drive on.
Praia Mole early, water cold, swim short, coffee hot. Perfect June.
Sol forte, mar azul demais. Desenhei a varanda de Bia por 20 minutos e depois fiquei com sol nas costas por dois dias. Ainda valeu.
Winter solstice, shortest day, but the sea was still there at 5:40 p.m., doing its thing. I made soup and drew the steam. Tiny drawing, nothing important, the best kind.

Low tide this morning. I walked out far enough that the water was only at my ankles and found tiny shells, all white, all perfect. I brought three home and put them on the windowsill next to Limonada. The lemon tree has company now. She seems unimpressed but cooperative.
Festa Junina week. I bought a little red ribbon for Limonada because she is festive now. She did not ask for it. She looks like she is going to a party in a small hat.

Tio, I played 'Asa Branca' on the violão you left at my apartment last weekend. I missed the second verse again, but only by two beats, which is practically professional. Come visit and bring the bolo de fubá recipe, the real one, not Mom's dry version.
Tio Beto, se você ler isso, eu ainda tenho o violão e ainda toco mal. Mas toco até o fim. Obrigada por não perguntar de novo até o dia em que eu pude perguntar sozinha.

At the comics fair today a teenager asked me if I still draw the bus. I said yes, but the bus is different now. She said she liked the drawings anyway. I gave her a print of Juca. She called him 'o papagaio brasileiro'.
Bia, Júlia sang off-key at dinner and you pretended to tune her with a fork.
Mom sent a voice note saying she printed page 12 of 'Menina do Mar' and put it on the fridge. She didn't say she liked it. She said 'the hands'.
Portuguese day: Choveu a tarde inteira e a Limonada ficou cheia de gotas. Tirei foto tentando fazer parecer uma floresta tropical, mas é só um vaso de limão na varanda. Acho que é suficiente.

I swam 400 meters today, not stopping. Dona Cida isn't here to cry, so I cried for both of us. The sea was warm and small fish kept bumping into my legs like they were curious. I chose to interpret it as approval.

Opened an old sketchbook and found a drawing of Vó Lúcia's hands from 2020, before she got sick. They look like they're holding something invisible. I used it as reference for page 47. It worked, finally.

Dreamed of Curitiba, the old república on Rua XV, the fridge with names on yogurts. I was looking for Limonada in a yogurt cup and woke up laughing. Sometimes nostalgia arrives disguised as absurdity. The sea dream didn't appear. I'm not worried.

Early swim, fog over the water. For a minute I couldn't see the shore and wasn't scared, which is new. The sea dream person next to me had Vó's laugh, but that's for another capsule. I just wanted to record: no fear, briefly.
Half my income illustration now, and Thaís still pays me four days a week. Lucky, careful.

PT-BR: Dia nublado, barulho de vento na janela. Trabalhei o dia inteiro no desenho do Coronel e depois fui andar na praia sem guarda-sol. O pé ficou frio, o resto quente. Esse é o tipo de dia que eu queria aos 18.
Thaís liked the new diagram with the little sun wearing sunglasses again. It is now in two decks. I am becoming the sun company.
Dreamed of the república on Rua XV, four girls and one bathroom. Woke up grateful for one bathroom and suspicious of nostalgia.
Thaís asked for a technical drawing and I gave her one with a tiny lemon tree in the corner. She said 'this is getting out of hand'. She kept it.

PT: Sonhei de novo com o mar, mas dessa vez eu não estava nadando. Estava desenhando na areia, e a onda apagava tudo. Eu não ficava triste. Acho que é progresso. Acordei e desenhei a onda antes do café, o que é um milagre.

Limonada is ten years old and gave me one ugly beautiful lemon. I made limonada. It was sour and I drank all of it. Bia said I looked like someone who had won something small and important. I think I did.

Swam with Bia at Praia Mole at 7am. She's slower than me now and furious about it. I told her floating is about trust, not technique. She splashed me. Some lessons don't transfer, but the company does.
The book has a title page now. I keep opening it to look at Vó Lúcia's hands in the drawing. They are right. I still don't know how I did that.
Choveu e a varanda virou lago. Limonada não reclamou.

Bia, thank you for saving the room facing the sea in 2019. I still stand at the window before checking my phone. Today the water was silver and you were still asleep, so I texted you a photo instead of waking you.
Dreamed I was back in the república on Rua XV, same old wood smell, and the sea drawing was still above the bed. Woke up before I could check if the lemon seeds had sprouted.

PT: Uma gata apareceu na varanda e adotou a Limonada como cama. Ficou lá a tarde toda, ronronando. Coloquei água e ela bebeu como se fosse dona do lugar. Bia disse que temos uma gata agora. Júlia disse que temos um problema. Eu desenhei os dois, a gata e a árvore, juntos.

Portuguese day: Mãe, o livro está pronto. Não mostrei para você ainda porque toda vez que penso em entregar, parece que estou entregando a Vó para alguém. Vou levar no cemitério em Irati e depois decido. Você pode vir se quiser.
I swam 25 meters in the sea today and then stood up and walked back. Dona Cida would have clapped. I clapped for myself, which felt ridiculous and necessary. Eight years ago I couldn't float.
Portuguese: O mar estava calmo demais hoje, quase desconfiado. Nadei um pouco e voltei antes de me acostumar. Acho que ainda tenho medo de achar fácil demais.
Júlia taught me a card game I immediately lost four times. I blamed the sea view distracting me. She said the sea view is the same view I've been looking at for two years, so that excuse is expired.
Picked a lemon and put it on Vó's old framed sea drawing, just to see.

Sunday drawings at Vó time. Page 58 of the book, Coronel getting braver again. I walked to the praça after and sat under a tree that doesn't remind me of jabuticaba but tried. The small publisher hasn't emailed back. I'm choosing not to check my inbox every ten minutes. I checked it nine times.

Same sea dream, first time in years. I was already swimming. I turned around and the person swimming next to me was Vó Lúcia, young, laughing like stairs. I woke up and drew it before it faded. It's the last page of the book.
Bus 7am had a baby in a tiny raincoat. The parrot man would have loved it.

Júlia brought home a bag of jabuticabas and I sat on the kitchen floor eating them and pretending I was at the farm in Irati. The skin stains your fingers purple for a day. Vó would have said I was eating them wrong. I was eating them wrong. It was perfect.
Swam next to Bia today and she kicked my goggles off by accident. I surfaced laughing, which is new. Eighteen-year-old me would not recognize me. Good.
Limonada has one tiny green fruit now. Could be a lemon, could be a decorative marble, I don't care. I took a photo and sent it to nobody because some things are for me.
PT-BR: Tio Beto perguntou pelo livro. Eu disse que estava quase pronto e ele disse 'quase não publica nada'. Riu, me entregou um café e não perguntou mais. Ele sabe.

Tio Beto, I practiced 'Asa Branca' today and got through the second verse without stopping. That's the part that always broke me. I thought of your 'one more year' and laughed out loud in the empty apartment. One more year, apparently.
Drew Vó Lúcia's farm from memory again. The jabuticabeira is always slightly too big, because that's how it felt. Some things you draw true by making them wrong.
Swimming at night is different. The sea is black and you hear yourself breathing. I stayed close to the shore. I'm not brave enough for the dark water yet, and that's fine. Bravery can wait.
Bia tried my new drawing tablet and drew a cat with six legs. She said it was 'modern'. I am keeping the file as evidence of her taste.
Swam 25 meters without stopping, again, because bodies forget and need reminders.
Mom visited and asked if I'm eating enough. I showed her the soup. She ate two bowls and said 'a little more salt, Marina' anyway. Some things are permanent and I love it.

Portuguese day: Sonhei com o Rafa, mas não triste. Ele estava na cozinha de uma festa segurando uma caixa de pastel e rindo. Acordei e deletei a playlist de vez. Não foi dor. Foi só o fim, finalmente.
Apanhei chuva voltando do supermercado e o saco de laranjas virou uma pequena fonte no caminho. A vizinha riu. Eu também. São Paulo me pareceria idiota nessa hora.
Money check: illustration pays 52% of the bills. The book fund is small but real. I named it 'MAR', which is dramatic and also accurate.

Money check: half from illustration, Thaís gave me Friday off again, savings renamed from 'MAR' to 'book' and then back to 'MAR' because I couldn't decide. The bills are paid, the lemon is dry, and I bought a new sketchbook with hard cover. Small victories, all of them.
The weather turned cold and I brought Limonada closer to the door. She has a small green lemon again, maybe. Or a stubborn flower. I don't want to decide what it is yet. It's enough that it's there.
Read three pages of 'Menina do Mar' aloud to the wall. The wall had notes. I fixed a sentence and felt like a real editor, or at least a person with a highlighter and opinions.
Mom, I still call Sundays, even though the line is quiet on your end sometimes.

Mom, the publisher meeting was fine. They liked the book and asked for 'a few changes', which is editor for 'please rewrite your heart'. I said I'd think. I'm thinking by drawing badly in the margins of their notes. It helps. I'll call Sunday, maybe Wednesday too. I know you don't like Wednesdays. I like Wednesdays now.

Worked all weekend on a diagram for a solar farm and drew the panels with little smiley faces in the margins. Thaís found them and said 'investors will think we're unserious.' Then she sent them to the whole team. Nobody complained.

At the comics fair in Curitiba, a kid asked me to draw a parrot. I drew Juca and the kid said 'that parrot looks sad'. I said 'he's moving to Ponta Grossa'. The kid didn't know what I meant. That's fine. Some jokes take 10 years.
Went swimming and Dona Cida's postcard fell off the fridge. Put it back with tape. Her handwriting says 'float first, swim second', and I keep meaning to send her a copy of the book.

A little girl at the bus stop drew a parrot on her foggy window and showed me through the glass. I didn't know her name. I waved. She waved back. That was the whole interaction and it fixed the afternoon.
Bia asked if I'm lonely living with two cats and a lemon tree. I said no, I have the sea window. She said 'that's not an answer'. I said 'it's the best one I have'.
Mãe, você viu o desenho da Limonada no meu feed? É ela antes do limão. Eu sei que você vai dizer que está parecendo o vaso e não a árvore. É vaso também.
The publisher from Curitiba emailed again. I read the email three times and then closed it. I'm not ready to say yes. I'm also not ready to say no. This is what 'thinking about it' actually means.

Swimming lesson memory: Dona Cida's voice in my head every time I panic. 'Trust, not technique.' Today I swam farther than I meant to and had to walk back along the beach. My legs were shaking. My grin was worse. I'm keeping both.
Júlia bought a lemon tree for their balcony. Now there are two, watching each other.
Money check: R$ 5.100, illustration now more than engineering. The bank app still calls the fund 'MAR' even though I renamed it 'book'. Some things don't get renamed.
PT-BR: Passei a tarde desenhando o Coronel como cachorrinho velho, deitado sob a jabuticabeira. Ficou triste e bonito ao mesmo tempo. Acho que é assim que memória funciona: não é fiel, é carinhosa.
A thunderstorm knocked out the power for three hours and I drew by candlelight because candles are cheaper than panic. The page is messy and I like it.

Bia and I took the car to Matinhos for the day. She drove because I still hate highways, and I drew the road from the passenger seat. The sea was gray and enormous and I put my feet in and didn't go further. Old habits. She didn't say anything, which is why she is my person.

Portuguese: Passou frio hoje em Florianópolis e lembrei do cobertor da república. Ainda tenho medo de quartos que cheiram a madeira velha, mas menos do que antes. O desenho da Vó Lúcia continua acima da cama, respondendo à pergunta de 2014.

Swam 400 meters today without stopping. Not a big deal, apparently, except that 18-year-old me would fall over. I didn't even think about her while swimming, which might be the biggest progress of all.
Bia, you still ask 'are you drawing?' and I still say 'yes' before I even check.
PT-BR: Fui ao mercado e comprei limão, por ironia. A caixa da despensa não tem nada a ver com Limonada e mesmo assim pedi desculpa para ela ao passar pela varanda. Estou ficando estranha, mas em paz.

Bus ride today, not even the Interbairros, just the local line to the market. A man had a small dog in a backpack and the dog was wearing sunglasses. Nobody reacted. I drew them in the margin of my shopping list. Some things never change, and I'm grateful.
Mom visited for the weekend. She stood at Bia's balcony for a long time looking at the sea and then said, 'your grandmother would have liked this window'. We didn't talk about it more. We had lunch.
Found an old bus comic strip in a folder: 'Seu Ivo e o Papagaio'. I didn't delete it. I almost did. I closed the folder and went for a swim instead.
Ran into someone at the market who said 'você é a engenheira do ônibus?' I said no, then yes, then I bought more fruit than planned because the compliment made me weak.

First lemon from Limonada, the one from January, finally ripened. I held it for a long time before cutting it. It tasted like lemon. Obviously. But it also tasted like ten years of watering something and not knowing if it would answer.

Dreamed I was standing at the edge of the sea and the water was warm. Same dream from 2014, but now I walked in before I woke up. Vó Lúcia was not there this time. I think that means she's done waiting for me to be brave.
Desenhei o gato da varanda dormindo no livro. Ele virou mascote sem autorização.
An old Interbairros reader sent a message asking if Juca the parrot ever got a friend. I wanted to say no, he had the bus. But I said maybe. Fiction is allowed to soften.
Tio Beto, toquei Asa Branca na varanda hoje, sem parar, e a Limonada não caiu nenhum limão. Acho que ela prefere música ruim. Prometo tentar de novo no Natal.
Found a green parrot on a balcony near the grocery store and said 'bom dia, motorista' to it. The owner stared. The parrot said nothing. Still counts in my heart.
Bia's invitations are done and Tio Beto approved them by saying 'bonito' once and then going back to his coffee. Highest praise available.

Thaís asked for 'something less technical' on a diagram again. I drew a tiny sun with sunglasses holding a clipboard. She laughed and said put it in the appendix. I did. The appendix now has two jokes and one serious diagram, which is my preferred ratio.
Limonada has three small lemons now. Ugly, green, perfect. Bia wants to make caipirinha with them. I said over my dead body. Then I said maybe half a lemon. Growth.
Tio Beto, o violão voltou para casa e a corda Sol continua desafinada.
Thaís asked for a 'less emotional' diagram. I gave her the least emotional drawing I could manage and it still had a tiny sun with sunglasses in the corner. She sighed and kept it. Compromise.
Portuguese: Limonada tem um limão. Só um. É feio e pequeno e eu já tirei foto de todos os ângulos. Prometi não mexer nele, mas todo dia vou lá conferir se está firme.

PT: Limonada tem três limões agora. Pequenos, tortos, perfeitos. Tirei uma foto e mandei para a mãe, que respondeu 'finalmente'. Bia diz que ela vai fazer caipirinha com o primeiro. Júlia diz que vai fazer bolo. Eu vou comer uma fatia crua com sal, como Vó fazia quando ninguém via.
Started a tiny drawing of a parrot saying 'bom dia, motorista' on the back of a receipt. Don't know why. Maybe because some characters don't die, they just move to Ponta Grossa.

I sent the book to the publisher. Then I went for a walk and ate a pastel and came home and opened my email six times to see if they had already replied. They hadn't. They won't for weeks. I know this. I opened it anyway.

I opened the capsule from September 2025 about the comics fair and the woman with Seu Ivo's strip. I still haven't written her back properly. Tomorrow, future me, tomorrow. I'm drawing the reply instead of writing it. Some things only work as pictures.
Bus was late and I stood at the stop drawing the station instead. A woman asked if I was an artist. I said 'sometimes'. She said 'that's not an answer'. I said 'I know'. She got on the next bus.
Limonada's lemon is yellow now. Yellow! Small and ugly and magnificent. I photographed it from six angles like it's a celebrity, which it is.

Portuguese day: A Limonada tem um limão que está dourando. Fico olhando toda hora como se fosse sumir. Acho que é isso que a Vó sentia quando eu dizia que iria desenhar 'um dia'. Um dia virou hoje, devagar.

Bia's garden wedding photos arrived. In one of them I'm crying at the wrong part, as usual, and Tio Beto is handing me the violão. My face is a mess and I look happy. I printed it and put it on the fridge.
A publisher in Curitiba wants to see the book. I am thinking with the window open.

Went to Irati in my head today, not in person. Drew the jabuticabeira from the story versions I wrote down in 2020. Coronel got braver in every version, so I gave him a little hero pose. He earned it.

Bia, your wedding invitation drawing took me four attempts because I kept making Limonada too small. She's not a background character in your life either. She's on the final version, slightly too big, which is correct.
Júlia fez bolo de cenoura e eu desenhei a cobertura derretendo como mar. Bia disse que eu vejo mar em tudo. Talvez. Acho que sim.

PT-BR: Domingo de desenho. Três páginas do livro, uma caminhada até a praia, um café no quiosque. A terapeuta disse para eu notar quando os dias são bons sem precisar explicá-los. Então: hoje foi bom.

Walking home from the bakery, a woman stopped me and asked if I was Marina from the bus comics. She said her son had printed 'Seu Ivo e o Papagaio' for a school project. I said Juca would be proud. She didn't know who Juca was. I explained. Both of us left happy.
Worked all day on a diagram for a solar panel array and caught myself sketching a parrot in the corner of the sheet. Thaís didn't notice. Or she did and said nothing, which is worse/better.

Tio Beto, I finally told the publisher yes. I signed on a Tuesday, which felt right because Tuesday is when Vó died and I'd rather make it a day with two meanings. 'Menina do Mar' comes out next year. I'm terrified and I'm going to be sick about it daily. Thank you for the violão, the chords, and the 'one more year'.

Went to Curitiba for the day and walked past UTFPR. The building hasn't changed. I didn't go in. I just stood there and thought about 18-year-old me in the back row drawing the sea instead of paying attention. She was right to.
Dream of the sea changed again: I was floating, and Vó was on the sand, clapping.
The small publisher asked for two more sample pages. I opened the file and stared for an hour. Then I drew Vó Lúcia's laugh as stairs and it was fine.
Hoje a Bia mandou foto da Limonada pela janela dela. O mar e a árvore no mesmo enquadramento. Escrevi 'finalmente' e ela respondeu com um coração, o que ela nunca faz. Guardei o print.
A tiny publisher in Curitiba emailed again. I haven't replied. The email sits open on my desktop between diagrams and a drawing of Vó's hands.
Read page 64 aloud to no one, just to hear how it sounds. The last line is 'menina do mar'. My voice cracked on 'mar'. I think that's correct.
The publisher in Curitiba asked if I could send the manuscript by October. I opened the email, closed it, made tea, opened it again. The tea cooled. I am very brave in small steps.

'Menina do Mar' is finished. 64 pages. I printed one copy and took it to Vó Lúcia's grave in Irati and read it out loud, which is ridiculous and I don't care. A small publisher in Curitiba wants to see it. I said I'd think about it. Future me: did you say yes?

The publisher emailed again. I read it three times and closed the tab. I'm going to say yes. I just need to sit with the fear for one more day, like the therapist taught me, except she probably didn't mean three months.
Portuguese: Outubro começa e eu ainda não decidi nada sobre o livro. Mas desenho toda semana, e isso não é nada.
Six years. The sea dream from July was Vó Lúcia, young, laughing like stairs. I drew it before it faded. It is the last page and I think it's the truest one.

Six years without Vó Lúcia today. I lit a candle on the balcony and Limonada shed a flower, dramatic tree. I drew her hands from memory again, because Mom said I got them right once and I want to keep getting them right.

Six months of savings again. I keep counting because counting makes the courage feel real. The fund is called 'MAR' still, even though now I live closer to the sea. Names don't have to update just because you moved.
Money check: book fund bigger than sea fund. The bank app still says MAR.

Morning swim and the water was so calm I could see my hands under it. Dona Cida's words came back: floating is about trust, not technique. I floated for one minute and thought of Vó Lúcia's cold hands in 2020. I didn't sink. I never sink anymore.
Went to Irati for the weekend. Ate bolo de fubá at a bakery that wasn't Vó's and cried a little in the car. Tio Beto said 'menina do mar, you're allowed'. I drew the bakery from memory.
Woke up from the sea dream with my calves loose, not tight. Small difference, enormous news. I wrote it in the margin before it disappeared.

A woman messaged me saying her grandfather was Seu Ivo's neighbor in Ponta Grossa and that he used to whistle 'Asa Branca' to Juca every morning. I didn't invent that part. Some stories just find their way to you if you draw long enough.
Said yes. The email took forty seconds to write and cost me a night of sleep. Feels like jumping into water you know is warm but your feet still hesitate.
The publisher sent the first layout proofs. My name on the cover looks too small and too big at the same time. I stared at it until Fermento bit my toe and broke the spell.
Pastel de feira na praia, areia no desenho, limão no pastel. Bom dia.
Júlia made bolo de fubá using Vó Lúcia's recipe from my notebook. It was closer this time. Mom ate a second slice without commenting, which is her highest praise.
Ate a lemon from Limonada today. It was sour and perfect and I cried a little at the kitchen sink, which feels like the correct response to a tree keeping a promise.
Woke up with my calves tight again, the old dream, the sea at the edge. This time I hadn't even reached the water. I drew it in three lines and felt better.

The sea dream returned, but shorter this time: just the water, warm, no one swimming next to me. I woke up and drew it before coffee. It's not the last page of the book anymore. Maybe it's the first page of the next one.

Tio Beto, I played 'Asa Branca' this morning without the sheet music. Not perfectly. I missed a chord and laughed at myself, which is new. You would have said 'one more year' and meant 'one more year'. Obrigada por esperar.

PT: Acordei de um sonho em que Vó Lúcia me ensinava a tocar 'Asa Branca' no violão, devagar, nota por nota. Ela errava também. Isso foi o melhor: ela errava e ria. Desenhei a mão dela no braço do violão antes de esquecer. Acho que vai ser a capa do livro. Ou não. Ainda não decidi. Gosto de não decidir.
Limonada's lemons are getting slightly bigger. I measured one with a ruler like a lunatic. 4.2 centimeters. I'm not sure what that means except that I care.
Desenhei Seu Ivo de memória e Juca saiu maior que o ônibus. Vai ter que ficar assim.
Found the Interbairros postcard from Lisbon taped behind my monitor. The parrot man had a bandage. I never drew the bandage. I think I will now.
Swam with Bia on Sunday. She's faster. She always was. I don't mind; the sea doesn't care who wins.
PT-BR: Chuva forte, luz caindo. Desenhei uma strip de 'Interbairros' por puro saudosismo, Seu Ivo e o Juca na chuva. Não postei. Guardei no caderno. Alguns personagens podem descansar.

Bia's wedding invitations are almost done. She asked for 'something with the sea' and I drew the window from her room with two chairs. She cried. Júlia said it was 'very tasteful', which in Júlia language means she loved it.

PT: O mar hoje estava verde, quase esmeralda. Nadei até a bóia e voltei. Ninguém na praia me conhece. Essa frase, que aos 18 seria triste, hoje é só liberdade. Desenhei a bóia com a onda passando por cima. Vou usar no livro novo, se houver livro novo.

Hoje nadei no mar cedo e depois desenhei Vó no caderno, jovem, rindo. A última página do livro está quase pronta. Quando eu terminar, vou até Irati e vou ler tudo em voz alta. Ridículo. Não me importo.
Swam in the sea before work. A small fish crossed my lane, which is to say I crossed its. We both survived. This counts as a successful morning.

Finished a drawing of Limonada at ten years old, flowers and one ugly lemon. Put it next to the yogurt-cup photo from 2016. The difference is ridiculous and tender. If anyone asks, I will say I'm not emotional about a lemon tree. I am.
Bia, Júlia and I watched the fireworks from the balcony; Limonada survived with two lemons.
Portuguese day: Bia, se o casamento tiver música ruim eu vou tocar 'Asa Branca' no violão sem pedir licença. Você sabe que eu consigo. Também sei que você vai chorar. Está anotado.
Fiz um desenho da Limonada com três limões pequenos pendurados, embora hoje ela só tenha flores. Talvez seja desejo. Ou propaganda interna.

Ate pastel de feira at the market and thought about Rafa for one second, then about the pastel for the other 30 seconds. Progress. The pastel was better than I remembered. Time helps pastels too, apparently.

Drew Mom at the stove from a photo on my phone. She has the same expression as Vó when concentrating: mouth slightly open, not listening to anything else. I didn't know I noticed that until I drew it.
Money check: four days of work, three of drawing. The bank app still says 'MAR' on the savings fund, even though it is the book fund now. I'm not renaming it. It's the same sea.

Portuguese: Hoje é aniversário de quem não está mais aqui e eu não sabia o que fazer. Desenhei a mão dela, porque é o que sei fazer melhor, e ficou parecida. Guardei o desenho na gaveta, não na parede. Ainda não é dia de parede.
Bia and Júlia's wedding photos arrived and in every one Bia is laughing at the wrong moment. It is the most Bia thing. I saved three for the book if she lets me.

Mãe, hoje eu acordei com saudade da sua voz antes do café. Liguei e você me contou que a impressora parou de funcionar e que você já desmontou ela inteira. Você vai consertar, eu sei. É de onde eu venho: de gente que desmonta as coisas até entender.
November started hot, no wind, and I worked on the balcony until my sunscreen gave up. Thaís asked if the solar diagram was 'beach themed'. It is now.

Daylight saving ended and I forgot, so I showed up to swimming an hour early. The beach was empty except for one old man fishing. He offered me a piece of his bolo. We ate in silence. I think that's the best conversation I've had all month.
Drew the bus driver from memory, old route, old light. He had a mustache I'm not sure was real. Memory edits things. I let it.
Swimming lesson energy at 30: I still swallow water when I'm not paying attention. Dona Cida would call me a engenheira. I call myself a work in progress. The sea doesn't care either way.

Mom called to ask if I'd 'given up on the drawings yet'. I said no. She was quiet and then said 'good'. That's the whole conversation, and it was enough to make me sit at the table and draw for an hour.
Tio Beto sent a voice note saying the violão needs new strings and asking if I am 'still one of the musical cousins.' I said yes. The violão arrived by bus with a note that just said 'uma vez mais.'
Mom, I found the strip you printed years ago, the one with the old man. It's in your kitchen drawer, behind the receitas. You were right, he does look like Grandpa. Thank you for keeping it there.

Bus ride to the market, windows open, warm. A kid was drawing on the fogged glass with one finger. I wanted to tell him to keep going but he got off at the next stop. I hope he draws on real paper too.

Mom stayed for a week and learned to water Limonada by measuring with her finger. She said 'your grandmother would have talked to her.' I said I do talk to her. She said 'then you're doing fine.' That's the whole review.
Mom came up for the weekend and sat on Bia's balcony for an hour without saying anything. Then she said 'your grandmother would like this view'. I didn't answer because my throat closed.
The publisher sent a contract with a font so small it looked like a dare. I printed it, read it slowly, and called Bia. She said 'say yes'. I'm thinking about saying yes.

Portuguese day: Hoje é aniversário de quando comecei as aulas de natação em 2021. Dona Cida, se você estiver lendo isto em algum lugar, ainda engulo água quando não presto atenção. Mas nado. E isso, para a Marina de 18 anos, já é milagre.

Júlia found my old sketchbook from the república years. She held up a drawing of the sea and said 'you already knew'. I said I didn't, not really. She said that's the point of drawings, they know first.

The publisher in Curitiba emailed back. I read it three times and didn't answer because answering would make it real. Then I answered. I said I'd think about it, which is what I said before. I think I already know. I just need to say it out loud, maybe to the sea.
Finally answered the publisher. One sentence: 'I'd like to see your terms.' Pressed send and then went to make tea because my hands were shaking.
PT-BR: Limonada ganhou um limão. Pequeno, torto, do tamanho de um dedo. Eu quase chorei no meio da varanda. Bia me viu e fingiu que não, o que foi o melhor gesto possível.

Bia, your mother-in-law sent me a photo of Júlia's wedding dress hanging in their closet, and I cried in the supermarket. The cashier asked if I was okay. I said allergies. In November. She didn't believe me either. Thank you for letting me be the person who cries at the wrong things.
Swam in the rain because the pool was empty and Dona Cida's voice is in my head saying 'trust, not technique'. I trusted the rain. It worked.
Worked on a diagram of a solar panel that looked, by accident, like a very serious sun. Thaís said 'keep it'. The sun industry continues.

Found an old 'Interbairros' notebook in a box. The parrot man's bandage, the 7am bus, the algebra margins. I'm not scanning it or posting it. I just wanted to sit with it for a while and remember that 18-year-old me drew on everything.

The book has 64 pages and I'm afraid to send it. I put it in a folder on my desktop called 'draft' because 'draft' is softer than 'finished'. Future me, if you're reading this and it's published, I hope you remember the fear was small compared to the story.

I said yes to the publisher. Out loud, to the sea, on a Tuesday. The sea didn't answer, which I appreciate. Now I have to make the book real, and the fear is quieter than I expected. Not gone. Just quieter.

The book has a cover now, a rough one. Vó's hand, the violão, the sea behind. Thaís saw it and said 'that's not a diagram'. I said 'no'. She said 'good'. I'm considering this my performance review for the year.
Rain in Floripa and Limonada got her first real lemon. Small, lopsided, green. I held it in my palm and it felt heavier than it was.
Mom called to ask if I'm 'still drawing that grandmother book'. I said yes. She said 'good' and hung up. It was a long good.
Swam in the sea with Bia at Praia Brava. She was faster than me, which she will never let me forget. The water was green and cold and exactly right.
Money check: the book advance is small and will be spent on paper and ink and probably too many coffees. Still the best money I've ever been paid. It has a smell. I'm keeping it.

Portuguese: Noite quente, janela aberta, o mar fazendo barulho de quem não quer dormir. Bia ronca no quarto ao lado. Júlia também. Limonada cheira a sal. Acho que esta vida é a que eu pedi em 2014, só que com mais gente.

Dona Cida sent a postcard from her pool. She still calls me 'a engenheira'. She said the water was cold and she swam anyway. I put it on the fridge next to Limonada's flower photo. The fridge is doing a lot of work lately.
Sunday, no one calling anymore, so I called Tio Beto. He played Asa Branca over the phone and I sang, badly, until the second verse. Then I stopped and laughed.

PT: Chuva forte o dia todo. Fiquei em casa desenhando a Limonada com seus três limões. Coloquei um detalhe: as raízes da árvore saindo do vaso, porque é assim que me sinto ultimamente, meio fora do pote mas viva. Tio Beto ia dizer que isso é coisa de artista. Ele teria razão.
Tio Beto sent a voice note playing 'Asa Branca' with mistakes in the same places I make them. I replayed it four times. Some inheritances are not genetic. Some are musical and wrong in the same way.

Money check: illustration paid for Bia's wedding invitation paper. The book fund is back to starting over. I moved R$ 50 into 'MAR' just to see it light up. It's still a silly fund and I still love it.
PT-BR: Desenhei Vó Lúcia jovem, rindo, com as mãos no rosto. Página 63. Demorei três dias porque queria acertar o começo do riso, alto, caindo como escada. Acho que consegui.

Decorated Limonada with a tiny green ball again, like last year. She looks ridiculous and beautiful. Bia says she's the most decorated lemon tree in Florianópolis. I said 'she's the only lemon tree I know', which is both true and sad.

Tio, I played 'Asa Branca' for Limonada on the balcony. She didn't clap, but she has two lemons now, so maybe she was listening. Obrigada por não desistir de me ensinar, mesmo quando eu esquecia o segundo verso por nove anos.

Rain again. The balcony smells like wet leaves and something citrus. I stood there for ten minutes with my hands in my pockets and thought about nothing important. These are the moments I want to keep and can't, so I'm writing them down.
Drew the kitchen at the república from memory, four girls and one bathroom. I got the fridge wrong; there were too many yogurts. Nostalgia is not reliable, but it is warm.

I went back to Curitiba for a weekend and took the Interbairros for old times' sake. The 7am bus. No parrot. No Seu Ivo. But the driver was the same one, I think, and he said 'bom dia, motorista' to himself as a joke. I laughed so hard I missed my stop.
Decorated the balcony with one string of lights. Limonada looks festive and slightly ridiculous. I relate to her strongly this month.
Bia found a tiny Christmas ball and hung it in Limonada's branches. The lemon is still there. Green and red. I didn't plan that.
Bia, Limonada gave a second lemon. Smaller, greener, equally impossible. I showed it to Júlia and she said 'finally, she's employed.' I laughed so hard I missed my bus. Worth it.
Thaís asked if I could stay one more year at the startup. I said maybe. The maybe felt honest, which is new for me. Limonada's lemon stayed on the branch, so I said maybe to her too.

Put up tiny lights on the balcony. Limonada has one lemon left and the lights make it look like a small green planet. Bia says it's tacky. Bia came back twice to look at it. Tacky is just beauty that doesn't apologize.
Made bolo de fubá from Vó's recipe, the one Mom keeps in her handwriting. It came out right this time. Not as good as Vó's, but right. I cried while grating the coconut and called it allergies.
Money check: R$ 200 left and it's the 12th. I bought coffee I didn't need because the man at the counter has a parrot on a poster behind him and it felt like a sign. It wasn't. It was just coffee.
Portuguese: Achei um esboço antigo do Seu Ivo e do papagaio em um caderno. O papagaio tinha nome errado, Juca. Só depois soube que ele era Valdir. Alguns nomes errados viram verdade de outro jeito.

The publisher sent the first layout of the book. Sixty-four pages look different on a screen than in my hands. I printed one page and taped it to the fridge next to the old 'Interbairros' strip Mom printed in 2018. They look like they belong to the same person. I think they do.
Read the last page of 'Menina do Mar' out loud to the sea, which is a strange thing to do and I recommend it. Vó Lúcia laughed like stairs in the last line and it stayed in the air.
Went to the sea at night, just to look. The waves sounded like stairs going down. I didn't go in. I didn't need to.

PT-BR: Fiz uma lista de coisas que não fiz em 2026: não publiquei o livro, não voltei para Irati, não aprendi a fazer pão. Nada disso parece falha hoje, só promessa adiada. Acho que isso é maturidade, ou cansaço. Quero acreditar que é maturidade.
Portuguese day: Último desenho do ano: a Vó nova, nadando do meu lado, rindo como escada. É a última página do livro. Não sei se vou publicar. Sei que terminei. E isso, por enquanto, é o suficiente.

New Year prep: Bia wants champagne, Júlia wants farofa, Mom wants early bedtime and pretending she'll make it to midnight. I drew the four of us on the balcony with Limonada between us. We look ridiculous and loved. I'll open this when the fear is gone. If it's gone.
Money check: the book fund is still small, but the MAR fund has water in it again. I like that my savings account has two personalities, one for dreams and one for courage, and both smell like salt.

Mom, I made the bolo de fubá with your recipe and the wet cloth trick. It's still not Vó's. But you ate two slices and said nothing, which is your highest compliment. I'm framing that silence. Merry early Christmas. Bring the printer paper, we're printing the proof.
Final swim of the year. The sea was rough and I didn't go far, just far enough to feel the current pull and know I can stay. That sentence would have been a fantasy in 2014. It's just Saturday now.

Packed for Curitiba for Christmas. Brought the test copy of the book, not to show anyone, just to have it near. Also brought Mom's printer ink because she always forgets. Some gifts are not gifts, they're maintenance.

I called the publisher and left a voicemail. I said I'd send the book. Then I deleted the voicemail and sent an email instead, which is less brave but more legible. The email is still in my outbox. I'll press send tomorrow.
Last Sunday before Christmas, Júlia made bolo de fubá with Mom's recipe. It was right this time. Nobody said anything. Nobody needed to.

End of the year. Limonada has three lemons. The book has a cover. Bia and Júlia are arguing about cat food in the kitchen. Mom is on the phone. The sea is doing its usual thing outside. Nothing dramatic. Everything I wanted.

Bia and Júlia put lights on the balcony railing and Limonada has a tiny star on top, not a green ball this year. I took a photo before it got dark. The sea was black behind her and she looked like she belonged there.
Mom called to say she is coming up for New Year's. She also asked if I have 'given up on the drawings yet.' I said no. She laughed. It sounded like she expected that answer.

Christmas Eve. Mom made the bolo de fubá and it was almost right this time. Nobody said 'almost.' I said it, and Mom laughed and said 'you got my hands right,' which means she was paying attention. I'm writing this ten years before the next capsule opens because that's how time works here. Future me: I hope the lemon tree is still there. I hope you are too.
Christmas Eve at Mom's. The bolo de fubá was right again. Tio Beto played 'Asa Branca' and this time I sang, badly, from the kitchen. Mom didn't say anything. Tio Beto nodded like I'd passed an exam.

PT: Primeiro Natal com Júlia officially na família, embora ela já fosse. Mom trouxe o bolo de fubá e eu trouxe o violão. Tocamos 'Asa Branca' até o fim, Bia cantou errado, Júlia filmou. Limonada tem quatro limões pendurados e uma gata dormindo embaixo. Achei que ia sentir falta de Curitiba. Não senti. Senti falta de Vó, mas isso é todo dia, e todo dia também é dia de desenhar.

PT-BR: Última semana do ano. Trabalhei pouco, desenhei muito, dormi cedo. Acordei com a janela azul e pensei que 18-year-old me teria achado isso impossível. 30-year-old me achou normal. Esse é o milagre.
Portuguese: Limonada está com dois limões agora. Pequenos, feios, lindos. Fiz lemonade com um e ficou azeda demais. Mesmo assim bebi tudo, porque é o primeiro fruto de dez anos de espera.
Last night of the year. Limonada's lemon is still there, small and ugly and perfect. I'm not picking it yet. Some things need to stay on the branch a little longer, including this.

Tomorrow is New Year's. I am writing this early so the capsule can join the others. If future me reads this, know that 2026 smelled like salt, tea, and lemon leaves, and that I am less afraid than I was in January, which is all I ever asked for.

Last day of the year. I'm writing this on the balcony with the cat on my lap and the sea doing its usual thing. The book is coming out in March. I'm scared. I'm also swimming tomorrow, first swim of the year, early, before anyone is watching. Eighteen-year-old me asked if I still have a lemon tree. I do. I have a whole life around it now.

New Year on the balcony again. Mom, Bia, Júlia, me, Limonada and her one remaining lemon. The sea did its usual thing. I swam out a little at midnight and Bia screamed. I hope 2036 me still knows this exact sound.
